top_reviews.content:
Visiting our daughter and son‑in‑law in Williamsburg, we decided to order takeout from a place they had enjoyed before. We chose a variety of dishes—rolls, chirashi, and an outstanding eggplant with garlic sauce. I never imagined eggplant could be prepared so deliciously. Everything was packed thoughtfully, with hot and cold items separated, and the rice bedding for the chirashi packed on its own.
The sashimi and sushi were fresh and expertly prepared. Since the foundation of good sushi is the rice, A‑un absolutely nails it. Prices range from moderate to high, but the quality makes it feel like a worthwhile luxury—something we’re happy to indulge in on special occasions.

Great experience ! Food was good and service great . The food was so flavorful I had the oyster crunchy rice bowl and loved the crunch and flavor and my partner had the curry udon which was also flavorful . Food came out pretty fast the server was knowledgeable helpful and friendly. Definitely go!

Me and my boyfriend have been coming here quite often. A Un is our favorite place for sushi and just good Japanese food in general. If you are having a bad day, go to A Un and you will leave happy and relaxed. We fell in love with the atmosphere and the food from our first visit. Coming here makes me happy! You absolutely have to try their eggplant-it’s amazing. Their curry is delicious, I love their vegetable croquette. They have delicious buns-I’ve had the vegetable croquette and the oyster one :) their sushi is always so fresh. The salmon is like butter! I recommend adding the crispy topping. We also love their chicken katsu bowl. I’ve tried the garlic shrimp and it was 10/10. I plan to try more of their items! Wonderful service, the staff is attentive and friendly. The dishes they serve their food and drinks on are beautiful, everything is always plated so nicely. You can tell they prepare their food with love and attention to detail. Wish I had taken more pictures to share but I don’t usually photograph my food. Anyways, we love A Un and will continue to dine here and try all of their amazing dishes. Thank you for bringing such wonderful place and experience to Bushwick.

I honestly hate to leave a low review like this for a place with such amazing food, but sometimes 1 inconsiderate action and bad service can ruin the entire experience. I sent my partner here to have a solo dinner because they had a bad day. She arrived and ordered her food, the place was empty but filled up shortly after she arrived, still no issues, delicious food. However right after she paid and TIPPED her server was rushing her to leave, this was very rude to do because she was just waiting for her cab. It’s very cold outside and we just didn’t appreciate that. I understand restaurants get busy and this is kind of a small space it’s just not the right way to go about it. The way she was treated as a solo diner ordering multiple items was just very rude. She wasn’t even there for more than an hour. If they would’ve just sat her at the bar or at a smaller table there would have been no need to rush, but because they couldn’t anticipate it getting crowded she got rushed out. So just keep that in mind if you decide to have a nice dinner to cheer yourself up you might get rushed out to seat a larger group. If she wasn’t alone they wouldn’t have done that. It’s was weird and rude once again.

Their wagyu udon was so good, and a reasonable price for brunch. Loved the sweet broth that they used. Pork cutlet curry was also so cleanly cooked 👌 Would definitely come back here again to try more items!

My first visit to Peaches Lewis and it was so good. Definitely soul food with a variety of people enjoying the menu items.  I ordered the salmon entree with artichokes  and, a side of brussels sprouts and a side of cornbread that was so delicious, it could be it's own best item.  It was within walking distance of the Akwaaba Bed n Breakfast where I'm staying.  Definitely will go again next time I visit Brooklyn.  It's in the Park Slope area.  The staff was attentive to details and very gracious.   I will be recommending Peaches Lewis.

If you’re looking for a good soul food spot, Brooklyn… look no further than Peaches. This place never disappoints.
Located in a historic Bed-Stuy brownstone, it has that classic Brooklyn charm while still feeling like a go-to neighborhood gem. I tried the over-baked grits, blackened catfish with a Caesar salad, Brussels sprouts, a grand mimosa, and the baked ziti—and honestly, I enjoyed everything.
The flavors were on point, the portions were satisfying, and even the prices were reasonable, which is always a plus. The vibe is chill, welcoming, and perfect whether you’re dining inside or taking advantage of the outdoor seating.
If you’re in the area, this is definitely a must-try

Stopped by with a couple friends and the wait was as expected for seating 5.
The waitress was very attentive. We started with catfish fritters and wings with mimosas. We all had some variation of the French toast platter. Everyone enjoyed their meal. I will be back.

I had brunch with a couple friends at Peaches this past Monday and had a great time! Our server, May, was knowledgeable, accommodating, and very kind. I ordered the fried chicken and French toast and it was incredible. We will be back!

top_reviews.content: Jerk Salmon is amazing, tender and juicy, on the bit spicy side. Drinks are consistently good and many flavors to choose. Music and the vibe are definitely upbeat and cheering. This is what I need and truly recommended.

Overall rating: 4.7

I went here with my parents for my birthday. We wanted something lowkey and also it was 5pm. It was pretty empty and there was one host/waitress/everything. She was really nice and very patient as we tried to figure out what we wanted. Whenever I don’t drink, my service dips but this one stayed consistent which I lied. We ordered the below:

- Fried chicken sandwich 5/5 - absolutely delicious, a must
- Smash burger 3/5 - a tad too spicy
- Tacos: 3/5 - okay, nothing special
- Chocolate hazel cake 5/5 - very rich. When they realized it was my birthday the whole restaurant sung and it was sweet.

The only odd part is when we got our bill, it was for Zuri Lee Restaurant. And when we charged the card, it was for Brooklyn Bathhouse. Not sure if they’re all the same owner.

Definitely want to come back for brunch or a happy hour. The service was so nice.

If you're looking for me, I'm probably still thinking about these mimosas.

$24 unlimited mimosas? Say less. I accepted the challenge and proudly sampled every flavor. For scientific purposes, of course. Every single one was delicious, and my glass never had a chance to get lonely because the refills came faster than I could finish them.

Now let's talk about the food because WOW. The jerk chicken waffle deserves its own fan club. The chicken was so tender and juicy it practically melted. Then came the oxtails and grits...that meat was falling off the bone like it had somewhere else to be. The portions were HUGE. I couldn't finish it, so it became my midnight snack—and somehow tasted just as amazing hours later.

The vibe? Immaculate. The service? Top tier. The waitstaff and bartender were friendly, attentive, and kept everything moving without ever making us wait.

Come for the unlimited mimosas, stay because the food will have you questioning every brunch you've ever had. I would recommend this place a thousand times over...just make sure you don't have any important plans after brunch. 🍾🥂😂

If you want it even more over-the-top and comedic, I can make it sound like a viral Yelp review.

I have come to this spot for the cycling services multiple times over the years and just never had the time to stop in for food till this evening with a friend. It was an amazing experience, the Jerk Salmon was flaky, flavorful and hot. My friend Thor if hay enjoyed the double stack burger as well. The Rum punch was fruity, flavorful , and potent. Across the board great service from begin to end. I will be returning for sure with my wife next time!

Took my mom for dinner for her birthday. This was not a pleasant experience. The restaurant was a bit warm. The waitress was not very pleasant. She came back once to ask if we were done, then told us whenever we were ready for the bill to let her know. Never asked if we needed anything else or how was the food or if the drinks were ok, nor did she suggest anything. In addition, I asked for a container to take the rest of my food home, and I was given a container with bo bag. Also charged an extra 3 dollars for a coke, when I never ordered a coke. Good thing I checked my bill. I love to support black businesses, but not with mediocre service like this.

I loved everything about this place. I’m not sure if the young was the manager or the owner however she was so nice to me, my mobility is limited so she helped to and from my seat even going so far as to help me walk to the car. I’m definitely going back so I could reward her for all her help.

Absolutely awful experience from start to finish. The service was terrible, and the food was bland and overpriced. The worst part was how I was treated. I went to the restroom and had only been inside for about five minutes when the biracial waitress knocked on the door four separate times. I never saw her do that to anyone else, and it made me feel singled out and racially profiled. It was humiliating, unnecessary, and incredibly unprofessional. Instead of feeling like a valued customer, I felt rushed and unwelcome. There are far better restaurants with better food, better service, and staff who know how to treat people with respect. I will never return and would strongly discourage anyone from dining here. Save your money and go somewhere that actually values its customers.

Went in passing by and ordered to go. Food was amazing. Fast forward I have ordered via Uber Eats a few times and it was great. But today was horrible. The jerk wings had feathers on them, and the jerk chicken mean  was a mess. The jerk chicken was under cooked, the rice overcooked (should have been the reverse). The plantains were the same.

top_reviews.content:
Time Out Market New York is a fantastic place to sample a wide variety of food under one roof while enjoying stunning views of the Brooklyn Bridge and Manhattan skyline. The atmosphere is lively and energetic, making it a great spot for both locals and tourists.

We enjoyed exploring the different food vendors and found the quality to be consistently good. There is something for everyone, from classic New York favorites to international cuisine. The rooftop seating area offers spectacular views and is a wonderful place to relax with a meal or drink.

It can get quite crowded during peak hours, so finding a table may require a little patience. However, the vibrant atmosphere and excellent food selection make it well worth the visit. A must-visit destination when exploring Brooklyn and the DUMBO area.

Great place to visit if you’re with a group or just can’t decide what to eat. There are plenty of food and drink options from some of NYC’s most popular restaurants, so everyone can find something they like. The atmosphere is lively, and it’s a fun place to hang out.  ￼

Don’t miss the rooftop after your meal. It has fantastic views of the Brooklyn Bridge, Manhattan Bridge, and the Manhattan skyline, making it a great spot to click pictures or just take in the scenery. Best of all, the rooftop is free to access.  Look for the elevator or stairs next to the entrance .

A fun place with lots to do and eat! We had a wonderful time here, especially on the rooftop. The best views of the Brooklyn & Manhattan bridges. My only complaints are the lack of women’s restrooms. I waited in a very long line for at least 20 minutes during peak time. But the restroom was very clean and maintained! The unisex bathrooms had much shorter lines, but are not cleaned and maintained throughout the day...GROSS. Also, it took a while for staff to clean up dining spaces where guests left their trays and leftovers. Otherwise, we had a great experience and will return when the weather warms up!

6/2/2026, Went to this place to see and taste some of the foods of the small businesses. To my surprise I decided to try the Pastrami Sandwich and to my surprise it was tasteful though I had better. You have a variety of small businesses of food vendors to try their food. I was truly impressed with the amount of food vendors. It has been years since a visited Dumbo area and a lot changed.

Time Out Market New York is where great food meets the true energy of the city. The atmosphere perfectly captures the spirit of New York — stylish design, vibrant ambiance, excellent service, and a well-curated culinary concept. The market brings together some of the city’s strongest food concepts, each delivering quality and attention to detail.
The food is outstanding: fresh ingredients, bold flavors, and beautiful presentation. What makes this place special is the diversity — from elevated street food to creative chef-driven dishes. This is far more than just a food hall; it’s a modern gastronomic destination worth visiting again and again. A perfect spot for both tourists and anyone who genuinely appreciates great food and the atmosphere of a world-class city.

Time Out Market New York has a wide array of fantastic food, drink and dessert options. We ordered the barbecue and was BLOWN away! We got the carnitas (plaited on top a smashed fried plaintain, cilantro lime salsa) with a side of fried plantains and Mac and cheese and the flavors and textures were amazing. The line was very long for barbecue and the brisket sold out right as we got to the front as it’s very popular. We also got a bolognese pasta dish that was very good too.

The views of the city are also next level. From the second floor you can get a view/photo of the Brooklyn view that rivals 5 star dining restaurants but at a fraction of the price.

A great spot, especially on a rainy day. The market brings together a huge variety of food vendors under one roof, offering everything from different cuisines to coffee, desserts, and ice cream. It’s a perfect option when everyone in your group is craving something different.

There’s plenty of seating, the atmosphere is lively, and the whole space is well organized. One of the highlights is the outdoor area at the back, which has a beautiful view of the river and makes for a nice place to sit when the weather is good.

We loved having so many choices in one place without needing to decide on a single restaurant. Whether you’re looking for a full meal, a coffee break, or something sweet, you’ll probably find it here. Definitely worth a visit while in New York. 😊🍽️☕🍦🌉

Time Out Market New York was an amazing experience! Super busy and full of energy, which really added to the atmosphere. There are so many great food options all under one roof, making it perfect if you want to try different cuisines with friends or family. The highlight for me was definitely the view from the 5th floor — absolutely stunning, especially overlooking the Brooklyn Bridge and skyline. Even with the crowds, the place was well organized and the vibe was fantastic. Definitely worth visiting when in NYC!

top_reviews.content: The Resturant is an absolute joy!!!  The atmosphere was filled with smooth grooves, ethnic, diverse, and the food melts in your mouth.   The service with Amanda was on point and Danny knows how to make a mean Lemon Drop.

We went with the steak frites and wings, and both were tasty choices. The steak was supposed to be medium rare but came out more medium, which was a small miss. That said, it was still juicy, flavorful, and enjoyable. The wings were cooked perfectly and had a nice tender texture. Overall, we had a good meal and liked both dishes. I’d give the steak another try next time and would definitely order those wings again!

Food was alright.  The chicken and waffle.. the chicken was over fried and  quite dry.  The fudge brownie was delicious.  We had a birthday group of 8 next to us, so it was quite loud and hard to hear ourselves.

I went for a memorial there and the food was very good so I ordered wings to go and it took well over an 1hr to receive my order. I asked did they have to go kill the chickens , pluck? Clean and then cook them🤔. The young waiters didnt seem to wanna work and are dressed in scantily clad clothing very un professional for the establishment. There was no air conditioning despite it being very hot outside that day because had the doors open. No ceiling fans made it worse.
Let me tell you this bbq chicken is DELICIOUS! 10 out of 10, perfect spicy level, the salad with a perfect sweetness and the Mac&cheese literally one of the best that I have tried!
I enjoyed my experience at Rustik tavern for bottomless brunch. The waitress was very attentive to our table, despite not making a reservation we were accommodated! 10/10 experience!

We have been a couple of times and the food has been good. Today we had chicken and waffles and fish with fries as well as mimosas. The main complaint is there was no discernable part of chicken, just humks of breading with some chicken inside... almost like tempura but more crunchy. We took home leftovers but it turned out to be just more breading and very little chicken. I'd probably just get shrimp and grits like last time. That was excellent.

Amanda made our brunch experience amazing! From the moment we sat down, she was warm, friendly, and just had that genuine, down-to-earth energy that makes you feel comfortable right away. She was super attentive without being overbearing, and her memory was honestly impressive—she didn’t miss a single detail of our order.

I ordered the French toast with scrambled eggs and home fries, and everything was delicious. The French toast portion was HUGE—definitely enough for two people to share, which I loved. And of course, we had to do the bottomless mimosas, and Amanda kept them coming perfectly.

What really stood out to me was her vibe—she’s truly a girls’ girl. She was honest, personable, and made great suggestions. You can tell she genuinely cares about her customers having a great experience. Some of us remembered her from last year.

If you go for brunch, ask for Amanda—you won’t regret it!

Do yourself a favor and try it out! You’re welcome!

Great experience and comfortable place to hang out. We ended up lingering after finishing our food for quite a while. The egg sandwich I got was delicious. Menu is absolutely massive, tons of options. Thought prices were slightly high. Will return!

Amazing amazing amazing!  I came here with my family for my mom in-laws birthday on Cinco de Mayo. The seating for three and fast. The food was the best thing. It was amazing delicious very authentic to its heritage. We were entertained by mariachi band on cinco de mayo. It was festive and memorable. Will be coming back for sure !!

Wow, simply just wow.  Excellent Mexican breakfast joint.  Friendly staff. Food came quick.

Got a big burrito with all the fillings. There are many options for whatever you want. Their spicy hot sauce will wake you up in the AM. Good for big groups and kids too. Good stuff!

The NACHOS are amazing!!!  Black beans in the nachos makes me feel like I was in abuela’s kitchen.

top_reviews.content: Super cute atmosphere with a cozy, charming back patio. The food and drinks are good, though not particularly memorable, and the portions are on the smaller side. Overall, it’s a lovely neighborhood Italian spot with a great ambiance.

Came here for dinner. Had the oxtail ragu with a spring mix salad and mezcal Negroni.

The atmosphere is great. Intimate setting accompanied by light jazz. The food is good. Salad was fresh. Service is great. I’d recommend this spot to anyone.

I came here for dinner recently and had a pleasant time! This cozy Italian spot in Brooklyn is the perfect spot for a date night with it's intimate and warm setting. Service here was pretty quick and very nice.

We ordered their olives, brocollini, and chicken liver to start and their seafood pasta, oxtail ragu, and wild boar ragu for mains. Everything was delicious. I loved their chicken liver and thought that it was a great pair with their olives, bread, and brocollini. I was pleasantly surprised by their wild boar ragu as it was so flavorful and didn't taste gamey at all (sometimes wild boar does). Overall, great spot for some pasta and I would love to come back!

Very pleased to have found this place. We didn't have a reservation on a busy Saturday night, but luckily there was a cancelation and we got a table. Service was fast and friendly. Our group tried the 2 specials: the meatball appetizer and oxtail risotto as an entree, while others tried some of the pasta dishes from the regular menu. Everyone was happy. I had the mushroom paparadelle--pasta was cooked perfectly and the mushrooms were very fresh. Would definitely visit again.

Absolutely amazing! I recommend eating inside much warmer, if you don’t mind a bit of a chill the patio is not bad.

The calamari mix with shrimp and fish was absolutely a 10/10 ! Everything was absolutely delicious!

S/o to our amazing waitress who was attentive and very accommodating we appreciate her so much!

Don’t wait please make a reservation!

Unfortunately, the food is not very good here though the ambiance was decent and the cocktail was fine. Soggy breadcrumbs, tossed with chopped broccoli rabe and cooked until barely recognizable? I was expecting a nice hunk of sourdough with the olives for $13, but it looked and tasted like cheap thinly sliced plain white bread. The pasta didn’t have much flavor either. We regretted coming here for a special date night :(

I liked it! It was good. My entree oxtail ragu with  was delicious as was my friends dish she got the mushroom pasta.

The appetizers weren't amazing. I thought the burrata was too hard (but they gave us lots of toast)  and the calamari was a bit over cooked.

The wait staff there was on point and there was no wait for a table. Great place for an intimate conversation relaxed vibes.  If you're looking for something yummy to eat with good friends and you're in the area come here!

Headline: order the potatoes because you will need it to fill up.

Kind of a strange/hilarious dining experience here. Lovely atmosphere and the food was delicious but extremely overpriced for the portioning.

We had 4 people and we split several pasta dishes and oxtail - no joke, the entree pasta dishes are about 1/4 cup of cooked pasta served on a side salad dish smaller than your individual plate for apps. I wish I took a picture. The Amatriciana was sooo good but we each had 5 bucatini noodles each it was crazy!

The service had us cracking up though - our first server told us we had to order the whole ticket at once. Another server came by and said not true lol and took our order for starters. And this happened on several other occasions! Anyway…We devoured the spoonfuls of pasta and capped it off with a normal sized tiramisu and a martini-sized glass of grappa. I would come again but not hungry!

Whether you’re planning a casual dinner, a night out with friends, or a special celebration, it provides an experience that feels both relaxed and elevated.

From the moment you arrive, Luna’s Kitchen & Bar makes a strong impression with its modern yet cozy ambiance. The lighting, décor, and layout create a space that works just as well for intimate meals as it does for lively group gatherings. It’s an environment that feels energetic without being overwhelming, striking a comfortable balance for a variety of occasions.

The menu is one of the restaurant’s highlights, featuring a diverse selection of dishes that blend comfort food with contemporary culinary flair. From shareable appetizers to well-crafted entrées, each item is prepared with attention to flavor, presentation, and quality ingredients. The kitchen’s focus on fresh preparation and balanced seasoning helps ensure a consistently enjoyable dining experience.

The bar program is another standout feature. Luna’s offers a thoughtful selection of cocktails, wines, and spirits, with drinks that are both creative and well-executed. Whether you prefer a classic cocktail or something more inventive, the drink menu adds a fun and social dimension to the visit.

Service at Luna’s Kitchen & Bar is friendly, attentive, and professional. Staff members are knowledgeable about the menu and help create a smooth and enjoyable experience from start to finish.

Overall, Luna’s Kitchen & Bar delivers a well-rounded experience with great food, excellent drinks, and a lively yet comfortable atmosphere, making it a popular choice for both casual outings and special evenings.

Highly recommend the Luna special salad. Best salads in the neighborhood. Very fresh, amazing dressing.  Shrimp pasta is good too. Good portions. Guacamole is only ok, does not have much taste, needs a bit more lime.
A great spot for brunch, very friendly staff. A little tight on the seating but overall everything was great. If you get the Eggs Benedict be aware the sausage that comes on it is spicy.

The staff was incredibly polite and helpful when we had questions about the menu. The Hulk smoothie and turkey panini were delicious! Other items in the photo include nachos, avocado toast, berry smoothie, and Mexican burger. We’ll definitely return for the happy hour and brunch offers!

We had brunch at Luna’s and ordered the French toast with coconut flakes I substituted the blueberries with bananas and strawberries it was amazing. My husband also enjoyed his food. The service was top notch. Luna’s is a wonderful establishment we are so happy we found this hidden gem.

The food was good, I particularly liked the berry salad. The coffee wasn't that good, it tasted like diner coffee. The place was kinda loud, and it was weird to start Sunday brunch with the news on the TV.
This restaurant should be a lot more crowded than it is.  The food is fresh, visually appealing, and scrumptious.  Service is spot on, too.
Impressed with the delicious food and the server was very attentive. Had a comfortable dining experience.

top_reviews.content: This place is a lot of fun but also a celebration of the people who take care of us, from first responders to military. It's especially amazing on the day before America turns 250! Oh, and the food is really good. I had the veggie burger (no upcharge for being vegetarian, unlike most places in Seattle)... Very yummy, as were the fries! Also, really really great service.

No better place to go immediately after visiting the WTC area and Museum than O'Hara's! It was a rumor, I believed it, tested it and it was, in fact, true! You feel like you are almost walking into a time capsule the moment you see the door and I won't spoil the surprise by telling you what happens AFTER you open the door.

It is a beautiful spot with so much personality, friendly service and the biggest burger I have ever seen. I couldn't even finish HALF. I think there was an entire pack of pack on it. ;) It was SO good.

Not to mention, really reasonably priced, especially considering it would have fed me three times. I was able to swap out reg fries for sweet potato fries (always a win). The photos of the HAND-WRITTEN menu will tell you everything about the vibe of this unique place..... And the prices are on them. Those portions are HUGE, people! Enjoy!

Will definitely be back!

Love this place! Great atmosphere! Incredible service! Burger was delicious. Came here after the 9 11 museum. Touching since I am married to a retired battalion fire chief! Love all the flags and patches on the wall!

This place has so much personality, it’s a really good option around that area, they have burgers, sandwiches and many other things. I loved it. Service is great and prices are fine too. I’d definitely go back. Beers are good but lemon juice not so much, not natural juice. We ordered the sliders and fries, the shepherds pie for two and the chipotle chicken wrap. They were all very good. Fries are not the best but they are ok.

Ohara’s is one of the best spots in Lower Manhattan. Walking in and seeing the place covered in thousands of first responder patches sets a unique vibe. This place is perfect for pulling up a stool, grabbing a beer, and catching a game. The bartenders are great! My girlfriend and I found this to be one of our favorite pub spots in the city.

If we could give higher than 5 star I would. As soon as you walk in, you feel the importance, the warmth of the people here and meaning of what they do for the remembrance of the fallen first responders in 9-11. There are 1000’s maybe 10’s of 1000’s of badges and symbols from all over the world covering the walls and ceiling.  Service was so efficient, Wolfgang is a great waiter, the food was so delicious, like home cooked, menu had simple items, everything at our table was eaten up to last crumb. We’re coming back. Located in the calmer financial district, it was a Sunday night, so not sure how crazy it can get other nights.  But it was a great choice for eats.

Very nice Irish Pub style place.  Near 9/11 memorial with police and fire patches covering the walls.  Black and Tan was spot on.  Food is basic pub fare - fries were well done and came out hot and crispy.  Staff was observant and professional on busy Memorial Day weekend Sunday.

Fantastic food, drinks and people. On a quick trip into the city at the WTC area, I found this little gem. Sat at the bar and had a lovely pint of Guinness, along with the Ten House burger. Everyone was super friendly. I highly recommend stopping in.

reviews_snippets.content: "Great prices, service, selection, and staff."
"Nice place to grab a bite to eat, very cool, the service si quick and very kind."
"Burgers tasted homemade and the nachos had high quality steak!"

name: BKB | Brooklyn Brasserie
address: 327 Stuyvesant Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11233, United States

business_details.details: 327 Stuyvesant Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11233, United States
Closed · Opens 4 PM · See more hours

top_reviews.content:
BKB from the moment you walk in feels like “ah I’m finally home” after a long day at work. Immediately upon entry is a welcoming couch you can see people sitting, talking and enjoying each others company. The owners all work here and it is refreshing to see as they greet the regulars by name. It truly feels like a second home for everyone to wind down, have a drink and enjoy sports activities or a nice date. The best way to describe the ambience is warm, inviting and “why don’t you stay a while”.

The shakshuka which is I ordered had a fantastic twist as it had ratatouille for the vegetable base which was creamy and absolutely deliciously paired with the poached egg.  After requesting a tequila lime soda, the bartender kindly recommended a drink which I was pleasantly surprised by. Restaurants/bartenders don’t normally provide recommendations for me, but this was welcomed and I felt the bartender went above and beyond by curating my drinking experience.
I’ve had the pleasure of arriving for dinner before as well and I have to say I was just as pleased then as I was this time with the food, the drinks and the entire experience. You can tell the team works seamlessly with each other and has love for one another.

If you haven’t been to BKB yet, do yourself a favor and get over there ASAP as you are missing out on a fantastic experience! I promise you won’t regret it.

We came here last Saturday to watch the World Cup game and beginning of the knicks game. The food was wonderful - I had the steak (not pictured).  If you like Vodka - get the Euporhia! It is so good. Overall great experience 10/10

BKB Brooklyn Brasserie feels like a true neighborhood restaurant, but one that operates a notch above the usual formula. Tucked into Bed-Stuy, it carries the spirit of a European brasserie without turning it into a theme. You walk in and immediately get the sense that this place was built with intention. Regulars at the bar, a relaxed dining room, but with a concept that’s clearly thought through rather than improvised.

What I appreciate is that the Belgian influence is real. The team behind the restaurant includes people with roots in Belgium and European hospitality, and the menu leans into that tradition in a straightforward way. Moules are the obvious order here, and they deliver: generous portion, properly cooked, flavorful broth, the kind of dish you settle into with bread and don’t rush. The roast chicken is another highlight, simple but well executed, juicy and comforting in the way a brasserie classic should be.

But the real surprise for me was the Negroni. It’s aged in a small barrel and it’s honestly one of the best I’ve had in New York. The aging rounds the bitterness, smooths the edges, and gives the drink a depth that most Negronis never reach.

Overall, BKB captures something rare: the warmth of a neighborhood spot with the discipline of a restaurant that actually has a point of view. It’s casual, but not careless. And that combination is harder to pull off than it looks.

BKB was such a great place for our girls night dinner! From the moment we walked in, the vibe was warm, lively, and effortless. The staff were incredibly welcoming and attentive, and every cocktail on the menu felt elevated and thoughtfully crafted. Each of us loved the cocktail we ordered!

We shared the oven roasted chickpeas, Caviar d’Aubergine, Croquettes de Fromage, and olives. All were so delicious! For my main, I had the Steak au Poivre with potato gratin, and it was perfectly prepared and absolutely fantastic!

And the tiramisu… honestly probably the best I’ve ever had. I finished the evening with an excellent americano, which was the perfect ending to such a delicious meal.

Already counting down the days until we come back this summer to enjoy the patio!  BKB is such a gem!

Excellent neighborhood brasserie with a solid food menu and an equally good drinks menu, all fairly priced. The restaurant itself is airy, enjoying wonderful natural light and comfortable seating, with impecable service. I stopped for a quick bite on my way home Sunday afternoon and was pleasantly surprised but the quality of the food and the vibe of the place. I will definitely come back for dinner or an extended brunch.

I was so excited when I learned that this Brasserie was opening, and they did not disappoint. The space is beautiful and I dined at the bar on both visits. The bartender Emilio is wonderful and in addition to serving up some delicious drinks, he made some solid food recommendations off the menu. The Moules Frites Dijonnaise and Tarte Flambée Classic, so good.  Halfway through my meal I saw the roast chicken arrive for someone near me and I had to return to try it.   This is the best roast chicken in Brooklyn, definitely come for this and don’t forget to get a side of green beans too. Thank you for adding this absolute gem to our neighborhood, can’t wait to go back and try the rest of the menu 😊

This newish spot in the neighborhood is amazing. Food is really good as well as the drinks. What I really love about the space is the aesthetic and atmosphere. This place is equally amazing from bar to the floor. I recently stopped by during our “snow storm” and it was the perfect place to be to stay cozy. As someone who works in the industry I’m always judging a spots vibe and this place is it. They’re usually playing some sort of Spanish house music that is such a vibe. I’ve shazamed multiple songs here.
The owners, or maybe managers, are so friendly. You can tell they just genuinely want everyone to have an amazing experience. Only ever sit at the bar, but the bartenders are great as well.
There’s other little details and could add to explain my experience but I’ll leave it as exactly that. This place cares about the little details. In the way they’ve decorated to the way they take care of their patrons. So glad I live close to this spot because it’s definitely my new go to.

BKB was aesthetically pleasing and provided an elegant, warm, and welcoming dining experience, perfect for a romantic date night or a simple casual dinner with friends.

Victoria (Tori) took such amazing care of us throughout the entire night, she was sweet, warm, friendly, and her service was reflective of what exemplary service looks like! The other staff were also pretty on point and helped replace plates quickly without us asking, which we appreciated! Only thing that was a bit off was we got our complimentary bread late where it arrived alongside our main entrees and not alongside our appetizers to start our meal, which kinda overwhelmed us with everything coming all at once.

Our appetizer, the chicken wings with creme fraiche dip was delicious and highly recommend, along with their crispy frites! Now let's talk about the entrees!

The mussels, steak, and chicken stew pastry were all phenomenal with great flavors and I highly recommend them! However, there is room to make them even more amazing. The mussel were plentiful, fresh, and meaty; it came in a pretty tall pot, where the extremely flavorful broth only reached 1/4th of the mussels on the bottom, resulting in the top being a bit drier than we'd like, which is a simple fix! The steak was very flavorful and paired perfectly with the salad and potato gratin, but it could use a bit more peppercorn sauce since only the top pieces had the most sauce (as evident in the photo) that didn't trickle down to the other slices; another extremely easy fix! The chicken puff pastry was perfect in flavor and texture (though could use a bit more puff pastry), it just didn't really look that aesthetically pleasing as you can see from the photo, where it looks like just a blob; I believe a bit more pastry or a bigger piece of pastry on top can make it look more appetizing!

Overall, we had a wonderful time thanks to Victoria and the manager's kind and welcome nature! Their food is very reasonably priced and its quality is top tier, with our critiques being quick fixes that can further elevate them easily! BKB offers such creative and delicious selections that I have no doubt they'll continue to surpass expectations moving forward! Will definitely be back to try their many other selections and I can't wait to come back to give them the 5th star I know they're capable of easily getting! Please continue to do your best and become one of the best French restaurant in all of Brooklyn that I know for sure BKB has the potential of being!

Thank you Tori and Clauss(?) for the wonderful and memorable experience! Please give BKB a try, I promise you won't regret it!

Thank you for reading and best of luck! (:

reviews_snippets.content: "Juicy meat, creamy sauce, on a French pastry, fresh fries, and homemade mayo."
"Went for brunch had a wonderful time food, drinks and service was outstanding"
"Nice place, good for watching sport and family and friends gatherings"

name: Ernesto's
address: 259 E Broadway, New York, NY 10002, United States
description: A daily-changing menu of pintxos, mains & desserts is served in a relaxed space with globe lights.

business_details.details: 259 E Broadway, New York, NY 10002, United States

top_reviews.content: The service could be a bit more attentive, as the staff seemed more focused on chatting with each other than on the customers at times. That said, the food was excellent. I’m from Barcelona, and I can confidently say that this is authentic Spanish food done right. The outdoor seating area is very pleasant, and the vermouth was delicious, although the portion was quite small. Overall, a great spot for genuine Spanish cuisine!!

Side notes- Prices aren't online, and the menu changes frequently. In general, as of a few months ago, the pintxos/bites are $14 to $16, the entradas/appetizers are mostly in the low or mid-$20s, and the platos/entrees are mostly in the $30s and $40s.

Anyway, I was at this dimly lit Basque restaurant a while back with a small group. The place got pretty loud eventually, and the service was friendly. As we were waiting, I had some time to kill and ordered a tasty vermut. In this case, it was the Lustao Blanco for $16 on the rocks with an olive. In terms of small bites/Pintxos, someone ordered the Gildas for $14 while waiting, and another person enjoyed the similarly tiny Croquetas de Jamón for the same price point. Speaking of prices, I am unsure exactly how much everything cost, and I can't find descriptions of everything I ate, so I'm approximating, which is why you'll see the "~" before each price point.

My entrada, or appetizer, was the Salmorejo de Atún for ~$25. Salmorejo is essentially a much thicker version of gazpacho, with olive oil, tomato, bread, and a few other ingredients. In this case, it was topped with plenty of raw tuna, cucumbers, and other greens. The cold soup worked surprisingly well with the high-quality fatty tuna, and I would order this again if I came back here. Another person ordered one of the appetizers as their entree, the Bikini Hemingway, which is a type of sandwich. In this case, it was ~$25 and was filled with txistorra, queso, shrimp, and pan de cristal. They seemed to like it but not love it.

My main dish/plato was, unfortunately, the Magret de Pato for ~$40, with grilled magret duck breast, port and foie sauce, and pomme purée. Unfortunately, a few pieces of the duck were a little chewy, especially the ones with more fat. The sauce was alright, tasting like a slightly above-average red wine demi-glace with a touch more richness and sweetness than usual. The pomme purée was good, being rich with a nice texture. Overall, I think a bit of acid would have helped as well.  This was alright, and I would have appreciated some bread to mop up the remaining sauce. Another person thought the Bacalao for ~$35, which was topped with two shrimp in this presentation, was pretty good.

This place reminded me of Txikito in many ways. Both are a bit too pricey for the quality, with comparable food. For spending around $100, there are many other spots I would prefer, such as Casa Mono, El Pote, or a few others. If I were to go back, I'd probably just order appetizers. I'll leave the same score as the other restaurant, a bare 4/upper 3, and I would give a 3.5 if available.

This place was overall very tasty. Despite the portions seeming a bit small, the food is overall on the heavy side so I think that the portions are appropriate. I would recommend getting mostly items from the appetizer/tapas section of the menu

This is a typical trendy Manhattan restaurant. Charming interior, great mixed drinks, delicious food but like all Manhattan restaurants expensive. You’ll drop $100 per person if you include drinks.

That being said the food and mixed drinks were delicious so absolutely no complaints. We walked in early and had no problems getting seating but I would recommend getting a reservation if you plan to eat later. The restaurant was quickly filling up.

Can’t believe I’ve lived in New York this long and never made it here before. SO good.
We stopped in for the World Cup, and everything was incredible. Favorites? The gildas, the patatas bravas, and our bartender Riley, who made the experience even better. We’re already planning a return trip for dinner so we can work our way through the rest of the menu. Amazing food, amazing vibes, can’t wait to come back.

The food was absolutely amazing and our server was so helpful helping us order. I took one star off of the atmosphere because it is a little bit loud so if you’re sensitive to noise, please keep at in consideration.

Long time fan but finally visited for the first time on my birthday.

The staff was amazing and made for a really really fun dining experience, especially our server Matt and (please forgive me for not remembering) our beverage director who helped us pick out some lovely wine.

I was cranky when I came in and left extremely happy.

Delicious food, great vibe, and exceptional hospitality. I’ll be back for it all very soon.
Had an amazing time with my friends. We were celebrating my friend getting married and they took amazing care of us. Matt, the sommelier, was as knowledgeable as he was fun. Food was great too.

reviews_snippets.content: "Great service, good ambience, okay food that did not justify the price tag."
"The crab with scrambled eggs and the rabbit with soft rice were incredible."
"The place was packed so I guess people are fine with the prices."

name: HOUSE Brooklyn
address: 50 Norman Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11222, United States

business_details.details: 50 Norman Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11222, United States

top_reviews.content: The food, the atmosphere, and the service were out of this world. It was one of the best culinary experiences I’ve ever had. The food was exceptional, each bite filled with multiple dimensions of flavor. The crew was so charming. The space was thoughtfully curated and truly felt like a home I’ve been invited to. All around an amazing experience!

My favorite fine dining restaurant in NYC. Ive been to the shops outside of this restaurant but I never knew this restaurant existed. Its private, homey, and so welcoming. Our hostess was fantastic. She provided the best service I have ever received and her knowledge about food and alcohol pairings is so good.

The food was fantastic. It was just the right amount and they combined french and japanese very well. This restaurant is also listed in the michelin guide as “hidden gem” and I couldnt agree more. There were so many times I had my jaw open because the food was so good.

I had the best sake of my life here too. Just ask the hostess for her recommendations and you wont regret it.

The entire staff spoke w us during the dinner and we had some nice interactions w the people next to us as well.

What a fantastic dining experience!

Came with my family and had some dietary restrictions, so they called in advance. The team was so accommodating and helped tailor the menu for us — we really appreciated the extra care💕

The food was outstanding, and they took the time to walk us through each dish. The sake tasting was perfectly paired with the meal and made the experience even better.

Can’t wait to come back and try the spring menu!

Didnt want to post too many snapshots of our dinner because I loved the surprises each dish came with but had to share the most lovely dinner experience I've had in a while. Set in a lovely chic Japanese variety and cookware shop, HOUSE brings a homey but elevated feel in terms of both experience and food. Everyone from the host to the chefs to the service workers were all the kindest and most professional.

The food is phenomenal and teeters between fresh and bright bites to savory and rich dishes. Every dish is well balanced and the textures are amazing. They even included an anniversary dessert and were just the most thoughtful and engaging - definitely worth coming back! Worth every penny and more.
Impeccable service. Keiko was so kind and informative, as well as the rest of the staff. The chef prepared amazing courses and the flavor profiles were incredible. I will definitely be back again

reviews_snippets.content: "Wonderful experience, amazing food and stellar service and people"
"However, the portions felt a bit small for the price."
"Great fine dining experience with a touch of home cooked food taste."

name: Evelina
address: 211 Dekalb Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11205, United States
description: Mediterranean and Italian locale serving pastas, small plates, and wood-fired dishes, plus cocktails.

business_details.details: 211 Dekalb Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11205, United States

top_reviews.content:
I recently had dinner with friends at Evelina and had a nice experience. We started with the zucchini blossoms, which were just okay, and the fritto misto, which was delicious. The calamari and shrimp were perfectly crispy, although I wish the portion included more than two shrimp.

For drinks, I ordered the Lavinia, and it was excellent—a refreshing blend of tequila, lime, orange, and a nice touch of honey. For my entrée, I had the grilled pork chops, which were cooked perfectly. The pistachio gremolata added a unique burst of flavor that really elevated the dish. My friends ordered a variety of pasta dishes, which I tried and were tasty, everyone enjoyed their meals.

We ended with dessert and tried both the traditional tiramisu, which was very good, and the budino—a butterscotch pudding with pistachio gelato—which completely stole the show. It was absolutely amazing. Overall, a great dining experience, and I’d definitely return.

First time visiting with a group of five and we had an awesome experience. The space isn’t huge, but it does not feel crowded. It’s modern, and well decorated.

The food was delicious across the board. All the pastas were fantastic, well balanced without being overly salty or oily. The dry-aged ribeye is on the pricier side, but it’s a great statement dish when you are treating and it’s grilled to perfection.

Desserts were a highlight. The tiramisu was light, fluffy, and perfectly balanced, and the gelatos were incredibly smooth and creamy, honestly some of the best I’ve had.

Our server was super friendly and personable, which made the experience even better. Highly recommend and will definitely be back.

Never disappointed! We have been coming to this establishment for many occasions. The food is top-notch, and the service is beyond exceptional! Our waiter today was Chase! He was so attentive, kind, and very knowledgeable. The food has always been amazing, flavorful, and the plates look like works of art! I will recommend this place for a cute dinner with the girls or an intimate date night ✨

I love eating at Evalina's.
I made it on time from the lemon ricotta pancakes! Had a date with mom one morning and it was lovely.. a little chilly inside during the summer, so bring a sweater. They have a great assortment of teas.
And mom's mushroom feta omelet was amazing! The staff was very sweet as well. I've had had the gelato in the past... very good. It was so long ago I can't really remember which ones I loved. The only picture or video I had was half eaten food! Haha 😄  that's how good it was 🤭

I ordered two cocktails, the calamari appetizer and the tomato salad. Sometimes you have to take yourself on a dinner date by yourself, because honestly an incognito tab is just as good as a date, and you only pay half the cost for dinner.

The atmosphere was cozy. Other people were on dates, but not me. God gave me a right hand.

The servers were nice, and everything tasted amazing.

If you’re in Brooklyn, especially in this neighborhood, it’s an easy win.

First, I want to commend the culinary team here. The food was truly exceptional, particularly the chanterelle ravioli pasta and the NYC strip. The cocktails were also excellent.

However, the service we received is close to tragedy. While our server seemed to be pleasant gay dude, there was a noticeable lack of attentiveness and interest throughout the entire visit. We had absolutely no interaction, beside when placing our initial food order. We experienced zero follow-ups regarding our drinks or food, nor any general check-ins. This lack of engagement resulted in us waiting approximately 20 minutes to order dessert, which is completely unnecessary.
We end up tipping 20% because we plan to come back but this should not be a service standard for the restaurant of this caliber.

We had reservations across the street last week when my family and friends were in town and had spoken to several Evelina customers outside where we parked. They all raved about the food so we decided to try it. We sat at the bar and were served right away. The pasta dishes did not disappoint for brunch.... mushroom ravioli and oxtail ragu. The cocktails were also interesting. We would visit again.
Everything was delicious and refined. Squid ink risotto was excellent. My mocktail (Rosie) was refreshing and great. Great service, cute space.

reviews_snippets.content: "Enjoyed the food, the atmosphere, the music and excellent service!"
"The food was tasty but it is a bit pricy with small portions."
"Great cocktails, neighborhood spot, nice outside seating, awesome staff :)"

name: Meadowsweet
address: 149 Broadway, Brooklyn, NY 11211, United States
description: Mediterranean-influenced New American dishes & craft cocktails in casually hip digs with a bar.

business_details.details: Closed · Opens 3 PM · See more hours

top_reviews.content: Great meal courtesy of our friends at Tasting Collective. Beautiful, elegant airy space. Set menu was generous and varied. One dish not to miss was the spiced duck breast with escarole, sweet potato, oaxacan mole, peanut-almond dukkai & sesame. Also of note were the smoky octopus and chorizo and the vanilla pana cotta with raspberries and passionfruit sauce. Fantastic unfussy service. And a nod to their choice of Threes Brewing The Long Game Pale Ale. Great beer from a great local brewery.

The brunch and coffee is so delicious, and amazing service! I highly recommend the almond muffins. They have a summer 3-course set for $45 and it is a great deal. Also really appreciated how nice and open the staff were.

Wonderful team working here, they really make the experience.

The rosemary oil Gibson is absolutely delicious. The burger was yummy, tho a little small for the dollar amount.

Chill, vibrant, nice food and wonderful front of house.

Came during restaurant week for brunch. It was $45 pp and well worth it. Firstly, every single dish was perfection. Had the muffin to start and it was warm and fluffy on the inside yet crisp on the outside.

Same for the empanadas - crispy but the filling was soft and delicious.

Probably one of the best omelettes, it was evenly cooked and the fillings (spinach and mushroom) were also seasoned and cooked to perfection. Not a bad bite throughout.

Finished with sorbets and it was the most flavourful sorbets, especially the lemon and raspberry. I was surprised how jam packed the flavour was.

Only downside was we order coffees and those took a really long time to come to the table.

This place used to have Michelin stars but now it feels more like a neighborhood spot. Little pricey for a casual meal but great for a first date, or to make someone’s day.

We visited Meadowsweet on a snowy Sunday for brunch and were immediately impressed by the warm and polished experience from the moment we walked in. The restaurant was fairly quiet because of the weather and our group of four was seated right away. Water was brought to the table immediately and the front of house staff seemed completely in sync. The service felt smooth and professional without ever being stiff.

None of us ordered cocktails and instead stuck with coffee which everyone at the table kept praising. It was rich, balanced, and exactly what you want on a cold morning.

To start we ordered the donuts and the empanadas. The donuts were fun and reminded me of sugar coated munchkins. They were good but not particularly memorable. The empanadas on the other hand were excellent in terms of flavor. The filling was well seasoned and satisfying. The only critique is their size. At nineteen dollars for three empanadas we all felt they could be a bit larger to really showcase the filling.

For my main dish I ordered the duck pastrami hash with sunny side eggs and it was phenomenal. The dish had great depth of flavor and the eggs were cooked perfectly. In hindsight I should have ordered the sourdough bread with the hash instead of as a starter. The bread would have been perfect for soaking up everything on the plate.

My girlfriend originally ordered the bacon omelette but was accidentally served the mushroom spinach omelette. Luckily the mistake worked in our favor because it ended up being one of the best dishes on the table. The eggs were incredibly fluffy and cooked perfectly. The mushrooms absorbed a ton of flavor and created a savory richness that balanced beautifully with the spinach. Nothing felt overpowering and every bite was well composed. I tried a bite myself and was equally impressed.

Another friend ordered the burger and really enjoyed it. It was simple, satisfying, and executed exactly how a good brunch burger should be.

Overall the experience was excellent. The atmosphere was comfortable, the service was attentive, and the food showed strong technique and balance across the board. If brunch is this good I can only imagine how strong their dinner service must be.

Considering the price point, the quality of the food, and the level of hospitality, Meadowsweet easily earns five out of five stars. I would happily come back for brunch again.
Very delicious fresh made. Homemade French fries crispy avocado sandwich were soo good. Thank you for your service and great team   Decided to come back again. Recommend 100%

I can’t rave about this spot enough. We came in on July 4th with our baby en tow to celebrate my birthday and they were not only accommodating but so, so kind! The service is truly 12/10. They provided a high chair, offered to store our stroller .. the wait staff was knowledgeable about the wine and helped us pick a great one. But the food .. omg .. the food!!!!!!! We started with the fried green tomato’s (as a southern girl this was very good), burrata and fruit (phenomenal) and the absolute star of the show - the gnocchi and braised duck ragu. I told my husband it’s my new favorite meal in Williamsburg - the duck ragu appetizer is beyond. We also had the burger and the wagyu steak. Both were great. Excited to come back for a happy hour and try some cocktails and other menu items!
I loved the food here and the service was very friendly! We tried a bunch of appetizers that we shared and each had our own main. There wasn’t anything that I didn’t like. Cocktails were great too.

reviews_snippets.content: "Excellent service, attention, energy, timing and scrumptious brunch."
"They have a great selection of drinks, including cocktails, wine, and beer."
"Very nice crispy and crunchy veggie and a nice tasty sauce."

name: Cent'Anni
address: 742 Franklin Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

business_details.details: 742 Franklin Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

top_reviews.content:
Cent'Anni is a charming Italian restaurant that feels like a hidden slice of Italy tucked into the neighborhood. The dining room is cozy and intimate, with close quarters that add to the warm and inviting atmosphere rather than feeling crowded. Every detail contributes to the feeling that you've stepped into a small neighborhood restaurant somewhere in Italy.

The bar is fully stocked, and the cocktail program feels thoughtfully curated, making it a great spot whether you're stopping in for dinner, drinks, or both. When the weather is nice, the front windows open up, and there is bar seating that creates a lively connection to the street outside.

One of the highlights of the restaurant is the back patio. It feels like a hidden gem and provides a beautiful outdoor dining space that many visitors might not expect from the front of the restaurant.

The staff was friendly and welcoming throughout our visit, and the overall experience felt relaxed and special. Between the atmosphere, drinks, and intimate setting, Cent'Anni is an excellent choice for date night, celebrations, or anyone looking for a memorable Italian dining experience in Brooklyn.

I went here on a whim and thank god I did! The frozen martini was yummy and unique but definitely would recommend it post meal as it is very sweet and gives more of a dessert vibe 8/10. The sauteed calamari was delicious and soft I loved the sage and fresh herbs in it, 11/10! The homemade pasta with lamb was soooo tasty not too acidic and just the right amount of meat to sauce ratio 10/10. The penne ala vodka was a bit of a disappointment but also a very basic dish. We ordered chicken with it, the grilled chicken was a bit dry but had a flavorful char, the pasta itself 7/10. Surpringly the french fries were some of the best fries I've had in a while. I'm not sure if they coat them with starch to get a crunchy outter layer but 10/10. The sauteed broccoli rabe was simple but yummy 9/10.

The pasta was underwhelming. I’ve certainly had much better around town. The Buratta was a gorgeous serving and very delicious. The salad was also a bit underwhelming. The cocktails looked fun, but we didn’t partake. The staff was friendly and the place itself is very cute. The backyard is definitely worth sitting in. Everyone was kind and attentive but the food didn’t make much of an impression on me. I wouldn’t be opposed to trying something else, but there isn’t much pulling me back aside from maybe wanting to try their cocktails.

All in all, it’s cute and the staff is friendly but the food didn’t meet my expectations.

I’m still thinking about this place!!!
Food is delicious and yummy, good portions, we ordered full course dinner for 2 and the price for everything was jaw-dropping
Surprisingly the food came up first that the wine tho, beyond that I’ll be back

I had an extremely disappointing experience at Cent'Anni, not because of the food, but because of the way we were treated by the staff.

When we entered, I asked a female staff member if there was a table available inside. She told us there was seating available in the garden and led us toward the outdoor area.

As we were walking there, I noticed an indoor table that appeared to have just been vacated. Since it was a hot day and I was with my granddaughter, who is very sensitive to mosquito bites, I asked if we could wait for that table instead. The staff member told me that the guests were still there and had only gone to the restroom. I accepted her explanation and took a table in the garden.

A little later, while taking my granddaughter to the restroom, I saw that the same table had been completely cleared and cleaned. I politely asked if we could move to it.

This time, I was told that the table was reserved.

That was very confusing. First I was told the guests were simply in the restroom, and shortly afterward, once the table had been cleared, I was told it was reserved. When I expressed my concern about these contradictory explanations, instead of explaining the situation or trying to resolve the misunderstanding, the staff member avoided responding to me.

At that point, I was uncomfortable enough that I decided to leave. On my way out, I asked if there was a manager available and also asked for the staff member's name. Again, I received no answer. Another male staff member then became involved and immediately defended her without, as far as I could tell, first asking me what had happened.

What bothered me most was not whether we were ultimately given that particular table. A restaurant has every right to manage its seating and reservations. The problem was the inconsistent explanations and the way my questions and concerns were handled afterward.

If the table was reserved, simply telling us that from the beginning would have been completely understandable. Instead, I was given one explanation and then another, and when I asked why, I was essentially ignored.

Good hospitality requires clear communication and basic respect for customers. Unfortunately, I experienced neither here.

Based on this experience, I cannot recommend Cent'Anni. If zero stars were an option, that would reflect how I felt about the service we received.

I placed a mobile order and picked it up myself and have nothing but good things to say about the service. I recieved my food hot and in a timely manner. The food itself on the other hand was a huge letdown. I ordered the roasted garlic bread and rigatoni with grandma's ragu. Grandma must be rolling over in her grave right now because that was the most bland sauce I have tasted in my life. The meatballs were mush and also flavorless. It didn't even taste like the meal had been salted at ALL. The pasta itself was fine it had a nice chew to it but i reiterate the sauce and meatballs were abysmall. The roasted garlic bread unfortunately was soaked completely through with butter and entirely soggy even though my apartment is no more than a 5 minute walk from the restaurant. It also tasted as if they had burnt the garlic, not roasted it. Extremely disappointing meal all around I will not be returning to this establishment.

This is a surprisingly spacious restaurant with the back patio lit by candles. The handmade pasta is delicious- I got the tagliatelle with mushrooms. Their seasonal pear fig gelato was amazing! The waitresses were so helpful and prompt. Highly recommend!

Good place cute backyard seating. Attentive service and nice ppl.
My mushroom pasta was good w the grilled shrimps. Calamari also good. Love chili flakes. Kale was also a good side for my pasta.

No one else really enjoyed their meals tho, chicken parm is not good, the chicken is dry and taste like cafeteria school lunch pizza. Ragu meatballs was good, but the pesto couldve been more creamy.

top_reviews.content: Made a reservation and came on a Saturday for a special occasion. From the initial walk in, this place is stunning with velvet interior everywhere, even in the elevator. The decor,  ambiance and lighting is again stunning. and elegant. The staff is extremely attentive. YaYa was our server. She made great recommendations and explained in detail what certain entrees entailed. We had Confited Duck Ravioli with Pesto, Seared Scallops, Branzino Filet and the Blackened Chicken. The drinks are also topnotch. The Rita Hayworth is their signature go to drink. Highly recommended 👌. All and all we had a great experience, this is definitely a place to go for special occasions or if you want an elevated mature dining experience. Loved it.

Wow, Casa Cruz is stunning—the whole six-story townhouse setup with the art and elegant vibe feels like stepping into something special. The food was excellent all around, but that octopus carpaccio? Seriously a must-try—super tender, fresh, and just melted in my mouth with the olive oil and lemon.

Big thanks to our waitress Melissa—she was funny, on top of everything, and made the evening even better. Great spot, definitely going back!

Our party got there with an extra guest … we sat then got sent to the bar got sent back to the table it was a bit tight after about ten mins they moved us to a bigger setting comped a glass of champagne for the mix up … I’m not goi g to lie the door reviews had me scared but I ordered the roasted duck Brest and it was amazing , the steak was good the crab tortellini was superb. Lychee martini was good
It’s a cute place definitely a tight space but very beautiful and nicely built  cute date night idea
Definitely going back for the duck again 🤏🏽🤏🏽

My boyfriend & I had a reservation at casa Cruz & was highly disappointed. The restaurant was pretty to look at but the food was terrible. Everything from the appetizers to entree was disappointing. No flavor at all. Very tasteless & basic. But to make things worse I had the raw oysters & immediately after leaving the restaurant I got serious stomach pains & nausea, I vomited all over my boyfriend’s car & my fur coat. We had to end our date night early, got home & threw up more, along with stomach pains & diarrhea!!  The worst restaurant experience. Not only was the food bad but it made me sick & to top it off it was over priced. I called the restaurant to make a complaint & was told I couldn’t speak to a manager I had to send them an email & hope I get a response.  Never again.

came here for a special dinner and honestly the whole place feels really upscale from the moment you walk in. the atmosphere is beautiful without feeling too stiff, and the service was excellent all night. food was impressive too, every dish looked great and tasted even better. portions aren't huge, but the quality definitely stands out. cocktails were fantastic and probably some of the best i've had in a while. prices are definitely high, so it's not somewhere i'd go regularly, but for a celebration or date night it felt worth it. overall a really memorable experience and i'd gladly come back.

I recently dined at Casa Cruz in the Upper East Side. The ambience is undeniably beautiful — chic décor, warm lighting, and a glamorous setting that makes a strong first impression. However, the atmosphere felt a bit heavy and formal, which took away from the relaxed dining experience we were hoping for.

I ordered the steak while my husband had the lamb chops. Unfortunately, the food was just average in taste and presentation; not bad, but certainly not memorable. At first, our server even brought the wrong dishes despite the restaurant not being very busy, which was a little surprising.

That said, the service overall was polite, and the restaurant itself is stunning to look at. If you’re going mainly for the interior design and vibe, Casa Cruz is worth seeing. But if you’re looking for an exceptional dining experience, it might not fully deliver.

I had the pleasure of dining at Casa Cruz New York, and it was an absolutely delightful experience from start to finish. The food was exceptional each dish beautifully presented with bold, refined flavors that showcased the freshness and quality of the ingredients. Every bite was a true pleasure.

The service was outstanding as well. The staff was not only knowledgeable about the menu but also genuinely passionate about guiding us through the dining experience. Their attention to detail was impeccable, making us feel well taken care of without being intrusive.

What really stood out, though, was the manager’s personal touch. They went above and beyond to ensure every guest was having a fantastic experience, checking in with us throughout the evening and offering thoughtful recommendations.

Overall, Casa Cruz provided a perfect evening great food, professional service, and a team that clearly cares about creating an unforgettable experience. I highly recommend it!

Casa Cruz was not what I expected in the most wonderful way possible. It isn’t just another midtown upscale bar/restaurant based on my assumptions. Casa Cruz is a very well created establishment where every corner of the room was well designed and articulated for its guests. With the perfect atmosphere we felt cozy and sophisticated, the staff members were well coordinated between their uniforms and spectacular services.

We only had light bites at the bar but the focaccia was delightful, the shrimp cocktail was refreshing and fresh, and my French seventy five was just the perfect combination. This has become my favorite midtown restaurant of all times.

Los Dos Hermanos is located in a lovely neighborhood in Brooklyn close to Fort Greene Park. The indoor area has a very pleasant atmosphere but since the weather was nice we chose to sit at one of the outdoor tables in the front with my family. We also had a nice conversation with the friendly lady who took our order and later learned that she is the owner’s wife.

We ordered the Dos Hermanos Churrasco Steak Sandwich, Shrimp Quesadilla, Pulpa, Mix Ceviche, Chips with Guacamole, Modelo Especial, Michelada, Victoria, and a Classic Margarita. The service, food and drinks were all top notch. We truly had a wonderful time and will likely come back more often.

I would definitely recommend it to anyone who enjoys Mexican cuisine.

I love it here, the food is so good, location is convenient and the staff is always on point, I’m coming back every now and then.

This time I got to try the churros Ice cream as a dessert and y makes me want more.
What I love the most is how welcoming the staff makes you feel not to mention the place is warm inside and makes you feel like is your new to go spot you must stop before going anywhere else

The food was amazing!!! Ordered steak tacos & shrimp tostadas & they were to die for!!! The service was incredible & the wait staff was so friendly & welcoming. Additionally, the aesthetic & vibe of this restaurant are unmatched! Highly recommend & will most definitely be back soon!!

Beautiful atmosphere, service is top tier and lovely vibes all around! Food is so delicious I couldn’t recommend this place more!! Paloma is super attentive and lovely! Had a great time talking to the owner Oscar and learning more about the place! Would 100% come back.

Our server was amazing,  the food was phenomenal,  even the other patrons were extremely nice,  we'll be back very soon 😃

And to the beautiful couple next to us..whom we stole the last piece of bread from 😅 and they even paid for our dessert . If you see this.. Thank you so much,  I hope your chef career in queens blooms into everything amazing

We visited Fausto not having any prior idea of what to expect. It was a family celebration, and we could not have chosen a better restaurant for it. The level of service was outstanding - my husband remarked how attentive and perfectly timed was the arrival of each of the courses and the beverages, the food temperature exactly on point to be eaten for full flavor and enjoyment. The staff work was flawless, fully involved and yet unobtrusive. A feat, in all senses. The focaccia and crispy potatoes were delicious, and four different pasta dishes wonderful and distinctive im flavors and freshness. And what to say about the gelati - the fior di latte was simply a poem. I recommend Fausto wholeheartedly. Thanks to the team who makes possible such a satisfying experience, particularly Sean.

Fausto was absolutely wonderful. I brought my boyfriend’s mom here last night for her birthday and it was a great experience~ Ordered a bunch of apps to share — Little Gem salad and crispy potatoes were our favorites! The mushrooms were incredible, and the lamb was also outstanding. Every dish felt thoughtful and really well executed.

The service was also amazing and not overbearing. I called ahead to secure a quiet corner since my party was hard of hearing which they kindly arranged. Our waitress was incredibly sweet and honestly reminded us of a modern-day Betty Boop — super cute, charming, and just really warm and attentive. Another waitress who cleared our plates did it with such gusto~ The whole team made the night feel really special 🫶🏼

Beautiful atmosphere, great food, and lovely service — we’ll definitely be back!

Love Fausto particularly for nicer dinners and bringing out of town guests! Always great, and am also loving their gelato cart - the ricotta cannoli flavor was so incredible I can’t wait to try again!

Fausto, a Brooklyn restaurant with a focus on house-made pastas, offers a delicious and innovative take on Italian cuisine. The warm and inviting atmosphere makes it a great choice for a cozy meal.
The highlight of my meal was definitely the appetizers. The salad was bursting with fresh flavors, and the arancini were absolutely heavenly. The homemade pastas were also a delight, and the extensive wine list with options from both Italy and France was a perfect complement to the food.
Overall, Fausto is a great spot for a delicious and memorable Italian dining experience.

Excellent restaurant! Love that the menu has some dishes that stay the same (the excellent little gem salad, for example - it's so good I think it's addictive!), while other dishes change seasonally to keep things interesting. We recently brought a particularly fussy group (one gluten free, one vegan, one vegetarian, one fussy toddler...) and they were very accommodating. Highly recommend.

amazing food, really good vibes would give 5 but we had such a horrible waiter! Which sucked cus everyone else was so nice! Fausto was one of the first restaurants we visited when we moved to the neighborhood and my family and I have been going regularly for 7 years.  The food is delicious, the staff is welcoming and the service is always great.  It’s elegant without feeling stuffy.  We love it!

Lets talk about it!!
I've been to all Peaches locations and today I've discovered something new about the Prime location. Service as usual is always amazing. Nahuel was our bartender and definitely serving with an amazing attitude although busy. Ilia was on tables and still stopped to speak to those in need.

Con: I ordered new items on the menu. Short ribs were clearly reheated and didnt taste fresh which was a disappointment. Cooking method matters with reheated food. So instead get the steak and eggs. Never steers you wrong.

Pro: Drink service will always be amazing as the drinks are consistent across all locations. Salmon cake is good. Depending on if you're a southerners or not.

Peaches Prime has a great environment that works well for date nights, celebrations, or business dinners. The lighting and overall atmosphere really set the tone and were a highlight of the experience. Food was mixed—calamari came out a bit too salty, but the steak was cooked perfectly. Mashed potatoes and spinach were good in texture but lacked seasoning. Solid spot for ambiance, with room to improve on consistency in the kitchen.

My friends and I arrived earlier than our Brunch reservations were scheduled, but we were accommodated right away. The atmosphere was modern, warm, and welcoming. The server Rita, was pleasant, knowledgeable, friendly, and efficient at her job. The food was DELICIOUS!! It was 6 of us and we tried different starters, which was sufficient and everyone was able to get whatever they wanted to eat from the different choices that we made. The main dishes arrived fresh, hot, and presented beautifully!! The drinks and desserts, did not disappoint. It was my first time here, and definitely won’t be my last time!

It was very mediocre the oxtail linguine is just not good to me. Oxtail don’t go with everything. The flavor was also a no for me. I will never order again my husband had the rib and grits I will give it a 3 son had fries and tenders a 2 fries were nasty I guessing they were Cajun burnt taste my toddler did not eat them.the brownstone drink again a miss for me. Not a place. I will recommend the calamari to breaded and overly crunchy. Tried to take it home I just can’t eat it. Don’t taste lol me black folks in the kitchen!!!

Quickly becoming one of my favorite spots! 🥰 The atmosphere is mellow and perfect for dates or a girls' night out. As for the flavors — wow! The Butternut Squash Soup was the perfect starter, and the Short Rib and Grits were incredible. Definitely save room for the Belgian Brownie Bar! Highly recommend! Can't wait to go back for brunch!
Insanely delicious food and great atmosphere. 10/10 recommend! The shrimp and grits was phenomenal.

Went there for Mother's Day brunch. It was a tad on the pricey side, but as they say, you get what you pay for. We ordered the fried calamari appetizer; shrimp & grits; steak & eggs; french toast, bacon, eggs & grits; also the bacon egg & cheese sandwich. Everything we ordered was spot on delicious. Waitress was very friendly & attentive, she took real good care of us. Definitely will come back.

Large place with a great atmosphere with absolutely delicious food. This is a place for a date night or catching up with friends over a nice meal. Went here for dinner prior to a concert down the street at the Barclays Centre. Considering the location, the place is very reasonably priced with respectable portions. Would definitely go back if even in Brooklyn for dinner.
