top_reviews.content:
Park slope in Greenpoint. The staff were helpful and always smiling. Making the energy of the place uplifting. The dining area was small but situated well. I was very excited to try the pancakes after watching eater but they were disappointing. The edges were crispy but the center was dry. The flavor of the lemon and vanilla overpowered the pancake, while the syrup was not of higher quality. Investing in a high quality maple syrup along with whipped butter and separating the bacon strips before cooking them might result in a better flavor.
I was eager to visit for brunch as I had high expectations but unfortunately they were not met. I would not travel to eat here.

We had a great experience at Chez Ma Tante both in terms of food quality and service. We arrived around 9:20 without a reservation and were seated right away at 10am, but the restaurant filled up quickly by 10:15.

We came specifically for the pancakes, and they absolutely delivered. They were made with simple ingredients but elevated by a subtle hint of lemon zest that brightens each bite. What really stood out was the texture: a golden, lightly crisp exterior that gives way to a soft, fluffy center, almost as if they were delicately fried. They were easily the highlight of the meal.

It is on the pricier side, especially the cocktails, which felt small for the cost. That said, we would definitely return, there are plenty of other items on the menu we’re eager to try.

I can see why these could be someone’s favorite pancakes- if you like super crisp and slightly saltier pancakes. Just too saturated in butter/oil for me that it tastes more like fried dough rather than pancakes. I wish the inside was more fluffy and soft. They are very rich pancakes and only want to eat a few bites. There is a hint of lemon in them that I like. Surprisingly really liked the biscuit and sausage gravy- really good biscuit and executed dish overall. The chips were very solid and enjoyable but not the best I’ve had.

I really enjoyed this place a lot. The screw driver with tangerine juice was awesome and strong. The waiter was very knowledgeable about everything on the menu. The country pate looked kind of like spam but tasted magical. The chips (French fries) and aioli was outstanding reminded me of the ones at 4 Charles or Au Cheval. The Shakshuka egg and tomatoes was fire too. The sausage biscuit in the gravy was really good. The star of the show however was the pancakes they were perfect. Crispy edges but fluffy and the perfect amount of syrup. The cutlet that was with the Cesar salad was awesome too. I definitely would return.

I stopped in here with a group of 4 on Saturday for brunch, our group had a reservation and was seated promptly. The server came to our table not to long after we were seated and took our drink orders. We ordered beers, coffees and Bloody Marys ,which were the star of the show. As for food we ordered the chicken Caesar sandwhich, quiche, chicken liver pate, gigante beans, pancakes and chips with aioli. The star of the show was the chicken liver pate, it had a great rich savory flavor with a hint of sweetness and was served on a nice soft piece of sourdough. The Scottie Pippen of the food order had to be the pancakes, they were savory and sweet with a hint of lemon. The only weak link of the bunch was the under seasoned gignate beans, which had an off day. Would recommend this spot to anyone looking for a brunch spot in WB or Greenpoint.

As a neighborhood resident I am so thankful that CMT is so close by because it’s one of my favorite spots in all of NYC. This place is incredible! A+++ food and service. They do a great job of balancing old favorites with new options on the food menu, and the cocktail and wine selection are top notch. And don’t sleep on the incredible desserts - we usually get the chocolate cake and one of their amazing ice creams.

This place is an absolute must-visit! The food was incredibly delicious, and the portions were generous. The appetizers, main dishes, and desserts were all exceptional. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a fantastic dining experience.

Our dinner was so outstanding! The Dorade main entree was absolutely spectacular! The lentils in the pork dish were the best we’ve had! The server was delightful and attentive. The homemade sausage with cockles was also a favorite. We will be back and we highly recommend!

name: RH Rooftop Restaurant at RH New York
address: 9 9th Ave, New York, NY 10014, United States
description: Glamorous rooftop restaurant offering American fare amid chandeliers, greenery, and skyline views.

business_details.details: 9 9th Ave, New York, NY 10014, United States
RH New York | The Gallery in the Historic Meatpacking District

people_also_search.name: The Dining Room at RH Guesthouse New York

top_reviews.content:
RH Rooftop Restaurant is one of those places where the setting alone makes the visit worthwhile. Having previously visited the West Palm Beach location, we were excited to experience the New York restaurant, and it absolutely delivered.

Located atop the beautiful multi-level RH furniture gallery, the restaurant offers a stunning rooftop setting with elegant chandeliers, fountains, lush greenery, and an open, airy atmosphere. It feels sophisticated yet incredibly relaxing, making it a wonderful place for brunch.

We arrived as walk-ins and, despite not having a reservation, only waited about 20 minutes for a table, which was more than reasonable given how popular the restaurant is.

The food was excellent. The Mini Lobster Rolls with Caviar were so good that we ordered them again—they’re an absolute must. We also enjoyed the Italian Benedict with Crispy Rosemary Potatoes, which was perfectly prepared, and the Shaved Ribeye Dip, another flavorful and satisfying dish. Everything was fresh, beautifully presented, and consistently well executed.

To accompany brunch, we had a Mimosa and an Aperol Spritz, both of which complemented the meal perfectly.

Service was friendly, attentive, and efficient throughout our visit, adding to the relaxed and refined atmosphere.

Overall, RH Rooftop Restaurant offers much more than just great food—it’s a complete experience. Between the beautiful surroundings, quality cuisine, and welcoming service, it’s one of the best places for a memorable brunch in New York. Whether you’re shopping at RH or simply looking for a unique brunch destination, this is a place I would gladly recommend and happily return to.

Stunning Decor and Ambiance with great views make this rooftop an awesome choice for a date 🌹 or any kind of elegant night out.
Excellent food. We loved the Caviar and the Chocolate Chip cookies for desert.
Wait staff is attentive but also lacks a bit of specific knowledge as they got a few things mixed up on our orders.
They serve beer and wine but no liquor.
Great overall experience.

We always come to RH rooftop to celebrate our birthdays. It was my best friend’s 26th and we knew exactly where we wanted to have Saturday brunch. We have been here a handful of times in the last 5 years. You come to RH for the atmosphere. This rooftop is one of my favorites in the city. It’s elegant, the decor is beautiful, the views are awesome and the outside patio is one of my favorite places to sit. I do have to say, the portion quality has gone down a decent amount in the last 5 years. We would come here and get huge pieces of grilled toast, the eggs were the entire plate and the avocado toast came with a poached egg. Lately, the portions felt smaller and its slightly disappointing. Flavor is still great. Drinks are great. Another thing to note is we told them we were celebrating a birthday and they brought us a cookie with a candle in it and then charged us for the cookie without asking if we wanted a $4 cookie. The issue is what you are getting for the price. You really come here for the atmosphere and that’s what you end up paying for.

I chose RH Rooftop for my pre-birthday celebration and had a great experience. I mentioned in my reservation that I was celebrating my birthday, and the staff remembered and wished me a happy birthday when I arrived, which was a nice touch.

They gave me a confortable table, and I really enjoyed the overall atmosphere. The space feels elegant, bright, and thoughtfully designed, with a refined sense of polished luxury . Service was friendly, attentive, and professional throughout the meal, and the food was very good.

I also love that it’s located in Chelsea, where there’s always something to do before or after your reservation. Be sure to take some time to explore the rest of the building, because the décor and design throughout the different levels are part of the experience.

This is a popular spot for brunch, so I would recommend booking ahead. Overall, a beautiful venue for a special occasion or a nice day in the city.

This restaurant is supposedly one of the must visits in NYC, all over the internet as one of the top rooftop places, but this place was a letdown.

Food - nothing special, their burger is just okay, and does not come with fries (servers don't tell you that, though). the burrata is nothing special, sauce is almost nonexistent in terms of taste.

Service - not great, switched servers in the middle of our experience and were relatively slow. Reservations are absolutely necessary.

The ambiance of the building is amazing, though. Interior of the restaurant looks amazing. Building is on the 5th floor, and the lower floors are interior design showcases. The view is nothing special on 3 of the 4 sides, only one side has a good view towards the World Trade Center.

Overall, this restaurant is just okay.

The long time favorite penthouse brunch spot in meat packing district on top of ludicrously priced designer furniture store. Finally taking reservations instead of 90 min+ waits, though do missed the bar floor below where ppl can mingle and browse the 5K coffee tables and 2K lamps. The class roof gives the dining space great open feel, and place was packed as usual slowing service somewhat. Good menu, delicious lobster roll, crispy sprouts and juicy French dip.

The RH Rooftop in New York offers a stunning experience with its beautifully restored space featuring elegant finishes and chandeliers, making it a perfect backdrop for photos. The food was impressive; the ribeye was cooked to perfection, the salmon was delicious, and the lobster rolls were a crowd favorite. Despite a casual crowd, the place was bustling with activity. Additionally, there's an outdoor rooftop deck that likely provides an amazing view during the summer.

Dined here in February 2026 with coworkers. I wasn't aware of this setup inside the Restoration Hardware store. It was a pleasant surprise. The restaurant is on the top floor of the location. It was winter so sat inside. The decor and ambiance suited to the location and flair and the type you'd expect from RH. The service was spot on, the attendants and the waitstaff very attentive. The options for dining were just as you expected and diverse for anyone and everyone. The location we sat was comfortable and it was quite yet vibrant. The place was humming for a Thursday night with both visitors and locals. I would definitely find myself dining here again in the future.

top_reviews.content: I finally got to try a restaurant on my bucket list and man was it worth the hype!!! For context, I have been to Oaxaca, Mexico and have been in search of food that meets the quality, taste and freshness that I experienced in that region. This place is the best bet in the city. Everything we ordered was incredibly tasty but the chocolate cake blew my mind!!! The drinks too. Service was amazing, attentive without being smothering. Never felt rushed (which sometimes happens in busy/popular restaurants)

Went there with my wife and daughter and what a lovely time. Talk about Mexican elevated yet soulfull food and service. We ordered guacamole taco salad, tacos and salsas, octopus and lamb tacos and beef birria tacos. Let me start with the guacamole...it was just perfect and the some made tacos were, fried and excellent. The salsas were lovely especially the habanero and the Chile which contained more than one type and it was evident. I ended up slurping the habanero salsa with a spoon, it was that good. The octopus was sublime and the lamb and beef tacos were out of this world. The dessert was a chocolate fudge with ice cream and God knows what but it was heaven on earth....just great food and warm service....this is a place I would eat at everyday if I could...love it love it love it.

Great service and atmosphere. Their restrooms are disco balls haha. Our server was friendly and attentive. The food was great. We ordered the Shrimp Ceviche and Tuna Tostadas. We also ordered their in house Guac and the Aguachile. Definitely a must try place!

This Mexican eatery is located in Greenpoint, Brooklyn. Lock in your reservations since apparently it’s extremely difficult to secure one.
Restaurant was beautiful aesthetically from the countertops, to the decorative plants hanging from the ceiling.
Our server was extremely friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. He recommended all of our dishes and it was absolutely delicious. This Michelin Star restaurant has earned their awards consistently and it’s very telling why.

If you want to travel to the 70’s use their bathroom and you’ll see.

The wagyu steak sauce could be replaced with something more flavorful. I would have paired it with something other than potatoes but the sauce accompanied with the potatoes was delicious. The lamb Barbacoa tacos were excellent. The drink was tasty.

As we ended our experience, the server became slightly inattentive and handed us our check without asking other than that excellent food and atmosphere.

Highly recommend.

We came here for a brunch at Oxomoco this past Sunday, and wow, what an amazing experience. We started off with the guacamole, then with oysters followed by many other delicious plates such as the Caviar Tuna (out of this world), lamb barbacoa tacos (a must), Steak tacos, and papas bravas. Thank you Oxomoco for providing and organizing an amazing experience for my guests and I and having amazing tasteful food.

reviews_snippets.content: "Delish food and drinks, excellent service, warm, yet modern ambience and decor."
"Ordered many dishes: the steak the chicken the lamb tacos the corn guacamole."
"More like it came packed with tasty chicken chunks and crunchy chicharron bites."

business_details.details: 141 Leonard St, Brooklyn, NY 11206, United States

top_reviews.content:
I wanted to share a thoughtful review after my visit. The restaurant has a beautiful atmosphere, especially the outdoor area, which felt very warm and inviting. The food was honestly delicious, beautifully presented, and the wine selection was excellent. I ordered the Tagliatelle alla Bolognese, and it was absolutely flavorful and well prepared.

That being said, there are a few things that could be improved. Unfortunately, the service was not the best during my visit. I ordered an additional focaccia, but it never arrived, which was a little disappointing. I also felt that the menu could offer a few more options, as many of the dishes were vegetarian or vegan. For example, I was hoping to try a traditional lasagna, but the only option available was vegan.

Overall, I had some really enjoyable moments because the food, presentation, and ambiance were great. I truly hope the restaurant continues to grow and improve, as it has a lot of potential. Thank you for the experience!

Ordered gluten free pasta but was served regular. Did not realize until my leftovers were repacked with a completely fresh meal with Penne instead of Pappardelle. Waitstaff did not apologize or make note of the mistake.

I’ve been here twice now and both times the food was absolutely divine. Service is excellent and they’re always super friendly. The veggie lasagna is a can’t-miss dish for me: it is so packed with flavor and the noodles are perfectly cooked. The gnocchi pesto is fantastic as well. Affogato is delicious and a great way to end the meal. I’ll 100% be coming back again and again!
We went there on Friday for a date night & will 100% be returning. Food was incredible, service was amazing. Found my new neighborhood go to

I have never had anything but a 5 star experience here. With daily specials that will blow your mind, Testo is one of the best Italian restaurants in the city. Don’t forget dessert either, they have THE BEST ricotta cheesecake I’ve ever had.

reviews_snippets.content: "Fantastic atmosphere, quality of food, friendliness, service, music, and price."
"A vast wine selection and homemade pasta for unbeatable prices."
"Beautiful neighborhood Italian restaurant with a great selection of dishes."

name: Sungold
address: 96 Wythe Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11249, United States

business_details.details: 96 Wythe Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11249, United States
Open · Closes 11 PM · See more hours

top_reviews.content: We absolutely loved our experience at Sungold from beginning to end. It was a beautiful, quiet atmosphere, delicious food, courses were spread out well. Our server Israel was wonderful and attentive would highly recommend and return in the future.
Had a great veganized pizza! The taste was awesome and the chef was accommodating. I also liked the atmosphere for my friends bday party :)

Had a terrible dining experience here. We came in for an early dinner and ordered the Dirty Caesar and Cristo’s Seven Star pizza. We preferred no kale in the salad and kindly asked the server if he could accommodate that request. He proceeded to roll his eyes at us.

It wasn’t a huge deal, so we asked whether the salad was pre-mixed and whether separating the kale would inconvenience the kitchen staff. All he said was, “No, it takes more time for the chicken to cook.” He made no effort to explain his clear attitude problem.

The pizza came out before the salad, and it was really bad. The cheese and toppings slid off almost immediately when we lifted a slice. It seemed like the pizza wasn’t cooked evenly: the undercarriage was soft and doughy in some areas, while other parts were heavily charred. Obviously, we expected some char on the pizza, but some spots were completely burnt and inedible. We weren’t expecting a Dave Portnoy 10/10 — just edible pizza.

Then the salad came out. The croutons were stale, and the chicken was obviously not fresh. We promptly left and ate somewhere else.

Bad food is one thing, but the fact that the server didn’t have the maturity to simply explain that our request might be an issue was astounding.

Obviously, this place has great ratings, so our experience may not be typical. Maybe it was because we dined early on a Tuesday night. Still, it was absolutely unacceptable.

Very tasty menu for restaurant week! Will definitely be happy to come here again. As you can tell it's more of a quality over quantity restaurant, as most fine dining places are. But I was fairly full by the end of my meal and we'll worth it!

Came here for brunch with my friend and made a reservation just in case. The ambience is warm, modern, and perfect for a relaxed weekend brunch. Service was friendly and attentive the entire time. I ordered the mushroom sandwich with grilled chicken, which came with crispy fries and a side of spicy mayo absolutely delicious! My friend got the grilled chicken sandwich with fries as well, and we both loved our meals. To share, we ordered the brown butter maple old-fashioned pancake, and wow that was the highlight! Perfectly fluffy with just the right sweetness. We paired everything with lattes, which were smooth and creamy. It’s a calm spot to unwind, chat, and enjoy good food with great vibes. Overall great vibes. I’d absolutely come back again! ✨

Most amazing, relaxing atmosphere. The food was delicious, and the service was exceptional. Juan was exceptionally professional, polite, and welcoming. We spent our engagement weekend at the Arlo and Juan really made this experience all the more special. We are immensely grateful to Juan, the Sungold and the Arlo!

I wish I could give this place five stars because the people who work here worked their TAILS off to ensure we had a good time. Hilarious, kind, generous and so welcoming. We loved ebwryone we met. So to be fair, if we had come here JUST for the vibes, the vibes were immaculate and it was a total 5-star resort experience. The hostess, the doorman, our server Israel... everyone was SO kind and accommodating. Unfortunately, we came for the food. And the food was super lackluster and not an experience I would want to return to and have again. Thankfully, again, our service did everything they could to make up for the food and gave us great attention and effort. 🩷 Love them DOWN. But the cooking/kitchen could use some work to make the food match the experience and expense.

Came here tired after my red eye, and desperately needed a coffee. Caesar came to my rescue and made the best latte and also provided great service that was warm and friendly. The atmosphere is also beautiful and a vibe, perfect workday location! Would definitely come back!

reviews_snippets.content: "Stopped in for brunch, Good atmosphere, great food, and very kind service."
"Highly recommend scallops, pasta, salad, pancakes, chicken…"
"We ordered a Chicken Parmesan, Second Street burger, and the lamb meatballs."

business_details.details: 284 Grand St, Brooklyn, NY 11211, United States

top_reviews.content:
one of the best pasta i’ve tried! sooo good! the pasta perfectly cooked, love the sauce, everything. my favorite was the farfallone with butter chili, it’s salty, spicy, savory, a must try!! 10/10

- the salad and the seabream is fresh!🥗 8/10
- the porkchop is huge and shareable portion, love the sauce is umami and sweet, must try:) 8/10
- mezze maniche ragu is also delicious! 9/10

loved the ambience and vibes in here, alive but not loud, definitely a must visit restaurant!❤️ overall 10/10!

Quite surprised — not in the best way. Overall it was good, but nothing mind-blowing, especially the pasta. You can skip the cucumber salad, but the focaccia with whipped ricotta is a must-order. The highlight was the tiramisu (truly the best I’ve had in the city — not even exaggerating), which is what made the experience feel a bit uneven. On the plus side, the wine selection is phenomenal. The service is top notch as well.

One of my new favorite restaurants in NY! All of the food was inventive but not overly experimental, fresh, and delicious. The service was wonderful; we actually didn’t know who our server was because we were equally attended to by several warm people without it being too attentive. We also brought a birthday cake for one of our friends and the staff were very gracious about needing to refrigerate it for us until dessert. Ambiance was great as well, it wasn’t aggressively loud. Cannot wait to come back!

This place is the sister restaurant of the popular Four Horsemen. Waitlist line is pretty long but worth it. We put our name down at like 5:30pm and didn’t get seated until almost 9pm.

Everything was outstanding. The dishes are small but highly recommended.

Standouts:
- Tuna crostini
- Farfallone
- Malloreddus
- Pork Chop

Tried Cavallini for the first time after seeing someone I follow on IG; thought I’d give it a try. Found out that resy is  limited and always booked. The menu is so simple and so flavorful. Serving sizes are small but if you order a few dishes you’d like to try you will be full! We were served by Beau whom explained any questions we had and recommended the favorites of the guest. The service was amazing. I will be back!

reviews_snippets.content: "Impeccable service, ambiance, food and drinks."

name: Chef Katsu Brooklyn
address: 143 Greene Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States
description: Unadorned Japanese restaurant specializing in burgers, plus rice bowls & miso soup.

business_details.details: 143 Greene Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

top_reviews.content: After 10+ visits I can safely say that Chef Katsu consistently delivers! The humble establishment punches far beyond its weight with the food quality rivaling that of fancy restaurants at 2-3X the price point. The menu is not long, demonstrating careful restraint by the chef. One cannot go wrong with any item. My go-to orders are the salmon ikura rice bowl or the pork katsu curry. Haven’t yet tried the shrimp katsu burger, which looks scrumptious. Don’t skip the desserts like panna cotta or yuzu cheesecake.

Small spot with indoor and outdoor seating, so keep that in mind if you’re looking to dine in during peak times.

The salmon & ikura bowl was pretty good but feels a little overpriced for the amount of salmon you get. The ikura carries it. The staff were very courteous.

ordered the special katsu of the day- the shrimp katsu burger! it had the perfect bite and the bread was nice and fluffy. the shredded cabbage was crisp and well seasoned too.

the pork katsu burger was a bit forgettable in comparison but still enjoyable overall. i wish the pork katsu was thicker. i think that would've enhanced the dish. for the price, it was acceptable.

finally, we got the salmon and ikura bowl, which was fresh. the sushi rice was more flavorful than the standard stop and go spot.

i'd visit again to try their salmon dashi chazuke. seating is limited. we got lucky and came in 30 mins post opening and were able to sit wherever we wanted.

Absolutely phenomenal bowl of curry, so flavorful and rice and the chicken katsu was crispy and delicious even sitting in the curry. Some of the best curry ive had in the city. I will definitely return for more!!

This place has a small, local and casual vibe with very high quality salmon. Every time I eat from here I feel truly nourished and satiated and immediately look forward to coming back. I always get a salmon rice bowl and it never disappoints.

I got the salmon katsu burger, which I thought was pretty good. However, some friends got the katsu bowls and said they were fairly average.
My main complaint is that amongst the 8 of us, the staff got 3 orders partially incorrect. I understand that it was a busy evening and mistakes happen, but it seemed a little odd.

Simple and mighty spot for katsu dishes. Loved the chicken katsu curry. There is seating inside and outside. There's also a restroom. Reasonably priced, good portions, and casual vibes. Would recommend if you're in the neighborhood.

Haven't seen any reviews mention their shrimp katsu sandwich, which I think is amazing. The patty tastes fresh and you can see whole pieces of shrimp in it, and yet it's still incredibly juicy and crispy. The bun is fluffy, the tartar sauce is perfect -- it's just such a well-done sandwich that you can't find in many places!

As other reviews have mentioned, it's a small space, so it might be easier + more efficient to order takeout, especially at peak hours.

reviews_snippets.content: "Delicious food, reasonable prices and simply the nicest owners/staff."
"This place has a small, local and casual vibe with very high quality salmon."
"Food was great, we got the pork Katsu burger and the chicken Katsu rice bowl."

name: miss KOREA BBQ
address: 10 W 32nd St, New York, NY 10001, United States
description: Chic, zen-like Koreatown restaurant for barbecue, bulgogi and hot pots.

business_details.details: 10 W 32nd St, New York, NY 10001, United States

top_reviews.content:
Great Korean barbecue place. Ideally located near the train station. The atmosphere is relax and quiet. The service is very fast.
We all took the barbecue dish, which was good but the vegetarian one is very pricey for only vegetables and tofu, so not worth it. But there are other vegetrarian options on the menu.

Good food and very good service. The quality of the dishes is excellent, not cheap, but worth the price because of the overall experience. We went in a group, and a 20% gratuity is automatically added to the bill, which is fine because the service was very attentive and friendly. One thing to note is that the BBQ smell is quite strong inside the restaurant, so be careful—your clothes, especially jackets, may carry the smell after dining. Overall, a solid Korean restaurant with great taste and service, just be prepared for the strong grill aroma.

I visited Miss Korea BBQ and had such a great experience!
The food was amazing, but the meat is definitely the highlight — absolutely incredible 😋 So flavorful, tender, and perfectly cooked. You can really tell the quality is top-tier.
The kimchi jjigae was also delicious — rich, comforting, and full of flavor.
The atmosphere is warm and cozy, making it a great spot to relax and enjoy a meal. Overall, everything was just on point, but the meat truly stands out.
Highly recommend if you’re in Koreatown!

Underwhelming and totally overpriced!
My friend wanted to try something new and Miss Korea BBQ has amazing reviews. Having eaten there now, I have no idea why. Located on the south side of 32nd St’s K-town, Miss Korea BBQ is on the 2nd and 3rd floors. They used gas grills in the table (vs wood briquettes which definitely provide a better flavor). The wait staff moves fast and are efficient. They are used to handling as we saw lots of large parties at other tables.
Miss Korea BBQ serve the typical banchan, side dishes that are served ahead of the main dishes: Kongnamul (seasoned soybean sprouts), Eomuk bokkeum (fried fishcake), broccoli, kimchee (spicy pickled cabbage), scallion salad, etc. We ordered the marinated grill platters: pork belly, short ribs, galbi, bulgogi, prime ribeye. The stone pot bibimbap bulgogi lacked the crispy rice edges. The Sundubu Jjigae, Korean spicy tofu soup, was delicious. The BBQ portions were small and the prices high – probably spent almost a quarter or double what we spend at other Korean BBQs. Overall the food was good but just not as good as other nearby Korean BBQ places and way pricier.

Visited with friends, and we all thoroughly enjoyed our dinner. We ordered the marinated meat combo and loved every bite. The spicy beef noodles were excellent as well. Thank you for the attentive and friendly service, which made the evening all the more memorable.

reviews_snippets.content: "High quality food, just the weekend full of people need to wait for the service."

top_reviews.content: I decided to have an early dinner with a friend who suggested this place. We arrived around 5:30 and were seated immediately. I ordered some apps with a half-n-half, and my friend ordered the Lumberjack breakfast with an Iced Coffee. Our waiter and the staff were terrific. The restaurant was packed with great energy and a friendly buzz from couples and family groups. I love the vibe of this diner situated between Bed-Stuy and Crown Heights❣️

I really enjoyed how I was welcomed as I enter the diner. I also wasn't sure about the wine and was allowed to sample two kinds. Jerry is very pleasant, patient and accommodating.  He made sure everything was up to par. The food is delicious! Kudos to the chef. You can order anything on the menu at anytime of the day. I will be returning to try something new.

I definitely recommend it. They cook the best meat in all of Brooklyn here, absolutely delicious no matter what time you feel like coming. Everything is super delicious, and the staff is very friendly and helpful. Very pleasant, and the prices are good. 👍😋

The outdoor atmosphere is fantastic! We had breakfast and the food was good not great, typical diner food! The service could use a lot of improvement! It was like they were all just waking up! Food took a while to arrive! We would return for the atmosphere hoping the staff was just having an off morning!

The absolute best diner I’ve been to in New York! I love to come here late night after a party but it’s also great in the daytime for breakfast lunch or dinner! It’s such a classic old school vibe with a great ambiance for dining indoors or on the patio. The portions are massive and it’s a great value for your money. I usually get a sandwich but last time I had this bbq chicken salad which was delicious. Such a solid spot with great service

Had a late breakfast after a night partying. We were waited on by William, who was accommodating and pleasant. We had french toast, omelettes, and coffee. It was your typical diner food; it helped us sober up a little bit.

After hanging out it was 3:30 am and we were looking for a diner that was open. So here I am... My food was delicious 😋. I had corn beef hash with scrambled eggs with cheddar cheese. White toast and a hot tea. We had a tasty turkey sausage as well.

My family and I had a great time here! The food was absolutely perfect! Prices were great. I had a burger with fries and chicken tenders with honey mustard. It was all wonderful. My wife had eggs, bacon and French toast. I tried the French toast and it was amazing!!!! I couldn't stop eating it. Service was friendly and super fast. Bathroom was clean and smelled great. Employees were cleaning the dining room and chairs. Music was good. Couldn't ask for more from a diner. I will definitely be coming back very soon!!

reviews_snippets.content: "Breakfast, wraps, pasta, burgers, kid meals - they have a great menu."
"Vast menu selection, good food, good service and very friendly staff."
"I love the atmosphere though the music was pop but I enjoyed it eating my food."

name: Sisters
address: 900 Fulton St, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States
description: Cozy eatery focused on local and organic produce, with a dining room and a covered patio.

business_details.details: 900 Fulton St, Brooklyn, NY 11238, United States

top_reviews.content:
I took my mom to Sisters on Mother’s Day since everyone says we look like sisters 🙂‍↕️ The first time I came here was during my buttery last year so I thought it’d be a full circle moment to celebrate another year of life with my mom here! There was an event happening f along with the Mother’s Day holiday so the spot was pretty busy. Despite that, servers and staff were as attentive as they could be and super sweet! One of favorite things about this restaurant is just how open and light it feels ✨ In a world where many places to eat are super dark, hard to talk in and overwhelming, the bohemian and modern decor is a breath of fresh air 😌 To start, I got the spicy mezcal margarita (of which I got two; they know what they’re doing behind that bar, okay?)and Mom got an amaretto sour (which she said was PERFECT!)

We then shared the Cesar kale salad and coming from someone who believes they make the best kale salad in the world, Sisters is a CLOSE second 🥬 also that artichoke dip is TOO GOOD! I had to ask if there was something besides artichoke in it! Our Server told me they used to add crab but removed it (due to expenses) while still doing their best to keep to that original recipe and in my book? They succeeded✨

For our entree’s, I got the veggie burger (7/10) and mom got the fish sandwich (8/10)

It kind of dissapoints me when a veggie burger is so well dressed but then is kind of lack luster in taste, know what I mean? The patty itself probably just needed a bit more seasoning. As for the fish sandwich, my mom wasn’t a big fan of the house tartar sauce and also said it could’ve been more seasoned.

All in all, we had a great Mother’s Day dinner at this beautiful restaurant in Brooklyn. Highly reccomend this spot as a place to catch up, enjoy some sunlight and catch a good vibe ✨

I had the matcha and the Nicoise salad with tuna. The salad portion was small, the protein was even smaller, and it needed more dressing. It looked good but did not match the price.

My date had the fried chicken sandwich with fries and she enjoyed it. She kept talking about the fries, so I tried one. They make a great French fry. Crispy, well seasoned, and done right. If you judge a spot by the basics, they pass that test.

Service was solid and the atmosphere felt good, but the value on my dish missed the mark. I would go back, just not for the salad.

Gorgeous and popular brunch spot. They get super busy and strict 90-min table seating.

Food was amazing as was service. Had the shrimp and grits, French toast, and fried chicken sandwich. Would come back.

Visited yesterday, 6/27 around 1PM and were disappointed by our experience with the hostess. I completely understand being fully booked and having a wait for tables, but there’s a way to communicate that without being dismissive or having an attitude.

We ended up sitting at the bar, but every interaction with her felt unnecessarily unpleasant. The final straw was being told to move because we were in the way as we were literally standing up to leave after paying. Throughout the entire visit, we felt uncomfortable and unwelcome, like we were an inconvenience simply for being there.

The food was good, but the hospitality was not. Unfortunately, the hostess’s attitude completely overshadowed the experience.

What a cute place for brunch! The space has a ton of natural light and the wood and greenery makes you feel warm and cozy! The food is absolutely delicious. Bravo on the menu as everything we tried it was so good. The mimosa’s are good as is the Bloody Mary. This is a great place for a couple or a small group. There is lots of seating but often busy so I’d suggest making a reservation.

Delicious fish sandwich, perfectly crisp sweet potato fries, and a great cauliflower starter—plus lots of dishes with labneh, which I loved. We walked in as a party of two on a Tuesday night and grabbed seats at the bar for dinner, which ended up being the perfect spot. The staff was friendly, the ambiance was warm and lively, and the whole place just had a great vibe.

Worth noting: there are a few small steps up into the restaurant, but once you’re inside, it feels cozy and welcoming.

Would definitely come back!

On 4/20/26 chat gpt unfortunately recommended this place. I was a part of a table of three who came In for our last stop before going home to Pennsylvania. Me and the other two people in my party all ordered a well done steak all the same way just one with the sauce on the side they all came back medium. we kindly asked for them to be upcooked to well done. Once they came back. They looked the same if not even less cooked somehow I’m not sure if they tried to give us a new Steak considering they push a well done out in “15 mins”but it definitely appeared to be more red than it was even the first time around. ( when taking our order for 3 WELL DONE steaks she asked “is it okay if it takes about 15 minutes) we thought it was odd but just kept the visit going with high hopes and an open mind considering the ambiance was actually cute in there. It took her about 15 minutes to come back to ask if they were up cooked to our liking and then when we did tell her that they were the same- from the minute she took the plates away to the minute that we got our check both of the cooks are standing in the window staring making DIRECT EYE CONTACT talking about us like we’re the problem for Not wanting to eat a medium steak when we ordered well done all three of us. when the server dropped the check. She didn’t say thank you have a good night. Anything like that. thankfully for her i work in the service industry and still tipped. The whole restaurant just seemed mad at us for them not giving us what we ordered pretty backwards I know in New York it can be normalized to be rude and that’s just how stuff is, but I’ve never had a restaurant experience like that in my life will never be going back.

Amazing, professional, and very personable service. Got the kale salad with chicken and a boiled egg. The kale was good, could have been even better chopped more finely. Nice happy neighborhood boho vibe, the interior could be a little nicer with a touch of cosmetic TLC. You feel that this place is well-visited and long-established.

reviews_snippets.content: "Ordered the fried brussel sprouts, wings, fries, & cocktails."
"Beautiful space, great drinks, high quality food, great location on the C train"

address: 8210 Sepulveda Blvd, Panorama City, CA 91402, United States
description: Serves a variety of Thai noodle, curry, rice & seafood dishes, with lunch & dinner deals.

business_details.details: 8210 Sepulveda Blvd, Panorama City, CA 91402, United States
6G9M+X4 Panorama City, Los Angeles, CA, USA

top_reviews.content: I have frequented this establishment since before it relocated from the Topanga Canyon site where it was run by the husband and wife team(Wat & Apple...nice people), to the Panorama City location. Surprisingly, the quality has not changed in all these years. I say surprisingly, because originally, the chef that prepared all the dishes at the Topanga Canyon location was the husband and he is no longer doing so at the Panorama City location. Since I was spoiled by the first location, I was somewhat worried that the quality would diminish yet found out that he helped with the transition by working with the new cooks by offering his skill and experience. I have been promoting this restaurant as one of the hidden gems for the more discerning palate. Some of my favorite selections are as follows: Beef Panang or Fried Spicy Catfish , Tom Kha Gai, Tom Yum, Pad Prik Kang, Pad Woon Sen, Pad Thai ("Bohlan"/Traditional Style), Cashew Nut Chicken, Indian Curry Noodles Soup, Chinese Broccoli With Crispy Pork, Ground Beef Noodles, Green Curry, Duck Curry...really any of their curries, Pad King Ginger, Tofu Soup, Spicy Mint Leaves With Bamboo Shoots and the list goes on. Highly recommend paying this place a visit.

Original Khin Dang Thai is just one of many very good Thai eateries in the valley.  We tried it for the first time and came away fans of the diverse menu, warm service and delicious food.

The place was half full on a Saturday afternoon with families and couples happily eating.

It took us a long time to go through their good sized menu which had some really tantalizing options, like larb, spicy fried catfish, and a variety of noodle soups. Being just two of us, we settled on two of our usuals: Pad Thai (the more expensive special one as opposed to the standard one on the menu) and green curry chicken, plus steamed rice. Both were great but the Pad Thai was truly special, with little chunks of fried tofu, chicken and shrimp and plentiful bean sprouts. We really enjoyed the Thai chili vinegar condiment, which is served on a little tray along with chili flakes, chili paste, and green chilis in vinegar.

The service was really kind and attentive. We look forward to returning to try some more items very soon!
We’ve been here with our family multiple times, and every visit has been consistently satisfying. We always leave happy with our orders.

WOW! This place is truly a gem in the San Fernando Valley. I highly recommend coming here with a large group and ordering tons of different plates to split amongst everyone family style. We seated a party of 12 easily in the back room and our waiter was on point with our orders and ensuring everyone got what they needed. The ambiance itself is pretty standard, nothing that screams fancy, but it doesn’t need anything on the walls when the true star of the place is the food.

Every single dish I tried, and we ordered over a dozen, was extremely well done! Our plates came out one after the other, barely giving us enough time to divvy up the options amongst our party, and all of them were freshly prepared, steaming hot as they arrived. My favorites were the Seafood Soup, Duck Curry, and Mongolian Beef, but honestly you can’t go wrong here.

*Delayed post from May ‘25

Having been to Thailand not long ago, this review might be biased 🙈

The food (Pad See U & Spicy Pork Noodle Soup) was okay and the drinks (Thai Tea Boba & Thai Coffee Boba) were okay - though, I appreciate the coffee wasn’t super sweet… thank goodness 😅

top_reviews.content:
Visited SuihoEn Japanese Garden on a warm afternoon, and even though it was a bit hot, the garden was absolutely beautiful and worth it. The peaceful atmosphere, koi ponds, bridges, and perfectly maintained landscaping make it one of the most relaxing places you can visit in the Valley.

The garden is wheelchair accessible throughout, with smooth paths and gentle slopes that make it easy for everyone to enjoy the scenery. There are plenty of shaded areas to take a break, and benches positioned along the walkways for resting or just taking in the view.

They are currently doing some construction on parts of the grounds, which is expected to be completed in early 2026, but it doesn’t take away from the overall experience — most of the garden remains open and just as stunning.

Parking is free and convenient, and the small admission fee is well worth it. If you’re looking for a quiet place to unwind, take photos, or enjoy a peaceful walk, SuihoEn is a perfect choice. Even on a hot day, it’s a serene escape right in the middle of Van Nuys.

Plenty of fish, lush grounds, and honestly a real standout compared to the surrounding basin parks. Would recommend stopping by for a few hours to enjoy the nature and peace/quiet.

Went near mid-February for the first time and was pleasantly surprised! I expected it to feel smaller but it's a good sized area, despite a small portion near the entrance being closed off for guests for some remodeling.
The entrance is a little odd, somewhat hard to miss if you don't know where you're going. The gate had a no trespassing sign but also an open sign, so we just looked over at the guard to be sure we can go in and he waved us off.
Decent amount of parking; I hope entering on foot will be made less awkward once construction finishes.
We entered through the Admin building and there were some interesting little artifacts and displays. The architecture is really cool, looks kinda brutalist with all the concrete; it's definitely unique for the Valley. The inside does smell a bit musty since some of the water does pool into the interior. But it's not too bad, just like maybe an indoor pool that doesn't get treated with chlorine.
That musty smell does stay whenever you're around the water and, of course, when you to the observation deck over the treatment plant; but again, it's not that bad, though sometimes you will get punched by a random bad whiff.
The garden itself is beautiful, surprisingly well kept, it's good to see people respect the space here. There wasn't a crowd at all when we went either, so you definitely got some of the visual peace intended by the garden. Only sad thing is the surprisingly distracting noise from the airplanes going in and out of Van Nuys; but that's beyond anyone's hands and if you like planes, it could be a good place for plane spotting.
Most trees had shed most of their leaves except for the evergreens and the camelias were looking very full; some cherry blossoms were even starting to flower, but most were just budding which was still beautiful to see.
One thing I hadn't expected was the amount of mosquitos. There were some points where you had to cover your mouth and wave through literal clouds of mosquitos at risk of getting them in your mouth, ears and eyes. I think they're the tiny male ones, since they tend to cloud up like that, which is good because at least those don't bite. I'm not sure if they're more or less common in certain seasons, it had rained the day before so maybe that brought them all up. But considering how many there were, I'm guessing the mosquito fish were on strike or something.
The birds are another highlight of the garden. Lots of ducks of all kinds hang out in the pond, as well as egrets and cormorants. Only downside is that they also do their business in the garden, so that musty smell might be partially their fault!
In all, it's a very cool spot and definitely worth visiting often. It's cool to see a public utility, the treatment plant, be host to a space like this.

Winter Restaurant Week Review 3/6-

Recommendations for restaurant week: Apps- Goat cheese salad or pappardelle. Mains- Pomegranate duck, schnitzel, or branzini. Desserts- Persian lime pie. Lime pie is Steve's quality, and you can quote me on that.

Drink: Hot Toddy with bourbon, St. Germaine, honey, lemon, and clove for $12, which was standard and helped warm me up after walking across the bridge to get there.

Bread- Focaccia and olive oil to begin with.

For appetizers, my favorite that didn't have an extra charge was the Pistachio Crusted Goat Cheese Salad. The highlight, of course, was the goat cheese, which was nutty and slightly funky. I wish there were more roasted beets, and otherwise, I found the dressing a bit light. For $3 extra, there was the Pappardelle with buffalo oxtail ragu, which was small but tastier. The pasta wasn't the biggest portion, but it was perfectly cooked, and the ragu had a good consistency. If you don't mind paying a bit more, I would recommend it. The remaining appetizer, the Ozark Bar-B-Q Ribs, was a bit disappointing. While I liked the sauce, which had a sweet and spicy flavor, the ribs were very tough and a bit too fatty.

For the main course, my easy favorite was the Duck, which was a $6 supplement. The portion was very large, consisting of several pieces of sliced duck along with a duck breast. The sliced duck was tasty, but the larger piece was even more tender and flavorful. The sauce itself had a mild sourness and sweetness, and at the end, a few folks were mopping it up with the remaining bread.

Also tasty, but $3 extra, was the Pan Roasted Branzini. The fish was cooked well, being tender with crispy skin. The beans were mildly cooked and still had some texture, and I particularly liked the fish with the escarole, as the mild bitterness worked well. This was pleasant but perhaps a bit mild, and I think a light sauce would have helped, possibly with garlic and other ingredients. We also got Grilled Scottish Salmon with three mustards, cream, and horseradish. The fish was cooked nicely again, but I found it a bit too pungent.

The remaining dish with supplements, the Venison Bourguignon, was good, though a bit small compared to the other dishes. This was $6 extra, and the meat itself was tender, while the sauce was rich. I found it just a little bit salty, and I presume that was from the bacon, but it was good and honestly better than many of the generic bistros in the city. Speaking of bacon, we also got an $8 side of Brussels Sprouts, which were decent.

The best main dish sans supplement was the Chicken Schnitzel. The chicken had a nice light breading and was very tender. The mushrooms added earthiness, and the mashed potatoes were soft and buttery. Also lightly fried, but worse was the Veal Lemonese. Outside of sauce preferences, as both were prepared well, the veal was unfortunately much less tender.

For dessert, most of us got their highly recommended Persian Lime Pie. Instead of being a wide piece, this was more of a pie jar, similar to how Mia's in Cobble Hill, among other locations, serves it. However, the comparisons end there, with the flavors being much better. The filling had a perfect mix of sourness and sweetness. In terms of NYC, this was honestly the closest thing to Steve's Key Lime Pie that I've had. Another person had the Flourless Chocolate Hazelnut Cake, which was a bit above average but not comparable to the pie.

We overall had a pretty good meal here at this neighborhood spot. It's not the best for any particular dish, but it was mostly worth it for the price, especially if you don't mind paying extra for some things. Mid 3 bumped up.

I’m not big on a sit in dinners, so when someone mentioned a place that serves wild game, like not a situation where a  friend shot a deer and now there’s to many steaks, but surly qualified, the other dish my friend had gotten was turtle soup, she seemed disappointed because there wasn’t chunks of turtle…? It’s a soup, not a stew… and then the qual (not mine) I was told was good, but she was confused were the ribs were… I had to tell them that it’s commonly removed in order to stuff what is potentially a song bird, and last but not least was the elk! I never had elk but I have had that ~friends deer~ and I love mustard so I kinda new what was walking into, but I wasn’t expecting it to be straight to pure heaven, if I could have just a rack, made this way, I would die a happy woman!
4 dinners and a drink came to about 215… they don’t leave prices on the menu so you know you eating top notch.
I come from Thomaston CT, my partner lives in Catskills, and our other friend came from road island, so we came a distance, and tho it was tiring, I would go back for 3 helpings of that elk I’m still dreaming about.

Nice Japanese restaurant with great ambience and decor. I had yellowtail carpaccio, 1/2 dozen raw oysters, and some nigiri (which are sold as individual pieces). It was all very good. The oysters were on the small side, but they were a happy hour special at the bar. Bartender was very nice, but she was pretty busy.
I liked the place a lot and will probably hit it again before I leave.

The atmosphere of the restaurant is really cool. The restaurant is decorated with a lot of posters and it’s pretty spacious. Would definitely recommend the appetizers. Tip was calculated on tax though

I've been craving Japanese izakaya food for so long and glad I stopped by. The yakitori was decently priced and there were a lot of options. The food was flavorful and the cocktails were beautiful and delicious. I will definitely go back with more friends! Just be sure to book a reservation or you will have to wait a while! We ended up sitting at the bar but the bartenders were so nice and fun!

The only thing I would suggest they rethink is the music selection. The volume was great, didn't distract from our conversation. But when I did catch the music in my ear it was the same birthday songs over and over? Maybe just the day I went. But othet than that the vibe was great. Decor was amazing!

So this is after my second visit here, both times during weekdays.

First off, the price here is very cheap. You can chug a Blue Label on a rock for only $30 a pop. For reference to whiskey lovers, they used to be $40~$50 a glass back in ~2020 in the city.

I'm an Izakaya-goer, particularly for the ones in NYC as I rarely go to any venues in Flushing but this place is on par, if not better than some places around midtown.

The quality of food is what you can expect from an Izakaya standard, especially for its low price point. It's technically a sake bar with some small portion dishes to fill you up with.

You're not paying for Cote or Howoo KBBQ quality, let's be real.

The atmosphere, I love the oriental yet contemporary touch they have for the rooms and the hallway, particularly the bar.

And speaking of the bar, the attentiveness of the staff can be pretty inconsistent at the bar. I had some few trouble getting someone to take additional orders or close out my tab as I wasn't just hollering at a random staff,  considering they're probably all assigned to certain tables.

Overall, a bit mixed experience between 2 visits so far but props to Wei at the bar for making the first visit smooth. The bartender was literally grilling, serving, making cocktails and closing out tabs like a one-man brigade.

P.S. Like some other reviews have mentioned, their suggested tip calculates from the total with tax applied, not a deal breaker but kind of leaves a bit of bad taste.

Beyond amazing. Closest I’ve had to a Japanese experience outside of Japan. Accuracy to the izakaya styles of shinjuku and shibuya is crazy, with the added epic scenery in the back with some old Japan styled decorations and a fake Sakura tree. The food is a bit pricer than store nearby but def worth it, as the quality is far better. The speed at which the food came out after ordering was great and the menu selection is pretty large, so great for a large group and/or people with largely different tastes. Did a random spot selection for a birthday dinner and now this is def a continuous return spot.

I’ve been quite obsessed with una-tama don lately, so I made the trip to Izakaya Nana just for this. The giant piece of grilled eel definitely lived up to my expectation. The unagi was so massive it barely fit on the bowl!

The japanese street style decor and private dining booths make it feel super immersive, and even the restrooms are covered in Demon Slayer and anime posters.

＊Impossible Unadon $34.99 **
The bowl was topped with a giant piece of unagi and tamago over rice. It had a charcoal-grilled aroma, crispy caramelized edges, and a buttery center. The sauce was so delicious with white rice. If I had to be picky, I would've loved a fluffy dashi tamagoyaki instead of the simple tamago.

＊Kaki Fry $8.99 *
Crispy on the outside, juicy and briny on the inside. It was so yummy dipping into the tonkatsu sauce.

＊Hako Sushi $21.99
The last time I had hako (pressed) sushi was in Osaka, so I was excited to see it here. Each piece was beautifully presented like a tiny jewel, topped with colorful fish roe. The rice part was dry and dense though.

＊Yakitori platter $26.99
You can't go to an izakaya and not order skewers, so we got the 7-skewer platter. The beef skirt, pork belly, king oyster mushroom, and zucchini were the standouts. The chicken tender and chicken wing were a bit dry though.

My partner and I come here every chance we get; she loves the curry omurice! Great food, absolutely the friendliest staff, and drinks that always hit the spot. We, uh, kind of over-ordered food and our waitress was so nice in helping us pack up. We'll be back again soon, Izakaya Nana ;).

I saw tons of great reviews for Izakaya Nana, so my friends and I decided to check it out. We didn’t have a reservation and were quoted a 35 minute wait, but ended up being seated in under 10 minutes around 9 PM.

PSA: after 10 PM, I believe sake and oysters are buy one get one free!

Here’s everything we ordered:

Yakitori platter – 7 assorted skewers. Solid. The pork belly being the standout for me.

Fried soft shell crab – tasted good, but it seemed like only half a crab instead of a full one, which was a bit disappointing.

Karaage chicken – nicely fried and paired with a mayo based sauce, but the chicken was dry.

Sashimi platter – fresh and well presented. No complaints here.

Mentaiko cream udon – just OK. Not as creamy as expected and a bit bland. The dish didn’t really stand out.

Impossible Unadon – definitely worth it! Grilled eel with tamago over rice, generous portion.

Tornado omelette fried rice – the egg was slightly overcooked so it lacked that creamy texture, but the fried rice and curry had great flavor.

Overall, the food was good but not exceptional. I’ve had better, but it’s still worth trying.

top_reviews.content:
We were staying in the area for the last Ariana Grande concert at Barclays and this restaurant popped up on my husband’s social media. They advertised a pre-fixe menu, one of my favorite things in life.

We checked it out and were pleasantly surprised. They gave us freshly made focaccia to start. I had the meatballs & ricotta to start, while my husband got the zucchini fritters. All of that was great - off to a good start.

I had the chicken parm and my husband had the   francese. Both were delicious! We had the cheesecake (a little dense) and the tiramisu (perfection!) for dessert. For $45, that’s a great deal. We had a great time!

the steak is too good, still thinking about it. been here like three or four times and service is always amazing. food is reasonably priced. their brunch options are also good. had the bottomless mimosas and whenever i finished a glass there was another waiting for me.

It was my first time here, I traveled from the Bronx and My Bestfriend Girl picked this spot and we both loved it! The Best Authentic tasting Italian Food! Everything is Homemade and Chef Deserves All the Kisses 💋🇮🇹🍝🍤🍾🫶🏾

Phenomenal brunch. Bottomless mimosas were definitely worth it. The eggs were loaded with all of the fixings, food was quick to come out and the service was very fast as well. Highly recommend here for brunch!

Stopped in for brunch and it did not disappoint. The food was flavorful, the atmosphere made it easy to relax and enjoy your time. If you’re looking for a dependable brunch with a great vibe, this is definitely worth checking out.

name: Soothr
address: 204 E 13th St, New York, NY 10003, United States
description: Intimate space with al fresco dining, offering Thai noodles and soups, plus cocktails.

business_details.details: 204 E 13th St, New York, NY 10003, United States

top_reviews.content:
I visited Soothr a couple of years ago, and when I came back to NYC from Seattle for a football game, I knew I had to bring my friends here. It did not disappoint!

As a Thai person, I can honestly say the food is incredibly authentic, every dish is full of flavor and tastes just like home. The food came out surprisingly fast, and the service was just as impressive. The staff were warm, friendly, and attentive throughout our meal.

The best part? Every single one of my friends loved the food, and they’re already talking about coming back. It’s easy to see why Soothr has earned a Michelin Star.

We only have 3 days in NYC but we visit Soothr twice in this trip :) If you’re looking for authentic Thai food in NYC, this place is an absolute must-visit. Highly recommended!

Beautiful restaurant with lots of ethnic charm and décor that you can’t miss the moment you walk in. The space is impressively large, much bigger than most Asian restaurants I’ve visited in New York City.

We ordered Tom Yum seafood hotpot, mii moo tod, beef pad see ew, Panang duck lychee, moo krob, and a couple of vegetable dishes. The Tom Yum hotpot was packed with fresh seafood, and the broth had a great balance of sour, spicy, and sweet. The Panang duck lychee was wonderful. I never had duck in a Thai restaurant. The duck breast was so tender in creamy and flavorful curry. The moo krob was excellent too, with crispy skin and moist, tender pork belly. The beef pad see ew had a nice smoky wok flavor.

The service was efficient despite how busy it was. Great variety of Thai and Chinese dishes, and definitely worth coming back to try other items on the menu.

SOOTHR was honestly one of the best Thai restaurants I’ve had. The restaurant was packed when we went, which made it a little hard to have a conversation, but the food definitely made up for it.

The Yum Nuer was my favorite dish. The beef was tender and flavorful, and the combination of flavors was really good. I loved it so much that I could’ve easily ordered another one.

The Beef Pad Si Iw was also really good, with a nice savory flavor and just the right amount of sweetness. The Chicken Khao Soi was probably the most flavorful dish we had. It was a little too spicy for me, but still really delicious.

The Thai tea was also really good and went perfectly with the meal. Overall, everything we tried was flavorful and well done. The Yum Nuer was definitely the highlight for me, and I’d definitely come back.

Tucked away in a little storefront is this absolutely gem. You have 90 minutes to eat, but trust me that is plentyyyy of time. Menu is very extensive and drink options looked super cool as well. After you order the food comes out almost instantaneously. This was some of the best food I’ve had in the city. Staff were all super friendly and welcoming, the food was prepared to perfection and although the space can get tight, they run it like a well oiled machine. Would recommend coming here with friends for a quick dinner!

This review is based off my experience of a special collab dinner hosting chef Yia Vang however I feel that it is still a clear reflection of how the restaurant is run and the clear genius that comes out of that kitchen. Every item was so carefully prepared with flavors that were reminiscent of a mother’s cooking but were presented in a fine dining fashion. I’m not very fluent in Thai food but the staff was very attentive and knowledgeable about every element that was presented to me. My favorite dish of the night was the whole cooked branzino. It was steamed to perfection and Maintained great flavor from head to tail. I look forward to going back and trying more from the Soothr team

top_reviews.content: Heard about this place for a long time from my Thai friends and this place is amazing! We ordered fish curry and crab curry. So tasty! I’d say it’s over the spicy level of American standard but I personally loved it so much! Will come back and try others!

I’ve kept this review to myself because it was a hidden gem, but because it got so popular over the years… they deserve all the stars from me. This is my go to Thai spot and we’ve been coming here since the day they opened (not kidding, we’ve tried almost ALL their dishes. See pics yourself) We usually order +1 dish than how many are dining, so 3 dishes if 2 people.

The staff is the best crew ever, always explaining the new dishes on the menu and always welcoming everyone in with the widest smiles.

The menu used to be fixed with the same classic dishes but these last two years they started rotating seasonal menus with new ingredients. Don’t worry, their spicy duck Laarb will always be there!! We love how innovative their menu is, pushing everyone to try something new. Not gonna lie, there’s some wild shit on there — but they’ve never let us down!!

Goated spot for actual authentic Thai dishes, especially underrated ones involving fish. My favorites were definitely the crispy fish as well as the one in a soup, but really everything we got was excellent. The menu is rotating, but I trust whatever they have cooking up recently is going to be good. The staff is extremely helpful in helping decide what meals to select as well as what drinks would pair well with the selections. Overall, an excellent experience and would recommend for anyone looking for Thai food.

I was told by someone that this Thai restaurant is the best in Brooklyn. I was quite skeptical just because I am Thai and not easy to be pleased with the food in Thai restaurants in NYC in general. But I thought I should give it a try. I was surprised when saw the menu. The dishes are not the typical ones you usually see in Thai restaurants here. It is a small menu but has interesting dishes; some from the north and some from the south of Thailand. I ordered a northern pork curry called Hung Le. It was absolutely delicious and the picked garlic gave it an interesting flavor and texture. So I will go back and try other dishes for sure. Aroi Mak Mak ka!

Updated: I went there again on 10/11/2024 with 2 friends and it was absolutely delicious. My friends were impressed by the food and the overall experience. This time, we ordered 3 dishes. The portion of each dish was big enough for the three of us. I loved that they changed their menu to present interesting Thai dishes and their menu is small and simple.

I know. I was warned. But some of the dishes were way too spicy. And I ordered a dish that wasn't marked spicy but turned out to be quite spicy.

The flavors were quite good but eventually my face couldn't handle it anymore so I wasn't able to finish my meal because of the pain.

The service is attentive and fun. They checked with us several times about the spice and advised I don't drink water because it makes the spice worse.

The whole restaurant is very cramped and claustrophobic. Other than the colorful flatware and tabletops, it also felt pretty sparsely decorated. It feels like it's having a little identity crisis between being just casual / homey and more vibrant / artsy.

top_reviews.content: When we first saw this restaurant we thought it was closed. It looked super dark en there was no one sitting inside where we could see. Coming in there were around 4 people. We had a group of 5, and there was 1 table to accommodate us. We almost immediately got to order drinks, which took about 5 minutes to all arrive. We ordered food, which took 15-20 minutes to arrive. I got the mac & 3 cheeses, which wasnt macaroni but penne. I didn’t mind. It was VERY hot. I had to wait to wait to start eating, and finished 15 minutes after the rest of our group. I didn’t like it, but maybe mac & cheese just isn’t for me. The rest of my table gave the restaurant 3 stars, or 3.5. The kitchen makes a lot of noise and it was hard to hear the waiter at times. Though she was very friendly, that was the best part.

This spot was such a pleasant surprise. The steak was incredibly tender and full of flavor, and those fries with the sauce on top were next-level — crispy, rich, and seriously satisfying, I love the service, friendly, attentive, and just the right balance of professional and warm. Places like this are hard to find in Brooklyn. Highly recommend.

I had a wonderful experience at Brooklyn Bridge Bistro. The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared, with generous portions and excellent presentation. The staff was friendly, attentive, and made sure everything was perfect throughout the meal. The restaurant had a cozy, welcoming atmosphere that made it a great place to relax and enjoy good food. Overall, it was an excellent dining experience, and I'd definitely return to try more of the menu.

Daydreaming Brunch!
Cozy vibes: Must to try Banana Walnut French toasts and the delicious shashuka eggs!! Perfect combo❤️‍🔥 also amazing hot coco and fried chicken with waffles and breakfasts sandwich!
Lovely place, food and service! I will be back for sureee

Every time I cross the bridge, I stop by this restaurant! The avocado toast is my favorite, and you definitely have to try the caramel latte. The service is top-notch, and it's one of the most delicious places in New York.

The whole experience was negative. First we had to wait 35 minutes to get our food, which wasn't a large or complicated order. We ordered a burger, a chicken sandwich, and a bowl of soup. They could have brought the soup out first, but waited until they brought the sandwiches as well. Meanwhile, a family that had just been seated 5 minutes prior got their whole order just after us. The soup was clearly from a can and heated in the microwave. The salt that was missing from the soup was coating the fries. My dining partner couldn't even eat the fries they were so salty. After bad food and a long wait, the 18% automatic gratuity was not earned. They put it on the menu that the gratuity is included, but diners should have the option if the food and service is bad. The included picture shows some of the concentrated salt on the fries. Overall, not worth the hassle.
Everything was Amazing. Food very tasty. Personal very kind.

I understand why some businesses limit restroom access, but this policy left a bad impression. I urgently needed to use the restroom and was told I had to buy a $5 bottle of sparkling water first.

I’d rather remember a restaurant as the place that let someone use the restroom than the place that turned them away.

top_reviews.content: Loved everything about this place. It was the quintessential neighborhood date night place. The menu was not your run of the mill Italian menu. Every dish was delicious and well prepared. We loved every dish but you must have the artichokes and The abbacchio.  Sorry that my photos do not do justice to the food. We went all out from cocktails to dessert but you can certainly eat well here for less money than we spent .

The first time I came here was great! The food was reasonably priced and simple but flavorful. The other two times I visited, I had a different experience. One time I had to send a chicken entree back to the kitchen since it was so overcooked, it was almost inedible. Both times, the pasta was undercooked for my partner and I to the point of also almost being inedible. I'm unsure why the quality dropped but hope they focus on these issues going forward.

I’ve been coming here for about 5 years. It’s a wonderful place. The food is always excellent and the service amazing. However, I recently ordered the tagliata (steak dinner), and it just came with the steak and arugula…in the past it’s always come with mashed potatoes. I had to order them separately for an extra 7$…40$ and it only comes with arugula on the side?? It was absolutely delicious as usual, but I think it’s insane that it doesn’t come with a proper side dish. BRING BACK THE MASH!!! (I had eaten a few pieces of steak before I took the photo, it was a proper 8 ounce sirloin) I’m not sure I will order that again. I also had the salad misto as a starter, and a lemon and sage spritz. All told my bill was like 80$. To spend 70 plus dollars on a dinner out and not get a full meal with proper sides is just wild. Like I side, the food is always excellent superb and I love the staff, but I’m not sure it will stay in the rotation, at least for that meal anyway.

I came to camillos with my sister and we have a wonderful time.The atmosphere is so warm and welcoming as soon as you walk in and that's very important for us.Service was on par and waiters were very kind and attentive where it was needed.Pizza was actually very delicious probably one of the best crusts I've ever had.I ordered the goat,cornmeal and  collard greens

I have been coming to this restaurant for around five years, and it has always been one of my favorite places. The food quality has consistently been excellent, and the service has always been friendly and professional. However, my most recent visit left me a little disappointed, especially with one of the menu changes.

I ordered the tagliata, which is the steak dinner, and while the steak itself was absolutely delicious as always, I noticed that it only came with arugula on the side. In previous visits, this dish included mashed potatoes, which really helped complete the meal. This time, I had to order the mashed potatoes separately for an additional $7, which was frustrating considering the steak dinner itself was already around $40.

The steak was cooked well and tasted great, but paying that amount and only receiving a small side of arugula felt disappointing. A proper side dish made the meal feel more complete in the past, and I truly hope they consider bringing back the mashed potatoes as part of the dish.

For starters, I also had the salad misto, along with a lemon and sage spritz, and both were enjoyable. The overall quality of the food remains very high, and the staff continues to provide great service. My total bill came out to around $80, and while I don’t mind paying for a good meal, I do expect a more complete dining experience at that price point.

It is unfortunate because this restaurant still does many things right. The flavors, atmosphere, and hospitality are all excellent, and I have always enjoyed coming here. However, small changes like removing a traditional side dish can really affect the value of the experience.

I would still recommend this place because the food and service are consistently impressive, but I am not sure I would order the tagliata again unless the original sides return. Hopefully, they take customer feedback into consideration and bring back what made the dish feel special.

Overall, a good experience, especially if you appreciate culinary creativity.

Interesting and inventive menu, but the food presentation was not quite a match.

Our waiter was exceptionally courteous and friendly, although they were clearly stretched thin. So service was pleasant, while understandably a bit slow at times.

Cozy and comfortable design, with a few elements that felt a little out of place. Art for sale displayed on the walls was a fun and interesting detail, although it's hung too high so hard to see/appreciate the details.

Despite the minor logistical and aesthetic quirks, the quality and flavor of the food, and interesting menu make it a good place to visit.

My wife in I were wandering and found this place, prices looked reasonable so we went in. Was very good she had stroganoff and I did meatballs and dumplings. Server said he makes a mean espresso martini and he delivered. I never got the Brussels sprouts I ordered tho. But food was good enough I’m not dropping a star.

Had the best experience hosting a surprise birthday brunch here! From start to finish, everything was seamless. Olga was so easy to communicate with while planning, and Conrad took amazing care of us on the day.

The food was absolutely delicious across the board, and the atmosphere made it feel extra special and fun for the celebration. You can really tell the team knows how to create a great experience.

I’ve been here a number of times before and this just reaffirmed why I keep coming back. Could not recommend it more and will definitely be back again!

A wonderful place for lunch with a warm and cozy atmosphere. Every dish is thoughtfully prepared and full of flavor — you can truly taste the love in every bite. The service was exceptional, and the staff were friendly, attentive, and welcoming. Huge thanks to the team for making the experience so special. Keep up the great work — I’ll definitely be coming back soon!

The aesthetic was super cute—definitely a cozy, stylish spot. We started with the Crispy Feta Cigars and the Beef & Pork Dumplings with caramelized onions, and both were absolutely mouthwatering. For the main, I had the Steak Frites (petite tender), which was incredibly satisfying—especially paired with those perfectly crisp truffle fries.  We had a fantastic server—warm, attentive, and really added to the experience. And the cocktails? Total hits. Definitely looking forward to coming back! Also The music selection was very cutesy very mindful. 🤍

The food was good. Let me start with that. It wasn't anything spectacular. The menu was fixed, but the variety was pretty good. I don't personally think it was worth the price. Now the details.

The beet salad was delicious. It was one of the appetizers. The oysters were good, however, one of the oysters had a pea crab in it. That really put us off.

The lamb was the best part of the meal. It was cooked perfectly, and the brussel sprouts they sat on were so flavorful.

The lobster ravioli were rather underwhelming. And again, for the cost, the quantity and presentation were both lacking.

Overall a good meal. We most likely will not be back

The food here is absolutely fantastic! The atmosphere is also really lovely; it's the perfect place to relax and enjoy a good meal. And the best part is, you usually don't have to wait for a table. I can't understand why this restaurant isn't as popular as it should be – it's a real gem! I highly recommend giving it a try.
