top_reviews.content: Number 7 is exactly what you need in a relaxed neighborhood joint. No pretentions. Great cocktails and solid wine and beer options. A tasty burger and over-flowing plates of fries. And a long inviting bar with no TVs blaring away. The perfect place for a casual meal or a drink and good conversation. The only downside is it's only open Wednesday through Saturday.

No. 7 is a perfect restaurant for a night out in Brooklyn. It’s casual and also beautiful. There is always something new and fun on the menu. This time the Haloumi was amazing! The service is great and the wine list is superb while being fairly priced. Love that you’ll see families in the early evening and first dates later on. Must visit spot!

I don't write reviews often but I had such a stand-out experience here a couple weeks ago, I have to share. I was in the area with a friend after seeing a local theater performance and wanted to sit down for a nice bite to eat but not be in the middle of a loud bar, and given it was around midnight we were doubtful we could find a spot. We happened to be maybe a block from No.7 restaurant and it was exactly what we were looking for. Everything we ordered was fresh, HOT, and truly so delicious. We got the fried baby artichokes to start, absolutely incredible I wish we ordered two, and I got the broccoli/seitan veggie cheeseburger which was maybe the best veggie burger I've ever had. So flavorful and they don't skimp on toppings (points). My friend got the giant minimal burger and said the blue cheese on the fries was exceptional quality (worth noting as blue cheese can be hit or miss) and the burger was definitely big. And while I'm at it the fries were super crispy shoestring fries, loved those too.
We got the grilled pineapple for dessert, which I didn't see anyone mention in the reviews and that is a TRUE SHAME because it was such a unique and delicious yet simple treat. First off the pineapple was ripe, and it had such a tasty charred flavor to it. Man I wish I had some right now writing this review is killing me.
As far as drinks, we tried the "if you please" gin cocktail from the menu which is made with Lillet, neither of us knew what Lillet was but went for it anyway. Turns out something about the cocktail had a pretty licorice-y flavor and neither of us were really digging it. We didn't say anything and drank maybe half each, but when our server noticed we didn't finish them before ordering another drink she asked if anything was wrong and if we wanted her to take them off the bill. We said no it's okay, we just tried something new and didn't love it but it was no fault of the bartender's or anything. She wound up taking them off the bill anyway which I really appreciated especially that we already told her it wasn't necessary. I'll be back here for sure

This is the epitome of a neighborhood GEM. Nice and cozy inside with welcoming staff, and delicious food.  Party of 5, we ordered various burgers, pork chop and broccoli Tacos.  Everything was superb, and the fries her are so tasty.  They brought over a couple of absolutely scrumptious desserts, the cake by far the best cake I’ve had in a while!  Given I live in Arizona, it is a tragedy that I can’t be a regular.

Broccoli Taco: order every time I go there, how are tacos made with broccoli??  But they are delicious.
Giant minimal cheeseburger: medium cook. Came with French fries. Pickles, wow sour, spicy, sweet bunch of flavor in one slice of pickle.
So yeah, No.7 highly recommend

top_reviews.content:
This place is truly a hidden gem! It definitely deserves more attention because everything is on point.
Our server, Saul, gave us excellent recommendations and took great care of us throughout the evening. The prices are more than reasonable compared to nearby places, and every dish we tried was delicious. Fish tacos are a must try.
We'll definitely be back to try more dishes!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
This place blew me away! It’s a Mexican restaurant, but the chef blends in Asian influences beautifully every dish feels layered and creative. I had the Chef’s Tasting Menu with eight courses plus two desserts, and everything was outstanding.

Unlike most Mexican or South American dishes that lean sour, the flavors here were perfectly balanced not too tangy, not too salty, just right. The seafood and pork dishes were the highlights (if you don’t eat pork, definitely let the kitchen know in advance).

The duck liver course completely stole the show melt-in-your-mouth smooth, richer and more refined than foie gras. The fried chicken wings were another surprise the skin was coated in corn flour, making them chewy and crisp at the same time, and the staff even brought a little bowl of water for cleaning my fingers. So thoughtful!

The service was warm and attentive, and every plate looked like art. The desserts were stunning both visually and in taste tying the entire meal together beautifully.

Honestly, this is the best Mexican restaurant I’ve ever tried, no exaggeration. Highly, highly recommend it!

Came here on a weekend dinner and it was packed by 7:30, highly recommend to make a reservation.  10 courses for ~$60 and every dish is so flavorful and creative. Loved the first appetizer, chips and bloody orange guacamole, tostada was refreshing and delicious, the small bites with various seasonings and flavor. We got to try the softest ribs with handmade tortilla with some pumpkin sauce, bbq sauce and furikake. The desserts were banging! One star off since the dishes were on the oily side

Xixa deserves nothing less than five stars!! In the past, I have found that top quality Mexican food can be hard to come by in the city, but after dining at Xixa I can take back that statement. I have found THE spot. Not only was the flavor profile of each dish divine, but the service was great. Our waiter was attentive, and even brought us comped drinks! Two of my favorite items on the menu probably had to be the seasonal guac and the braised short ribs. I have never tasted meat so tender. It fell off the bone. Also, all of the sauces that came with it tied it all together. The entree came with house made blue corn tortillas to put all of the fixings in. Orgasmic! We also ordered drinks, and they were amazing! They have a deconstructed menu which is really fun! If you want to enjoy some incredible food and a romantic atmosphere then this is the place. 12/10!!

The chef's tasting menu was of good value @$58/pp. The menu changes seasonally and some highlights this time included: bone marrow taco, mole beef taco. Their flan was some of the best I've had (almost like Panna cotta)  Don't expect to be wow-ed but the reasonable price makes the experience with it.

Just FYI they change 20% service fee directly on the bill so you don't need to to tips extra

name: Junoon
address: 19 W 24th St, New York, NY 10010, United States
description: Sophisticated Indian cuisine and a notable wine list offered in an elegant space with ornate accents.

business_details.details: 19 W 24th St, New York, NY 10010, United States

top_reviews.content:
The taste profiles here are genuinely inventive. I’d never encountered food built this way, and for sheer creativity it earns full marks. We did the tasting menu, which ran about $1,300 for six. Steep, but that’s the territory for a restaurant at this level.

A few things held the experience back. The ordering process was confusing. More than once, two different servers approached us asking the same or conflicting questions, and tightening up that coordination would go a long way. Pacing was also on the slow side, with 10 to 30 minutes between courses, though the payoff made the wait feel worthwhile.

On the food itself, the concepts were exciting but a few dishes didn’t land in execution. The pani puri had no crunch, and some of the bread courses tasted off. Texture was the recurring issue, with a few dishes coming out soggier than they should have.

Being honest, this was a one-time experience for me. There wasn’t a dish I’d return specifically to eat again.

Their garlic naan was one of the best one I have ever had. The menu was well constructed, and the service was great. The flavor of condiments and side dishes was also taken care of, so overall I had a great experience here. Their garlic naan was really superb.

We chose the four-course dinner at Junoon, and it was an exceptional experience from beginning to end. What impressed us most was that this wasn’t simply a meal it felt like a thoughtfully curated journey through modern Indian cuisine.

Every course arrived beautifully presented, with an incredible amount of attention to detail. Before we started each dish, the staff took the time to explain what we were being served, the ingredients, flavors, and how the different elements of the plate worked together. That small touch made such a difference. Instead of simply eating one course after another, we were able to appreciate the thought and creativity behind each dish.

The food itself was excellent. The grilled dishes had wonderful char and depth of flavor, while the curries were rich, aromatic, and beautifully balanced rather than overwhelmingly heavy. The breads came out warm and fresh and were perfect alongside the main courses. Even the accompaniments felt intentional rather than like an afterthought.

One of the things we appreciated most was how Junoon takes traditional Indian flavors and presents them in a sophisticated, contemporary way without losing their identity. Some of the combinations were unexpected, but everything felt purposeful. The plating was almost too beautiful to disturb edible flowers, carefully placed garnishes, contrasting sauces and textures, and even touches of gold leaf made each course visually memorable.

Dessert was a perfect ending to the four-course experience. Just like the savory courses, the desserts were creative, elegant and beautifully presented, with different textures and flavors that made them much more interesting than a typical restaurant dessert.

The service deserves special recognition as well. The team was attentive and knowledgeable, and we never felt rushed through the courses. Their explanation of every dish added so much to the experience and showed the level of care Junoon puts into its food and hospitality.

Overall, our four-course dinner at Junoon was much more than just going out for Indian food it was an experience. From the first presentation to the final dessert, there was a clear attention to flavor, technique, presentation and service. If you appreciate Indian cuisine and want to experience it through a more refined and creative lens, Junoon is absolutely worth visiting.

A memorable evening, beautiful food, outstanding presentation, and excellent hospitality. We would definitely return.

While everything was great, their service was by far the most impressive part of our experience today. Will absolutely come back again. Today we were a party of 4, but the can certainly accommodate parties as large as 12

Michelin-starred Indian restaurant in Midtown Manhattan. We came here for dinner and enjoyed the special fixed menu option for Valentine’s Day.

Course #1 (Starter): three tiny handheld bites. The first was an interpretation of Pani Puri, the second was a Saag Rota with Truffles and the third was Uthappam topped with a seaweed caviar.

Course #2 (Appetizer): we got the Smoked Chicken Vindaloo Tikka and the Tuna and Caviar Phuckha. Both were absolutely perfect, I particularly enjoyed the grilled flavor of the chicken.

Course #3 (Entree): we chose the Lobster Moilee served on a bed of coconut cream sauce along with the Xacutti Chicken, served in a gravy of coconut, tamarind and red chilies. We loved both dishes, especially the lobster which was cooked to perfection. The entrées were served with rice, daal done two different ways, crispy stringy okra and a basket of naan.

Course #4 (Palatte cleanser): A small
Dragonfruit sorbet.

Course #5 (Dessert): We chose the chocolate mousse/cake served with this frozen fruit circle which we couldn’t identify but tasted pretty interesting and we also got the sticky toffee pudding which had whole pieces of dates in them. Both desserts were fantastic.

Special shout out to the service team: we ordered some mocktails in the beginning that we absolutely hated and they were so generous to switch them out for mango lassi free of charge. On the bill they even deducted the charge for the mocktails.

We really enjoyed this Valentine’s Day dinner.

We had a wonderful experience at Junoon NYC! The service was excellent, and the menu was beautifully curated with plenty of vegetarian options, which we really appreciated. We visited for my birthday and ordered the 4-course menu for four people. The bill came to around $500 before adding an 18% tip, which felt fair for the overall experience and quality.

The team was also very kind and accommodating with my child, and they even brought out a cake for my birthday, which made the evening feel extra special. Overall, it was a lovely spot for a celebration and a memorable dining experience!

Very good Indian fine dining and an excellent lunch option in New York. The food was creative, well presented and full of flavour, while still clearly rooted in Indian cuisine. The atmosphere was elegant but relaxed, making it a pleasant place for a longer lunch.

The service was professional and attentive, and the overall experience felt refined without being overly formal. A very good choice if you are looking for Indian food at a higher level than a typical restaurant, particularly for lunch.

Junoon definitely lives up to its reputation as a Michelin-star restaurant. The food was beautifully executed and full of bold, balanced flavors.

The mango fish curry was very flavorful, with a great mix of sweetness and spice that didn't overpower the dish. For dessert, the ma rice pudding was excellent creamy and comforting, topped with toasted almonds and pomegranate that added a really nice texture and contrast.

One of the highlights was the pani puri with tuna. It was very good and refreshing, and a creative, modern take on a classic Indian street food.

Overall, a great dining experience with thoughtful dishes and high-quality ingredients. Definitely worth a visit if you're in Flatiron and looking for elevated Indian cuisine.

top_reviews.content:
Stellar service, very nice staff!

Unfortunately the food was flavor overkill. I ordered heirloom tomatoes + watermelon. Perfect summer foods. But the dish was drowning in some weird jam, and mint, and herbed croutons. Too much. Same with the brownie dessert. There was a brownie with chocolate sauce with some kind of crumble and some salted cream thing over it AND ice cream. Also, it was absolutely freezing in there. It was 75 degrees outside or so but maybe 60 inside. Unnecessary!

The place looks nice :) and as earlier stated, staff couldn't be nicer.

What a fantastic experience from start to finish. The food was absolutely outstanding—every dish was beautifully presented, full of flavor, and clearly prepared with great attention to detail. You can really taste the quality of the ingredients and the care that goes into every plate.

What made the evening truly special, though, was the staff. Everyone we interacted with was incredibly warm, welcoming, and genuinely kind. It’s rare to find a restaurant where the level of hospitality matches the quality of the food, but Otis does exactly that. The team made us feel at home from the moment we walked in, and their friendliness and professionalism elevated the entire experience.

The atmosphere is cozy, inviting, and perfect for a relaxed dinner. Between the exceptional food, the thoughtful service, and the wonderful people behind it all, this was one of the most memorable dining experiences we’ve had in Brooklyn. We’ll definitely be back and highly recommend Otis to anyone looking for an outstanding meal and truly genuine hospitality.

We knew it when we walked in the door!

The smell of spices hit us first and we knew it would be an enjoyable dinner. Our server (Carla?) bought just the right amount of humor and whit to the table and made excellent recommendations. We order one of just about everything and everything was excellent. We thought the P.E.I. Mussels might have been the weakest dish - not the most tasty broth and the mussels themselves just didn't taste fresh. On the other end of the spectrum, the Rainbow Carrots were to die for - an amazing Smokey dish.  The Braised Pork Pasta and the Burrata were also notably tasty as was the Gnocchi with oyster mushrooms. An accidental splash of water into my wife's lap lead to a complimentary strawberry-rhubarb crumble dessert that we shared and devoured. We'll go back again for sure!

Otis has truly become our signature restaurant. We’ve celebrated anniversaries, birthdays, and so many special date nights there, and every experience has been amazing. The atmosphere is warm and intimate, the food is always incredible, and the service makes you feel so welcomed every single time.

It’s one of those places that feels special no matter the occasion, and it has become such a meaningful spot for us over the years. We always leave happy, full, and already looking forward to coming back. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a memorable dining experience.

Food and atmosphere were amazing! Gem lettice salad and scallop risotto were my favorite.

P.S. I come here often and always wonder why this place isn’t listed under the Michelin Bib Gourmand. My guess is that the food takes quite a while to come out between each dish, which might be the reason. Other than that, I’m always satisfied with the meal.

Went here tonight with my wife. Let her pick the apps which is always a gamble. She got us the burrata and these carrot things. Frankly, those carrot things were off the charts. Was wild. Thought they’d be trash. Main courses and drinks all good too. Ambiance was what you want for the hood.

I was nearby and came in looking for a place to eat dinner. It was a good call.
I ordered the braised pork pasta and a beer.
The pork was tender and paired well with the gigli pasta. The sauce smelled good and tasted nice too.

I asked for a beer recommendation, and they suggested one that fit my taste, which made the meal more comfortable.
When I visited, I was the only one dining alone, but sitting at the bar still felt relaxed and easy.

At Otis, the food delivers with quiet confidence—nothing flashy, just deeply satisfying execution across the board; the pastas are the clear highlight, rich yet balanced with perfectly cooked textures and bold, clean flavors, while the small plates feel intentional rather than filler, each offering thoughtful contrasts and precise seasoning; entrées carry the same composure, showcasing strong technique without overcomplicating the dish, and even dessert, though simple, lands exactly where it should, rounding out the meal without trying too hard—if there’s any critique, it’s that portions lean refined, but the quality more than justifies it, making the overall experience feel polished, memorable, and worth returning to.

top_reviews.content:
As someone who loves Thai curry, I had been wanting to visit Pranakhon for a long time, and now I understand why it’s consistently packed.

Instead of ordering the usual favorites, I focused on their curries. The Kaeng Tae Po had a wonderful balance of sweet, sour, and herbal flavors with tender pork belly, morning glory, and fragrant kaffir lime leaves. The Kaeng Rawang was my favorite—a rich coconut and turmeric curry with crispy soft-shell crab, young coconut, lemongrass, and crispy okra. It was creamy, aromatic, and full of flavor without being too heavy. The Short Rib Massaman was comforting and deeply flavorful, with fall-apart braised short rib in a thick, mildly sweet curry served with potatoes, onions, and lotus seeds.

The restaurant itself has a warm atmosphere inspired by old Bangkok, with beautiful décor that feels both traditional and modern. Service was friendly, and despite how busy it was, the food arrived at a good pace.

If you’re looking to explore regional Thai cuisine beyond the standard menu items, Pranakhon is definitely worth a visit. I can see why it has earned its Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition, and I’ll be back to try more of the menu.

Pranakhon interior captures the atmosphere of Bangkok, and the staffs were friendly and attentive throughout our visit. The restaurant is also conveniently located and has a lively ambience.

As for the food, it was generally enjoyable, but I personally didn’t find it as authentic as I had expected. The flavors seemed to be adjusted more towards local preferences. The Massaman curry, while traditionally on the sweeter side, was noticeably sweeter than it should be, which overpowered the balance of spices. The duck curry had a similar issue, with the sweetness standing out more than the rich, aromatic curry flavors.

Overall, the food was acceptable and the presentation was good, but if you’re looking for a more authentic Thai dining experience, the flavors may not fully meet your expectations.

Had lunch here with 4 adults and a child, we enjoyed the flavors of the food. Especially the big noodle soup we shared. The crab fried rice was good and we enjoyed our drinks. The only thing we weren't fond of were the curry pancake and the pad thai being overly moist but all in all a great meal. We loved the decorations and the staff was great!

Amazing restaurant. This should be a definite stop for good, flavorful Thai food. We orders thai pancake, Pappaya salad, Chicken wings, and couple of other appetizers.  Everything was tasty. But what stole the show was Shrimp Tom Yum, Crab fried rice and chicken massam curry. Pad Thai was ok and chicken fried rice od good. Place is loud but has great vibe and very attentive service.

Dishes have great flavour overall. Highly recommend the crab fried rice and pork belly with morning glory. The short ribs were also quite tender and flavourful. Would avoid the soft shell crab in curry (way too much batter).

On top of the food being hit or miss, the kitchen and store looked dirty and outdated, which only made the experience worse. Between the processed frozen beef and lamb and the lackluster chicken, this isn’t a place I’d come back to.

Do yourself a favor and just go.

The food itself looked beautiful and I'm sure tastes great, but as a strictly vegetarian customer (for religious/faith reasons, not a trend I'm following), I had a genuinely uncomfortable experience watching it get made.
I chose a seat at the bar specifically because I could see the prep area, and I'm glad I did, because it showed me something I wish I hadn't seen. The person preparing my cucumber salad had just finished marinating and frying chicken. She was wearing gloves, which I appreciated, but instead of changing gloves or washing with soap between handling raw meat and my vegetarian dish, she just rinsed her gloved hands briefly with water and went straight into cutting my cucumbers.
I also ordered the bao bun with eggplant, and watching the single fryer in use, I have to wonder if the eggplant was fried in the same oil as the chicken. For someone who keeps strictly vegetarian for personal or religious reasons, this isn't a minor detail, it's the whole point.
I want to be clear I'm not trying to start a pile-on. I genuinely don't know if what I saw is just an industry-standard shortcut that most people wouldn't think twice about, or an actual lapse. But from where I was sitting, it didn't look like there's a real separation between meat and vegetarian prep, and that matters a lot to those of us who eat this way out of conviction. I'd love to see more attention paid to glove changes, separate utensils, and dedicated fryers for vegetarian items. Until then, I'll have a hard time trusting the "vegetarian" label here, even though the food on the plate looked excellent.

Burrata starter was super tasty.
Sancerre by the glass was very nice and fresh, also very good coffee quality.
I will probably go back, but for dinner to try their well-known pizza.

Such an amazing find. A cozy, warm hug against the cold.

I rarely find myself in NoMad, but before heading to the Madison Square we decided to grab a bite nearby — and I’m so glad we chose Cecconi’s. I completely fell in love with the place. The food was absolutely delicious and yes, they even make excellent pizza, and the overall atmosphere was warm and inviting. What really stood out was the staff, Andrea and Jesus: incredibly friendly, attentive, and very respectful of our tight schedule that was the most import, especially when our best niche awaits us with the game of a night of professional hockey between the New York Rangers and the Philadelphia Flyers in the iconic stadium Madison. I can’t wait to come back to Cecconi’s restaurant.

The ambience and overall vibe were great. Stylist, relaxed and not overly crowded. If felt like a perfect setting for a confortable dinner where you can actually take and enjoy it the space.

Loved the experience and can’t wait to come back. Highly recommended!!!

I love this restaurant. I've been several times, and the service is always excellent. The manager and the waiters are very friendly. They're always attentive to even the smallest details. I loved the ricotta dip and the beef tartare. I highly recommend them. Also, the cocktails are great!

I have to say that I’m so surprised but the food and drinks here everything was perfect and especially our a manager. I didn’t catch his name, but he’s just very kind Asian man who just give the best service. I will literally just come back for him.
Food was delicious and did not disappoint. Very attentive, and professional/friendly waitress. Best olive oil cake I have ever had. ✨💥💥

There are restaurants you go to eat.
And then there are restaurants you go to be seen without trying to be seen.

Cecconi’s NoMad belongs to the latter.

Polished wood. Low amber lighting.
The kind of room that flatters everyone and forgives nothing.
It doesn’t shout. It doesn’t perform.
It simply understands Manhattan.

The truffle pasta arrives understated — aromatic, restrained, confident.
A martini at the bar feels less like a drink and more like punctuation.
Dinner here isn’t rushed; it unfolds.

In a city obsessed with what’s next,
this is where you sit back — and let the night edit itself.

Had a great experience overall. 👌🏼
The food was delicious, the service was good, and the atmosphere was very enjoyable 🍝🍹
The staff was friendly and attentive. 😊
Definitely a place worth coming back to!

top_reviews.content: We loved our dinner at Vinegar Hill House. It might be the poster child for the “hidden gem“, tucked out of the way along the edge of Vinegar Hill. It’s a great restaurant, one of the best in Brooklyn. The atmosphere is, rustic chic? It’s casual and inviting and the service is warm and understated. All the dishes we tried were fantastic. However, I think they do vegetables best and we adored the snap peas and asparagus. The summer squash side is the best preparation of that vegetable I can recall ever having. The lamb rigatoni and the Arctic char were fantastic. And don’t skip dessert, the Guinness chocolate cake was super moist and decadent, a perfect way to end our meal. We can’t wait to go back, maybe for brunch next time as we hear it’s amazing.

If you’re looking for classic American brunch then this place is good for you; simple menu with all the classics. Personally I was not fan of the Apple sourdough pancake but others like it — so if that’s your thing then great. My only suggestion: offer freshly squeezed orange / grapefruit juice. Service was excellent: all the staff were the kindest. Atmosphere was cosy and welcoming; we were sat in the dining room area but they have also opened the backyard seating now which is great for warmer weather. Tables are quite small and seating is pretty tight but it’s okay I guess.

I cannot say enough great things about this place after my meal today! Had an absolutely scrumptious brunch after wanting to try this place for a while. The apple sourdough pancake was HEAVENLY. I think they actually did cook it up in heaven and bring it down to Brooklyn. The small size was the perfect size for 2 to split! And the omelette?? So simple, no frills tbh but so soft and creamy and delicious I honestly have no notes. I think this has to be one of my new favorite restaurants. The staff were so friendly as well and a lovely cozy atmosphere inside. What a perfect establishment!!!! 1000000% recommend coming for brunch.

An absolute hidden gem tucked quietly away in the back of Vinegar Hill. The restaurant is dripping with passion and character, and was the perfect romantic refuge during a warm spring downpour. Simple, tried & true dishes that use quality ingredient and thoughtful preparation to transcend simplicity and ascend to comfort food nirvana.

Phenomenal food, service, ambience, and more. The food didn’t try too hard. Seasonal ingredients with balanced flavors. Chicken liver mouse and beets were one of the best I’ve ever had. I LOVE that they didn’t hide any ingredients in drenched sauce but rather just showcased it with accompaniments. Besides the food, their wine list is actually one of the best in the region. No overpriced, overhyped names but rather unique smaller producers. Such a unique and eclectic mix of wine that again doesn’t try too hard to be complex. The server was so nice and welcomed my wife and I right away. I’m only upset this is the first time I’ve been here after living in Brooklyn for 4 years.

top_reviews.content:
Louie’s Pizzeria & Restaurant is a fantastic neighborhood pizza spot that absolutely lives up to its reputation. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, with a classic New York pizzeria feel and a clean, comfortable dining area.

The cheese slice was outstanding—thin, crispy crust with just the right amount of chew, flavorful tomato sauce, and perfectly melted cheese. Fresh, simple, and incredibly satisfying. The display of specialty pizzas looked amazing as well, with plenty of delicious options to choose from.

The staff were friendly, efficient, and kept orders moving quickly even during a busy time. You can tell they take pride in what they serve.

If you’re looking for authentic New York-style pizza with generous slices, fresh ingredients, and great service, Louie’s is definitely worth a visit. I’ll definitely be back to try more of their menu. Highly recommended!

Location across from Elmhurst hospital can be chaotic and parking is tight, but the pizza here is impossibly thin and crispy. Haven't had any pizza like this since Pizza Palace on Bayard Street by Columbus Park closed.
Easy to eat half a pie by oneself. Crispy, thin crust, perfect amount of sauce and oil (about 2 drips per plain slice, not drowning, but reminds you that this is true NYC pizza), lightly cheesed, but still has a good stringy mozzarella pull. For a similar, but slightly thicker (100% yum factor) NYC slice, it's Manos in Ridgewood. For, the thinnest and crispiest plain slice in NYC, Louie's is the standard bearer.
Parked in front, ordered a whole pie, ran inside, threw down some cash, waited outside for the fresh pie to bake. 10 minutes later the owner (possibly Louie hisself) delivers the fresh pie to my car outside and actually thanks me. True Twilight Zone stuff. I scarf a fresh, hot slice straight from the carton before stowing the balance back to Long Island for additional reheat confirmation.
With all the political nonsense ongoing, thank Goodness that a righteous, NYC plain slice is still alive, well and residing in un-hipster, un-gentrified, un-apologetically  friendly-neighborhood Spiderman Elmhurst.
"Best NYC style pizza" is a term that is minimized and bandied about every time some new $60, limited-run, kraft pizza from Japan is the current darling. We submit that this is not the case here. May Louie's be here after all the LES, deep dish, 3 Michelin star bakers and pizza itamae have exhausted their day in the limelight - and leases.
$20 all-in (until the hipster masses beat a path here to make Louie's their pizza crusade 😞)
Thank you Louie for giving us working class masses the best, true, unlimited, unpretentious, no-lines, no soup Nazi, no upsell, satisfyingly NYC pizza a $20 can still buy.
PS: please don't renovate or move as your pizzeria is a time-capsule whose prime ingredient is sincerity.

Was looking for excellent pizza within walking distance or a short train ride from Citi Field. Outstanding grandma slice. Salads are massive. Old school feel. Army vet who opened the restaurant 17 years ago. People come in with a smile on the face. Louie talks to everyone. A gem in Elmhurst. Legit ingredients- slices of mozzarella, basil, chunks of tomato. Delicious. Highly recommend.

First time having proper pizza after leaving NY 5 years ago. I’m glad I didn’t go anywhere else. The pizza is on point and hit the spot immediately. Had a great conversation with the owner too. I’ll definitely be back next time I’m in town.
Visited from AZ such friendly staff and delicious pizza. Veal parm hero did not disappoint. Sad i was not able to comeback one last rime!

A Must-Stop Slice in Elmhurst!

We love finding local spots when we travel, and of course when you come to NYC you have to get a slice. I’m so glad we chose Louie’s Pizza in Elmhurst! Louie himself was behind the counter, and he could not have been more friendly. He chatted with us in between taking orders, and his whole staff was just as welcoming. The restaurant is small, clean, and has that cozy neighborhood feel we love.

And the food… AMAZING! We tried pepperoni, margherita, the grandma slice, and buffalo, plus garlic knots and agnolotti. Every single thing was delicious!

If you’re anywhere near Elmhurst, you should run (not walk!) to Louie’s to get your pizza. And Louie, if you see this — thank you for a wonderful dinner and such warm, friendly service. You made our NYC trip even better! 🍕❤️

Louie! I hope you see this brother. My goodness I have been dreaming of that grandma slice. The best pizza I've ever had. Everything was great here. We showed up about 45 minutes before closing. We had a late flight, and Louie greeted us, took our order and made us feel welcome. This was a great introduction to NY pizza for me. Louie, you made us feel like we were at home at your shop. Thank you for your wonderful service and welcoming us to enjoy your food. I will be flying back to enjoy your pizza again. Unless your willing to mail me a whole pan of grandma slices ha ha. Thank you again.

- Your customers from Texas.

Louie’s Pizza is one of our family’s favorite places. The pizza is absolutely delicious, and the pasta dishes are excellent. The food is always fresh, flavorful, and consistently great. It’s also very family-friendly and perfect for kids. Our son loves coming here, and Louis and his father are always incredibly kind to him. They joke around with him, make him laugh, and always make him feel welcome. Their warmth and hospitality make every visit special. Great food, great people, and a wonderful atmosphere. Highly recommended!

top_reviews.content:
Got there 1.5h early on a Friday to get a walk-in and was the first person in line for the waitlist and first to get seated. Exact timing: arrived at 4pm, waitlist opened at 5pm, and got seated at 5:30pm. Managed to get an actual table for my walk-in instead of getting seated at the bar like I noticed other walk-ins after me were.

Came here as vegetarians and was a little unsure if we'd have enough food to eat as it's a rotating menu, and we were pleasantly surprised by the options. They kindly labeled which ones vegetarian for us and ordered all of them. About 5 dishes shared among 2 of us.

Every dish was excellent! So much flavor, perfectly balanced, filling by the end. They let you keep the menu at the end too, which is a nice keepsake.

This place has a Michelin star yet doesn't feel pretentious. Casual even. You can come dressed as you are. The music was great, and it's cool how it was started by LCD Soundsystem, a New York band we love!

This is my third visit to the four horseman and every single visit they never fail to deliver! I did not have reservation but I got there at 4.45pm and was second in line. Got seated about an hour later which I think isn’t too bad! Came for their early spring menu in April. I’ve always been a big fan of their risottos and this seafood risotto was absolute perfection. They also have a great selection on wines so don’t skip on that! Immaculate vibes, food and drinks. Definitely not an overhyped restaurant and worth the visit. I will be back!!

My husband and I came here on a Friday for brunch and we were served by Monet. It was our first time here and she guided us on the right amount of food to typically have to benefit our hunger. She did inform us that the plates had small portions so 4 different plates would be ideal. We got 5 since Monet saw that we were missing some veggies and I am very happy with the choices we made. Bluefin tuna + gnocco fritto, sea scallop + leek custard, winter chicories, soft-boiled egg + blue crab, ibérico pork collar, and a wonderful maple syrup sesame custard for dessert. The food was so fresh like eating from a garden or fresh farm. There was a lot of citruis flavors in the dishes and a lot of cheese or custard but it went very well. Though the plates were small we were both full and very much satisfied with almost every dish. I was not a big fan of the pork collar to fatty for my taste but my husband liked it. The dessert was so creamy and the combination of sesame and maple was absolutely amazing. We ended the day with dessert and tea and we were grateful for the experience. We would definitely love to come back hopefully to experience dinner.

Outstanding Michelin starred restaurant. Great service and even better food. Recommend getting there at 4:45 if you’re trying to make the waiting list for the bar. That should put you in the top five people if you are trying to get in at open. I went on a very nice day. 75° out and it’s like the first or second true spring day in Brooklyn. So maybe more people were trying to get out and we were willing to stay online. But that’s the time I would stay online for.

I had the fried spearing which was unique and great. I prefer to try things that I can’t make it home or I’ve never had. So that’s why I chose that.

I also had the ibérico pork collar with roasted cabbage, madeira. The pork was absolutely stellar.

They made us wait some time for our table but gave us each a complimentary glass of wine to makeup for it. I remember the food being alot better to be honest.. don’t get me wrong, it was good, but I wasn’t as impressed as I used to get with their dishes..

We got the bred and oeuf mayonnaise to start.. arguably the tastiest thing on the menu. Yellowfin tuna was simple but tasty. Chilled red shrimps were fresh but nothing special. Lamb shank was a special of the night and was good but wasn’t a fan of the style / accompaniment it came with. Seafood rice wasn’t a favorite for any of us.

For dessert, we got the sticky toffee cake (a must!) and the millefeuille (was okay but didn’t stand a chance next to the sticky toffee).

After spending a week in New York City with one goal in mind—to eat at the very best restaurants the city has to offer—we can confidently say that The Four Horsemen was the standout meal of our trip.

From the moment we walked through the door, everything felt intentional. The restaurant strikes that rare balance between refined and comfortable, creating an intimate setting that immediately makes you feel welcome. The space is beautifully designed, but it’s the attention to detail that truly sets it apart. Every element, from the pacing of the meal to the presentation of each dish, feels carefully considered.

The service was simply flawless. Professional without being pretentious, attentive without being intrusive, and genuinely warm throughout the evening. The staff demonstrated a deep knowledge of both the menu and wine program, making thoughtful recommendations and ensuring every aspect of our experience was perfect. It’s the kind of service that elevates an excellent meal into an unforgettable one.

The food was extraordinary. We shared the Bangs Island mussels, broiled razor clams, yuba pomodoro, yellowfin tuna, and the Berkshire pork chop. Each dish showcased remarkable creativity while remaining incredibly balanced and approachable. The mussels were beautifully prepared, the razor clams packed with flavor and nuance, and the yellowfin tuna was one of the most memorable dishes we had all week. The yuba pomodoro was a revelation, transforming familiar ingredients into something entirely unique. The Berkshire pork chop was cooked perfectly and tied together an incredible progression of flavors.

What impressed us most was how effortlessly the kitchen combined unexpected ingredients into dishes that felt harmonious, elegant, and deeply satisfying. Every plate delivered a new combination of flavors and textures that made us stop and appreciate what was happening.

New York is filled with great restaurants, but The Four Horsemen is something special. After a week of dining across the city, this was the meal we kept talking about. Exceptional food, impeccable service, an intimate atmosphere, and meticulous attention to detail make this a true five-star experience. We will absolutely plan future trips around returning here.

We had a reservation for 6 but showed up with 7. After speaking with the chef on a packed Friday, they were able to accommodate. I was thoroughly impressed with every aspect of this restaurant. The food, service, wine list, ambiance, and creativity is out of this world. Much like a small kitchen 2/3 star Michelin that pushes to innovate their dishes.

What amazed me the most out of the entire from the set course menu was that they were able to take something that I’ve never enjoyed (tofu) and turn it into the highlight of my night with the noodles shaped tofu skin dish. And the fresh bread with butter/creme fraische and caviar, was one of the best things to ever enter my mouth (see picture).

It is definitely worth to spend time exploring the wine list and speaking with the servers to see what is the best option that you will enjoy the most within your price range.

I would like to say this is my favorite restaurant in all of NYC and though it was a bit out out of my price range, it is worth the visit and to come back to try a new menu.

This spot delivers thoughtful cooking with moments of brilliance, even if consistency is not perfect. The bread is excellent, and the crudo was bright and well executed. The oeuf mayonnaise with squid ink and caviar felt disjointed rather than inventive.

The fennel salad refreshed the palate nicely. The little gem salad lacked creativity. The beet dish stood out, made richer and more layered by brown butter.

Meat courses were handled with care. The tartare had bold yet balanced flavor. The sirloin came perfectly cooked with a flavorful sauce, though the anchovy butter felt unnecessary.

Seafood ranged from forgettable to impressive. The halibut did not stand out, while the Boston mackerel was full of character with a great fry.

The uni risotto was the most refined dish of the night. The mushroom crostini had depth, although the bread was too firm. Desserts were excellent. Worth a visit, especially for those who like to explore a variety of plates.

top_reviews.content: High expectations were not met. Felt rushed, food wasn’t special and didn’t justify the cost. Many reviews commented on their Korean fried chicken, today they offered wings. They were flavorful but not what I was expecting. The pastry “room” wasn’t any better than what you find at an average airport lounge.

Unique and Delicious! The food is exquisite! The duck, the steak is heavenly, the fish ,the desserts, the people  amazing! The Clement is Way beyond my dreams! The people and the Service is beyond amazing, we loved their personal touch, fantastic!! we are happy  we chosen The Clement to celebrate our Christmas and Birthday!❤️❤️❤️

Located in the Peninsula Hotel upon entering you are greeted with absolutely beautiful floral arrangements.The restaurant is to the left of the entrance on the second floor. We were seated and immediately greeted by our server. There were multiple specials of the day since we were there for lunch we ordered lightly. Soup was very tasty! Nothing special about the chicken ceaser salad and avocado toast was good, my friends ordered salmon which I was told was good but not over the top. Elegant and pricey!

Absolutely phenomenal breakfast! The portions are huge so well worth the money and most i’d say can be shared between 2 people, visited during Christmas & from the decor to service everything was 11/10!! Amazing place as a first breakfast on our trip in NYC & cute  bday surprise as well!🎀🎉

4 stars because it is not going to change your life… But it is a great little bar with wonderful cocktails and fantastic service.  located just upstairs to the left as you enter the peninsula hotel - worth a stop if you need a break while enjoying fifth Avenue. (the free miniature desserts were a charming and delightful surprise)💕

An Unforgettable Brunch Experience at The Peninsula NYC

My experience at the Peninsula NYC was nothing short of extraordinary. Even a month after dining there, I find myself continuously reminiscing about the remarkable brunch I enjoyed. Allow me to share the highlights of this unparalleled culinary experience.

The Korean Fried Chicken was a delightful symphony of umami flavors, leaving a lasting impression on my palate. The Tuna Tataki was an exquisite dish—light, refreshing, and evocative of a perfect summer day.

However, the pièce de résistance was undoubtedly the pastry selection. The croissant transported me to Paris with its perfect execution. The exterior was wonderfully crunchy, each layer was impeccably flaky, and the interior was soft and warm. It was truly a masterpiece. Chef Richard's Mandarin Petits Fours were equally impressive. The dessert, crafted to resemble an orange on the outside with a delicate cake hidden inside, was a revelation. It masterfully balanced flavors of sweet, sour, bitter, and umami, showcasing the chef's artistry and precision.

Another highlight was the raspberry chocolate with pop rocks, which added an element of fun to the meal. The delightful flavor, combined with the nostalgic sensation of the pop rocks, brought back fond childhood memories.

The service at the Peninsula NYC was impeccable, further enhancing the dining experience. Every staff member demonstrated a high level of professionalism and attentiveness, making us feel truly valued.

In conclusion, our brunch at the Peninsula NYC was an extraordinary experience that I highly recommend. It is a must-visit destination in New York City. My heartfelt thanks to Chef Richard and his exceptional team for an unforgettable meal. We look forward to returning many times in the future.

Update 2024: the drinks and service are still good, prices are steep as expected. A good thing that there is always a place by some chance for an after work drink with a colleague. Three alcohol-free cocktails available.

2021:  I am a big fan of Peninsula hotel and I often come to their rooftop and to Clement for drinks. The service is ways top notch, the ambiance is understated and luxurious.  But $13 for a takeout coffee (Americano) - seriously?

Amazing service and breakfast but you (or a corporate card) pay for it. It's impeccable service and food. I wish I could've worked my way through the menu.  I chose the Avocado Toast with poached eggs. I wish ordered the cornflake-crusted brioche French toast but then I would've been napping under my desk all day. Their green juice was fresh and energizing. Our waiter was beyond professional and polite. Expertly attentive.

top_reviews.content: This has quickly become my favourite restaurant in NYC! They take such good care of their guests and the steak is always cooked to perfection. You really can’t go wrong with the menu or wine list. 10/10. Must go!!!

Took a flyer and picked this place because it had good reviews, served steak, and wasn't a fancy schmancy place; basically, all my criteria.

From the moment I walked in, I felt like family.
Seriously. Everyone had worked there for years and years, and I think at some point I met each and every one of them. The owner came by to check in, but it wasn't intrusive at all... more like your Pops swinging by your table to see if ya need anything.

I went solely for the beef, and got the grilled blood sausage and the 30oz. Bone-In Loin Strip. Dry aged. Cooked perfectly Medium Rare. That was a legendary piece of meat, and it'll be brought up in many conversations down the road.

This place is a gem. Support it. You'll have a great time, I promise.

​I visited last Friday for a company celebration lunch. We had the entire back room, which felt like a private oasis. The service was absolutely wonderful! The atmosphere was "victorious" (think Argentina)—you’ll understand exactly what I mean once you visit.

​Because we were a large group, the food took a bit longer than expected, and my steak had cooled down by the time it arrived. However, the Pollo Organico al Champignon was delicious; my coworkers saw it and immediately had "order envy." I suspect if you come in a smaller group of 2 or 4, the steak would be perfect.

Overall, a great experience. Go Messi!

We had an incredible time at Buenos Aires watching the Super Bowl with friends — everything was amazing from start to finish! The atmosphere was lively and perfect for the game, the food was packed with rich Argentine flavors, and the wine list complemented every dish beautifully. A huge shoutout to our waiter, Julio, whose friendly, attentive service made the night even more enjoyable. We’ll definitely be back soon — highly recommend this spot for great food, great drinks, and unforgettable service!

Truly the best most genuine Argentinian food you can possibly find in NYC. Coming from someone born and raised in Bs. As. ARG. THIS PLACE IS WHAT HOME TASTES LIKE!
From the corners of your hometown you grew up in, to the smell that drew you into this same place. A place to remember and make it your go to spot. It didn’t disappoint, and WE WILL BE BACK! ♥️

Si podes leer esto, la milanga Argentina está acá!!

I have had my fair share of steak houses and this is one of the best steak houses in New York. The steaks are always cooked perfectly, especially the skirt steak(Best in the city). The atmosphere is amazing, the signed football shirts and photos, game scarfs and flags. Highly recommend this place, it never disappoints.

We had such an amazing experience at Buenos Aires. It was like stepping into a real traditional Argentinian parrilla, and the meat was delicious and made exactly as we ordered it. Thank you to Mauro and all the wonderful staff who made our visit so special. For me, it was like being home. ❤️

The atmosphere alone is half the experience at this restaurant—but the food truly takes it over the top. The sausage is exquisite, and the skinny sausage is an absolute must.

You cannot leave without trying the crêpes dulce de leche—they’re unforgettable. My personal favorite is the ribeye, perfectly done every time.

The French fries with garlic and parsley are something to rave about, and the staff is incredible—warm, lively, and genuinely welcoming. It feels like home every time.

top_reviews.content: This place is on Flatbush Ave and I had no clue it was there. Hidden in plain site. Nice spot, the outdoor area in the back was cute and welcoming. friendly staff and the food was very good. Had brunch (Avocado Toast w/Egg):with a friend and we enjoyed the ambiance. Love the plants every where and I like that you could have drinks at the bar as well. Cool spot.

Risbo is such a gem, I feel lucky I can walk here whenever I want. Been multiple times, tried both the chicken and lamb and various sides. Everything is so perfectly cooked and seasoned, the flavors are bold and interesting - somewhere between French and Carribean.

Some of the best chicken I’ve had in NYC hands down. They also have this French cider here that is so funky and delicious, never seen it anywhere else and now crave it.

Absolutely beautiful backyard to boot, don’t sleep on this spot if you are coming from the park and looking for a casual-ish place. You will not be disappointed!

Food incredible. Sauce game 10/10. Loved the roasted duck and seasonal veggies. Great pickled cabbage that added a lot of brightness and tang to round out the richness of the roasted meat. Cobbler unremarkable. Very very long line moving at a glacial pace next to the kitchen’s heat lamps. Cocktails served without ice on a hot day. Sticky tables that you self-buss, but no one was wiping them down in between settings so my napkin/elbows adhered to the table in a really unsettling way.

I recently dined with members of my family at Risbo .The atmosphere was warm, inviting and laidback, with the most beautiful decor and lighting. The decor has a Paris - Brooklyn theme, but I loved that they were playing more reggae music that evening- gave it a Jamaica/Caribbean vibe. We chose different platters to share, so we could get a taste of their various dishes. The presentation of each platter was delightful, and every single bite was amazingly delicious - so flavorful. Discovered that they marinate their proteins for 2 days, no wonder!!The cocktails were off the charts - so good! I would recommend this restaurant 100%. Looking forward to returning with friends very soon.

Damn😭😭 that food was INCREDIBLE. I love when you leave a place with a smile and feeling like your money was well spent. Every employee is so lovely! That lamb hash??? The spicy cabbage… the chicken and waffles.Unlike any other! I was texting everyone I know as I ate. Will be back over and over!

I highly recommend the coconut Tres Leches. The watermelon salad was a large portion and a great starter!

Highly recommend for everyone to make this their local hot spot or a one time experience if you’re passing by!
A very lovely Latin restaurant. I had the shrimp mofongo; it was amazing. Cozy atmosphere with outdoor patio seating. Staff was very friendly and attentive.

Not what I expected but definitely exceeded expectations is the best way to describe Pablo Santo. Everything felt right. A must try and bring good company it’s all worth it ! MUST TRY
- Heart of Palm Salad

The food was great! We got the skirt steak, the Brussels sprouts salad and the tortillas.
The steak comes with great sides, chimichurri sauce is fresh. The steak was a bit overcooked for medium rare. Service was great though they took time to take our orders.

Really nice vibe and cute outdoor sitting. Great for a date 😉

I went to Palo Santo for a friend’s birthday brunch, and wow—I was seriously blown away by how delicious the food was! They offer a bottomless brunch, and we went with the sangria, which was super flavorful and refreshing. Definitely appreciated that it wasn’t watered down like some other places.

The space itself is cozy and intimate—yes, it’s a little tight, but it adds to the charm. What really stood out to me was the service. The staff was incredibly attentive and kind, making sure we were taken care of throughout the entire meal.

Now, let’s talk about the food—absolutely incredible. My entrée was bursting with flavor, seasoned to perfection, and cooked just right. I couldn't stop raving about it. Of course, I had to sneak a few bites of my friends’ plates, and everything I tried was just as good. You can tell the kitchen puts a lot of love and thought into each dish.

This spot is definitely a hidden gem in Brooklyn. I’m already looking forward to going back and trying more of the menu. If you're looking for a flavorful brunch with great vibes and service, Palo Santo is a must. Thank you for such a wonderful experience!

name: Haenyeo
address: 239 5th Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11215, United States
description: Playful takes on Korean classics & seafood in cozy, white-walled space.

top_reviews.content:
Service was quick, everything came out at a good pace. The only thing I would say is that it’s a bit chilly so it would be good to bring a thin sweater.

I went with a group of 6 people, and we got a lot of dishes to try and share. My favorite were the fluke crudo, crispy wings, Hwe dup bop, and bulgogi, in that order.

I would also recommend to try the spicy dishes last, since it was pretty spicy and overpowers some flavors.

Creative Korean inspired new American restaurant whose drink menu is much longer than its dinner menu.

The tuna seafood pancake was delicious and creative; Galbi jjim priced at $55 for 3 pieces was not worth it. You can get the same if not better ones in other Korean restaurants for way cheaper. The pork bulgogi was good but again you can get same ones in other restaurants for way cheaper. The Squid and Whale cocktail ($22) I got was a little underwhelming. The flour less chocolate lava cake was excellent. And yes. Their free side kimchi was outstanding. Overall to me the restaurant is a little overpriced for what it is offering. If it could reduce its price a little, it could be a 5 stars for me.

The service was phenomenal! Such a friendly and lovely greeting upon entering! I loved the greeting. It sets the tone. The service was great and everyone was very attentive not just my main waiter. The server made great suggestions and the cocktails were also very nice! I was solo and truly enjoyed my meal.

What a fantastic experience!! We entered with high expectations and enjoyed a meal that exceeded them. The food and service were impeccable.

Starters we sampled included the expertly composed Fluke Crudo (which was refreshing and delicious), Gamja Buchim (tuna sashimi on a potato pancake with wasabi-infused sour cream!), Dukboki Fundido (an incredible internationally-influenced dish incorporating Oaxacan cheese and Mexican chorizo alongside thick Asian noodles) and Grilled Oysters (savory and delicious with butter and herbs). All were exceptional.

For entrees, we greatly enjoyed Maine Uni Bibimbap (possibly our favorite dish of the night, absolutely delicious!) and the Bulgogi (some of the best I’ve had anywhere).

Throughout the evening, we tried 3 cocktails: The Squid & The Whale was my first drink of the night, and the sesame oil and egg whites were a fantastic treat for my palate. Drink 2 was Seoul Train, similar to a Manhattan with a clever addition of plum wine. My final drink of the night was the NY Sleepover, a delightful sour topped with a Chianti float.

The desserts are impressive as well — the Beignets were soft, fluffy, fresh, and impossible to deny even with a full stomach. The crème brûlée was a sweet and elegant finish to a perfect meal.

Thanks to the kind and attentive staff, the talented chefs, and everyone who made our meal and evening unforgettable. Park Slope is blessed to have Haenyeo, but diners from all over should make an effort to visit this exceptional restaurant.
Had an early dinner here with a close friend. My first time having Korean food!! We had the scallion pancakes to start. Light, crispy and fresh.

Excellent takes on Korean food, and you will leave happy and full. The dukboki with oxaca cheese is incredibly balanced, tasty, and perfectly sized. The vegetable pancake is full of yummy veggies and nicely fried. Our waiter suggested using it to mop up the sauce from the dukboki. Great idea! The deji bulgogi is some of the most succulent pork Ive had, and all of the accouterments make for many tasty varied and tasty bites. Finally, the beignets are light, fluffy dough pillows with the ever slight crunch and chew. A great ending to a meal especially if your feeling stuffed. Absolutely incredible.

This is definitely not average Korean restaurant, it is so contemporary that you get hint of it's Korean heritage only by reading menu (for better or worse). The place, if I am not mistaken it is mentioned in Michelin Guide, but in my opinion worth a star. The food was delicious and although by the end I was so full I couldn't stop eating until the plate was clean. Kalbi jjim which is short ribs and Bulgogi were out of this world! Again I have failed to try their dessert,  but definitely will make another trip to this place, hopefully getting chance to try them. The place is very popular so reservation is recommend.

I wish I came to Haenyeo earlier on because I’d hands down say this is the best restaurant in Park Slope. The vibe inside, the staff, and the food are up to standard with some of the best restaurants in the city. Some standouts are their kimchi and bulgogi but I really didn’t have anything that was below average. I 100% will be back soon, hopefully when people are in town so we can show them some delicious food. Would highly recommend if you’re in the area (or even outside the area and are reading this).

name: Grimaldi's Pizzeria
address: 1 Front St, Brooklyn, NY 11201, United States
description: Casual, Brooklyn-based pizzeria chain serving brick-oven pies & calzones, plus wine & beer.

business_details.details: 1 Front St, Brooklyn, NY 11201, United States
Closed · Opens 11 AM · See more hours

top_reviews.content:
Grimaldi's sits right under the Brooklyn Bridge in DUMBO, which already puts it in one of the better spots in New York before you even talk about the food. The red-and-white gingham tablecloths, wine bottle chandeliers, black-and-white photographs on the walls, jukebox in the corner, it all feels like it has been exactly this way for a long time, because it more or less has. The coal-fired brick oven is visible from the dining room and the pies come out with a char on the underside that gas ovens simply cannot replicate.
The plain Margherita is the place to start and also where the kitchen has the least to hide behind. Fresh handmade mozzarella, house sauce made from a recipe passed down through generations, and dough prepared fresh daily. The crust has a slight chew toward the center and a proper crunch at the edge, with char marks from the coal fire that add a subtle smokiness to the whole thing. We also did a pepperoni pie and a white pizza with garlic, pesto, mushrooms, and white onion, which was the table's favorite. The cannoli showed up for dessert, fried pastry shell, sweet ricotta filling, chocolate chips, and that's about all it needed to be. They don't serve slices here, only whole pies, so come with people or come hungry.
Walk across the Brooklyn Bridge from Manhattan and have lunch here. That is a day that works.

We ordered a Margherita pizza and a mixed pizza, and both were delicious. The food was excellent, and the restaurant itself had a nice atmosphere. The only reason I’m giving it four stars is that our order took a long time to arrive. However, the waitress apologized several times for the delay, which we appreciated. Overall, it was a great experience. I really enjoyed the pizza and would definitely recommend this place.

I love the food at Grimaldis. I visit NYC twice a year, and Grimaldi's is on the top of the list of places to go eat. I took some friends over and the loved the food. The pizza is loaded with toppings and so cheesy, their Greek salad with feta is a great starter salad. Their Calzone is huge, enough for like 3 - 4 persons, and their cheesecake desserts (they have seasonal flavors) are for me - the best cheesecake I have tried. The servers are knowledgeable of their food items and always offer a very warm service. I wanted to bring a Calzone back home (West Coast) and the girl went out of her way to cut it and wrap it up nice and tight so that It would survive the trip. You gotta try this place....especially in the winter season where the building feels cozy and warm. See ya January 2027 Grimaldis 👏😉

We went on a Tuesday evening and got in about 5:15p with no wait on the third floor. Great vibe up there. We started with the bruschetta trio and it was pretty good. Definitely not the best bruschetta I’ve ever had but still pretty solid. We then had the margherita pizza and it was really good. Nice coal-fired taste. Definitely a 5⭐️ overall experience due to the historic vibes and the good food. Service was solid too and pretty fast.

Great service and wonderful atmosphere from n the building.

Love the taste of the coal fired thin crust pizza. Crust could’ve been a tad more crunchy.

Overall I would recommend stopping in and grabbing a pizza for lunch or dinner.

top_reviews.content: Such a great experience.  We went for our anniversary and we were so happy that we spent it at shota omakase. An amazing omakase dining experience at Shota. Premium ingredients and amazing taste. Each and every course was finely prepared and beautifully presented. Service was top notch throughout. Sake list was also impressive with massive selections of both common and rare sakes. Some rare ones were priced pretty steep.
This restaurant is a treasure on South Street in Brooklyn. Definitely recommended!

Dining at Shota was nothing short of phenomenal. From the moment we sat down, the chef created an experience that felt both personal and educational. He was incredibly warm and delightful, taking the time to explain the proper etiquette of fine Japanese dining and the philosophy behind each course. It felt less like a meal and more like being guided through a masterclass in traditional omakase.

The most memorable moment for me was trying uni. I’ve never been a fan before, but the chef encouraged me to give it another chance—and I’m so glad I did. It was, without question, the best tasting uni I have ever had: incredibly fresh, delicate, and perfectly prepared. It completely changed my perspective.

Shota isn’t just dinner—it’s an experience that deepens your appreciation for Japanese culinary tradition. A truly exceptional omakase that I would highly recommend to anyone who wants to understand sushi at its highest level.
Great food, great service and great value. The quality of the fish is top notch. I got the premium omakase counter with Chef Tanaphan. His skills with the sushi were that of a true shokunin

top_reviews.content:
We have long considered the service here to be a masterfully conducted symphony, with every detail attended to with a precision that borders on art, all paired with cuisine that consistently sets the standard for fine dining in the city.

Yet, during yesterday's visit, we noticed a distinct, beautiful shift in the room. The impeccable, world-class standard we always crave remained entirely intact, but the staff carried a different aura—one filled with renewed warmth and an effortless, vibrant energy.

We quickly realized the catalyst for this wonderful evolution is the new manager, Carlos. He was an absolute delight, taking the time to chat with each table in a way that felt genuinely welcoming. It was equally wonderful to witness his interaction with his crew; his leadership radiates a positive, uplifting energy that clearly inspires the entire team. Kudos to the whole team at Gabriel Kreuther—that third star is surely on the horizon, and we remain as loyal as ever.

This is one of those restaurants I would have only dreamed of being able to go to not too long ago.

Always thought with its location and Michelin stars it was too fancy for me, but decided to give it a try before hitting a Broadway show at the Hudson Theater.

While we didn’t have enough time to do one of the tasting menus for the full experience, we were able to nibble on a few amazing bites and grab drinks. Service and ambiance at the bar/lounge area were impeccable. Will definitely have to come back for the full experience!

One of our favorite places to dine in NYC. The ambience is warm and inviting and sets the perfect tone from the moment you walk in. The staff is incredible—attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely welcoming. Every dish feels is offers bold new flavors. From the exceptional food to the outstanding service, this is a place we find ourselves returning to again and again. Highly recommended.

Outstanding evening at Gabriel Kreuther.
Last night, my wife and I dined at Gabriel Kreuther, and it’s one of those rare restaurants where—while you’re still seated, mid-course—you find yourself planning your return. (We actually said, “We have to bring the kids here.”)
We chose the tasting menu, and from the very first course, it was clear how much thought and intention went into each dish. Every plate was a success—beautifully composed, flavorful, and creative. Each course flowed naturally into the next, making the tasting feel cohesive rather than just a collection of highlights.
The beverage pairings were equally well executed. Each drink was thoughtfully selected to elevate the dish it accompanied, adding nuance and balance without stealing the spotlight. Together, the food and pairings felt precise, measured, and complete.
Service is where the evening truly stood out. At this level, hospitality must be a seamless team effort, guided by calm leadership and real awareness of the room. Angie, our captain for the evening, embodied that role perfectly—warm, attentive, and always a step ahead. Zanetta, one of the managers, worked tirelessly throughout the night to ensure every detail was handled with care. Mission accomplished.
The dining room itself deserves praise. The interior design, lighting, and seating are all beautifully considered, and the view into the open kitchen adds an extra layer of energy to the experience. The large, inviting bar is a destination on its own—we arrived early and enjoyed a drink there before being seated, and it set the tone for the evening perfectly.
An exceptional dining experience from start to finish. Highly recommended.

I tremendously enjoyed the 4-course menu at Gabriel Kreuther, and couldn’t recommend it more for anyone looking to celebrate a special occasion. Other than the sheer excellence of the food - the team went above and beyond to make this a special night for us. I would go as far as saying this was the best meal I’ve had in the city.

I’ve been to a quantity of Michelin star restaurants across the world, and I can say this truly earned its stars. I’m a tough critic and I can’t say the same for a lot of the other NYC Michelin restaurants - which have generally been a disappointment in comparison to those in Europe.

top_reviews.content: This was truly a hidden gem that we found after endless scrolling on Google Maps. They have an excellent menu with a great variety of dishes, and the portions are more generous and better value than those at many other restaurants in the neighborhood. The staff was very friendly, made us feel welcome, and created a warm, homely atmosphere. The food was excellent. I highly recommend this place if you're looking for great food and drinks.

We had a fantastic experience at Cozy Royale! Our server Rachel was attentive and so helpful! She gave great recommendations for the cold brew martini and the beertini! She also had some great recommendations for the food especially the New England style steak tips as a starter! The perogis are also a much get! The Rigatoni alla vodka that I ordered for my main was absolutely delicious as well!
One of the best burgers I’ve had in a while. Got the happy hour special smash burger and fries and sticky toffee pudding for dessert - both phenomenal. Cute little spot!

Walked into Cozy Royale on a Sunday around 5:30 with no wait and grabbed seats at the bar. Water came out right away and service was quick throughout. The kind of place that gets the basics right before you even look at the menu.

We came specifically for the dry-aged smashburger. On Sundays they serve it all day, which is worth knowing — weekdays it’s limited to 10 per day. It’s a 30-day dry-aged patty on a potato bun with a solid sauce and good pickles. The burger itself was an 8 out of 10. Well-executed, classic smash with good flavor. My only note is that a few more toppings would have pushed it further. But honestly, the fries were the real standout — crispy, well-salted, and better than the burger.

We also got the sticky toffee pudding. It was good, but very sweet. The Maldon sea salt on top helped cut through it, and the cream cheese icing added a nice tartness as a contrast. What it’s missing is a scoop of ice cream. A warm, dense toffee pudding paired with something cold would completely elevate the dish — even a cream cheese ice cream as an add-on would do it. They should consider it.

One heads up: the online menu doesn’t fully reflect what they’re actually serving or the current prices. Worth knowing before you go.

The drinks looked great from what we saw around us. Someone next to us ordered an espresso martini, another had a beer-tini. We didn’t drink, but the bar program looks solid.

Reverse happy hour is a nice touch and a reason to come back later in the evening.
Still need to try the steak frites and the chicken. This is the kind of neighborhood spot you keep coming back to, and the vibe earns that.

4 out of 5 stars.
We took the happy hour smash burger & fries and dirty martini special and both were fantastic. Food was delicious, space was good, and service was good too. Very pleasant experience.

Came here for brunch on a Sunday, it was everything we wanted and more. the ambiance and vibe is cozy and elevated. the staff was very welcoming and warm. we got a cold brew that was perfectly done and the portion served was appropriate 🤌 I had the steak tartare, which was amazing, served with sourdough. My husband and I were blown away by this place! We dined here last Friday and got there early so we could lock in one of the special burgers and the happy hour deals. Also $10 martinis for happy hour!!!!

top_reviews.content:
We were looking forward to trying Cafe Kestrel, and while it was a good experience overall, it didn’t fully meet our expectations. The service was refined and thoughtful, though our server did not seem to have the strongest grasp of the wine list, and the recommendation we received didn’t quite align with their description.

Our primary disappointment was the food. It had the potential to be excellent, but the aggressive use of finishing salt overshadowed the dishes. Both the burger and the steak felt like a bit of a gamble where each bite could either be perfectly balanced or leave us with an overwhelming mouthful of salt. The halloumi and bread starters were lovely, and the apple sundae was delightful, but the heirloom tomatoes lacked the fresh, vibrant flavor we were hoping for from a summer dish.

Overall, Cafe Kestrel was neither a hit nor a miss. There were thoughtful touches and some genuinely enjoyable dishes, but given the experience, we probably won’t be rushing back anytime soon.

Sam, the general manager, made this an unforgettable night for my mom and me. We agreed it was one of the best meals we’ve ever had.

The bread and the halibut were delicious beyond words. The tuna with greens was surprisingly delightful (more my mom’s taste than mine, but I’m glad I tried). We could have done without the chilled shrimp crudo, missed the mark for us.

The drink list was incredible, and our bottle (the Patapon white) was perfection. Well worth the trek to Red Hook! Thanks to Helen Rosner for the rec and lovely write-up!

Food is delicious. Price is steep. A bit of sticker shock at first as the portions aren’t very big and the prices are on the higher side. But we left really pleased with our experience! The food is incredible. By far the best burger I had in a long time! Worth a visit. Excellent service

I celebrated my birthday dinner at this spot my wife stumbled upon on Resy, and it was such a hit!! Super friendly, and attentive service punctuated by Sam the GM. We had a variety of small plates and shared an entree, and each dish was just as good if not better than the last. The apricot cake with butterscotch sauce was the most decadent end to a great celebratory meal! We will be back!

Overall fairly disappointed.

We spent $20 on a salad for two leaves of radicchio, a quartered beet, two small corners of a block of cheddar cheese and sprinkled ?gorgonzola. I’ve never seen such a skimpy salad in my life and I’ve lived in NYC for years and my partner grew up here. 1.5/5

The zucchini with lamb and tomato sauce — fine. But the lamb wasn’t seasoned, zucchini overcooked, and tomato sauce was actually decent.  2.5/5

Here’s the most aggravating part. Spent $55 for duck confit with only tomatoes. The skin of the duck was the best part! Taste was mediocre, only had a handful of small tomatoes as the side. 2/5

We spent $140 and both left hungry and disappointed. Nothing tasted bad, but easily could’ve been better. Inflation sucks but I can spend less and get such better tasting food in the local area and in many other parts of the city.

Wait staff was really nice and helpful, the place was cute and a great date spot but be prepared to be underwhelmed.

I’m not coming back
