top_reviews.content:
Aged Steakhouse in Forest Hills was a really nice experience overall. The ambiance is upscale but still relaxed perfect for a date night or a nice dinner out.

We started with the crab cake and calamari & both were so good. The crab cake was crispy on the outside soft and flavorful inside & the calamari was fresh, light, and not greasy at all.

The porterhouse steak was definitely the highlight perfectly cooked juicy & packed with flavor. You can tell they really know what they’re doing when it comes to steak.

We also had a side of veggies (forgot to take a pic lol) but they were fresh and a nice balance to everything else. The truffle mac & cheese was creamy & good but honestly tasted more like a regular mac & cheese we were expecting a stronger truffle flavor so that was a little disappointing.

Service was attentive drinks were great & everything came out at a nice pace.

Overall still a great spot in Queens for a quality steakhouse experience just a small miss on the truffle mac.

We came here on a Saturday afternoon for lunch. Wasn’t packed and was seated right away. The server was helpful and attentive. The food was good but I felt like their portions were a little small. The steak and eggs were delicious. Steak was cooked to my order but also very small portion. The restaurant nicely decorated. The drinks were also delicious. Overall a little pricey for the food portion you get but very good food.

Recently stopped by for brunch on a hot spring day in NYC. The AC was not on, so it was quite warm in the restaurant unfortunately. Thankfully their iced cappuccino cooled me down. I ordered their steak and eggs, requesting for rare since restaurants seem to mess up my doneness preferences often. Lo and behold, it came medium rare and was so nicely charred and marinated, I ate the entire plate ... including the eggs and salad that accompanied the meal. I also chugged my cappuccino before I left!

Ended up going just to try it out cause I've been craving steak.
They have a lunch special which can range from $20-$30 which is not bad at all considering there's an appetizer and a main plus $10 on select cocktails.

The place itself has a nice vibe, great to bring a date or small group of friends with.

I have no issues with the service or the food but whatever tequila they used for the margarita had a soapy smell and taste that it threw me off. Other than that, would come back again.

Came in with high expectations for a steakhouse, but the food was honestly just okay. Nothing really stood out or felt worth the price. The ambiance is nice and the service was great attentive and welcoming but unfortunately, the food didn’t match the overall vibe

Had such a great time!
(I asked for a pasta that wasn’t exactly on the menu-I’m THAT annoying customer-and they made it happen with zero hesitation. They even adjusted the sauce so it still tasted amazing!)
Their espresso martini is lit perfect and pls also do yourself a favor and try the Salmon !
(It is not the cheaper restaurant in the area, but it definitely worth the prices…)
Definitely coming back !

I have passed this place a few times and actually planned for this visit with a group from work for lunch. The waiter was excellent. He was patient when taking orders for a table of 7 with three checks. We ordered from the $20 lunch menu which was a pretty good value with a starter and meal. Portion was good for lunch. I actually had enough to take for later. The only thing none of us liked was the steak on the menu was an additional $10 which we felt shouldn't be an option if not in the $20 price point for the options. I had the chicken pasta with pesto sauce which was tasty. We sat outside and the water assisted us with the table placement so we could all sit together. The chairs weren't all that comfortable but it was nice being outside. I would return if in the area again.

The service was really good and atmosphere is great. Place is beautiful and plenty of space. We had the tuna tartar and calamari. Both were great especially the calamari with the spicy kick. For dinner my wife had the half chicken that she says was really good. I had the ribeye, I did not like the steak. Meats was meh and char wasn't good. More medium than medium rare and extra fatty.

top_reviews.content: Mom and I went here twice in a week. We’ve been coming for a while. Never disappoints! Sitting down outside was pleasant. Fish and grits are my fave.

We were looking for a brunch spot while we were in New York for a little overnight trip. Shane's came up. Wait was 15 mins. I noticed while going to the bathroom that they also have downstairs seating. Place was packed. Food was excellent. They fried that fish to perfection, mac n cheese 💯💯mixed vegetables also (not pictured)..Service was also on point. I'm the only one who didn't have anything to take home. Lol🤷🏾‍♀️🤷🏾‍♀️🤷🏾‍♀️..We all agreed that we would most definitely come back when in the area. Prices were not bad either. Great soul food spot!! Better get you some..💃🏽💃🏽💯💯

I attended brunch at Shane’s yesterday, and overall I’d give my experience a 7.5/10.
The ambiance and overall look of the restaurant were pretty standard. I do think the venue could use an upgrade, especially the basement seating area it gave me more of a backyard BBQ feel than a brunch atmosphere.
That being said, the staff was very polite and accommodating. The Thai wings were delicious and definitely one of the highlights. For my main entrée, I originally ordered the catfish with cheese grits. The catfish was a little too over-fried for my liking and was cut almost like a pork chop, which I didn’t really enjoy. However, the manager handled it perfectly and changed it out with no problem. I went with the grilled shrimp instead, and paired with the cheese grits, it was really good.
My friend ordered the steak, which I also tried, and that was delicious.
While I think the atmosphere could use some improvement and my original entrée missed the mark, the good food, polite staff, and the way the manager handled my concern made a difference. I would definitely return and try some other items on the menu.

Food here is fantastic!! Really great comfort food. Came during off-hours and service was a bit slow, but still pretty good.

Highly recommend the caramel brûlée latte!

Such a warm and charming atmosphere. Lovely restaurant!
Good service and great food:) would 10/10 recommend!

I’ve been here a number of times and overall I’ve had a good experience. One thing I appreciate is that I never have a hard time finding parking, which is a huge plus in Brooklyn.

The food is consistently good. My go to order is the whiting with the red velvet waffles..they’re definitely worth trying. The prices are pretty standard for what you’d expect.

My biggest complaints are the hours and the ordering process. They close pretty early, which can be frustrating, and I wish they accepted phone orders. Having to place every order in person or third party isn’t the most convenient.

Overall, the quality of the food keeps me coming back, but extending the hours and allowing phone orders would make the experience even better.

Overall the place wasn’t bad, I came for girls brunch and the food was edible. The flavors are there for sure, but my food was overcooked. The chicken was very dry but the cinnamon waffle was delicious enough to get over the dryness. Loved my waiter, he was a joy. My friend very much enjoyed her grits.
I tried to be generous with the atmosphere but the downstairs had no service, hated that.

Beautiful neighborhood spot. They need to turn down the heat some onnthe eggs. Omelet was dry but the salmon and scallions was good. Service? I got passed off to two different people. Never got an offer of a coffee refill and had to run them down foe the bill.

top_reviews.content:
If you’re looking for one of the best brunch spots in North Hollywood, Hungry Fox Diner is a must-visit. This classic diner blends that nostalgic, cozy vibe with a menu full of comforting, flavorful dishes that truly hit.

We started with the drinks, and honestly… they set the tone. The café de olla had that rich, spiced sweetness that feels like a warm hug, while the Thai iced coffee was bold, creamy, and perfectly balanced. The Thai jasmine green tea was refreshing and light, and the Thai iced tea had that signature smooth sweetness so good and definitely a must-order if you love unique drinks.

For food, everything was just as impressive. The chicken and waffles were perfectly crispy on the outside, juicy inside, and paired with fluffy waffles that had just the right sweetness. The skirt steak chilaquiles were packed with flavor tender steak, rich sauce, and that perfect brunch comfort vibe. And of course, you can’t skip the pancakes… soft, fluffy, and classic in the best way.

The atmosphere is super welcoming, giving you that old-school diner feel in North Hollywood with friendly service that makes you want to stay longer. Whether you’re coming for a casual breakfast, brunch with friends, or just craving something comforting, this spot delivers.

If you’re searching for “best diner in North Hollywood,” “brunch in NoHo,” or “chilaquiles near me,” Hungry Fox definitely deserves a spot on your list. Highly recommend this is one of those places you’ll keep coming back to.

I go here a lot with my Hubby. We love this place. We drive far for the delicious fluffy pancakes and the chicken and waffles are amazing! Love the coffee too! The service is the best. Love the energy and food here. 🥰

This place was Amazing for breakfast and lunch. My Husband and I tried it for the fist time and we Loved the size portion of the food was perfect and the Quality was so perfectly cooked . Thank you to the cook for making our food delicious and to Eddie who was so friendly and so Welcoming. Our Experience was perfect. The food taste so fresh and the coffee de Olla so bomb. The place was clean and Eddie was so nice and helped us decide on what to order. Great job.
Wow. Great food, lots of choices. Packed with good reason and the staff were very friendly and accommodating. Would definitely eat here again.

Great food, service, and atmosphere. Wanted a simple waffle combo and it came out really fast. The diner is really peaceful and not chaotic so it was a good experience. Very crispy bacon and waffles, didn’t feel heavy at all. Overall, great breakfast spot.

The Hungry Fox in North Hollywood is that old school diner that surprises you with some seriously standout plates. Their chicken & waffles are the star crispy, juicy, and paired with waffles that hit that perfect soft buttery sweet spot. The marinated steak is another sleeper hit, tender and full of flavor, and the chilaquiles come out bold, saucy, and comforting the way they should be.

And if you’ve got a sweet tooth, the Biscoff Bomb pancakes are exactly what they sound like over the top fluffy, and absolutely worth the indulgence. Friendly service, big portions, and a menu that goes way harder than you’d expect from a neighborhood diner. A NoHo classic for a reason.
Really great local place with a wonderful variety of food options. The fried chicken and waffles are what they are famous for but their breakfast in general is excellent.

Awesome place to come to if you're feeling hungry and ready to eat a filling meal. The pancakes had to be the best ive ever had no exaggeration needed. Mind you I got the classic one no topping and they were so fluffy and buttery. Couldn't finish so im definitely taking them to go to enjoy them again a bit later lol. And when I come back I will indulge in the many options of toppings they have.

top_reviews.content:
TL;DR: Grab a table outside, enjoy a glass of wine with a plate of pasta, and do some people-watching. This is an amazing spot to wind down the evening!

Food:
I have had the orecchiette (brunch) and the lasagne (dinner). I have also tried the chicken milanese panini. The food really is quite spectacular here: I love that you can really taste how high quality and textured the pasta is. For seemingly simple dishes, they do an amazing job at the flavor. They have good wine selection as well with some affordable options. There is also a happy hour as well to look out for!

Service:
The waiters here are quite friendly and very attentive. They regularly ask if you need anything, and they’ll come do water refills as needed. No complaints at all.

Ambiance:
Located on a street with a good amount of foot traffic but is not that loud. It’s very comfortable outside, and they have seating indoors as well (although I exclusively choose to sit outdoors here). There is a clean restroom downstairs as well.

Tried a Delivery tonight but despite being relatively close to my house (only a few blocks away) and having ordered the meat cooked  “Rare” and an appetizer of 3 cold cuts (that’s why I know the order didn’t take long in the making) the food arrived at my house after almost 1 hour! So I don’t recommend delivery. I’ve had a steak that wasn’t bad but definitely not  “rare”  and lacking salt and it came with a side of what I first believed was arugula but it was something green right out of the bag and inedible because it only tasted like plastic! Now for the 3 cold cuts, I’ve had the sopressata (which I remember being spicy and this was not, so to me it was salami), Prosciutto Di Parma (which arrived sweating, like partially cooked because it was put above the fries container) that didn’t taste like how I remembered, good, but not Parma in my opinion (and I am Italian, born and raised) and the Speck was just as good but not the high quality I’m used to (like Senfter Süd Tirol). Overall the food is pretty good and the quality is similar to Italian excellence, but not quite like it. Oh, the rider also gave me a pizza with mushrooms and pancetta that wasn’t mine but when I called him back he didn’t pick up the phone! One free pizza you’d say, too bad I don’t eat mushrooms! I’m sure this restaurant is not bad at all but with NYC competition every detail counts!

Even though I know the neighborhood, I was delighted to recently discover Osteria Cotta when I was on an extended trip to NY.  It was one of the highlights of my trip! It is the quintessential UWS neighborhood Italian restaurant. The menu has a very appealing menu, with options from “Small Bites” to full entrees. The woodburning oven is great feature, not only in terms of cooking but in terms of ambience.
The bar is very welcoming and offers the optionality of dining there as well as at rustic tables.

Amazing dining experience! The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. We tried a few dishes from the menu, and everything tasted authentic with generous portions. The ambiance is cozy, and the staff was friendly and attentive throughout our visit. Definitely a place worth visiting if you're looking for quality Italian food. Highly recommended!

I have been to Cotta a few times before and had very good experiences. So when my friends were coming to celebrate my birthday i thought this would be a great safe choice. I was extremely disappointed. We ordered a steak and asked for it to be cooked Medium, and the middle was completely raw as you can see below. When we told the waitress she said she would tell the kitchen but then all she offered was a free dessert and still charged us for the steak. i was appreciative of the free dessert, but when celebrating a birthday, getting a raw steak is extremely disappointing. I do not think we will be returning for a while.

Solid neighborhood spot. The downstairs is more of a bar (but still serving real food), while upstairs is sit-down and family friendly. The orecchiette was tasty, and the pesto had a nice fresh flavor. The sopressetta and hot honey pizza was a great balance of flavors and a touch of heat. For dessert, we had the banana bread pudding, which was cinnamon-y and cozy.

Met my brother here while visiting the city last weekend. When he told me they had the best wings in the city I was skeptical. Boy was he right!!! Perfectly cooked, with a nice crisp. The show stopper...the flavor! Rosemary Wings! We're originally from Central NY where buffalo wings are king. Im am now torn. We also had a nice pizza with basil, a pasta dish and some drinks. Throughout the few hours we were there the servers didn't let our glasses empty once, whether it was water or adult style! Will be a must stop anytime we visit!

Great Italian spot on the Upper West Side.
Warm, intimate atmosphere.
Pizza with real flavor and character.
Simple, well executed, and worth coming back.

top_reviews.content: My friends and I wanted to try Venezuelan food and decided to dine at Casa Ora. Walking in, the ambience and decor of the restaurant is nice. The staff is friendly and attentive. We had several appetizers. The yucca fries, ceviche and empanadas were good. The arepitas were a bit hard. For entrees, we also ordered the Asado Negro (short ribs). Priced at $109, it was definitely NOT worth it for the price!!!. It was extremely, clawingly sweet. It was covered with so much micro greens you didn't know what the dish was. The brisket and spaghetti dishes were good though. I wanted to try the Patacon, but was told it was only for grubhub & door dash delivery, which was disappointing. Overall, the food was tasty. I would go back to Casa Ora and give them another try.

Had a nice time at Casa Ora! The service was a bit shaky at first upon entry. After seating we received our drinks (decent!) and started well with street food/appetizers. The ceviche was a hit and beautifully plated, not appearing like regular chopped ceviche. The arepitas were yummyyyy inside but the tortilla was a bit dry :( but the plantain chips and guac were amazing as expected!!

The menu changes occasionally I believe? For entrees, the Pabellón a Caballo brisket was an overall very good and filling plate. Nooo complaints! The salmon entree (forgot the name on menu) was a hit as expected also! One more entree we ordered, a shrimp fried rice, was very tasty and refreshing!

The girls got the strawberry très lèches for dessert and it was such a large piece they couldn’t even finish it. Very very sweet if you have a sweet tooth, they loved it!

Starting from the beginning: this is my second time visiting Casa Ora, and I’m still blown away by the incredible and delicious flavors in every dish, in every bite. I’m not sure if it’s because it reminds me of the flavors from home, or because they might even be better but either way, it’s something special. Thank you, Casa Ora, for the amazing work you do in the kitchen.

As for the cocktails: I tried the Canta Claro. I wouldn’t say it was amazing… but it was good just good.

The wine we had was the Garnacha Rosa, and it was absolutely exquisite.

In summary: the food is something everyone should experience. As for the drinks, I’d definitely try more
I’m sure there’s a standout cocktail waiting to be discovered.

10/10

5 stars

Amazing atmosphere and such friendly service! The food came out perfectly prepared every time. Loved the vegetarian options — everything was flavorful and sat well afterward, no heaviness at all. The salmon was a standout: crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, with a delicious coconut-ginger flavor. Don't skip the arepas and the sweet pancakes.
Incredible food. So unique. Amazing team. Drinks were incredible. It’s the real deal when non alcoholic drinks pack so much flavor. My fiancée and I had an incredible time.

The atmosphere felt very intimate, it was dark but inviting and a great spot for a date. Service was phenomenal, they were very attentive and gave great recommendations. The cocktails were a 9/10, I had a spicy mango drink. The arepas were incredible but the number one dish was the bollitos pelones. Highly recommended. The baby shark dish was our least favorite but each dish was plated with care and very aesthetically pleasing.

I came all the way from Manhattan to meet friends here for dinner, and it was absolutely worth it. From the moment we arrived, we felt incredibly welcome. We ordered a variety of dishes from the menu, and I had the chance to try almost everything, every single dish was delicious and beautifully prepared.
The atmosphere is very cozy and inviting, making you feel comfortable right away. It’s the kind of place where you want to stay longer and truly enjoy the evening. A big thank you as well to the lovely staff for their warm hospitality and excellent service. I can wholeheartedly recommend this place and would definitely come back again.

The food was superb, the customer service was awesome and the drinks were lit as well. The cuarto leche dessert is a must. I am Venezuelan and I always wanted to visit this place! It was such an honor see the attention to detail in everything the service, the food and drinks. If you want a Venezuelan restaurant with quality and amazing 5 star food. top_reviews.content: Walter’s Diner in Fort Greene does exactly what it says on the tin — it’s a diner, it serves food, you eat it, life continues. Nothing stood out, good or bad, which isn’t the worst thing a meal can be. Service was perfectly fine, the kind of fine that doesn’t ask to be remembered. I’m not going to make a special trip back, but if you’re hungry in the neighborhood, it’ll take care of you just fine.

Granted, we got one of the simpler items on the menu and the picture is from a shared plate with my son, but we got the Soft Scramble which is grilled sourdough, smoked salmon, soft scrambled eggs, parmesan, and hash browns, but from a place like Walter’s I’d expect it to be livened up a little bit. It felt like it was the bare minimum put on somewhat soggy sourdough. No seasoning, no sauce on the side or on it, nothing special at all - for a $22 price point. I’d say their service and ambience was awesome but for how good it looks from the outside I’d expect more than what I got which was the ingredients with nothing else.

I have been here many times. I like it but it's not very consistent. First time I had the burger, I was in LOVE. Second and third time, super mediocre. Have had fried chicken here- just okay. Not seasoned well. Salads are good. Brought my family here from England and they were not super impressed. The desserts are also just okay. Marked at $12 each but eh. The fries are the best thing here. Shoestring but fresh and delicious. Service is pretty great. Love the outdoor seating as it's much more quiet than inside which is way too loud. Expect waits Fri and Sat eve.
I came today not realizing the brunch menu was weekend only. None the less, I was so pleased. I had beat the lunch crowd and service was nice and quick.

If you’re looking for a solid spot for a comfort food night, this is it. It’s a small restaurant in Brooklyn that’s clearly a local favorite—it’s always busy, so I’d definitely recommend making a reservation ahead of time. The menu is full of those reliable dishes that never really miss. We went with:
-Steak & Fries: The steak was great, and the fries were exactly how they should be—thin, crispy, and perfectly seasoned.
-Green Salad with Grilled Chicken: We added chicken to the green salad, and it was a generous portion. Fresh and satisfying.

Don't come here expecting groundbreaking or experimental flavors; it’s not the kind of food that’s going to "surprise" you. Instead, it’s traditional, consistent, and dependable. The portions are hearty, the quality is solid, and it’s just a great, no-fuss meal.

Bro I was riding my bike through the city on my way to get some Dollar wings on a weds. Solid move. I rode by Walter's its like alive alive. So I investigate.  Ask a random lady on a bench she says they have a second secret venue in the back. It's a sushi resteraunt!?!? NANI!!!!???? Had the eel and a drink both well above board. I have to find the name of the Japanese restaurant in back and leave them a review too.

Tonight I finally met my girls at Walter’s—a place that had come highly recommended by both of them, though it was my very first visit. From the moment we arrived, the experience felt seamless. We had a reservation and were seated immediately, which set the tone for a relaxed and enjoyable evening.

We kicked things off with drinks, and every choice was a winner. The Prosecco was crisp and refreshing, the Penicillin was perfectly balanced, and the Manhattan was smooth and classic—an excellent way to start the night. For appetizers, we shared the wild oysters and deviled eggs, and both were absolute hits. The oysters were some of the freshest and best I’ve ever had in New York. The mignonette sauce was incredible, and the other two sauce options were just as impressive—I honestly could have eaten raw oysters all night.

When it came time for our main courses, the food continued to impress. Everything on the menu sounded tempting. My friends opted for the steak and frites and truly enjoyed every bite. I chose the Caesar salad with added salmon, which was cooked to perfection—crispy skin and all—flavorful, fresh, and beautifully prepared.

Beyond the food, the ambiance was warm and inviting, making it the perfect setting for a great night out. The waitstaff were exceptionally kind, attentive, and helpful without being intrusive, which elevated the entire experience even more. I absolutely loved this place and will most definitely be back.

From front to back of the house, service was excellent and cuisine consistent with Walter’s long standing reputation as one of Fort Greene’s best places to dash in last minute or reserve ahead of time for a wonderful experience. Menu is quality, and cocktails…one of the best programs we’ve seen in a long time, refreshing 100!!

top_reviews.content: I came across this restaurant through a Google search and decided to try it out for dinner cause the menu looked interesting. Let's start with the good; the service and the atmosphere was nice. The waitress was attentive and kind and the atmosphere was nice. It gave kind of a chill and/or romantic vibes depending who you went with. Nice, dimly lit, and plenty of booths. Now as for the food... well there was a lot left to be desired. We've had the mushroom croquettes, crispy potatoes, chicken skewers, the braise short ribs paella, and churros. The mushroom croquettes was the best out of everything but still lacked flavor itself (the truffle aioli carried the tapa) and barely had mushrooms. The crispy potatoes was decent but the salsa they used and put at the bottom was salty and the potatoes wasn't really crispy. The chicken skewers wasn't memorable. As for the braised short ribs paella, I was disappointed. The roasted bone marrow had no flavor, the rice was too sweet, and there was few short ribs meat and even that was bland. If I was to order this for myself, I doubt I would finish the plate but thankfully I was sharing this (and the tapas) with 2 other people. Lastly, the churros tasted like only fried dough with hardly any sugar and cinnamon. The sauces they gave us which was chocolate, Nutella, and dulce de leche helped elevated the churros but only a little. The dulce de leche tasted burned and the chocolate wasn't personally my taste but my friends liked it but we all agreed Nutella was best. The good thing I will say is thatthe portion for tapas, paella, and dessert was big enough to share among 3 people but what good is a shareable portion if it wasn't good. Overall, I would come to this place for drinks and small bites but as for dining, it's a no.
The food was generally good but found the paella a tad bit disappointing. Overall we had a great experience though. Sangria was also delicious. The staff were awesome.

My visit coincided with Happy Hour! We picked many dishes from the happy hour meanu, and several from the stardard menu. Everything was delicious, and the cocktails we excellent. Everything was outstanding.
I had been to another location several years ago, and I was so happy to have come back. Last thing, reasonably priced 😃

The atmosphere is great, and the food absolutely delicious, it brought me right back to Spain.  Our favorites were the gambas al anillo, half chicken, broccolini, jamon Serrano grilled cheese, and churros with the delicious dulce de leche.  The HH prices are exceptional, so take advantage of the low prices and fill up on sangria!  Yum!

We'll be back!  Thank you from Minneapolis, ope!  Minnesota strong!

The place is such a vibe the moment you enter. Moody tones and great booths. Cute bar and dining at the pass with full view for all diners. Our server Jason was super attentive and easy to talk to about the tapas menu, drinks and history of the restaurant. Overall wonderful evening with my daughter before going to see the new Spider-Man movie!!

Classic staple tapas and small plates. Nice, beautiful restaurant with great quality bites. If able to go for happy hour- they have quite a deal. Went with a friend to enjoy both drinks and bites. Enjoyed small bites of croquettes, Brussel sprouts, meatballs, and more. Overall really a staple and service was great/quick. Defs recommend

Really good food, the service is great from when you come in. All happy smiles and warm welcomes specially from Tiffany and the server Brian. The drinks were really good and they get the day going! There was a family celebrating their birthday infront of me and the server sang for them so that was really nice to see. Whenever I needed something the server was very attentive. I would recommend this restaurant if you’re willing to have a nice time (the drinks are really good)

The experience from start to finish felt thoughtfully curated, the kind that reminds you how powerful great hospitality and well-executed food can be.
From the moment we arrived, the service set the tone. Karla (with a “K” 😊) took exceptional care of us throughout the meal, attentive without ever being intrusive. She had a warm, natural way of making us feel welcomed and comfortable. Manager Tiffany also stopped by and went above and beyond to ensure everything was perfect. That level of attentiveness elevates a meal from simply good to genuinely memorable. The atmosphere itself deserves recognition. Even during the lunch hour, the space maintained a calming, relaxed energy.
We ordered the paella, and although it required a bit of patience, it was absolutely worth the wait. The rice was cooked beautifully, with a superb texture that struck that delicate balance between tender and structured. It was hearty and deeply satisfying. For my personal taste it leaned slightly salty, but the overall execution and flavor profile still made it a standout dish.

Among the tapas, the croquetas were easily the highlight of the meal. Crisp on the outside and wonderfully creamy within, they delivered that perfect contrast of texture that makes this classic tapa so beloved. Each bite was rich, comforting, and incredibly flavorful—without a doubt my favorite small plate of the afternoon.

I forgot to mention that the coffee was delicioussss 😅

Sociale nails the vibe, cute space, good energy, solid bar seating for a drink.

The food is where it plateaus: lamb ragu was fine, tartare was forgettable at best, and whatever they’re serving as “pizza” should probably be reclassified as a different food entirely, because it committed a crime against the name. Service was good, so nobody’s fault here, the kitchen’s just playing it safe elsewhere.

I’d come back for the aesthetics and a cocktail, but I wouldn’t build a dinner plan around it.

Chef's kisses for this beautiful restaurant! From the moment that we walked in we felt like family. This is what quality food is about. The smells, the sounds and the atmosphere is so beautiful. Trust me when I say you will not be disappointed. These meals are prepared with the utmost care. The lamb was out of this world. They do offer gluten free options. Make sure that you ask the waiter. My favorite dessert is the lemon one. I get it every time we go. They can make this gluten free as well. The prices are great for the quality and amount of food that you get. They spare no expense with making sure that you are fed well. The wine pairings are perfect! and the cocktails are great as well. Sociale also offers a private dining space if you want to host a private party.

We had dinner at Sociale Celler and really enjoyed the experience. The basement private room is small but very cozy, comfortably fitting around 20–30 people, and being next to the wine cellar creates a warm, intimate atmosphere that works well for a group dinner.

Starters were served family-style. The Napoli-style Pizza Fritta was a highlight—crispy on the outside, soft on the inside—and the meatballs were flavorful and well balanced.

For the pasta course, I chose the Carbonara, which was rich, well executed, and made with very fresh ingredients. The Branzino was extremely fresh and simply prepared, allowing the quality of the fish to shine.

Desserts were shared and included the Tortino al Cioccolato, a classic Tiramisu, and the Meyer Lemon Catalana, which was bright and refreshing. The family-style setup for the desserts worked well overall; however, slightly larger portions or individual servings could make it even better, given the no double dipping rule.

Overall, Sociale Celler offers a cozy setting with thoughtfully prepared food and a relaxed, enjoyable dining experience, especially well suited for group dinners and private events.

Wow! René is super attentive and friendly. The bartender was also very attentive and really knows his cocktails. The drinks were amazing, and the pizza was perfectly cooked. The service was more than excellent. Thank you so much! Highly recommend — we’ll definitely be back soon!

top_reviews.content: The interior of the restaurant had a nice dark and sexy vibe without being super pretentious. I loved how the server talks about each dish and writes it out. The food was delicious and fresh and my wine was nice too. I want to come back and try more of the menu.
Great food with a charming old-time atmosphere. Every dish was well-executed, but the scrambled eggs truly stood out—creamy, soft, and full of flavor. They elevated the entire meal.

I came to this restaurant by chance I was just looking for a restroom. When I walked in, I said I would order something and asked if I could use the restroom first. The staff were very kind and told me that I didn’t need to order anything and that I could go ahead and use it.
I was very impressed. After using the restroom, I ordered a burger and a beer. I definitely hope to come back again

I am on a mission to find the best brunch/breakfast spots in 2026 and Diner was the 5th and best spot thus far! Very tiny, cool space and tables fit up to 4 people but 3 was a tight squeeze already. We had the Caesar salad, French toast with chocolate and cherries, side of potatoes and breakfast sausage, the burger and the gravlax.

The hits at the table were the gravlax and the side of potatoes and sausage. Some of the best breakfast potato’s I’ve had!

The French toast was very good but I knew the cherry/chocolate combo wouldn’t be my favorite. I’d try it again with a lighter topping like apples and with more people to share it with.

The burger was good but I’d try another sandwich before ordering it again. I also personally prefer a thin patty and this was a thicker style.

Loved the salad and would definitely get it again.

Can’t wait to come back here to try some of the seasonal options but I’d come back for that sausage and potatoes anytime.

Solid service as well! We will be back.

Food was flavorful and well done. Fresh ingredients, good consistencies, and balanced flavors and original. Limited vegetarian options. Cozy interior, but the concept seemed like…trying too hard to be different and hip…? Why do you make your waiters write down the menu on the table for each group of guests? top_reviews.content:
We dined for my birthday brunch at the SoHo location. From beginning to end, the experience was a delightful experience.
We enjoyed a variety of cocktails including a not-too spicy and delicious Bloody Mary. The espresso martini not only boasted a full flavor, it was also beautifully presented.
The food far exceeded our expectations in both visual presentation and gastronomical expression.
We sampled salad, avocado toast and the seasonal quiche with carmelized pinions, goat cheese and spinach. Crème brûlée branch toast was light, airy and delicious. The flavor and presentation were magnificent.
The tower of pastries outshined the brunch menu! Macarons, cakes, lemon tart , and quiche gave us a lovely sampler of the delectable delights available in the bakery.
Following the meal, we sipped handcrafted cappuccinos, latte’s and different hot teas.
This is a must see when you visit SoHo.
Rafael runs the restaurant with such grace. The staff works together as an efficient team, everyone working hard to ensure the success of everyone.
Rafael guides the staff while also welcoming and attending to every guest. His careful attention ensures that everyone enjoys a wonderful experience.

A visit to Ladurée is a sensory delight from the scent of freshly baked brioche to the soft clink of porcelain tea cups. Nestled in the heart of the city, it offers a moment of calm sophistication, where every detail is curated for elegance. The interiors are romantic and nostalgic, ideal for lingering over a pastry or enjoying an unhurried afternoon tea.

I ordered a café crème and a selection of macarons (vanilla, raspberry, and salted caramel), and each one was exquisite. The textures were delicate, the flavors bold yet refined, and the presentation beautiful. The service was attentive without being overbearing, which added to the overall experience. Ladurée is not just a café it’s a celebration of tradition, taste, and timeless luxury.

We came here for my friend’s birthday, and I’ll start by saying this place is undeniably beautiful. The whole tea house vibe, especially the outdoor seating surrounded by greenery, makes you forget you’re even in the city for a moment. It’s definitely one of those spots you go to for the aesthetic and a cute girls’ day.

We had a reservation for three and were seated right on time, so I highly recommend booking ahead because it does get busy. Now, onto the food… the menu is honestly very overpriced for what you get. I understand it’s SoHo, but paying around $25 for a sandwich that’s literally the size of a finger is a bit much.

We ordered the tea for two ($95), which included a small selection: 4 macarons, 4 chocolate biscuits, a mini croissant turkey sandwich, a mini croissant salmon sandwich, two very small avocado toast pieces, and two biscuits with butter and jam. You also get a choice of coffee, tea, or champagne, which is nice but portion-wise, it definitely felt underwhelming.

We added a Caesar salad and truffle fries, and I will say those were actually really good.

Service wasn’t the best. It felt like our server was overwhelmed, so I don’t fully blame her, but it did affect the experience. One thing that stood out (and not in a good way) was that the jam we were served was expired (March 2025). We let them know, and they apologized, replaced it, and brought out a slice of cake, which I appreciated but still, that shouldn’t happen.

Overall, I wouldn’t come back for the food or service, but I would recommend visiting at least once for the vibe. It’s a perfect spot for pictures, catching up with friends, and enjoying a pretty atmosphere but don’t go in expecting to be wowed by the menu.

I had a wonderful experience at Laudrée SoHo in New York. Absolutely exquisite. This is truly top-tier French bakery at its finest.

Everything felt refined and beautifully crafted, from the pastries to the overall atmosphere. You can really taste the quality and tradition in every bite. It’s the perfect place to enjoy authentic French flavors in the heart of the city.

Highly recommended if you’re looking for an elegant and delicious bakery experience.

If you’re ever in SoHo, I’d definitely recommend checking out Ladurée. The food was great, but what really stood out to me was the atmosphere. The interior design, colors, and overall Parisian vibe made the place feel unique and worth visiting. The macarons are a must-try, and everything felt well put together. The only downside is parking—it can be a challenge, so plan ahead if you’re driving. Other than that, it’s a spot I’d happily recommend.

Ladurée SoHo experience.

I rarely leave bad reviews or provide this kind of feedback, but my experience at Ladurée SoHo has been the worst so far.

Let’s start with the hostess, who clearly hated her job. She was obviously annoyed by our presence during lunch and my birthday celebration. We politely asked if any tables were available, but she gave a short, cold answer and even rolled her eyes while walking away to check for a table. When she came back and asked if we had a reservation, I told her I made one online, since it seemed necessary to do so. Our table was in the middle, under a tree, and, unsurprisingly, our glasses were covered in bird droppings. What a lovely start! The service was miserable, unprofessional, demanding, and somewhat ridiculous. Our server never said more than he needed to—taking our order and bringing the check. I believe his name was Rodrigo M., based on the check. All staff members stared at us, making us feel unwelcome. We decided to have a drink and some food, hoping to enjoy my birthday despite the poor experience. I ordered an almond croissant, but it arrived with chocolate inside, which was not what I ordered. The truffle French fries were soggy, and there wasn't enough ketchup for us to share. We didn’t want to bother the busy staff, who seemed more focused on checking if guests belonged there. When we finished, it took 20 minutes to get the server’s attention for the check. So, what’s the point of tipping 40-50%, as we usually do, when they don’t bother to acknowledge a “happy birthday” or apologize for the poor service? Throughout the entire visit, no one smiled. I understand people can have a tough day, but come on, people come to Ladurée because it’s known for great customer service.
Now, here’s the worst part: since I love Ladurée, I wanted to get our usual that we get for snack, smoked salmon cucumber croissant and some pastries. But the person working there tried to sell us items that weren’t in the fridge, and they were displayed with flies all over the food. This is a serious health concern that needs to be addressed by workers, and by management team. If not, then by the health department, as someone could get sick! This situation is utterly ridiculous.

I want the management team to contact us via email so we can discuss this issue, as it was very poorly handled.

Thank you!
I look forward to hearing from you.

Maison Ladurée
Ladurée Soho, 398 W Broadway, New York, NY 10012
Afternoon tea outdoors is not easy to find in New York City, but Ladurée Soho offers a classy concierge service in a beautiful garden. Take a look at Ladurée's tea menu service, from finger sandwiches to sweets.

Ladurée celebrates the exclusive elegance of taste through its exceptional macarons and pastries. Great atmosphere, service, cocktails, and of course, their full tea service.

Not for eating.

I am genuinely shocked by how far this place has fallen. For a restaurant with such a long history and a mandatory $35 table minimum, the current quality of food and service is completely unacceptable. This wasn't my first visit, but it will definitely be my last because it has gotten significantly worse.
I ordered the burger, and the meat was distinctly sour—just completely unpalatable. To make matters worse, the service was totally nonexistent. No one brought napkins or bothered to refresh my drinks, so I literally had to do it myself. When the waitress finally asked how the food was and I told her I really didn't like the burger, she just said, "I understand," and walked off. No apology, no attempt to fix it, nothing.

If you just want to sit in a cute garden, drink tea, and have something sweet, maybe it's fine. But if you actually want a proper meal, do not come here. This is definitely not the place anymore.

Bar with a formal dining room and wonderful backyard patio! Perfect for summer nights. Adjacent to a LIRR station. Servers are super nice but food is a bit lacking. Nonetheless will definitely be going back.

My boyfriend and I came here after finishing long shifts at the hospital, hoping to unwind. We’ve driven past this place for nearly 10 years and finally decided to give it a try. The restaurant had a great atmosphere, and we were excited to eat here.

Unfortunately, the service was very disappointing. We received our drinks and placed our order, but after waiting about 45 minutes with no updates, we asked when our food might be ready. We were told there were several outdoor orders and that ours would be out shortly. After waiting even longer with no communication, we asked for the bill for our drinks so we could leave. Only then did a very kind gentleman immediately bring out our food.

To make matters worse, my water glass had lipstick on it. After it was replaced, the couple seated behind us—who had arrived just a few minutes before us—also found lipstick on one of their glasses. They received their food within about 10 minutes, while we had waited nearly an hour.

The food was decent, but it didn’t make up for the experience. I happened to find a Groupon during our wait, which I was thankful for because I couldn’t justify paying $92 for what was simply one appetizer, one entrée, a glass of wine, and a beer—especially with the level of service we received.

The staff did offer to comp another drink, which I appreciated, but by then I just wanted to leave. After wanting to try this restaurant for years, our first visit was unfortunately very disappointing.

Horrible service! Disappointing and left feeling disrespected.
My mom and I came here on September 7th before my birthday for a hangout. We ordered appetizers and drinks, first we never received our drinks. We did get the appetizers. No one came to check on us or ask if we needed anything for probably 35 minutes. When we finally called a woman over, she asked, “Did she [the waiter] not come over?” When we said no, she just shook her head. We cancel the drink and order entrees not too long after.

After again having to call someone over because no one came to check on us the entire time. another 20 minutes had passed. We ordered our entrees. I asked for my steak medium-well. The server told me that “medium well-done” was not a real thing and laughed. After I looked it up, she said, “Yeah, it’s medium-well.” I understand if I said it incorrectly, but I have never had someone talk to me like I was stupid and laugh in my face.

After feeling ignored and uncomfortable, my mom and I decided to cancel our entrees. When we went to pay, the first waiter, who had forgotten our drinks, charged us for everything, including the entrees we never received. She said, “Wow, sorry, I don’t know how that happened,” and told us to sit down while she fixed it.

She took our card inside and was gone for a while. I went to see what was happening and watched her handling other receipts, going into the kitchen, and bringing out a drink before finally noticing me. I told her that it was disrespectful to have me waiting while she handled other things, especially since my card was sitting there with my bank information.

She denied handling any orders and said she “wasn’t doing anything.” I told her that I had literally been standing behind her watching what she was doing. She then stared at me, rolled her eyes, and walked away.

Also want to point (for people of color) we were the only brown people and the ones who forgot their drink and  no one came to check on. We saw waiters going to everyone else and drink flying by ( everyone else was white).

Either way horrible service, horrible experience, horrible waiters.

I went to Austin Ale House last Saturday for the Knicks game, and it was an outstanding experience from start to finish.

This place really feels like a local gem in the Kew Gardens area. The atmosphere during the game was lively and fun without being overwhelming, and it’s a great spot to watch sports with a crowd that’s actually into it. The food was excellent—way better than your typical bar food, with solid portions and everything coming out fresh.

What stood out the most was John, the manager. He was hands-on the entire time, checking in on guests, making sure everything was running smoothly, and genuinely caring about the customer experience. That kind of presence makes a big difference and really elevates the whole place.

Overall, great food, great vibe, and one of the best spots around to catch a game. I’ll definitely be back.

top_reviews.content:
Go Nonna is absolutely worth going out of your way for. It’s a small place, but they had us seated quickly, and we never felt rushed even though we took our time after a long day around the city. That alone goes a long way.
The food really delivers. The shrimp pasta was out of this world, easily the standout. The meatballs had a great texture and flavor, and serving them with polenta and spinach is a nice touch that sets it apart. The carpaccio was elegant and really well done. The octopus was a little tougher than I’m used to, but still had good flavor, so not a dealbreaker.
Only small knock was the wine being a bit warm, likely just a bottle that hadn’t been fully chilled yet. It was still smooth and not bitter, so clearly well handled overall. Between the food, the relaxed atmosphere, and the service, this is the kind of place you remember and come back to.

I am usually very hesitant when trying Italian restaurants in Queens. I do not think I have been to many where I walked away truly very happy with the food. That being said, this place, as one reviewer put it, is quite a gem.

We came here for a rainy Sunday lunch, so getting a table was not very difficult. The atmosphere felt very homey, and our server was very sweet.

For starters, we ordered the tuna tartare. In my opinion, it was a little more bitter than I would have liked. I am not sure if that bitterness came more from the capers or from the lemon we squeezed over it. Still, the texture was very good and the rest of the flavor was nice.

The entrees did take quite a while to come out, even though the restaurant was not especially busy. Our server apologized for the delay and mentioned that some of what we ordered, like the lasagna, takes longer for the kitchen to prepare. At the time, we did not mind too much since we had a lot to talk about.

Because I have been a little jaded by a lot of Italian restaurants lately, I played it safe and ordered a Caesar salad with grilled chicken on top. My friends ordered the salmon and the lasagna, as mentioned earlier. We also shared a few vegetables on the side, namely the Brussels sprouts, spinach, and zucchini fries, which were very delicious.

Honestly, I regret not ordering a pasta dish. Everything was delicious, at least from what I and my friends tried. I was able to taste everything except the lasagna. The salmon was cooked just right, the potatoes that came with it were baked very well, and my salad was also very good. The sliced grilled chicken breast was juicy, the salad was not overdressed, and the lettuce tasted fresh.

Since we enjoyed the entrees so much, we also ordered dessert. We got the flan with a small serving of dulce de leche and the tiramisu, both of which we were told are made in house. These were also delectable.

Overall, this was a great experience. The food took a while, but in the end it felt worth it. I would not mind coming back here and trying more of what they have on the menu.

Nonna Italian and Argentina Restaurant was such a warm, inviting place to spend the evening. The service was attentive, welcoming, and made the whole experience feel relaxed and special. You can tell the cooks truly know their craft. Bien hecho.

It is a great spot for a small party or a night out where you want to unwind, enjoy fine food, sip good wine, and share a little conversation and gossip in a comfortable setting.

I had the Chicken Parmesano, and it was excellent. The chicken was breaded but still juicy and moist, with a light crust and a thick layer of hot, gooey cheese on top. It was full of flavor, with oregano and spices that brought everything together beautifully. It came with spaghetti cooked al dente and a rich, thick red marinara sauce that was flavorful, well-seasoned, and perfectly salted.

The artisan bread was a lovely touch, the Pinot Noir paired beautifully with the meal, and ending the night with a Limoncello was the perfect finish.

A wonderful delightful dining experience from start to finish. Big smiles, happy tummy, and cheers. 🍷

The food was amazing and very delicious. The lasagna was very good. The texture was very soft and the sauce was very rich and thick. The lemon linguine’s flavor wasn’t as strong, allowing for a refreshing break. The breaded chicken was also very good however it wasn’t very crispy probably due to it being covered by a layer of cheese. Overall the food was really good. Excellent ambiance with customer service, music with a nice outdoor area. The Mediterranean style branzino was absolutely divine accompanied by the afagatto was a sweet treat. If you're near LIC, or can access it easily, go at least once because I assure you that you'll want to return thereafter.

All in all, worth every cent and second spent.

⭐⭐⭐⭐☆
Quarters Korean BBQ offers a great ambiance and an overall enjoyable dining experience. The atmosphere is stylish and lively, making it a nice place to dine out. While the food and service are good, for a price point of $80+ per person, it didn’t fully feel like I got my money’s worth. We did order the beef tartare last time, which was really bland, so maybe just stick with the bbq meats instead, which are excellent.
My only other complaint is it's really loud, so often hard to hear your date or friends. But the food is so delicious so I'll def be back.

My friends and I went to Quarters Korean BBQ as walk-ins and had a very interesting and somewhat uncomfortable situation during our visit. However, the management handled it really well, and I truly appreciate that. A special shoutout to Lily at the front desk—she was absolutely amazing. She was kind, professional, and made us feel comfortable throughout the whole situation. She is the best, and honestly, I feel like I could be friends with her! Thank you, Lily, for making a difficult moment so much better.

This is the best kbbq in America and nothing else compares. I am Korean too and I’ve had a lot of KBBQ in Seoul and this compares with those spots as well. The meat here is top notch, the quality is amazing and even without getting the wagyu menu it still melts in your mouth. The service here is also phenomenal, the waiters cook everything here for you. Although the wait time can be long the line moves pretty fast and there is an outdoor bar in the waiting area so you can order drinks while you wait for your table which is also nice. Whenever I am in LA I always stop by here despite being out in South Bay.

I’ve been to Quarters Korean BBQ multiple times over the years, and I keep hoping it’ll improve. It hasn’t.

The biggest issue is consistency. Every visit follows the same pattern: a 20 to 40 minute wait minimum, even with the constant turnover. Once seated, the service feels rushed and indifferent. It doesn’t feel like anyone is invested in the experience.

As for the food, the quality of the meat just isn’t where it should be for Koreatown. The cuts lack the depth of flavor and marbling you expect at this price point. Compared to other KBBQ spots nearby, especially Parks BBQ or Mun, it’s not even close. The difference in meat quality is noticeable immediately.

Quarters does have one thing going for it: the energy. The plaza vibe is lively, loud, and great if you’re looking to drink and hang out with a group. If your priority is atmosphere over food, you’ll probably enjoy it.

But if you’re going for high-quality Korean BBQ, there are better options within walking distance. Parks delivers stronger meat quality, and Mun has both better service and a more refined overall experience.

It feels like as Quarters has grown more popular, the focus has shifted away from the product itself. When there’s always a line out the door, quality control tends to slip. That’s what it feels like here.

This was my first time at Quarters (9/27/25 at 7:15pm). We were seated at table #13 in the corner, and the smoke constantly blew straight into our faces and eyes, making it hard to breathe and leaving our eyes burning. It was uncomfortable and distracting throughout the meal.

The food itself was the highlight. The beef combo and marinated beef short rib were both juicy, flavorful, and cooked perfectly. We really enjoyed the quality of the meat.

Unfortunately, the service was a big letdown. Daniel rolled his eyes multiple times from the moment he took our order. Yes, the restaurant was loud, but instead of clarifying, he gave us nothing but attitude when one of my friends asked a simple question. Yomi wasn't any better--she kept a blank, unfriendly expression the whole time and stepped on my partner's foot twice without a word of apology. The lack of basic courtesy from both of them made the experience frustrating and unpleasant.

The only person who stood out was the manager. He was professional, warm, and checked on our table more than our own servers did. Honestly, if not for him, the service would have been a complete disaster.

Overall: good food, terrible service. The management deserves credit, but the staff's attitude ruined what could have been a great experience.

A solid spot for gukbap with a warm, inviting atmosphere that makes it especially enjoyable on a cold day. The interior is simple but comfortable, with a cozy ambiance that feels intentional rather than overly designed.

The gukbap itself is well-executed. The broth is rich and deeply flavored without being too heavy, and you can tell it’s been simmered with care. The meat is tender, portion sizes are satisfying, and everything is served at the right temperature. The balance between the broth and rice is done properly, allowing the flavors to come together without feeling overwhelming.

Service is efficient and straightforward, which suits the style of the restaurant. Overall, it’s a dependable place if you’re looking for a comforting, well-made bowl of gukbap in a warm and relaxed setting.

Even the Kalbi Tang is loaded with vegetables. The Dolsot nears the level of being Temple food. The Ban Chan is super fresh. The Pajeon super fresh spring onions.

Jin sol gukbap is by far my favorite go to restaurant in ktown. They’re always super friendly, fast, and the food is so good every time. I get the cold noodle combo, jeju noodle soup, and they’re both so tasty, nostalgic, and heartwarming!

(Last visited July 3rd, 2023.) Hanging out in NYC for the Independence Day weekend and we're turning up! We discovered that De Mole in Brooklyn was doing their bottomless food + drinks brunch on Monday because it was a holiday so we made reservations and pulled on up! Here's how it went.

Atmosphere/Appearance: Out in Williamsburg on the corner of Roebling and Hope Street lies this gem. Naturally, there's no private parking so good luck finding a place on the street or a nearby structure to put your fly ride. The restaurant was very welcoming and felt traditional with lots of tasteful Mexican theming. It was brunch of course so it was certainly a party inside, but it wasn't too loud. You could definitely still talk to one-another.

Service: I can't remember who took care of us, but with the speed of which everything was coming out, we were pleasantly satisfied. We had no complaints at all.

Food: So their brunch is bottomless everything. It includes both food AND drink. There are literally 12 different alcoholic beverages you can choose from and rotate between throughout your 2-hour time limit. I stuck to mimosas and margaritas. I was delightfully turnt. Lol. There are 20 different tapas to choose from as a part of your brunch and there's something for everybody! We had shrimp ceviche, strawberry dulce cake, multiple kinds of tacos, Spanish corn, just so much. Everything was good, but nothing was outstanding. I didn't expect that, but for it to be bottomless, the food came out hot, fresh and tasty. Period. I loved this concept.

Value: If you want bottomless food it'll be $59.00 for 2-hours of fresh plates. If you want to add drinks then it'll be an extra $10.00 more. $69.00 for all you can eat and drink is a little steep, but it was totally worth it!

In conclusion, I had a blast here at De Mole for their bottomless brunch and highly recommend it to anyone looking for sample a lot of different flavors. I love not being tied to choosing one entree and one drink option to have repeatedly. Tapas and tasting menus are my favorite ways of dining so I'm glad to checked this place out!

This was probably one of the best brunch spots I have ever been to! I went with a group of friends and we did the bottomless brunch. The staff was extremely attentive, respectful and kind! Truly an amazing dynamic between aml the workers, we had so much fun and not to mention the food was absolutely delicious!!! I highly recommend the bottomless brunch! HUGE shout out to Lauren, Alex, Sarah and Janelle!!! Love you guys 🩷🩷🩷🩷

top_reviews.content:
I had dinner here last week, and overall it was a decent Italian spot with some clear strengths, but also a few things that held the experience back.

The best part of the meal was definitely the pasta itself. The pasta was cooked properly al dente, which I always appreciate because it shows the kitchen knows what they’re doing on the fundamentals. The texture had that nice bite to it, and that alone made the meal feel more authentic than a lot of casual Italian places where pasta can come out too soft or overcooked.

That said, one of the bigger disappointments was that several menu items were unavailable. I understand that restaurants can run out of things, but when multiple items are missing, it does affect the experience—especially when you go in expecting to try certain dishes. It made the menu feel a little more limited than it looked on paper, and it took away some of the excitement of ordering.

Dessert was more of a mixed bag. Some items were enjoyable and felt like a nice way to end the meal, but others did not hit as strongly. It was not terrible by any means, but it felt inconsistent compared to the pasta, which was the stronger part of the dinner.

Service and atmosphere were fine overall. The place has a neighborhood Italian restaurant feel, and it is the kind of spot that can work for a casual dinner. I would not say everything was perfect, but I also would not write it off. The kitchen clearly has ability, especially with the pasta, but the menu availability and dessert inconsistency kept the experience from being better.

Overall, Sole Luna is a solid option if you are in the area and craving pasta, especially if you care about pasta being cooked al dente. I would probably come back, but I would go in with slightly adjusted expectations and maybe ask early what is actually available that day.

We were a party of 9 stopped by, without reservation and luckily were seated after approximately 10 min waiting time. Food was okay/good taste wise, but it was served excellent. Atmosphere was also very good. Overall a good Italian Restaurant.

My family and I have been coming to SoleLuna for years — it’s one of those rare spots that just feels like home. ❤️ Everything on the menu is incredible (truly, you can’t go wrong), and the food is always made with care.

As Sunnyside continues to change, SoleLuna somehow manages to capture both the old charm and the new energy of the neighborhood. It’s not just a restaurant — it’s part of the community, and one of the reasons we love living here. Highly, highly recommend. 🍝🍷

top_reviews.content: What a pleasant surprise.. decided to meet a friend and coming from out of town, decided on this spot for the right location that works for both of us. Well, it ended up being perfect in all directions - food, ambiance, service, and the reviews about valet ($9) with validation from the restaurant for 3 hours was super helpful. The coffee was fresh and the fries were tasty too! If I’m in the area again, I’d come back for more of the goodness this Front Yard has to offer.

All of our family were quite pleased to have this restaurant right on the hotel premises.  The decor is very welcoming with tropical groovy vibes.  I recall that  most of staff were extremely friendly.
The spot can get busy as one morning. We were turned away without a reservation over the next morning we were able to just cruise in.  As a vegetarian, there’s not a whole lot to order, but I was able to find a few things. The kids absolutely loved their stuffed French toast.  Prices are on par for a hotel.
I appreciated all the different dining spot we could have our meal- from indoors to outdoors all; quite nice.

We ate here a couple of times for both breakfast and dinner during our stay at The Garland, and had a lovely time! In the morning they have a fantastic breakfast buffet with eggs, fresh juice, fresh fruit, etc. We had the wild mushroom flatbread and the cheeseburger for dinner, as well as  a delicious biscuit appetizer that was recommended to us. I was pleasantly surprised with a large portion and everything was great! It has a great atmosphere both for breakfast and dinner.

The Front Yard was alright, but nothing especially memorable. The setting is nice and the patio has a good vibe, but the food were just average for the price. It’s a decent spot if you’re already nearby, though I wouldn’t go out of my way for it.
Got a couple of dishes and all were just okay.  Some needed seasoning.  The crab salad tasted like canned crab they threw on a salad. Hummus tasted homeade but lacked seasoning and flavor.

Took my mom here for brunch and overall we had a really nice time. The space is beautiful — very Palm Springs energy with the greenery, open patio, and warm California light. It feels like a little escape in the middle of Studio City. My mom loved it, which automatically makes it a win.

We had a couple glasses of wine and the bill actually came out pretty reasonable, which was a pleasant surprise for a place that looks this polished.

A couple things that were slightly annoying: they make you wait at the bar if your table isn’t ready (which is fine), but then you have to close out your tab at the bar before going to your table. It just feels unnecessary and breaks the flow. Not the end of the world — just mildly irritating.

Food-wise, it’s solid but not mind-blowing. There aren’t a ton of brunch options. The burger was easily the best thing we had — definitely recommend that. The chicken sandwich was… fine. Not bad, just kind of mid.

Parking isn’t the best, and fair warning: if you’re not paying attention, you can easily miss the entrance and end up doing an awkward U-turn near the freeway.

All that said — beautiful vibes, good energy, great for taking your mom or meeting friends for a laid-back brunch. I’d go back, probably for the burger and the atmosphere alone.

Cute, Great Vibe, Easy Parking, Our server was awesome. That is where it kind of ended. Paying $9 5 deviled eggs that came toppled over  and stuck to each other.  ….I was like uhmmm, it happens. The fruit bowl was fresh and nice. However, after eating 2 of the 5 deviled eggs the entries came out.  2 starters, 2 share plates, 2 entires, 2coffees and water. There was no room, our main food was getting cold while try to eat the starters. Then the entires….decent but both needed flavor and some salt and pepper( which took forever to come).  Good sizes but that was about it.  Good spot if you are with a group and want a fun vibe but not a spot if you are looking for a WOW meal.

The atmosphere was terrific but I was not enjoying my food. It needed flavor and for the price it wasn't worth it. To boot the cold brew coffee we ordered was from a can and given to us to open. I wanted this place to be better. It still can be. The most disappointing was the sausages they were just underwhelming. The best part of my meal was the eggs and the table preserves in little jars.

This entire resort was so cute, and the Front Yard restaurant was no exception!

Their indoor/outdoor space was beautifullly decorated to make you feel like you'd stepped back in time to the late 60s/early 70s. If you are reading reviews, it's probably not just for the ambience, but because you want to know about the food - and it was all very good.

We went for brunch and they had pitchers of mimosas and palomas available for $28. We only tried the mimosa and it was surprising delicious! We also enjoyed their deviled eggs, the hot chicken sandwich, and the Royale. Everything we tried was a hit!

top_reviews.content:
I had brunch here recently, and there is so much to love about this spot!
The Vibe: The atmosphere inside is incredibly inviting, and they have a great playlist going that sets a really nice, relaxed brunch mood.
The Patio: The outdoor patio area is beautiful and well-decorated—perfect for a weekend morning.
The Food: Absolutely delicious. Everything we ordered hit the spot.
One quick heads-up: The patio had quite a few bugs flying around while we were trying to eat. If you are sensitive to that, you might want to ask for a table indoors or bring along some bug spray!
Overall, it's a fantastic Brooklyn brunch spot that I’d definitely recommend. I would absolutely go back—I just might sit inside next time!

First time to French Louie and we were very pleasantly surprised.  The space was very understated, but quietly elegant.  The service was attentive and efficient and the drinks from the bar were great.  Now , lets get to the food....  we ordered a lot, let me try to remember it all.  We got the Paté, which was some of the best we've ever had, we got the bread and butter, which was great, but the butter was surprisingly fantastic (realized it was likely more because of the Maldon Salt, but still really good), the  fried anchovies were EXCELLENT (dont skip the lemon, its not just a garnish!!!), the escargot was unlike any other escargot we've had, not sure if it was better or worse, just different.  Then we had the gnocchi, which was rich and delicious, and the tartare, which was creamy and delicious.  For the mains, we got the mussels, which were tasty, but were lacking just a little something,  the Hake, which was OK, and the Bavette, which was a little dry, and the pasta (dont remember the exact name), which wasn't my favorite, mostly because im not a fan of pesto, but the rest of the group thought it was great.  To close out, we got the profiteroles, which were not overly sweet ans tasty and espresso all around.  Overall, a great time was had, and we will ABSOLUTELY be back.  A new neighborhood gem unlocked.

Amazing service from start to finish. The team was attentive, welcoming, and made the whole experience feel enjoyable.

The food was excellent. Ordering the steak is an easy decision here. It was perfectly prepared, and the homemade steak sauce truly elevated the dish. The sauce added a rich, balanced flavor that made the meal even more memorable.

We also tried the mussels and the beef tartare, and both were very well done. Fresh, flavorful, and thoughtfully prepared.

The atmosphere is another highlight. The vibe feels warm and stylish, making it a great spot for a date night or a small gathering with friends. It has that comfortable yet slightly upscale feel that works well for special evenings.

Overall, it is a wonderful dining experience.🫶🏻 The steak and that homemade sauce alone are worth coming back for. Highly highly recommend this place for anyone planning a date or a relaxed night out. 🍷🥩✨

French Louie is the kind of neighborhood spot that makes you feel like a regular on your first visit, which is either great hospitality or mild sorcery. I’m not ruling either out.

Stopped in for drinks and apps, and the food was solid without being the kind of thing you text someone about. The wine list earns a respectable nod. But honestly? The bartender is the whole plot here. The energy was warm, unhurried, and vaguely like being looked after by someone’s cooler older sibling. I’ll be back, and it’ll be because of them.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

I came here for brunch with a friend and initially had a great impression. The host was friendly and welcoming, but unfortunately the service from our waitress was disappointing.
She brought out a matcha martini that was dripping all over the outside of the glass and carried it without a serving tray. As she handed it across the table, the drink spilled onto my bag and stained the leather handle before being placed in front of me. I had to ask for napkins to clean both the glass and my bag. What bothered me most was that she did not apologize until I pointed out that my bag had been stained. I later noticed her using serving trays for other drinks. I understand that she may have been new, but this experience put a damper on what otherwise could have been an enjoyable brunch.

Every time I walk through the door, the experience feels effortlessly elevated. The food is outstanding: rich, comforting plates executed with precision and real care. If you’re craving elevated French comfort food without pretension, Recette delivers every single time. Easily a repeat favorite—highly recommend.

A true hidden gem! We chose to sit outside, and it made for such a wonderful dining experience. The atmosphere was charming, relaxing, and perfect for enjoying a great meal.

If you’re looking for a cozy French restaurant with amazing food, excellent service, and a lovely outdoor setting, this place is a must-visit. We can’t wait to come back!
