top_reviews.content:
I came here during Restaurant Week for the $60 per person menu, and unfortunately, the experience was pretty disappointing.

For a restaurant at this level, the food felt surprisingly ordinary and, in my opinion, below the standard I expected. Compared with other restaurants I’ve tried at a similar price point and level, the Restaurant Week menu did not feel particularly thoughtful or well executed. To make matters worse, I found a strand of hair in the curry chicken, which obviously made the experience even less enjoyable.

The service also fell short of what I would normally expect from a French restaurant at this level. Simple things like refilling water and clearing or resetting the table were not handled very promptly, at least from my experience that evening. These are small details, but they do make a difference when a restaurant positions itself at this level.

That said, the atmosphere and overall vibe of the restaurant are great, and that was probably the strongest part of the evening.

One other thing that made me uncomfortable was the seating arrangement. I noticed that guests of certain ethnic backgrounds, including myself, seemed more likely to be seated in less desirable areas, such as corners or tables along the main walkway, unless they specifically requested otherwise. I can only speak from my own experience and observation, but the pattern was noticeable enough to make me feel uncomfortable and somewhat differently treated.

Overall, the space is beautiful, but based on the food quality, service, execution, and my overall experience, I did not feel that the Restaurant Week menu reflected the level or hospitality I expected from this restaurant.

Ordered the Lily of the Valley option for high tea & Lily of the Valley drink (cucumber vodka drink-super refreshing). I have a huge sweet tooth but I am also a picky eater when it comes to pastries and they met my expectations-everything was delicious!

This review is only about the afternoon tea served at Majorelle. My aunt treated me to the holiday tea, which was $125 per person (it’s our holiday tradition since I was in high school, and over the years we’ve been to many beautiful hotel teas so I'm comparing against the St. Regis, Plaza, Pierre, Baccarat, etc in my mind). This one was great, and I say that as someone who is very critical.

I do think $125 is a lot, but it also seems to be standard for tea most places now. I loved that we were seated at a four-top (though we were just 2 people). When you’re used to cramped NYC restaurants, having a large table feels like such a luxury esp since the three-tier tea trays take up so much space. At small tables I always feel like I’m about to knock something over (this is how I felt at Kings' Carriage House).

I don’t really like tea itself (the leaves), so I can’t speak to the selection (sorry). The teapot was kept warm by a candle (see my photo) and the tea was fully steeped before it came to the table. I sometimes enjoy the ritual of straining it, but this was nice too.

The area of the restaurant we were seated in was quiet and not crowded, and the waiter kindly offered to take photos of us without us even asking. Service was excellent, which for me mostly means we were not rushed. They were attentive, and whenever we needed anything it only took a moment to get someone’s attention.

Everything was delicious. The scones were good (not dry), with plenty of clotted cream (they were not stingy with anything). The desserts were excellent as well. At my last few teas I’ve found the desserts to be overly sweet, but I really enjoyed these. The tea sandwiches were great too, especially the banana bread “sandwich” with jam.

The setting wasn’t especially beautiful--it felt mostly like a nice but regular restaurant, but it was very comfortable. That actually worked perfectly for us, since we really wanted to talk and catch up, and the booth we got was very conducive to that.

They did bring around a dessert cart where you could order additional items, like a bûche de Noël or madeleines (see my photo), for an extra cost. Honestly though, there was so much food included that I can’t imagine having room for more desserts on top of everything already served.

When I judge a tea, my criteria is sort of nebulous. I'm basically trying to answer "does this feel how tea should feel?" (special occasion-y, formal in a fun way, also a little decadent) -- and this tea very much did.

I celebrated my 23rd birthday at the Majorelle on 2/25/2026 and had the most amazing experience. Not only was very single bite I had phenomenal, with clear artistry and culinary skill present in each bite, but the service and hospitality easily matched. Basil was a lovely server, constantly keeping our cups refilled and indulging in all of my questions and topics of conversation. Matt kindly showed me to the restroom and allowed me a walk through of the club room. All in all I would highly highly recommend making a trip and enjoying a lovely high tea experience at the Majorelle. Make sure to say hello to Basil for me!

Amazing afternoon tea experience. Highly recommended. The pink cake slice was $28 and we got it to go.. it was the smallest piece of cake I’ve ever seen in my life. It wasn’t my thing but my partner enjoyed it.

We had an absolutely wonderful meal in this beautiful setting. I appreciated that it wasn't too loud. The service was impeccable, we were recommended a fantastic bottle of wine and the food was truly delicious. The one thing I didn't enjoy was the cherry souffle but everything else was really perfect. Would go back for any special occasion or business dinner. Also the bar scene looked super fun and hopping--it was loud but far away enough from the dining room that our meal was quiet and serene. Go here!

HOW TO GET IN: you will definitely need to book this online beforehand but it’s very easy to get a reservation.
I think this may be the best place I have had afternoon tea in the city. The service was excellent. Costa treated us so well and made us feel so special. The space is absolutely stunning as well as all the Dior tableware. The desserts and sandwiches are some of the best I’ve ever had. Each one was great. We also ordered the dips which are a must. I appreciate we could switch tea flavors. I also liked that we got the scones after, so there was enough room on the table for all the jams and cream.

My bf and I took my mom out for a fun afternoon tea at the Majorelle. Unfortunately, comparing to our other afternoon tea experience in the city, the food and service were both disappointing. As I read thru the review on Google, many people spoke so highly about the warm scones. I was looking forward to trying them. However, they served three different flavors, I stopped after trying half because they are just so dry and hard. The sandwiches were extremely basic, cucumber, chicken curry, lobster and egg sandwich. None of those really stood out to us. The pear puff was the only highlight of the pastry. And another star goes to their delicious green tea.

The service was not attentive at all, even rude. Our server was 6 feet tall male, dark hair, wearing black frame glasses. There was no welcome, nor introduction or greetings. The entire time service was very cold and lack of even politeness, came off as arrogant tbh. He never refilled our tea once. The only time he smiled was after tipping, so frankly he didnt do much to deserve that. The one star of service goes to all the other servers who has been help refilling a little. But most of the time, we did it on our own. I do have to say the managers are all super professional and attentive. Maybe training needs to improve on servers. All in all, this is not the service we expect from a top afternoon tea place in the city.

Also the size of the main afternoon area is quite small. Just felt kinda tight and a little noisy if you are close to a big group. The real flower arrangement was beautiful.

Overall, we would not go back again.

My partner and I got married at River Café on June 7, 2026, and we truly cannot say enough good things about our experience.

From start to finish, everything was exceptional. The level of service, attention to detail, and care that went into bringing our vision to life exceeded all of our expectations. Every member of the team was incredibly attentive, professional, and genuinely invested in making our day perfect.

We especially want to recognize Destiny, the day-of coordinator. She was an absolute joy to work with and one of the best vendors we had throughout the entire wedding process. Not only is she incredibly kind, but she is also organized, responsive, thoughtful, and exceptionally good at what she does. Having her by our side made the entire experience feel seamless and stress-free. She truly went above and beyond, and we are so grateful for everything she did for us.

River Café is a truly magical place to get married, and the people behind it are what make it so special. The setting is stunning, the service is impeccable, and the team and specially Destiny makes you feel completely cared for every step of the way.

We’ve also dined at River Café outside of our wedding and can confidently say it’s a wonderful restaurant in its own right. But if you’re considering it as a wedding venue, don’t hesitate for a second. We would choose it again in a heartbeat.🥹🤍

I went to The River Cafe with a friend while in NYC and had a great time. The view of the River is beautiful and we had a gorgeous sunset. I will say that they had very predictable options to be a Michelin Star Restaurant, but for the most part the meal was great. We had great service and had to return the mashed potatoes that came with my friend’s dish due to being a bit too salty for our taste.. but, they brought us the most perfect French fries I have ever had. So kudos to the chef for providing such a great substitute. I would definitely recommend this spot for date night or a special celebration while in NYC.

Our team has had the opportunity to work several weddings at The River Café, and every single experience has been exceptional. Beyond the obvious beauty of the venue and views, we are always blown away by not only the incredible food, but the level of hospitality and service provided throughout the entire experience.

Allison and Destiny are wonderful to work with during the planning process. Their communication is excellent, they are incredibly accommodating, and they are always willing to answer questions, offer guidance, and help ensure everything runs smoothly leading up to the wedding day. As a planner, having a venue team that is collaborative and responsive makes such a difference, especially for complex events.

On the wedding day itself, the staff consistently goes above and beyond for both the couple and their guests. I do have to give a special shout out to King, who has truly made an impression every time we have worked together. He has a way of making everyone feel like they are the most important person in the room, and his personality embodies exactly what hospitality should feel like. Warm, attentive, genuine, and effortless.

I cannot recommend The River Café enough for couples looking for a wedding venue with exceptional food, stunning views, and a team that genuinely cares about the guest experience from start to finish.

Amanda Briggs
Briggs & Co.

The view is absolutely worth it and is probably what drives people to frequently dine here.

The appetizers we chose were unique. The Agnolotti was absolutely amazing. The Wagyu Steak Tartare was mediocre.

Our main course choices were: char grilled Niman Ranch strip which had a great char but had several gristle spots which with price in mind is disappointing. The Russet potatoes were excellent!! The Black Sea Bass was a great choice all around. Both had great presentation.

Desert we had Raspberry Soufflé which I would recommend and Chocolate Brooklyn Bridge which I would not recommend. The presentation is awesome but the cake portion is less than desirable.

So presentations were  10/10

Staffing and attention to detail (timing, cleaning off table between meals, refilling water, courtesy) 10/10

View 10/10

Food was not as expected for price and quality 5/10

Drinks were pricey at $22 but were all very good 6/10

Wait times between meals 5/10

Wait time after finishing for the check 1/10 (30 minutes after we were done)

Dining at The River Café is truly about the experience. We had the three-course meal, and the overall presentation was elegant. The environment was very cozy and romantic, with beautiful views under the Brooklyn Bridge, and the staff was nice, attentive, and amazing throughout.

While the courses were well presented, the desserts felt quite costly and didn’t fully meet expectations for a Michelin-level experience, as the flavors were a bit bland.

I’d recommend visiting in the summer if you want to fully enjoy the atmosphere and surroundings. Overall, it’s a memorable place mainly for the setting and service.

The culinary experience was beautiful and good but not unforgettable. Obviously, the view is great...but the service is one of the worst we have experienced. Definitely not warm and authentic. From what we saw, this place runs on views, not hospitality. We honestly ended the night wishing we had just got some pizza and sat at pebble beach or Brooklyn bridge park. Probably would have had an even nicer night out. I would strongly consider an alternative...you don't need this dinner for these views. The bartender was coughing in drinks. There was a fly landing on tables. The table light was flickering. Inconsistent sommelier. Presentation was rushed. I had the rabbit for an appetizer, the lobster for an entree, and carrot cake souffle for dessert. It was all pretty good, nothing bad, but for me, the only bite that stopped me in my tracks because of how good it tasted was the amuse-bouche of smoked trout. My wife ordered oysters for an appetizer, duck for an entre, and tiramisu for the dessert. Oysters were very good, and her duck was good (the crust was amazing). But offering dessert drinks halfway through dessert. No assistance or guidance to the bathroom. Just too many things. The internal atmoshere, feeling, and attentiveness fell way short of expectations compared to many other fine dining experiences, which was a bit disappointing for a place like this.

From the beginning to the end our birthday dinner was an incredible experience. We were celebrating her birthday and she truly enjoyed it! The simplicity, but sophisticated restaurant ambience, to the mellow live music in the background complemented with an amazing view of the city and Brooklyn bridge at night time made our experience to be out of this world. The food was absolutely incredible, with a bold flavor and every bite taking us to a different level of joy, more gratefulness and sharing each other's dishes for more discoveries of childhood and times when food actually had taste. Each dish was unique in its own way and the chef's complementary side or dishes took us to heaven. Now, the drinks, outstanding and well done, strong as they should always be made.  The attention of the staff was incredible, from the moment we entered until the moment we received  the check. An absolute dreamy birthday that came to life in the city that never sleeps, they say, but we slept like babies after this incredible diner at the River Cafe.

Service and Quality isn't cheap, the food were delicious, the Service was exceptional and we loved the atmosphere there. Each staff that passed our table wish our daughter a happy birthday and did everything in their power to keep her happy.

Thank you

Also there is complimentary valet parking once your dining in the main area.

I had a wonderful experience here celebrating someone’s birthday! The staff were very attentive and every dish was a hit.

We splurged for the 14 day aged duck and it was so worth it — it’s now my favorite duck I’ve had in NYC! I’d recommend coming with st least 4 people if you order it.

The pan con tomate and frog legs were surprise hits for me, and I loved the chai tres leches cake for dessert.

Discovered Nudibranch through the Red Book and honestly thought it was a bit mid. The portions were very small, though I assume that's intentional since most dishes are designed to be tapas style.

Mushrooms - 4/5
Enjoyed the cheesy mushroom flavor. Simple but satisfying

Chicken Sandwich - 4.25/5
Probably the standout dish. The chicken was big, juicy, and very tender. Highly recommend.

Hamachi - 3.75/5
Liked the tangy sauce pairing with the clementine

Uni Soba - 2.75/5
The uni tasted quite fishy and the soba itself was fairly bland, though the flakes added a nice bit of texture

Sea Bream - 3/5
A bit disappointing for an entree portion. I did appreciate that it was perfectly deboned, but the grilled top with added dill and pumpkin purée didn't pair that well IMO

Frog Legs - 2.75/5
Not usually something I order, but we saw a lot of tables getting it so we gave it a try. Unfortunately it had a noticeably fishy taste, would skip next time.

We had a wonderful experience at this restaurant, and a big part of that was thanks to Selena, the manager. She was extremely professional, attentive, and made sure everything ran smoothly throughout our visit. Her customer service was outstanding, and she handled everything with confidence and a genuine smile.

We actually asked for her name because her level of service stood out so much. She made us feel welcome from the moment we arrived and helped create a great dining experience. Selena is a real asset to this restaurant, and we look forward to coming back.

Highly recommended!

Nudibranch is such a gem. Great atmosphere, excellent service, and a wonderfully executed menu of inventive dishes that blend Korean and Spanish flavors. I started with a couple of small plates: the patatas bravas and duck croquettes. Both were excellent, flavorful, and the perfect way to kick off the meal. The star of the night, though, was the pork chop with gochujang glaze. It was perfectly cooked, incredibly tender, and the glaze added just the right amount of sweetness to balance the dish. Overall, an outstanding dinner. I’ll definitely be back.

Pretty good! I liked the celery salad the most, and the duck croquettes. I found some dishes missing somethings, though it was all still good. The frog legs were a bit salty and over battered for my taste, really tasted like old bay which I don't love. The pork chop was really good I just wish they put more sauce and a little bit more vegetable vegetables because splitting one mushroom and one small piece of bok choy was a little annoying especially because it was so delicious there should've been more of it. Sea bream was yummy. Really liked the coconut semifreddo, really well balanced with sweet tart creamy and pepper. Refreshing and a great way to end the meal not too sweet at all.
Really like the ambience, nice wooden furniture, good art, great lighting, good volume level.

top_reviews.content:
Good friends of mine have been recommending Chavela’s for a while, so I was glad I finally had the opportunity to try it — and it definitely lived up to the hype. I was honestly surprised by how busy it was for a Sunday night, but that only added to the energy. The vibe inside is great: dim, cozy atmosphere with really comfortable booths that make you want to stay awhile.

The food and service were both wonderful from start to finish. We started with the nachos and guacamole. I’ve never had nachos served in a disc shape before — they were excellent and really unique, though I’d be lying if I said I didn’t still slightly prefer traditional nachos. The margaritas were awesome and paired perfectly with the meal.

For my entrée, I had the carnitas dish, which was absolutely out of this world. It came with tacos, refried beans, and salsa, and every part of the plate was packed with flavor. We also tried the carnitas taco, shrimp quesadilla and the steak and shrimp fajitas — everything we had was incredible.

I’ll definitely be back. And if you go, I’d also recommend stopping at Ample Hills Creamery across the street afterward for dessert.

8/10 times when I am deciding where to eat on Franklin Avenue, I pick Chavevla’s! I have been coming here for years. It is one of the most consistent restaurants on Franklin. Their service and food is always top notch. My favorite drink is the La Diabla, adding sugar on the rim. The margarita and sangria mixed drink is also really good. The Camarones al Ajillo is my favorite appetizer. The Sopa Azteca is really good. My favorite main dish is the fajitas Mixtas! Everything is good. Their holiday specials are always on point. I was here on Valentine’s Day and had amazing dishes. Make this a stop on your Franklin Avenue restaurant crawl!

The place has spectacular interiors and an insipid menu. The quessabirria was underwhelming.  It was very mild and I had to look long and hard for the cheese part. The margarita was tiny and all ice cubes. The salsas were white people salsas. Delicious but no spice. The restaurant is GORGEOUS though. A beautiful mixture of Brooklyn and Mexico. Kitsch and antique.  Mexican pastels and Brooklyn neutrals. Come for the decor! Bring your white friends.

I found this place on Google looking for a Mexican restaurant with vegetarian options with a high rating. I was excited that it was so close to The Brooklyn Botanic Garden.
It was everything that I hoped for! We were greeted by very lovely and professional hosts that sat us immediately. I am sure we were just lucky with timing because it filled up quickly afterwards.
The server was super awesome and knowledgeable about my dietary guidelines.
The food was delicious and generous portions. Beautiful presentation as well.
I highly recommend this restaurant.

Food wasn’t good. My fiancé and I went for lunch. I ordered enchiladas. The chicken was super dry. Not marinated
Or soft. The sauce itself was great. But it had many layers of tortilla and little chicken. Same thing with my fiancés burrito. It was super layered, very little meat and beans/rice.

It was tough chewing and cutting through.

name: Saqartvelo Georgian Cuisine
address: 15317 Vanowen St Unit A, Van Nuys, CA 91406, United States

business_details.details: 15317 Vanowen St Unit A, Van Nuys, CA 91406, United States
5GVM+M6 Van Nuys, Los Angeles, CA, USA

top_reviews.content: Amazing Cuisine, great smiling service and very heart warming atmosphere. The ladies are definitely Georgian and know exactly how to make Georgian food. Everything is from scratch and made to order. I kept passing by and decided to go in, asked for their famous Ajarski (Eye Shaped Egg Pizza) and it was well worth the stop. 10 out of 10 for sure. Delicious, crispy and not doughy, right out of the oven and into your mouth. I also wanted to try the Khinkali and that too was nice, big, and very juicy. The meat was not over cooked and was packed with lots of flavor. (PS if the the Georgian Dumpling)

Tasting Georgian cuisine took 29yrs & grateful to have found this place — worth the drive! The team are kind, warm, super helpful with navigating the menu — I literally wanted to order it all. 🤤☺️We ordered enough food to eat there & for takeaway. Everything was super fresh, delicious, and made with such care & craftsmanship. We want to go visit Georgia. 🇬🇪🥰The only thing that would have made this experience even better is a sip of Chacha or wine from a Qvevri. We’ll be back. Thank you for taking great care of us. J & T

Food from Georgia is new to me. There were several soup options. We chose Kharcho, the soup of the day, and the Khachapuri both were excellent.  The staff was friendly and gave us a bit of background story of when the Khachapuri is made ny the wives of fishermen.  They also allowed us to taste a few of the different soups. Next time we will try the Lobio, a kidney bean soup.  The food is very worth the price.

I am going to begin by stating I still hate eggplant, but they actually made it palatable which is amazing.  The spinach and beetroot are both incredible and tasted fresh.  The Satsivi (a cold soup for a hot day) really hit the spot. When they informed me it was cold I hesitated a moment but really glad i tried it.  Every dish I tried showcased the ingredients while not shying from fresh garlic and rich spices.  The bread (came with the food) is worth the visit on its own.
It’s a simple place, but very welcoming and warm.  The staff were so kind and happy to answer questions and educate their customers.
Sorry no food photos I jumped the gun and had bite marks in everything 🤷‍♂️

We visited this Georgian restaurant and were very impressed. Everything was truly delicious and filling. We especially loved the khinkali — large, juicy, with a perfect filling, just the way they should be. The portions are generous, so you definitely won’t leave hungry.

The Adjarian khachapuri was also excellent — fresh, ароматic, with stretchy cheese and soft dough. The kind of dish you want to finish down to the very last bite.

The chakhokhbili deserves a special mention — rich, flavorful, and clearly made with care.

The staff was very friendly, everything was served quickly, and the food was fresh, as if straight out of the oven. Thank you so much for the warm hospitality — we’ll definitely be back!

reviews_snippets.content: "I give them 5 star for food, service and communication."
"Great little restaurant with warm family vibe and chill atmosphere."
"We ordered khinkali — they were served quickly, hot, and absolutely delicious."

name: Kyochon Chicken
address: 3833 W 6th St, Los Angeles, CA 90020, United States
description: Korean-style spicy chicken wings with soy, garlic & other sauces draw crowds to this no-frills spot.

business_details.details: 3833 W 6th St, Los Angeles, CA 90020, United States
Closed · Opens 11 AM · See more hours

top_reviews.content:
My Korean friend told me that their K-fried chicken was very good. So even though it's far from our house in K-town, we just had to have it. Alright, let's go!

This place is more of a self-service spot; you place your order on a screen, and then the food arrives. However, the person at the front desk was very friendly.

We ordered the boneless soy-garlic chicken, which had a pretty typical K-flavor, fries, mixed greens, and chicken gizzards.

The food was served at a decent speed. Honestly, the soy-garlic sauce could have been better, it was lacking flavor, and the meat was a bit dry inside. The good thing was that they used drumstick meat, so the juiciness wasn't completely lost during deep frying.

Fries were okay, nothing special, but the hero of the night was the chicken gizzards, which saved the meal. The wasabi dipping sauce perfectly complemented the caramelized batter.

Overall, I believe it could be better for a place called the best K-fried chicken in town. But I'll give it another chance later and hope server stops by our table or refill the glass of water that we had.

Mostly take out. A few tables to sit.  Chicken is amazing crispy, crunchy. Great flavor. Almost as good as the ones in Seoul.  The cheese balls are a bit sweet but delicious. The Yangneom sauce was sweet and perfectly spicy and sweet.   The Red sauce was 5 times spicier than the Red in Seoul. It tasted a bit different too.  We could only eat a couple pieces.  Still delicious though.  Valet parking is only $5. Worth the trip for real korean fried chicken.

First time to Kyochon after hearing great reviews from my girlfriend.  Glad it is finally reopened.  The place was closed for a few months for renovation and expansion of the kitchen and dining areas.  The place has a refreshed look with modern furnishings and an ordering tablet at each table.  There is a large TV perfect for game nights.  Take out orders are still very popular in addition to more tables.  Regarding the food, this place is known to be very popular in Korea.  Trying the wings and it is true that they are superior.  I highly recommend the honey chicken. The soy garlic wings were just average but still good. I thought the radish and coleslaw was pickled very well.  We also ordered potato wedges and they were crispy on the outside and deliciously soft on the inside.

4/4 Update.  Delicious especially the honey wings.  We got the special with 10 wings and 5 drumsticks plus fries which was a lot more food than expected.  The chicken wings here are the very best.

I helped my son move to his place in KTown. We were both hangry and happy to find Kyochon within walking distance.
Service was great. The young person who helped us was polite, friendly, and answered all of our questions.
Space is clean and cutely decorated. We enjoyed the K-Pop music vids playing on a large screen.
Portions are generous.
Free coleslaw is a nice touch.
We both opted for lunch specials -$5 off regular prices.
I had the 3-wing sampler with potato wedges and fried rice.
K-wings are the best, so incredibly crispy, flavorful, and not the least bit greasy.  Same with the potato wedges, some of the best I’ve had.
The fried rice needed more seasoning.
My son had the Chicken Sandwich combo with Yangyum sauce, and waffle fries. The sauce was delicious. We both liked the potato wedges more, though both are good. The chicken in his sandwich was tough and some of it was inedible due to the texture. Not sure if this is normal or he just got a bad piece of chicken. Minus one star for this.
Next time, we will both order wings.

I had the Honey Combo and tteokbokki, and I also ordered a beer. The food was really good, and I was pleasantly surprised when they brought out cassava chips for free. It was a nice extra touch and made the whole experience even better.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Amazing chicken, great service, and such a cool vibe! The food at Kyochon Chicken was absolutely delicious, but what really made me want to leave this review was the staff.

I accidentally left my bag there with my sunglasses, car keys, medicine, souvenirs, and all sorts of important stuff inside. I didn’t even realize it until about FOUR HOURS later! 😭 I called the restaurant, and thankfully they had found it and kept everything safe for me.

Even better, they’re open late (until 2 AM), so I was able to come back that same night and retrieve it. Everything was still there. Such a huge relief!

Great food and genuinely trustworthy, helpful staff. We had a fantastic experience and would definitely come back. Highly recommend! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

I’ve been waiting for this location to reopen, and now it finally has!
The whole indoor atmosphere has changed a lot—in a very good way—and the design in front of the restroom was quite impressive.
The waitress at the front of the house was so friendly and attentive, which made the experience even better.
And the taste—obviously, absolutely great!
To be honest, it was even better than before.

My friends and I fell in love with the honey chicken, tteokbokki, and garlic fried rice.
Especially the Salsal chicken—it was my little one’s favorite!
We really enjoyed our time here, and we’ll definitely be back soon!

Used to be my favorite Korean fried chicken spot. Came back after 5 years and ordered the soy garlic chicken, but it tasted very different. The breading is completely different now. Very disappointed ☹️

top_reviews.content:
Gersi is truly one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in Brooklyn. The food is absolutely incredible, the atmosphere is warm and inviting, and the staff goes above and beyond to make you feel welcome.

The Chicken Parmigiana was outstanding—perfectly crispy, tender, and flavorful, topped with rich sauce and melted cheese. Every bite was delicious. The Aperol Spritz was refreshing, perfectly balanced, and exactly what I was craving.

A special shoutout to Luis, the bartender, who is incredibly attentive and makes amazing drinks. His service and attention to detail elevated the entire experience. David, the host, was so sweet, welcoming, and accommodating from the moment we walked in. The managers were also fantastic, making sure everything was perfect and that every guest felt taken care of.

Exceptional food, exceptional service, and an amazing team. I can’t wait to come back. Highly recommend Gersi to anyone looking for a memorable meal in Brooklyn!

🐾 They had me at sausage.

Late weekend brunches are even better when they’re quiet… and when your human orders you a side of sausage. 🐶 My tail was wagging before the steak and eggs even hit the table.

The staff was incredibly sweet to me, the service earned two paws up and I loved having both the front patio and cozy backyard patio to lounge in while keeping an eye on the neighborhood.

The food made my human happy, the hospitality made me happy and that’s what really counts. I’ll definitely be bringing my pawfriends back for another brunch date. 🐾

I had an amazing experience at Gersi. I took my dad for his birthday over the holidays and when we arrived, they have a “happy birthday” sign on the table. Everyone working there was extremely friendly. The espresso martini I had was very tasty. We ordered three pastas to share… carbonara, spaghetti al limone with grilled chicken (my favorite) and rigatoni ragu. Delicious dishes! We will be back :)

I was looking for an authentic Italian experience and I found it! Handmade pasta and the BEST house sauces (lemon, cream, red - everything is uniquely delicious). Generous portions of crab and other proteins. Try the veal meatballs and mushroom bruschetta. Explore vegetarian options too!

They can sub today’s house pasta in most dishes which I love. Ask for the specials because they tend to have many off-menu options every day. Seating is somewhat intimate but never uncomfortable. The server was so attentive despite a full house on a weekend.

Made a reservation online. Waited 20 minutes before we were seated. 1st table was outside near the dish pit. We asked to move tables, waited another 20 mins to be sat inside near another trash pit. Took another 30 mins to take our order and when the food finally arrived it was just okay. Bad service and mediocre food was a bummer. I remember this place being good years ago.

top_reviews.content: Small and quaint location that locals go to. Limited menu but everything we had was excellent.

Salads are fresh good but portions smallish  for the money.Tends to be noisy . service not warm and fuzzy but adequate. I mistakenly ordered a salad with anchovies which I hate, and they refused to take it back.. Tacky. Yes my fault but a better restaurant would have taken it back..I think I'll stick to Gracie Mews Diner with huge delicious Cobb salad for same money, friendlier service, and nothing is ever a problem . So much for upscale French cafes.

Le Moulin a Cafe, cute french bistro , serves various variety of pastry and macarons and serves wonderful brunch menu croque madame was delicious and fried egg hit the palette with a side of salad and vinaigrette balanced the becemel. Also Le burger Du moulin( sirloin burger)cooked as requested with side of fries and Earl gray tea. If your in the area give this cafe a try, your palette won't disappoint.

Fantastic little authentic French bistro. The owner is also French, Every meal that we’ve had there has been executed with precision and care. Especially considering the limitations of importing French products into the United States. They even have a micro pantry store to get all those hard to find items Like grenadine and béarnaise. 100 out of 100 would recommend This hidden gem of a Yorktown eatery.

Over priced and not very authentic. Brittany buckwheat crêpe looked more like a burrito. (See picture. Google what it should look like.) Avocado toast with fried egg was under par for over $20.

It was over $160 (before tip) for 5 people. They included a tip AND they trick you and ask for another tip when you pay.

Take note of your receipt!!!

top_reviews.content: Solid Neighbourhood pub. I believe it is a third oldest continuously operating bar in New York City. A watering hole for all residents of the Woodheaven area. A great bar and great layout. The Honduran mahogany wood bar top is amazing. The history behind the bar is really cool. The fact that Goodfellas was shot here and Anthony Bourdain was also a beloved patron of the bar makes it amazing. The bartenders are really cool and insightful. Will definitely be back anytime I’m in the neighborhood. Their burger is also pretty solid.

Been there a couple of times in the past. Can't wait to go back. The best bar I've been too. Food and service was great. Everyone was friendly especially Mr. Loycent Gordon who gave a history of the place. Really nice guy. P.S. Congratulations on your location at JFK!

I took my spouse, brother in law and sister in law there for an overdue group date night...we had a great time, great food, great comedy show just a wonderful evening.  Place isn't to big but we were sitted comfortably..the patrons and wait staff were fantastic.  Due to my own personal beliefs I didn't like all the comedians but overall a great show.  My favourite were Aaron,  Momjombo ( I'm sorry if I misspelled your name) and the last lady who resides in NJ (my condolences). The comedy host was fantastic and very polite too.  Food was delicious.  We had pretzels, wings, fries, burgers, sodas, beers and mixed drinks...not super expensive either.  I believe this will be our new hangout spot.  Although parking is terrible.

Cool, local, historic spot where you can grab a tasty burger and drink a pint or one of their signature cocktails. The bartenders were friendly and attentive. Some folks think it’s hard to get to but honestly it’s a 10 minute walk from the J train in a quiet neighborhood.  Neir’s is a spot that doesn’t coast on their lore, history and reputation. They actually serve great food, amazing cocktails, and you can actually feel the history while you’re there. They will definitely see more of me at Neir’s

I visited this bar because it used in the amazing Goodfellas film it was 50mins from central manhattan on the subway in queens but so glad I went super cool inside great vibe sat at the bar sports on the screens and jazz was getting played also had a couple of beers and neirs tavern old fashioned it was yummy I'm a big souvenir person so bought a t-shirt and fridge magnet definitely go back for sure

They were very accommodating for our large party being late. Our waiter Alex was awesome, he made some great recommendations and was a blast overall. My favorite was the lobster and crab fried rice. The steak was yummy and the drinks were nice and strong.

Went here for a friend’s birthday recently and we really enjoyed our experience dining at this place! The service was excellent and our server Alex was super attentive with our table, often coming over to check on us and making sure that everything is well. Food itself was all so very delicious! The porthouse steak in particular is well worth the price and big enough to share with the whole table. I also really enjoyed the mac and cheese. Highly recommended if you are in the area!

OMG! This is a must. We are there on Christmas day. It was busy as hell. The restaurant is cozy yet spacious.
Our food took a minute but worth the wait. Steak was perfect, shareable were flavorful, drinks were perfect. The Chinese food was amazing with a good portion. Fried rice was not salty and just right did not need additional seasoning.  I loved my meal. Yes, thd food was pricey but damn it was worth every penny!!!

Went to Brooklyn Chop House for the first time with some friends and honestly had a great time. We shared the steak, dumplings, and a few sides. The steak was really good and cooked just the way we liked it. The dumplings were also a favorite at our table, and the portions were pretty big.

It was busy when we went, but the atmosphere was fun. Our server was nice and checked on us during the meal. The prices are definitely not cheap, but we enjoyed everything and left happy. I’d definitely come back and try some of the other dishes next time.

Loved the decor and the ambiance. Service was med. Waited way too long to get our food and two ppl forgot when I asked for a straw. The drink was great, the asparagus that I got were probably the best I’ve had but my steak was just ok

top_reviews.content:
Ay Papa Que Rico is a fantastic Cuban inspired charbroiled chicken restaurant.

Had a craving for Cuban food after a recent rewatch of the movie, Chef. Stopped here for the first time and had to try the chicken based on the delicious smell as well as a Cubano.

Both were mouthwatering. The chicken was perfect and the black beans and yellow rice I got with it were great.
The Cubano was near perfection. I look forward to coming back and trying more of the menu

We tried Ay Papa Qué Rico and honestly, it was really good. We ordered the whole charcoal-grilled chicken, congri, yuca, a salad, and a jugo de maracuyá. Everything was flavorful and satisfying. The charbroiled chicken is definitely the star — juicy, well-seasoned, and cooked perfectly over charcoal.
The congri and yuca were solid comfort sides, and the passion fruit juice was refreshing and not overly sweet. For about $65, two of us ate well and still had leftovers to take home — easily enough food for three people.
The vibe is casual and relaxed. It feels like a neighborhood comfort spot with a mix of Cuban, Salvadorian, Guatemalan, and Mexican influences. It’s centered around the charbroiled chicken, but you can tell there’s a little bit of everything on the menu.
If I had to describe it, I’d say it’s comfort food — the kind of place you go when you’re hungry and want something satisfying. It’s definitely an upgrade from places like Pollo Loco. I’d go back.

I was persuaded to visit this location.  I was told they have a lot of options.
It is true. They had a bunch of selections.  Unfortunately, none of the food options we chose were actually decent. We ordered potato balls. Super cold inside like if it was just pulled out of the fridge. Asada quesadilla, cheese wasn't completely melted and I gotta admit, I thought my daughter was just not trying to finish her food, but it did not have a good taste. I don't know what it was. The pupusas were probably the only thing we finished. Anywho, I heard they have multiple locations.  I'll try a different one and see if it's any better.

Know for their chicken but I eat mostly veggies right now. The veggie wrap with spanish rice was okay. Definitely could be better but overall service was amazing and their pastries & ice cream looked incredible. Next time will try that. My friend had the chicken plate and loved it. They have a lot of sitting space and great art.

The grilled food tastes as good as the smell!
The chicken and the short ribs are both fantastic and will come back for more. The sausage has good flavors but was a bit dry.

On our arrival, the place was quite busy, felt almost chaotic as the maître d’ checked us in and at the same time barking his orders at his waiters to make sure service was moving. Our coats were checked and everything calmed down once we were seated. George our waiter was engaging, helpful with the menu, and patient with our slow pace.
Food recommends by George were great, tuna tartare was excellent to start with, highly recommend the lemon veal piccata, excellent.
The pasta dishes were excellent also.
Service did slow down after our mains were served as our waiter may have left for the evening, and the waiter who stepped in to help did not check on us to see how are meals were, hence the 4 stars on service.
Overall my family enjoyed the restaurant’s ambiance, food and service and we would definitely revisit again on our return to NYC.

What a wonderful night out! For the delicious food to the impeccable service to the amazing ambience, Harry Cipriani dekivwrs am unforgettable experience. Many thanks to Ricardo and Fabrizio for their generous hospitality.

Wonderful holiday lunch- One of those rare experiences where everything feels special. The food was delicious and what made it even better was the service by William, which was impeccable. He was attentive, warm and gracious. He made me feel welcomed and very well taken care of from start to finish. It is an elegant atmosphere and timeless cuisine. I will absolutely return as Harry Cipriani remains a New York classic which I highly recommend.

I love this place. It is such a classic atmosphere with exceptional service. Every bite was delicious. The caviar was perfection. I love their Bellini‘s and lemon cake. I had the spaghetti with Seabass and cherry tomatoes. It was so good. Everything here is so fresh and you never know who you’re going to see sitting next to you such a fabulous New York experience. .

Had date night at Cipriani, the pasta was cooked to perfection along with the sauce! The vanilla cake was the real star of the show it was the fluffiest creamy cake I’ve ever had. Staff was great and attentive from the moment we stepped out of the car throughout the night.

Cipriani is a classic/rich Italian cuisine - each city you visit worldwide, you have to check if they have it so you visit. I love their food and vibes. You should reserve in advance to avoid any waiting. Cipriani is a renowned Italian restaurant chain that offers classic and opulent cuisine. It is a must-visit destination for food enthusiasts and travelers alike. The restaurant’s ambiance and culinary offerings are exceptional, making it a popular choice for dining experiences. To ensure a seamless dining experience, it is advisable to make reservations in advance to avoid any potential wait times.

Iconic in all ways. I sat at their petite bar and had a perfect Negroni up, along with an incredible hamburger.
Elegant solitude. Good for the soul!

Harry’s Cipriani is timeless New York elegance at its finest. From the moment you step inside, you’re transported into a world of old-school glamour, impeccable service, and effortlessly refined Italian cuisine.

The room itself is stunning — crisp white linens, polished wood, and an energy that feels both sophisticated and warm. It’s the kind of place where power lunches, celebratory dinners, and long, memorable evenings all feel perfectly at home.

The food is consistently excellent. The classics are where Harry’s truly shines: the carpaccio is delicate and perfectly seasoned, the baked tagliolini with ham is rich and comforting, and the Bellini — their signature — is as iconic as ever. Every dish is prepared with precision, simplicity, and respect for tradition, allowing the quality of the ingredients to speak for itself.

Service is polished, professional, and quietly attentive. The staff moves with confidence and grace, anticipating needs without ever being intrusive. It’s the kind of hospitality that feels increasingly rare and incredibly refreshing.

Harry’s Cipriani isn’t about trends or flash — it’s about consistency, elegance, and doing things the right way, every time. Whether for a business lunch, special occasion, or classic New York night out, it delivers an experience that feels both luxurious and familiar.

A true New York institution that never disappoints.

I first came to this place 6 years ago and remember it fondly. My options and time for food where limited at the time, and having this place felt so abundant and delicious. The food is pretty dang good, especially if you go for your favorites once you find them, and they're not trying to be gourmet or transcendent.. it's an AYCE buffet. You pay your chunk of money, around 28 bucks, and you eat as much as you want... Simple... I gravitate towards their sushi, chicken wings, fried shrimp, and surprisingly good barbecue ribs.. the pork buns have always been on par with a good quality home steamed version too. Some of the stuffed clams and creations often end up being favorites too, but that changes every visit. If you want buffet desserts following your savory meal, this is not the one, there's a few mid to bad cake squares and such. I think this place is worth your time and money if you are really hungry and craving some simple, good food from the cuisines they offer. I give it 5 stars because they're doing exactly what they're trying to do.. offer a big selection of decent foods and as much as you want of it.
Very busy buffet. Long food line food was good. Sushi was good. Not cheap but drinks are with the price of the buffet. Went on a Sunday was $24.95. The place was packed.

top_reviews.content: We got the Moroccan Benedict, Moroccan Eggs, and a mezze with pita & hummus and they were delectable. The Moroccan Benedict and these crispy potato wedges that were golden and cooked to perfection. The Moroccan Eggs were poaches so well and when we cut through the egg the yolk oozed out so perfectly. Had a great time! The outside seating was shaded and comfortable.

A business associate took me here for lunch and I  have been dying to go back ever since. I was pressed for time and only had a chance to try one menu item. I was thoroughly impressed with the quality the dish. The menu description of the Bastilla sounded like something worth checking out and I have no regrets. The flavors and textures inside this pastry were unforgettable. The filling was savory and delicious; slow cooked, Moroccan spiced chicken paired with sweet raisins & crunchy almonds. The pastry was served with a side of chick peas cooked in their signature Casablanca sauce. I wish this was available to buy because I'd put it on everything. The order included a side salad that was better than average. Unfortunately this was a quick visit but all I can say is I can't wait to go back and try more. A must try for anyone who loves this type of cuisine

Love, love, love the food here! Such a great spot for brunch with a variety of options. Super busy on weekends - definitely make a reservation and expect noise level to be a bit high. Waitstaff is super sweet. Overall a reliable spot in Williamsburg.

I had the Eggs Benedict and it was absolutely delicious. My friend ordered a halloumi dish, which was also very good. The mimosa was excellent as well, and the prices were reasonable for the quality of the food and overall experience.
The only issue was that although we had a reservation for three people, we were seated at a table for two because our third guest had not arrived yet. I don’t think that was the right approach and it felt a bit disappointing.
Other than that, everything was great. The food, drinks, and atmosphere were all enjoyable. I would definitely come back.

More like a 3.5, nothing too special but the food was well seasoned, tasty, and satisfying. Would recommend the Kefta Kebab. Service is friendly and timely. Ambiance is dark and a little loud, but nice overall. However, definitely places I’d recommend over here in the East Village.

top_reviews.content:
Cozy German Spot with Great Food! 🇩🇪🥨

If you’re looking for authentic German comfort food in a cozy atmosphere, this place is definitely worth a visit. The restaurant has a charming old-school German lodge vibe, and the staff dressed in traditional attire make the experience even more special.

We ordered many dishes : the Giant Pretzel, Steak Tartare, Wurst Plate, Sirloin Steak, Broiled Filet of Salmon, Breaded Pork Chops, along with a few side dishes. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and cooked perfectly. The portions were generous, and the prices were very reasonable for the quality and quantity.

The warm atmosphere, delicious food, and friendly service made for a wonderful dining experience. We’ll definitely be coming back!

What a great place! The atmosphere is lively and festive during our visit, and the staff couldn't have been sweeter. You really can't go wrong with their giant pretzel paired with three fantastic dipping sauces, and having Warsteiner on draft was phenomenal. It's super family-friendly, too—my kids had an absolute blast. Cant wait to return!

lecker!

i have been to this restaurant with my family multiple times for many occasions and it’s always fabulous. you will love the atmosphere. the food is always great. I enjoy the chicken schnitzel and the goulash. Some of my favorite side dishes are the red cabbage and the creamed spinach. It doesn’t matter when you go, you will enjoy whatever you order (for food or drink) and you will leave full and happy. This German restaurant feels like you are having dinner at your favorite German relatives home.

It was the first time I was in this restaurant. And I liked everything, perhaps because I have European roots and this kind of food is familiar to me. Or maybe because I didn’t try these particular dishes in the original in Germany. But I want to say that the service was very fast, the waitress was friendly and the food was fresh. I also drank dark beer, tried Pilsner and liked both varieties. I would also like to point out Schnapps, it is very weak in terms of alcohol, so feel free to order in addition to food.
Auf Wiedersehen und alles Gute!

Food was great, short wait with fantastic service, and an unforgettable atmosphere! Warm bread, fresh soft pretzel with great mustards and dipping sauce, phenomenal Roast Duck with mashed potatoes and red cabbage. Fantastic experience and would highly recommend this authentic German experience and food! Valentine's Day evening and a packed restaurant by we were well taken care of by our attentive and kind waitress!!
Everything is so good! Go on Saturday to get the duck special, it's the most tender you'll ever have. My Chinese family all loved it!

The food is absolutely stellar. One of my favorite German restaurants. From the authentic layout to the service. All of it is top notch. I recommend this German restaurant to anyone. One of the last bastions of an old German establishment. My favorite is the pork shank or beef rib with horseradish sauce on the Friday specials. 👏👏

had an outstanding lunch today at Zum Stammtisch, and it exceeded every expectation. From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere felt warm, authentic, and welcoming—exactly what you’d hope for in a traditional German restaurant.

The highlight of my meal was the steak, which was cooked to perfection—tender, flavorful, and beautifully presented. Every bite reflected quality and attention to detail. The portions were generous, and the sides complemented the dish perfectly, creating a well-balanced and satisfying meal.

The service was equally impressive—attentive, friendly, and genuinely hospitable without being overbearing. You can tell the staff takes pride in making sure every guest has a great experience.

If you’re looking for authentic German cuisine in Queens, this place is a must-visit. I’ll absolutely be coming back.

top_reviews.content:
I’ve been to Miss Ada a couple of times already and finally leaving a review. The main dining room is quite small, so I recommend the heated patio in the back. It’s pretty warm, more spacious, and a great place to sit.

The food is always delicious. The dips and hummus are fantastic, and the pita bread is soft and cut into smaller slices which makes it easy to share. The bluefin tuna crudo special this time was especially good.

This visit everything tasted a little saltier than we remembered from previous visits, but overall it was still a great meal. Service has always been consistent and fantastic.

Definitely worth being a neighborhood favorite and we’ll keep coming back.

The Hummus with shortrib takes the prize!

Quick rank of the food I tried here:
1. Shortrib hummus - Super creamy and full of flavor!
2. Branzino - perfectly cooked with enough lemon and herbacious flavors to keep it interesting
3. Beef Kofta - wrapped around a cinnamon stick! Tender and fresh!
4. Red Snapper Ceviche - delicious and refreshing but a small portion
5. Stracciatella - home made cheese was delicious
6. Half baked chicken - interesting burning sauce
7. muhammara - I am typically very interested in this, but it was a little too sour for my looking.

Miss Ada is an absolute gem! Every single thing we ordered was delicious. You can’t go wrong with any of the skewers, although the salmon belly and kofte skewer deserve a special shout out. Order all the dips, I can’t choose a favorite. The whipped ricotta and sweet potato hummus were amazing. Their dumplings Stracciatella is to die for. Don’t skip dessert! And their cocktails are not to be missed. The space is cozy and the service is great. Miss Ada is special, can’t wait to go back!

Excellent pita and desserts! Loved the steak and salad here. Each of the dips were excellent but I especially liked the hot pita.

Great choices of tapas style and sized meats. Excellent wine selection as well.

I honestly wish I could give the service a 6/5, but I will make do with what I got! My fiance and I came here on NYE to do the pre-set menu of house favorites. The place was decorated so cute and they had little party favors everywhere for NYE. When we arrived, we got seated at the bar even though we made a reservation at the back patio on Resy. When I let the manager know, she was so apologetic about the Resy app incorrectly placing guests into the wrong areas of the restaurant and asked us if she could purchase our first round of drinks to make up for it. No problem! So we are eating dinner at the bar and she kept coming up to us after we were done with the cocktails offering us wine, refills, and even a great dessert wine that the bartender recommended with the babka. When I tell you this is some of the best food AND service i’ve ever experienced- what an incredible way to end 2025!!! At the end we expected to pay for the drinks completely and were told they were all on the house. Shocked and on cloud 9, beyond full, we left the restaurant so happy and a little tipsy.

As for the food, obsessed with the hummus and ricotta cheese, as well as the kofta was the best I’ve ever had. Babka was amazing and everything else was so yummy, my fiance never had Israeli food before and was cautiously optimistic going into the dinner I chose, and left saying that was his favorite meal from our NYC trip! Thank you so much to the team of Miss Ada!! highly highly recommend!!!!

We ordered whipped ricotta, sweet potato hummus, chicken shawarma, red snapper ceviche, winter greens salad, crispy cauliflower, short rib skewer, whole branzino, and chocolate babka for four people. The dishes were small and just enough for each person to get a few bites. Everything was packed with flavors and the complimentary pita was warm and fluffy. I’ve been wanting to come here for a long time and Miss Ada stood up to its fame!

Miss Ada is the best date night dinner spot on Dekalb. Will you be able to get a reservation? Maybe. Can you walk in at 5 PM on the dot and get bar seating? Yes!

You have to get the short rib hummus. A must, must, must! The halloumi is a strong second. The branzino in third place. Other notables to share with the table—octopus skewer or their sometimes season beef skewers, the hanger steak and za’atar crusted salmon (this is definitely on the smaller size).

I often dream of their short rib hummus, and when you have it, you’ll start dreaming too.

This place is a dream if you have dietary restrictions because almost everything is GF, and there are dishes for those who are DF, Vegetarian or Vegan. The staff is also super kind. On busier nights, there might be a bit of a wait between dishes so be sure to get at least one app to hold you over. Again, this place is great for date night, don’t try to bring a party of six—she’s a little tight inside.

Highly recommend if you’re in Fort Greene!

I don't usually go to the hyped up restaurants but I indulged my friend this one time since I love Mediterranean food. We sat in the backyard patio which is really not at all a backyard; it's basically an extension of inside with more natural light, it's fully covered. We had to flag down a server to get our order in, which is weird because they refilled our water bottle about seven times during our stay so I don't understand the disconnect between the two. We got our food before we got our cocktails, which is odd, but fine. The mezcal cocktail was okay, nothing special but mezcal is so strong of a flavor it's really hard to mess up. (We unfortunately didn't have time to try another round of cocktails just because the first ones took so long to arrive.) Food wise, the babaghanoush was a miss, but it was the first thing brought to our table: overly pureed to the consistency of babyfood, couldnt taste the eggplant, couldn't taste the smokiness that it's known for either, it was basically just an indescript brown spread. The halloumi skewer was phenomenal though. The stracciatella toast was good but lacked cohesion... It was a mess to try to eat and the asparagus seemed so out of place, a roasted marinated tomato would have brought it together much better. The sourdough was very good though and luckily quite thick bc it got super soggy by the time we got to eating the last slice. Would not recommend this spot. The area is oversaturated with restaurants and this isn't one where the service or offerings warrant spending the $$$.

top_reviews.content:
First time to Anju House it very much has an "house" feel with cute and chill décor with in and out seating.  I went there around 6pm and did not have an issue finding street parking, but I could see it being an issue later in the night.  When I initially entered in, there was no one at the front desk so I waited....and waited...and waited.  After about 10 minutes, I walked into restaurant and found a server.  He said that when it's not busy, no one really mans the front desk.  I guess customers are supposed to just know to walk into the back.  Very strange.  As for the menu, I was very happy with the food options.  It had so many things that I liked or sounded interesting.  What wasn't happy were the prices.  The prices are high considering portion size.  Like really high.  The prices for the "Small Anju" dishes seem reasonable, until you see the portion size.  The "Big Anju" are regular sized dishes that are very expensive.  Like, how do these young people ( a definite younger crowd that comes in later in the night) afford to eat out at places like this?  Order one or two dishes and share?

I ordered the Spicy Seafood Udon, Spicy Korean Fried Chicken, and the Fried Rice Cakes and Sausage.  The Spicy Seafood Udon was good, but nothing unique.  The Spicy Korean Fried Chicken was very well seasoned and tasty.  The Fried Rice Cakes and Sausage was just okay.  I felt that it needed more sauce and have had much better at other places.  I would be interested in trying some of the other dishes, but considering the prices, I would hesitate to come back.  The food wasn't extraordinary enough for me to ignore the prices.

Overall, I wouldn't be opposed to going back, but not my first option.

They say that Anju House serves serves Korean bar food with beer, soju, and cocktails, but it is so much more. They have some of the best Korean food and I swear some of it reminds me of Italian food. You can get small bites, order a bunch of stuff and share or order a full meal. It is all great. There is nothing not to like and you will be happy.

The service is great. They are kind and will explain the menu to you. They get your order right and are all smiles. Now, it can get very crowded at night and I don't know if they take reservations so call and find out. We have been several times and have done take away a few times when it is crowded. Either way, you will get great service and be happy.

The place is super clean and really pretty. It is very comfortable. They have a full bar and Anju refers to food that is consumed with alcohol, but we have never had a drink there.

It is a tad pricey, but the food is worth it always. We love their calamari and their noodles and any shrimp dish is the best. They have things I had never tried before. Just ask the server and you will be guided.

This was our first time here and it won't be our last. This restaurant was a house that was converted into a restaurant. The restaurant is in the backyard and it feels like you are at a backyard cook out with tour friends.  We saw people eating and then playing cards just having a good time. This place really is a vibe. RSVP because its a long wait. The service is slow, but the bus boys help out alot. We felt like the bus boys do most of the work. They really should promote the bus boys because they are doing everything the waiters should be doing except taking orders. We live an hour away and the food was worth the drive. The valet messed up my car and didn't say anything.

It was my first time, and I was totally 100% disappointed with the service. The service was horrible. The servers did not even let us know how we could order the food. You actually have to scan the barcode to see the online menu, but we didn’t know that because nobody told us. So we were sitting there for like 10 minutes doing nothing.

After that, there were no recommendations about the food. After like 20 minutes, the server came and asked if we were ready to order anything. I said, “I have no idea,” and he said, “ok,” and just left. This is the worst, most horrible service that I have ever had so far in my whole life. Thank you.

Tried Anju House and was really impressed!

Furikake Fried Chicken (5/5) – Wow. Boneless, super savory, perfectly crispy on the outside and juicy inside. Even the pickled radishes on the side were tasty.

Animal Fries (4/5) – Fries were perfectly cooked with just the right amount of sauce—flavorful without being too heavy.

Cracked Corn (4.5/5) – Nice and crispy, almost like a fun twist on Mexican street corn.

Ambiance: Great spot for dates, groups, or just hanging out—chill and stylish vibe.

Service (3/5): Staff were friendly and checked in often, though one dish came out about 20 minutes late and servers seemed a bit distracted at times.

Overall, would definitely recommend and would happily go back!

Being around this area you expect late night food after walking all day at Universal and avoiding bad food at the Hilton . WHAT A GEM 💎  THIS PLACE IS !!!!!! ( sᴏʀʀʏ ғᴏʀ ᴛʜᴇ sᴄʀᴇᴀᴍɪɴɢ) like an oasis in the middle of the desert accompanied with friendly service and meals out straight from heaven. Forgot to mention …. Don’t skip the cocktails

Came here with a big group of 10 adults plus a baby and honestly anju absolutely delivered. We were looking for a fun Koreatown spot for large groups, family-style Korean food, drinks, and a place where everyone could actually relax and enjoy themselves without feeling rushed. Found Anju while searching for best group dinner spots in Koreatown Los Angeles and now I completely understand the hype.

First off, making the reservation was incredibly easy. Being able to book a large party online without having to jump through hoops was a huge plus. When we arrived, we got seated almost immediately, which for a large group in KTown on a busy night felt impressive.

Parking initially confused us a bit because of the plaza setup, but they offer valet and it ended up being super convenient and worth it.

The vibe here is awesome. It's technically an outdoor restaurant, but it still feels intimate and lively. Perfect energy for groups, celebrations, birthdays, catching up with friends, or just hanging out over Korean BBQ and soju.

Kyle was our server and genuinely made the night. Super attentive, very accommodating with our large party and baby, constantly checking in, pacing the meal well, and just brought great energy to the table all night. Service like that really changes the whole experience.

Food-wise, the marinated beef was phenomenal. Easily one of the standout dishes of the night. So flavorful, tender, and the kind of dish everyone keeps reaching back for. We also ordered an octopus and pork dish that completely blew me away. Probably one of my favorite bites I've had in LA in a while.

The asado-style platter wasn't my personal favorite compared to the marinated meats, but it still came with a generous amount and was great for sharing with a large table.

We ordered a ton of food, beers, soju, shared plates, and left absolutely stuffed. Considering the amount of food, drinks, and the size of our party, we all felt like the value was really solid.

Dessert is definitely more simple and traditional, so don't come expecting some massive dessert menu, but honestly the focus here is the food, drinks, atmosphere, and group dining experience.

Overall, this is one of the best large group restaurants in Koreatown if you want great Korean food, strong service, fun social atmosphere, and a place that actually handles big parties well. Will absolutely be back.

This was a great find. We had originally planned to go somewhere else but they weren't able to accommodate a vegetarian. We ended up coming to Anju House and are so happy we did.

The portions are big and for the price I think it's very reasonable. The food was well spiced and tasted good. The atmosphere was also very nice especially the outdoor patio area. It looks like it would be a fun spot to come at night and would definitely be more lively.

Service was also quick and we didn't have to wait too long for our food to come out.

top_reviews.content: An amazing little place to stop to eat in Little Italy! While we did come at an odd time around 3 pm, I have to say the service was incredibly quick. Our appetizers came out right away after placing out order, the mozzarella sticks were absolutely amazing! I had the ravioli marinara and there was little wait to receive that as well. The sauce was perfect and the ravioli themselves came out great too! Theres also a nice painted mural on the walls of the resturant! Overall just a great place!

Overall, we really enjoyed our visit to Puglia.  It was surreal and very cool to be eating in a restaurant that opened in 1919 and the fact that we were in NYC's "Little Italy" made it even better.  The food was excellent.  Our server was great (we were a party of 8, but she took very good care of us).  We tried a bottle of the house white wine, and it was quite good (especially for the price...$16.50 for the whole bottle).  There was live entertainment (2 singers).  They were fine, but very loud.  Honestly, we were glad when they took their break.  Unfortunately, the air conditioning was not working when were were there, and this was early July, so we were pretty uncomfortable.  They had some fans going inside the dining room, but that helped only a little.  All of that aside, we would definitely come here again.  The food and service make a return visit totally worth it.

I just had my birthday dinner there a couple night ago and it was THE BEST EXPERIENCE I’ve had in this city in a while. The food was incredible, the staff was so friendly and the entertainment was so much fun!!!! We did the prefix menu and it was worth EVERY penny. I believe our waitresses name was Adriana (but if I’m wrong you can blame the delicious bottomless wine) she was an absolute sweetheart and took great care of us!

I don’t usually leave reviews, but this place was too good not to share. We walked right on in and were seated almost immediately. Food was good, and the garlic bread was amazing. I got the rigatoni and it was great. The fried zucchini was like French fries, and the portions were big. I recommend this as a good place to eat.

Loud fun great entertainment food was good
Went on a thursday night week after valentine’s day so it wasnt packed. This place def good for group dining.  Go for the experience
I didnt dare dance on the tables or chairs but it was fun to sing along.
Staff is very attentive w us. Loved it
Dinner: shared bruschetta, lasagna and chicken parm linguine (a lil surprised they didn’t give bread)
Drinks: Moscato wine and coffee
For dessert we shared chocolate cake w ice cream

If you want a restaurant experience that doubles as a full-blown party, Puglia is the spot! The festive, lively atmosphere with live music and crowd sing-alongs makes it impossible not to have a great time. Beyond the incredible energy, the food hits all the right notes for classic, rustic Italian comfort. The Chicken Parmigiana was huge and perfectly cheesy, and the family-style pasta dishes were fantastic for sharing with a big group. Perfect for birthdays, large gatherings, or just a night where you want to sing, laugh, and eat great food.

This is a fantastic restaurant! Went to Puglia's on Sunday January 18th for an early 5pm dinner with a group of 18 people. Made reservations about 6 weeks in advance. When we walked in 15 minutes early at 4:45 our tables were ready and the staff kindly welcomed us and sat us! Truly nice, efficient, and smart people are working there! (BTW - a little tip...eating before restaurants typically get busy can make life a lot easier if you have a group. It also means restaurants might be able to seat you a little early if you show up on a cold and snowy day like we did.)
We all enjoyed an amazing meal! We loved the garlic bread, salad, chicken marsala, chicken parm, and baked rigatoni that we had! I would go back to this restaurant in a minute if I didn't live in Miami! And next time I am in NYC I am going back!!
This place has been around for 107 years! That tells you they've been doing this right for a very long time!

Absolutely a must go! The food was fantastic and the staff was amazing! The ambiance is so much fun! They start dancing and singing live around 7pm every night. Don’t waste time reading too many reviews, just go and have the experience, it’s worth it.

top_reviews.content:
Stopped by The Cottage for brunch with a group of five.

We went right when they opened, so there was plenty of seating, but the space filled up quickly.

The food was amazing, and the prices felt very reasonable for the area. The waitress kept our coffee cups full, so no complaints there.

Great spot if you’re looking for a traditional Irish breakfast in the heart of Queens.

I really wanted to love this place. The decoration and atmosphere are homey. The waitresses have been nice. The bangers and mash were good last time I went. But I've been here 3 times and really expected this to be a regular place for me. But I brought a new friend here and she didn't have a good experience.

We both ordered the brunch special and shared an appetizer. After bringing us our Mimosa and soda bread, a few minutes later we were told they were out of broccoli quiche and only had ham quiche. My friend didn't want ham so she changed to the mini sheapards pie.

The food was ok, her sheapards pie was ok, French onion soup was ok, my ham quiche wasn't good. It was greasy, over cooked, no flavor, I only had a few bites.

When the bill came my friend was charged 9.35 for her small mimosa. I asked for it to be taken off the bill because it wasn't our fault they didn't have the brunch item she ordered and she didn't want ham. The manager told our waitress no, that my friend changed her mind and didn't get the brunch so now she has to pay full price for the mimosa (but they didn't charge for her soda bread).

This should have been handled differently. They could have given her a discount, brunch, happy hour price.  We never would have paid 9.35 for a mimosa and we do get them a lot at other brunch places. Or it should have been mentioned when she had to change her order that since they already brought her drink and bread so she should chose another brunch item or would be charged for the drink.

So we left feeling slighted, had to make an effort to forget it and have a nice day. But we were both annoyed. The Manager should have compromised since it wasn't our idea to get drinks first then change her order.

My friend will never go back and I'm bummed, I wanted to like the place so bad. We spent $88 on brunch for two and are always good, polite customers that take and post pics and always tip minimum 20 percent.
We were outside. The light and quiet music are so good. The service personnel are very nice and polite. I liked food and enjoy the atmosphere.

Classic Irish pub and a neighborhood staple, with a homey atmosphere, great service and solidly delicious pub standards. We had the beef sliders, mini shepherds pie, onion rings and buffalo wings- all served quickly and with excellent service. We came on a night that was absolutely slammed due to a concert in Forest Hills Stadium being cancelled. The servers here handled the rush with grace and speed, and kept everyone happy with attentive service.

Large portion sizes for the price.
Love the pub atmosphere and decor is very cute.
Servers didn't go above and beyond. Cordial but they don't come by to refill your water when it runs low.
