top_reviews.content:
This was our first time visiting with the whole family, and we had a wonderful experience!

The restaurant’s lemon-themed décor creates a bright, fresh, and welcoming atmosphere that immediately makes you feel comfortable. The menu offers so many tempting choices that we honestly wanted to try everything.

Our family loves Thai food, and we’ve been to many Thai restaurants over the years, but this one really stood out. Although the wait for a table was a bit long, the food arrived surprisingly quickly once we were seated.

What impressed us most was the quality of the flavors. Many restaurants rely too heavily on MSG, leaving you thirsty and reaching for water afterward. Here, the seasoning was perfectly balanced and tasted natural, allowing the freshness and authenticity of the ingredients to shine through. You can tell the chef puts great care into every dish.

Everything we ordered was delicious, and the overall dining experience exceeded our expectations. Highly recommended for anyone who enjoys Thai cuisine. We’ll definitely be back to explore more dishes on the menu!

Went to lemongrass Brooklyn for dinner with my friend and we had a such good time! I loved the whole vibe, especially all the flowers and lemon decor. We got the pineapple fried rice, calamari, and a couple appetizers to share. Everything came out looking so good and the portions were definitely enough for us. But the pineapple 🍍 drink was my favorite part 😂 it was huge and so pretty. Such a cute dinner spot in Brooklyn, especially if you’re going with girls 🤍

I had such a great lunch at Lemongrass Brooklyn. The space is beautifully decorated and has a fun atmosphere, but it still feels relaxed and comfortable. I went during the week at lunchtime and loved how calm it was while still having a nice energy.

The food completely exceeded my expectations. I ordered the Pad Thai and really appreciated that I could make it both vegan and gluten-free, which isn't always easy to find. It was absolutely delicious. I also had the alcohol-free watermelon margarita, which was so refreshing and flavorful.

As someone who loves photography, I couldn't help but notice how beautiful the presentation was. Everything that came to the table was colorful, vibrant, and thoughtfully plated. On top of that, the staff was incredibly kind and helped us decide what to order. Overall, such a lovely experience and definitely a place I'd love to come back to.

Ps. The caramelized bananas dessert is a must!!!

2 times here the food and service are consistently excellent. I had fried jumbo shrimp and spicy coconut soup as appetizer. Main entree I had tried the duck ramen and pineapple fried rice. The ramen and the soup are bit on the salty side, good if you get a cocktails/beer to balance it out. Great variety of cocktails as well. This place is a must try.

Had dinner at Lemongrass on Court St in Brooklyn with my little one. Ordered the crab fried rice—on its own it was nothing special, but once I mixed it with the sauce on the side, the flavor really came through. What worked well for me as a parent: I could scoop out a plain portion for my kid first, then mix the sauce into the rest. One dish, two ways.

The clam soup was quite savory, no fishy taste, and the clams were tender. The broth had that Thai-style sourness that wakes up your appetite. The shrimp the server brought out was crispy with a creamy sweet glaze—enjoyable to eat. The short rib was tender and well seasoned. Also tried two non-alcoholic drinks—the mulberry one leaned more fruity and tart, while the rose one had a noticeable floral aroma. Neither was overly sweet; both were refreshing. Overall a comfortable meal, the kind of place I'd go back to.

It really does not get better than this. Came on a Saturday night with my girlfriends at 9pm (prior reservation) and had a blast. The service was great, served came by plenty of times to refill our water. The sushi was amazing!!!

The live show by this magnificent trio deserves all the accolades in the world. I have not seen any other restaurant where people got up from their tables to dance to each song. This place is perfect for birthday celebrations or any kind of milestone celebration.

The staff will come and sing happy birthday to you as well. Pretty impeccable ambience.

Sushi rolls range from $14-$20 and it comes with 8 pieces each. Great deal.

This place is beautiful awesome playlist. The burger and fries very solid, the el mensajero drink was excellent, I had some toast with ricotta, honey and almonds that was really good as well. It's my first time coming to Aura Cocina for valentines. I has a wonderful time. The live band was awesome. Give the atmosphere a extra kick. The food was also delicious. The staff was very friendly and awesome.

First time here was this last Saturday 5/23, my fiancée and I had an amazing time, the place is big enough to enjoy an amazing dinner, our waiter Jose was amazing, attentive we had the hibiscus margarita, and coquita matcha drink, for dinner the Peking chicken with yuca mash, she had the skirt steak, both so good filling, side of amazing truffle fries, Maria Raquel and her band uplifted the evening with her salsa singing, best part no matter where you sit you have an amazing view of the stage, most places you have to pay an arm leg, but not at aura and this is why we will most definitely return, many blessings to the owner and staff at Aura we will be back for sure.

top_reviews.content:
Stopped in for a quick meal and was pleasantly surprised. The bowls were fresh, filling, and nicely balanced — the grilled salmon was cooked well, and the katsu had a good crunch without being overly greasy. The miso soup was a solid bonus and hit the spot.

Ordering was straightforward, portions were generous, and everything came out quickly. The space is casual and clean, more of a fast-casual setup than a sit-down sushi spot, which works well for lunch or an easy dinner.

Knocking off one star only because presentation and flavors, while good, didn’t quite hit “wow” territory — but still very solid overall. I’d definitely come back when I’m in the area and want something reliable and satisfying.

It's a cafeteria vibe. I came with my BFF and ordered a veggie tempura 🍤 and a katsu roll. Great price, I just wish the tempura had more of a crunch than a soft feel. Free miso soup just add it to your order

Absolutely loved my experience at Roll Roll Roll on Wilshire! It's not easy finding high-quality halal sushi, but this place exceeded all expectations. The fish was incredibly fresh, the rolls were creative and packed with flavor, and everything was beautifully presented.
The staff was friendly, welcoming, and attentive, making the whole dining experience even better. I also really appreciate having a halal-friendly sushi option that doesn't compromise on quality or taste. Whether you're a sushi lover or trying it for the first time, this spot is definitely worth visiting.
Highly recommend the specialty rolls and will definitely be coming back soon!

We went there for a family dine in on a Friday night. The staff and service were amazing. Very welcoming and friendly. The owner personally welcomed us. The best part of the service was, they were so kid friendly.
We tried few different types of sushi.
Chef special, Mexican, crunching tiger, rainbow. All of them were spot on.
My personal favorite was the Chef special and crunching tiger.
Our daughter loved their chicken Katsu.
Would definitely go again.
Highly recommend.

Roll Roll Roll Sushi has only gotten better under the new management! The quality of the food is outstanding… fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. The service is just as impressive and the workers are very friendly and welcoming. It’s quickly become one of my favorite sushi spots, and I highly recommend giving it a try.

I’m honestly very grateful for this place. I used to live nearby and go to the gym next door, and after almost every workout I’d come here.

This is probably one of the best spots if you want something healthy, filling, and actually affordable. It’s rare to find food that’s this good and still cheap.

Their salmon bowl is my go-to — big portion, fresh, and super satisfying. You really feel like you’re getting great value for your money.

I respect whoever created this place — giving people access to quality food at a reasonable price is a big deal.

I recommend it to all my friends, and I think more people should know about it. Definitely worth trying.
I’m a loyal customer; I enjoy both dining at the restaurant and ordering online. The salmon and cream cheese sushi with eel sauce never disappoints. Tasty and affordable, just the way I like it.

Our favorite new sushi place, even though Uber ate our lunch that one time.

We can recommend the spicy tuna roll, the California roll, and cooked salmon roll.

Never any leftovers.  ♥️♥️

top_reviews.content:
Casa Enrique is good, but has dropped off a bit in terms of creative spark and meticulous service.

Most of what we ordered was tasty. It’s comforting and accessible, but it stops short of being truly outstanding or memorable. The Rajas con Crema gets an honorable mention for being the least liked and eaten dish. It felt like an afterthought in preparation, presentation, and flavor (on paper sounds delicious but in person it was like a bunch of random ingredients thrown together with no seasoning. It could be so much better if refined and tweaked).

While the portions were appropriate, our server could have guided us through the menu more efficiently (like not letting us order so much rice but silver lining more leftovers).

It’s a solid 3.5 star experience, but I wouldn't rush back or say it’s worth crossing boroughs for ($18 guac, $20 cocktails). This kitchen plays it very safe and unfortunately makes for a static meal. I hope they consider taking bigger risks with unique ingredients and bolder flavor profiles/textures.

Great spot! Came with a friend who’s been wanting to check them out. We went early and had a ressy so we were seated right away. They do have an outdoor patio which is nice for the warmer months.

They have lots of cocktail options, too many to choose from but we really liked the ones we got, the Aguachile margarita and Jamaica margarita. Very unique!

We started with the Aguachile de camarón that was extremely delicious! Highly recommend getting it. Has a little kick but nothing crazy. We then got an order of the lengua and pastor tacos and shared. Both were delicious but I think I liked the lengua more.

Really great spot!

had high expectations since i have heard great things about this place and also know of their past michelin star. we came for brunch and tried a few items: complementary chicharron with sauce (addictive), guac (must get), chilaquiles red & green (i preferred the green but red was tastier), french toast, huevos con chorizo (enjoyed the beans the most), and tacos.

My friends and I were excited to finally try Casa Enrique after hearing so much about it and seeing it recognized in the Michelin Guide. Unfortunately, the experience didn’t quite live up to our expectations.

The food was good, but nothing really stood out as memorable. I ordered the pork shoulder special, which I enjoyed, but it wasn’t a dish that would make me rush back. One of my friends ordered a soup dish and was particularly disappointed with it.

The atmosphere was probably the biggest challenge for us. We were seated in a corner at the end of the dining room, and despite the restaurant not being especially crowded, the music was very loud. It was difficult to have a conversation at our table and even hard to hear the staff at times. The seating also felt quite tight, and we noticed the guests seated next to us struggling to get in and out of their seats comfortably.

Service was another area that could be improved. While I didn’t personally have any major issues, several people in our group felt that some interactions came across as rushed and somewhat unfriendly, as if the staff were exhausted and didn’t really want to be there.

Overall, the meal was decent, but given the reputation and expectations surrounding the restaurant, we left feeling underwhelmed. It’s not a bad restaurant by any means, but it didn’t deliver the experience we were hoping for.

This restaurant is a gem located in Long Island City, and it was a short train ride from Manhattan. Our server from last night, Marcelo, was super friendly and attentive ( 🌟 )!  The food was homey yet classy with bold flavor and just the right amount of spices.  We had Sopecitos de Chirozo (well seasoned and earthy) Cocktails de Camarones (fresh and zesty), Pozele de Mi Tia (deep and savory), Chille Relleno (rich and creamy) and their roasted pork shoulder special (moist and soft). For desserts, their cheese ice cream blended with rich milk and a mild cheese tang was a delight to our palette, and their Tres Lèche cake was moist and creamy melted in our mouth.  Last but not the least, their cocktails were fresh and delicious! They also have a decent selection or wine.  We will definitely come back!

Excellent service from the moment I arrived for our reservation of five people. I was warmly greeted by someone who seemed to be the manager, and almost immediately another staff member, who I believe was the host, approached me. Both were very friendly and welcoming, almost like a family style atmosphere. They asked if I wanted to be seated right away, but I declined since I wasn’t sure how long the rest of my family would take to arrive.
Once we were seated, everything went very smoothly. The food felt very traditional and authentic. The drinks were good, although they could use a bit more “buzz” or strength.
Our table was located right in front of the restroom, and I think it would be a good idea to place a curtain or divider there, since it feels a bit too direct every time someone goes in or out.
We ordered dessert because it was my daughter’s birthday, and the staff came over to sing “Happy Birthday,” which was a very nice touch.
One thing I really want to highlight: when I received the check, the server had circled that the gratuity was already included. I truly appreciated that, because I’ve been to places where gratuity is included but not clearly mentioned, and the bill still suggests adding 20%, which can lead to tipping twice. That honest gesture from the server actually made me want to leave an additional tip.
Would I come back? Absolutely!!! 😀

Food was AWESOME! Everything tastes homemade and packed with tons of flavors and spice. We had the special shrimp ceviche, the enchiladas, branzino, the cheese ice cream was out of this world and the tres leches was the best. Cocktails were delicious and made with fresh juices not that sugary bottled stuff. Can’t wait to return, I highly recommend.

The food is absolutely delicious! The suadero taco was splendid. The tender beef and the crunch of the refreshing radish and carrot slices contrast very nicely. The cochinito chiapaneco were well-balanced with the beans and rice, the ribs themselves were spicy with a touch of salt. For desert, we had the pastel tres leches, the cake itself was super moist and absorbed the condensed milk at the bottom , creating a sponge effect in your mouth. Overall, the experience was very great.

top_reviews.content:
Had a great meal! Katrina the dining room manager and her family (many of which are there on site) provided awesome hospitality for a wonderful culinary experience.

I would definitely return and recommend it to anybody hungry for some great Italian food anywhere in the San Fernando Valley area. The restaurant is definitely casual and friendly. You can tell straight away they have a following of regular local guests. And after eating there I can see why they do.

Definitely worth the drive if not close by. They do have parking on-site. It fills up fast. To supplement the lot there is street parking with an easy walk both metered and non-metered.

I recently discovered Gio Cucina Napoletana in Encino and I can confidently say this is a true hidden gem.

This is a family-owned Italian restaurant where everything is made the right way — house-made pasta and sauces prepared fresh daily. You can genuinely taste the difference. The texture of the pasta, the balance of the sauces, and the overall craftsmanship stand out immediately.

We started with warm bread and olive tapenade, which set the tone beautifully. I had the Olmo’s Pappardelle (named after LA legend Edward James Olmos), and also tried their whole wheat fettuccine — both were fresh, well-balanced, and thoughtfully prepared.

To finish, I had their sorbet, which was light and refreshing — the perfect ending.

I also appreciate that they offer gluten-free noodles and vegan-friendly options, which makes the experience inclusive without sacrificing quality.

Whether you’re planning a date night, birthday dinner, or just looking to support a restaurant that truly cares about what they serve, Gio Cucina Napoletana is worth visiting.

Encino is lucky to have this spot.

Chef Roberto keeping me safe with my Celiac disease.
The sand dabs, vegetables and potatoes were delicious and all was good with my health afterwards.  🙂. It is so wonderful to go to a restaurant and to relax knowing that I will not get ill with gluten.

We also would like to commend waiter, Miriam.  She was so professional, mature, and especially kind to our woman friend who dined with us.  Our friend is going through a very diffiult time in her life and is not quite herself just now.
Miriam seemed to sense that she needed extra patience and kindness and calmness.  Miriam was fabulous in dealing with her always treating her with respect as well.

We have dined here for 25 years as well as taking cooking classes.  Chef Roberto and his staff dish up some fabulous Italian food with warmth and caring.  You will not be disappointed.

In the restaurant it felt so welcoming, the food was so amazing and I was shocked how much I enjoyed the pumpkin ravioli because I'm not really a pumpkin fan! What  impressed me was how caramelized the chicken ravioli was because I honestly couldn't tell if it was chicken! I would definitely come back here again and try their other services like the wine tasting!
Amazing homemade pasta. The chef is absolutely wonderful, service is incredible! Don’t miss out!

The food is very solid to great. The little gem and blackout cake were very good, the mortadella was great, and the cheeseburger is low key one of the better in NYC. The cocktail program is making some very tasty gems as well.
Had a wonderful brunch at Ingas Bar. The standouts were the morel toast, chilaquiles and cinnamon roll. The vibes were fun and our server Cassidy was lovely. Very much recommend!

An unforgettable experience.
From the warm welcome to the thoughtful birthday touches, everything felt genuine and full of care.
The team and the restaurant owners truly made me feel special.
The meal was exquisite, the halibut with parsnip purée and lobster reduction was perfectly balanced, and the onion soup to start was comforting and flavorful.
The dessert was the perfect ending, gently confirming the sweetness of the entire experience.
A place with heart, and I will definitely be back

They accommodated our walk in party of 4 around 6pm on a Saturday and told us we had an hour and 45 before their reservation (plenty of time!) even gave us their “favorite table” in the house. Buzzy, great music, and overall vibe. Highly recommend!

Dinner at Ingas Bar was lovely! It wasn't perfect, but I loved the coziness of the restaurant and food was overall fantastic. It will definitely be a go to spot in our neighborhood.

The good: gem salad, octopus, burger, and the poached pear dessert (which I think might be a seasonal item). The octopus was amazing - it may have been my favorite octopus dish I've ever tried.

Not the best: the roasted chicken was too salty for me. I would skip this item. Service wasn't bad but it wasn't the best. It was fast/efficient but the way our server put down our starters felt off (like I wasn't sure if they wanted me to take the plate from their hands or if they were going to put it down) and they seemed kind of annoyed. It was a packed and busy restaurant so I get it.

Title: Google Maps Review
We had a nice experience here. Making a reservation was easy, and even though we arrived a little early, they were able to seat us inside. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, and the staff was friendly and attentive.

The food was good overall, but honestly, nothing “wow” or particularly memorable. Still, we enjoyed our visit and would come back for the atmosphere and service.
4/5 — a pleasant experience with good service and a cozy atmosphere, although the food could be more impressive.

This place was exceptional. It’s some of the best Italian food I’ve had, and the service was wonderful.

Every single dish we got was fantastic, but I specifically recommend the grilled calamari, the arancini, and the lasagna. From dessert, I adored the tiramisu, which they prepare at the table with freshly whipped cream and freshly brewed coffee, and it softens nicely over a few minutes.

Lastly, I want to appreciate the service in a few ways, in addition to being attentive and quick, the staff here really helped figure out how solve my dinner problem: 3 of my 6 person group was late, and 2 of them had no eta. The hosts were flexible and got us seated at a smaller table first and later added an adjacent table when that party cleared out, so that our late comers were able to join.

One of the best Italian meals I’ve had in New York — and I spent 10 days exploring SoHo’s food scene, so that means something.

The food is outstanding. Authentic Sicilian flavors done with real care. The ravioli is exceptional — perfectly layered, hearty but not heavy. The pasta alla Norma is a must-order.

And do not skip the tiramisu. The waiter prepared it right in front of us, bringing the ingredients together at the table — simple, fresh, and unforgettable.

But what truly sets Piccola Cucina apart is the service. The staff are warm, genuine, and make you feel like a regular from the moment you walk in.

If you are visiting SoHo and want one meal that truly reflects what Italian food should taste like, this is the place. Highly recommended.

Absolutely worth it. The lasagna was outstanding — rich, perfectly layered, exactly what you want from a proper Sicilian kitchen. And the tiramisu is phenomenal, easily one of the best I’ve had in the city. Great atmosphere too 🫶🏻

We did a walk in after a long haul at SoHo. Starved, we were not expecting much taste but we were taken by surprise by the focaccia bread the house offered along with fresh olive oil.

Our order started with grilled calamari.. it was fresh and delicious - reminded me of a juicy ceviche. Followed by our pasta dishes ragu gnocchi and seafood scampi fusilli pasta. They were out of the world! We weren’t expecting anything over 3/4 starred food in this corner but were taken by surprise how amazingly flavored the pasta sauces were. Just when we thought we couldn’t eat anymore cos we clean swiped whatever we ordered, our server tempted us to look at the dessert menu. Totally fell hard and jumped in joy that we didn’t miss it - that lemon cheesecake was like a cherry on top of our wonderful order. We were so happy that we took cards so the next time we are in this neighborhood, we will definitely swing by.

A restaurant I almost visited every month. One of the best Italian foods in NY, recognized by me and all of my influencer friends. The tiramisu is made in front of you. Very fresh and creamy. They had special menu for the Olympic Games. The lobster pasta is the BEST BEST BEST one. Remember to try it before you leave New York.

I only had one time that I found a piece of iron brush in the pasta. But the restaurant apologized immediately and waived the cost of that pasta. So in general, it’s nice. It’s rare to find a restaurant with good attitudes in New York.
The food, the service and atmosphere was amazing. This was our first time and we are definitely coming back!! The prices are reasonable.

name: Hanbat Sul Lung Tang
address: 4163 5th St, Los Angeles, CA 90020, United States
description: Informal joint serving traditional Korean Oxtail soup with add-ins such as tripe, brisket & tongue.

business_details.details: 4163 5th St, Los Angeles, CA 90020, United States

top_reviews.content:
Another ktown classic which I’m so glad I finally got to try. Sul lung tang is such a comforting dish for me with the warm hearty soup. I got the mixed which came with brisket, flank, intestine, tripe, tongue etc, although you can customize it however you want. I topped mine with a generous helping of spring onion, seasoned with salt and paper, poured in my bowl of rice and proceeded to slurp the bowl till I could lick the bottom. Thinking about it makes me drool. Highly highly recommended!!
We got lucky and there was no wait when we arrived but by the time we were done eating, the line was out the door! Service is quick they only serve cabbage and radish kimchi for banchan.

There is a reason this place is an absolute institution in K-Town! They specialize in one thing (sullungtang) and do it flawlessly. The broth, rich, milky, and incredibly comforting flavor, meat is melt-in-your-mouth tender, and their kimchi and kkakdugi (radish kimchi) are fresh, crunchy, and absolutely top-tier, authentic, soup very HOT!
They do one thing and they do it deliciously!!! No frills. Fast service. Dump in some salt, pepper and spring onions and enjoy the most delicious broth that will heal you on a molecular level. YUM.

SO delicious and comforting. The service is fast and efficient, the staff is kind. There is parking in the back for $3, and with to go containers I ended up spending $30 total. It was so worth it. The kimchi was excellent, the broth is so layered and flavorful. For the full experience, add your own salt, pepper, and heaps of green onions. I went with the brisket as I don’t love the bite of tripe and spleen and the meat was tender and very generously portioned.

We’ve been coming to this Korean beef soup restaurant in Los Angeles for over 15 years, from when a bowl cost $9 to now around $20, and the quality has never changed.
The soup is still the same pure beef broth, with no added salt or seasoning. It tastes very clean and comforting, and you never feel thirsty after drinking it. That’s how we know they don’t use MSG. The milky-white beef bone broth is light, nourishing, and very easy to drink.
Whenever we’re not feeling well, we come here for a bowl—it instantly helps restore energy. We usually order the Mixed, which includes intestine, flank, brisket, and other cuts.
The aunties working there are very attentive and will regularly check if you need more kimchi or radish, which makes the experience feel very caring and homely.
Parking is relatively easy to find, which is another plus.
The only downside is the restroom. It’s been the same for many years and feels quite old, a bit dirty, and has an unpleasant smell. If they could improve the restroom, it would make the experience much better overall.

name: Sabai Thai
address: 432 Park Ave S, New York, NY 10016, United States
description: Serves traditional Thai cuisine and cocktails in a modern space with a stylish bar and golden accents.

business_details.details: 432 Park Ave S, New York, NY 10016, United States

top_reviews.content:
The first thing you'll notice is how beautiful the space is. Gorgeous interiors, a warm atmosphere, and genuinely friendly hosts made for a great first impression.

We started with the curry puffs and satay buns, both of which were easy wins. No complaints, I would happily order them again.

The Khao Soi was the highlight of my meal. Rich, comforting, and packed with flavor. I love when restaurants get this right. They also do super thin noodles in the khao soi which is a plus for me. I also tried a little bit of the crab fried rice which was also incredible.

I also ordered the lychee mocktail. The drink itself was fairly average, but it came with a lychee mochi that completely stole the show. I honestly enjoyed the mochi more than the drink itself.

Overall, this is just good, no-nonsense Thai food. Nothing feels overly gimmicky. The restaurant focuses on solid flavors, a beautiful space, and warm hospitality. I'd happily come back to work my way through more of the menu.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Had a great experience at Sabai Thai! The food was delicious, fresh, and full of flavor, with great portions and beautiful presentation. The atmosphere was warm, relaxing, and perfect for a nice dinner. The service was friendly, attentive, and welcoming without being overbearing.

The drinks were also excellent and paired perfectly with the meal. Overall, a great spot for authentic Thai flavors, good drinks, and a relaxing atmosphere. Definitely worth checking out if you’re in New York! 🍜🍹

Not the best, but far from the worst. The food is overall pretty good compared to many other popular Thai places in NYC, it's a NYC 5* but a personal 6.5/10. The flavors are there for the most part, but it's not intense enough (understandable) and unfortunately it's American level spicy). The cost:quanity ratio could be a bit better, but nothing egregious for Manhattan standards.

The service is excellent overall and there are absolutely 0 complaints there. The staff is very attentive despite for many people were there on a Friday night.

The atmosphere is intimate and not to loud, but you need to talk a little bit louder because of how close you are to other people and the music volume. But the ambiance makes it a great date night spot.

I can see myself coming back for the service and the vibes overall.

My friend and I made reservations at 6:30pm on a Friday. We had intended to go for restaurant week, and the website said that Sabai was participating. However, when I got to the restaurant, I was told that they were not participating. When I brought this up to the staff, they did comment that several people made the same mistake earlier in the week. If that was the case, then why not correct the restaurant week website, or make it very obvious on your website that you aren't participating? Both of us were starving, and I had put in a birthday request at the restaurant, so we decided to stay. The ambiance is classy, and this would be a great spot for a business dinner or date night.

I ordered a massaman curry with roti and chicken ($29), and my friend ordered the chuchi shrimp ($30) and curry puff ($16). Prices are a bit above average for the portion size, but justified by the area. We both enjoyed our dishes; the flavors were on point! Then, for my friend's birthday, they gave us mochi ice cream and a card signed by the staff! That was a nice touch that overrode the restaurant week debacle.

Service was fantastic. There were multiple check backs and water refills. I would recommend Sabai Thai for a fancy night out, and I would return to try other dishes.

Came with a few friends and we all loved it. We split the vegetable dumplings, the sauce was great. Could be more for the price. We each got pad Thai and the portion is good. Service was fine, nothing notable, a bit slow. Place is pretty and quiet but a bit dark.

Sorry but I’d give it a 1 star if it weren’t for the drink. The hype is somewhat true. Service needs to go robotic.
Service was quick! Just got a regular iced coffee and it was delicious. I recommend this place if you’re in the area (which I was). They got my order out quick 👍🏽

Nestled in the lobby of the LINE hotel, this coffee shop is a hidden gem worth discovering. While it can get busy, the line moves swiftly thanks to the efficient and friendly staff.
The cleanliness and tidiness of the place are evident, creating a welcoming ambiance for patrons. But it's the quality of their coffees that truly steals the show. Each cup is expertly brewed, delivering a rich and flavorful experience that keeps customers coming back for more.
Overall, my experience here was fantastic, and I wouldn't hesitate to return. If you're in need of a caffeine fix in a stylish and convenient setting, this coffee shop at the LINE hotel is the place to be.

This well-regarded coffee shop is in the Line Hotel lobby in Koreatown, Los Angeles. The coffee beverages offer a robust flavor profile complemented by a subtle acidity. The menu includes various pastries, gluten-free and vegan options, and light meal choices such as burritos, bagels, and sandwiches. The ordering process is efficient, with drinks typically prepared within a few minutes. Additionally, a spacious seating area in front is shared with the lobby bar, providing a welcoming atmosphere.

I'm a crackhead for caffeine, and I'm slowly getting back into cafe hopping. This spot was across the street from where we just dined.

Parking: Every man for themselves. Paid metered parking in front or paid parking garage in the back. Follow the signs to public parking. Complimentary 3 hour parking. $5 + service fees after 3 hours paid via online.

Ambiance/Environment: This coffee shop is located inside the lobby of the Line Hotel. The lobby area is large with plenty of indoor seating. Very clean and modern inside. They also have limited outdoor seating. It was pretty busy when we visited.

Service: The cashier that assisted us was knowledgeable about the menu and even asked us questions before giving us recommendations. The barista was extremely quick and efficient. He made the drink while I was ordering lol.

Drink: I ordered their featured drink - Cloud Cream with espresso, plant-based coconut foam, and organic whole milk. This drink definitely felt light like a cloud. The foam gave it a very, slight coconut taste. The coffee was sweetened from the vanilla. If you like your coffee light and slightly sweetened, then this is perfect for you.

Pricing: $7.50 for 12 oz .. I knew LA was expensive but oof. I'd probably visit once in a while if I'm ever in the area again.

Alfred Coffee in Koreatown never misses. Great coffee, immaculate vibes, perfect for a grab-and-go or a full-on chill. Huge shoutout to Pablo, Grant, Stanley, Dom, Nathaniel, and Luis for the laughs and top-tier service -- absolute legends. If you're in K-Town and need caffeine + good energy, this is the move

Great coffee!

Had the breakfast bacon burriton and the Mocha. Location seems to be inside a hotel lobby. Parking is not ideal. Metered parking taken by food trucks-Food trucks leave at 3pm.

It has been over 20 years since I last stepped foot inside a Sizzler, but decided to give them another try this past weekend when I was up in the valley. I was pleasantly surprised of how good it was. Basically it’s a smaller version of Soup Plantation but I think much better than Red Lobster and other chains. The shrimp at Sizzled is actually better than Red Lobster, they just have the cheddar biscuits.

This location works by you place your order at the counter and then opt to add salad bar or not. The salad bar is only $12 so it’s a really fair deal and it comes with all sorts of options as well as tacos and a dessert station. For my meal I ordered the New York steak and thought it was pretty good. It’s not like a premium steakhouse, but it does taste like a really decent steak that you would purchase at the grocery store and cook yourself. It was not too fatty and I really enjoyed it. It is a bit expensive compared to the average lunch and is a lot of food so I would not suggest it for an everyday meal, but I definitely will give Sizzler another chance again in the future and would suggest to others looking for a good mini buffet option.

I always eat in this place and have to ask for a fresh non-rotten baked potato, which they never provide for me. Why do they have to serve Rotten baked potatoes? Potatoes are the cheapest thing you can buy! Aside from that, I do enjoy eating at Sizzler.

Really gross environment.  The people working there are nice but food was horrible and place looked like a cheap motel from the 70s. Hasn't been updated probably since then. Prices are higher than other Sizzlers with less options of food. They dont even have chocolate frozen yogurt that ALL of the Sizzlers have. We paid $50 for a terrible meal and atmosphere.
Had a great dining experience with my son. Staff was excellent and courteous. Thanks for the good time.

Came with my mom to dine in at this location. Even though the steak tasted great, my biggest issue is The waiters follow you around like rats and spy on you like inspectors over what you eat. They act stingy and scold you for sharing some salad, even though we paid for the salad bar. Also the salad bar is expensive and the hot bar items suck, Quality of food is not too good, doesn't taste amazing. I ain't trying to pay another $14 for my own self for cheap quality food. And the waiter probably expects me to tip her big too. In her dreams.

Also don't like the fact that they removed some of my most favorite dishes from the menu like the corn chowder soup and the fried chicken wings along with some others. Sizzlers downgraded over the years. not the same like it used to be a several years ago

top_reviews.content:
If you're looking for authentic Portuguese food, O Lavrador is a must-visit!
The seafood was absolutely outstanding. The highlight of my meal was the grilled lobster, which was a perfect 10/10—fresh, juicy, and grilled to perfection with just the right amount of seasoning. Every dish we ordered was packed with flavor, from the seafood to the rice and plantains.
The atmosphere was even better because I got to enjoy an exciting World Cup soccer match while having dinner. The staff were some of the friendliest and most welcoming people I've ever encountered. They made us feel right at home and provided excellent service from start to finish.
The food, drinks, service, and overall experience were all exceptional. I highly recommend O Lavrador to anyone who loves amazing seafood and authentic Portuguese cuisine. I'll definitely be back!

As a Greek, I can be pretty demanding when it comes to food, because I grow up with strong flavors and real ingredients. This place truly impressed me. If you are looking for real food, fresh ingredients, and dishes made with care, you are in the right place. Everything tasted authentic, rich, and full of flavor. You can tell the kitchen pays attention to quality, not just presentation. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone who wants a genuinely great meal

After a hard drive of 4.5 hours north we arrived in the neighborhood of our hotel. We decided to have dinner before checking in. Yelp reviews highly rated O’ Lavrador so my husband and I gave it a try. And what a treat it was! The food was amazing, atmosphere charming and stupendous waitstaff.
We are not familiar with Portuguese cuisine so we asked lots of questions and decided to share mussels with garlic and white wine sauce to start our dining experience. Delicious is all I will say!  I opted for one of the very tempting specials - the Portuguese seafood stew of shrimp, clams, mussels, and calamari in a light tomato broth, delightfully seasoned, with rice in the broth. This is not soup, but is instead a loose stew that begs you to spoon it up. My husband’s grilled lamb chops in rosemary sauce was equally delectable. We finished our experience with crème brûlée and Portuguese style poached pear. OMG, I have never eaten a better version of poached anything!
Sarah’s recommendations were spot on! We could not have been more pleased if we tried. Go! Give this restaurant a try. It will be well worth the drive! You won’t regret it.

Went to this restaurant last night for Mother’s Day. The food was absolutely impeccable. I had chicken and it just was unbelievable melted in my mouth. We also had steamed clams and fried Gala as appetizers and it was absolutely unbelievable. The service was absolutely impeccable. The atmosphere the place was so clean. It was absolutely beautiful. I enjoyed it and I can’t wait to go back again. Thank you folks for such a great time on Mother’s Day for my wife my children absolutely beautiful thank you so much.

Just came here with my parents for an early Father's Day. Everything was absolutely wonderful! Especially our server, Sara.

We started with fried calamari, and it was hands down some of the best I have ever had. The calamari was fresh, the batter was light but flavorful, and they were fried to perfection.

Then I had the caldo very, which was super. The broth was rich and creamy, and the leafy vegetables were a beautiful contrast. The sausage was a delicious addition.

For lunch my mom and I had the Francesinha sandwiches, which were delicious and unlike any I've ever had. The combination of bread, cheese, and meats, with the sauce and egg on top, was fantastic.

My dad had a seafood Parrilhada Seafood, and he reported that his was excellent as well.

Sara was an absolute highlight, kind, attentive, and helpful.

Cannot wait to come back!

Went in on a Thursday night the week before Christmas. We walked from staying close by and I didn’t really see any parking so not sure how that would go. The vibe once you walk in transports you to quintessential 80s European themed restaurant. Painted murals, dark wood, fake plants. It’s fantastic nostalgia. The menu is huge and sort of overwhelming. So just trust me when I say order the verde. We ordered the tasting platter and it was awesome but considering the serving sizing here, we didn’t need an appetizer at all. In fact the small servings of the mains could have been enough to share between two. This is how seafood, lobster is supposed to be cooked and served.
It was expensive. An appetizer for 2, a main each and 2 drinks was $170 with tip and tax. But it was an experience.

Came here on a whim and ordered the skirt steak.  The portion was huge and I thought there is no way i would finish it. However it was cooked to perfection and the flavor was soooo good.  I finished it and almost everything else on my plate.  I do not know when i will find myself in this neighborhood again, but I would love to enjoy this steak a second time.

Came here for an early dinner before driving back to CT during rush hour. Food was delicious, service great and staff was very friendly. Convenient parking and prompt service. We would definitely return!

What I loved most was that the portions were perfect and not overwhelming, which made it easy to try several things. I had a few flatbreads with lettuce, pizza sauce, mushrooms, and Spanish jamón, along with raspberry cookies and sparkling water. Every bite felt thoughtful, fresh, and satisfying.

I had an amazing time and left very happy. Next time, I am definitely trying the wines.

This is one of many locations of the franchise in the city. Their main selling point is pastries but this location expands greatly with a dine in area to accommodate tastes for savory pizzas and other offerings. Of their pastries, perhaps the most popular is the bombolone, which is a subtype of Italian doughnut. They can be pricy if you buy a couple, and you won't get any discount for a baker's dozen!

top_reviews.content: Late night KBBQ hits different at Road to Seoul in Koreatown, especially when you go all in on their top-tier AYCE. From juicy giant short ribs and tender filet mignon to that must-order lemon herb ribeye, every bite delivers. Pair it with steamed egg, tofu soup, and corn cheese for the full experience, then level it up by making your own Korean tacos with all the banchan or wrapping it in rice paper. Seafood lovers can’t skip the baby octopus, and ending with garlic shrimp just seals the deal. Open until 1 or 2AM, this is the move when those late-night cravings hit.

Cool place. AYCE with minimum of 2 people. The options are great and when we ordered they said you can pick three meats to start and get more later. No problem.

We got our first order and I was stunned at how much meat our first 3 options were. There was no way we could order different choices.

I have never been to Korean bbq where the servings were so large. We couldn't even try the other various things we wanted to try.

My advice to management is to make the portions smaller and avoid waste as people can always order more.

Other than that, I would go back as long as I have more than 2 or 3 people with me for sure.

The food was amazing! The quality of the steak and ribeye was really good! The shortrib was my favorite! It was huge and marinated perfectly. The service was great they kept coming to check in on us! We always had a clean gril and plenty of meat to gril! The sides were really tasty! We cant wait to comeback! Its definitely worth it because all the meat is really good quality!

As soon as you walk in they don’t even ask what you would like to drink and you have to ask for a cup with ice because they give your drinks in a can. When asking for more sides or new meats they act like we’re bothering them by asking them. Many plates had cracks and a water cup had crust of food droppings. They pick and choose who to treat right ; there was only one waitress that actually does a great job and unfortunately we didn’t get her. Our first time trying this place and we were excited but our expectations were set too high. First and last for sure.
Between this location and the one on Western, this one didn't seem to get too crowded. The selection was good and service was pretty attentive for an all you can eat place.

Average korean BBQ, nothing too memorable. Service could be better, they spilled water all over our table and my husband, no apologies were made really. Will be giving 5 stars anyways, restaurants have hard time surviving as it is. Will not be coming back though.

Came here with a couple friends and went with their AYCE Tier C at $61.99, which felt like a fair price considering how many premium cuts are included. Autism family here. We love the service and environment. This is one of the few go to places as a family. Everyone walks out satisfied. The staff is so friendly and attentive. The meat variety is delicious, and pairs well with steam egg and salad. Scallion pancakes are a must for kids.

top_reviews.content: Chef Guo in Midtown by renowned Chef Wenjie Guo is offering a taste of the State Banquet President Xi and Trump enjoyed without ever leaving NYC. Chef Guo at age 14 became the disciple of Master Chef Ding Guangzhou, a seventh generation disciple of royal chefs and it started his journey in mastering fine Chinese cuisine. Today he’s known for blending traditional cooking philosophies with modern techniques that you can experience with all five senses. Doors open up to a luxurious traditional Chinese setting that sets the stage for the meal. Each course is served with royal level attention using premium ingredients and unforgettable flavors. This exclusive State Banquet Experience is available for a limited time making it the perfect chance to experience Chef Guo’s fine Chinese dining.

Chef Guo in Manhattan positions itself as a pinnacle of "Imperial Cuisine," but the actual experience feels more like a high-priced theme park attraction than a legitimate fine dining establishment. While the $199 nine-course menu offers edible fare, the overall atmosphere is marred by a bizarrely "fake" aesthetic and a glaring lack of basic luxury amenities like a coat check. The evening is dominated by servers with accents delivering long, uninspired monologues about ginkgo trees and tambourines instead of focusing on the meal. The restaurant makes grand, questionable claims about being the only "government-approved" culinary system, yet the food fails to live up to the hype, consisting largely of deep-fried dishes or standard high-end staples like sea cucumber porridge. Between the tacky artificial decor and the total absence of a cocktail menu, the experience feels entirely unauthentic and hollow. It is a masterclass in "fake" fine dining that prioritizes strange storytelling over actual hospitality or culinary innovation.

In the middle of Manhattan where everything feels rushed, Chef Guo’s restaurant slows time. No walk-ins, only reservation and bell-entry, you step into a world of stillness, intention, and artistry.

Every dish tells a story, with ingredients chosen for meaning as much as flavor. The attention to detail awakens every sense and transports you to a different state of mind. Servers in embroidered robes share the cultural significance of each course, adding depth to the experience.

This is not a regular restaurant! It is dining for Royals. A hidden sanctuary where calm meets complexity, and minimalism becomes pure meaning.

The food was so good that it pains me to give them 4 stars. The service was so misaligned with the $800pp price tag that it pains me to give them 4 stars.
The bad - We had 2 servers for our table of 4, the only 4 people in the restaurant. One would expect that a 2:1 ratio for the wait staff would allow for the precision of a world class restaurant. This purports to be 'imperial cuisine' but here are some of the elements of service that certainly would *not* be acceptable when serving at court: Jessica our main server interrupted conversation (twice literally cutting someone off mid sentence loudly) to introduce our dishes, silverware was placed crooked at every refresh, the lids of many dishes were crooked on the dish when presented, one of the elements on one of my dishes fell over as they were setting it down because they tilted the plate too far when reaching and they meditated for a good 30 seconds before looking at my face and suggesting they will take it back to have it fixed, one of the servers showed up late and changed into her uniform while I sat there and waited for my group to arrive (again, tiny restaurant), and one of our servers rolled up their sleeve and scrolled their apple watch next to our table.
I know that other than the interruptions these are seemingly insignificant offenses, but the cost is not meaningfully less than The Alchemist in Copenhagen and that is several hours with 50 "courses" across several rooms you move through. Of course they're very different experiences but I am just setting a perspective on how few restaurants command such a pricetag. If the servers aren't proud of their work, there are many servers getting paid less at michelin restaurants that do their jobs several step functions better than the staff here.

The good - finally I get to talk about this. Having a restaurant to yourself by design is a singular experience. The intimate space was thoughtful. Most importantly, the food truly was world class. Guo is a master of his craft. He uses traditional Chinese cooking techniques on ingredients both Chinese and global. His mission is to offer a meal that is so good at what it does that even palates unprepared for eastern textures, flavors, and combinations will enjoy it - all while refusing to sacrifice his commitment to accurate representations of that cuisine. It is an extremely tall task - saltiness, viscosity - but, for anyone with even the most remote flexibility in their enjoyment of non-american fare, he does this remarkably. Across many of the world's top restaurants I have certainly seen plating and flavor balancing done just as well, but rarely if ever have I experienced a chef so boldly eschew reverting to the mean of the western palate when the pricetag is this high. His understanding of his craft is nothing short of profound mastery.

Lastly I will add (sort of in response to some of the less favorable reviews) that sharing history and story about the space, food, and country, servers with accents, and non-scandinavian design of the restaurant space are all incredibly authentic to the culinary story being told here. Chinese culture, aesthetic, and cuisine are different to America's. If you are unwilling to shift your frame of reference when judging the experience... go to a different fine dining restaurant. There are, like, 500 options for that experience in NYC. If you go here, go as a curious visitor to the physical manifestation of another person's lens of the world.

My review for this restaurant is awesome!!!!🤩
As soon as I entered the restaurant I was shocked by the decorative style inside, which simply arrived at the feeling of a palace dinner. I have rarely seen some restaurants so richly decorated with Chinese cultural characteristics. For the food, I don't even dare to break its shape🤣🤣because the food is as exquisite as if is fake, and at first glance thought it was a painting.

Overall, the environment and the food are top-notch, at least one of the tops in my case. Compared with Michelin's three-star restaurant, I prefer Chef Guo, more to my taste.  I really really really really super recommend trying it! 🥹😋

top_reviews.content: I came with a large appetite after donating plasma. Welcoming, fresh, clean, feels healthy. I ordered with hummus, cucumber yogurt, and dressing for salad. Yummy.

Wow!! The rice was so buttery & fluffy, which was already a standout. The chicken was also very juicy, but really I kept going back for the rice.

The hummus was so good I ordered a large to go :) give them a try when in the neighborhood! Hope I have more errands in the area just to come back lol.

Chelo Taste of Persia is a good Persian restaurant on a busy street with dine in, delivery and takeout options.

I came here based on the online reviews and pictures for takeout. I ordered a grilled chicken plate with rice which came with garlic sauce, pita bread, hummus and lentil soup.

The employee who offered me some friendly advice about the menu and took my order gave me some helpful recommendations and a generous amount of food for my takeout order.

While I was waiting for my order, I noticed an unhoused person walking around the restaurant, probably taking momentary shelter from the extreme heat outside that day. Different employees and restaurant owners will respond differently to these types of situations in my experience.

The employee asked the person if they needed help or assistance and stood behind my chair, seemingly offering me a little safety for my heavy purse. Then the employee proceeded to load up a large cup with ice and gave it to to the non paying customer as a gift, which in consideration of how hot it was outside, I think was a pretty special gift.

Some of us know how valuable a cup of ice can be on a hot day, I used to buy a cup of ice when I couldn't afford to buy a beverage as a child and it was sometimes pretty important for my health.

Everything I ordered was very good and it all stayed warm for a good amount of time so that I ended up eating two warm meals that afternoon.

The rice had a nice texture and flavor, like a pilaf. The thick yellow lentil soup was my favorite part of the meal, five stars. The grilled white meat chicken was lean, and lightly seasoned, which I prefer to highly marinated myself.

The interior of the restaurant is cute and very clean. The service is excellent. Good people= Five stars!

This spot caught our eye. We stopped in with quite an appetite. This place looks like a takeout spot, but they have a nice small dining room. You order at the counter and they call you when ready

We started with some Pita and the Garlic Shallot Yogurt dip. It was good. Note, the Persian Iced tea is good but very sweetened.

I ordered the Shish Kabob and the Chicken Kabob. Both were tender and delicious. The saffron rice served made a perfect complement.

My wife had the Chicken Koobedeh and the Shish Kabob. Both plates came with a small lentil soup.  They also give you a choice of small dips, such as hummus, to go with the pita bread.

The best item was the chicken kabob. It was very moist and flavorful. All the other skewers were good but not as good as the chicken.

The portions were generous; we took half of each plate home! Definitely filled out appetite. Lastly, I couldn't resist the homemade bakklava.

Next time I'm back in Van Nuys, I'll have to stop by again.

Chelo is AMAZING! I’ve eaten at the restaurant and ordered delivery, and it never disappoints. The food is always fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned — that’s why I keep coming back! Their lemonade is also a must-try, it’s so good. I absolutely love this place!

My falafel sandwich was good, but there wasn't enough sauce in it. The lentil soup was tiny, and there wasn't enough seasoning in it.

My order was ready when I walked in, but I sat there and waited for a while, even though I let the person know that I ordered a falafel sandwich over the phone. Finally, I was handed the order once I approached him again and asked about it again. Overall, I liked the food and the place.

Awesome experience at Chelo Taste of Persia!

Parking: There is metered parking on Van Nuys but I prefer to park on the street called Friar which is still metered but less heavy with traffic.

The storefront is between the People's Bail Bonds and FCS Insurance Services with Van Nuys Barber right at the corner. They have daily specials and catering available too!

The saffron lemon chicken kabob was tasty and soft, not dry like other places. I actually like how it's made to order and not sitting in a warmer some where. I got full rice but should have gotten half rice and half salad because from other pictures the salad looks really good!
Hummus plate was okay.

Overall, clean ambience and friendly service. Great experience and no negatives.

My mom and I have been coming to Chelo’s for years now. My mom got pissed one time when we went on a Saturday and they were already closed and we had to go across the street to another Persian restaurant. She complained the entire time that it wasn’t like chelo.  So we always have to remember they close at 5 pm Saturdays lol but Chelo gets better every time. We love the drinks and food so much.

top_reviews.content:
Took the kids out for a late dinner because they were craving Filipino food, so we ventured out to Panorama City and tried Bamboo Bistro for the first time. So glad we did! They’re open until 1 AM, which was perfect for our late-night adventure.
We ordered some of our favorite Filipino dishes, and everything really hit the spot—definitely satisfied all the cravings. Our server was helpful and attentive to our needs. What we didn’t expect was the fun surprise of karaoke night on Saturdays starting at 8:30 PM. It turned into a full-on Filipino party—so lively, joyful, and full of energy!
The host, Bo Carnation, was absolutely hilarious and kept everyone entertained the whole night. Our daughter even sang a few songs, which made the night even more special for us.
We laughed so much and truly enjoyed the experience. Great food, great vibes, and unforgettable entertainment. We left with full bellies, happy hearts, and big smiles. We’ll definitely be back! 🎤✨

Not an everyday thing, but when I'm craving Filipino food, this spot hits the spot.

They offer weekend breakfast and lunch buffets--pay upfront before grabbing your first plate. It's about $27++ and includes a drink.

The spread is solid. It's not the most mind-blowing flavors, but it's AYCE, so it definitely satisfies those cravings. You'll leave full... like really full.

Was looking forward to some authentic Filipino food and this place was highly recommended.
Well, 1st it was hard to find but eventually me and my friend found it . I arrived first so I paid for both of us.  For all you can eat and drinks included $56.00 was not a bad price.
The buffet looked to good, lots of choices but everything was cold. The only thing warm was the soup.  The rice was cold , so was the pork lechon, Kare Kare , Caldereta in fact nothing was hot or remotely warm. The beef Sinegang was sour and bitter. I know its called sour soup but it should have a tangy taste. The Kare Kare would have been good if it was hot.
Sorry I was so disappointed.  We ate very little then just sat there and talked.
I apologize for the low rating but I had to be honest.
We will not be coming back since it was not what I was expecting.

My first time to visit here. We had a hard time finding the place even with google maps. Kuya Dan said we should have called for direction. We came in at 2 pm and buffet closed at 3 pm. So I was expecting fewer selections. But I was surprised. There were plenty of choices and food was great. Kuya Dan is very easy to talk. Very accommodating and friendly. I will bring my husband next time.

One of the few great Filipino restaurants here in Los Angeles area. The restaurant is located right in the middle of Panorama City.

Don’t be discouraged by the hustle and bustle of the busy Panorama City , once you step inside Bamboo Bistro, you’ll be greeted by cheerful staff and eventually taste the great food of the Philippines.

This is my first time in this place and I was not disappointed. Will definitely go back for more.

3/5 for the food. Although the food is okay the vibes here was phenomenal. The food was not that hot when it came and I felt like it was not fresh. Got the nilagang baka, beef steak, and liempo. Liempo was really good though

I used to come here a lot of times in the past. We always enjoy watching Bo. We even brought some of other Mexican relatives and friends here a couple of times. Yesterday, I came with my friends for lunch buffet. My husband is an American Mexican and wanted to have Mexican food yest.  So he bought a take out Mexican food from outside and planned to eat with us inside. It was just a small food and will just take one chair to join us. There are still a lot of chairs available. I was thinking that would be fine though I know that outside food is not allowed. It was our first time to do that. The owner said that’s not allowed. So I just let my husband eat outside with his take out food. While the 4 of us was eating the buffet inside. I felt offended. I was hoping for a little consideration. I know there’s a rule but being a good customer for years, ordering for catering, promoting their restaurant, their food, the comedy nights… A little consideration could have been given. Sanford's Restaurant in Astoria is a true neighborhood gem. With so many classic diners disappearing, I'm glad places like this are still around. It offers that traditional diner experience but with a more upscale atmosphere, a diverse menu, and excellent service.
I ordered the Cheeseburger Deluxe, and it was cooked perfectly and full of flavor. I asked to swap the French fries for home fries, and they were happy to accommodate the request, which I appreciated. The only downside was that the home fries were a little undercooked for my taste, and I'm personally not a fan of square-cut home fries. Overall, it was a great meal and a place I'd definitely return to. If you're looking for an upscale diner in Astoria, a great cheeseburger, or a restaurant with an extensive menu and welcoming atmosphere, Sanford's is well worth a visit.

Excellent service and great brunch. My friend has the regular eggs benny, I got the crab benny… so yummy! Good crisp on the muffin and good seasoning on the crab, sauce, etc. Good wine. Very good service. Nice interior, well appointed. Recommend.

Sanford's is one of those neighborhood restaurants that never disappoints. Whether you're stopping in for breakfast, brunch, lunch, or dinner, it's always a reliable spot with a welcoming atmosphere and a menu that has something for everyone.

The truffle mac & cheese is an absolute must-order. It's rich, creamy, and easily one of my favorite dishes on the menu. Their breakfast is just as good, especially the pancakes, which are fluffy, flavorful, and perfect if you're craving a classic brunch.

One thing I really like about Sanford's is how easy it is to stop in for a meal. It has a relaxed, casual atmosphere that's comfortable whether you're dining alone or with friends. Even when it's busy, it never feels overwhelming, and I've always found it to be a pleasant place to sit and enjoy a meal !!

The atmosphere was very pleasant & upscale. Enjoyed coming here for the first time. Services was excellent, serving apps and entrées on time. A bit expensive on the specials, but good food overall. Steak was cooked with perfection. Wonderful selection of Wine, beer and whiskey.
I'd recommend anyone looking for a real American restaurant in Astoria. It's definitely here.
Delicious! Portion sizes a little small but ambiance is good and they have a big space. Their happy hour oysters are so good and big too! Drinks are standard.

One of the best whiskey bars in the country and certainly among the very best in NYC. I love the private barrel selection and prices, they curate some of the best whiskies by whiskey advocate, but they have also won awards for the best espresso martini in New York! We’ve had good here before and it’s great, it’s also just a classy, comfortable bar. We love coming here, wish it was closer, it’s a great experience!

First thing I noticed when I entered was the decor and vibe. Very cozy but upscale at the same time. The waiters were really on point and super attentive. We started with the Risotto Ball which was scrumptious. It wasn’t dry inside and the mushroom gave it a nice meaty texture.

I then had the Sesame crusted Yellowtail Tuna. I absolutely loved it. It comes in top of a bed of Jasmin rice and some vegetables. Truly packs a great amount of flavor.
Wish we could have gone for the brunch! It looks so good lol but we went for dinner and the apps and lobster ravioli were soooooo good. Definitely recommend trying a bit of a few things on the menu.

They also were able to easily accommodate my request to make it vegetarian and placed large,delicious, perfectly cooked tofu instead of chicken for me. A beautiful location, not far from Grand Central Station. The back dining room is gorgeous, window seating available also.

My husband and I both said that we need to come back one time when we’re hungrier because we need to try more of these menu items. The crispy chicken cashew was perfection and I have no doubt that the curry and noodle dishes are also amazing. We also got the ribeye summer rolls, and those were fresh, delicious, and served with a beautiful spicy dipping sauce. Service was quick!

Of all the Thai food I’ve had up to this day, this is definitely THE best Thai food I have ever had. Especially recommend the Pad Thai Ew and rib eye summer roll, also the kimchi French fried is a must to have. I’m so glad that I found this place, and also a big Thank You to Jana, our cute little server who made this experience splendid!

The Thai dishes here are delicious. I didn’t get a chance to try the Vietnamese dishes, but I’m sure they are delectable as well. I had the crispy pork belly app and the crab fried rice entree (with a Thai fried egg and grilled shrimp on the side), and both were excellent. The service here is great - the bartenders, especially JJ & Rose!, and wait staff are all so very nice and thoughtful. I really enjoyed my dinner here and will definitely come back. They also have HH specials from 11:30am-6pm so extra plus!

top_reviews.content: Came here for the first time today. Had always had Korean BBQ and this was an introduction to more Korean cuisine. Loved everything we ate here. It's a set menu you order and it comes with a lot of different food items that you can add to your rice bowl. Everything was fresh and tasted amazing. Will definitely visit again.

Be prepared to walk away feeling very full. We got the set meal here, which came served with appetizers, barley rice, a lot of banchan (and by that I meant a LOT), soup, congee, dessert, etc.

It was definitely more than enough food. We also got an additional order of LA kalbi for some protein. The meat quality was good but I felt like the meat was not marinated long enough and so the flavor was a little bit lacking. If only it just sat in the marinade for a couple more hours, I think this would have been perfect.

The tofu soup was not my favorite, to be very honest. There was some flavor in there that made it smell like a stinky towel. Very different from other soondubu soup places and unfortunately not for me. Everything else we had was excellent and I would definitely come back again just for the barley rice and banchan.

Service was quick and servers were nice. We also came at 3pm on Saturday so there was no wait. Recommended!

Beautiful assortment of high quality, homestyle banchan that you can’t get elsewhere in Ktown. It’s a lot of food for their base sharable meals, but you taste comfort and it’s hearty. Come with a group who’s into a variety of different, veggie forward Korean dishes.

Would recommend if you’re into having something unique that isn’t the typical kbbq or soups. This feels like you’re visiting home.

Easy parking in the back!

Tried Borit Gogae for Mother’s Day since I’d heard so many good things about it and was craving Korean food. If you’re lucky, you might be able to grab a parking spot right in front, plus there’s street parking nearby too.

The place was super busy and completely packed, so the food took a while to come out. I really liked the traditional Korean vibe inside , it felt cozy and authentic. I especially loved the barley rice. The food was solid overall, but nothing really stood out to me as a must-order dish. Glad I gave it a try, though I probably wouldn’t go out of my way to visit again. The service was really friendly and attentive.

A top-tier destination for traditional Korean cuisine. The lunch set here is phenomenal, featuring a wide array of fresh mountain vegetables and rich soybean stews. The perilla seed soup was a standout highlight. While the mung bean pancake was a bit too thick for my personal preference, every other dish was flawless.

The pork Bossam is a must-try side dish—incredibly flavorful and well-prepared. It’s a great place for a nutritious meal that leaves you feeling energized. Perfect for both business lunches and casual dining

Wow, I honestly don’t really know what to say. I’ve never had Korean food like this. I thought I’ve had everything that Korean food could offer living in ktown. But I was very wrong. This place felt like I just went to my Korean cousins house and his aunt just served us dinner. Not really sure how else to explain it. It was quite a unique experience, and you might be alone by the price, but do not fear. It is very filling and quite unique to say the least.

While Korean BBQ is undeniably delicious and something we absolutely love, it really only scratches the surface of traditional Korean dining culture. If you truly want to introduce someone to the authentic depths of genuine Korean cuisine, Boritgogae in Los Angeles Koreatown is the perfect answer. Helmed by the renowned Korean Chef Jung Sun-hee, this restaurant delivers an absolute masterclass in traditional, nourishing homestyle cooking. 🇰🇷🍚

The centerpiece of the experience is the Bori-bap Jeongsik (barley rice set meal), which is accompanied by an array of incredibly clean, refined, and beautifully prepared banchan (side dishes). There is simply not a single plate on the table that falls short of perfection. Because of the diverse and thoughtful spread, it is the ideal dining destination for absolutely any group. Whether you are bringing a vegetarian friend, dining with a dedicated meat lover, sharing a meal with family, or even enjoying a cozy date night, this place effortlessly caters to everyone. 🥗🥩

The absolute standout of our meal was the Ganjang Gejang (raw crab marinated in soy sauce). This dish is notoriously difficult to perfect, but Boritgogae executes it flawlessly. It is exceptionally fresh with zero fishiness, and the marinade strikes a magnificent balance of being neither too salty nor too sweet. The meal's progression is equally thoughtful, starting with a warm, comforting bowl of sweet pumpkin porridge to soothe your stomach, and concluding with a refreshing glass of sweet plum tea to cleanse the palate and aid digestion. 🦀🥣

What else can you call this experience other than absolute perfection? For anyone looking to taste the real, deeply comforting flavors of traditional Korean food, we cannot recommend this restaurant enough. If it were possible, we would easily give Boritgogae 100 stars!

I'm a tour guide, so I get around quite a bit.  Over a month, I went to 4 different Korean restaurants in 3 countries: a 2 Michelin star with a 9 course tasting menu, a bib gourmand with a 5 course tasting menu, a "best of the city" Korean Buddhist temple inspired restaurant, and Borit Gogae.  Guess which one blew all of them away? Hands down Borit Gogae has THE best tasting menu around. Let's start with the rice.  Good barley rice has this nutty, buttery flavor.  Borit had it in spades, and served it from the first course as a palate cleanser between each course.    It's extra-strong miso soup is amazingly good.  All the vegan options were phenomenal, and there was a wonderful balance of various traditional ingredients.  Many "so-called" high end Korean restaurants get stuck on their one favorite ingredient or technique, be it perilla oil, or pickling.  But Borit took two thousand years cooking history and used a variety of flavors and techniques.
Also, at 1/10th the price of the fanciest, it was a bargain. I recommend you come for a late lunch and beat the dinner parking

If you are looking for a comforting pasta dish that hits every single flavor note, you need to try the signature Bucatini Carbonara at Hole in the Wall. This isn't your standard, everyday carbonara. The scene has changed alot in NYC dining. After a 30 min walk in williamsburg at around  9:30 pm we found a restaurant still open and would allow a child. The service was warm and food decent. I’ve been coming to this Gyu-Kaku Midtown East location for well over 10 years. It used to be one of my favorite restaurants. The food was consistently great, the service was excellent, the prices were reasonable, and the overall experience kept me coming back year after year.

Unfortunately, over the years I’ve watched this location slowly decline. The restaurant itself looks worn down, as if it hasn’t been renovated in years, and it’s nowhere near the place it once was.

Even the signature dishes aren’t what they used to be. We ordered the garlic fried rice, and it was always, up to last month, part of the experience. The server would bring it to the table, crack and mix the egg in front of you, cook it fresh, and serve a generous portion. Last night, we were given what looked like a small, pre-made portion that resembled nothing like the original. It was just another reminder of how much this location has cut corners.

But what happened during my most recent visit was beyond disappointing—it was unacceptable.

I watched an employee carrying a soaking wet mop while wearing gloves. Without changing those gloves, he immediately began clearing dirty dishes from another table. I kept paying attention because I couldn’t believe what I was seeing. A few moments later, the very same employee brought us raw meat for grilling while still wearing what appeared to be the same ripped gloves.

I politely asked him how he could be handling cleaning equipment, dirty dishes, and customers’ food with the same gloves. His voice started trembling, and he quietly replied, “No, I promise I changed them.” But I continued watching throughout the evening, and an hour later he was still running around wearing what appeared to be the exact same pair of gloves.

To make matters worse, communication has become difficult because much of the staff barely speaks English, which was never the case during all the years I had been coming here.

When the manager stopped by our table, I told her the staff urgently needs much better hygiene practices. I didn’t identify the employee because I wasn’t trying to get anyone fired. My concern is food safety. There is simply no excuse for someone handling a wet mop, then dirty dishes, and then serving food to customers without proper glove changes and hand hygiene.

This location has gone from a five-star experience to zero stars in my opinion. It feels like ownership or management changed and cost-cutting has taken priority over quality, cleanliness, and customer experience.

It’s genuinely sad to see what was once one of my favorite restaurants fall this far. After more than a decade of loyal visits, this was my last one.

So long, Gyu-Kaku.
