top_reviews.content: I’ve been to a couple of great tempura restaurants in Asia and loved the experience, so I’ve been looking forward to trying Tempura Matsui for a while. And it definitely delivered. Service was outstanding, as you’d expect at a small, counter-style restaurant like this, and the food takes tempura to a completely different level than what most people are used to. Each piece was cooked with incredible precision, and there were some really memorable combinations, like the snow crab wrapped in shiso leaf. Honestly, every bite was excellent. I also appreciated how they explained the best way to eat each course, guiding you through the different salts and sauces. Overall, a 10 out of 10 for me. I’ll definitely be back.

Not sure why I haven’t reviewed this spot before bc I’ve been about 6 times over the past 10 years, but this is hands down one of the best restaurants in NYC. TM offers an elevated take on tempura and literally every bite is incredible. I’ve never seen this level of dedication to tempura outside of Japan. Tempura at most spots is a bit of an afterthought. Not here! Each bite comes with a special salt or flavoring that heightens the experience. And the additions like Japanese custard with shrimp or rice with green tea to the tasting menu are pretty hard to beat. It skews towards seafood and veggies. Service is very precise but understated. It’s definitely pricey but worth every cent. There are plenty of Japanese restaurants or Japanese inspired places but Tempura Matsui is pretty unmatched.

Superb from start to finish. It’s hard to explain how tempura can be so elevated, but it is. There are also other dishes I haven’t had before and all were excellent. The foie gras chawanmushi and the persimmon with shrimp were standouts. The service was precise yet welcoming and warm. It is also a lot of food in total, so expect to feel full by the end! Small and intimate setting, perfect for a dinner with a date or a good friend.

Tempura Matsui – A True Once-in-a-Lifetime Dining Experience

Tempura Matsui was a fantastic and truly unforgettable dining experience. If you’re planning to visit, please come hungry and with an open mind—you will be rewarded in every way. Despite what many online videos suggest about small portions, our experience was quite the opposite. We were served about 14 dishes throughout the evening, and every single one was excellent.

The service was absolutely top-notch from start to finish. The chefs preparing your food are very friendly and engaging, which adds a personal and welcoming touch to the entire experience. You can really feel the care, pride, and precision that goes into every dish.

The menu encourages you to be adventurous, featuring ingredients like conch that some people might not initially find appetizing. However, everything—from the fried tempura dishes to the delicate egg custard soup—was prepared to perfection. Each course was beautifully presented and full of flavor.

While the experience is definitely on the pricey side, believe me when I say it is worth every penny. You will not regret it. This is truly a one-in-a-lifetime dining experience and one that I would highly recommend to anyone looking for something exceptional.

An experience of absolute refinement, quality and respect. A gorgeous, spare room where we had seats at the bar to see the preparation of our lunch. Every course was beautifully presented with detailed instructions on how to eat it optimally. The respect for the ingredients, the attention to detail, the care for us…all of it was top notch. From the pumpkin, hen of the woods mushrooms, shrimp heads and smelt that had arrived from Japan just prior to service, the ingredients were of the best quality and expertly prepared. No wonder they have maintained their star for many years. An experience not to be missed.

I visited Social Corner on Sunday to celebrate my birthday with my family, and the experience was disappointing from the moment we walked in.

The first red flag was that the restaurant was practically empty, with only a few people sitting at the bar. Despite that, the seven of us walked in and were never greeted. We stood there waiting to be acknowledged and were completely ignored. Eventually, we had to seat ourselves and find our own table. Then we had to track someone down from their smoke break just to have tables pushed together for our party. No waitress came to greet us, and we were never offered menus.

Then we noticed the chairs.

The dining chairs were covered in dark stains, what appeared to be built-up grime and debris, worn upholstery, and even damaged fabric exposing the padding underneath. As customers, we shouldn’t have to question the cleanliness of the furniture we’re expected to sit in while eating.

When I brought my concerns to the owner’s attention, instead of apologizing or acknowledging how the chairs looked, she became defensive, annoyed, and visibly upset that we pointed it out. I was told the chairs are bleached and sanitized every day and every night and that the stains “just don’t come out.”

If that’s the case, then they need to be professionally cleaned or replaced. The appearance alone is unacceptable for a restaurant. They looked worst then a park bench!!!! Cleanliness and presentation are part of the dining experience, and these chairs did not inspire confidence.

At that point, my family and I made the decision to leave. Seven paying customers walked out without ordering a single thing because we didn’t feel comfortable dining there.

I came dressed up and excited to celebrate my birthday with my loved ones. Instead, I left feeling ignored, unwelcome, and disgusted by the condition of the establishment and the way our concerns were handled.

Poor customer service. Poor first impression. Poor handling of a legitimate concern.

Seven customers walked out that night, and unfortunately, we won’t be back.

My wife & I were in the neighborhood for show & decided this would be just the right restaurant for our evening out.
We made reservations for 5:30 but arrived at 5:00.
The hostess happily showed us to our seats- smack center in the restaurant.
Milos is a beautiful restaurant and has a fresh upscale feel.
We knew we were on a tight schedule so we already had our dinner pre selected- to save time.
We were ordering off the Pre-fixe theater menu- something i've never done before- and may not do again.
For the sake of saving money, and or time- perhaps...its a good idea but I personally didn't feel comfortable- or at ease ordering this way- I felt like the portions didn't quite live up to expectations.
We ordered Lychee Martinis- they came out very strong.
We returned them for a house Cab & a Mezcal Margarita which were both very good.
We ordered  the whole grilled Dorado & The lobster pasta. I can happily report- both were delicious.
Id definitely go back, but perhaps to the other location just to mix it up a bit.
I do recommend.

Had a wonderful experience at estiatorio Milos Midtown. The seafood was incredibly fresh, beautifully prepared, and the quality really stands out. Service was polished, attentive, and professional without feeling overly formal. The atmosphere is elegant yet comfortable, making it perfect for both a business dinner or a special night out. The grilled fish was outstanding, and every dish felt clean, simple, and focused on premium ingredients. Definitely one of the top spots in Midtown for high-end Mediterranean seafood. Looking forward to coming back.

We had an exceptional lunch today. Every aspect of this restaurant is world-class. The sauted scallops, the big eye Tuna tartare, the fingling potatoes, white beans, and the star of the show, the whole red snapper, the Greek yogurt w greek honey, and the walnut cake. Each dish was so tasty, perfectly prepared and presented, and of the absolute best ingredients available. And a big shout out to Anne, so knowledgeable, friendly, and food savvy.

Absolutely incredible experience. Milos is a well oiled machine and the attention to detail with the service reminded me of the “Forks” episode of The Bear, where every little detail was paid attention to. Amazing spot before a show because they have a fixed pre-theater menu if you choose to go that route (3 courses, $75/pp) which you can add onto as well. They immediately ask you what time your show is and they make sure they get through their whole service and get you out on time to make your show. Most importantly the food was incredible. Highly recommend.

Milos in Midtown is an experience. The moment you walk in, the pristine ice display of whole fish and giant lobster sets the tone: this place is about ultra-fresh seafood, simply prepared. The lunch special is still one of the better deals in Midtown-$40 or so for a three-course meal featuring their famous Greek spread, fried zucchini, and a generous piece of grilled fish. Dinner is another story entirely, with prices that can easily hit $150+ per person before drinks.
The standout for me is the Atlantic lobster (appetizer-sized, but huge) and the grilled Mediterranean sea bass, which is filleted tableside. The saganaki cheese is theatrically flambéed, and the olive oil is so good you'll want to drink it. Service is polished and professional, though it can feel rushed during peak hours.

We love Milos. It never disappoints. Ordering the Special is required eating.  I think the octopus is in that category as well.  It we keep wandering around the menu and enjoy almost all of it.  We tried the red snapper sashimi prepared 2 ways and it was excellent.  The lamb chops are delicious but the price is a little ridiculous.  Which leads me to the “why not 5 stars?” The last 2 times we were there, we were rushed.  No - we did not tell them we were going to a show.  If you order the food it will show up fast.  They are trying to turn the table and it is obvious.  The other is price. I understand they cater to the business account crowd and can keep doing it.  But it makes it unapproachable for most.

Great food, delicious flavor combinations, beautiful atmosphere, and amazing customer service.
The location is excellent as well — super easy to find, especially if you’re coming from Central Park and looking for a good meal.
We had the three-course menu and it was fabulous! The fish was incredibly fresh (you can even see it near the kitchen), and the presentation and taste were impeccable.
I recommend making a reservation in advance since it’s a busy place.
Next time I’m in New York, I’ll definitely come back!

Oh, forgot to mention, the waiter brought fresh herbs and cut them into the olive oil in front of us for the pre dinner bread. It was a nice touch.

top_reviews.content:
What a nice, serendipitous experience. I typed “sandwich” into the Google Maps search bar as I was leaving K-Town, and it routed me to one of my new favorite sandwiches in town.

A gem tucked away on Wilshire, Open Market’s creative expression and curation of cute nostalgia and gadgets had me hooked before even taking a bite.

It was my lucky day, getting the last Beverly they had. With a flavorfully fried exterior, juicy chicken to complement underneath, and a mayo x shredded lettuce top layer between two buttery milk buns, everything is to love.

See you again soon, Open Market.

Holy moly I don’t need a hook for my review; this place lives up to the hype. After my first bite of the Normandie, all I could do was eat more of it.

The sandwich was perfectly hot (very important for my Asian standards lol), perfectly juicy on its own but even more with the au jus, and so flavorful and cheesy. I used to be a sandwich hater and I genuinely think this could solve my parents’ main gripes with sandwiches being hard or dry, plus the meat isn’t cold deli meat.

The drinks are also well-crafted. I got an americano with their original cream top. The coffee was smooth and the cream top wasn’t too sweet, with flavors reminiscent of the buttercream found in Swiss roll cakes.

Interior is very littlefatboyfrankie coded — very thoughtful design that bridges tradition with innovation.

My only two gripes: Can you guys PLEASE turn down the AC?? And maybe make the WiFi a little better?? I can’t tell if it’s a tactic to get us to not study there but your college student audience loves you 😭

It is also a little expensive for the portion but also I was full on half a sandwich so I guess that’s not really a complaint if it lasts me two meals. Also there’s validated underground parking because parking in that area is a nightmare.

Kinda late in joining the club, but made it there! The place looked fun with all the hillarious wall posters of probably their past seasonal menus.

Highly recommended to pre-order probably 15 minutes before you arrived as the line was quite long and the prep time took even longer. Good point it meant everything made fresh to order.

We got their Olympic and Normandie, both of which we were really impressed by, so it really depended on your protein and seasoning preference. I fancied the Olympic which combined flavorful grilled chicken with fried chicken skin. You literally got the combo of juicy meats and crunchy skin. My husband’s pick was the Normandie with tender brisket and melty provolone, which interestingly came with dipping sauce that somewhat reminded me of LA’s iconic long-standing dipped sandwich #IYKYK.

People also seemed to love their drinks and cookies so would certainly try those next.

I ordered the Beverly and the Normandie.

The Beverly was a burger, with crispy fried chicken and kewpie mayo sauce.
The Normandie sandwich had fresh brisket and cheese.
The flavor was good, but the baguette bread made it feel a bit hard.

Americano was rich and had no acidity, so it suited my taste well.

The vibe was lively, and they also sell various items like wine and goods, so it is a place worth visiting.

top_reviews.content: Everything was exceptional—the food, service, and ambience. This is one of the few restaurants I’ve visited where I couldn’t find a single thing to criticize. The only minor thing to note was the madai tempura course, which was a bit too hot. I had to take it out after trying to eat just one bite. Shoutout to every server that day; they truly went out of their way to make my birthday special. Every course was carefully described, beautifully presented, and creative. I was especially impressed by the fluke and sawara courses—both were exceptionally well executed. Other favorites included the venison, the tea course, and the dessert course.

There are meals you enjoy, meals you remember, and then there are meals that fundamentally alter the way you think about food, art, hospitality, and culture. My experience at Saga belongs firmly in that last category.

From the moment you step into the space, the atmosphere is immaculate. The decor is minimalist in the most intentional way, nothing distracts from the experience itself. Every detail feels curated: the lighting, the pacing, the skyline pouring through the windows, the music (which was COOL as hell), the movement of service. It felt cinematic without ever feeling performative. Luxurious without stiffness. Effortless in the way only true mastery can appear effortless.

And the food? I honestly don’t even know how to describe what Chef Charlie Mitchell and his team are accomplishing there.

Every bite was technically stunning, yes, but more importantly, it was emotionally recognizable. During the meal, I found myself identifying very specific flavor memories that felt deeply familiar to me as a Black woman. One seafood course immediately brought to mind a fish fry — and not just any fish fry, but specifically a Detroit fish fry, which I later learned was indeed part of the inspiration. Another dish contained collards and a broth beneath the seafood that I instantly recognized as pot liquor. Not “greens essence.” Not “vegetable broth.” Pot liquor. Living culinary memory. I was shocked to learn that many diners had not picked up on those references because to me they felt so beautifully, unapologetically present.

That is what moved me most about this experience: the elevation of Black foodways without erasing their identity.

This was fine dining that understood lineage.

Chef Charlie’s work feels culturally fluent in a way I have rarely experienced in luxury dining spaces. There is deep technique here, but also deep humanity. You can feel history in the food. Migration. Family tables. Regional Black traditions. Resourcefulness transformed into artistry. It felt like witnessing Black culinary memory treated with the reverence usually reserved for European tradition.

And I have to specifically acknowledge Amy, the sommelier, who was phenomenal. Seeing a Black woman operating with that level of excellence and authority in a space like this genuinely meant something to me. Her presence elevated the experience even further. She was warm, knowledgeable, confident, and absolutely belonged in that room.

Carlos at the bar was equally incredible — charismatic, thoughtful, deeply skilled, and refreshingly himself. Not polished into blandness. Not culturally flattened. Just excellent hospitality with personality and soul intact.

And Harris, our primary server, guided the evening with such care and grace that by the end of the meal, after I asked to leave a note for the chef, he took us into the kitchen to meet Chef Charlie himself. That moment honestly meant the world to me because I needed the team to know: some of us see exactly what they are doing there.

What struck me emotionally was that this space felt profoundly Black in spirit, influence, flavor, rhythm, and cultural reference — and yet I was one of the only Black patrons in the dining room who wasn’t staff.

More Black folks deserve to experience this level of Black excellence.

Because this is not simply “a nice restaurant.” This is art. This is cultural storytelling. This is Black culinary tradition being honored, expanded, elevated, and placed unapologetically within the highest tier of fine dining in the world.

I will think about this meal for years.

top_reviews.content: My first venture out to find a Chinese restaurant in the Flushing Queens area did not disappoint and this was the top spot that Google recommended.  They have received a number of Michelin stars and for good reason.  The service was exceptional and the food was both hot and full of flavor. The chili chicken had the perfect amount of spice and flavor, and the Peking duck was crispy, tender, and honestly one of the best I’ve had. Everything came out fresh and flavorful, and the service was great too. Definitely a spot I’d come back to and recommend to others!

We absolutely love this restaurant! We come here at least twice a month just for the Peking duck and it never disappoints. It’s always crispy, flavorful and so delicious. If you’re visiting, the Peking duck is a must-order, we highly recommend it! Great food every time and we’ll definitely keep coming back.

We ordered Peking duck for takeout, and it was really delicious. One nice option is that for the remaining duck bones, you can choose to have them made into soup or salt-and-pepper style for around $15. We chose the salt-and-pepper version this time because we had tried the soup before.

While waiting for our order, we sat inside the restaurant, and the interior was really beautiful. The decor feels elegant and stylish, which makes the place feel more special even if you are just waiting for takeout.

The prices are definitely not cheap, but the food is truly very good. The Peking duck was flavorful, and the extra salt-and-pepper duck bones were a nice bonus. Overall, it is a great place if you are looking for quality Chinese food and don’t mind paying a little more.

Jiang Nan is a Chinese Fusion restaurant that aims to offer an indulgent and comforting dining experience. Their menu includes traditional entrees (such as Peking Duck, Xiao Long Bao, and Grill Fish), seasonal menus with trending ingredients, and creative drink menus. While a bit on the pricey side, I do think it is worth the cost.

The Stir-fried Shredded Cabbage w. Pork Belly was different than expected. The cabbage was not as crispy as I hoped, but was still delicious. Surprisingly, the pork belly was shredded, rather than the usual thinly sliced. Nonetheless, this dish was delicious and I highly recommend it.

Another highly recommended dish is the Kimchi & Cheese Fried Rice. Delivered in a wooden barrel, there was a perfect mixture of kimchi and cheese. After mixing them, you get an even balance of both flavors and it retains its light touch.

I would also recommend the Braised Beef Flank w. Potato! The beef flank and potatoes were super soft and tender. The chef's special marination was heavenly. I truly wished I ordered a second portion of this. But another light beef dish that is also tasty is the Cutlet Beef W. Nori. The sliced beef cutlet was thinner than I thought, but it made it really soft and easy to bite into. The nori and okonomiyaki sauce is quite strong for this dish, so only order it if you do not mind the taste of nori or okonomiyaki sauce.

The cuisines of the Dominican Republic & Puerto Rico aren't famously vegan-friendly, which makes this spot such a treasure. My wife, our daughter and I had Cauliflower Wings, Salmon Con Coco Mofongo, Birria Tacos & the Sweet & Spicy Oyster Burger. Everything was delicious, and portions are generous, (we were stuffed before we got to the Oyster Burger, which made a very tasty snack as next day leftovers). Spice-averse folks needn't worry, as nothing we ate that was listed as "spicy" blew our lids off. Looking forward to a return visit!

wowowow what a great spot! we spent the day in brooklyn for our honeymoon, and this was one of the highest rated vegan spots nearby. and i will say it was for very good reason! the food was absolutely amazing. we got the empanada duo, which was sooo well priced and very yummy. it was also my first time, as a vegetarian, trying birria tacos and oh my goodness they did not disappoint! i wanted to DRINK the broth. my wife got an oreo cheesecake with ice cream, and it literally melted in your mouth.

i also wanna mention that this place seems very beloved by local vegans; there was a crowd of folks in here who were chatting, hyping up the food, and just generally having a good time.

shout out to our amazing server denzel, who congratulated us on our marriage and was super friendly throughout the night! i wish we were locals so we could try everything this menu has to offer. if you're in brooklyn looking for animal free eats, this is THE spot to stop.

As a 20yr vegan I highly recommend Next stop vegan when in NYC. It’s Caribbean food inspired dishes. The service is really good and very helpful and knowledgeable of the dishes. Also give great plate recommendations depending on your hungry-ness! Having Caribbean food often, I wanted to try things that aren’t as widely available in other restaurants, so I got the Sancocho soup, which was very delicious and I highly recommend. I also got the ribs since not many places offer vegan ribs. Very delicious and tender. I got two meals for myself and the menu is on the pricey side, though splurge on yourself, it was definitely worth it!

Absolutely delicious food. Entire staff had great energy and amazing service, very attentive. I went there today with my family for my birthday and as the only vegan, I was happy they all enjoyed the food. Serving sizes are large as well, we all had to go boxes 😅 would definitely recommend! You won’t be disappointed. The alcapurrias also taste great!

I finally made it to NSV and Wow!!! The food was soooo good!! I had the coconut sauce mofongo with shredded zalmon and it was absolutely phenomenal! The flavors were perfectly balanced and every bite was packed with deliciousness! I could have licked the plate clean!!! I sort of did lol (photos for reference)
I also had the alcapurrias, crispy, flavorful, and just like I remember my mom making them. Everything was amazing and the experience was great from start to finish. I’ll definitely be back!!

top_reviews.content: Our waitress, Eva,  made the whole night wonderful for us! From helping orient me that this was a FRENCH not Italian restaurant (even though there are Mona Lisa portraits)...😂 But who cares. The meals were outstanding, the piano in the background was just the right touch, and you MUST try the Glace a la Lavende Provence ( yep it's French). It is to die for. When we are back in town we will be back for another wonderful time. Really everyone was so welcoming and just sweet. I felt right at home ♥️

From the moment we walked into Rampoldi New York, it felt like an experience rather than just dinner. The ambiance, lighting, elegant design & live music instantly transported us, creating the perfect setting for a special night out. The manager and staff were incredibly warm, attentive, and welcoming throughout the evening, making us feel genuinely cared for.

To start, we both ordered the **Rampoldi** cocktail.. how could we not? It was the perfect balance between sweet and tart. The passion fruit added just the right touch and it was easily one of the best cocktails I've had in a while.

For appetizers, we shared the **Calamar et Courgette Frits** and the **Torchon de Foie Gras de Maison**. The calamari was perfectly crisp and light, while the foie gras torchon with tomato chutney and brioche was rich, decadent, and absolutely delicious.

For our entrées, we ordered the **Filet de Boeuf** and the **Flan de Parmesan "Rampoldi."** The filet was cooked beautifully and paired perfectly with the peppercorn sauce and potato purée.

The Flan de Parmesan was delicious, with layers of eggplant parmigiana, ricotta, spinach, tomato sauce, pesto, and parmesan fondue that came together beautifully. Best I've had!

To finish, we shared the **Meringue au Citron** light and refreshing combination of lemon meringue, vanilla sponge cake, and lemon mousse. It was the perfect ending to an exceptional meal.

Oh!! & let's not forget the espresso Martini we had after dessert. It was the perfect after dinner drink.

I can't wait to return ✨

I had an amazing experience at Rampoldi. The food was absolutely outstanding — every dish tasted fresh, authentic, and beautifully prepared. The pasta was especially memorable, perfectly cooked and full of flavor. What made the evening even better was the service: attentive, professional, and genuinely welcoming without ever feeling rushed. The staff made us feel truly taken care of from start to finish. Definitely one of the best dining experiences in NYC

We discovered this restaurant completely by chance and were truly pleasantly surprised. Everything here is simply perfect — very clean, a cozy and elegant atmosphere, delicious food, and top-level service. You can really feel the attention to every detail — from the presentation to the music, which creates a special ambiance. Live piano music adds even more charm and sophistication to the experience. We were served by Milena — incredibly kind, attentive, and professional. I was genuinely impressed by such outstanding service. Truly a perfect restaurant.

Great italian restaurant close to lincoln center. Beautiful marble walls, beautiful bar. Price fixe menu wiuh  good welections  i strayed and ordered the cod putanesca. Wife had the pruce fixe salmon. Both were rather tasty and well presented. The pea soup was delicious with a generoud serving. We had the sorbet and gelato. Both were excelkent. David was our attendant with an ample crew and the service was excellent. Yo finish it all off, thereis a puano, bass and drums playomg live background music. Prices were not bad for NYC. I would happily rrturn.

top_reviews.content:
A hidden gem inside the Hannam Chain Market! This spot specializes in donkatsu, but today I tried their dakgangjeong (Korean sweet crispy chicken) and was honestly shocked.

The portion size was HUGE — not your typical bite-sized dakgangjeong at all. The pieces were more like full fried chicken size, and the price was super affordable for how much you get.

They also give a separate dipping sauce made with serrano and jalapeño, which I loved. It helped balance out the sweetness of the chicken and added a nice kick.

I also tried the sikhye slush, which was refreshing and sweet (pretty typical for this drink), but perfect after something fried.

Next time I definitely want to come back and try their donkatsu — at this price, it’s hard not to!

Free parking is available, and the service was great. The staff was very helpful with recommendations.
Got the bulgogi tacos, but they were tasteless. Managed to get one taco down, but left the others.

Terrible food I ordered two different kind a kimbob and spicy rice cake. All tasteless awfully presentable nothing taste like authentic korean street food all the ingredients in the kimbop was old and tasteless one roll is -$6&up depending on the different options. I threw away almost more than half after trying there kombop no wonder there ratings are low. I do not recommend this place koreatown plaza parking is crazy inconvenience and over packed.

It's at the food court of the hmart plaza downstairs.
The rice cake is super crispy and the spice is just right.
The fish cake and oden soup was tasty and great for a cold day like today.
Food came out very quick.

Been to back in the days we call this place KTP aka Koreatown Plaza wow it has changed so much.. the pho place might be the only original restaurant still survive maybe the katsu place.. but this place Awoolim tasty and unique

Well I did give service 5 stars not really for the service since it’s not a full service restaurant but the ahjushi in the front who took my order was really nice and understood that I had my 3.5 year old and it was lunch time packed and he got my order really fast and I think I ordered not once but twice because my kids were not cooperating..

The tteokochi not pictured was not too spicy and tasty

The fried shumai was ok but the tacoyaki was tasty and fish cake soup.. basically this would be Korean version of street food except fried shumai you will not find in Korea as this isn’t Korea also tacoyaki also isn’t Korean food  other than that

I would return try others as they do have gimbap..

top_reviews.content: Our waiter TK was fantastic and he was incredibly kind and attentive. The food was amazing and it came out very fast. We got the “Family Table - Set for 4” and added a dish and mango sticky rice. Drinks were amazing as well! Highly recommend coming to this restaurant if you are looking for a great night spot for Thai food🇹🇭

My new favourite Thai restaurant in New York City!
As a Thai person this place have a nice twist on ingredients that still provides perfect Thai flavour!
There are a couple dishes that gave me nostalgia from things I had when I was young!
Love the cocktails and super impress how well they paired with food especially the Muangbao with Pad Thai and for dessert of Mango sticky rice paired really well with Leonardo on the beach, their version of Pina Colada with Pandan 🍹🍸
Absolutely fantastic service and friendly easy to approach staff!

Possibly the best Thai food we have ever had. Energy is great, service is polite and knowledgeable. We walked in, no reservation on a busy evening and the host was simply marvelous, not just because he made us wait not longer than 15” but his presence was radiant and professional. We ended up at the bar counter and had the pleasure to watch the amazing detailed work of the mixologists. Taste it too 😅 Perfection. We tried an array of different dishes, fish, lamb, curry, appetizers and one was better than the other. Flavorful, unique, well executed and quality you can taste. Food was expensive but excellent and we didn’t mind paying for the quality and the talent displayed by the chef. Divine chef. I so wanted to congratulate and to shake  your hand personally if even possible next time, soon very soon. Can’t wait to go back.
The restaurant is loud but loud of lively energy. Didn’t mind it!

I would give them 1000 stars if I could.  This was honestly thee most incredible Thai food I've ever had in my life. I have gone to so many Thai places in New York City and this one beats them all. I love the intimate set up. It feels cozy yet open at the same time. People from all different walks of life step foot in here. Atmosphere was flourishing. The food was like nothing I've ever tried before. Ingredients used to create such unique dishes,  appeared to be sacred because they are things I have not ever seen on a menu. I would 110% recommend this restaurant to anyone whether visiting going out on a date or just looking for a place to go to after a long walk, It will fit any aesthetic! Oh, might I add,  the service was top-notch. Our waiter was very helpful with the menu and accommodating to our dietary restrictions. He kept a gleaming smile on his face the whole night. Thank you for providing such an experience. I will definitely be back.

A table of three ordered Three shareable dishes, that included wings, beef, fried rice, and potato puffs .
One soup dish with fish and two desserts, which included ice cream and mango sticky rice and Four cocktails- Total around 230

We loved their 99$ menu option for 2 people.

Our fav dishes were:
- Baerng Golae (S): Coconut crisp, grilled shrimp, and famous curry paste from southern Thailand.
- Squid Ink Fried Rice: Fried rice, colossal crab meat, egg, and squid with the aromatic squid ink sauce, fried garlic, cucumber, and cilantro come with prik nam pla.

The crab curry was too hot (according the waitress it’s 7/10 spicy but it ended up feeling like way more for someone who never has hot food).

The veggies were very well cooked.

The Yum Som-O (Fresh Pomelo, fried cured branzino, chili, lemongrass shallot, mint, cilantro with nahm pla whan dressing) was fresh and sweet and we loved every bite! The only thing that surprised us is that the pieces of fish were way smaller than they appear in their website.

Finally, the atmosphere was great! It’s wasn’t too loud, too cold/hot, too dark. It was perfect.

The waitresses were fast and kind. We had booked a table for 2 and we had indicated that we didn’t want to sit right under the AC and when we arrived that’s the table we got. We asked them to change and they quickly adapted.

No complaints, we will come back!!

Excellent experience. Food was outstanding.  Very clear the seafood is fresh and each dish was prepared individually. Service was excellent.  We asked a lot of questions and for recommendations.  Service was fast and the staff was friendly. Atmosphere was calming.  Had lunch there on a Friday and while the place was busy, it was not loud in there and having a conversation at your table was very easy. The only comment that I would make is for people to know that the spice levels cannot be adjusted.

Love this spot!
Food is flavorful, service is great.

Definitely get a reservation and it gets packed lunch or dinner.
Seating can be tight but that’s not a surprise.

The pad Thai is my go to. Since it’s a southern style pad Thai, it’s more creamy and personally, more tart/ketchupy.
The squid ink crab fried rice has a lot of flavor with the added squid.

Desserts are no frills, delicious.

Highly recommend! One of my tops!

The absolute best! Every dish was delicious and flavorful and a very fair price, and the service was top notch. Will be back many more times!

Recommend the fried branzino, shrimp curry, 6 hours braised pork belly, and the squid ink fried rice!

top_reviews.content: They have a little bit of everything here. Irish fare, lobster, oysters to steak, burgers and wings. Haven’t had a homemade Caesar dressing in Sunnyside for a while, and my Caesar salad was to die for. My kid loves the homemade ranch sauce to dip everything in. The burger was top tier along with the brioche it came on. Ribs were fall off the bone and sauced with bbq.The Steak was prepared nicely and the sauce it came with was zesty and yummy too. Oysters were fresh, grilled octopus was tender and the wings were really good standard wings. The server, Leah was pleasant, attentive and informative.  Bartender made a very good happy hour margarita so, I’ll be back for brunch or Sunday dinner. Hopefully both.

Recently my partner and I went to eat cousin larry’s. The server/bartender had informed us that they just opened when we got there and sat us down immediately.

Our server was great, took care of us and kept us informed that the kitchen needed a minute to set up before food came out.

The food unfortunately was lackluster. My partner ordered the steak with baked potato but they mentioned the potato would take awhile and offered to substitute for french fries and I got baby back ribs with broccolini.

Both of our meals weren’t hot to start off, and my partner’s steak was overcooked when she ordered it medium. I didn’t go crazy for my portion size of ribs. Flavor was there but it wasn’t hot which was disappointing.

You’d think that since they just setup stuff they would take more time to cook the food properly but it was a bummer to say the least.

Our server once again was solid and she definitely took good care of us along with more guests coming in throughout the day.

Hope this helps anyone who’s looking to go. Nice atmosphere, but the food was disappointing.

This restaurant does not reinvent the wheel, but everything is SO well done! I got the fish and chips and my friend had the salmon with mash potatoes and broccolini. Both dishes tasted amazing. The drinks were also super good and well priced, and the ambiance was nostalgic and dreamy Americana. Can’t wait to go back.

Update: After talking my boyfriend’s ear off about this place, I brought him here two weeks after my initial review and he finally understood why I love it so much. We can confidently say that their brunch burger is the best burger in Woodside/Sunnyside too. And their drinks are strong. Delicious and STRONG.
Very good Foodies. The pancakes are bomb, the mozzarella sticks are good but it's so big (Pause on that).Very nice/pretty waitress

AMAZING PLACE! From the moment we stepped into Cousin Larry’s, we were greeted with a warmth and hospitality that made us feel like longtime friends. The staff goes above and beyond to make every guest feel welcome and well cared for, creating an inviting atmosphere that made our visit even more enjoyable.

The handcrafted margaritas, made with fresh ingredients, was a standout! We opted for the brunch special, which included bottomless margaritas at a great value! The pancakes, sausage, and eggs were delicious, with the maple syrup butter bringing them over the top. The breakfast burger, served with crispy French fries, was both flavorful and cooked to perfection.

We enjoyed ourselves so much that we decided to stay through dinner, where we had the opportunity to try the beef stew—it was absolutely phenomenal. The flavors were rich and comforting, making it the highlight of the evening. Chef’s kiss!

We also had mozzarella sticks and cheesecake, which we devoured so quickly that we forgot to get any photos! 😂 Both were fantastic.

Overall, Cousin Larry’s exceeded expectations in every way. The combination of delicious food, excellent service, and a welcoming ambiance makes it a place I highly recommend. Whether you’re stopping by for brunch, dinner, or just a drink, you won’t be disappointed.

10/10 – I’ll definitely be back!

Came here for dinner as a family last night and spent over $100 on a meal that was filled with missteps (food took at least 45 minutes to come out, they were out of fries so we ordered roasted potatoes and a baked potato that were so undercooked we couldn’t even pierce them with a fork, burger patties were way overcooked and too small for the bun so the burger tasted like all bread, and we were charged for 3 rib entrees when we only ordered one). We mentioned these issues to the staff when they finally came to clear our plates, and received an apology and half-hearted offer to take off the inedible potatoes, which we declined because it felt like too little too late, and we weren’t complaining to try to get free stuff. We left feeling still hungry and annoyed with our experience at Cousin Larry’s and definitely won’t be going back.
Nice place to eat. I had a strip steak (cooked rare as I had requested) with some excellent fingerling potatoes and a good au poivre sauce on the side.

I have been here last year and i had solid experience. Couple nights ago i had smoked ribs and was fine altough glass off beer came with a lipstick mark on. While waiting for a server took eternity so i just finished the beer and got new one.
Today i visited and ordered a steak, so disappointing, Bartender that i ordered with didnt even check on it, steak was fully overcooked and chewy.
New bartender came and I said that steak was bad and ordered just some wings cause i was still hungry. Not even offered to replace items or anything at all. Got fully charged for the both meals and  didn’t even had 2 bites of the steak.
And it’s not even about the money, it’s just about the service and respect to the customers.

top_reviews.content: Loved the food, me and my girlfriend love Mediterranean food, fries were great we both loved them, first time going there so will try them again, to try different foods. They also have a kids menu which was great, plus crayons and activities on a paper. Also, good thing I called because they were ful,l so I reserved for 30 minutes later and was all set. So try calling before you go there just in case

I stopped by Yasouvlaki on a Sunday evening before heading home, planning to have a couple of appetizers and a glass of wine.

What I expected to be a quick stop turned into one of the highlights of my evening.
Everything was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared.

The grilled shrimp were perfectly cooked, tender, and packed with flavor.

The dips were absolutely delicious—creamy, vibrant, and impossible to stop eating with the warm pita bread.

Paired with a glass of sparkling wine, it was the perfect way to slow down and enjoy my trip to home.

What I loved most was how comfortable and welcoming the restaurant felt.
My server MADISON was amazing♡
She offered a top notch service!

Sometimes it's about finding a place that serves great food, makes you feel welcome, and turns an ordinary Sunday into something special.

Yasouvlaki did exactly that, and I can't wait to come back for a full meal next time.

We were able to get a table last minute, quickly on a Friday night, which was great. The place was packed around 7pm then cleared out by 8pm.

The food is well portioned, tasty and reasonably priced. This is why they have such a robust take out operation. Their wine list is almost exclusively Greek, but have no fear these are French/Californian tasting options and fairly priced per glass, as well.

This was our first time dining in and it was sadly an underwhelming experience. The serving staff let us know there would be a delay in the kitchen, but after almost an hour in between our appetizer and main dishes, and the staffers not keeping a pulse on how we were doing, I have to give a lower service rating.

They did give us comped dessert which my wife really appreciated.

This is an upper east side easy putt no brainer option especially if you’re in the mood for Greek!

Had the lunch special and really enjoyed it. The salad was the highlight a huuuge portion, super fresh, great ingredients = 10/10. The chicken souvlaki was excellent (and better than the salmon, which I also tried and which is nice). Service was a little slower than expected (the salad took over 20 minutes), but the portion more than made up for it and so did the young server who was very friendly (we joked that he had a Greek face, apparently his grandparents lived in Spain, so there is the Mediterranean tie!). Overall it’s a great lunch spot, should definitely come back

I had a 5-star experience at this restaurant. I ordered the kefta platter, and it was excellent—very flavorful and cooked perfectly.

The staff were friendly and accommodating, which made the visit even better. The service was smooth and welcoming from start to finish.

I would definitely come back and highly recommend this place.

One word: Amazing! Food was absolutely delicious, and the service was top-tier. A special thanks to our wonderful waitress, Madison—her recommendations were spot on, and we thoroughly enjoyed every dish, including the dessert. She made the experience even more memorable with her kindness and attention to detail. I highly recommend this place and will definitely be back!

Coming here is a trip to the Mediterranean! I got Brussel sprout salad with chicken skewers and me and my partner enjoyed it. Tender and moist chicken and flavorful salad, very filling. We got some other stuff but this is my favorite. Staff is very attentive and kind.

Had the lunch special and it was so worth it! The portions were generous, the food was fresh and delicious, and everything came out perfectly. The servers were also very nice and welcoming which made the experience even better. Definitely coming back again!

top_reviews.content:
Robert is a wonderful destination for a leisurely weekend brunch or an elegant fine-dining experience. Overlooking Central Park, it offers breathtaking panoramic views of the city skyline and its iconic skyscrapers.

The menu is exquisite, with a thoughtfully curated selection of dishes. I particularly recommend the Green Pea & Asparagus Soufflé and the Roasted Vegetable Quiche, both of which were delightful. I also tried the Short Rib Reuben Sandwich, which was fairly decent and a satisfying choice.

Overall, Robert is a lovely spot to enjoy delicious food while taking in spectacular views of the city.

Amazing views and a wonderful meal! The server was incredibly kind and attentive.
I visited during Restaurant Week, and it was such a memorable experience. I was a little worried that the cooked salmon might taste fishy, but it was absolutely delicious. On top of that, we were even treated to a complimentary dessert, which truly made the experience special.

I visited as I’m about to graduate from my language school, and it turned into such a wonderful memory. I’d really love to come back one more time before I head home.

Upon walking in we saw that it’s currently pink and orange like a verrrry fancy Dunkin Donuts haha ~ and while the view is show-stopping & breathtaking ~ the service was actually bad. My friend got hit in the head THREE times by the waiter delivering items. I got stared at with no smiles while I was walking in and to the bathroom. There was a bit of a snuff at the way we wanted to take home the leftovers…

The food however was beautifully presented, and great especially for my vegetarian friend. I got the chicken which was nice and classic but a little bit boring, and my other friend got the salmon which for me was much too curry-forward. The veg risotto had a bit of a wine taste still, like it didn’t cook off all the way. The meatballs were tasty, but seemingly not “stuffed” with mozzarella. The best parts of the meal there were just the cauliflower purée, green beans, salted butter with fresh bread, watermelon salad, & the beautiful macaroon style dessert with fruits & chocolate cake. The truffle fries were nice but extremely greasy and gave us all little stomach aches.

The service needs to be revamped completely! It’s not friendly and it’s not posh. It’s something in between and it does not work. In the end I would go back for the DELICIOUS mocktails and that perfect NYC Central Park view 🏙️

Just perfect.  Everything from the ambiance of the location, which gorgeously overlooks Central Park West and the park itself, it's a gorgeous restaurant.  The service was very friendly, at times slower than we wanted, but it made up for it with stunning looking dishes and unbelievable taste.  It's an experience I will not forget and highly recommend.

We have chosen this restaurant for my girlfriend’s birthday celebration and they didn’t disappoint us at all . Place has a nice beautiful view overlooking the Columbus circle area where the hustle of a city meets the calm of Central Park . Beautiful view. Service was outstanding. Our waiter Victor was very professional and very attentive , helpful and sweet ! It was so nice of him to provide kind of birthday treat for my girlfriend, like a plate with some small cakes with candles and her name written with chocolate. That was so sweet and it also was complimentary. Food was good, drinks were delicious. Atmosphere is so relaxing and enjoyable. There is beautiful piece of art on one of the walls in restaurant, which makes this place delightful as well. Also you can enjoy the live music vibes , which makes the experience even more wonderful. We loved everything about this place  and we would definitely come back 🫶

Oh the view of Central Park makes it fabulous and I am completely surprised by the fantastic food and service. We were walkins after a museum visit. Drinks walking by made the decisions easy....may I have one of those? See the photos of.our food. Even the bread was delicious. Go. Make a reservation just to help them accommodate you.

This restaurant is so beautiful, it really matches the modern, artsy aesthetic of the museum it sits on top of (the Museum of Art and Design).     The staff were amazing, they made a special event even more enjoyable, and were always ready to help. Brought the family to Maison Pickle and left seriously impressed. The lobster mac & cheese was rich and decadent without being heavy — creamy, loaded with lobster, the kind of dish you want to order again before you’ve finished it. Steak frites was cooked exactly right, and the fries were crispy perfection. The lobster escargot was a standout — a clever, elevated twist that surprised us in the best way.

The deluxe French dip sandwich was hearty and packed with flavor, and the garlic butter parmesan pull-apart bread might be the sleeper hit of the meal — warm, savory, and dangerously easy to keep pulling apart.

We finished with the 24-layer chocolate cake (an absolute showstopper, both visually and on the fork) and a classic crème brûlée that hit all the right notes — crisp top, silky custard underneath.

Great food, great vibe, perfect spot for a family outing on the Upper West Side. Highly recommend.

Another birthday dinner for the books! Maison Pickle is a very cozy, beautifully designed restaurant in the Upper West Side.

I also got the steak tartare, which was fresh and fragrant. Joe got the spinach artichoke dip, which was some of the best spin-art we’ve both ever had. For my entree I had the maison signature cheesesteak and Joe got his classic steak frite. My cheesesteak was delicious, and the bread was fresh and crispy. I was already too full off pull-apart bread, so I ended up taking my sandwich mostly to go. Joe’s ribeye was cooked to perfection and if you don’t know, the man loves a hand-cut fry.

It was my birthday, so even tho I was full, I had to order dessert. This place is known for many things including their 24 layer cakes. We are already planning our next trip back, and it couldn’t come quicker!

I had an Amazing expérience at Sylvia's Restaurant !
The cornbread was absolutely outstanding without a doubt one the best I've ever had. It was perfectly moist, flavorful, and simply unforgettable.
The fried chicken was also incredibly delicious: crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, and packed with flavor.
You can really taste the soul and tradition in every bite.
If you're looking for authentic soul food in Harlem, I highly recommend Sylvia's Restaurant without hésitation. Great food, great atmosphere, and a truly mémorable dining experience. I would definitely come back !

Sylvia's has been here since 1962 and the whole place feels like it knows that. The walls are covered in signed celebrity photos, the room is loud and warm and packed with people who all seem to be having a very good time, and the staff moves through the dining room with the kind of easy confidence you get from feeding people the same beloved food for generations. Sylvia Woods started this with 35 seats on Lenox Avenue and it now takes up nearly a full city block with multiple dining rooms and space for close to 450 people. That's not an accident.
Hot cornbread shows up at the table when you sit down and it's buttery and good and the kind of thing you have to be careful not to finish before the food arrives. The fried chicken is the thing most people come here for first and it delivers exactly what you want: dark meat, properly seasoned, with a crispy crust that stays together when you pick it up. Every entree comes with two sides and that's where things get competitive because the mac and cheese is the one that keeps coming up in everyone's meal for good reason, three-cheese baked and creamy without being loose, the kind of mac you actually remember afterward. The candied yams are sweet and soft, the collard greens have a good depth from the smoked turkey they cook with them, and the BBQ pork ribs in Sylvia's "sassy sauce" are the other thing worth ordering if you're going all in. That sauce is tangy and a little sweet and clings to the ribs the way a good BBQ sauce should. By the time the peach cobbler arrived we were already well past the point of reasonable consumption and it was completely worth it.
The Sunday gospel brunch is its own separate event and draws a crowd for good reason. If your timing works out, that's the version of Sylvia's to experience at least once.

Either way, it is definitely a treat for a palate desiring the exotic spices of Asia. Don’t forget to get some pistachio ice cream and yogurt to cleanse the palate. Once you stop trying to see all of it and just start eating, it clicks.
We landed at La Pizza & La Pasta, which is the sit-down restaurant inside the main floor where Neapolitan-trained pizzaioli work a wood-burning oven in full view of the room. The Margherita Verace is the pizza to start with and it's the real version, San Marzano tomatoes, proper fior di latte, a soft and slightly charred crust that doesn't try to do more than it needs to. The spaghetto al pomodoro is listed on the menu as the dish that represents Italy, which is a confident claim, but it backs it up: just spaghetti with tomatoes, olive oil, basil, and Sicilian sea salt, cooked in a way where the simplicity is entirely the point and entirely the achievement. We also grabbed a portobello panini from one of the market counters to eat standing up, which is honestly one of the more satisfying ways to experience Eataly. The housemade focaccia is worth picking up at the bread counter as you wander. And the gelato at the end is the thing that gets most people, the pistachio in particular is one of those bites that makes you understand why people line up for it.
The rooftop beer hall is open year-round and is a genuinely good spot for a drink and a view before or after eating. The whole place is worth at least two hours of your time if you're the type of person who likes to wander through food.

It’s the kind of comfort food that hugs you from the inside out—rich broth, perfectly balanced flavors, and ingredients that taste like they were prepped just hours before.
And don’t even get me started on the lunch specials—they are unbelievably worth it. Generous portions, great variety, and prices that make you feel like you’re getting way more than you paid for. It’s become my go-to midday spot because the quality and value are unbeatable.

Otto Sushi has been our favorite sushi place for years, and honestly, no matter how many other places we try, we always come back.

One thing we love most is consistency. Every single time we order, we know exactly what we’re going to get: incredibly fresh fish, beautifully prepared rolls, and food that is clearly made with care and attention to detail. There’s never any disappointment and never any guessing whether this order will be as good as the last one.

What sets Otto Sushi apart is the quality. The fish is always fresh and flavorful, the portions are generous, and every ingredient feels thoughtfully selected. Nothing tastes mass-produced or rushed. The sauces, seasonings, and flavor combinations are balanced perfectly, allowing each ingredient to shine without overwhelming the others.

It’s hard to describe, but you can genuinely taste the difference between sushi that’s simply made and sushi that’s crafted by people who care about what they’re serving. Every bite feels fresh, clean, and incredibly satisfying.

At this point, whenever we place an order, we actually look forward to its arrival because we know Otto Sushi will never let us down. The food is always delicious, consistently high-quality, and prepared with the same attention to detail we’ve come to appreciate over the years.

Thank you, Otto Sushi, for setting the standard so high and for being our go-to place whenever we’re craving great Japanese food. Highly recommended!

5 stars, no notes, will be coming back to try more of their delicious food. Welcome to Astoria Burmese Bites we are so glad you came to the neighborhood!

The food was just as delicious as I remembered. We tried the keema palata, nan gyi noodles, fried wontons, and Burmese milk tea( literally hit the Myanmar taste) and everything was fresh, flavorful, and full of authentic taste.

I’m really happy they found a new home in Astoria.

If you’ve never tried Burmese food before, this is the perfect place to start.

TL;DR: Halal Burmese joint with excellent curries in particular. Might be closer to a 4, but I'll bump it up until I try it again

I went to the new Burmese Bites location with a group about a week ago, having had their food before at the Queens Night Market but never having unfortunately gone to their whole location in a mall in Elmhurst. There were many people waiting for tables or takeout while we were eating, and especially afterward, so you may want to come early.

The first dish that arrived was their alright take on the Burmese national dish, Mohinga for $15. As we were splitting everything, they provided bowls and extra spoons for everyone, and the portion was definitely decent for the price. The dish was decent, but it felt like it was missing something. I like the amount of fritters, but I wish there were more banana blossom for texture. I also felt the flavor was a bit too light compared to either Sophie's or Asian Bowl, and less thick. I'm not sure if it's because they're straining it too much, but the dish needed the fish sauce on the table to add more flavor, which is usually not the case. The most comparable version is at Little Myanmar, which definitely isn't my favorite version of this soup.

The other comparable dish, but better, was the Lahpet Thoke for the same price. Compared to other places, the size was between Asian Bowl and Sophie's, and the flavor was much better than Asian Bowl's, as theirs was a bit wet. The dish otherwise had a nice fermented flavor with a good amount of crunchiness, as it should, though it could have used a little bit more heat. Overall, I liked it, with the only better version being the much more expensive one at Little Myanmar.

Our only other appetizer was something I added to the meal. This was their excellent Keema Palata for $12. I decided to add this partially because I love this dish, and it was one of the things I liked a lot when they served it at the Night Market. The portion was plentiful, and the chicken inside was well spiced with a bit of butteriness from the palata, which is the Burmese version of a paratha, of course. I guess the only complaint I can make is that some of the crust felt a bit overcooked, but not so much that it wasn't enjoyable. I would recommend this.

The other main dishes all came with rice and were less comparable and better. My favorite, barely, was the NgaShint Chaut Sat for $25. It reminded me of a better version of a similar dish you can find in many Szechuan spots. By comparison, the dish had a nice mix of sweetness and spice with a definite kick. I also preferred the eel, as it was cut up into bigger pieces and it wasn't overly fried, so you could still get a bit of texture. The fried garlic added a nice aroma throughout the dish, as well as some good crunch, along with the chili and other spices. This was wonderful.

Most people's favorite was the $19 Ah Meh Tha Hin. The beef itself was fork-tender, so a knife wasn't necessary. The spices from the rather thick curry included some nice herbal sourness from the lemongrass, along with some heat and a bit of sweetness. Due to the thickness and spices, the curry reminded me, to an extent, of some semi-dry rendangs, but less coconut-forward and a bit less fiery. I would highly recommend this.

The last dish was the other $19 curry, the Nga Hin. The fish in this case was swai, or basa/catfish. The fish itself was tender, but it didn't fully fall apart in the curry, which I liked, as it kept some texture. The curry itself was on the slightly sour end, but not too much for any of our palates. This was also very tasty, and I would recommend it if you want a curry that is flavorful but not spicy.

I would prefer to go back to this place before giving it a true rating to try the Shan Noodles and other dishes I am more familiar with, but based on what I tried, I liked it. This is another nice option in the area for those looking for a different halal food experience, and it's great if you're not in the mood to go to Elmhurst for other Burmese options.

Been following them even before they were in the Queens Mall food court, and now they finally settled in a much bigger place in Astoria, with an even bigger menu! Truly the best new addition to the neighborhood.

It’s incredible, unlike any other fish curries I’ve tried before. It’s feels light and refreshing and hitting all the notes. Beef Curry was almost Rendang-like. Their blanched peashoot salad with salad was a surprise hit! I probably wouldn’t get the crudites with the blended fish dipping thingy again next time. Excited to come back and try more!

Loaded with bold flavor and real ingredients—seafood and beef stacked so high you can barely see the noodles. The hand-pulled noodles are extra chewy and bouncy, and the spicy broth clings beautifully to every bite.

Non-Spicy Seafood Noodle
Perfect if you’re not into spicy food. The broth is milky and slightly creamy, almost like a white soup base, topped with bonito flakes—such an unexpected touch. The bowl is packed with seafood and vegetables, super fresh. Highly recommended.

Fried Pork with Sweet & Sour Sauce
Another crowd favorite. Think crispy pork bites with the sweet and sour sauce on the side so you can dip as you like. Tastes great on its own, but also surprisingly good added into the noodle soup.

Deep Fried Meat Dumpling
Korean dumplings are no joke—huge, crispy outside, juicy meat filling inside, and yes, they burst with flavor. Not greasy at all, and the house dipping sauce ties everything together.

A Classic New York Diner Experience at Court Square Diner

I recently visited Court Square Diner at 45-30 23rd Street in Long Island City, NY, and it was an outstanding experience from beginning to end. One of the things that immediately stands out about this diner is that it is open 24 hours a day, making it a perfect place to enjoy a meal at any time. Whether you’re looking for breakfast, lunch, dinner, or a late-night bite, Court Square Diner is always ready to welcome guests.

The diner has a wonderful retro atmosphere that captures the classic New York diner experience. Walking inside feels like stepping back in time, with its vintage design, comfortable seating, and nostalgic charm. It’s easy to see why this establishment has been serving American comfort food since 1946. The combination of history and character makes dining here feel special.

Another thing that impressed me was the massive menu. There are so many choices that everyone can find something they love. During my visit, I had the opportunity to try several items, including the pancakes, milkshake, steak, and omelette. Every dish exceeded my expectations. The pancakes were fluffy, fresh, and perfectly cooked. The milkshake was thick, creamy, and full of flavor. The steak was tender, juicy, and cooked exactly as requested, while the omelette was generously filled and incredibly satisfying.

Beyond the excellent food, the service was equally impressive. The server was friendly, attentive, and professional throughout the meal. They checked on us regularly, made sure everything was perfect, and created a welcoming atmosphere that made the experience even more enjoyable.

Overall, Court Square Diner is everything you want from a classic American diner: delicious food, generous portions, a huge menu, excellent service, and a charming retro environment. It’s a place that delivers both quality and consistency. I highly recommend Court Square Diner to anyone visiting Long Island City or looking for an authentic New York diner experience. Been seeing this place all over my feed – people have spotted LE SSERAFIM here, and my Ktown regular friends kept insisting the meat quality is top-tier. Finally made it right when they opened and it did not disappoint.

The vibe is great for date nights, birthdays, or just a fun dinner out. The bar area is gorgeous and the drink menu is extensive.

I will premise by stating I rarely sacrifice my free time writing a review, let alone a less-than positive one, as I'm not one to be negative. That said, I have no choice in this matter, and here is precisely as to why. In good conscience, I have to trade my personal time writing this, so others can know about this place and let it be their decision at that point to make the same mistake I did in going here or not. When I placed my order, I first asked if they had margherita pizza, as it was not listed on the menu. She asked, "You mean cheese pizza?" I said, "No, margherita pizza, with, yes, cheese does come on it, but it is fresh ball shaped mozzarella cheese, and it also has on it sliced tomatoes and whole basil leaves... you know--the traditional Neapolitan pizza?..." She said, "Yeah, cheese pizza." She said it in the most deliberately condescending way she possibly could have. For sake of efficiency at that point, I then stated, "Okay, to be clear, I would like fresh ball shaped mozzarella cheese with whole basil leaves and sliced tomatoes spread across the pizza." She responded with, "Basil?" I said, "Yes, the green leaf plant that sometimes is put on pizzas…" She, and again in an entirely condescending way, said, "Yes, that is what basil is." I shook my head yes, and again reiterated that I wanted a pizza with whole basil leaves, sliced tomatoes, and fresh balls of mozzarella on it. I also ordered a Peroni beer. She said I looked way too young to be 21, and asked for my ID. I didn't have it though I am 45 years old, and my beard and hair are all virtually completely grey. And it is quite obvious it's been decades since I looked anywhere near 21. But I said, "I will take an ice tea instead, as well tried to ease the tension by stating, "Thank you for the compliment for thinking I look so much younger than I am." This was met with a complete and utter glare of animosity from her. Then she went back behind the counter, and she stated, in Italian, quite loudly to the cook there, "Stupid tourist wants cheese pizza." She assumed I did not understand Italian. Though I do, having lived in Italy twice. Shortly after that, and to be fair, the cook brought out the pizza within five minutes. So it wasn't a long wait time at all. However, despite me having reiterated three times exactly what I wanted on the pizza, it arrived with only cheese, and not mozzarella either, and literally only two small basil leaves. I hate conflict, so I ate most of the pizza, and didn’t demand it to be “remade”, like probably most customers would have. And not that it was fresh to begin with in that amount time. The pizza itself was slightly better than a frozen Digiorno. The sauce and cheese were alright. It was clear the dough was the premade store-bought frozen kind, which wasn't very good at all. Right when I was finishing eating, two African American men came into the restaurant. She, the server, promptly told them, "The oven is broken." They left. Shortly after that, an Asian couple came in and she seated them. Take that for what you will. I can only state what I saw, and that was it. It was around $30 for a "12 inch" cheese pizza that was really more like a 10 inch and one ice tea. I live within a couple minutes of the Pier so I understand that food is relatively more expensive in the area, but the quality needs to be there. More importantly, the completely unprofessional and aggressive behavior by the server is what very much appears to be the reason this place was really slow business-wise on the weekend. NYC typically rivals the Chinese food you can find in the Bay Area and Hupo certainly helps that case. Focusing on Sichuan style cuisine, Hupo has a wide array of entrees and bites that will leave you full and wanting to come back for more. They certainly do deserve their Bib Gourmand. We had a reservation for 5 set for dinner and were glad we did so as the place was very busy when we arrived. The interior is clean and simple with no frills. Once seated we were informed that they only have digital menus through a QR code which was a bit difficult to navigate with 2 out of the 5 of us being older and not as tech savvy but we figured it out anyways.

We ordered a few different entrees and split them family style so we’ll go over them generally. Side note: although many of the dishes are noted as being spicy you can request that they be made without any spice. For dim sum/appetizers we ordered the scallion pancakes and pork soup dumplings. The scallion pancakes were okay, nothing special about them but the pork soup dumplings were a bit better with a tasty broth inside and nice chewy dumplings. For entrees we got duck fried rice, braised beef noodle soup, beef with broccoli, and dan dan noodles.

The duck fried rice was very good. Many places opt to use day-old rice for fried rice and you can often tell by the texture, but if they do that here then we were fooled because the rice tastes fresh and the duck was perfect. The braised beef noodle soup was also good, not the best we’ve had, but still good with the beef having a nice texture and the broth being rich. The beef with broccoli was great, the beef velvetized and delicious, the broccoli, well, broccoli. Lastly, the dan dan noodles were fantastic. The noodles were cooked perfect, the minced beef very delicious, and the bok choy tasty as well. As it is food wise, Hupo is a standout, particularly in the Western Queens area, the only knock being its service is a bit iffy with the workers being not too warm but for the meal you get, we’re willing to shut up and just eat. A fantastic restaurant all around!

I came here with my out-of-town guests, who chose this place. I didn’t know there was a restaurant that specialized in samgyetang, so I was excited to try it.

Since this is a samgyetang specialty shop, the menu is limited and mainly focuses on chicken stew. As it was my first time here, I had to try the classic samgyetang. One of my friends ordered the samgyetang with abalone, which intrigued me because I didn’t know they were served together. I was curious to see how it would taste.

My samgyetang arrived piping hot, and I ordered it at a medium spice level. We also ordered extra rice because we thought drinking soup alone wouldn’t be filling enough. However, the soup already contained sweet rice, and it turned out to be very filling. The broth was flavorful, and the chicken was tender. My friend, who ordered the version with abalone, had to wait about five minutes for the abalone to finish cooking in the hot soup. He said the abalone was tasty and was satisfied with his meal.

The servers here are mainly Mexican rather than Korean, which surprised me, but the service was adequate and attentive.

Parking is easy since the restaurant shares a large parking lot with other shops in the strip mall. Street parking is also available.

I would recommend trying the samgyetang with abalone, as it’s not something you find everywhere. I’ll definitely be ordering that next time!

Before I get into the review, it is very important for DineLA fans to know that Odyssey's Lunch DineLA ends at 4:00pm, not 4:30pm like it says on the website/menu.

First of all, the brand-new renovation is modern (in a timeless way) and gorgeous, and of course the views are as breathtaking as ever. My family and I all ordered the shrimp and the salmon, and both dishes were picturesque, delicious, and reasonable portions. Off of the regular menu, we also tried the four-cheese Mac and cheese, which was creamy excellence - you can't go wrong with gruyere! The server who served us was Jesus, and he did a phenomenal job. I'm so glad that the San Fernando Valley has a restaurant as scenic and high-quality as Odyssey 👍🏻

I visited the Odyssey Restaurant & Events Center for the first time in over 4 years, and what a great job they have done with the re-model! The Truffle Popcorn 🍿 Chicken & Chilean Seabass were delicious, and I enjoyed the tasty cocktails as well. I recommend visiting this restaurant with your loved ones for any special occasion!

Odyssey Restaurant & Events — Granada Hills
Perched on a hilltop with sweeping city views, Odyssey is one of those rare spots that manages to feel both elegant and approachable. I stopped by for a birthday party, and from the moment you arrive, there's something special about the place.

The Space
Indoor and outdoor seating, a stunning bar, and an oyster bar that doesn't disappoint. The real showstopper? That koi pond greeting you as you walk in, and the grand fountain out front. Inside, the lighting and decor strike the perfect balance — romantic without trying too hard. Plenty of parking and fully handicap accessible.

The Food
The menu runs the gamut: state (I'm guessing you meant steak?), Chilean sea bass, lobster, and genuinely excellent vegetarian options. Whatever you order, expect it to be exceptional.

The Vibe
The music is chef's kiss — present enough to set the mood, quiet enough so you can actually have a conversation. It's equally suited for a special event or a low-key date night.

The Extras
Service is attentive without being overbearing. Desserts are a worthy finale. Open seven days a week for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Expect to spend around $100 per person.

You could taste the seafood broth coming through, the shrimp and scallops were plump, juicy and perfectly cooked. I hen that fresh Parmesan hits your palate, HEAVEN. The misses enjoyed her lobster ravioli as well, and the drinks were an awesome, smooth glide and accomplice to a fantastic meal. Anyone who didn’t enjoy their experience here at Reef should try again.

If you’re looking for a delicious Mediterranean sea food in a heart of Queens, Reef is your obvious choice. We started our feast with oysters, and our taste buds exploded at the first bite - large shells were loaded with the fish and the horseradish sauce wrapped the flavors together well. For dinner we had their Branzino with lemon potatoes and Salmon with grilled vegetables. Both dishes exceeded our expectations. Salmon was soft and  tasteful, vegetables fresh. Branzino was otherworldly - I had no doubt I was eating the most delicious fish in my life. I always think of dining out as an experience, and now I know that his was one of those, we will not forget.
