top_reviews.content:
One of the finest dining experiences of my life. We did the tasting menu at The Modern, and while it was around $350/person, it genuinely felt worth every penny.

Every course was unlike anything I’d tasted before. Unexpected combinations, incredibly complex sauces, beautiful textures, and flavors that somehow worked together perfectly. The “Egg on Egg on Egg” was especially memorable. I also loved hearing the stories behind the dishes and learning from the chef how some of the components and sauces took days to prepare. It made you appreciate just how much thought and craftsmanship went into every bite.

The portions look tiny individually, but after eight or so courses, we actually left quite full! The service was exceptional too, warm, attentive, and never stuffy. They took lovely photos of us, and we were given our menu at the end as a keepsake, which was such a nice touch.

This wasn’t just a great meal. It felt like experiencing food in an entirely new way. My tongue genuinely discovered flavors it did not know existed. An unforgettable two-Michelin-star experience at MoMA, and absolutely worth doing at least once. ❤️

I came here to celebrate my graduation, it was my first foray into fine dining and I had a great experience here. I had Alex as my server and he was amazing! He was very genuine and did a really good job at translating the menu and feel approachable without ever being overwhelming. I was indecisive about two deserts and he surprised me with my second option complimentary. His attentiveness and service made the experience feel special and memorable beyond just the food itself. The support staff were also very nice with how they explained the dishes and presented the food. All around they were awesome.

The food was really great too! The eggs on eggs on egg was one of the best dishes I've had and I definitely recommend getting it. They offer complimentary bread and butter which was really great. I loved the dry aged duck as well, both the desserts I've had were really good as well. The portions may seem small but they filled me up for the whole day. It was some of the best food I've had, 10/10 when it comes to flavor, taste, and presentation!

Overall I had a really memorable experience, I want to thank Alex especially for making it memorable and all the staff. The food, service, and atmosphere was really amazing!

Hands down the best restaurant experience my wife and I have ever had.

We wanted to treat ourselves for our anniversary, and I had recently watched their Bon Appétit behind-the-scenes video. Their entire operation seemed so incredibly focused, meticulous, and inspiring that we knew we had to try it.

We started with the Iberico ham and the hiramasa tart, both incredible. Then came the chilled lobster, which was super fresh and refreshing, served with an amazing sauce that made me want to lick the plate clean. Every dish felt refined without being overly complicated.

The service was extraordinary. You can immediately tell the front-of-house team is operating at an extremely high level and is aware of everything happening in the room at all times. At one point, my wife stepped away to use the restroom just as they were about to serve the first course. Without saying a word or making anything awkward, the staff simply looped around a couple of times until she returned. The moment she sat down, they resumed service seamlessly without missing a beat. That level of awareness and professionalism really stood out to us.

Next came the rye bread, which was fresh and crispy on the outside, soft and fluffy on the inside, paired with delicious butter. Then we had the sea bass with crab, which was phenomenal and one of my favorite dishes of the night.

But the true star of the show for me was the lamb. My wife and I grill lamb racks often, and I genuinely had no idea this level of perfection existed. It was cooked flawlessly, and the sauce was absolutely incredible. If I was not in public, I probably would have been scraping the bone clean :)

Big shoutout to one of the staff members, Stephanie, who completely made our night. We were telling her how excited we were to finally visit after watching the Bon Appétit video, and she casually asked if we wanted a tour of the kitchen after dinner. Honestly, I thought she was joking at first. Then she came back after dessert and reminded us.

Even after paying the bill, I still thought maybe she was kidding, but then she walked over smiling and said, “Let’s go.”

My wife and I were completely geeked out. Seeing the kitchen in person was surreal. It was exactly like the video: super meticulous, orders being called out and repeated in unison, everyone moving with total precision and purpose. You could see the Omega clock, the Michelin stars on the wall, and just the overall culture of excellence behind everything they do. We were honestly in awe.

Thank you again, Stephanie. That experience meant so much to us.

Every time we visit a fine dining restaurant for a special occasion, I always wonder whether it will truly live up to the hype. Some completely miss the mark. Some are very good. But none have delivered on every aspect the way The Modern did.

This is officially our favorite restaurant in the world.

There’s two ways to enter this restaurant. They do in fact have a main door facing 53rd street. If you’re already inside MoMA, there’s a separate door by security. They have to let you in.
I didn’t have a reservation, but was seated immediately. Win!

I really should’ve asked questions instead of going rogue. My intention was to do the lunch prix fixe menu. The menu on the table was a la carte. This did however work out better for me as I had limited time since I was catching a broadway show.

Started with the olives then followed with the hot dogs and closed with the gem lettuce. They did come at different times. This gave me the perfect time to nibble slowly. The olives paired perfectly with the salad. The hot dogs were my favorite. The whole meal was perfectly balanced for me.

Just have to mention how amazing the service was. No table had anything waiting to be taken away because there was always someone walking around. At one point, one of the guys clocked I had just finished drinking my water and within seconds he was at my table refilling my glass. I mean c’mon.
Will took great care of me. He even suggested the dessert I ended up getting which was the peach cruller.
I’m gonna try to come back to do the lunch tasting before I go back home to LA.

Had an amazing time at this two Michelin stars restaurant, my first experience at such. From the moment you walk in there is an elegance that you feel. The hostess was very warm and inviting. Every server that came to our table was just as much so. Starting off we ended the melon lemonade and profunda. Both were super refreshing. My partner and I both ordered from the three course part of the menu. Our favorites were the lobster, the aged duck, and the mango rice pudding. It was so serene enjoying all of this where we were seated right at the window able to see the art covered plaza.

top_reviews.content:
This spot is honestly one of the best bang-for-your-buck places around. Prices are very reasonable, and the portions are solid for what you pay. The kimbap was fresh and well-balanced with a good amount of filling, and the tteokbokki had that perfect sweet and spicy flavor that keeps you going back for more. The fried items came out crispy and paired really well with everything.
Service was friendly and the vibe is casual and comfortable great for a quick bite without breaking the bank. If you’re looking for affordable Korean street food that actually hits the spot, this place is definitely worth checking out. I’d for sure come back again.

I love love love this place!

So glad I finally stopped by, the place is a cozy version of a Korean bar and the staff is super friendly

The sweet & spicy fried chicken gangjeong is crunchy, juicy, and has a delicious sticky sauce that actually isn’t too spicy and a bit Smokey with a touch of sweetness. The rice cakes are great with it as well but my only wish is that these were grilled or fried with the wings!

The tteokbokki also isn’t too spicy and has a great mix of flavors especially with the fish cakes

And the bulgogi kimbap is stuffed with a tasty filling mix of meat and veggies!

Great spot! Quick service and menu is small but varied. Me and friends shared some chicken. Both were small size and flavors spicy and soy. We ordered the medium size teokbokki with cream cheese and was enough for three people. A lot of sauce and could've been spicier but it was good! Budae ramen was a regular size and also decent. Would come back again :)

Let’s get right to the point!
Found this place on TikTok, and my husband and I decided to check it out. Here’s what we ordered:
We started with the fried chicken gangjeong. You can choose your size (small, medium, or large) and flavor (sweet & spicy or soy sauce). We went with a medium sweet & spicy, and it was delicious! The chicken was well-seasoned, super crispy, and came with a bit of tteokbokki on the side. What caught my attention was that the tteokbokki was fried — something I’ve never tried before! I personally prefer it soft, but my husband loved the crispy texture.
Next, we ordered the tteokbokki with noodles (about a $2.49 add-on). Definitely worth it! The tteokbokki itself was cooked well, though my husband didn’t love the soft texture — he would’ve preferred a crispy option if it were available. One thing we both agreed on was that the dish had a little too much sauce. It was flavorful, but a better balance between the noodles, tteokbokki, and sauce would make it perfect. I also wish it had a bit more spice!
If we had to pick favorites: my husband’s was the fried chicken gangjeong, and mine was the tteokbokki with noodles (just with less sauce and more kick!).
Overall, the atmosphere was chill, the restaurant was clean, service was quick, and the staff was friendly. Prices are great too! We’ll definitely be coming back again.

Please please please make sure you're supporting your local K-Town restaurants! Besides the food and the price, I think this is one of my favorite Korean spots to eat at in Koreatown. Their fried chicken is amazing and the tteokbokki is perfect. You cannot beat $5 a plate, especially in LA!

We tried two cocktails and both were great. We shared the ricotta fritters to start, very small portion but my girlfriend loved them (I thought they were alright). As mains we shared the kale ceasar salad and the duck confit. The salad was very disappointing but the duck was the star of the show. It is a very big portion so take that into account when ordering. The kimchi fried rice was delicious and paired perfectly. Would come back!

The cheeseburger was a soggy mess (even the patty - it crumbled into what felt like a wet rag and didn't even taste like beef) and the chicken sandwich looked promising but it failed in the taste and mouthfeel departments too. The sweet potato fries were good but the aioli was not. The service was wonderful, though

Got a recommendation for brunch at OpenAire on the 2nd floor pool deck (& converted greenhouse) of the Line Hotel near  downtown LA.  For a Sunday morning, it was less busy than I expected, but starting filling up as we were getting ready to leave (post-church crowd?)  Cool menu, interesting twists on old favorites, servers were all chill and helpful.  The execution of the menu was very good - we didn't put a mediocre bite in our mouths.  The Panna Cotta that I insisted on ordering, even though I was kind of full, was the perfect cap to the meal.  The hotel itself seems like it needs a refresh, and having this glass-ceiling, plant-filled space right next to the hotel pool was a little quirky, but the service and meal were excellent. Saw on Google Maps everyone’s order for this kimchi noodle bowl and it was so delicious!! I highly recommend this shop for its vibes!! Their kimchi side dish was legit and tasted right! Satisfaction made and wouldn’t needa come back to try what else they offer! Service was efficient and friendly! They serve buckwheat tea while food is being prepared :) my all time favorite. Parking is free because the shop is located inside a plaza next to a BCD location. Probably a very busy area during dinner time. 50 cent charged for take out box but they’ll inform you beforehand

So authentic Korean chicken broth handmade noodles! You can tell it’s handmade from the shape. It’s perfect Al dante style. Very nice juicy chicken and delicious chicken broth. Also got the rice cake dumpling soup. Also very nice. Love the variety of having rice cakes and dumplings. Dumplings have very tasty filling. Big portion. Didn’t even finish half. Easy to find parking.

Ordered the #1 Handcut noodles with chicken and a #2 “Feast Noodles” in Hot Anchovy Soup (Ma Dang Noodles). The menu selection has hot and cold noodles, these two are both hot noodle soups. The portions here are quite large. Meals are served with tea and two types of kimchi, a traditional red and a white. Both were distinct with the red kimchi having sweetness and light spice whereas the white kimchi was more cleansing and palate-refreshing. The #1 Handcut noodles with chicken was a delicious hearty soup with a slightly thick soup and nice chewy noodles. The shredded chicken was the right size and the greens in here brought color to the soup. For those who want to spice it up, there was a special spice oil that could be added on the side. The #2 “Feast Noodles” were a thin noodle type and also included shredded egg garnish. The anchovy soup here is flavorful and tastes great to warm up on a cold day. The noodles were the right tenderness and consistency for this soup, it’s certainly a very filling portion. They also sell packaged kimchi as well as jujube dates and sweet potatoes. Note that there is a $0.50 charge for to-go containers if you ask for them. Service was very fast-paced, a little mix of them being pressed for time in between very patient help with ordering and checking in on our meal. This restaurant gets a medium pace of foot traffic coming through the door, it’s often overshadowed by a few other major restaurants nearby. It’s part of a shared plaza so there is a large parking lot but it could get packed depending on the time of day.

It was simple, wholesome, and completely comforting. IPPUDO is the perfect spot for anyone looking for a bowl of ramen served just like it is in Japan.

Was here for dinner on an early spring weekday  - we were seated after walking in which was great given how crowded many other restaurants in the area were. The food is fantastic as one would expect from an Ippudo. They also happened to have on the menu a seasonal special which is a sukiyaki ramen that tasted pretty good. The Takoyaki is nicely prepared as well. I also enjoy their thin straight white ramen noodles. Nice ambience, good ramen option in NYC.

Cozy easy ramen spot.

I wouldn’t say it’s anything crazy but it satisfied our craving. We were attended to quickly and our food also came out quickly. I would definitely check it out if you’re in the area.

So our family had a little tradition when we travel and that is to visit Ippudo in every city that has one. It started in Japan and has now become a mission as we travel around the continental U.S.

It has been cold in New York dying our visit so a hot bowl of ramen was just what the family wanted. A mere minutes away from The Muse hotel on 46th street, we were able to walk right in close to 9:00 p.m. and were met by a warm and friendly server.

We enjoyed all of our favorites and a couple of cold beers. Great service, a welcoming atmosphere and delicious bowls of ramen goodness. They are even offering a free side of noodles if you’re still hungry at the end. We did and left satisfied.

We got delivery and the food was laughably bad. I think whoever is responsible for saucing the food actually went home already bc we did order around 8:30pm. Sesame noodles had no sesame sauce - nothing but a slick of mild sesame oil. Lo mein: no soy sauce, no SALT, nothing! Just some boiled noodles and w few wan vegetables. The fried eggplant was fine compared to the noodle dishes but nothing to brag about, at least there was some flavor amidst all the oil and finally, the only good thing on the menu: wontons with chili oil. I guess they could t skip the flavor bc chili oil was actually part of the title. All in, we spent $75 on some wontons and white rice and threw the rest out. Really pathetic experience. They get two stars bc one star is saved for food poisoning.

Han Dynasty at DeKalb Market Hall made for a convenient late supper after a movie, but the experience was uneven, with several dishes falling short of their traditional flavor profiles.

We began with the wontons in chili oil, a classic Sichuan appetizer rooted in Chengdu street food culture. Traditionally, the dish balances málà the numbing warmth of Sichuan peppercorns and the layered heat of chili oil. In this case, the wontons were small, noticeably overpriced, and coated in a sauce that leaned more sweet and salty than authentically spicy. Despite the generous amount of chili oil, the expected heat and numbing sensation were missing, leaving the dish oily rather than vibrant.

The Westlake beef soup was a steadier offering. This Cantonese origin broth, named after West Lake in Hangzhou, is known for its delicate texture created by minced beef, egg ribbons, and a lightly thickened, silky base. The version served here stayed true to that simplicity clean and comforting, even if not particularly memorable.

The salt and pepper scallops, served with rice, were the most disappointing plate. Salt and pepper dishes (jiao yan) are a hallmark of Cantonese cooking, celebrated for their crisp fry and harmony of salt, white pepper, and aromatics. Although the presentation here was impressive, the seasoning was not. The dominant and almost only flavor was pepper. There was virtually no salt, leaving the scallops bland and tasting mostly of fry oil rather than the bright, savory punch this dish is meant to deliver.

Portions overall felt small, which led us to add chicken potstickers. These, too, were overpriced for their size and lacked the juicy, savory filling that defines a good dumpling.

One thoughtful touch was the complimentary water and hot tea, which added a sense of hospitality to the meal.

While the setting is convenient and a few items offered comfort, several dishes missed the traditional balance and depth they’re meant to showcase. With so many strong vendors in DeKalb Market Hall, greater consistency and attention to seasoning would significantly elevate the dining experience.

I wish I could write a good review of this place. I booked here for my birthday dinner. The two female hosts at the front didn’t speak or greet my friend when he walked in. Normal maybe if we were in a fast casual bistro in lower Manhattan but for a quoted ‘fine dining restaurant’ is a pretty bad first impression. We get seated and the food is good and the service adequate, nothing super special or above and beyond but not anything too crazy to complain about.
The problems started when the bill came, all looked fine except a $52 charge split into two for still water. This was immediately confusing 1) because no one had ordered still water 2) we were never asked tap or still like every other restaurant I have been has asked 3) Water was being poured from a pitcher not a bottle. The second issue was they had charged us for one more soda than we had ordered, the rest of the check was accurate. Mistakes happen all the time, we just wanted the bill reflected accurately and did not ask for any concessions on this.
Once we approached that’s when the problem started, they tried to say we did ask for still water. The waiter continued to press us and say we did until we eventually asked for the manager. You would think a manager in a fine dining restaurant would have decorum? Well think again at La Goulue.
At one point, the same friend who had not been greeted had been identified by one of the managers as being the person who ordered the still which again, never happened. When we walked in he was the only one at the table, with one singular glass of water that had been poured from the tap. When my friend went over after hearing the man say ‘the guy with the big hood’ was asking for it the manager gets up in his face and says “Who do you think you are coming to me in my restaurant? Go sit down.” He looked like he wanted to punch my friend in the face. In years of eating at restaurants much nicer and more acclaimed than this I have never seen this level of pushback and hostility from a supposed manager. Eventually we did get the bill rectified but it took 30 minutes over something that in a restaurant around the corner with lower prices would immediately take off.
The restaurant itself is beautiful and the ambiance is great, but the managers are horrific.
I would never come back here and I would steer clear if you’re coming with a big party.

I was by myself, so I kept it simple - Panne Della Casa to start. Loved it - particularly the ricotta and olive oil dip. The focaccia was super fresh, salty, and flavorful. The pasta - the pasta was incredible. 10/10. I absolutely loved this dish. The Maltagliati with sausage and pumpkin. I love a great bolognese, which is on the menu, and this was similar but unique. We all started with some mocktails - two of us went with the cucumber drink and the other two went with peach. We all confirmed they were both very good.

All four of us went with the 3 course seasonal menu and shared the following apps: polpette, burratta, steak tartare and seasonal mushrooms. Standout was the mushrooms - these were phenomenal.

We ordered the following pastas: cacio e pepe, vongole, norma and bolognese. All four were delicious, but the standouts were the vongole and cacio e pepe.  Desserts were also delicious. The right level of sweetness for all three - tiramisu, pistachio gelato and budino with hazelnuts.

All in all, not a bad bite. A range of good to phenomenal. The staff were just attentive enough and gracious. Sitting at the counter is probably fun - we were a group so had a high top table (a little chilly being right by the door).  A little loud, but not too bad.

top_reviews.content:
I currently live in the Las Vegas area, but I travel to Los Angeles about once every month and a half. And every time I’m in town, one of my must-do stops is breakfast at Bulrocho. I absolutely love Korean soups, and Bulrocho’s Short Rib Soup with Young Napa has become a favorite that I look forward to with every visit.
I’m originally from Los Angeles and lived there for over 40 years, so I’ve had the opportunity to try many Korean restaurants over the years. Without a doubt, Bulrocho stands out when it comes to Korean soups. I’ve been coming here for many years, and I’m finally taking a moment to leave a review because it truly deserves recognition.
Their Short Rib Soup is outstanding. It's served piping hot—boiling, actually—which I really appreciate. The flavor is rich with a deep, savory bean paste base. The beef rib in the soup is impressively large, especially for a soup dish, and it's incredibly tender—so tender it practically melts in your mouth. The Young Napa is cooked perfectly: soft, flavorful, and not at all tough, unlike what I've experienced at other places.
The banchan (side dishes) are just as impressive. They typically include freshly made kimchi, crisp cucumbers with bean paste, and a variety of other small dishes that are all fresh and flavorful. They perfectly complement the soup.
I also want to highlight the excellent service. There’s one young woman in particular—with blonde hair—who has served us several times over the years. She’s consistently polite, attentive, and genuinely seems to care about making sure we’re taken care of. She always checks in to see if we need anything and does it with a great attitude. Honestly, if I owned a business, I’d want someone like her on my team. She’s one of the best servers I’ve ever encountered.
If you’re a fan of Korean soups, Bulrocho is a place you absolutely need to try. They offer a variety of soup dishes, and both the food and service are exceptional.
Get the "short rib soup with young napa" (우거지 갈비탕) it's crazy good. Customer service was great. They speak English too so don't worry 🤣 they're very friendly unlike other few Korean restaurants.

During my business trips to LA, I always have breakfast here!!

top_reviews.content: I loveeee kbbq and tbh yangmani was probably my favourite meal when I visited LA. We were told it would be a 30 mins wait and we were seated within that timeframe.  We ordered the chefs cut which had galbi and mega galbi. At first it didn’t register to me what mega galbi meant. Not until I saw the mega galbi was I like wowww, they weren’t joking about the mega! I’ve never seen galbi served like that before. Basically a big log on a long rib bone then they cut it off infront of u and grill it. It was sooo juicy and tasty. We lovedddd it! I also love that they serve perilla leaves here because they just elevate all the meat flavours imo. But don’t like the fact that you have to pay for it. Yes you have to pay for lettuce/perilla leaves! Overall I loved the food here, no regretsss! Our server was very nice too but it just felt a bit rushed because he was manning like 4 tables and cooking for everyone.

Delicious meal. We had the combo and could switch out some meat so we got the intestines instead of tripe - so yummy. The manager was very warm and welcoming. They cook all the food for you, although they move fast so we felt rushed to have the next meat. Sides are all delicious. I came here 2 years ago and I think the food is even better now than it was last time.

This place is very well-known as a Korean BBQ restaurant, and for good reason. They offer many different styles of meat, especially dry-aged cuts with a unique and memorable flavor. The service is outstanding—staff are always smiling, constantly coming over to grill the meat for you before you even ask, and making sure the table is fully taken care of. The side dishes are generous and refilled endlessly, including doenjang stew, begee paste stew, and other banchan that pair perfectly with the meat. The highlight at the end was the nurungji with doenjang stew, which was absolutely amazing. It was a truly new and enjoyable dining experience, and I’m already thinking about coming back again.
Oh, we was 6 people and ordered chef cut combo and variety combo large. Was enough .

I found this restaurant because of its great reviews and decided to give it a try. The restaurant was fairly empty, the woman who initially served us was incredibly kind, and the food was good. It wasn’t the best Korean BBQ I’ve had, but it was good enough that I fully intended to come back.

Unfortunately, the last five minutes of our visit changed that.

When I asked for two takeout containers for our leftovers, the second server told me I could only take the leftover meat—not the banchan (side dishes)—because “the owner doesn’t allow it.” This wasn’t an all-you-can-eat restaurant. Everything had already been paid for.

I honestly thought he was joking, so I asked, “So you’d rather throw the food away than let me take it home?” His response was, “Yep. It might seem like a waste of food to you, but it’s also a waste of a container.”

I asked if he was serious. He looked at me with a smug expression, said, “Nope,” and walked away.

Whether that’s truly the owner’s policy or not, the way it was handled was incredibly rude and unprofessional. One courteous conversation could have left me with a positive impression. Instead, I left feeling disrespected.

It’s unfortunate because they didn’t lose me over the food—they lost me over customer service. This was my first visit, and it will also be my last.

It was my first time visiting the new location, and I really liked the clean store and the spotless restrooms. The quality of all the meats were excellent, and the boneless short rib (Kkot-sal) and lamb were especially delicious. The side dishes (Banchan) were light and plain, which was great for pairing with the meat. We also separately ordered Myeongi-namul (mountain garlic leaves), and it is even more delicious when wrapped together with the pork belly (Samgyeopsal) and beef brisket (Chadol). The server kindly grilled the meat perfectly for us and refilled the side dishes. A unique point was the individual tongs provided, which were great and convenient for picking up both the meat and the perilla leaf side dish. One drawback was that the chairs were lower than the table height, which made eating a bit uncomfortable.

top_reviews.content: My boyfriend and I decided to dine here today as we were in the mood for Thai. We ordered salmon fried rice, beef Panang curry, crispy prawns and broccoli beef. Now, before I get into this review I want to say that I rarely leave reviews but this food pissed me off so much that I felt people should be warned. So let's start with the appetizer. Crispy prawns . When this came out it was few pieces of flavorless tempura shrimp, broccoli and carrots. Yes fried broccoli and fried carrots. No where in the description was this included. As a dipping sauce we had extremely watered down sweet and sour sauce. When I asked for a less watered down sauce, the waitress said they did not have any. At the time, I just brushed this off but now I realized that they were cutting back on cost by replacing prawns with vegetables and adding water to their sauce. The next item was the beef Panang curry. When it came out I was confused as to what this was. It was unlike any curry I have ever ordered. It was simply beef and curry sauce. Nothing else. I thought this is different than I expected but let me go ahead and try it. The beef was so tough I couldnt even eat it. Mind you on the menu it says melt in your mouth beef. My boyfriend described it as jerky. I wouldn't even give it that. This meat was flavorless and unchewable. The broccoli beef was also extremely sub par.The sauce had a slimy texture to it and it also had the flavorless  unchewable beef. Lastly was the Salmon fried rice. This was the only decent dish. Notice I said decent. When I mentioned my complaint to the waitress she took no accountability at all. I also over heard the people next to me complaining about their food and the waitress was once again taking no accountability.  In closing, if you are in the mood for Thai, think twice before coming here. Save your money, they are cutting back here and you will be paying full price for a budget meal.

One of my favorite places to get Thai food. I’m never disappointed. Their Pad See Thai is so delicious. Their surf and turf rice is amazing. And I love love love their sweet pork dish, the sauce they serve with it is amazing. Their lamb chops are always cooked to perfection. Plus the servers are fantastic.

Kinnara Thai Food in Van Nuys is a fantastic spot! The food was fresh, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. The staff were super kind and welcoming, and our food came right on time. Great service and even better food, highly recommend!

It's a nice and clean restaurant decorated with Thai theme.
We ordered the salmon curry and chicken skewers. They both come with rice and salad. Overall, the food is good, though the curry is slightly on the sweeter side for my taste.

When I moved back to the Valley from LA in 2012, Kinnara Thai was the first Thai restaurant I visited near me and I love it. Though I’ve noticed how a few things have changed in the 13-14 years, but nothing major. My favorite dish is the Fries Rice with added shrimp! Over time we receive a lot less shrimp and they’re not the colossal or super colossal shrimp like before they just extra large shrimp. They also do not add as many onions as before (even upon request) or tomatoes. I’m not sure why but tbh those are some of the things that unknowingly pushed me away for a bit. Nonetheless, the cuisine is still very good. I also love that Kinnara Thai is a part of several miles programs 🥳🥰 (AA, Skymiles, Milage Plus, etc❣️)

My brother has taken everyone he knows to this place.  They now know him personally.  The food has been a hit each time. He and I like to try something new each time.  Let me tell you, I have not found a dish that I didn't love.

I recently visited this charming Thai restaurant for the first time and I had an amazing experience! The food was absolutely delicious. I definitely recommend if you're looking for something new.

top_reviews.content: I absolutely adore a place like this! Affordable good food and easily accessible to everyone. The prices are great for the amount of food you get too. They are a Taiwanese restaurant with lots of variety and is served quick casual style. They have a little market up front with fun trinkets too. You can’t reserved for a small party but it’s a pretty quick turn and first come, first served. No dedicated service but they are helpful if needed. Definitely will be back!

Very interesting Asian fusion restaurant… I had an expectation of having “authentic Taiwanese” foods but it was definitely not. It had its own style and it turned out pretty good. The vibe and surrounding was very pleasant and relaxing.

Had a long layover in LA after my flight to San Francisco got canceled, so instead of sitting at the airport for 6+ hours, I decided to finally check out Pine & Crane in DTLA. It’s been sitting on my saved list for a while, and honestly, this turned out to be the perfect opportunity.

The space itself is bright, clean, and welcoming with warm woody tones throughout. Casual setup where you order at the counter and they bring the food out to you. I had already looked through the menu beforehand, so the real challenge was narrowing down what to order for one person. I failed at that… and I’m very happy I did.

Started with the Pig Ear Salad 滷豬耳朵. Braised thin sliced pig ears dressed with soy sauce, chili oil, sesame oil, scallion, and cilantro. OMG. So good. Tender, flavorful, perfectly braised, with that satisfying chewy texture done right.

Also got the Fried Peanut Salad 五味花生 with garlic, cilantro, scallions, vinegar, and Thai chili. Super crunchy, bright, refreshing, and honestly addicting.

I added a cup of the Hot & Sour Soup 酸辣湯 too. Organic tofu, beech mushroom, carrot, bamboo, woodear mushroom, and egg. Super comforting with a really balanced tang and peppery heat. Not overly thick or heavy like a lot of Americanized versions can be. Exactly the kind of soup you want during a long travel day.

For noodles, I ordered the Dan Dan Noodles 擔擔麵. Sesame-peanut sauce, cucumber, cilantro, crushed peanuts. Delicious on its own already, but I ended up adding some of the fried peanuts from the salad into the noodles and it became even better.

Then the Three Cup Chicken 三杯雞 with sesame oil, soy sauce, rice wine, and Thai basil. I do wish it had a little more wok hei, but overall the flavor was still really comforting and savory. Extremely good with rice.

Had a glass of Gewürztraminer alongside everything, which paired surprisingly well with the spice and aromatics. Their wine list leans more organic / natural wine focused, which felt very LA in a good way.

Ended up sitting at a high top next to one of the managers and had a great conversation throughout the meal. She ended up hooking me up with the Traditional Shaved Ice 傳統刨冰 with grass jelly, red bean, boba, sweet potato balls, taro balls, brown sugar syrup, and condensed milk. I was already planning to order it anyway, and wow… I finished the entire thing. The brown sugar syrup was incredibly fragrant.

Packed the leftovers to-go, and that ended up becoming my dinner after landing in San Francisco later that evening. Flight cancellation somehow turned into a really great food day.

Visited Los Angeles again with Hubby on his business trip.  Decided to look for authentic Taiwanese Food this time around. 😄

Since traffic in LA is beyond crazy 🤪, we found one near downtown LA closer to the hotel we are staying at and found this place!

To authenticate the Taiwanese flavor of this restaurant 😋, we went with the signature dishes such as Beef Noodle Soup and LuRuo Fan.  They are pretty good and we enjoy the taste.

We really enjoyed the decoration of this place!  The atmosphere and the environment was a big plus in my book.  Of course, had to officially end the meal with the Taiwanese shaved ice to complete this experience!

The only complaint was the location of our seatings which has a lot of traffic and the space was very tight.  Overall we really enjoyed the food and the restaurant as a whole - will recommend.

This is a great place to try Taiwanese food! Although it’s not as authentic as the one I tried in Taiwan, but it still tasted great. My friends and I shared the pork rice, which was a big size. Popcorn chicken is a little bit salty to me. And we all love the shaved iced !!! Must try the shaved ice, each part of ice is covered with brown sugar and dense milk, it’s so good, would definitely comeback for the shaved ice.

Breakfast: we came back for its breakfast menu, but it wasn’t as good as its lunch menu. The rice roll was smaller than I expected and not filling at all.

The mood is chill, outdoor patio seating, counter service setup. Plenty of seating. We went for lunch and we had the mapo tofu, the beef roll, fried chicken, the minced pork and rice and the pork steamed Buns. All were great, I’d say the buns stole the show.

This place is great for casual dining of Taiwanese food here in DTLA. I was able to get a table reservation for 20 which is nice but it's also a casual order and dine in place.

We had a prix fixe menu that had many of the menu items. The beef rolls, popcorn fried chicken,vegan mapotofu, three cup chicken and fried tofu & mushrooms were excellent.  The hakka mochi and smashed cucumbers were delicious and refreshing. Overall the food was great.

The staff was very attentive and nice. They came over several times to check in on us and see if we needed anything. The decor and atmosphere is cool and a modern. Lots of spacing for individuals to sit at and eat and it's fairly well lit.

I was really disappointed with this order. The food was extremely bland, basically no flavor except oil. The soup tasted flat and greasy.

The radish cake was even worse. It cost $9, and the portion was tiny, literally just four small pieces. On top of that, it tasted unpleasant and oily, with none of the savory flavor a good radish cake should have.

For the price, the quality and portion were really unacceptable. I honestly couldn’t finish it.

Definitely not worth the money. ALSO FOUND A HAIR IN THE SOUP!

Came here for the first time to celebrate a birthday as kbbq brisket is one of her favorites.  They have a $27.99 per person weekend/evening AYCE beef brisket special which includes an order of their soy pork spare ribs.  (During the weekdays, they have the same special for lunch at $22.99 per person). The quality of the brisket was good.  I think they use a prime cut.  Alongside the meats, they served banchan including pickles, kim chee, potato salad, pickled radish/diakon and salad as well as a spicy soup.  I think the banchan were okay (the salad has a bit of bitter lettuce stalk and the potato salad was just okay), but you come here for the meats and that did not disappoint.  The interior is modern and clean, and the staff continued to check in with us and ordering more meat for us.  Between two people, we had four plates of beef briskets for over an hour.  They have a limit of 90 mins but on our weekend afternoon, it wasn't too busy and most groups were leaving around an hour.  Parking is $10 at their lot (they include free parking for their weekday lunch) or it's $1/hr on the meter for two hours.  Parking in the residential area can be difficult since it's at the heart of ktown but you might be lucky.

top_reviews.content:
Restaurant Row – A Culinary Stroll in the Heart of Manhattan

Tucked just off the buzz and chaos of Times Square, West 46th Street between 8th and 9th Avenues—famously known as Restaurant Row—offers one of New York City’s most vibrant and diverse dining stretches. This single block feels like a miniature culinary theme park, where nearly every building houses a different restaurant, each with its own unique flavor, style, and character.

From upscale Italian trattorias and cozy French bistros to sushi spots, steakhouses, tapas bars, and Southern comfort food joints, Restaurant Row has something for every palate. Whether you’re a picky eater or a bold food adventurer, odds are you’ll find a menu that speaks your language here.

Yes, some of the restaurants can be a bit pricey, but this isn’t fast food—it’s Broadway-adjacent dining, and the atmosphere is part of the experience. The trick is to take your time: walk the block, read a few menus, feel the vibe of each spot. It’s like window-shopping for dinner. There’s no rush, and half the fun is exploring.

It’s a hidden-in-plain-sight gem that feels surprisingly relaxed given how close it is to the intensity of Times Square. If you’re looking for a one-block taste tour of New York’s food scene, Restaurant Row is absolutely worth the detour.

Sooooooo many wonderful options! With the weather finally breaking, it's a great time to take in an afternoon show and some good food afterward!

Can’t recommend Kantu enough! The food, drinks and ambiance were all 10/10!!

The restaurant is beautifully decorated with vibrant murals that make you feel like you’ve been transported to Peru. We started with the Classic Pisco Sour and the Pisco Mango Madness which were fantastic.

Our favorite appetizers were the Truffle a la Huancaína, the flavorful Causa Rellena and the Jalea, which was perfectly crispy and seasoned. For our entrées, the Chicken Arroz Chaufa was delicious, the Cordero a la Parrilla was cooked perfectly and the Churrasco de Pollo was hands down one of the juiciest and most flavorful grilled chicken dishes I’ve ever had. Don’t skip dessert because the Lucumisu and Passion Fruit Panna Cotta were the perfect ending to an incredible meal.

They also have all day Happy Hour Monday through Thursday and $15 weekday lunch specials, making it a great spot whether you’re celebrating or just grabbing lunch.

I’ll definitely be back and highly recommend Kantu to anyone looking for authentic Peruvian cuisine in Queens!

10/10! I will definitely be coming back! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

We most recently came to celebrate a birthday and tried the lomo saltado, tallarín saltado, churrasco de pollo, tallarín verde, and arroz chaufa—every dish was full of flavor and absolutely delicious. Whether you’re planning a date night or a family dinner, this place is always accommodating and makes you feel right at home. I’m already looking for an excuse to come back.

Had a great meal at YeoGiYo in Koreatown! Everything we ordered was delicious, and the portions were generous.

The Beef Bulgogi Hot Pot was warm and comforting with tender bulgogi, lots of vegetables, and a rich, flavorful broth that kept getting better as it cooked.

The LA Short Ribs came out on a sizzling hot plate and smelled amazing. The meat was juicy, tender, and perfectly caramelized with a sweet and savory marinade.

I also really enjoyed the Spicy Squid Stone Pot Bibimbap. The squid was surprisingly generous, and after mixing everything together, the crispy rice at the bottom made it even better.

The Seafood Pancake was crispy on the outside, soft inside, and packed with seafood. Definitely a great dish to share.

The meal also came with a nice variety of banchan, which was a great bonus. If you’re looking for authentic Korean food with quality ingredients and generous portions, I’d definitely recommend YeoGiYo!

The food was decent, but I was very disappointed by the lack of banchan refills. The portions were small to begin with, and for two people, they were gone quickly. As a Korean who loves enjoying a variety of side dishes with a meal, this was a major letdown and the main reason I wouldn’t return.

I think it’s a good place. A bit pricey but good. I guess the meat had an off day. So that’s why it’s a 4 instead of 5. But 👍

top_reviews.content: Food is not mainly Shanghainese, the menu contains mostly dishes typical of the Zhejiang province in China with influence from other regions. There are a few Shanghainese classics on the menu however. Standout dishes include the fried green beans, the vegetable rice, and red braised pork. Other dishes were good, but not exceptional. The beggars chicken is a good show, but ultimately lacking in flavor and was a bit dry. Service and atmosphere are both great. I must say their fried pork buns (shen jian) are not as good as Nan Xiang next door. Presentation of all dishes is very pleasant, and prices are very reasonable. Overall highly recommend for a nice dinner experience.

We somehow secured a Mother’s Day dinner here for 5 without reservations! We gladly accepted a smaller table to get in. We had tried the restaurant next door jiang nan before and when we first entered we thought it was the same restaurant due to the decor, but staff said it wasn’t.

Finding the restaurant - easiest by accessing it from in front of the Tangram mall, maps initially had us walking through large restaurant area outdoors and going in circles for a bit.

I broke my rule of never going out on Mother’s Day because service is usually subpar, food is too and it’s just too busy but we took my mom to NyC for the day so had to eat lol.

Food was quite good, though overpriced a bit. We had the soup dumplings, sweet and sour fish, beggar chicken (with a small show), ham and vegetable clay pot rice, and a veggie dish. It was all delish! I especially loved the rice and hope to replicate it at home. Osthmanthus dessert (warm) wasn’t good, I probably should have gotten the cool one.

Service left a lot to be desired, which may be due to it being so busy. Hard to get staff to ask questions about the order. For the prices, one would think service would be exceptional. The staff were busy and seemed annoyed at requests for water, tea, etc.

I would try it again on a less busy weekend.

CHELI is an authentic Shanghainese cuisine restaurant with a bit of a reputation, being on the Michelin guide. The interior is entrancing, the staff is very accommodating (especially for Chinese staff) and the food presentation is astounding. We found the pork soup, braised eel, shrimp, and beggar's chicken pretty amazing. The Beggar's chicken was so soft and tender! The most famous of them all, the Xiaolongbao, was just ok, however. All in all a hood restaurant. We had 8 dishes coming to $200 including tips.

We came here to celebrate a birthday and had a wonderful experience. The restaurant itself is beautiful, with a traditional Chinese style. The staff were welcoming and polite.

Every dish we tried was original, full of flavor, well presented, and clearly made with quality and care. We especially loved the Wine Soaked Chicken, the Salted Pork & Vegetable Fried Rice, and the Shrimp & Tofu Stew. Honestly, the « wine soaked chicken » and the fried rice are must-orders.
And yessss… we also ordered the Beggar’s Chicken as an homage to the « Legend of the Condor Heroes » 😂 It would be epic if they also played the theme song!!! The chicken itself was good, but the real highlight was the serving ritual: so fun and impressive to watch.
Super experience!

Soup dumplings are affordable & really solid for good and quick dimsum options.. but the desserts are amazing. I wasn’t expecting it to be so great, they are the perfect balance of not too sweet. The sweet osmanthus rice cakes & jasmine milk pudding are great either together or separate. Great price for what you get. Walkable distance from the flushing-main st 7 line

I went in with a party of 6, waited for a bit for a table to open up, and was immediately astonished by the decor, service, and food quality.

There is an energy of coziness and warmth with the ornamental wood pillars, golden lanterns draping from oriental roof tiles, and the blue seats that compliment a central white table.

You order from a handheld device, but if you need a personal server, you can request them in less than a second with a tap of a button from the tablet menu and get an equally fast response time.

The food was the best part. I ordered the osmanthus plum juice, and it had one of the most contemplative, yet refreshing taste I have ever experienced in the last 5 years. My party ordered over 5 dishes, and 3 of which had a distinctive and prominent taste. Chilled, quenching wine-soaked chicken; succulent crispy duck; savory stir-fried Shanghai noodles. I recommend the crispy duck the most, but all of them are of amazing quality for any new guest.

Great experience. Che Li is such a beautiful restaurant. The atmosphere feels elegant and peaceful, almost like a traditional Chinese garden. My family celebrated my birthday here, and the staff made it feel very special by preparing a birthday bouquet on the table.

The servers were incredibly friendly, kind, and attentive. They even gave me an adorable peach-shaped bun for my birthday, but I forgot to take a photo of it, haha. It was such a sweet and thoughtful gesture.

The food was, as always, delicate, beautifully presented, and delicious. The staff really care about your experience, and the whole meal felt warm and memorable. I would definitely recommend Che Li, especially for special occasions.

Cheli is a great restaurant to eat at with your friends! The atmosphere was especially nice, they had a consistent theme. Service was also great, ordering was super easy! Waiters warned us of the spicy foods and asked if any of us had allergies. The food looked very appealing to the eyes but they weren’t particularly for me.

Overall, I had a great time here!

top_reviews.content:
The only thing more unbelievable than the beautiful salt water fish tank when you first walk into Bistango was the taste of their gluten free offerings.

When I saw their menu showed "gluten free" as more of an alternative in fine print, I was pretty skeptical and expected a few salad options with grilled meat and a sorry excuse for gluten free bread. Lucky for me: I was very wrong.

I must have told our waiter 6 or more times he had to be lying because I couldn't believe how good the flavor and texture was of everything I ate.

From the starter bread to the ravioli, I was just shocked. Nothing felt rubbery or brittle like similar gluten-free alternatives. The calamari and meatballs were excellent and the tiramisu was great, although I wish they made it a bit more on the wet side.

A great happy hour with well made drinks and a menu that is in no way boring compared to the majority of gluten-free Italian options I've seen at other restaurants.

All the staff were nice and very attentive.

More Italian restaurants need to catch up with the times and follow Bistango's model for the GF community.

As a celiac this place is a must, to be able to have ANYTHING of the menu with the knowledge its prepped completely GF is outstanding. The food is to die for, truly authentic Italian & delicious. The short rib ravioli was tasty & the arancini amazing. Not enough room for desert so will have to come back. Service was great and waiter very knowledgeable. Thank you 😋

The restaurant  has a nice ambiance and the outside seating is great but my food experience was not so great . Ordered Kale salad with added grilled chicken. No place on the menu did  it say the chicken would be blackened ( which is very unhealthy. They served me burnt chicken and the waiter seemed appalled  that I didn’t like it and suggested other proteins like shrimp would be the same,  I cut off all the burnt parts as much as possible but left unsatisfied and feeling like I had smoked a pack of cigarettes .  Be kinder and more empathetic to your clients

This is undeniably one of the best gluten free restaurants I’ve had the privilege of eating at in the United States. We headed over after a fun morning of marveling at towering floats and spirited marching bands during the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. We braved the biting wind and eventually found ourselves in an elegant hotel lobby. To our left, bathed in warm lighting and shimmering holiday decorations was Bistango. A mesmerizing aquarium at the center of the dining room dominated the decor.

The food proved even more impressive! The warm, gooey, burrata encrusted in a crispy fried coating on a bed of zesty stewed tomatoes was tantalizing. For my main course, a lamb shank in a hearty sauce with buttery risotto was so tender it fell right off the bone. We savored each bite and were much too full for dessert. So the friendly staff packed them to enjoy at home.

The decor, very attentive staff, and unforgettable food makes this a 5 star experience. We can’t wait to return!

Went here on the recommendation of a friend for our anniversary while staying in NYC. Fabulous restaurant. Servers were all so nice. And to find an Italian restaurant where everything on the menu can be made gluten free is absolutely amazing. To actually be able to have arancini, flat bread, and lasagna gluten free is a game changer. My only complaint was that with our reservation for two, we were placed in the main walkway when there were plenty of other two seat tables available the entire time we were there. We will definitely be back here again.
I absolutely love this place. Gluten free upon request for EVERYTHING!  We had calamari to start. I had the linguine with clams and we shared a GF carrot cake. Must eat here if you’re GF.

I’ve been here 3 times now, and I love it every visit. I have celiac, and to be able to go somewhere where you can have anything on the menu, and it’s actually GOOD and not out of a frozen package, is a delight.
I’ve had ravioli, pastas, flatbreads, calamari, arancini… the sauces are perfect, the portions just right. And all the desserts are gluten free (the carrot cake is incredible).

The service is always spot-on and timely. I love this place!

What a delightful culinary experience. The place is gorgeous and the staff was impeccable in their service orientation. The music was fun and the ambience was luxurious.

My daughter and I have Celiac along with my food allergies of egg and dairy were no problem for this delightful kitchen. The food was fresh, hot, delicious, and surprisingly fast. Everyone was stuffed with great portion sizes and beautiful plating.

If you are in the area, and you have food allergies, you should stop by. A++ I would highly recommend adding Bistango to your itinerary. We are leaving happy for less of a bill than I was expecting with such an upscale experience.

The staff was friendly and attentive, making the whole experience even better. Highly recommend this place if you’re looking for quality food and a cozy atmosphere.
It was my first time with my wife during the lunch time. It was do good to have a lunch here. It seems one of the best Korean style restaurant in Korea Town.

This is probably my favorite Korean restaurant in LA! Their raw crab and shrimp are prepared with a truly unique recipe that is packed with flavor. The quality of the seafood is incredible—it’s fresh, delicious, and perfectly marinated. On top of the food, the staff is extremely friendly and makes you feel right at home. A must-try if you appreciate high-quality raw Korean seafood

What a fantastic spot to enjoy authentic Korean cuisine! The Soy Sauce Marinated Crab (Ganjang-gejang), Spicy Marinated Crab (Yangnyeom-gejang), and Braised
Short Ribs (Galbi-jjim) were all absolutely amazing. The service was top-notch, and I’ll definitely be coming back here again!

Next to Korea, Los Angeles has the largest population of Korean so we are lucky to have the best chef ! If you are tired of Korean bbq but wants to eat other cuisine thane I would suggest you come here ! We came here 3 years ago when it was first opened from a suggestion from my son and fell in love with this place since!! We love the Korean seafood pancake.. the crust is perfectly brown on the outside while inside is filled with leak, green onion and seafood.. absolutely delicious! The snail salad is outstanding! Yes! Snail.. don’t judge me until you try! The short rib soup is loaded with vegetable!!! Yummy!!

top_reviews.content:
10/10 will return again.

Galbi kalguksu - Soo good! I was craving a warm hearty bowl of noodle soup and this 100% hit the spot. Noodle had great texture and bite, soup was flavorful and hearty. Portion was big and came served with two beef ribs. Loved it.

Beef bulgogi - very tasty bulgogi, generous serving of meat and veggies. Will order again.

Pork belly and jowl combo bossam medium - it says feeds 2 but I think it actually feeds 3+. Comes with pickled veggies etc. definitely worth trying, doesn’t have the funk that sometimes pork has. Very well cooked and balanced. Don’t forget the sauce!!

Overall prices are high but portions are huge and flavor wise it’s on point so definitely worth it! Parking is a pain but there’s valet parking for $5.

I was visiting and came here with friends. We went on a Friday evening at about 7ish. There was a line. There’s a process to coming here. The hostess controlled the line so we wouldn’t be blocking the entrance to the other restaurants. As you get closer to the front, you’ll get a menu. The hostess will take your order. Once you place the order, you are NOT allowed to make any changes and cannot add on. Once it’s your turn to go sit down, the hostess will confirm your order, the seat you. Your food comes out pretty fast
I ordered the Bulgogi rice dish with a salad on the side. It was SO good! My friends split a seafood dish. Everything was delicious. It was a lot. I ended up having leftovers for lunch the next day.
They have a good system in place in getting getting ppl in and out of there. The service was great and the atmosphere was lively.  I would definitely come back.

What a place.  Just wow on their boiled belly pork and their other dishes too. First, parking is impossible…it just slow and we came here around 4pm and there is a valid parking but it just slow (no parking) and people just not moving their car at all.  We circled the block 2X and luckily got parking right in front of another store.  The place is simi packed but got table and menu is small and easy to pick.  Staff are nice, friendly, helpful and attentive.  The place clean and spacious and smell of good foods and great vibe.   The foods are just simply delicious and tasty.  Well marinated and perfectly cooked.  Fresh and yummy side dishes.  Prices are good but on the high end side, but then again, this is LA so.  Overall great dinner with delicious foods and great services.

Hands down the best Korean comfort food out here. My wife and I decided to hit up this spot after craving some Korean food on a hot day. Parking is valet ($4-5) but we decided to park across the plaza in H Mart and walked over.

We waited in line for about 5 minutes but the staff brought out menus for us to order in advance. When we got seated, we got our food pretty quickly, about 10 minutes or so, which is pretty quick because the restaurant was full and super busy.

We ordered the Medium Bossam (Feeds 1-2 people), and the MILMYON (Cold noodles) and my goodness the milmyon is beyond amazing. The noodle is different from other restaurants that serve milmyon. Their noodles mixed super well with the ingredients and it was very savory, amazing on a hot day.

The bossam came after the milmyon and the portions are pretty generous. Medium serves 1-2 people and it's very fulfilling. It's recommended to eat the bossam wrapped style but eating it piece by piece is also very tasty. The wrap ingredients matches really well and a must try for anyone visiting Hangari.

Overall, an amazing experience, wait wasn't too long despite the line. Staff were professional and fast. Food is top quality and very very tasty. This is absolutely hands down the best milmyon ever and the bossam is definitely top quality. Will be coming back often for the other dishes.

Visited Hangari Kalguksu on a cold, rainy Thursday afternoon, and the cozy atmosphere immediately gave us a sense of comforting warmth. We were promptly seated and welcomed with complimentary warm corn silk tea, which had a smooth texture and subtle sweet-corn flavor — perfect for the chilly day.
The banchan (complimentary side dishes) and sauces were well-fermented with a pleasant saltiness that paired nicely with the overall meal. For appetizers, we ordered the medium Bossam with the pork having a great balance between lean meat/fat, and when wrapped with garlic, jalapeños, spicy radish, and lettuce, it had a flavorful and satisfying taste.
The Spicy Seafood Kalguksu featured a rich, anchovy-based broth that was warmly spiced without being overpowering. The house-made knife-cut noodles were perfectly cooked having a nice chewiness. The barley rice topped with bean paste was also a great complement to the soup.
We also tried the Hot Stone Bibimbap, which arrived in a sizzling hot bowl. The vegetables, beef, and spicy gochujang sauce blended well together, and the crispy rice at the bottom added great texture.
Service was average but pleasant — the staff was approachable and attentive, checking in when needed and promptly clearing dishes.
Overall, despite the day trip it took us to get there, we’d recommend this spot to anyone looking for authentic Korean comfort food in Koreatown.

Noodle soup is one of my favorite comfort food and this place offered that simple, home cooking feel. The handmade noodles were very chewy and had a satisfying texture. The broth was a little mild for me though. Also it would be great if they could offer more side dishes.

"Hangari Kalguksu is hands-down the most famous spot in Koreatown for authentic hand-cut kalguksu, and it totally lives up to the hype! They make the noodles fresh by hand every day from flour dough, and you can really taste the incredible freshness and that perfect chewy (쫄깃한) texture—it's unlike anywhere else I've tried.
I ordered the kalguksu, spicy milmyeon (매운 밀면), and dakjuk (chicken porridge), and the dakjuk was my absolute favorite! The chicken was so tender and had that amazing chewiness that made every bite super satisfying. The portions are generous, the broths are rich and comforting, and it just feels like real homemade Korean comfort food.
Only one small downside: parking can be tricky (especially on weekends when it's super crowded), but they offer valet parking in the plaza, so come a bit early if you're going during peak times to avoid the wait.
Highly recommend this place—it's a must-visit for anyone craving the best Korean noodles in LA! Will definitely be back. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐"

It was my first time visiting this place, and I was really impressed — it’s clean and has a nice atmosphere. I had to wait a while before ordering because I was waiting for someone, but the staff were patient and didn’t rush me. When I finally ordered, the food came out generous and delicious.

The bossam was super tender with no unpleasant smell, and the hot stone bibimbap was perfectly sizzling — so good! The clam noodle soup had a rich, flavorful broth, and the noodles tasted fresh and chewy, like they were handmade. And the young radish bibimbap that came with it was honestly amazing.

I’m definitely coming back!

top_reviews.content:
A casual Korean-style pub located in LA Koreatown. The place isn’t fancy, and the food isn’t high-end, but it’s a comfortable spot to relax and enjoy a bottle of Korean soju.

They offer many classic Korean drinking dishes that pair well with soju, making it easy to keep things simple and enjoyable. The service is friendly and fast, which is a big plus.

The only downside is limited parking, especially during busy hours. Overall, it’s a solid neighborhood spot for a casual drink and a laid-back atmosphere.

This was our first time here. It's a nice, cozy place. It has a nice atmosphere, looks like those restaurants you see in Korean dramas, and they play good music.
We ordered a beef rib soup, kimchi soup and a plate with two fried fish that I can't remember what kind of fish they were, also fried dumplings and a bowl of rice for each of us. I gotta say that this is one of the best Korean restaurants we've tried. The beef rib soup was amazing, the best of all the dishes we tried I must say. The kimchi soup was also good and the fish were very tasty. The rice and dumplings were delicious as well. The sides? You can't have enough of them. We're very impressed with the flavors. The service is fast, the staff is very friendly and they recommend some dishes in case you've never been here, please listen to their recommendations. We're definitely coming back soon with friends and family.

The Service: Came during lunch time. Totally hands-on owners serving their customers. Always the best service! Attentive & efficient~

The Food: Thanks to the owner's recommendation. I tried a few of their signature dishes.

Butter Squid - Love the table service! They cut the whole piece of squid into bite size then fire up with the torch for the smoky taste. Very tender & flavorful! Great texture too.

Battered Fish Filet - really lightly battered, the fish is so fresh. No greasy at all! Love it~

Chicken Feet - saw this dish on K-drama all the time. Finally~ I got to try it myself! OMG! No wonder they call this "Korean Drinking Food". They are spicy & savory. It will go so well with beer or soju.

Very authentic Korean food will absolutely come back & try out different dishes soon!

The Parking: Private parking lot (valet $2). Street metered parking (1 hour).
Walk in, good service, nice food :D very quiet and clean environment

Great lunch deal for under 15!! I can’t believe this deal exists in KTown LA. The portion is huge (especially the sides). Rice is very tender and smell good. Bulgogi is my favorite meat option. Very delicious!!

Parking is available in a small lot. There was a person looking after the space so I got a spot despite being lunch time.

The only thing I felt was off was the smell when I entered the restuarant. Maybe it’s the korean seasoning smell but it’s not a pleasant smell to me.

First of all, the music their blare in this place, is exactly what it should be:  KPop that was made for Koreans, not the modern stuff that was designed to brainwash people all over the world with an international flare!  Plus, the food here is excellent!  Just like the music choice, it's all ol'-skool!  Can't ask for anything else!
Second time here and the ambiance and service are as good as their food. Chevk this place out if ever you crave for korean foods. It is a must try place. There is lunch special on the menu. :)
I come to eat here when I visit L.A great flavors and I love the fish. I brought my eoma she 💙 it too! So glad I got to bring her.

Had breakfast here. Conveniently located half a block south of a 7 train station. Portions were large and food was delicious. Had chilaquiles and huevos rancheros. Service was friendly and attentive.
Amazing service from Ruben and all staff! Came here with my family for brunch, a little of a wait for seating but it’s absolutely worth it. The food was amazing.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Review by Vanessa Caballero
Date: Saturday, October 18, 2025

I was born and raised right here in Jackson Heights, and I’ve visited many diners in the area over the years—but Florence Prime Diner truly stands out as one of the very best.

We visited on Saturday, October 18, to celebrate both my birthday and my daughter’s 11th birthday, and everything about our experience was absolutely wonderful.

The chicken soup was outstanding—rich, flavorful, and full of fresh vegetables. It tasted exactly like homemade chicken soup, the kind your mom would make when you were little. The broth was perfectly concentrated, and for that delicious soup alone, I give five stars without hesitation.

The coffee was excellent—fresh, smooth, and never bitter. The staff offered refills generously, which made our breakfast even more enjoyable. I would easily give the coffee a 10 out of 10.

We also tried the mini waffles with berries, which were light, fluffy, and perfect for sharing. My daughter had the green chilaquiles, and they were exactly as we requested—not spicy, since she doesn’t eat spicy food. They came beautifully served with rice and beans, and she loved every bite.

For my birthday meal, I ordered the carne asada, cooked exactly the way I asked—tender, juicy, and full of flavor. It was served with two over-medium eggs, potatoes, and a fresh salad. The meat was so soft that it was a pleasure to eat and enjoy every bite.

To make the celebration even more special, the waiters kindly sang “Happy Birthday” to both my daughter and me, bringing a cheesecake topped with fresh berries. Everything was so fresh, delicious, and made with care.

Our server was incredibly kind, polite, and attentive, always checking in to make sure we had everything we needed. We truly appreciated his warmth and professionalism.

It was a lovely family moment—especially since my son, who is currently away at college, joined us to celebrate. The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming, making our birthday celebration truly unforgettable.

We’ve often walked past Florence Prime Diner, but this time we decided to stop in—and I’m so glad we did. From now on, this will be one of our favorite places in Jackson Heights.

Ten out of ten for this beautiful diner—thank you, Florence Prime Diner, for making our birthdays so special!

— Vanessa Caballero

Best Diner experience in Jackson heights , you can walk past it if you donr keep eyes open , the best Service ,  decor and ambiance , the staff is super warm and attentive and the food is at another level , Mexican breakfast is the best and sandwiches is a hidden secret , Chuy and the gang will treat you like gold.

Absolutely delicious grilled skirt steak sandwich. I would say the best I’ve eaten. Just be sure to select medium rare as your meat temperature to do justice to the quality of the steak. Other mouth-watering choices are the grilled steak quesadilla and the grilled steak taco.

top_reviews.content: I visited last Sunday, and my experience was wonderful. I stopped by and was welcomed warmly by the staff. I sat at the bar and tried the Lobster Mac & Cheese with a beer, and everything was delicious. They also had live music, which made the experience even more enjoyable. I had a great time and would definitely come back!

Went here for dinner as a last minute decision. Thankfully they still had tables available. Such an beautiful place with mix of old and new. The menu has great selections and there are daily specials for the main course and appetizers. The appetizers portions were perfect. The staff were extremely attentive but not annoying. Love the open kitchen concept. I enjoy watching everyone work together and the different stations setup. Our app choices were the crabcake and watermelon with balsamic. Crabcake was mostly crab. Main course choices were scallops and an eggplant & tofu dish.
So glad we went. Such a great experience and outstanding food.

It was good and a fun experience, but certainly not the exceptional one we expected. The atmosphere was nice, but the view of the outside the glass area was completely blocked by green walls for an event so we just saw glass and fake greenery.  It was exceptionally loud, surprisingly loud. The staff was very nice and did a great job! Perhaps expectations were too high. We were anticipating fine dining in a business casual atmosphere. This is a hand you your plate type of service, which is fine but not usual for that price point. The food was pretty good. I had the sirloin that had good flavor but was wayyyyy over cooked at well not mid/rare at all.  For a $80 aged sirloin I anticipated a mind blowing steak and it was meh...decent.  The grilled veggies with humus was a little funny. At first it looked like a lot of food but upon eating it was a lot of grilled lettuce and some veggies but not. It was good for what it was, the humus was very good.  Brulee was very nice as was the motel chocolate cake.  The drinks were the stand out. At the servers recommendation we had the...Brooklyn I think, it was really really nice. It was obvious there were regulars. The table next to us had visits by several staff to chat. We had one man and one lady stop by ask if everything was good and went on their way....we assume they worked there. All in all with the amount of options when visiting New York we have had much better and certainly for more than $200/person. We'd not go back unless it was for the bar. Haha. Forgot to take pictures for the food but did get desert.

Great brunch, excellent service. Feels like a country club in Westchester without leaving NYC. Our waitress was lovely. Our drinks were great! Didn’t have to wait for anything for more than a few minutes. Live music was quite the treat. All the outdoor tables were pretty well shaded.

While exploring Central Park we grabbed lunch at here. We arrived a little past eleven, when it opens, and were seated right away in the dinning area.

Two options for visiting - meal experience or drinks with small bites in the lounge area. The dinning area has an open kitchen concept so you have the opportunity to watch the chef in action.

Our table opted for the New York clam chowder, figs with cream and honey, and the steak sandwich with fries. The food was filling and flavorful. The sandwich could be a shared plate. My clam chowder was good, but my brain was envisioning “New England” style clam chowder and was momentarily confused when what looked like vegetable soup was presented.

Our waitress was amazing! She gave pointers of things to experience while here and told us of some local favorites to grab some of the best food.

The views of the restaurant looking out into the park were relaxing. Great experience.

As a Ghostbusters fan, there was no way I couldn't pass up this restaurant. The food was amazing & to top it off my Wife & I celebrated our 26 anniversary here. When we come back to NYC, we will be looking at another dinner here again. The staff was amazing & on top of everything for as busy as the were. (They had a Wedding Reception going on as well)

Everything was amazing! Delicious drinks, food, and a great atmosphere. Our waiter was amazing and gave great recommendations. The short ribs were our favorite, so tender they just fell apart. Will come back next time I’m in NYC!!

Wow. Simple ingredients cooked to perfection, where art, food, and perfection mingle. I have the trout, with green beans and almonds, all served on a bed of beautifully preserved potatoes. I also indulged in the goat cheese, spring mix appetizer.  My friend had French fries, and a wedge salad, and even those were amazing!

The food is amazing, the staff is awesome, and the atmosphere is... well, it's the iconic Tavern on the Green! Don't forget to visit the gift shop, nice items at reasonable prices.
** Just a history lesson, but this building was built in 1870 and was actually a barn for the 200 sheep that grazed in central park.

Ingredients tasted fresh, portions were satisfying, and the sauces tied everything together really well. Staff were friendly and the place had a clean, modern atmosphere. Definitely worth trying if you like breakfast sandwiches or comfort food.

Wow what a fantastic breakfast. The menu is simple but at the same time has so many good choices. The staff was very helpful and friendly especially Henry. I got the bacon egg and cheese and added avocado to it. The eggs really were unique and fluffy and the bread was incredible. Great coffee too. I would definitely come back to try the spicy beef Patty sandwich.

The hype is real! I had the bacon and egg sandwich and it was the best I've had. The bread is delicious...the eggs are so soft and so delicious. The only.thing that would beat this would be adding more bacon. Confession I'm a bacon lover so what was provided is adequate. The tater tots were good I just needed a pinch of salt to mine. Once paired with the ketchup though it hit the spot. Attractive packaging and i love how it held sandwich together. Overall it was worth the parking and price. The customer service was great! I wish the outside area was clean then maybe I would've had it there...then again maybe not. Its a "lively" area. I'd definitely do a repeat in this order or try other menu items.

It’s a good option for a quick bite or to-go orders if you are an egg lover and in the area. The spread in the menu is quite decent and what I love about the place is it’s made mostly fresh and the scrambled eggs used as stuffings are really soft and will quite literally melt in your mouth. The one thing to bear is mine is that seating  is only outdoor and limited seats available as well. Best time to visit given their menu would be breakfast or brunch
Great place with very friendly and welcoming staff! They have a great variety of options to choose from. Really enjoyed the breakfast and would definitely recommend!
