top_reviews.content: I was expecting to love this place because it’s so raved about! But I wasn’t impressed. The food was okay and so was the coffee.  The top of the crème brûlée latte was so yummy but I didn’t like how it paired with their coffee and I don’t like the almond milk they use. Service was great tho and so was the atmosphere. Also everything was super beautiful. I think I’m going to go back and try the latte again with oatmilk

It’s a puzzling esthetic but as I sat down, enjoyed my coffee, and took into the actual vibe of the coffee shop, I kinda got it.  Sitting inside, I felt I was outside a coffee brewery on a cloudy sad day.  The 80’s music playing definitely made me reminisce of Midwest rainy days with little to no sun.  I appreciated it more the more I put my head up and looked around instead of on my phone.

I got a vanilla type iced espresso (einsplainer sp?) with focaccia prosciutto small plate.  Both were tasty and added to my experience in the shop.

Koreatown’s been buzzing lately, with trendy restaurants and coffee shops popping up all over the place. We’ve hit up a bunch of the popular spots around here, but on a recent visit through the neighborhood, we stumbled across The Alchemist, a super chic coffee shop. I grabbed a matcha latte, and it was solid—smooth, not overly sweet, just how I like it. They’ve got a tempting lineup of pastries too, though I didn’t try them this time. The vibe? Awesome. The place was packed with people chatting and soaking in the lively atmosphere. Service was friendly and quick, which sealed the deal. Definitely a spot worth checking out if you’re in K-town!

Tiramisu & creme brulee latte are genuinely so good
Matcha was good too but not the best ive tried in ktown
Great work study spot lots of charging
Their gochujang musubi toast was so good. You can’t go wrong with their single origin cold brew coffee either.

Loved the atmosphere & staff! Super friendly and very beautiful space. Got the matcha einspanner & tiramisu latte, both were okay. Matcha tasted like water at first but then you start to acclimate to it when you mix in the sweet cream. Others agreed it was sort of grainy tasting. Tiramisu latte was better but still watery. Pastries on the other hand were amazing! We got the Dubai chocolate, chocolate macrons, caneles & a coffee crumb cake! Highly recommend any of those pastries they’re all so good! I’d give this place another chance if I’m in the area.

I was back in town visiting a friend. On our last morning we decided to grab some coffee and maybe a croissant for the ride home.
The space was very open, clean, and a great place to come in with your laptop and get some work done while drinking your coffee.
The cashier was friendly and answered all of our questions and I was also trying to find a gluten free option for food for my wife.
We wanted to try a few items on the menu.  We ordered the Misugaru Latte and the Tiramisu Latte. The Misugaru Latte was a black sesame oat latte. It was on point and was delicious. the only thing I would order differently next time would to add another shot of espresso to it. I am not exactly sure but maybe because of the sesame and grain mix, the drink itself was a bit thicker. Don't let this deter you, order this latte. The Tiramisu lived up to the consistency and taste. Both lattes were not overly sweet and the coffee did shine.
We also ordered the GF Financier and I ordered an everything bagel with cream cheese. Now, I am a cream cheese lover and the amount of cream cheese was just what I wanted. Spot on for me!
Next time I'm back in KTown I will definitely be back.

I guess people like this coffee shop because it looks different than a Starbucks. I just had their large ice americano and it tasted a bit sour. Usually this means that the brew was too short lived. There were many folks studying and doing work on their devices and the shop provides Wi-Fi and many power outlets. I guess for Koreatown it is better than average for those who want a quiet place to work. Parking is bad since it is downtown area. Drinks are about 20% more than your Starbucks drinks.

Today I witnessed a master class in restaurant efficiency and customer service—if you can call it that.
The recipe seemed simple: take one customer, add a little attitude, mix in some unnecessary drama, and finish with a complete disregard for basic professionalism.

It's always fascinating to watch employees act as if customers and delivery drivers are inconveniences rather than the reason the business exists in the first place.

A delivery driver arrived at an almost empty restaurant, ( Check Photos ) checked in, and waited outside as instructed.
Since the restaurant was practically deserted, I assumed getting the order would be quick.

Silly me.
Twenty three minutes later, the driver was still standing there like a lawn ornament.
Nobody updated him.
Nobody checked on him.
Nobody seemed remotely concerned that a customer was waiting for their food.
Meanwhile, the employees responsible for the orders appeared to be participating in an advanced seminar on chatting, laughing, and avoiding work.

Then came the grand finale.
The order was finished and placed on the counter.
Not handed to the driver.
Not announced.
Not brought outside.
Just sitting there like a museum exhibit.

The driver eventually complained to the manager, who found the order exactly where it had been all along.
The explanation?
“He’s just a kid.”
Ah yes, the famous restaurant management strategy: put someone in charge of customer orders, then explain their mistakes by saying they don’t know what they’re doing.

Restaurant owners, here’s a shocking business secret: delivery drivers are not random people wandering around your parking lot.
They represent paying customers.

Customers come and go. Delivery drivers come and go. But bad reviews, lost business, and a damaged reputation tend to stick around.

​I recently dined at Gabin Korean Grill, and it was an absolutely phenomenal experience from start to finish! ​First and foremost, the service here is top-tier and utterly flawless. The staff are incredibly friendly, attentive, and highly professional, making us feel genuinely welcomed and well-taken care of throughout the entire meal. Their impeccable timing with grill management and proactive refills enhanced our overall dining experience tremendously. The quality of service alone easily earns a five-star rating.

The quality and marbling of the meat are exceptional, and every dish—from the pristine side dishes to the savory stews and refreshing cold noodles—is incredibly clean, fresh, and executed to perfection. Nothing felt overly heavy or greasy; instead, everything tasted beautifully balanced and well-prepared.

Once you experience the incredible atmosphere, the attentive service, and take that very first bite of their premium meat, you will instantly understand exactly why I am raving about this place. If you are looking for a clean, upscale, and genuinely delicious Korean BBQ experience, look no further. I will definitely be back very soon!

Wow I can’t believe how incredible the food is here. This is not your typical Korean bbq. This is elevated and intentional Korean food with impeccable, full table service. I tried the $185 combo today and added a $12 nengmyun. Keep in mind it’s Pyeongyang style nengmyun and is different than what you may think is “standard” nengmyun. The meat quality is fantastic here. Really nice marbling. The standout for me was the galbi. So tender and struck a nice balance between the soy and the sweetness for me. The ssam and banchan are also so beautifully presented. The soups at kbbq tend to be an afterthought type of filler dish, but they don’t do regular soups here. The doenjang jjigae was made like my grandma makes, with a deep, umami anchovy based broth. They even utilized shiitake mushroom in it, which I have never seen before. Definitely an additional umami flavor to the dish, but this is really what I mean by everything is intentional. The spicy beef rib soup is my recommendation for the soup for the combo. It’s like the best yukgaejang/galbitang crossover I’ve ever had. The clean aftertaste from the radish in it is fantastic. The flavors of the different ingredients used really stood out to me. The nengmyun broth had a deep beef flavor and touch of sweetness that was simply perfect once I added in mustard and vinegar. The noodles are not my personal preference (I like hamheung style), but the broth is just *wow*. I was quite impressed to say the least. The meal combo was enough for 3 of us. They began to really fill up around 6:30. I can’t recommend this place enough.

Capo – Santa Monica, CA
Rating: ★★★☆☆
Having come up in the industry working for Joseph Pignato at The Rivermere in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, I know exactly what technical precision looks like. When you’ve operated at that level—or dined at institutions like The Blue Strawberry—you develop a palate that doesn't settle for "almost." My standard for pasta is set by the likes of Lievito Bistro in Nicaragua, run by my wife’s brother-in-law who learned his passion for cooking in Italy. When you've experienced his daily handmade pasta—crafted with the authentic passion and soul of a chef straight from Italy—you know exactly when a kitchen is missing that heart. At a $687 price point, Capo's execution needs to be surgical, and tonight, it felt mechanical.
Technical Hits and Misses
* The Scallop Black Truffle ($96): This was the major disappointment of the evening. The sear was pushed too far, leaving a carbonized, burnt flavor that masked the delicate scallop and fought against the truffle. For nearly $100, that plate should be flawless; tonight, it was a technical failure.
* Lobster Pasta ($60): The lobster itself was the highlight—delicious and perfectly cooked. However, the kitchen was heavy-handed with the salt, nearly overshadowing the natural sweetness of the meat.
* The Pomodoro ($28): When you’re used to the fresh, vibrant pasta at Lievito Bistro, you notice the details.
Service and Logistics
Service from Roger was great, along with his hospitality.He earned the 20 gratuity. But adding it as a line item feels like a disconnect from a "guest-first" philosophy.
The Bottom Line
There is talent here, but the lack of consistency is glaring.
I have to say that my old fashioned was delicious and perfect and my wife's lemon drop was spot on. At $100+ per person, I expect much more  from the food consistency.  My wife is a USC graduate with a D.D.S. and also has high expectations... and noted the burt taste and smell of the scallops and the salty Lobster. Having grown up in New England and having a fisherman  and lobsterman deliver fresh live fish off the boat at the restraunt dock every morning I also know what to expect with such a dish.... So.... stick to the fresh daily made pasta dishes, and know that kitchen consistency may not meet the reputation or price.... yet expect an amazing dining experience in a staple of Santa Monica.

My visit to 88 Hotdog was an unexpectedly delightful culinary adventure, especially for someone with a penchant for creatively crafted fast food. Nestled in a bustling, crowded area where parking can be a bit of a treasure hunt, this gem stands out for its unique offerings and commendable service.

Starting with the mozzarella corn dog, it was a standout in both size and flavor, offering great value for its price. The corn dog was perfectly crispy on the outside, with a gooey, stretchy mozzarella center that was both satisfying and indulgent. It’s the kind of treat that brings a smile to your face with each bite, blending the nostalgic essence of a classic corn dog with a cheesy twist that elevates it to a whole new level.

The adventure didn't stop there; the yogurt drinks were a revelation in their own right. I indulged in a variety of flavors - peach, mango, blueberry, and pineapple - each one more refreshing and flavorful than the last. These drinks had a perfect balance of sweetness and tartness, with the fruit flavors shining through beautifully. They were not just good; they were exceptional, adding a refreshing contrast to the savory richness of the corn dog.

The service at 88 Hotdog deserves a special mention. Despite the crowded location, the employee was friendly, efficient, and quick to serve, making the overall experience even more pleasant. It's always a breath of fresh air to encounter service that is both warm and competent, especially in fast-paced environments.

While the parking situation and crowded surroundings might deter some, the culinary delights and the cheerful service at 88 Hotdog make it well worth the effort. It's a small price to pay for the joy of biting into a delicious mozzarella corn dog and sipping on exquisitely flavored yogurt drinks. For anyone in the area or those willing to brave the parking challenge, 88 Hotdog is a must-visit spot that promises a satisfying and tasty experience.

Never disappoints. Best k-dog I've ever had (yes, even in Korea) and the so-tteok so-tteok is exactly the right addition to round it out.
Friendship hot dogs forever!
Such friendly service and the hot dog is pretty good too - I got the half mozzarella half meat option…the mozzarella is perfect melted.

Really good Korean kdogs I got the full cheese/potato kdog with hot Cheetos (it is extra). I wish they had more sauces but they have honey mustard, ketchup and sweet chili. Oh and spicy mayo included on your kdog too.

We found paid street parking on a Sunday but it said free parking so yay we got lucky. The small parking lot they have in that lil strip mall seemed full and I think you pay to park in there.

But definitely a must try for the Korean corn dogs 11/10!

I found this spot via Google search. The parking is limited. Thank goodness I found a spot. The food plac itself is extremely small. The music was blasting. It was so loud I could barely here the man behind the counter. I had the number 3. It was a cheddar dog. The cheddar cheese sat at the bottom of thr corn dog. When I finally got to the cheese it tasted like kraft singles sandwich cheese. For the drink, I had the orange pineapple juice. That was amazing.

After a small snack at Kyochon just a few yards away came in to check out their Korean style corn dogs.
Pleasantly surprised how good they were. The wifey had seen a Mark Weins video eating some of these type of corn dogs and knew of this spot.
So we gave it a try.
At first the staff asked me if I wanted sugar on it. I was in total disbelief and said "Sugar on the corndog?"
Servee replied with have you ever eaten funnel cakes?
I said "Yes, but no sugar on my corn dog"
Server said "Ok I'll put just a little on the top and you try it and if you want more just let me know"
Oh yeah, I asked for a side of sugar and added it to my corndog. They also asked what kind of sauce, ketchup, or mustard, I wanted. I chose the sweet chili, which I won't get next time. It truly does wonders if you just top it with sugar. I love mustard on my corn dogs usually, however wanted to try something different. Sugar it is!
My wife got the cheese filled and daughter got the regular with sugar.
We loved it and want to come back and try their other corn dogs and then some of their ice creams and or fruit juices/smoothies.
Thier service was friendly and extremely helpful with all their suggestions.
They get ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ for their outstanding service.

Food is not bad.

name: Souvlaki GR – Midtown East
address: 231 E 53rd St, New York, NY 10022, United States

business_details.details: 231 E 53rd St, New York, NY 10022, United States

top_reviews.content: For those with taste buds that were refined summering in  Greece for many years, the taste of the souvlaki pita is unmistakably familiar. Warm pita break, pork pieces cut small, just the right amount of tzatziki, and, of course, French fries. The only question that remains is whether to order two, or go directly for three. They have other great dishes too, but the pita is a must.

Took me back to Greece. They have created a beautiful, homely (blue) ambience, food was on point. Authentic lemon potatoes, roast chicken and fish. And while it wasn't on the menu, they did give me some  of their Mastiha.

Amazing little spot in Midtown east, you step in and it’s like being in Greece. Perfect for a date or with friends. I was here for restaurant week and it did not disappoint, the menu for dinner was $30 and it exceeded our expectations. The portions were big and we liked everything. Special mentions: cheese croquettes and the mains (a whole branzino, perfectly cooked and seasoned and lamb chops).
We also got a couple of wine glasses and since I got a pine wine the waiter was very thoughtful and let me try it before pouring the full glass in case I didn’t like it.
Overall a very nice dinner and I would definitely go back!

From the moment you walk in, you’re welcomed by a warm and cozy atmosphere. The restaurant truly feels like a little piece of Greece in NYC.

The service was good. Our server was friendly and recommended the weekly deal which was hard to pass up! For just $30 per person, you get an appetizer, entrée, and dessert.

The avgolemono soup was absolutely phenomenal. Very comforting and perfectly balanced with lemony notes that tied all the flavors together beautifully.

The tyrokroketes started off delicious however, the aftertaste was a bit strong. If kefalotyri was one of the cheeses used, that would explain the sharpness. While not my personal favorite, it was still enjoyable overall and the dip made it much better.

The lamb chops were outstanding, perfectly marinated and full of flavor, paired with fries that were extra crispy and seasoned just right.

Unfortunately, the moussaka was extremely disappointing. Every bite was so bland. The béchamel sauce lacked flavor. I expected at least a hint of nutmeg. The ground beef was unseasoned, and the eggplant felt simply tossed in the casserole rather than properly being fried first, leaving it tasteless. Overall, the dish fell flat and in desperate need of more thoughtful preparation. But I don’t think it reflects the menu as a whole, since the other dishes we ordered were excellent.

As for the baklava, absolutely freaking DELICIOUS!! This is potentially the best baklava I’ve ever had, even better than the Lebanese version. The honey and walnut mix so well with the crunchiness of the pastry. Definitely a must have!

Hard to see from the street but glad I found it online! I was in town for work and wanted quick, easy, delicious food to take back to my hotel room. This was a perfect choice. Meat skewer, spanakopita, and baklava were all excellent. Really needed that spinach after eating a lot of bagels and cream cheese this week. The dining room was super cozy and the staff kind and courteous. I'd like to go back sometime with friends for dine-in. :)

Amazing food! I recommend this place 100%. The food is authentic, perfectly cooked, and the entire staff is very kind. We loved the Greek atmosphere and the local flavors. It felt like a real escape tonight—thank you!

Souvlaki GR is one of the very few places that truly deserves a shout‑out. I usually don’t rate competitors, but this spot is a trigger in the best way. Absolutely outstanding. The food is exceptional, full of authentic Greek flavor, tradition, and quality that goes far beyond expectations. Every dish tastes like it was made with real care and pride. The atmosphere and décor in each location bring Greece to life, creating a warm and inviting experience that feels genuinely traditional.

A place that honors Greek food the right way.
Thank you!!

I came here with my husband and we had a good time. The staff were friendly and welcoming, and the service was smooth. The fries and feta pie were definitely the stars—so tasty and well prepared.

The only letdown was the bifteki and chicken skewers, which were both pretty dry and overcooked. I’ve had the gyro here before and it was delicious, so I’ll probably stick with that next time.

An Absolute Gem – Beyond Expectations!

​The menu is incredibly sophisticated, with every dish crafted to perfection. A special shoutout to the steak—it was cooked flawlessly, incredibly juicy, and absolutely delicious.
​The service deserves the highest praise. The staff is remarkably attentive, professional, and welcoming—everything is top-tier.

I will come back again for special occasions.

Fia hosted a private event for us for about 45 people.  Sheena coordinated the whole thing for us, even going to the florist to pick up our flowers to save us a few bucks.  She did great.  Food was great.  Atmosphere as good as it gets (we reserved the outdoor area).  Priced about the same as the competition, but much better value.  Total transparency and no surprises.  Execution was great.  We had a few surprise vegetarians which they accommodated at no cost to us.  Their open bar was generous too - I know of several drink orders they didn't charge us for.   Highly recommend them for private events.

top_reviews.content:
I’ve been wanting to try this place for years and finally had the chance to try it. I’ve been vegetarian for 19 years and my boyfriend eats meat and we went together.

We each got a single vegan cheeseburger with everything on it. We both loved it and our 50/50 side, we devoured it all so quickly and no complaints!

hands down THE BEST plant based burger i’ve ever had. when i went vegan the one food i missed was in&out burger and fries, and Montys burger taste just like it but even better imo.

parking wise, im not sure if they have a parking lot. there’s plenty of street parking so that’s what i did.

I had dinner here yesterday around 7–8 PM, and this was my third time visiting. I’ve loved this place since my first visit, both for the food and for the wonderful service from the staff, so unfortunately, last night’s experience was disappointing.

While I was deciding what to try this time, I approached one of the employees when I was ready to place my order. She was still preparing something for the previous customer, so when she didn’t respond, I initially thought I hadn’t realized she was busy. I waited patiently until she was finished and then placed my order.

I chose to eat there, and when I went back to ask for a refill of my drink, I had a similar experience. She was preparing a drink, so I understood that she was busy and waited. However, she didn’t acknowledge me or say anything like, “I’ll be with you in a moment” or “Please give me a minute.” Instead, I felt completely ignored. Another employee noticed me and came over almost immediately to offer help, which I really appreciated.

I understand that employees can be busy, tired, or having a difficult day, and I’m always willing to wait. What made me uncomfortable was the lack of communication and acknowledgment. A simple “one moment, please” would have made a big difference.

I still really like this place, and the other employees I interacted with were great. That’s why I hope this is just an isolated experience. I’m sharing this because I would love to continue coming back and have the same welcoming experience I had during my first two visits.

I honestly had no idea this was a vegan burger place the first couple of times I ate here. I think it was around my third visit when I finally realized everything was plant-based, and I was genuinely shocked. 😂

I’m not vegan or vegetarian, so when I ordered the burger for the first time, I just ate it like a regular burger. The flavor, texture, sauce, and the way everything came together made me think I was eating a normal meat burger. I never stopped to question it.

When I found out it was actually plant-based, I couldn’t believe it. That alone says a lot about how good Monty’s Good Burger is. Usually, you can immediately tell when something is trying to imitate a traditional burger, but that wasn’t my experience here at all. It was satisfying, flavorful, and tasted like an actual indulgent burger rather than a “healthy alternative.”

I’ve been back multiple times now, and the quality has been consistently good. I usually get takeout, and the food still tastes great by the time I get home. The staff has also always been friendly and the service has been quick and easy.

Even if you have absolutely no interest in vegan food, I would still recommend giving this place a try. Don’t go into it thinking, “I’m going to try a vegan burger.” Just order what looks good and judge it as a burger.

The fact that I ate here several times before realizing I wasn’t eating meat is probably the best compliment I can give them. 😂

Definitely one of those places that completely changed my idea of what a plant-based burger can taste like. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Wish I took a picture of the burger - but we’ve had Monty’s before so many times - never at this spot though . We walked in and they made a delicious burger!!!! Probably the best one we’ve ever had . We’ll have to come back and have another 😝 update : we came back again the very next day ! And I took a picture - was craving the burger - sooooooo delicious !

The people behind me were checked on multiple times while I couldn't even get someone's attention.

I eventually had to wave down the hostess just to ask for a to-go box and my check because my server never came back. It honestly made me feel invisible.

The food was good, but not memorable enough to justify the price. Considering the service, atmosphere, and long wait, we left feeling disappointed. There are plenty of restaurants in New York that offer a much better dining experience for the same price. I’d recommend saving your money and going somewhere else.

One of the best meals I’ve ever had. Every bite was spectacular. The duck is most definitely worth booking a dinner reservation.

On top of that, I don’t think I’ve ever had better service in my life, and I’ve had incredible servers in the past. But the way the staff worked as team was absolutely incredible. My favorite moment of the evening was our server pairing the best dessert wine with my ile flottante - a pairing I’m still thinking about weeks later.

The city has some spectacular food, but I’d still return here every visit.

Le Veau d'Or was phenomenal from start to finish. The food and atmosphere were at the top of what you would expect from a rising NY star.

We started with the escargot, which was perfectly prepared with a crunch that takes this French classic to a different level. The half chickeywa a large portion which was great for sharing. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared and showcased the restaurant's commitment to quality.

The service was attentive without being intrusive. Our only opportunity for improvement was that our server gave the vibe that she didn't want to be there. The warm, intimate atmosphere shows why Le Veau d'Or has such a strong reputation.

This place is a delight
On the night after Dining at the Four Horseman I was fortunate enough to join friends here for dinner. I had the best server imaginable. The same person as last night!

Moritz Kissinger Brut nature for starters!
Staff there knew it was my bday, they treated me royally, I was moved by their graciousnes. Chef sent out loads of extra plates, delectable. It's a 4 course price fixe, we added frogs legs that arrived sizzling in a buttery gratin dish.

The kitchen produced the classics with expertise and elan.
Seamless, attentive and expert hospitality with bread and butter!

Tucked away on a bustling Midtown street, Le Veau d'Or hides behind what appears to be a simple residential door, a charming secret that opens into a classic French bistro adorned in elegant black and red accents.

I had the pleasure of celebrating my birthday here with my husband, and the hospitality made it feel special from the very first moment. The staff greeted us warmly and wished me a happy birthday multiple times throughout the evening. The menu is classically French at its heart, yet thoughtfully crafted with the seasons in mind, a balance that speaks to both tradition and care.

We initially worried that a three-course meal might not be enough, so we added a side order of fries dish just to be safe, but the generous, beautifully executed appetizers and freshly served bread were so satisfying that we found ourselves nearly full before the main course even arrived!

Le Veau d'Or is the kind of restaurant you want to keep as your own little secret, yet can't help but tell everyone about. Though with reservations as coveted as they are, the secret is very much already out.

At Le Veau d’Or, this wasn’t just a meal it was a culinarily pilgrimage. The kind you build a day around, maybe even quietly justify a whole trip for.

Some meals are convenient. This one required intention. A little planning, a little movement, a little luck with scoring a reservation. And the second you walk in, the intimate feel, red banquettes, and warm welcome makes you feel right at home.

The déjeuner is $85 and reads like a tightly edited love letter to French classics. No fluff, no trends, just conviction. Escargots Provençale? Obviously. Oysters? Non negotiable. There’s something deeply satisfying about a menu that confidently serves tripe and calf’s liver.

Then the mains. Steak frites if you’re leaning timeless. Duck confit if you’re leaning into the moment. Lobster salad if you want to pretend you’re being light. Everything lands with that effortless, practiced precision like it’s been done this way forever and sees no reason to change.

And somewhere between the first bite and the last sip, it clicks: this is the highlight. Not just of the day, the trip. The meal you’ll keep referencing, the one that makes everything else feel like a prelude or an afterthought.

It’s the kind of place worth going out of your way for, and then some.

Special shout out to Liz for setting the gold standard for service.

We enjoyed the restaurant from the days of Mr Treboux and his daughter and looked forward to return. We were delighted to see that the renovation under new owners has refreshened the menu, but has left the decor intact. But somehow L’ Veau d’ Or is more vibrant, certainly busier, and noisier.
We enjoyed the food, everything was very good, and the platings more contemporary.  Wish the duck confit with frisée was paired with something else. Their famed floating islands (the recipe was recently in the Wall Street Journal), a dessert I really looked forward to having and that I order whenever it’s on a menu, has changed to my disappointment. I am not a sugar-loving person, but they have reduced the sweetness tooo much. My second complaint is about the service, we just got a not-excellent server. No water refills, she took away our entree plates and brought us the check! didn’t even ask if we wanted desert or coffee. We had to flag another server and tell her what happened. She was extremely gracious, took our order, brought the desserts, and took care of us from then on as our original server disappeared, never to be seen again.

Finally checked out the new Le Veau D'Or for lunch and it far exceeded my expectations. Staff is wonderful, helpful, welcoming, super friendly. I ordered the mackerel, the lobster salad (sublime) and the Il Flottante (the best I've ever had). Also had two gin gimlets and big shoutout for the bread service (really scrumptious). The mackerel was the only thing that, for me, was underwhelming.
I was also extremely happy to see that they have redone the restaurant in a very gentle way that still pays homage to the past. Very warm and cozy ambiance.

top_reviews.content: Top tier place. I lost count how many times we ate here and ordered for takeout. My bf and I consider Iki Ramen as our spot. Our favorite? the Chashu don bowl, the best one I’ve had so far across all Japanese restaurants I’ve been at. I love as well the Matcha crème brûlée dessert, and I miss their King Crab Hand Roll that we had there during our first visit. Their ramen is so rich in flavor, we highly recommend the A5 Wagyu Ramen and Tonkotsu! We also always order the Squid Leg Karaage, Takoyaki, Soft Shell Crab Bao and their Chicken Gyoza. All worth it. Excellent service as well, plus the atmosphere is always so calm. 🤍🫶🏻

First off:  parking.  On a Sunday, it's all valet parking within the lot.  Find meter parking if you can - it's free on Sundays (at least at this time).

Food:  yuzu shio ramen.  Very refreshing, even for a hot dish.  If you're not looking for the typical tonkotsu broth which can be heavy, then this one is light and clean.  Ramen texture is standard, not too soft.  The chashu slices (4) were nice and tender with just a hint of char.  They gave a decent amount of bamboo shoot slices and maybe two tablespoons of green onions. too.  This was very good.

The blossom roll... I don't know.  The rice felt a little starchy?  There was a hint of being undercooked but not in the sense of being hard.  It's more of giving that rice scent that I associate with undercooked rice.  I don't know what it is but I didn't like it.

Service is fantastic!  My girlfriend ordered the Tai spicy miso ramen but ended up not looking it at all.  She didn't realize it would have the flavor profile she disliked, despite the description.  The waitress took care of it and replaced it with her favorite:  the Yuzu shio ramen.

The atmosphere:  dine-in with house music playing in the background.  There's a smell in the air that's chemical... Like a cleaning product used in the bathrooms of some restaurants.  Its not pine-sol... Either ways, it was off-putting.  Thankfully it didn't overwhelm the smell of the food while eating.

Would I come back here?  Maybe.  But if I do, I know the Yuzu shio ramen is 5 stars for me.

Very solid, classic ramen and sushi restaurant in Ktown. Their yuzu ramen is light, unique and refreshing. Their fried shrimp bao is a great snack.

The place is somewhat small, and parking is difficult. Reservations are needed for weekends.

Would recommend and one of the best Japanese spots in Ktown.

7 of us in our party came here for lunch and decided on the tasting menu. The restaurant is located in a strip plaza in K Town. We took the last 2 parking spots in the lot, so the 3rd car had to use street parking. The restaurant itself is not that spacious, perhaps 20 max. Beside the chef's tasting menu, there's also a omakase menu as well as a la carte menu as well. At the core of it, Iki is famous for its ramen, hence the name, and it's included as one of the dish in the tasting menu. I would describe it as an izakaya restaurant experience.
- Seabream Sashimi is fresh with wonderful yuzu dressing (4/5). The menu states halibut (hirame) Sashimi but we were served seabream (tai) Sashimi instead which is a letdown.
- The pork bao is better than the shrimp bao. The spicy tuna + crispy rice and the tomato burata is good but nothing special (3/5).
- Mentaiko mazemen with ikura is good. The spicy mentaiko cream gives it a bit of a kick (4/5). Tobiko might elevate it better than ikura?
- 5 nigiri set is fresh, but average lineup of salmon, squid, tuna, ikura and yellowtail. I was hoping for uni or amaebi. (3/5)
- A5 Wagyu Ramen is amazing. The broth has tremendous depth, the noodle is amazing. Alas, the portion is too small (5/5)
- Ube cheesecake: the dessert is like a forgotten step child. Don't get me wrong, I love Uncle Tetsu cheesecake, but I would have expected a bit more preparation to the dish, like a mango or lychee puree to go with it. (2/5)

We knew Iki Ramen from a friend who’s been a regular there and he had plenty of stuffs from the menu he recommended. Apparently Iki Ramen was popular not only for their ramen but also mazemen and sushi rolls.

Call us lucky, I thought we just arrived at perfect timing, right before the venue suddenly got busy and the line started to form. The petite space with dim lighting did remind us of local Japanese restos vibes.

We got couple of their favorites, the Mentaiko Mazemen and the Iki Rolls. Both were on the creamy side, which was perfect when shared. The Mazemen was more like creamy pasta but with ramen base for us. We love the sauce, the Ramen texture, but would prefer if it carried more protein. We even thought of ordering sides protein to accompany it. Whereas for the rolls, it was just flawless. Came with rich stuffing and literally felt like melt in our mouths especially that aburi sauce on top.
It was my first time here and it was amazing. The restaurant is super clean, food very fresh, and our servers were attentive and friendly. Glad I found this yummy place!!!

You gotta love LA for the hidden 💎gems you can find in so many strip malls around town. Iki Ramen’s Koreatown location is one such spot, an oasis of serenity and deliciousness just behind its door. I briefly wanted to gate-keep IKI bc it’s a small restaurant but of course I’m not! 😝

I originally went to the Hollywood location for ramen, which was delicious and comforting but not too heavy. But I definitely left wanting to come back for all the sushi that was also on the menu. And am I glad I did! Fresh fresh is a must and a given. You can start w appetizers like the well-salted edemame, miso black cod, or the house made, uniquely delicious MISO SOUP. Then take your pick from the many hand/cut rolls, signature rolls and sashimi offerings. They even have a few Bao “sandwiches” w ebi katsu, soft shell crab, pork and others.

But DO NOT skip the IKI GRAB HANDROLLS! Especially the PREMIUM one! The nori comes stacked separately from the mounds of rice and fish (or wagyu beef or scallops) so that you can leisurely (without worry of your nori getting soggy) put together your handroll. They were kind enough to cut each well portioned handroll “stuffing” into twos bc we were splitting it. Each one was incredible!!! The light touch of sauce/ seasoning is in perfect harmony with the fish/beef/scallops and absolutely melts in your mouth.

Don’t forget to save a little room for their delicious desserts. My favorite was the not-too-sweet black sesame crème brûlée.

The minimal concrete & wood decor plus the attentive but not hovering  and friendly service lets you focus on the food. I cannot gosh enough about what is now, for sure, my ⭐️ FAVORITE SUSHI 🍣 RESTAURANT in Los Angeles!! They recently opened Iki Nori also in Hollywood and I can’t wait to try that one too!

Haven’t tried the ramen yet but will be back for it! Service was caring and comfortable. Beautifully presented food. The most interesting cocktail list! The Dashi martini was so unique I had to try it.

Beautiful ambiance with stunning traditional Thai artwork that immediately transports you into a more authentic cultural atmosphere. The restaurant feels elegant yet cozy — perfect for dinner with family or friends.

Food-wise, the flavors were rich, balanced, and thoughtfully presented. The Tom Yum Koong had a fragrant broth with the right balance of spicy and sour, while the Gai Yang was juicy, flavorful, and perfectly grilled. The Pad Thai Bolan tasted more refined and less overly sweet than many typical versions.

The Crepe Dumplings were unique and beautifully plated, and the Kanom Tuay was a lovely traditional dessert to finish the meal. Even the Butterfly drink added a nice visual and refreshing touch.

Service was warm and attentive throughout the evening. Overall, this place feels more elevated than the average Thai restaurant in NYC — not just for the food, but for the atmosphere and experience as a whole. Would definitely come back.

The seafood spicy pasta had a nice kick without being too heavy or greasy, and the mentaiko pasta was delicious as well. I honestly didn’t expect to like everything we ordered this much! I definitely want to come back and try more dishes. Highly recommend this place!

This place has been operating at the same location under the same name since 1988. I used to visit frequently for their delicious and affordable lunch specials, and later on, I would drop by occasionally. I even remember going there with friends during the pandemic when outdoor dining was available. I rediscovered this spot after the nearby Concerto restaurant closed and I was looking for a similar place. During the meal, one of my companions accidentally splattered seafood spaghetti sauce onto someone else's shirt; a staff member quickly brought a cup with water and dish soap to help clean it up. We all agreed that the food was delicious. The three of us ordered a total of seven items: two orders of bulgogi tacos (three tacos per order), spicy cod roe pasta, seafood pasta, shrimp fried rice, bulgogi fried rice, and sweet potato fries. We also each ordered a drink; it’s worth noting that ordering a drink with a meal is cheaper than ordering it separately. The portion sizes were a bit disappointing, though—even after eating so much, I didn't feel particularly full. I visited during lunchtime, and the valet parking fee was $5.

Everytime I fly into LA it’s a must to stop at Nandarang to have great food, cocktails or beers. With 35 beer on tap this place is a hidden gem in Korea town. One thing that I truly love is that they have a few of the best Korean beers here in bottles TERRA & CASS. they do have a small wine selection for those of you that like wine. They also have a large selection of Soju and some high dollar Japanese whiskey. My favorite by the way hahaha. The staff has a fantastic vibe, lively and cool as hell. They are full service bar, with great prices, you won’t be disappointed. Definitely one of my favorite places to be at in Los Angeles when visiting. This time around I came in for drinks only. I’ll update with food pics the next time I’m in town.

My brother and I brought our father here for his birthday; first time for all three of us. $5 valet service was fast and convenient. We had an AMAZING time just chatting, celebrating, and eating together. We really appreciated the vibe. Loveddd the music; it was set at a perfect volume, which allowed us to have a conversation at the table. Food was tasty! Our server was friendly and attentive. We found another favorite! We will definitely be back with the rest of the family.
A decent place for late night hangout. Easy to place order and the food arrives fairly fast. Large selection of beer and alcohol. Not a big fan of the food though.
They have a very underrated selection of draft beers and I really enjoyed it! I did not get to try the food but I plan on it next time. I parked on a metered side street.

This place has so many different  beers omg I tried a peach pilsner it was very balanced it almost reminded me of a blue moon but more of a seeeter taste , also I still felt like I was drinking beer as opposed to other fruity beers that just seem like juice . My partner had another pilsner that was also very good .
Let's talk about the food😛, I am rice cake lover so that's what brought me here 😋 I've had tteoboki in other places and it's just too spicy where I have to dip my rice cake in a little water lol 😆, but these were perfect ! 🥰 loved the spice level and that you can add either ramen noodles or udon . I also tried the corn cheese 🧀  it was good but I didn't love the onion in it , but appreciated the uniqueness . Mozzarella sticks portion will feed a group of 8 very well 👌 we were just 2 but still devoured them lol. Pasta carbonara was very flavorful and the Korean BBQ tacos were flavorful as well .
Over all a good place to bring a crowd for sure 👌 💯 recommend this place !

OMG, amazingly good food to go along with a decent selection of beers. We ordered the kimchi pasta with bacon 🥓, Korean BBQ pork tacos, and animal fries. All of it was so dang good and portions were huge. There were 4 of us and we left with food.

Service was attentive, but not overbearing. Food came out quickly and piping hot 🔥.

Stumbling distance to the Wiltern.

Go.

address: 11 E 30th St, New York, NY 10016, United States

business_details.details: 11 E 30th St, New York, NY 10016, United States

top_reviews.content:
This is one of the many Korean restaurants in the area, and it is definitely one of our favourite! You will not be disappointed

We ordered their super famous Galbi Jjim (2 people portion) with fried rice, Sooyook, dumplings and cold noodle. The Galbi Jjim is absolutely the most wonderful dish of all. The beef is so tender and very tasty. The Sooyook, the pork meats are very tender and very well cook and their cold noodle is absolutely wonderful.

Best of all, their staffs are very friendly and generous, they replenished the side dishes very quickly.

Overall, one of the best Korean restaurant experience we’ve had in NYC.

Two thumbs up.

Btw, please make reservations in advance or else you may need to wait for a while.

Had dinner on a weekday here with a reservation and was seated almost immediately. They give you cold barley tea which was refreshing. We ordered the galbi Jim with the fried rice add on and hot white noodles, and the perilla leaf soy bean stew. The galbi jim was very tender an a big enough portion for three people. Adding the fried rice was a nice end to the meal and tasted great with the bits of beef. The stew was very interesting, never had that at other Korean spots and was comforting on a chilly day. The hot noodles were decent wish the noodles were a bit more al dente but the broth was excellent and very clean tasting. There were a bunch of banchans that came with the meal and my favorites were the soy egg, spinach, potato pancake, and kimchi. Overall, it was a good meal and everything tasted good and was fresh. Portions were just right and we were pretty stuffed for 3 people. Would also recommend the mocktails, they were light and refreshing. The menu is not that extensive but you can find a lot of interesting items that you don't typically find in other Korean spots.

We had a very positive experience here. Making a reservation was a breeze, and even though we arrived about 30 minutes early, they were able to seat us right away. Service was friendly and efficient, and our food came out very quickly.

Everything we ordered tasted good, and the restaurant itself was clean and well maintained, including the bathroom facilities.

Overall, a smooth and enjoyable dining experience from start to finish. I would happily return!

I heard their Naeng myun was a top seller and needed to try it since it’s getting hotter. I made a reservation for two, arrived early, and was seated early.
- Was pleasantly surprised by the cold barley tea they provide instead of water.
- Appreciate that they have pictures on their menu so you can get a sense of what you’re going to get.
- I went with a friend and we tried the Sooyook, mini Mool Naeng Myun (a personal favorite), and mini Galbi. We also got the Pear Ade and Green Grape Ade mocktails.
- Naeng Myun broth had a solid base flavor. I like mine a bit more acidic so I tend to add vinegar and mustard but if they didn’t have it I would’ve been fine with it. They didn’t use the usual buckwheat noodles which I would’ve preferred because I think they have a nicer chew.
-Sooyook was solid and I enjoyed the assorted condiments they provided. Would’ve loved to eat them with lettuce but overall I was pleased.
- Galbi looked amazing served with the bone and tasted great.
- Mocktails were refreshing. Highly recommend the Pear Ade if you love lean pear!

Wife was craving naengmyun tonight so we decided to stop in.  This restaurant is amazing.  We classify it as one of those "what if your halmonee went to culinary school" type restaurants.  Traditional classic Korean dishes but with an emphasis on quality ingredients, balance, precision, and process refinement. Like Danji or Hanjan.

Bibim naengmyeon was excellent, well balanced.  It wasn't too sweet, nor plastered over with sauce.

Mul naengmyun had a more dashi/myeolchi forward broth, and felt like they were leaning to make it more vegetarian friendly.

Banchans amazed us both with their quality and with the attentiveness of the staff.  We got kimchi (more on the savory end than the sour end) tteokbokki (perfectly cooked tteok), namul, potato and onion jeon (fried well, could be a bit crisper though).  And the staff restocked them every time they went empty. Wife and I were shocked everytime they brought more banchan, in Flushing we always have to ask for more everywhere we go.

A+

top_reviews.content: Great experience!!! My husband and I had reservations for Sunday June 7, 2026 and the entire experience was amazing! We ordered the Lobster Mac and Cheese as our appetizer and it did not disappoint. Huge chunks of lobster and the cheese was ever so creamy. For my entree I ordered the Wagyu Hanger Steak and it was delicious, not a sliver left on my plate. My husband ordered the Italian Basil Cavatelli with spicy Wagyu sausage that blew him away. Our dessert was a Mango cheese cake and it was amazing, paired with our coffee. All of our drinks from the bar were served perfectly and very tasty. Our server Lydia was nothing but the best. Lydia took care of us as if she knew us for years, and her recommendations were perfect! Having dinner at Valerie was amazing and my husband and I will definitely return to enjoy the atmosphere and the hospitality. Totally worth the visit! Loved it!

Came here for a slightly early dinner after a Broadway show with a party of 4 on a Sunday evening. We had a reservation, but it didn't seem like we would have needed one, but I suppose better safe than sorry. The ambiance feels straight of the golden age, which is an aesthetic I'm certainly a sucker for. Even their robust cocktail menu fits the bill and is one of the prettiest menus I've ever had the joy of perusing. Staff was able to sit us a little bit ahead of our reservation which was also much appreciated. Wait staff was also very helpful and attentive, I don't think I've ever had my water glass so topped off!

Starting off with cocktails, this place is a gin bar through and through and you'd be making a mistake if you didn't try one of their many options. I went with the 10,000 words, which you simply just give a spirit of your choice (I picked gin of course) and whether you antes) wanted your drink shaken or stirred and the bartender does the rest, so a bit of a surprise! I wound up with their version of The Last Word which was delightfully citrusy but I was hoping I'd wind up with something a little more adventurous app things considered. My girlfriend got the blackberry G&T, which was not only very pleasing to look at but delicious to boot.

For food, we started with splitting some zucchini blossoms and beef cheek bao buns (both come in portions of 3). Both were tasty, but I love a good bao bun and these were so light and pillowy, I could have just went for an order of those for my main course. For the entree I went for the roasted half chicken, perhaps the most unassuming choice on the menu but this was maybe the best roast chicken I've ever had. Prepared perfectly, cooked to perfection, excellent portion size, and the kicker of it all was the stunning gravy that I was tempted to lick my plate for. Chicken is very easy to screw up, and they nailed it on all fronts here. My girlfriend went for the Valerie Signature burger with white cheddar and this thing did not mess around! A very rich patty, cooked to her temperature of choice served alongside some garlic truffle fries that made an American classic feel just a little more elevated.

Our experience was delightful and I'd love to comeback here again, especially to check out more of the cocktail menu and soak in more of that golden age aura the place gives.

Julia, thank you for the best service ever! At Valerie, there are so many different areas for you to sit romantically in a candle lit quiet spot, or options of the bar and other lively spaces. I love carpaccio, Valerie has one of the best Waygu Carpaccio's...lightly salted, flavor forward Waygu, and the capers...less! The prawn and crab risotto was very tasty, prawns a bit overcooked, rubbery. However the risotto packed a bold seafood flavor that was spot on delicious.

This is a go to place for happy hour and dinner if in midtown. Chris is the BEST bartender ever. His recommendations for both the menu and some crafty cocktails are so on par! He’s got a gift! He was able to curate some awesome cocktails based on looking at a (and everyone loved them!). The hostesses are so sweet and accommodating (and pretty) it’s a welcome sight to walk into this nice place. Had the $1 oysters which were chucked to perfection. Everything was great! Highly recommend

VALERIE is an absolutely outstanding spot right in the heart of the city.

This bar has a real sense of history, and it’s definitely a place you must visit. Their oysters during happy hour (4–7 PM) are simply incredible — easily some of the best in the city.

I’m usually taken care of by a bartender there, and she does an amazing job — she somehow reads exactly what I want without me even saying it.

I genuinely love this place and highly recommend it to everyone.

Good service deserves applause. Bad service deserves notes.

Good travel gives photos. Great travel gives stories.

For my boyfriends birthday brunch before MJ the Musical, Valerie gave us a story.

We chose Valerie for its Midtown location, beautiful atmosphere, and reputation as a special-occasion brunch spot. The Art Deco-inspired space, live jazz, and overall energy made it feel like the perfect way to celebrate before heading to the theater.

Valerie also did an excellent job making my bf feel celebrated. The staff surprised him with a birthday shot and dessert, and our server was personable, attentive, and checked on us often throughout the meal.

We started with two cocktails, the Lemongrass and Tea with the Queen. Both were delicious and well-balanced. A pleasant surprise was the complimentary biscuits brought to the table. Crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and served with butter and jam, they were a delightful way to put a base in your stomach while enjoying a cocktail. After what was supposed to be a one-hour train ride turned into an unexpected three-hour NJ Transit adventure, those biscuits did a lot to take the edge off the initial sit-down hanger.

We also ordered the Dutch Baby pancake to start, which arrived hot, fresh, and absolutely lived up to the hype.

Unfortunately, our entrées told a different story.

We both ordered Benedicts, and both arrived cold. The hollandaise was refrigerator cold, which cooled down everything underneath it. The eggs were overcooked rather than runny, the chicken was room temperature, and even the English muffin seemed to have lost any warmth before reaching the table. The only warm item on my plate was the side of fries I substituted for home fries. My bf doesn't mind cold food, he ate it anyway.

To Valerie's credit, once I mentioned the issue, they immediately made it right. The dish was remade and served hot, this time with the hollandaise on the side. We learned that the hollandaise is prepared ahead of time and cannot simply be reheated without separating. Whether the original plate had been sitting too long or was assembled with cold hollandaise over food waiting under a heat lamp, the result was a dish that missed the mark. The second version, however, was exactly what we expected and was thoroughly enjoyed.

The atmosphere remained one of the highlights of the experience. The live jazz was a nice touch, the room is beautiful, and the Art Deco-inspired design creates a space that feels elegant without being stuffy.

Would I return?

Probably not.

Not because they made a mistake. Every restaurant has off moments. But in a city with endless brunch options, it's difficult to justify a return visit when a signature brunch dish arrives that far off the mark the first time. What I will remember, though, is that the staff handled the situation professionally, corrected it quickly, and helped make my bf's birthday feel special.

The Plot: Great service can recover a mistake, but it can't erase a first impression. Valerie earned our appreciation, but not necessarily our return visit.

Absolutely loved this place!! Such a smooth, classy vibe! It’s a great place to go with friends, on a company dinner or just for visiting NYC! Brendan was so kind and helpful and created the best experience for me! The chef was very accommodating of my allergies (gluten free) and was able to tweak a few things for me! Avery was my server and she recommended a martini for me and it was delicious! Overall, the experience at Valerie was one of a kind and I can’t wait until I’m back in NYC to come here again! Also the music was so fitting!

I went to Valerie with my family recently, and it was possibly one of our best choices for restaurants.

We went at around noon-ish on a Sunday for brunch, so there was a band playing. The lighting, atmosphere, and decor made the ambience feel comfortable and relaxing. All these factors gave the establishment have a nice vibe to it.

Not only that, the food was amazing and service was quick. 10/10, no complaints.

top_reviews.content:
Two of my friends live walking distance away, and the weather was gorgeous, so we decided to walk over. The space felt almost open air with the small fountain and high ceilings, and the ambiance and general vibe were fantastic.

Who knew Korean-Columbian fusion was a thing and that it could be this good?! The food was incredible as were the delicious non-alcoholic smoothies we tried (with dairy-free options available). Off hand, we tried chicken wings, the whole fried fish with coconut rice, yucca fries, and a few other things that were so good we fully consumed them before I remembered to take photos... Everything we ate and drank was fantastic as was the service!

They had a talented vinyl DJ playing for most of the time we were there, and I was shocked and impressed to learn he was the owner 😅 I was also surprised by our final bill, which was shockingly affordable, especially for DTLA. We’ll 1000% be back!

This meal was so good! Got to watch the WC game and eat and the atmosphere was welcoming. The Korean wings were such an amazing flavor - exactly what I was looking for. The ceviche was so fresh. Will be back soon! ◡̈

This is by far the best Colombian food in Los Angeles! I’ve been to a couple Colombian restaurants in LA and wasn’t really impressed and was disappointed, but I came across this place weirdly on TikTok. At first I was hesitant and skeptical because it was from TikTok, but I decided to give it a try and I was truly blown away. The food had amazing flavor, and the Korean mixed in with the Colombian cuisine was just fantastic. Don’t listen to any of the negative low ratings. I truly had the opposite experience. Give it a try and if you’re a true Colombian, you would really love it!

I’ve been to Escala in Koreatown a few times before, but this visit meant so much more because I brought my aunt, kids, and family to celebrate my aunt’s birthday. We’re all Colombian, and while we absolutely love our food, I really wanted them to experience Korean cuisine — and Escala did not disappoint.

The food was incredible, full of flavor, and honestly felt so homey and comforting. Everyone at the table loved what they ordered. Even my toddler and her cousins had the best time — the music and atmosphere made it such a fun space where they could enjoy themselves without feeling stuck at the table.

My aunt’s dish did come out later than the rest of ours, but we truly didn’t mind because the place was busy and everything we had tasted so amazing. What really stood out, though, was the level of care and service we received.

On my way to the bathroom, I recognized the owner and chef from social media and stopped to share how much I loved the food and the vibe. They were so warm and even asked if we were Colombian, which made the experience feel instantly more personal.

The highlight of the night was the chef — she went out of her way to come to our table, introduce herself, and genuinely connect with us. When she found out about my aunt’s delayed plate, she immediately took care of it and didn’t charge us, which we didn’t expect at all. It was such a kind gesture and showed how much pride and love she puts into what she does — truly taking care of people like family.

As we were leaving, she even came to find us to say goodbye. That level of attention and heart is something you don’t see everywhere.

Escala isn’t just amazing food — it’s an experience filled with warmth, culture, and genuine hospitality. We felt like family, and I will absolutely keep coming back.

Only been here for their late night happy hours M-Th. It’s chill and casual. Decently priced because of the happy hour menu. Love the whole wings in both flavors and empanadas with kimchi and with beef.

top_reviews.content:
Food during the happy hour is great and reasonably priced! I got the ribs, spicy salmon roll, and ceviche which I would definitely get again during happy hour. The restaurant ambience is also quaint and good for talking too.

I also came for dinner a separate time, however, the food wasn't too good. I liked the calamari and clam appetizer. I heard the popcorn shrimp was good too but I'm allergic. The tuna poke was very disappointing though; no flavor and mostly just fish, seaweed, lettuce, and ginger. Large portion sizes though.

Excellent experience! The food and service were amazing. A special thank you to Ian for going above and beyond. My drink was a bit too sweet for my taste, and he thoughtfully found a sour juice to add, which balanced it perfectly. His attention to detail and willingness to customize my drink made the experience even better. Outstanding customer service—I truly appreciated it and will definitely be back!

Pacific Catch in Santa Monica was a really solid experience from start to finish. The food came out fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. I ordered the Surf & Turf with grilled lobster tail, skirt steak, asparagus, mashed potatoes, chimichurri, and Hawaiian rolls. The steak was tender and the lobster had a nice buttery flavor without being too heavy.

The Lobster Roll was another favorite. The lobster tasted fresh and the griddled Hawaiian rolls added the perfect touch of sweetness. The sesame slaw balanced everything nicely.

We also shared the Pupu Platter which included coconut shrimp, sticky ribs, sea bass skewers, guaca-poke, and tortilla chips. Great option if you want to sample a few different appetizers. The sticky ribs and coconut shrimp were especially good.

For drinks, I had the Cloudline Pinot Noir and the Niña Colada. Both paired really well with the meal. The Niña Colada was refreshing and tropical without being overly sweet.

Dessert was the Chocolate Lava Cake with vanilla gelato and berries, and it was the perfect ending to the meal.

The atmosphere was relaxed, the service was friendly, and the overall experience was great. Definitely a spot I’d come back to in Santa Monica.

* be careful if you have a food allergy*

So we ordered a shrimp taco and crispy cod taco with sweet potato fries/black beans, the sea bass with brussels sprouts and kimchi fried rice that came with a sunny side up egg, calamari, skirt steak with mashed potatoes and asparagus, and black beans on the side.
The shrimp tacos and the skirt steak were the best parts of the meal. They actually had good flavor. The mashed potatoes were creamy and tasty too.

Everything else was pretty disappointing though. The sea bass was dry and stiff with no flavor at all and it was very overcooked. The crispy cod tacos were also flavorless and overcooked. The black beans had no taste and were undercooked. The calamari, brussels sprouts, sweet potato fries, and kimchi fried rice were all just mediocre.

What really bothered me was how they handled my sesame allergy. I told the server at the start that I have a sesame allergy and that it can send me into anaphylactic shock. She said she had let the kitchen know. But the kimchi fried rice still came out with sesame seeds on it. I did not notice until we were already half way eating. When I pointed it out she just shrugged and said it was only a garnish then offered to take it off the bill.

There was no apology. I felt really disappointed and let down.

After that I got very skittish about eating anything else on the table. The food runner brought the food out but our actual server did not come back to check on us for a very long time. I had already told her I could not eat the sunny side up egg and had put it on a side plate. By the time she finally came around most of the food was already eaten so it was too late to ask for a new one. She did not apologize then either.
Even though the skirt steak tasted good the portion was really small so it is not worth going back just for that.

Most of the food was mediocre and the service was not great especially with the allergy situation. For one hundred thirty dollars on lunch it was not worth it. I would give it 3/5.

Been wanting to try pacific catch for a while and it did not disappoint! I got the salmon with green beans and mashed potatoes which were all excellent. It came with charred lemon and a super tasty green sauce. My partner got the chirashi plate which was beautiful and super good. Very solid fish place, we'll definitely be coming back!

Great choice of food for seafood and tacos. Their food is super tasty and the service is good. The grilled fish is a must.  Prices are also moderate and the ambiance is good. Highly recommended for a casual lunch. Fernando is an amazing host. Thank you for your great service.

I've been meaning to write this for a while, but Pacific Catch Santa Monica was amazing! The food, drinks, and service were all great. Our waitress, Leanne (not sure about the spelling), was so kind and made sure our son's meal was adjusted for his allergies, which we really appreciated.

We had the coconut shrimp with Thai chili sweet sauce ,crispy and flavorful. The lobster roll was buttery and delicious. The spicy Sriracha grilled chicken taco had the perfect kick. For our son, we got the kids' teriyaki bowl with salmon, and it was cooked just right.

We also had a Piña Colada and a Mai Tai, both really good!

On top of that, the ambiance was great--relaxed, welcoming, and perfect for a nice meal. It's been a bit since we visited, but the experience was so good that I had to finally write this. Definitely a place we'd go back to!

I went here with my family and we all loved the food! I got the Korean BBQ plate which was amazing, the steak was perfectly cooked and tender while the sides were flavorful and thoughtfully paired with the meat. The fish is great as well, it is all fresh and tastes like it just came off the boat. Overall, I highly recommend Pacific Catch for any occasion.

top_reviews.content:
⭐️ Spacious Ramen Spot with Rich Broth & Fast Service in Van Nuys 🍜

Ramen Izakaya Van Nuys is a very nice and welcoming ramen spot with a spacious layout and plenty of tables, which makes it comfortable even during busier hours.

We ordered the Classic Chicken Ramen and the Spicy Miso Pork, and both were very tasty. The broth was rich, deep, and well balanced, which is always the most important part of a good ramen. Everything arrived hot and fresh, exactly how ramen should be served.

Service was impressively fast we waited less than 5 minutes from the moment we ordered until the food was on the table, which is a big plus. The staff was friendly, welcoming, and happy to explain the menu, creating a relaxed and pleasant dining experience.

The place itself is very spacious, with lots of seating and a comfortable atmosphere. There is pop music playing in the background, which feels a bit unrelated to the Japanese ramen vibe, but it didn’t really take away from the experience.

Overall, this was a very nice and satisfying visit. Good food, rich broth, quick service, and a friendly team. Definitely a solid ramen option in Van Nuys if you’re looking for something tasty and comforting.

🍜🔥

This is a good ramen place with alot of different options. The Spicy Miso had good flavor but the spice level was a 1. I asked for spicy paste to put in my ramen and they brought me more of the same sauce (the Spicy Red Miso) that was the dipping sauce for the bbq pork skewers which was more like a sweet chili sauce. The pork cha-shu in the ramen was very tender, but it didn't have alot of flavor. The egg was a little more done than I prefer but it had good flavor. The bbq sauce on the pork skewers was delicious! top_reviews.content: Pelicana is well known in Korea for their fried chicken and their Los Angeles location is no different.  The restaurant is situated in the Hmart plaza on western and is next to a courtyard offering a nice place to hangout if you want to get your wings and sit outside.  The chicken comes either as whole chicken, wings or boneless and there are different sauces to choose from. We opted for the honey soy.  They were delicious, piping hot and well flavored.  It certainly satisfied my crave for Korean fried chicken.  When comparing to other Korean wings though, I think I prefer Kyochon more, specifically for their batter and extra crispiness.  These were good but the honey sauce soaked through the batter quickly while the ones at Kyochon seemed to have the honey be part of a hardened glaze around the batter.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Pelicana – Crispy Korean Fried Chicken & More! 🍗

I recently visited Pelicana inside Madang Courtyard and had such a great experience! I honestly didn’t visit this place in the first place because when they first opened, the reviews were pretty questionable, but the chicken turned out to be exactly how I like it—super crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. I tried the new Spicy White Crunch (boneless only) and it was perfectly spicy for heat lovers like me! For something milder, I heard that their white crunch is also delicious. Oh and the Honey Soy was a huge hit at our table too.

They also have a variety of fun Korean pub-style side dishes—the White Garlic Fries were delicious, but my personal favorite was the Peli Choco Ball—so unique and addictive!

The vibe is very much like a Korean pub, chill but fun, and the fact that they have 4-hour validated parking made the whole experience even better.

Would I recommend it? Absolutely, especially if you want to enjoy some great K-chicken and drinks without worrying about parking.

Good chicken
Pelicana Chicken in Los Angeles is a popular destination for Korean fried chicken enthusiasts. Known for its crispy, flavorful chicken, the restaurant offers a variety of sauces, from classic soy garlic to a spicier kick, catering to different taste preferences. The chicken is double-fried, resulting in a satisfyingly crunchy exterior while remaining juicy inside. The menu also features sides like pickled radish and fries, which complement the chicken well.

The ambiance is casual, making it a great spot for a laid-back meal with friends or family. Service is generally efficient, though it can get busy, especially during peak hours, leading to longer wait times. Prices are slightly higher than some fast-food chicken joints, but the quality and flavor justify the cost. Overall, Pelicana Chicken offers a delicious and authentic Korean fried chicken experience in Los Angeles, perfect for those craving something crispy and flavorful.

Located inside the MaDang Mall in Los Angeles Koreatown, Pelicana Chicken is by far the best Korean fried chicken. Pelicana Chicken is a well respected Korean chicken brand that has been around since the 1980s. There are many Korean chicken brands in Los Angeles Koreatown, but Pelicana Chicken is the best.

I highly recommend getting the Crispy Chicken half and half with half original and half with the signature sauce (which is sweet and spicy).

Parking is free in the parking garage with validation.
Came in today to try this spot that I would always pass by omw to Somi somi in k town. Chicken was nice hot juicy and fresh. Amazing service as well!

My friend has never had Korean fried chicken before, and I wanted him to try it, so we came to this place. The taste of the fried chicken is great. We absolutely loved it. My friend said it was the best fried chicken he's ever had. I think he's exaggerating, but it's good—very delicious.

Now, you're probably wondering why I'm giving it a 2-star rating. It would have been a 5-star place in my book, but they really messed up in the service category. We ordered on the kiosk, and then we were told that we could not sit inside to eat our chicken because it's for takeout only if we order from the kiosk. We ended up having to find a spot in the courtyard and ate our meal on the concrete floor. It might have been our oversight for not seeing the sign, but it's disheartening and inflexible for a restaurant to refuse to let its customers enjoy their meal inside the restaurant. The place had only one table of customers and had plenty of available tables for us to sit. We even asked if we could sit outside, but they said no. I think they were worried about the tips, which we would have left them some if they let us enjoy our meal there. Later, they saw that I was taking a video, so I think they realized that I'm some sort of reviewer. Shortly after that, one of the staff members came out to the courtyard, gave us some napkins, and apologized. But that was a little too late. We were mostly done at that point. It ruined the experience for my friend's first Korean fried chicken.

The atmosphere was average. Nothing notable to mention, except for the few tables they provided for outdoor seating.

The only downside is that it is definitely overpriced for the portion size, especially compared to some other Korean BBQ places. Still, the quality and flavor were very good, so I can understand why so many people recommend it. If you are craving good gopchang and do not mind paying a bit more, it is worth trying at least once.

We went there to have a real bbq dinner! Yuna and Andy were amazing with us. Very kind and helpful with the recommendation. Both were so sweet with us and told us about when BTS were there to have a dinner. The food is excellent. I highly recommend this restaurant if you are in LA.

The Sizzle of Sophistication: An In-Depth Masterclass in Meat at Ahgassi Gopchang

In a culinary landscape often dominated by the overwhelming "quantity over quality" ethos of buffet-style dining, **Ahgassi Gopchang** emerges as a distinguished oasis for the discerning meat lover. This establishment offers far more than just a meal; it curates an extraordinary dining experience, expertly blending fire, fat, and an explosion of flavors that delight the senses.

**The Strategic Entry**
Entering Ahgassi Gopchang is an event that requires patience, often featuring **two-hour wait times**. We avoided this by making a reservation. Upon entering, we were greeted by a vibrant atmosphere and sophisticated design, where booking ahead is essential for a smooth culinary experience.

**Precision at the Grill**
Ahgassi Gopchang stands out by having skilled servers handle the grill, eliminating the "amateur grill-master" experience. Each cut of meat is expertly grilled to perfection, allowing the savory juices to shine through. This attention to detail creates a memorable dining experience, letting diners focus on their companions and the artistry of the meal.

The Menu: A Study in Marbling and Marinade
Ahgassi Gopchang consciously chooses to move away from the all-you-can-eat model, favoring instead a well-thought-out **a la carte menu** along with carefully curated combo packages. This approach allows the kitchen to dedicate itself to the integrity and quality of each protein that hits the grill. Our tasting journey comprised a thoughtfully selected progression of meats, each offering a unique symphony of textures and flavors:

* **The Marinated Brisket & Bulgogi:** The brisket was cut with surgical thinness, enabling it to sear almost instantly and capture the essence of the grill. The bulgogi served as a delightful counterpart, showcasing a classic blend of sweet and savory flavors that epitomize the essence of elite Korean barbecue.

* **The Marinated Hanger Filet:** This cut stood out for its robust and hearty flavor, often referred to as the "butcher's cut." The marinade was expertly balanced, enhancing the meat's natural flavors without overpowering them, making it a must-try for anyone serious about quality beef.

* **The Short Rib:** Undoubtedly the crown jewel of our meal, the short rib boasted perfect marbling and was handled with exceptional care on the grill. Each bite practically dissolved in your mouth, a testament to both the quality of the meat and the skill of the grill masters.

To complement our meat-centric feast, the supporting dishes were equally impressive. The **steamed egg** arrived at our table like a golden cloud—its texture was light and airy, with a delicate savory flavor that served as a delightful counterpoint to the richness of the meats. Meanwhile, the **tofu soup** contributed a spicy, soul-warming complexity, rounding out our meal and ensuring that each bite was balanced and satisfying.

The Verdict: A Perfect 10/10

From the vibrant, high-energy ambiance to the meticulous precision of the service, Ahgassi Gopchang provided an **unforgettable 10/10 experience**. This is a rare destination where the buzz of the crowd is not just a trend but is genuinely validated by the exceptional quality of food served. For those who appreciate the nuances of a perfect sear and the luxury of professional table-side service, this is undoubtedly the premier destination for Korean barbecue.

*Do yourself a favor: make that reservation, skip the line, and allow the professionals at Ahgassi Gopchang to showcase how Korean barbecue is meant to be savored.*
