top_reviews.content:
Was soooooo fun and so worth it!

The line outside looks crazy long but it moves relatively quickly. We were in in probably less than 20-30 minutes.
Service was also super fast, considering the restaurant was packed to the brim, but even if it took hours to get our food, I wouldn’t have minded because the servers put on such a delightful show. (Btw plan to bring a few bucks in cash because a bucket gets passed around for donations that go directly to funding the music education of these talented servers.)
The servers are crazy talented and also super nice! Every performance we heard was so good that I’d probably have paid just to hear them sing, not to get fed.
On the topic of food, my meal was delicious. I’d heard down the grapevine that the food was mediocre, but that was just plain wrong. The nachos were ENORMOUS and so good, and the pancakes were delicious. The caramel pretzel shake was also great. Huge portions too, so don’t expect to finish it all.

Overall a great experience, and all the more worth it knowing your visit is supporting the dreams of these talented people.

Great food, exciting entertainment by your own servers! I would highly recommend this 50 style restaurant if you’re looking for something unique in a very unique city!

We stopped in for breakfast. Catching the restaurant just a few minutes after it’s opening. There were plenty of seats for our larger group of seven, but our host quickly pointed out that the place can fill up very quickly during the rush-hour, especially over lunch and dinner in between Broadway shows playing nearby.  Everyone stopping by and leaving a post has certainly already mentioned the fact that this place is known for its servers who are trying to make it on Broadway. Enjoying the variety of songs, which can be requested is more than enough reason to check this place out.

I would like to talk about the food…

I thought the food was excellent. My family got a little bit of everything. My daughter’s bagel sandwich, which included a rainbow swirl in the dough of the bagel tasted amazing, they made our eggs to perfection.  The poached eggs that my wife and I enjoyed (Eggs Benedict) were perfectly cooked outer white egg layer surrounding a perfectly runny egg yolk on the inside-just like they should be.

The baked goods like waffles and bagels were very tasty, freshly made, and we enjoyed by those who ordered them.  My family enjoyed the coffee, despite the busy environment, my hat is off to both the servers and the chefs who prepared everything quickly and made it to perfection. Thank you.

I was on my first trip to New York City and my cousin wanted to go to this place. We walked from our hotel as it wasn't too far.

There was a line but it moved along pretty quickly. We didn't wait much longer than 20 to 25 minutes... but we also went on a weekday, earlier in the evening for dinner, which helped with our shorter wait time.

We were seated on the upper level, which was like a diner, counter type seating... which we actually liked better as it gave us a great view of the performances by the staff!

A lot of the staff if not all are Broadway performers working until they get offered gigs on Broadway... which was fun about this place! The entertainment was worth the trip alone... and I would say the food was actually pretty decent...

I got chicken and waffles and besides not being able to finish it all, it tasted great to me. The others in my party liked their meals as well... which was a club sandwich, and chicken tenders... they also got shakes which were very good!

The guy I sat next to was nice too... everyone at the restaurant was just there to have a good time, so I had fun conversations with the people next to me.

The staff and performers were awesome and fun and nice! They also told us they had recently lost 8 servers to Broadway musicals, which is their goal... and it also felt great to support the performers there too and to see them along in their theatrical journeys!

I highly recommend trying this place... my only caution is to pay attention to your bill as they automatically add gratuity to your bill... but unless you read it, most people would just add gratuity not realizing (I think it was 18% or 20%) was already added... so I didn't leave an additional tip on top of that as we also gave the staff their own tip when they brought Phillip the Bucket around, which any money donated to that goes to helping them fulfill their Broadway dreams by getting headshots or other things they need... that money is dispersed to them, strictly for that purpose... so that's my only caution is that you are already tipping on your bill, so pay attention to that!

Otherwise, I don't have any complaints and the staff was great and I wish them the best!

This is a well known and loved diner in the heart of  Times Square.  Serving up 50s diner classics in an energetic atmosphere, it’s a great place for a bite before a show.  Get there early as a line forms outside to get in.  We waited about 15 minutes to get in.

Try to get a seat on the main floor as you will have better view of the singing servers, many of whom are actors and singers! They put on a great show singing show tunes and classics!  Make sure you bring some cash for the tip bucket!

Food is classic diner fare served fast and in good portions!

This is definitely a unique experience, great for families, kids, and anyone!

My friend knew in her heartsoul that I would absolutely love this place, and she was so right. It was an incredible experience, so much talent to enjoy and fun to be had! The food was AMaZINg, fresh n hot coffee, and adorable memorabilia. The rainbow bagel was so beautiful, I almost didn’t eat it. Our waiter, Sean, was on top of everything and I literally cried when he totally nailed Waving Through a Window from Dear Evan Hansen! The staff sang hits from Rent, Wicked, Lady Gaga, Benson Boone, Wicked and more, all while providing exceptional service to a full house. It was utterly fabulous and magical and I will always make a point to go there when I visit NYC. It is a must-go experience and the food is great with lots of options. A Theatre District Gem thespians and fans will no doubt enjoy and love. I got the Salmon and Lox bagel and it was creamy and fresh and perfect. Make sure to tip your waitress/waiter, not just because they deserve it but because they earn it! They pass around a bucket to help with acting/singing classes too so show some support for local artist and stars in the making. 🌟👏Thank you, Ellen’s Stardust Diner, I love you! 💗 I’m seriously tearing up just thinking about how much fun we had. 🥲🥹🤩✨

The servers seem like they really love their job and they are very talented. Music was very entertaining. Although my table got pasta and didn’t like it much ordered chicken and waffles it was the best chicken and waffles I have ever tasted. Very sweet and savory and came with a special hot sauce for the chicken🤤🤤. I recommend coming here for a nice environment and their chicken and waffles!!! Very yummy

Such a fantastic experience. The performers were great and the atmosphere is super fun. The food was overall great. The burger was great and the waffle fries she tater tots were wonderfully cooked. The grilled cheese was mediocre. The bread tasted stale. We had the same issue with our order of the NY shmear. The bagel was stale (as in break your teeth, stale). We were also mistakenly given two of the orders of the NY shmear which we were told by the person who brought the food that we could just keep it. My child had started on the tater tots on that plate. When I asked the server for a to go box, she said that she had to bring it back to the kitchen or we would be charged for it. She did mention that if it is going to be thrown away, she would bring it back to us, but she didn't. So we could only assume it was given to another customer. I'm praying they do not get sick as my child has a cold. Didn't think that was a hygienic choice.

Regardless, the waiters/waitresses were phenomenal. Praying to see all of them on Broadway live one day!

Ellen’s Stardust Diner in the heart of Times Square is an absolutely spectacular, world-class culinary theater that stands as the ultimate destination for dinner and a show, leaving visitors completely in awe of its high-energy atmosphere. The entire retro-themed property is exceptionally nice, wonderfully vibrant, and kept remarkably clean, featuring a dazzling two-story interior packed with vintage memorabilia, glowing neon signs, classic 1950s cars, and a massive model train chugging along overhead tracks.
The iconic singing waitstaff—affectionately known as the "Stardusters"—are an absolute triumph and mind-blowing to experience firsthand. It is incredible how these talented servers balance taking orders and delivering milkshakes with belting out show tunes that genuinely rival Broadway's finest stages. Watching a waiter effortlessly transition from carrying a tray of burgers to hopping up onto a stool or racing down the center aisle with a wireless mic to belt out a jaw-dropping rendition of a musical theater classic is both laugh-out-loud funny and deeply impressive. Their comedic timing, witty banter with the crowd, and sheer vocal power create an electric, joyful environment that keeps the entire room buzzing with excitement.
Equally spectacular is the classic, comforting diner fare that fuels the fun. From thick, perfectly blended milkshakes topped with towering mounds of whipped cream to classic, juicy cheeseburgers and golden fries served on retro checkered paper, the food delivers a wonderful, nostalgic punch. Between the phenomenal comedic performances of future Broadway stars and the lively, upbeat retro charm, eating here stands as an absolute triumph and a beautiful, unforgettable celebration of New York City showmanship.

top_reviews.content: Awesome breakfast spot!! Such a steal for the cheep price. Beautifully fresh, tasty and staff are so lovely and accommodating

We have been coming to the various iterations of Chez Mimi (Chez Helene, Le Petit Chez Mimi) for over 40 years and still love it! Mimi's food is delicious, plentiful, thoughtfully prepared, beautifully displayed, in an adorable setting that makes you feel as if you have gone to someone's home for dinner. Don't miss this little gem!

Mimi is the best! She's an owner who truly cares about her guests. The food is delicious and the ambiance is romantic and cozy. Get the French onion soup - thank me later! This review was made in connection with a Toast promotion.

A tiny but delicious French bistro in a sleepier part of Santa Monica. I’m a huge fan of French cuisine and I’ve pretty much been to all the other options in Los Angeles but for some reason I missed this place. Everyone at our table was really happy that we chose this location because we all had a great meal and great service. Our server was very polite and all of our items that we ordered came out very quickly. The owner was also there and gave a very sweet goodbye when we were leaving. The menu is not very large, but it has all sorts of bistro classics that you would expect and everything that we ordered really had a great taste and a fair price. They also have a large free parking lot attached, which is a huge bonus, especially for Santa Monica. The restaurant size is really tiny but done well and it really feels like the French countryside. It almost feels like you are dining in someone’s house, but with professional service.

Being our first time we wanted try some of the classics on the menu. We both started off with the French Onion Soup and thought it was fantastic. It wasn’t overly salty, there was loads of cheese, and great overall flavor.  For my entree I ordered the Sanddabs Meunière because I love those flavors and sand dabs are a California classic fish. Only found on the West Coast so I order them anytime I get the chance. Everything was very light and buttery and it just had tremendous flavor. I was honestly sad when I finished it. We wanted to order a dessert, but by the end of the meal, we were just too full and decided to save that for next time.

Overall a fantastic bistro and I would recommend to any fan of French cuisine or anyone searching for a great dinner option.

It's hard to give Le Petit Chez Mimi 5-stars when I give Pasjoli 5-stars.  But if you want simple but good French cuisine, in a simple, home-like and charming atmosphere, then this place is for you. Whereas Pasjoli is on busy Main Street in Santa Monica, Le Petit Chez Mimi is located at the storefront of a business park, at the T-intersection of Yale and Colorado.  I pass by all the time either on the way to work, or running errands, but this place always looked closed: Only open for dinners Tues-Sun, and brunch on Sundays.

Therefore I made an effort to finally try this cute little place with my family.  The restaurant, the food and the service is very reminiscent of eating at a local cafe in Paris. You know, you walk around, look  around and finally pick a place for dinner, any place, because so many of the restaurants in Paris are good.  This is how I felt of my first experience at Le Petit Chez Mimi.

Many who dined tonight (Friday night) seemed to be regulars and locals.  The service staff dressed casually (blue jeans) and the service was good.  Whereas Pasjoli, the wait staff are uniformed and professionally trained - what you expect from a Michelin recognized establishment. With Le Petit Chez Mimi, its simply good food, not particularly IG worthy in its presentation.

Surprisingly, the prices were higher than I expected. I guess I was expecting a simpler, quaint French cafe to be more reasonably priced. But I guess this is to be expected for French cuisine.

Now for my food review:
-Escargot. Not bad. I've had better. I felt it needed salt and more of that greenish garlicky sauce (pesto-like.) Please excuse my lack of knowledge of the correct ingredients.
-Onion Soup. Excellent! One of the best French Onion soups in town.  The portion size was perfect. Sometimes, the portions are so big, you dont have room for the remaining courses, but theirs was perfect. Nice gooey cheese!
-Entrées: the 3 of us had 2 different steaks and one pork chop entrée. Again, all were tasty and the steaks were perfectly cooked, but the pork chop was overcooked.  This place isn't Michelin-worthy because of the simple presentation (not much presentation at all.)
-Dessert: The Tarte Tatin was excellent. It was like warm apple pie with fresh cold whip creme. It was perfectly spiced, slightly tart, and not overly sweet. Someone posted on Yelp! that this was an "award winning" dessert. Hmm, it maybe?

Le Petit Chez Mimi offered a warm and accommodating experience for our group dinner. We were a large group, and the owner was genuinely kind and flexible. They arranged individual checks, which was a thoughtful touch, even though I know that’s a lot of work. The atmosphere was charming, and the restaurant handled our group size very well. The food was decent—certainly not the finest French cuisine I’ve ever had, but good enough for a pleasant evening out. The à la carte options allowed everyone to choose to their liking, which made coordinating a large group easier. Overall, it may not be the top spot for the best French gastronomy, but it was a delightful setting for a friendly gathering. Thank you!

I’d give it 3.5 stars.

All of the dishes we tried were fine to good. Nothing was spectacular.

Service was solid.

Pepper steak was probably the best thing we had. The sauce is creamy and tasty.

Pass on the frog legs in the future but glad we tried them.

Wow we are new fans. After spending the summer in Paris we were jonesing for some regular French cooking and Mimi came through with a smooth and refreshing salmon mousse, a lamb stew and a snapper, all specials of the evening. Great wines and folks in a comfy room. Back soon for more. Merci.

First time watching a movie here. Absolutely loved it! I really liked the interior design. Everything was very clean. Seats recline and are comfortable. They come with a wide tray for your food. Not sure if the trays can collapse but if you’re a bigger person you will have to squeeze into your seat 😅Food was good. We ordered popcorn w/butter and a pretzel. The pretzel was so soft! We also got a boozy whiskey banana split shake. Delicious! The server we had was very nice and explained the process of how to order food. Theaters are small, which I prefer. It makes the experience more cozy and personal. Bathrooms are clean and unisex. So don’t be surprised about that. My only con was getting there. There is parking. Just remember to VALIDATE it. It’s $6 validated but $40 plus with no validation. We had to take multiple elevators to get there. And got a little lost trying to get back to our car. Anyways, their website gives you very detailed information about everything. So read it before you go. This will be my theater of choice for future movie outings.

I am extremely disappointed by how a staff member treated me during the 9:00 PM screening of Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey in Auditorium 8. I was seated in seat 511.

I live near the theater and decided to walk there instead of driving. Despite it already being 9:00 PM, it was extremely hot outside—almost like daytime heat. By the time I arrived, I was feeling unwell and my feet had become painfully swollen from walking in the heat.

The theater itself was cool, and the air conditioning was blowing directly toward me. However, swollen and painful feet do not instantly return to normal simply because someone enters an air-conditioned room. At the beginning of the movie, I briefly removed my shoes, hoping that the cool air would help me feel better. I kept my shoes directly under my seat, without blocking the aisle or disturbing anyone.

Another customer near me was also sitting without shoes, yet I appeared to be the only person repeatedly confronted.

When the employee instructed me to put my shoes back on, I complied despite the pain. That should have ended the interaction. Instead, she returned to me multiple times and repeatedly warned that if I removed them again, she would have me removed from the auditorium and stop the movie in front of everyone.

I told her that I understood and clearly indicated that I wanted to end the conversation and continue watching the film, but she would not leave me alone. Immediately after threatening to remove me, she returned once again and asked whether I wanted water. By that point, the interaction felt less like genuine assistance and more like continued provocation.

When I responded, “No, I don’t want water. I want to watch the movie because I paid for it,” she accused me of having an “attitude,” said I was speaking too loudly, and again threatened to remove me.

Approximately fifteen minutes of the film were taken away by these repeated and completely unnecessary interactions. My wife and I purchased two $25 tickets, as well as food and drinks, because we came here to relax and enjoy a movie. Instead, I became so distressed that I had to leave the auditorium and ended up standing outside crying rather than watching the film I had paid for.

I understand that a theater may have a footwear policy. My complaint is about the employee’s hostile, humiliating, and unnecessarily escalatory behavior—particularly after I had already complied. A professional employee could have communicated the rule once, calmly and respectfully. There was absolutely no need to keep returning, threatening me, commenting on my “attitude,” and disrupting my experience.

Customer-facing employees should know how to de-escalate situations, not manufacture conflicts and repeatedly intimidate paying guests. I sincerely hope management identifies this employee, reviews the available surveillance footage, and takes serious disciplinary action, including considering whether she should remain in a customer-facing position. In my opinion, someone who treats customers this way should not be working with the public.

I am requesting a full refund for both tickets and a formal response from management regarding this incident.

Went there on a Thursday and it was pretty chill and spacious. Their recliner seats are very comfortable.

My experience at Park and Quinn in New York was outstanding from the moment we walked through the door. Right away, the restaurant gave off a warm, stylish, and welcoming atmosphere that made us feel comfortable and excited for the meal ahead. The space had a great New York energy to it — lively but not overwhelming — and it felt like the perfect setting for a relaxed but elevated dining experience. We were greeted warmly upon arrival, and the service throughout the evening was attentive, friendly, and professional, which made the entire visit feel even more enjoyable.

The dressing was rich and well-balanced, coating the salad beautifully without being too heavy. It was a refreshing and flavorful start that felt both light and satisfying.

top_reviews.content: To beat the heat with something truly delicious- OAKOBING is tyhe best. Their shaved ice desserts are wonderfully light, airy, and incredibly refreshing, offering a great balance of authentic flavors that aren't overly sweet. With an impressive variety of fruit-topped and classic Korean bingsu options, it is easily one of the best spots around for a crisp, thirst-quenching treat.

More Instagram Than Flavor
The shaved ice is definitely photogenic, but the taste is just okay.

We ordered two small bingsoo, the mango and the matcha strawberry. The mango and strawberry on top were both mouth-puckeringly sour, and the shaved ice itself had an artificial, flavored-syrup taste to it. The space also felt a little dirty.

Cute for the photos, but I wouldn't go out of my way to come back.

I’ve been coming here around ten years and didn’t go for a little bit and suddenly had a craving for it. The last time I came was a few years ago and I’m pleasantly surprised to see that the quality has remained consistent, fruit is sweet, portions are still massive and shareable, and prices are still reasonable. $15.99 for a fruit stacked shaved ice that is easily shareable between 4 people is such a steal. The shaved ice is so soft and not too sweet. Glad I stopped back in again, such a nostalgic spot for me!

I ordered an Injeolmi bingsu & mango yesterday. The rice cake had green tea powder on it. I never ordered anything with green tea.

At first, I suspected the food might have been reused, but since I can’t verify that, I tried calling the store. No one answered.

I don’t need any explanation. I simply won’t be ordering again. It wasn’t good anyway.

Wishing your business continued success.

After countless trips to Los Angeles' Koreatown, I finally made it to Oakobing. Every previous visit ended the same way—I saw the long line, sighed, and walked away. This time, the wait was surprisingly short, and I finally got to see what all the buzz was about.

The first thing that struck me wasn't the desserts, but the crowd. Even in the heart of K-Town, the café was filled with people from every background enjoying Korean-style bingsoo. Seeing a traditional Korean dessert embraced by so many different cultures was both surprising and something I couldn't help but feel proud of.

I'm a fan of classic patbingsu with sweet red beans, but my son prefers fruit flavors. Like many Gen Z dessert lovers, he isn't a fan of red beans and always reaches for fresh fruit instead.
Although I wanted to sample several items, we had just finished dinner, so we settled on the Melon Bingsoo Combo and the Strawberry Bingsoo.
The Melon Bingsoo is as impressive as it is delicious. Served inside a real hollowed-out melon and topped with incredibly soft, fluffy milk snow, it's refreshing without being overly sweet. Each bite delivers the natural sweetness of fresh melon and melts effortlessly in your mouth. Even better, the combo includes an Injeolmi Latte, making it an excellent value.

The Strawberry Bingsoo was just as enjoyable. Packed with fresh strawberries and light, snowy shaved ice, it was bright pinky, refreshing, and disappeared from the table in minutes.
The only downside is the limited seating. For a café this popular, finding a table during busy hours can still be a challenge. But once the desserts arrive, you'll quickly forget about the wait.

If you're looking for a break from the usual ice cream shops, Oakobing is a refreshing alternative. Beautifully presented, generously portioned, and perfectly balanced, it's easy to understand why people keep lining up. Some desserts satisfy your sweet tooth—Oakobing leaves you planning your next visit before you've even finished the last bite.
Popular shaved ice spot in Ktown. It's tricky even trying to get a seat here. Nice flavors and I specifically like that they serve small individual sizes here.

I love this place so much, bingsu is literally the best, options avaliable are amazing and delicious. Really enjoyed the mango melon it was so refreshing. Only thing is, seating is limited so you'll have to wait for a table to open up.

One was making the shaved ice, and one was in the back and in the table area cleaning up, restocking, etc.

One suggestion to the owner: hire more workers so one worker is not slammed with 50 orders all at once. I felt bad for the kid.

The Best Kimchi!

I think this place is known for their bossam dish, but I actually haven’t tried it yet. What keeps me coming back is their fresh napa kimchi — it’s crisp, refreshing, and incredibly flavorful.

The dolsot bibimbap is good too, though I wish the rice at the bottom was crispier to give it that deeper toasted texture and contrast.

I’d say stay away from the mandoo guk, though. It’s not seasoned properly at all. The broth is overly salty, the meat is overcooked to the point where most of the flavor is gone, and the dumplings don’t taste fresh — they seem frozen. The dumpling filling is actually overseasoned, which clashes even more with the salty broth. The whole dish falls apart because the flavors don’t complement each other. It feels like there wasn’t much thought put into balancing the broth with the dumplings and glass noodles.

The bossam was absolutely outstanding. The pork was perfectly tender, sliced just right, and had a rich, savory flavor without being overly heavy. Each bite practically melted in my mouth. Paired with the fresh napa cabbage wraps, crisp radish slices, and a variety of thoughtfully prepared banchan, every combination felt balanced and satisfying. The kimchi served alongside had just the right level of tang—bright, slightly spicy, and incredibly fresh. The staff were warm, attentive, and happy to guide us on how to build the perfect bite. The complex can be quite busy but valet parking is available as well as public parking around the corner on Vermont.

This was a nice experience for me. From where I'm from, we rarely have any good Korean restaurants. The interior was beautiful and I was seated pretty quickly. My waiter asked me immediately if I had any questions, which was nice! This place screamed authentic, and with a good bit of history, opening in the 80's. They did have valet parking.

I was happy to see the prices were pretty fair. I decided to get Dolsot Bibimbap & Bindae Tteok (mung bean pancakes), the banchan that came with it was excellent and very fresh. The kimchi was very nice as well! The egg wasn't overcooked when the bibimbap came out. The veggies were fresh, and may have been the best bibimbap that I've ever had. The mung bean pancakes came out, and they were pretty huge! They were pretty good - and it was my first time having them, so I don't really have much to compare them to, cooked very well and golden brown. The purple rice was pretty nice, also my first time having purple rice! Overall, it was a really nice experience for me.

Saw good reviews on their seafood pancake so I came to try that out and ordered some bossam as well. The bossam was delicious, very good quality pork belly with delicious sides. I ordered ssammjrng and garlic to give it some more punch. The seafood pancake was good, well balanced with its’ ingredients. I just wish it was thinner and crispier, but maybe next time if I can request it to be cooked well-done and crispy, that’d be perfect! Will be back to try more!

What more can I say? This K-town staple consistently delivers when you're craving Korean cuisine. We started our meal with a generous portion of Haemool Pajeon (Seafood Pancake), which arrived sizzling on a hot plate reminiscent of a Chili's Fajita Plate. Next came the main attraction: the Bossam Plate, featuring simmered and cooled pork belly sliced to perfection. When you wrap all the other ingredients together, they create the perfect bite. Just after the Bossam Plate hits the table, a bubbling cauldron of Kimchi JJigae (Kimchi Stew) follows behind just in time to help wash down the delectable bites of bossam. Don't forget to order some rice because you'll need something to soak up the stew which turns the rice into a whole meal by itself.

The service was jovial and welcoming, and like other Korean establishments, they have a handy-dandy button that jolts the attention of every server working whenever you're in need of service. The small space is very cozy, just the way I like it when I'm visiting with my loved ones. They don't have an extensive menu, just the OG staple items, but I feel the taste has improved over the years. I wish Kobawoo were closer to where I live, or I would be here this weekend, but perhaps it's a good thing we're so far apart.

top_reviews.content:
If you know, you know. 🙌

We found Corner Grille years ago, and it has been amazing every single time. It’s such a unique Korean-Mexican fusion spot — flavors you truly won’t find anywhere else. The combination sounds unexpected, but somehow it works perfectly.

We’ve tried a few different items over the years, but the Chicken Korean Fries are our absolute favorite every time. Nothing like it exists. The flavors are bold, layered, slightly sweet, savory, and just combined so deliciously. It’s one of those dishes you crave again and again.

It’s definitely a hole-in-the-wall spot in a small shopping center — super unassuming — but don’t let that fool you. It’s 100% a must-try. Some of the best, most unique food is always hiding in places like this.

If you’re looking for something different and seriously delicious, put this on your list. We’ll keep coming back.

I had such a fantastic time stopping by this spot on Sepulveda. Everything was served fresh and hit the spot perfectly.

The loaded fries were a highlight for me. They were topped with generous slices of fresh jalapeño and a delicious creamy sauce that tied it all together. Every bite was packed with flavor.

If you are looking for a satisfying meal, this is the place to go. I cannot wait to come back and try more of their menu soon.

I have been eating here at least twice a week for the past four years, and the food is consistently excellent. The fried chicken sandwich is hands down the best I’ve ever had! Everything is always fresh and delicious. Every time I decide to try a different dish on the menu, I am positively surprised by the incredible flavor and top-notch quality. On top of all that, the prices are very affordable. Highly recommended!

The term Diamond in the rough fits this place like a glove! Food was excellent. I had the teriyaki burger which was not your standard beef patty with teriyaki sauce it was thinly sliced beef like what you'd get in a teriyaki bowl... EXCELLENT FOOD! *BONUS* here's a fun fact this place has a ramen bowl challenge where if you can finish the whole bowl of ramen in 1 minute you get a $30 meal voucher for the restaurant. While I was there someone attempted the challenge and failed... No one has claimed victory of this challenge yet... Will 🫵🏼 be the first ☝🏼?

Was quite surprised by Corner Grille. The location is kind of sketchy and from the outside it doesn't seem like much. However once I ordered I discovered this may be one of my new favorite spots in the valley.

It can take a minute to get your food but the wait is definitely worth it. I've been here several times and have never been disappointed. Pretty sure I've tried half the menu at this point. There's only a few people on staff but all the food comes out piping hot and fresh as soon as it's ready.

Their chicken strips are phenomenal. Very crispy and good flavor.
The Loaded fries are also a MUST have with the beef on top. Just utterly delicious. This is a meal in itself.
I've also tried the wings, Tacos, Kalbi Beef Burger, Chicken Teriyaki, and Xango. All of them where just outstanding.

The staff has always been very nice and helpful as well. I highly recommend.

OP:
My family and I had reservations for my birthday dinner here as we enjoy dining at Daedo for special occasions. My family had a great birthday dinner here a few months ago for another family member so we expected the same quality of service but we were disappointed with our waiter, River, and his unwelcoming attitude, especially with elder Korean members of this community seated at our table. I don’t normally write negative reviews and I understand not everyone has a good day at work, but for a restaurant of this caliber of fine dining, this type of interaction was unacceptable and very disappointing. I’ve only taken down 2 stars because our second waiter (sorry I didn’t catch his name) made up for his coworker’s lack of tact with his own exemplary service. I was impressed with cleanliness, no odor, modern setup and great service. Highest quality beef is served cooked in front of you by the server. Lean beef that tastes proves it. The Bulgogi is lean and delicious. The fried rice and the side dishes were all the best quality. When we arrived, the table was setup with all the side dishes, water and very impressive choices of sauces house made. We ordered the Seoul Nights Soju which was outstanding. They also have Suntory beer that tastes incredible. If you love beef and you do not like a big piece of meat in front of you that disgusts some people, then this is your place. The small cubes of different kinds of best quality beef cooked in perfection can be dipped in your favorite sauce accompanied by great side dishes. Parking is very convenient with valet service.

Prime Angus Perfection & Bold Korean Flavors — Daedo Sikdang Brings Seoul’s Finest Steak to LA 🔥

From the moment the sizzling ribeye hits your table, you know you’re in for something extraordinary. With a rich heritage from Seoul since 1964, this upscale Korean steakhouse has perfected the art of showcasing Certified Angus Beef® Prime cuts — delivering flavor, tenderness, and quality that’s second to none.

We indulged in the Daedo Cut (8oz) — ribeye roll, ribeye cap, and ribeye strip — each one offering its own bold personality. The ribeye roll was luxuriously tender and buttery, the ribeye cap delivered an explosion of rich, beefy intensity, and the ribeye strip had that deep, satisfying flavor steak lovers live for.

The sides elevated the experience — the kimchi fried rice was savory and addictive, while the cold noodles provided a refreshing contrast to the richness of the meat. Add to that a sleek bar stocked with luxury wines and a private karaoke room for an exclusive twist, and you have a dining experience that’s as refined as it is unforgettable.

From the immaculate interiors to the unmatched quality of its Prime Angus cuts, Daedo Sikdang delivers the bold flavors and elevated atmosphere that keep you coming back.

The place is well-kept, and clean. We went in a bit early than the dinner rush hour, so there was no wait. After we ordered, the waiter cooked our meal for us at the table. It was bit pricey, but everything was top quality and very delicious. Definitely would visit again.

The food was delicious, and the staff were very friendly. In particular, the young male cashier was extremely nice and welcoming. The interior is clean and stylish, creating a great atmosphere. I highly recommend this place if you’re looking for a good Korean BBQ spot.

top_reviews.content: Taylor's is a great steakhouse that doesn't break the bank. My favorite is their Spencer Steak which is a boneless ribeye. It's always seasoned well and cooked to my liking. It pairs really well with the peppercorn sauce. For desserts they have a tray they bring around for your choosing. Some options tend to rotate, but my favorites are their bread pudding and chocolate cake. Can never go wrong with those.

Taylor’s Steak House had been on my Los Angeles steakhouse bucket list for a while, and I’m glad I finally made it. The moment I walked through the door, I knew I had found exactly the classic old-school steakhouse atmosphere I was looking for. No gimmicks, no trendy concepts—just a traditional steakhouse focused on good food, strong drinks, and a relaxed dining experience.

We ordered the New York Strip, the 20 oz Ribeye, and a Caesar Salad. The steaks were the highlight of the meal: quality cuts, cooked well, full of flavor, and served in generous portions. The Ribeye in particular was rich, juicy, and satisfying. Service was attentive and friendly without being overbearing, which fit perfectly with the laid-back vibe of the restaurant.

The Caesar Salad was decent, although the lettuce could have been fresher. It wasn’t a deal breaker, but it was the one part of the meal that didn’t quite match the quality of the steaks.

Another pleasant surprise was the pricing. For the quality, portion sizes, and overall experience, Taylor’s offers excellent value compared to many steakhouses in Los Angeles.

Overall, this was a great experience and the first item officially checked off my LA steakhouse bucket list. If you’re looking for a classic, no-nonsense steakhouse with quality meat, reasonable prices, and a genuinely comfortable atmosphere, Taylor’s is easy to recommend. I’ll definitely be back to work my way through more of the menu.

I originally came here just for a smoothie and coffee, but I didn’t try the food at first. Later, I met one of the employees, and he told me that I really needed to try something from their menu. So when I came back the second time, even though I didn’t have much time, I decided to order a sandwich.

Honestly, it was very good. I always write only honest reviews, and I never leave reviews for money because my Google account and reputation are important to me. The coffee was excellent, with nicely roasted beans. The sandwich was perfectly toasted, fresh, and tasty. The bread was fresh, the turkey was very good, and their special chef’s sauce made it even better. The greens were fresh and nicely dressed — I’m not exactly sure what they used, but it tasted great.

They also have a big menu, and I definitely want to come back and try more. One more thing I really appreciated: I came almost at closing time and needed to use the restroom. It was for employees only, but after I kindly asked, they helped me and allowed me to use it. When I passed by the kitchen, I noticed how clean everything was, and that made me trust the place even more.

Overall, great food, great coffee, clean kitchen, and kind staff. I will definitely stop by from time to time.

The food is delicious, the people are kind and sweet. Yesterday was my first day here and I had the spicy chicken sandwich which was phenomenal. Came back today for the breakfast burrito with organic chicken sausage added inside, I didn’t know I could like chicken sausage so much 😅 the food is delicious, but it’s not the filling yourself up for the sake of it kind of delicious. It’s the kind of where your body actually feels like what you eat is good for you. I almost never entered this area because the parking area looked intimidating, but I realize that it does flare up, but it stays relatively open after those bad moments.

There was a gentleman helping me yesterday. I don’t know if he was the owner, but he was also very kind, today there was a Sweet cashier I think by the name of Ately but I’ve probably got that name wrong. 😅 they are both very welcoming, it’s refreshing to enter an establishment and almost feel as though they’re happy to see you. Not get the sensation that the people are just clocking in and they want you to leave immediately after your purchase. The food does take a few minutes to prepare, and evidently they bake all of their goods,

The music is a little old school, but I like it. There isn’t a lot of seats not exactly the best place possibly for a big group, but unlike other establishment that is revolving, people are coming and going consistently. That’s usually a good sign. They don’t stay open past 5 PM so they don’t really have a dinner menu but it seems like it’s more of a breakfast to lunch kind of thing.

It’s impossible for me to sit here and tell you how good the food tastes in my mouth so I’m not even gonna bother. I will tell you that it’s absolutely worth trying at least once. That the smoothie is appeared to be almost exclusively, fresh fruit, coffee is not bad at all. And conveniently they give you your coffee in it to go cup so you could just dip whenever you want.

I see myself coming here very often now. I’ve been pretty bored with a lot of the food selection in my area. I’ve been honestly looking for a place like this and I’m happy I found one.

They have desserts and pastries,  but honestly aside from the delicious food, the thing that’s most significant to me and my favorite part is this. At least, with the current staff, it’s warm and welcoming. Sitting down to eat in this restaurant doesn’t feel like any other fast food joint or the fake pleasant trees of overwork waiters in other places. It’s a nice and comfortable atmosphere. As a guy who lives alone and spent most of his time either working or alone. It’s hard to ignore how cozy the feel is at this place. I hope that stays the same.

Highly recommend, and I would like to be more of a regular there personally…

I’m the person who usually walks into businesses hired to restore them. It’s rare these days I write a review. This is written not just due to a quick impression by one visit, or how invested I am as a consumer based on one meal or one employee who was friendly - this is a 360 perspective on a business doing it right.

When I pause to look and recognize somewhere who “gets it” organically, it means something. This is long but, they’ve earned it.

Context - I just moved back to Los Angeles from Seattle. I’ve never lived North of the 101, I have no local haunts up here, and I’m still getting settled. Finding a new role, not yet in a groove and all I knew was that I missed good food. One morning I searched for an almond croissant and landed on Victory Cafe.

I typed a note on my delivery receipt warning them in jest and CA humor I’d be ordering batches of five croissants at a time because I was in love with their menu. And I meant it. I’m a creature of habit - Salads for dinner, sandwiches, quesadillas, kids’ scrambles with fruit and sides of bacon — all with four to six croissants added every time.

By week two, order three or four, my phone rings after I place an order. It’s the owner, Efren, talking to me like I’ve been a client for years. He tells me I’m a VIP to him and his team. They know my orders. That day they were out of my almond croissants, and he asked if I’d mind if he stayed late, made a batch himself, and personally dropped them off on his way home at 7 pm. He threw in some other pastries and muffins to try - c’mon - has that ever happened to you?!

He’s not the pastry chef. This was a homemade croissant — not a waffle. He didn’t even ask how far away I was. And he did exactly what he said he would. He told me he remembered my receipt note about just moving back to LA, and he wanted to make sure I was taken care of by his team.

I just placed another order and my phone rang again. I braced for a substitution call — fair enough, it’s 4 p.m. and I ordered eight pastries. But it was Efren, just saying hi. Checking on me. “We have everything for you today, but I wanted to say hello and see how you were.”

The food is outstanding. I get enough to last me two to three days for under $50 and it’s better than anything else I’ve found. It’s fresh, healthy and it’s home cooked meals. They cater to vegans if that’s your preference. But where else are you treated like this without even walking in — just ordering through Grubhub? Imagine when I dine in! I’m treated like family and I am confident I’ve moved to the right place if I’ve landed near a restaurant with people who are this wonderful.

I’ll be loyal to Victory Cafe for life. And I’ll drive to them no matter where I end up getting an apartment down the line. It’s a simple but rare thing: quality, consistency, genuine kindness, and a customer relationship that’s actually substantive. I’d trust Efren with more than an order, and his team reflects training that is preparing them for careers and life long values — at his organization and beyond. Keep an eye on Victory Cafe. It takes more than an owner to create this kind of magic. Well done, team.

Stopped at Victory Caffe on our drive back to SF from LA after seeing the great reviews, and it definitely lived up to them. It’s a small family-run spot with a really welcoming atmosphere.

The owner, Efrien (hope I got the name right), was incredibly kind and patient. While we were there, another customer was upset about a delayed online order, but he handled the situation calmly and respectfully the whole time. That alone left a great impression on us.

We ordered the spicy chicken sandwich, an egg sandwich, and cappuccinos. Everything was fresh, flavorful, and reasonably priced for the portion sizes. The coffee was especially good.

They also offer many vegetarian and healthy options. Definitely worth a stop if you’re passing through the area!

Loved my visit here! The person was very kind to my mother and i. The caramel latte had the perfect balance of sweetness and rich espresso, and the Nutella croissant was warm, flaky, and packed with flavor. Will definitely be coming back sometime!

Delicious! 💯 ❤️ I got the Spicy Chicken Sandwich today for lunch (the most popular) and a coffee (Americano, organic coffee 🥰 ☕️ ) Great food, nice menu, super friendly staff, cute place and super clean. I recommend it definitely and plan to come back! 😉

This is one of my favorite spots in the valley. I religiously get the vegan breakfast burrito but everything is really good. The avocado toast (which sounds hard to mess up) is the best avocado toast I've ever had.

My friends always get the spicy chicken sandwich here, and it's never failed anyone I bring. My good friend also swears by the Salmon toast and orders extra salmon. I also often get the green juice, and the vegan waffle, but have never had a bad item yet.

I get it for delivery but they have a good sitting area when visiting for walk up.

Definitely worth a visit.

Don’t miss this place. Food was exceptional, high quality ingredients.  Fresh roasted organic coffee which made my vanilla latte amazing!  Service was incredible, very friendly and attentive.  The only downside to this experience is that I sat next to part of the door chime that loudly announces front door each time someone enters.   Definitely will come back.

Very busy, but also very quick service. Staff was friendly, quick, and attentive in our last few visits. They also have validated parking as well and they do have a nearby sister location nearby, about an 8min walk.
The food was great and the portions are great too. That 54.99 as of April 2026 for the all day pricing is steep at first glance, but anything on the menu is fair game, food-wise, appetizers and entrees included. So if you like either basic sushi rolls, nigiri, appetizers such as: takoyaki, gyozas, miso soup and etc., entrees like chicken katsu, and the extravagant rolls such as: baked rolls, tempura rolls, and fresh rolls, this is all included in that 54.99 all you can eat, AYCE, price. Not sure how that 19.99 sashimi add on works as of yet. But this place is a great value if you were planning on getting more than 1 roll and more than 1 appetizer per person. If you were planning on eating less than that then you can buy each entree, appetizer and side individually a la carte.
They do have a cheaper menu option available every day they are open for lunch as long as its not the weekend (Friday - Sunday the All Day Pricing is the only option available for AYCE)
Word of warning if you do get the AYCE option and your friend/partner decides to do a la carte, the person that has the AYCE option cannot share their food which is very fair. The rice - fish/roll ratio is perfect. They have lots of premium fish such as toro, hirame, harasu, and many more. All super tasty and has the rich feel while savoring.

We also had a extra round of fish with different styles, seared, garlic, and regular. All super tasty but the seared ones soaked in mayo are definitely a stand out.

My standout dish is definitely the "screaming orgasm" and the orange salmon. Both dishes are just perfect as they melt with the seasoning and sauce.

All the sushi rolls were perfect, you can do half (4pcs) or get a full plate (8pcs). All the usual types of rolls you see elsewhere are also here so we gave them a try and they were perfect, if not way better than other restaurants.

Portions are perfect, bite size, and extremely flavorful. Plus points for complementary ice cream to finish the meal.

Here Fishy Fishy is a very well rounded sushi spot and it's great that it's nearby and easily accessible. Great staff as they're very professional, quality sushi, and very generous. By far my favorite AYCE sushi spot

Surprisingly tasty Japanese spot on Mid Wilshire hidden behind tinted glass. The menu featured a wide array of creative dishes and the fish tasted very fresh. Went for lunch and would recommend for an affordable but very good Japanese spot.

Very good all you can eat sushi.

All sushi’s and dishes were amazing. Probably the best nigiri sushi I’ve ever had in United States so far in an AYCE restaurant.

The pricing is very easy to understand, the menu is very visual, and the service is very good.

Make sure you find the address for the parking if you are driving, although the parking is in the same building, it’s hard to find the entrance.

From the moment you enter Michael’s in midtown, you feel something different. You realize why certain places are deserving of the title “institution”. This decades-long power dining restaurant is a class above the rest.

From the cozy decor to the amazing art collection, to the attentive and courteous staff led by dining legend Steve at the helm as manager to the decadent expertly prepared cuisine, this place is deserving of every single accolade.

The dongchimi noodles are a "must try" here. I ordered them with the bulgogi, thinking, "How good could radish noodles really be?" But they turned out to be the perfect match. The two combination was incredibly delicious.

A True K-Town Classic That Has Stood the Test of Time.
I’ve been a regular here for decades. This is the place to go for authentic, generous portions of Korean BBQ at an honest price.
In a time when so many classic restaurants are disappearing one by one, I am truly grateful that this place has kept its consistent taste and quality for so many years.
The Dongchimi Guksu (Cold Radish Water Kimchi Noodles) is an absolute must-try to finish your meal.
It’s rare to find a place like this anymore. I sincerely hope they stay in business for a long, long time. Thank you for keeping the tradition alive!

The Korean bbq here is ok, the two sets for 2 with 3 meat choices are decent and the portions are generous enough to make even 3 ppl full. The beef tongue, house special, ribeye and chilmok special gui (boneless plate short rib) was the better meats. The Korean cold noodle was very good. A tad bit pricey imo. It felt a bit of a nickel and dime type place given they charge you for extra rice and even lettuce. The restaurant has a lot of air vents but it gets pretty smokey so they open their entrance door which I feel is a bad idea since flies and bugs can get in.

I recently went back after quite some time and ordered the grilled sirloin along with the dongchimi cold noodles. The atmosphere remained warm and inviting, making it a comfortable place to enjoy a good meal. The servers were impressively fast and attentive—almost a little too quick at times—but it showed how well-organized and efficient the service was. Compared to many other restaurants these days, the overall value and experience here were definitely above average, and I left feeling very satisfied.

Santa Monica Pier is one of those iconic places that truly captures the spirit of California. The combination of the historic pier, Pacific Park, the beach, street performers, and the endless Pacific Ocean creates an atmosphere that’s full of energy, fun, and unforgettable memories.

Walking along the pier at sunset was a highlight of our trip. The ocean views are spectacular, the cool sea breeze is refreshing, and there’s something exciting around every corner. From the Ferris wheel and amusement rides to the local food and live entertainment, there’s something for everyone to enjoy.

One thing to keep in mind is that parking can be quite difficult to find, especially around midday and on weekends, and the area gets very crowded. Arriving early in the morning or later in the evening will make your visit much more enjoyable.

Despite the crowds, Santa Monica Pier is absolutely worth visiting. It’s more than just a pier—it’s the heart of Santa Monica and one of the most memorable experiences on the California coast.

Santa Monica Pier was one of the coolest stops on my trip! The views of the Pacific Ocean are amazing, but the Pacific Wheel Ferris wheel is definitely the main attraction. Riding it gives you an awesome view of the coastline from over 130 feet up, and the lights on the wheel at night make it even better.

As a huge Dead Island 2 fan, walking around the pier was extra fun because so many familiar spots from the game’s The Pier area are based on this real-life location. You’ll recognize the Ferris wheel, Funland Arcade, Pier Grill, Lifeguard HQ, and more.

Seeing the Ferris wheel in person after fighting zombies around it in Dead Island 2 felt pretty surreal. The game’s “Boardwalking Dead” mission even takes you through the pier toward the Ferris wheel.

With the ocean views, amusement park vibe, shops, food, and all the Dead Island 2 references, Santa Monica Pier is a really fun place to check out. Definitely worth a visit, especially if you’re a gamer and a fan of the Dead Island series!

Beautiful and lively beach right next to the iconic Santa Monica Pier. Pacific Park adds a fun amusement‑park vibe with the Ferris wheel, roller coaster, and classic boardwalk games. Great mix of ocean views, entertainment, and photo spots. Easy access, plenty of food options, and a perfect place to enjoy the beach and the classic LA pier atmosphere. A must‑see location for all GTA fans — this is the real‑life inspiration for Del Perro Pier in GTA V.

There’s just something about the open ocean that feels so therapeutic. Also there’s plenty of parking nearby and the parking prices aren’t terrible. If you decide to buy some souvenirs, wait till you get to the store further into the pier, their prices seem to be way cheaper than the ones closer to the entrance.

Iconic LA spot, definitely worth a quick stop. Fun to walk around and see the rides and attractions right on the pier. It brings tears to my eyes as I write this review on the eve of my move out of LA. I’ve probably eaten here over 50 times in the last 10 years and can confidently say this is a top 3 favorite restaurant in SoCal for me. Surawon is not your fancy “pinkies up” type of place. It is the home to the most delicious, authentic and welcoming Korean food that only a Korean mom and grandma with decades of excellence, love, and care can produce.

The star is the thick-cut Galbi - smoky, sweet, savory, and incredibly juicy from what can only be premium, highly marbled beef. The other star is the large offering of banchan - each executed perfectly and with a different flavor profile that can balance any meal. Of course the brand is centered on the soondubu, which blends a rich and flavorful broth with generous portion of fresh tofu.

The service is truly 5/5. It doesn’t matter if the restaurant is full or empty, the ajummas will always serve you with a smile and make sure your banchans are replenished.

After so many meals here, I can go on for a very long time about the great memories I’ve had at Surawon. But I’ll stop and let whoever is reading this make their own and hope that when I come back in a few years, this wonderful place is still around, unchanged.

The service was great, and the food was even better. From the outside, it's not easily noticeable that it's a restaurant. But once inside, the staff are terse but very welcoming. The tables and chairs don't have much flair. It felt like a cafeteria. Every table is close to each other, so it's an intimate dining experience. If you can get past that, the food makes you forget about the sterile like environment. Your taste buds just transport you to another place, a place where bellies are fulfilled and smiles on faces are everywhere.

Hanta completely exceeded our expectations. From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere felt warm, modern, and inviting, and the service was genuinely friendly and attentive throughout the meal.

The standout dishes for us were the cold noodles and galbi. The cold noodles were incredibly refreshing, with the perfect chewy texture and a flavorful broth that was light, tangy, and satisfying. They paired beautifully with the galbi, which was tender, juicy, and packed with rich, smoky flavor. The meat was expertly cooked and practically melted in your mouth.

Every dish we ordered showcased fresh ingredients and thoughtful preparation. The portions were generous, the presentation was beautiful, and every bite felt like it was made with care.

What made the experience even better was the hospitality. The staff was welcoming, knowledgeable, and attentive without ever making us feel rushed.

Hanta is the kind of place that makes you start planning your next visit before you’ve finished your meal. If you go, don’t miss the cold noodles and galbi—they’re a perfect combination and truly memorable.

What a nice find. The room is brand new and spotless, and there's a warmth to the place that you can't build into a space — that comes from the people running it. Everyone was so kind, and even though it's a no-tip, self-serve setup, it never once felt like less service. If anything the food gets to you faster. The station up front has vinegar, mustard, water and a hot broth dispenser with brass cups, which is a lovely touch. The yukgaejang was excellent — deep, properly built broth, generous with the beef, served genuinely hot. Five banchan with purple rice, all of it fresh. And the prices are so reasonable for this quality that it almost doesn't add up. I'll be coming back often.

Remember tipping is not required here but appreciated at your convenience.

You got to try the galbijim, it was worth $80 and enough amount for 2 to 3 people. Also, they have free hot broth for you. Really nice staffs too.

I had the cold noodles and the galbi combo, and it was absolutely delicious! The naengmyeon was refreshing, flavorful, and had a great chewy texture. The galbi was tender, juicy, and paired perfectly with the noodles. Everything tasted fresh, and the portion was satisfying. The service was friendly, and the restaurant was clean and welcoming. I’ll definitely be coming back to Hanta Naengmyeon. Highly recommend if you’re looking for authentic Korean cold noodles and great galbi!

The food was alright, but the game tablet fell off the table and landed on my friends foot. We asked if they would return it, and they stated that they could not fix it. They did not offer to move us to a table with a functioning tablet.

Chi Chi never disappoints! The food is always fresh, flavorful, and made with care. The staff is friendly, attentive, and creates such a welcoming atmosphere every time I visit. Great vibes, great spot for a night out. Our server Sean was amazing, made sure we were taken care of with amazing and timely service the whole night. 10/10 recommend for anyone trying to have a fun night out.

If you plan to dine at Chi Chi LA, remember this: Reservation is a must! This place gets incredibly busy on weekends, and it's no wonder why. Chi Chi LA is a restaurant like no other, offering an extraordinary blend of dining and entertainment.

The atmosphere on a weekend night is positively vibrant and bustling. The reason? Well, it's all thanks to the special feature at every table – the personal ordering devices. These nifty gadgets aren't just for placing your food orders; they're a gateway to a world of fun and games.

Each table has its own ordering device, which not only allows you to select your dishes but also provides a variety of interactive games. You can enjoy mini-games by yourself or challenge other tables. There are even spontaneous group challenges initiated by the restaurant. Plus, there's a chat room where you can strike up conversations with diners at other tables.

Now, onto the food. Chi Chi LA offers a tasty menu, though portions are on the smaller side. The flavors are delightful, and I highly recommend trying their flavored Soju cocktails. They come with eye-catching glowing lights and adorable duck decorations that add a cute touch to your dining experience.

The only drawback is that engaging in conversation can be a bit challenging due to the continuous sounds of excitement from people playing games all around you. But if you're here for a fun and interactive dining adventure, this might not bother you too much.

Chi Chi in Koreatown, Los Angeles, is an incredibly fun spot that offers an authentic Korean dining experience. The food is outstanding, with highlights like the bulgogi sliders and ramen that are simply amazing. Ordering is done through a device that also lets you play games with your group of friends or against everyone in the restaurant. The device includes a live game chat feature, so you can interact with others while you play. Winning coins from the games can be used to purchase food and alcoholic beverages, adding an extra layer of fun. The atmosphere is vibrant and energetic, making it the perfect place to visit with a large group. Highly recommended!

Chi Chi LA is one of the most fun restaurant experiences I’ve had in Los Angeles. The coolest part is the interactive screens at every table where you can play games and compete with other tables in the restaurant. Our table ended up battling another group and everyone around us got into it. It turned dinner into a full on game night and had the whole place laughing and cheering.
Great energy, great crowd, and a really fun vibe all around. If you want a night out that’s more than just eating and drinking, Chi Chi LA is definitely worth checking out. It’s the kind of place where you go for dinner and end up staying way longer because you’re having so much fun.

Chi Chi is such a fun spot in Koreatown! The wait can be long on weekends, but it’s totally worth it. The interactive tablets make the experience fun - you can chat with other tables, play drinking games, and even join all-restaurant competitions (where I ended up winning a prize!). Their drinks are good, though on the pricier side, but the food is amazing. Definitely try the tteokbokki and bulgogi sliders. Great vibe, great energy, and a super unique experience.

This intimate, chef-owned restaurant is run by a single chef who somehow cooks, serves, and keeps everything running seamlessly. We were honestly amazed at how quickly our food arrived, and every single dish was packed with rich, incredible flavors. We loved every bite.

The chef was so focused, passionate, and genuinely kind, which made the experience even more special.

My only complaint has nothing to do with the restaurant itself, the neighborhood felt a little sketchy, so we were a bit nervous about parking. Luckily, we found a spot right in front, which gave us some peace of mind.

If you’re here for amazing food and a unique dining experience, it’s absolutely worth the visit. We’ll definitely be back.

We had a fantastic meal at Sora Craft Kitchen! Every dish we ordered was delicious. The içli köfte was incredibly flavorful, the eggplant salad was fresh and perfectly seasoned, and both the shish kebab and köfte kebab were cooked beautifully and full of flavor.

The pekmez-marinated chicken was a standout—tender, juicy, and unique. We finished with the rice pudding and halva, and both desserts were outstanding.

From start to finish, everything was thoughtfully prepared and absolutely delicious. We’ll definitely be back and highly recommend Sora Craft Kitchen to anyone looking for exceptional Turkish cuisine!

I discovered this gem a few months ago browsing Google Maps. I made a reservation back in June for July 5th to celebrate my partner's birthday. Man, this place lives up to the 5 star reviews. Unfortunately, my partner and I were too into the food that we didn't bother taking pictures past the falafel appetizer. Lol.

We ordered half of the menu (we can eat!). We got the Siverek Tava, Corti Taplamasi, Pekmez-marinated Chicken,
Dry-Aged Tenderloin Shish Kebab, Root Vegetables Falafel, Spicy Eggplant Salad and Garlic-Spiced Kebab. EVERY SINGLE DISH WAS A HIT! My favourite was the dry-aged tenderloin shish kebab. It was seasoned and cooked perfectly. The falafels were my second favourite dish. Everything was so good! The chef was nice, attentive and caring.

The chef checks you in, you order your food at a kiosk and you sit at the table that the chef assigns for you. The food comes out pretty quickly. There's plenty of metered parking and it's free after 6:00 p.m. Do yourself a favour and book a reservation. It's very intimate and perfect for a date, special occasion or just for an evening to eat great food.

Incredible Turkish and Mediterranean food tucked away in a very unexpected part of DTLA. Stepping into the restaurant felt like stepping into the chef’s living room— cozy and inviting. There’s a kiosk to place your order, and a handful of tables which made for an intimate dining experience. The food came out quickly and the pacing was good. Everything was absolutely phenomenal, and very reasonably priced. This is now my favorite Mediterranean restaurant in LA, hands down.

Fantastic experience. Calm and peaceful dinner in LA? The atmosphere reminded me of dining in Japan. I thoroughly enjoyed everything we tried. Reservation is probably a MUST. For the uninitiated, order your meal from the kiosk.

Great food, everything we tried were very tasty. You order your food from kiosk, and unfortunately no alcohol served, also it’s in the sketchy part of downtown but that makes the parking easier,
since street in front of the restaurant was empty. However, food taste made up for those.

One of the best restaurants we’ve been to in LA! The story of the chef, the restaurants atmosphere, the small selection of lovely dishes and the extraordinary taste of the food make this a highlight.

As a Turk, I can say that this place serves very authentic food with an excellent twist.

Chef Oktay is very dedicated and his values are reflected in the dishes he creates. Bonus points because he does not serve alcohol in his place. A very bold move, which we much appreciated.
The food here is insanely good.  The chef is running one of the best hidden gems in LA right now.  Hard to find this level of craftsmanship and taste even in Turkey

It had been far too long since my last visit to 71Above, and it was every bit as wonderful as I remembered. The breathtaking panoramic views, beautifully crafted dishes, elegant atmosphere, and warm, attentive service are still as impressive as ever.

We watched Los Angeles transform from a glowing sunset into a sea of sparkling city lights while enjoying each thoughtfully prepared course. The steak was cooked perfectly, and the dessert was a lovely finish to a truly memorable evening with friends.

71Above remains one of those rare places where the view, food, atmosphere, and service all live up to the occasion. So happy to be back!

We visited this restaurant because it is included in the Amex Platinum Dining Statement program and we were blown away by food, wine, service and views. We were seated on a semi-private window table. The service was quick, friendly and proactive. The food was delicious and presented brautfully. The real standout however was the wine list, which could rival many Michelin starred restaurant. We found many options off the beaten track (many by the half bottle) like a wonderful 2000 Chateau Musar which is very difficult to find and was absolutely singing at the moment and was also really well priced! The wine pairings for the desserts were also a beautiful match and the staff was very knowledgeable. Would definitely visit again and highly recommend anyone visiting LA to stop by!

The entire experience was a 10 out of 10. I recently went here for my birthday and let me tell you food is an art and the chef was an artist who takes their craft seriously. Every dish had amazing flavor and had me truly appreciating the perfect flavor components. I got the raw oysters as a side order that had a perfectly balanced brine of ocean and savory taste that takes your taste buds on an amazing ride containing Fresno Chili Escabeche Mignonette,
Tomato Granita, Cilantro, Black Lime. I then had a nice amuse bouche compliments of the chef. For my first course i got the grilled octopus that far exceeded my already high expectations which is always a plus because sometimes the opposite can happen when you expect too much but it was more than i imagined containing Smoked Chimichurri, Sunflower Seed Dukkah,Lemon, Sweet Peppers, and Squash. It had the perfect crisp and and tenderness to it that lets you know it was cooked to perfection with vegetables so perfectly balanced, flavorful, and aromatic. For my second course I had the a5 waygu strip sirloin and when you hear someone say its the best steak you will ever have its no exaggeration. It was buttery perfection that melts in your mouth leaving you want to savor every taste with a sauce,garlic, and vegetable filled garnish that was worth every cent. For dessert I had strawberries and cream which includes Chiffon Cake, Crème Fraîche, Raspberry, Sesame Crumble, Vanilla-Rose Ice Cream, Citrus Po with very ripe and flavorful berries and I left feeling extremely satisfied and full. Something you should experience at least once and you'll definitely want to come back for more

Great restaurant on top of Bank of America Building in downtown LA. It is very fancy and chic. You need to book ahead of time. They are very communicative leading up to the day and time of reservation to make sure you are ready for the reservation. I thought that was a great touch on their part. They do not guarantee window tables at all. However when we went they give us a window table. The menu is a 3 course menu. You pick one item for each course. The service is fast and actually the portions are reasonable. We felt full after the 3 courses. The staff is super friendly and nice. It’s a perfect location for a special occasion or date night. They have valet parking or you can find parking in any of the public Parkings in downtown LA. Highly recommend them.

This is a 3 course dine-in experience. There is a small list to choose from for each of the 3 courses. To start, yellowfin tuna tartare and grilled octopus were both very flavorful, I had no textural issues with the octopus.
For the 2nd course the ribeye with beef croquet and the barramundi filet were also both very good and flavorful. I could eat a whole bowl of the broccolini/mushroom veggies that came with the beef. So delicious.
Citrus (orange) pound cake and the chocolate ganache one with green tea dust were also both very good.
Drinks, if you imbibe, were unique and well balanced.
Valet parking was easy and from the time you walk into the 1st floor lobby to the time you leave, going to 71Above is a lovely experience.

This is the fanciest restaurant I’ve ever dined at, located on the 71‑floor of the U.S. Bank Tower. There are no à‑la‑carte options, only set‑course meals. It’s fairly pricey, yet the food tastes really good. The oysters are small, but the toppings bring out distinct layers of flavor. The views are spectacular and put you in a great mood.

Well worth the price for the beautiful meal and views. Fixed menu makes ordering easy. Everything came out piping hot and perfectly prepared. Desserts were excellent. Highly recommend for any celebratory dinner.

Took my husband for his Birthday dinner here. To say, Carl B was outstanding! His level of hospitality and attention was above and beyond. He explained in great detail about the 3 course meal and what pairs great with it. We loved every second of it. The food was delicious, the bread and butter was so good. We definitely recommend. Make reservations, we gor window seats and the view was magnificent.

As someone who travels often and enjoys trying different cuisines, I was a bit disappointed with the food. I ordered the steak fajitas based on the bartender’s recommendation (“you can’t go wrong with them”), but they didn’t live up to the hype. The presentation was nice, but the portion was small, the steak was quite chewy, and the tortillas were served cold and dry.

That said, I’d definitely come back for the atmosphere, drinks, and service. I may give the food another shot and try a different dish next time—just not the fajitas.

Stay away from this location, they cram you into a small establishment, with tacky customer service and disgusting food for a price point which isn't reasonable at all. For the taste, sounds, and excitement of Mexico, this establishment spans three vibrant levels where the fun never runs out.

Upon entering, for some of us as first-timers, the patrons feel relaxed and have a nice time characterized by playful colors and modern accents that evoke energy in every corner of the space, the street-level dining room, and the bar. They also have a spacious mezzanine and an outdoor rooftop patio, weather permitting.

There was a live DJ in an upbeat party atmosphere, with various birthday celebrations taking place. This did not detract from the bartender providing us with excellent service.

Luckily, there were three seats available at the foot in the bar. We decided on Margaritas and a Sangria. The drinks were excellent, well crafted, and perfect for the afternoon.

Well worth the visit!

We had a great time and lots of fun. We were a large group, and the drinks were strong and good. The appetizers were delicious. I really liked that they allowed us, and my group really enjoyed ourselves, and we didn't feel rushed. Also, the dessert was good

My FAVORITE restaurant ever! 🤍 I’ve been about 10 times— have taken family members & friends and they all love everything about it. Atmosphere & service are a 10/10, everyone is so nice. ☺️ & the nachos + frozen margs are my favorite: definitely recommend 1000/10
It was my first time and I definitely wanna go back again. The food was unbelievably fresh and delicious. Especially, with this little hint of spice. The drinks were perfect..

The place was a good spot for a brunch, I wish the tables had a bit more space for two so we can fit the dishes. The wings and empanadas were really good, my favorite was the Al pastor tacos, Birria was a bit underwhelming so I recommend the fish/ shrimp options, Al pastor, or steak. The margaritas were good as well I got the passionfruit, overall not bad we came for a quick bite and they were able to seat us quickly which was nice! Very loud with the music so not a place to chill on the weekends, I am sure it is more relaxed on weekdays, deff a place to come for brunch to get lit and enjoy your time

Fantastic after-work, Happy hour or dinner spot!  Rooftop pretty cool!  Ambiance just right, music nice, great location near Transit. Entre and tapas are delicious 😋 with perfect portions!  Frozen Margaritas or Classic are both smooth and refreshing!

top_reviews.content: First time eating KBBQ here; heard about the coal grills so I had to try it out. The meat is a little pricey but good quality. The House Special Soot Bull Galbi was perfectly marinated but some pieces were a little chewy. The jumulleok did not disappoint; love me some beef short rib. I do feel like the griller for our table was rushing a bit, but I appreciate how the meat was cooked.

This was my first time visiting this restaurant. I ordered beef ribs and pork ribs, and they were incredibly delicious—not too sweet or too salty.  They also have a secret menu item that's not on the regular menu: "ice rice," which is rice served in a refreshing cold radish kimchi broth. It was so refreshing and delicious that I started eating it before I even thought to take a picture! They also have kimchi noodle soup, which is a perfect palate cleanser after eating the meat. I'll definitely visit again when I'm in LA.

The Soot Bull Galbi here has absolutely perfect seasoning and flavor. The meat is well-aged, tender, and full of depth. The staff are very friendly and grill the meat to perfection for you. Although the prices are on the higher side, I highly recommend this place if you want to experience authentic, delicious Korean charcoal-grilled galbi like in Korea.
For reference, the beef galbi is much better than the pork galbi.

Great food and great service. Charcoal at the table is a real treat. Ventilation was pretty good and I did not have any issues, although your entire outfit is going to smell like campfire guaranteed. We didn’t have any issues with charcoal spitting up at us. We really enjoyed our meal here and definitely intend to return next time we visit LA!

Superb. We had the tongue and pork ribs. Meat quality was excellent and the marinades and dips really enhanced their flavor. Grilled over real charcoal so you get that unmistakable taste. Banchan were notably excellent as well- we refilled the house made kimchi it was so good. Great welcoming helpful people, real ktown smoky kbbq joint vibe. A real winner.

reviews_snippets.content: "The selection of beef, pork, and chicken were quite tasty."
