name: KingChang-La
address: 3732 W 6th St, Los Angeles, CA 90020, United States

business_details.details: 3732 W 6th St, Los Angeles, CA 90020, United States

top_reviews.content:
Absolutely amazing experience at KingChang LA! From the moment we walked in, the staff made us feel incredibly welcome—they’re not only friendly but also very attentive throughout the entire meal. One of the best parts is that they grill the meat for you, so you can just sit back, relax, and enjoy everything without any hassle.

The meat quality is truly top notch—every bite was flavorful and perfectly cooked. The standout for me was definitely the marinated beef rib—it was incredibly tender, juicy, and packed with delicious flavor.

If you’re looking for high-quality Korean BBQ with excellent service, this place is a must-visit. Can’t wait to come back!

If I could only recommend one Korean BBQ restaurant, King Chang would be a must!

Anyone who hasn't tried King Chang's grilled beef intestines will regret it!

For just $30 per person, you can experience a completely hands-free Korean BBQ experience – just eat!

The walls are covered with autographs from various celebrities; many famous Korean singers, actors, idols, and other stars frequently dine here! It's said the chances of bumping into a celebrity are very high! Open until midnight from Sunday to Wednesday, and until 2 AM from Thursday to Saturday – a great late-night spot!

Authentic Korean bbq place specialized in grilled intestines. We had the spicy intestine combo and it was quite impressive. The quality of the meat was great, and combination of the ingredients was well thought out, with everything complementing the meat and enriching the flavor. The combo offered variety of banchan, soup, pancake and steam egg. Great experience, will come back.

Came here on a weekday around 8 pm, and it wasn’t too busy, which was nice. We ordered the beef combo and the intestine combo. The meat quality here is supposed to be prime, so the prices are a bit higher than other spots. I like that they cook everything for you at the table, and the food itself was good overall.

What I didn’t like was how rushed the cooking felt. Two of our friends were still on the way, and while we were just hanging out, drinking soju, and waiting, the server started cooking all the meat pretty fast. By the time our friends arrived, the beef combo was already cooked, tossed onto their plates, and looked kind of burnt and cold. It would’ve been nice if they waited for everyone to show up before starting.

That aside, it’s still a solid Korean BBQ spot, especially if you’re into intestines like I am. The flavors are good, and the meat quality is there. Also, just valet when you come it’s only about $4 and saves you the hassle of finding parking in K-Town.

The BBQ itself was actually very good, and the staff who helped us grill the meat were friendly and professional.

However, the experience was completely ruined by the woman working at the front desk. Her attitude toward us was extremely rude and dismissive. We are Chinese, and it was very obvious that she treated us very differently compared to Korean and white customers, whom she spoke to politely and warmly.

It felt uncomfortable and honestly discriminatory. There is absolutely no excuse for treating customers differently based on who they are.

Good food cannot make up for this kind of behavior. Until the management addresses this issue, I would not recommend this place.

address: 60 E 54th St, New York, NY 10022, United States

top_reviews.content: Great food and ambiance.  Would say similar vibes to polo bar but although polo bar has a meaningfully better, sharper martini but monkey bar has a better French dip and burger… so it’s a toss up which one is ultimately better.  We got the rigatoni, French dip, burger and rib eye… French dip was hands down the best thing and I would go back just for that

This place is definitely worth the hype. It was so hard to get a reservation. We ended up with a 10:30pm table so it basically became our second dinner. I just wish I had been hungrier.

The truffle bread was incredible. It had a slight sweetness that paired perfectly with the butter. The steak tartare was another favorite. The bread was super crispy and complemented the tartare so well. The spicy shrimp pasta was also delicious with just the right amount of kick. The burger and fries were good but nothing standing out.

I’m usually not a huge mac and cheese person but this one completely changed my mind. It had such a rich, strong truffle flavor that made it so addictive.

For dessert the chocolate tart was great as expected but the strawberry vacherin was really good. I’m usually a chocolate dessert person but this was honestly one of my favorites. It had a crisp meringue shell with whipped cream, strawberry icecream inside, and marinated strawberries outside. so light, refreshing, and the perfect way to end the meal. We weren’t huge fans of the drinks but everything else was excellent!

We went on a Friday afternoon around 3:45pm without a reservation and didn’t need to wait long as two people but waited a bit for a table even though there definitely would have been bar seating sooner. For two people, we got a bourbon old fashioned, Wagyu burger, prime rib French dip, and truffle Mac and cheese. The burger does not come with fries but mixed Google reviews of fries influenced us to get the truffle Mac and cheese instead. All the food was good. One person liked the French dip more while the other liked the burger more. Service was fine. Our waiter immediately asked us if we have any dietary restrictions. The restaurant with low ceilings still has somewhat of a moody vibe.

I was really excited to try this restaurant out as i have heard many great things. We did not have a reservation as we know it’s extremely hard to get. So we decided to walk in around 8:45 pm and put our name down. The hostess was friendly and reassured us she can’t guarantee we get a table. We waited around and by 10 pm she came up to us and let us know that she could seat us. Shout out to her! I don’t remember her name but It’s a breath of fresh air when you get to experience nice front of house staff in this city.

Our waitress , well two of them were very nice and let us know their opinions on the menu.

We decided to order the ..
famous monkey bread 8/10 the butter is what saves the bread. But i feel like it could’ve had more flavor
Crab Rangoon 7.5/10 i thought there would be more crab filling , but the flavor was good.
Double cheeseburger 8/10 it was good but nothing to seriously rave about. I like the au cheval burger better.
Maple thick slice bacon - 9/10 it was very good! I really enjoyed the flavor profiles and the perform added a nice touch.
Fries - 7/10 nothing special just fries . The aioli was decent but kind of a tangy aftertaste.
Drinks :
Vera - really delicious, fresh yet strong !
Old fashion - hubby said he enjoyed his drink as well

We did have leftovers and i am quite disappointed to find out the man who packed out food did not include any of the condiments / sauces that went with our food. I asked him to include everything and I didn’t check the box considering I can trust someone to do their job correctly at this type of establishment , however he fell short on that part :/
Overall the experience was pleasant and I will return to try some of the other dishes!!

I am glad I checked this place off my bucket list, but there will be a lot of buts in my review. The atmosphere screams old New York and the bar area is way more fun than the dining room in my opinion. The service was top notch, but it took a very long time for our entrees to come out. I understand it was Father’s Day, but it was too long. The Monkey Bread was great, but definitely not worth the price (I am glad I tried it though). Next the French Dip, it was good, but I can think of at least 2 restaurants that have a better french dip. The double cheeseburger was great (perhaps the star), but for the price at least throw in some chips. The Mac n Cheese was very cheesy, I loved the pasta they used and top was crispy. Now our server, she was great and apologized for the slow service and even bought use complimentary ice cream. She deserves 5 stars. This place is worth trying, just expect to drop a lot of dough.

top_reviews.content:
??Spicy Eggplant 🍆
This flavor was recommended by my friend and it's really good! It's fragrant and spicy, and goes well with rice. I think I'll choose this one next time and make it even spicier.
??Steak🐮
This is their popular one. Big chunks of beef with eggs, sesame, and scallions. It's hard to say it's not delicious, right? Haha. I don't really like the steak sauce they serve on the side. It's a bit sour and not my taste. It's still better with mustard.
??Mackerel 🐟
This is mashed mackerel that has been fried until fragrant, mixed with rice, and can be eaten wrapped in seaweed. It's also very flavorful!
Every meal can be turned into a soup-rice dish by pouring the soup over the rice. Each meal comes with a side salad and soup, and they are all very distinctive and not disappointing at all! After the meal, they gave us a very cute Korean version of Yakult. I also want to take a few Dubai chocolate cookies away, they are really delicious🤤. It's easy to sell out on weekends, but it seems easier to buy on weekdays. It's a small and very cozy Korean store.

I’ve already been here multiple times, and Damsot has quickly become one of my favorite Korean restaurants in LA. The pot rice dishes are seriously delicious, especially the steak, eel, and abalone options. The crispy rice at the bottom is the best part!! mixing everything together and then finishing with the tea poured over the remaining rice is such a comforting experience.

The eel was flavorful and perfectly cooked, the steak was tender and juicy, and the abalone pot rice tasted fresh and unique. We also ordered the fried shrimp, which was super crispy and came out hot and fresh.

Tried Damsot in Ktown – super popular in Korea with 50+ locations. We got the eel rice bowl and the steak rice bowl. You mix everything up, eat the rice, then pour barley tea into the leftover scorched rice, cover it, and let it soften. The eel was tender and flavorful, and the tea‑soaked crispy rice at the end was such a unique texture. The steak bowl was juicy too. Also had salmon sashimi – very fresh. They even gave us a Korean version of Yakult after the meal. Parking is tight on the street, but there's a lot downstairs – just ask them to validate.

Damsot just opened their first U.S. location and I had to experience it for myself — and I’m so glad I did.

This spot is known in Korea for their signature Korean pot rice, and the presentation alone sets the tone. Everything comes out hot, steaming, and full of flavor in a traditional stone pot that really elevates the experience.

As someone who is vegan, I appreciated that there are options that can be modified. I tried the spicy eggplant pot rice and the tofu with shishito peppers — just removing the meat and egg — and both dishes were incredibly satisfying. Rich, comforting, and layered with flavor without feeling like anything was missing.

They also had crispy fried tofu on the side and a smooth drink to finish, which brought everything together perfectly.

The experience felt thoughtful, warm, and elevated. Definitely a place I’ll be coming back to and recommending to anyone looking to explore Korean cuisine in a new way.

Great spot for a solo meal! The pot rice is comforting and generously portioned. The summer special cold soba was so refreshing on a hot day.

Plus, parking is also convenient. The restaurant validates parking in the plaza, which is always a nice bonus. Will definitely be back!

An extremely cost-effective restaurant! It mainly offers set meals, which is very suitable for people working nearby. The menu is also very diverse. This time, I and my friends ordered beef rice and sukiyaki pot. We all thought they were delicious! Personally, I really like fried chicken. It's not very expensive but very crispy.

I liked the steak rice pot here especially with the wasabi! But actually the raw fish(?) banchan on the side was my favorite with the rice. It was super flavorful and had good chewy texture. I ate 2 of my friends' portion of it. Their fried shrimp eggplant appetizer was also super yummy. I also tried my friend's vegetarian eggplant rice pot and thought it was tasty.

Damsot has an incredibly fast and efficient reservation system. Go in, write your name in the wait list and go outside and wait a bit. My wait was 15 mins at most. They keep everything moving very efficiently. Service is fantastic, everyone from the host, to the server, to the food runner and even the busser were great. The Steak Pot Rice is usually limited to 15 for lunch and 15 for dinner but I was able to order it and I quite enjoyed it. The barley tea to be poured into the stone pot with the leftover rice still in it makes for quite a cool after-meal soup. We even got Yakult-style probiotic small drinks with our check after the meal was over. Great experience with short wait times, great staff and fantastic ambiance (the inside is very clean, well lit-up and nicely decorated).

top_reviews.content:
Do not eat here if you want to avoid food poisoning.
My girlfriend and I recently ate here, and it was a terrible experience. The food we were served was undercooked—there was raw dough that was completely inedible, along with two small pieces of fish. Serving food in that condition is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about food safety.
To make matters worse, they charged an extra $0.50 for a to-go box, which felt like a cheap way to squeeze more money out of customers after we had already spent $28 on our meal.
For the price, I expected much better quality and, most importantly, food that was fully cooked and safe to eat. Unfortunately, the raw dough ruined the entire meal, and the extra charge for a takeout box only added to the disappointment. I won’t be returning, and I cannot recommend this place at all.

I bought food from this stall and ended up with a lot of leftovers. When I asked for a to-go container, I was told it would cost 25 cents. Unfortunately, I didn't have any cash on me, and they don't accept card payments for purchases that small.

I showed the staff member how much food I had left, hoping she might make an exception, but she still refused to provide a container. It was disappointing that so much food was more likely to go to waste over a 25-cent box.

Thankfully, another nearby stall, Ellie Julie, was kind enough to give me a to-go container without hesitation.
Bebeembap was as delicious as it is beautiful 🍜 We shared it and the lady at the counter offered the second bowl without me even asking!!

Service wasn't bad. Food did take a while to get to me. If I wasn't a white girl with texture sensitivities I would've just absolutely loved my dish. The seasoning in the sauce was fantastic and all of the seafood seemed to be cooked pretty well. I'd love to try more food from there

I’m really disappointed with my experience at this Korean restaurant in the food court, especially given how much I was looking forward to the meal.

I understand that it was busy (it was President’s Day), and as a Korean American, I completely get how hectic Korean food spots can get during rush times. That said, being busy doesn’t excuse being rude.

My seafood pancake took an extremely long time to come out — so long that the rest of my party had already finished their meals from other food court vendors by the time mine arrived. Because of that delay, I wasn’t able to finish my food. The pancake was $20, which isn’t cheap for food court dining.

When I politely asked about the delay, it seemed to offend the staff. The two women working at the front that day were extremely rude and dismissive. To make things worse, when I asked for a to-go container since I couldn’t finish (due to the late timing), they flat-out refused. I tried to explain the situation calmly, but they were unwilling to accommodate.

It’s really not hard to be kind and respectful to customers. A little politeness and basic customer service would have gone a long way. Unfortunately, the attitude completely overshadowed the food.

I won’t be returning

name: MUSE Santa Monica
address: 108 W Channel Rd, Santa Monica, CA 90402, United States

business_details.details: 108 W Channel Rd, Santa Monica, CA 90402, United States

top_reviews.content:
Small, intimate space inside. Very well decorated - creates an elevated vibe.

Food was all excellent. I don’t usually get bread, but the brioche is dense and croissant-like flaky at the same time which is delightful. Duck cappelletti and the tuna tartlets were highlights food-wise.

The cocktails we tried were all delightful. Highlight was the tropical old fashioned.

My only critique is price point for portion. I’m not expecting extravagantly-sized portions, but they were quite small for the price point.

5 stars without a doubt!

To be honest, after reading a few negative reviews on Google, I almost decided not to come. But my husband convinced me to give it a chance, and I’m so glad he did.
This place was an absolute 10/10.
The food was exceptional, every dish was beautifully presented and absolutely delicious. The service was equally outstanding.
A very special thank you to Sthefani. She was truly incredible - attentive, graceful, professional, and genuinely warm. You could immediately tell that she loves what she does and sincerely cares about every guest. Her recommendations were excellent, her timing was perfect, and she made us feel welcomed from the moment we arrived. People like her are rare and make all the difference in creating a memorable dining experience.
If I had to mention one tiny downside, it would be that the tables are quite close together. However, considering how intimate and small the restaurant is, that’s completely understandable and probably unavoidable.
Everything else was flawless. The food, the atmosphere, and especially the service exceeded all expectations. We left already talking about when we’d come back.
Thank you for such a wonderful evening!

Brioche Feuilletée with Softened Bordier Butter
The butter aroma hits as soon as it arrives. Ultra-crispy, flaky exterior with a soft, pull-apart interior, finished with flaky salt that really highlights the butter. Basically a must-order—almost every table gets it.

Sunchokes with Castelfranco & Orange
Ordered out of curiosity. The sunchokes (ginger-like in appearance) have a texture similar to crunchy potatoes, paired with slightly bitter chicory leaves. Dressed heavily with vinegar, so the overall flavor leans salty and acidic.

Mussels Dressed in Sesame with Pear & Eggplant Purée
Pear and eggplant don’t add much flavor here, so it mostly tastes like sesame-dressed mussels with chili oil. Garnished with nori, but otherwise fairly one-note.

Matsutake & Chanterelle Risotto with Midnight Moon
Very rich and layered, but extremely salty at first. The kitchen kindly remade it, and while the second version was less salty, it ended up tasting a bit flat.

Pomme Pavé with Citrus Hollandaise
Essentially fried potato mille-feuille—crispy outside, soft and creamy inside. Delicious, but the portion is tiny. Potatoes really are the perfect food.

Vanilla St. Honoré
Beautifully done and petite. Perfect caramel crunch on the choux, visible vanilla bean in the cream, and not overly sweet overall—though the pastry base was a bit too sweet.

Chocolate Tart
Gorgeous presentation with a lifelike chocolate rose. Dark chocolate lava center with a cookie crust. Tastes good, but the visuals really steal the show.

Lemon Tart
Possibly the sourest lemon tart I’ve ever had—in a good way. Loved the sharp lemon custard, but if you’re not into sour desserts, skip it. The meringue on top is heavy, clearly meant to balance the acidity.

Tiramisu
Very underwhelming. Not fresh, overly sweet, and the texture was already firm—would not recommend.

I love Muse so much! I went here for my birthday, and I have absolutely no regrets. All the food at Muse is great, but the appetisers are truly stellar. The veal bon bons are perfectly juicy and crispy on the inside (it’s a mystery to me how they retain their structure being that juicy inside), and the sauce verte goes perfectly with it. The hamachi is so simple yet well executed, the bitterness of the olive oil pairs deliciously with the chili coulis. The tuna tartlets are so cute and tiny, but don’t shy away from great flavors and textures. And the brioche - unironically the best bread I have ever eaten, it’s super croissant like, rich, and buttery, the salty butter that comes with it pairs perfectly. The saffron risotto is technically super well executed, and aromatic. The rack of lamb tastes as delicious as it looks, I’m still dreaming about the herb crust and the sauce it came with. Our server recommended to pair it with the pomme pavé, and boy was that genius!
They have 0 misses with the deserts here - the Vanilla St. Honore is beautiful, the vanilla chantilly cream goes perfectly with the salted caramel profiteroles. The chocolate tart is decadent and great. I had to take the tiramisu to go since I was so stuffed by then, but when I finally got a chance to eat it at home I thought it was excellent (it also comes scooped tableside which is the only valid way to serve tiramisu). Our server was super friendly and nice, genuinely the best service I’ve experienced in a restaurant. I never thought I would rave about the interior design of a restaurant, but believe me when I say it’s etched in my mind and I’m in awe and inspired. Thanks so much for making my birthday great, Muse!

Dining at Muse Santa Monica was truly one of the best restaurant experiences I’ve had in a very long time. From the moment I walked in, every detail felt thoughtfully executed. The ambiance strikes a perfect balance between chic and inviting — stylish yet comfortable, with an atmosphere that makes the evening feel special without being pretentious.

The service was exceptional: attentive without being overbearing, with a staff that clearly cares about elevating the guest experience. Every interaction felt warm and genuine, which is rare to find.

The food itself was outstanding from start to finish. The brioche was a highlight —while every dish impressed, it was the dessert that completely stole the show. Truly unforgettable, it left me with the perfect lasting impression of an already phenomenal meal.

All around, Muse delivers on every level — ambiance, service, and culinary excellence. It’s the kind of place that reminds you what dining out is supposed to feel like. I can’t recommend it highly enough and look forward to returning soon.

This was my third visit, and the food continues to be excellent—I truly enjoy it every time. That said, the overall experience feels misaligned with what’s presented as fine dining. Prior to arriving, I emailed and called multiple times regarding scheduling, and the interaction at the front of the house was disappointing. The hostess was not only rude but dehumanizing, which was especially surprising given the level of prestige the restaurant aims to convey.

While the manager attempted to course-correct, the experience remained uncomfortable, and midway through the meal I was misgendered twice. Ultimately, the food is absolutely worth the price, but I would recommend coming for the cuisine rather than expecting elevated or thoughtful service.

We had a truly WORLD CLASS EXPERIENCE at Muse! ❤️Our dinner was truly extraordinary! The food was exceptional, the ambiance was perfection - and what impressed us most of all was the level of service! It went so above and beyond great service and into another sphere entirely! It was truly world class hospitality at a level that would stand out as exceptional anywhere in the world. Having been blessed to visit some of the best restaurants and hotels in the world - I can truly say this is in the top .000001%! Everyone on the team exuded a warmth and kindness that made it a singular experience! Thank you to Max and Fardad! True perfection! CHEFS KISS!!!🎉

Great anniversary dinner at MUSE! Food was spectacular and felt like dishes you couldn’t find elsewhere. The crispy branzino will live rent free in my mind forever! Lamb chops were a must have. We also got Corn Risotto, Creamed Kholrabi, and as others have mentioned, the Vanilla St Honore is wonderful! Cocktails were great but the woman at the bar was a bit cold and unfriendly. All other waitstaff from the hostess to the servers were 5 ⭐️ though! Also this was a pricey dinner, for 2 people expect to spend $400-500 all in if also ordering drinks/wine. Overall, 9/10. Would come back for sure for another special occasion.

top_reviews.content:
✨ Le Café Louis Vuitton NYC — 8.5/10

The building is absolutely stunning. The first few floors are the LV boutique, the café is on the 4th, and the 5th is furniture, which I was told is appointment-only. Everything was impeccably clean and beautifully designed. The bathroom was almost too well concealed  — it genuinely looked like part of the wall.

Just before the café is Le Chocolat Maxime Frédéric, and this was probably my favorite visual detail. The chocolates are incredibly intricate, with monogrammed designs and limited-edition pieces inspired by LV handbags and characters. Unfortunately, most of the more elaborate pieces were sold out during my visit.

My only criticism was the lack of storytelling. When you’re paying $50 for a chocolate bar or hazelnut spread — and some pieces are several hundred dollars — I want to understand the craftsmanship, inspiration, and concept behind it. I found myself having to ask most of the questions, and even then, there wasn’t much detail provided. At this level of luxury, I think the story should be part of the experience.

I purchased the $50 hazelnut spread, and my brother got the $50 two-piece chocolate set with one dark and one milk chocolate bar. Beautiful presentation and surprisingly substantial portions.

The café itself was gorgeous. The ambiance was elegant, relaxed, and very clean. We were seated earlier than our reservation, which I appreciated. The only service hiccup was that we weren’t initially given enough menus, so we had to share while they brought additional ones over. Minor, but at this price point, you do expect things to be fairly seamless.

Our waitress, however, was wonderful. She was incredibly kind, knowledgeable when we asked questions, and every recommendation she made was excellent.

The food and cocktails were genuinely delicious, and the overall experience was lovely.

8.5/10 — Would absolutely return. 🥂✨

Want to highlight that the monogrammed food is really picturesque, photogenic, instagram-worthy.

For food, I recommend the ravioli! It came out monogrammed, the flavor was actually delicious, had a rich creamy sauce. Pasta was al dente.

The tea “an exquisite journey,” can be a singular person at the table. It doesn’t have to be everyone participating. The tea sandwiches were absolutely adorable miniatures of their best sellers like the lobster roll, turkey club, tuna taco, croquette, and poupon de legumes. The tuna taco was the perfect bite. Anything with bread was quite dry and felt a little stale.

The desserts were delightful - our favorite: pistachio petula. Exotic Charlotte was a close second for a fresh creamy bite. The desserts were not as flavorful as expected though.

Cappuccino was mild coffee flavor. Not a strong flavor. Skim milk available.

In terms of atmosphere, it doesn’t seem like a high end luxury experience. It’s more casual with laid back lounge chairs with cushions, a very noisy cafe, and kind of a crowded restaurant. The music was a bit loud as well. The sunlight is nice and the decorations are of course iconic.

Plates and furniture were a nice touch. Friendly  waiter who came just the right amount of times. Bread for the complimentary bread and butter service was cold.

Restaurant located on 4th floor of LV. Make a reservation on resy! But they do take walk ins with a long wait time at the bar.

Great food and service! We went here for lunch as a big group and the staff was very friendly. We had a baby and a toddler in our group and the staff was very patient as we got our orders in and kept our kids entertained.

The food was great! I’d say the desserts were spectacular and the savory dishes were very good. The portions are on the smaller side so just be mindful when ordering.

Personally, I think this would be an amazing place to stop by for a post meal coffee and dessert. I saw many reviews discussing how expensive this spot is but that is to be expected.

What the cafe does is really make you feel part of the LV family and give you a very luxurious meal and experience while you’re there. Definitely worth checking out!

Finally, we were able to reserve seats and visit the Louis Vuitton café. The restaurant definitely offers an elegant and luxurious atmosphere, with many details thoughtfully decorated with LV’s signature monogram.

For Louis Vuitton fans, it is a unique and memorable experience. The staff were warm, friendly, and professional, which made the visit feel even more special. The dishes were beautifully crafted and presented with a fresh, creative French-cuisine approach. While I felt some dishes could have had a bit more uniqueness or personality, the overall presentation, quality, and service still made the restaurant worth visiting.

My favorite part was actually the dessert. It was layered, flavorful, and beautifully balanced between bitterness and sweetness.

I would definitely bring friends next time for the full Louis Vuitton experience.

Scoring a dinner reservation at the Louis Vuitton Café was one of the highlights of the day. Exceptional service, (Nathaniel was amazing), a beautiful atmosphere, and thoughtfully crafted dishes made for a memorable experience. The portions are designed as small bites, but each one is packed with flavor. We sampled several menu items, with the lobster rolls, sliders, ravioli, filet and desserts standing out as favorites. Every detail felt intentional, creating a dining experience that was both luxurious and approachable. Highly recommend for anyone looking to combine great food with an iconic setting.

Shocked at low reviews because I had the most incredible 40th Birthday at Louis Vuitton and Le Café Louis Vuitton! Everyone was so sweet starting with what looked like the manager. She offered me water and apologized for not bringing me a glass! I was like omg please don’t apologize I was absolutely grateful for the water! Our client advisor Karen was also so helpful and so kind. She asked if my husband and I would like a picture together to celebrate the occasion and offered us champagne! She escorted us upstairs to the cafe where we were still treated like royalty! The hostess wished me a Happy Birthday and sat us down fluffing the pillows on the seat for me. The waiters worked so fast (without rushing us) to get our orders in. My husband was excited to take pictures of the beautifully presented food and the waiter backed up with the plate to make sure my husband got the best angle for his picture! We all laughed. The food was the most delicious food we have eaten in a very long time and they even brought out a sweet little treat with a candle for my birthday! We were done with all of our courses in an hour! The service was incredible! Overall, my experience (my first time here) at Louis Vuitton was unforgettable and I’m grateful to everyone for making my 40th Birthday extra special!

While it's hard to get a reservation at the Café, once you dine here you can see why. The atmosphere is not as pretentious as you'd imagine it to be.Staff are well versed in the art of "serving".

Our waitress explained the menu to us fairly easily as it was our first time dining. Our food was brought out in an efficient fashion. Everything was delightful, from food temperature to plating

For me to dine more frequently, I need to be able to make a reservation for one - four people easily. I need to be able to walk in for a quick bite if necessary. It was soooo hard to get the reservation I had, so when one popped up I jumped at it.

What an unforgettable dining experience at Le Café Louis Vuitton. From the warm welcome upon arrival to the impeccable service throughout the afternoon, every detail was exceptional.

A special thank you to Stephanie Castro who assisted in arranging the reservation. And a person who was one of nicest servers we’ve had in a while, Heidi, whose professionalism, warmth, and knowledge elevated the entire experience. The Afternoon Tea Experience was beautifully executed, with stunning presentations and extraordinary flavors. It was a pleasure meeting Executive Pastry Chef Mary George and Eunji Lee and learning about the inspiration behind their collaboration. Every item was thoughtfully crafted and showcased remarkable creativity and skill.

The cuisine, desserts, and coffee service were all outstanding. As someone who frequently enjoys fine dining experiences, I can confidently say this was one of the most memorable culinary experiences I’ve had. The attention to detail, hospitality, and passion from the entire team truly set this restaurant apart.

I look forward to returning and highly recommend Le Café Louis Vuitton to anyone seeking an exceptional dining experience. Also, don’t miss their Chocolate Shop!!! Wow!

We are deeply grateful for the wonderful dining experience provided by the staff at Capital Grille and truly appreciate their great service in celebrating our anniversary!!! It’s an experience that we’ll treasure forever and we highly recommend for everyone to visit and dine at this outstanding steakhouse restaurant!!!

top_reviews.content:
Essential by Christophe is a classic French fine dining spot with nods to Robuchon (where Chef Bellanca previously worked) including the signature dishes of mushroom cappuccino and mashed potato. The French cooking style results in a procession of soft proteins in buttery sauces with global accents such as turmeric and omija berry. The experience is the definition of fancy: a modern and elegant dining room (sans the white tablecloths) staffed by highly attentive folks who will take care of your every need.

Personally, I found the tasting menu monotonous. There was nothing wrong with any individual dish, but taken as a whole it was just a terribly constructed tasting menu. It lacked variety; it lacked ups and downs; it lacked any sense of progression.

The mushroom cappuccino was a great “welcome drink”, warm and thick and comforting with the mushroom and sweet potato. But then it went into the uni dish that felt twice as big as it should be. I was starting to get disgusted halfway in as it was just a bowl of goo. The pickled radishes didn’t save it. I wished the bread had arrived then. The langoustine was bursting with its natural sweetness, the mild green curry taking a backseat so the langoustine could shine, but again the entire dish was soft, the pasta having zero bite. I was so glad to have the bread then—really deliciously fluffy and crispy.

The following scallop dish was a highlight, the nutty sauce and smoky aroma beautifully balancing the scallop’s sweetness, but by that point I couldn’t enjoy it to its fullest because of all the dishes leading up to that point. I grew tired of it. The black bass didn’t help, as it was softly poached and served with fork-tender artichokes, though the turmeric sauce was deliciously fragrant. The pork was likewise thinly sliced and tender, served in a tasty fruity jus. The mashed potatoes of course required zero chewing. At this point I wanted something else other than baby food.

The desserts tasted especially delicious because they provided the burst of acidity lacking from the rest of the meal. Also, the meringue shell of the vacherin finally provided something interesting to chew on.

If it weren’t obvious already, I desperately wished I had something to chew on throughout the meal besides the mind-blowingly delicious crispy and crusty bread—or did the bread taste extra delicious precisely because everything else lacked texture? As someone who highly values variety of texture, the cooking here’s the antithesis of my preferences, but I sort of expected that going into a French spot. The flavors were fine; the textures were not.

Objectively, this spot is great for people who judge food by how it melts in their mouth and the abundance of butter. And the dining experience itself was nice. But if you’re like me, this isn’t the spot for you.

I’ve celebrated so many special moments here my birthday, our anniversary, and even my partner’s birthday. The atmosphere is always amazing, and the food is absolutely delicious. This place holds such great memories for me, and I’ll definitely comeback again.

My husband and I booked a private dining room at this restaurant to celebrate our marriage with friends. While I will give credit where it’s due—the food itself and the service we got were good—the overall experience was deeply marred by sneaky pricing tactics and unacceptable billing incompetence.

1. Deceptive Water Upselling:
At the beginning of the dinner, the waiter asked me and my husband if we wanted "still or sparkling water," completely omitting the option of tap water. Confused, I assumed "still" meant tap water. It wasn’t until I looked at the receipt the next day that I realized we were charged a staggering $150 just for still water. We have dined at numerous Michelin-starred restaurants in NYC, including three-star, and never has a restaurant hidden the tap water option like this. It felt incredibly cheap and deceptive.

2. Major Billing Error and Subpar Customer Service:
A month prior to the event, I provided my credit card information and paid a $1,500 deposit. However, looking at the final receipt and my credit card statement, I noticed they charged me the full event total of $5,300 on top of the deposit. When I emailed the manager to ask about the $1,500 refund, I was told the deposit was "non-refundable and already applied to the total." after a day. Knowing the math was completely wrong, I called the manager.

During the call, I had to explain three times that we were overcharged, but the manager repeatedly dismissed my concerns, insisting the receipt was final. It wasn't until the fourth time I pushed back that she finally agreed to actually look at the receipt and said she needed to check with her own manager. An hour later, they finally admitted they made a mistake. All I received was a breezy "please excuse us for the error."

What if I hadn't meticulously checked my bank statements? This blatant lack of attention to detail and the defensive attitude of the staff created a lot of unnecessary stress and work for me.

A Michelin-starred restaurant should present flawless execution, not only on the plate but also in their service and financial integrity. Sadly, they failed on the latter. I cannot recommend this place for a hassle-free special occasion.

———————————————
Follow-up: The director of operations reached out to me to apologize for their mistake and invited me to visit the restaurant again. I accept the apology and am glad to see that management values feedback and cares about their guests' experience.

Wow, Essential by Christophe was truly one of the best experiences I have had at a restaurant in the city! Every detail was made with intention and care. I truly fell in love with the atmosphere, service and the delicious cuisine.

I sat at the bar and Crystal was my bartender. Her knowledge of the menu was top tier. Her and Mario guided me through the menu. Their service was catered to me and my desires, they wanted to know what I was looking for and they gave me just that. Crystal was so attentive, kind and intuitive. I felt so taken care of.

Now for the food: The scallops were lightly roasted to perfection and topped with delicate caviar. The bed of sauce the scallops were submerged in was so delectable that I used the sauce for the fresh bread I ordered on the side. Now for the main event: The Lobster Pasta. The lobster was fresh and cooked with accuracy. As a seafood lover, the quality was undeniable! The pasta was the perfect texture and so was the sauce. The Parmesan foam glazed over the dish was a super unique twist. And I can’t forget the Soufflé that sent me to heaven! Light, fluffy, warm and sweet. Just what I needed to end the night.

There were so many surprises and each one made me feel so special. My mind was blown and I had to write this review because I can’t stop thinking about it. Thank you Christophe for creating magic in the city! From the moment I walked through the door, I felt Essential. What a memorable night, thank you.

An underrated and underdiscovered elegant restaurant with amazing service. A Well deserved Michelin star, they went out of their way to make my friend's birthday a fabulous experience. The burger (not on a tasting menu) was top class and tasting menu was also a hit, especially caviar topped scallops. The dessert was a bit too sweet though.

Aside from the desserts, every course was phenomenal. Textbook level of cooking for the perfect temp/texture on the main ingredient highlighting its natural flavor, which is then flawlessly balanced and enhanced by all the other components. Loved the progression/composition of the tasting menu as well. Definitely one of the most memorable dining experiences in recent years. To me this is a minimum 2 stars in nyc. At $255pp right now, I'd go as often as I can before they receive additional recognition and the prices increase.

I didn’t take it because it was honestly fine, but I was genuinely touched by their generosity :)

The pacing of the dishes was just right, they gently wiped our table between each course. They were super thoughtful. I had a truly wonderful experience, and this was definitely one of the highlights of my short trip.

Absolutely Exceptional Dining Experience

We had the most incredible experience at Essential by Christophe. We were there celebrating the newlyweds, and choosing the Chef’s Room truly made the evening unforgettable. The level of service was unlike anything I’ve ever experienced, every single staff member made us feel welcomed, comfortable, and genuinely cared for. They anticipated what we needed before we even asked and made sure every guest had exactly what they wanted.

The food was outstanding. The Wagyu beef cap was melt-in-your-mouth perfection, the scallop was a clear highlight, and the mushroom cappuccino was one of the most unique and delicious dishes. Every course was beautifully executed and thoughtfully balanced.

If you’re looking for a place to celebrate a special occasion or want a dining experience that exceeds every expectation, I cannot recommend this restaurant enough. Absolutely five stars.

I ordered catfish with two sides which were candied yams and Mac. The catfish was seasoned and not salty at all and it had a crunch. I went for brunch today, and as always, business was booming. The place was full—people dining in, grabbing takeout, and even filling the bar. There’s often a short wait, which isn’t surprising given how consistently packed the dining room is.

The brunch menu is stacked with crowd favorites, and the music always sets the vibe—something you can really enjoy while you eat. But the food? Phenomenal. The fried catfish was seasoned and fried to crispy perfection. The turkey wings were tender, flavorful, and cooked just right—fall-off-the-bone good. And the yams? Sweet, rich, and perfectly seasoned… honestly hard to stop eating. The macaroni was rich and satisfying, and the potato salad is always a standout for me.

For dessert, I had the chocolate cake—and it was exactly how I like it: moist with real, creamy frosting that doesn’t miss.

The brunch sangria was also a hit. I mixed red and white, and it was smooth and refreshing. Portion sizes are generous, so you definitely leave satisfied.

And Danny, the owner, really sets the tone—he’s always present, checking in with guests, jumping in to help the staff, and clearly running a tight operation.

Nettie’s continues to be the go-to spot for soul food—consistently good, every time.

I ordered the Kale Chicken Caesar Salad and added grilled steak cooked medium. The salad comes with grilled chicken, kale, Caesar dressing, croutons, Parmesan cheese, and a large piece of buttered bread. Both the chicken and steak were flavorful, and adding the steak made the salad a really satisfying meal.

I also tried the Strawberry Margarita, which was $10 as part of their all day, everyday margarita pricing. It was STRONG but still tasted delicious, definitely a good value if you enjoy a cocktail with your meal.

I loved the atmosphere too, especially the wall filled with different artwork. There's seating for different group sizes, and as a solo diner, I appreciated the small booth I was given. It would also be perfect for a couple. Service was quick as well.

Worth Ordering 🍽️
⭐ Kale Chicken Caesar Salad + grilled steak
⭐ Strawberry Margarita

Good to Know 💡
- $10 margaritas all day, every day.
- Comfortable seating for solo diners, couples, and larger groups.

fried octopus

baked veggies trios
A few steps away from the Disney Concert Hall and the opera house (which offer 10% off with a ticket), it features a high ceiling, wood shutters (or wood-like?), an open kitchen, and tiles, with thin stems; it just feels right for me.

We sat by the bar because tables are all booked - it's an opera night. We learned of this Italian restaurant from two ladies we met at last night's concert at Disney - go figure -:).

The bartender doesn't have a fancy shaking motion but is keeping a close eye on us: constantly asking if we need a refill or something. I don't consider it pushy, even though our glasses are half empty. When the bar area got busy, they asked two people to move to accommodate a foursome.

The only TV monitor is showing sports, with eight events going on simultaneously. I glanced at the volleyball from time to time, but was unable to follow: just too hard with seven other things going on. Maybe just one? Change the channel when someone asks?

They've two corporate events going on that night: one with 150 people and one with 50. The hors d'oeuvres look so yummy that it gives me the urge to sneak in, ha ha ha.

By 6pm, the house is packed to the brim. One staff member came looking for wine, which is behind us. He asked the bartender for help - sorry, I don't speak Spanish, but my best guess is that he couldn't find the wine his table had ordered.

Desserts are made in-house except macrons.

Oh, the 10% off with the opera ticket, of course, I forgot all about it when paying.

Candles on the table would be nice. I would go again. The patio looked delightful although we were seated inside. The place is a bit difficult to find, there is a lot of construction going on and if you go up from behind/below the restaurant (up the steps) they could use some signs down there. Poor service, lacking basic conversational etiquette (eg eye contact, acknowledging you said something, etc.). Ouch! Food wasn’t bad, but also wasn’t good. For the price, it should at least be good (if not very good?). Atmosphere is fine, albeit not notably better than your local Applebees/pick random suburban casual eatery.

Whelp, food truck for me next time! You live, you learn.

Wow, wow, wow, wow, wow. Hole in the wall place with amazing Korean food. Best Samgyetang we've had. Better than the one in the most famous restaurant in Korea. Eun-Daegu - Black Cod Braised black cod was so flavorful and good. Must visit. Take out with only a couple tables.

Tiny hole in the wall spot in K Town. Was a top restaurant on Beli and Michelin recommended in 2019, and for good reason.

The restaurant only has 4 items, and we tried 3 out of the 4, enjoying all of them thoroughly.

The Samgyetang was heartwarming with flavours like pine nut, ginseng, and great chicken, and a perfect start to our meal paired with their banchan.

Their Galbijjim was stellar, some of the best I've ever had, more memorable and flavourful than Sun Nong Dan and other Korean spots renowned for 갈비찜. Meat was tender, fatty, and sauces were tasty, yet not overwhelming the flavour of the meat. Additional tteokbokki, potatoes, and other ingredients added great texture as well.

Despite their Galbijjim being immaculate, their Eundaegu-jolim was probably my favourite dish. Reminding me of Chinese style sea bass, the black cod was tender and packed with rich oil and flavour. Something that was truly special and not like anything I had at any other Korean restaurant in LA yet.

Service was also lovely - I felt like I was in a family home, being served the tang into my bowl personally by the owners, and being treated to sliced caracara oranges as dessert.

I’m rating it honestly from my experience because that’s what google reviews is for, but with love in my heart, if you like miserably loud, cramped spaces, full of desperate 20-somethings and 0 ventilation, you will think this place is peak. In order of when I ate them, I tried the:
~ Popcorn Cauliflower - 1/5
This cauliflower tasted like it was frozen in 1983 and defrosted and deep fried just for us! It was almost salty enough? But it had this profound gritty quality which made it hard to eat until I was quite high and ran out of other things to munch. Ketchup served it much better than the orange sauce it came with.
~ Blistered Brussel Sprouts - 0/5
Whattt a disappointment. Blistered is a hilarious detail to add, because these brussel sprouts were seriously undercooked, very hard to chew, very much blisterless, and then the bacon was supposed to cut the sweetness of the sauce, but idk what happened there because the bacon had that stale greasy crunch, and it itself was salty, but nothing strong enough to cut the sweetness. It was overall just sweet and poorly cooked.
~ French Fries - 2/5
These came as a side with the double smash burger, the kitchen was rationing ketchup for some reason but the waiter brought more when we asked, they were stale and undersalted, I’m sorry but they were. I ate them all, but only because they were marginally better than the popcorn cauliflower.
~ Ahi Tuna Sliders - 3/5
These were almost good!! I was excited for them to be great, but they were missing some fullness, maybe it was just the proportions of the ingredients, but these were definitely the best appetizer we got.
~ Double Smash Burger - 4/5
The first winner of the night, but to be fair I was munching atp, I appreciated the extra pickle spear it was served with because there weren’t so many on the burger itself so it made for a more rounded experience.
~ Smore Dessert - 4/5?
I couldn’t eat much of this because I was full, also the portion was very formidable!!! It’s like a small bread pan sized loaf of dessert. It was chocolaty and the texture was decent, but like with all smore things, it is mostly sweet so it’s hard to eat a ton of.
~ Apple dessert - 2/5

We made reservations for Valentine morning. An hour prior to leaving for this reservation we received a text message confirming that we are coming. We get to the restaurant and there’s a sign saying that there was a water outage, but they never communicated that with the customers as there was other people waiting outside reading the same poster. Everyone wasn’t sure if we could leave because we would get charged a $25 fee per person.

There was no communication. There were servers inside. However, instead of communicating to us that there would be a late opening. They just stared and didn’t want to open the door when we wanted to ask what would happen next or if they would be open for the day.

After 20 minutes of waiting with no answers, the manager finally went in and let us know that they would probably be opening in like five minutes. It really turned out to be another 15 minutes. We didn’t get in there until around 11:40.

We decided to still give it a try because we were excited about trying the restaurant however it probably wasn’t the best sanitary decision and that was our fault.

We ordered the croissant sandwich, it was okay. We also had the waffle sandwich. We ordered one of their cold brew coffee however we didn’t finish it because it tasted off. Instead, we decided to just order mimosas which were good. We did their bottomless mimosas deal.

It was not worth the price. We also didn’t get any discount or apologies from the restaurant, not disclosing that they were having a water outage at all. We found that very displeasing and unprofessional because they didn’t let us know about the issue and on top of that they didn’t offer anything complementary, given the issue at hand.

Myeongdong Kyoja has been a staple in the same location for years, specializing in Korean-style noodle soups (kalguksu).

Their signature kalguksu comes with chewy, uniform noodles and a rich, thick broth served with ground beef — deeply flavorful and satisfying.

The anchovy kalguksu offers a lighter, cleaner taste with a refreshing broth that’s equally impressive.

The cold spicy noodles (hoe bibim guksu) are made with chlorella noodles and have a well-balanced mix of sweet, spicy, and tangy flavors. The side of beef broth served with it is also excellent.

Portions are generous — almost like a double serving at other places — and they offer a free bowl of rice if you’re still hungry.

In my opinion, this is one of the best places for kalguksu and Korean noodles in Koreatown. Highly recommended for anyone craving authentic flavors and hearty portions.

For dessert, we enjoyed the “Coconut Mousse” and paired the meal with red wine and the “Land of the Sun” cocktail. The restaurant has an excellent selection of red, white, and sparkling wines.

The service was friendly and attentive without ever making us feel rushed.. We took our time, enjoyed the food, the drinks, and the stunning views, making it a memorable birthday celebration.

Manhatta has officially become one of my favorite restaurants of all time.

The experience starts with the stunning views from the 60th floor overlooking New York City, but the food and service are what truly make this place special. Every member of the staff was warm, knowledgeable, and attentive without ever being overbearing.

We ordered the four-course menu and every course was outstanding. For the first course, we had the Jonah Crab with asparagus, apple, and sorrel, along with the Bluefin Tuna with jicama, shiso, and white soy vinaigrette. The crab was honestly the best crab dish I’ve ever eaten—sweet, delicate, and perfectly balanced. The tuna was equally impressive, incredibly fresh and beautifully prepared.

For the second course, we chose the Seared Scallop with nduja, watermelon radish, and pea shoots, as well as the Glazed Sweetbreads with morel mushrooms, arugula pesto, and horseradish. Both dishes were expertly executed and packed with flavor.

For our mains, we had the Butter Poached Lobster and the Lamb Loin & Rib. The lobster was excellent, but the real surprise was the Koshihikari rice—it was absolutely amazing and one of the most memorable components of the entire meal. The lamb was perfectly cooked and paired wonderfully with the fava bean pesto, almond, and pecorino.

Dessert was the Pistachio Cake with strawberry and crème fraîche chamomile ice cream, which was a fantastic ending to the meal.

We also enjoyed several mezcal cocktails and wine pairings throughout dinner, all of which complemented the food beautifully.

Between the breathtaking views, exceptional service, creative menu, and unforgettable dishes, Manhatta delivered one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in NYC. Highly recommended, and I can’t wait to come back.

The entire experience was seamless. From checking in downstairs to guiding us to our table and everything in between. I think this is the highest server to patron ratio that I’ve ever seen. Commendable. The portion might be slightly on the smaller side, but the food was very delicious. And the view is simply unbeatable.

Definitely one of those places you leave already thinking about coming back. Highly recommend 💙💛5✨

OMG! Excellent new restaurant alert.  Papille Gustative in Santa Monica (Ocean Park.)  Now, you might think it is not new since technically they have been open for 5 years.  But not for dinner, and not with the current ownership and front of the house management.  I think they said they have been doing dinner about a couple of months or so. Chef is from Campanile, Mgr from Puglia.  It is a quaint little place, not hipster, very comfortable.  Nice big tables, quiet ambiance, very small but mighty menu.  Outdoor seating as well. They featured a special of Vitello tonnato and we have not had it that good since Piedmonte. A little pasta, some pizza, a couple of mains.  The Neapolitan pizza, OMG the best we have had since Italy.  I would go back from just this and the Caesar alone. The crust has the perfect chew, just the right crisp, marinara with incredible tomato flavor with just the right amount of acid.  It made Mozza look like Pizza Hut. The pastas were also delicious, not homemade "yet" but very high end and perfectly executed.  All ingredients are well-sourced and farm to table. The desserts brought us back to Italy -  wow we went to town. They were all very traditional, including one that had pistachio custard that was addicting.  They made us fresh Zepoles (fried dough.) This place is a diamond in the rough.  $30 corkage, wonderful service.  On Friday night when we were there it was empty as they are not doing enough marketing.  Please go and support them.

The pizza is incredible-very similar to what you eat in Italy. If you really want to taste something authentic, visit this place. I know that a change of ownership can sometimes create different expectations, but in this case, the change was for the better. The prices and service are good

My partner, mom, and I came here for lunch on a Thursday. Near full outside nice weather. Ivan was very kind, patient, and helpful as we had many questions on the menu. I always try to eat nutritious foods and this spot was great! My favorite was the rye bar trio appetizer. Thanks again!

The food was very delicious. Finally i had a good cup of coffee that is satisfying. The brunch plate is very flavorful in all aspects. And the signature french toast is truly a special!
Definitely coming back whenever in LA!

We had an amazing dinner at Papille. The pastas were great but the pizza really killed the show. It was very authentic food and the service was extremely friendly. Highly recommended!

Stopped here after a concert at Radio City Music Hall and was not disappointed. They have a late happy hour as well so that was a treat. Everything we ate was delicious, absolutely no complaints. You can order a pre fix burger or customize to your liking and pay per topping.

The wings? Yummy! They give you 6, which worked since it was the 3 of us.

If I’m ever in the area I’d definitely come back.

The service was great too. Friendly staff.

We didn’t have to wait to be seated. Not sure if it usually gets busy because they did ask us if we had a reservation which we didn’t. There’s indoor and outdoor seating but we sat indoors.

After spending a great day walking around Central Park, we stopped by Black Iron Burger, and it completely blew us away. Even though it's a new spot for me compared to some of my usual NYC standbys, the experience was head-and-shoulders above places I've been to multiple times.
First off, the service and atmosphere were wonderful. The restaurant is exceptionally well-decorated, creating a really cool, clean vibe—complete with nice, clean bathrooms, which is always a huge plus in the city. The staff was incredibly welcoming and accommodating. My friend, who was visiting New York for the first time with severe dietary restrictions, had no trouble at all; they were more than happy to accommodate her with a great bunless burger option.
As for the food, it was top-notch. My burger was ordered medium and cooked absolutely perfectly. The fries were great, and they have an excellent selection of sides and drinks to choose from.
Everything from the food to the service and the atmosphere was fantastic. I was so impressed with Black Iron Burger, and I would definitely go back to one of their locations in the city again!

Everything was very tasty!
Good meat, good fries, perfect beer!
Very nice service.

We’ve ordered:

• BURGERS:
- mushroom truffle burger ($16,95): 5-oz all natural beef, mushrooms, duxelles, Swiss cheese, bacon bits, truffle tapenade, carmelized onions, truffle mayo: sooooo tasty. Recommend it!
- the American burger ($19,95): double 4-oz all natural beef patty, American cheese, thick cut housemade smoked bacon, espresso BBQ sauce: very good, nice flavours.

• SALADS:
- black iron caesar salad ($10,50): romaine hearts, cherry tomatoes, garlic croutons, red onions, Parmesan cheese, black iron caesar dressing: this is very nice - especially with an extra chicken.

• SIDES:
- french fries - large ($7,50): gooood!😁

​★★★★★ Phenomenal hospitality, top-tier burgers, and unmatched speed!

​From the second we stepped inside, the hospitality at Black Iron Burger was extraordinary. Veronica welcomed us with a warm smile immediately—even while attending to another table—making sure we were acknowledged right away. We were seated within moments, and another team member brought fresh ice waters to our table right after. The entire staff operates like a well-oiled machine.

​Veronica took our order shortly after and walked us through the happy hour specials. For drinks, I ordered the Ibiza Mocktail (a refreshing blend of pineapple, orange, lemon, and club soda), and my partner chose the Malted Chocolate Shake, which was thick, creamy, and delicious.

​For food, we ordered:
​The American Burger: Two 4 oz. all-natural beef patties, melted American cheese, generous slabs of thick-cut housemade smoked bacon, and rich espresso BBQ sauce.

​Cod Fish Battered Burger: Crispy housemade beer-battered cod topped with fresh coleslaw, tomato, lettuce, and spicy cilantro mayo on a soft toasted bun.

​Loaded Fries with Black Iron Aioli: A huge, crispy platter loaded with savory bacon bits, fresh scallions, and creamy aioli.

​What impressed us most was how attentive the entire team was—no customer ever had to wait more than 30 seconds to be greeted or assisted. Truly five-star service and incredible food!

Go for a great burger! I don't care for sports bars, but Black Iron Burger rules! The staff is exceptionally and genuinely warm. So I felt welcome as I was greeted as soon as I walked in. The burger was exactly what I wanted. I left full. It was delicious and the world was beautiful. Prices are good for NY as well. Thank you Black Iron Burger. Delicious.

The burgers here were awesome. The drinks were even better and the vibes were so cool. We actually went to the city to go somewhere else and they ended up being closed so we ended up finding this little spot and we were hooked on the burgers. Can’t wait to go back

We discovered Black Iron Burger in the Theater District because of its excellent Google reviews, and it definitely lived up to the hype.

The restaurant is conveniently located right across from our hotel, so we made an online reservation. From the outside, it looks rather small and unassuming, but once inside, we were pleasantly surprised by how spacious it is and how stylishly it is decorated.

The service was outstanding from start to finish. We ordered a variety of burgers and salads, and everything was delicious. The food was fresh, served hot, and arrived quickly, with all dishes brought to the table at the same time.

What impressed us most was the exceptional attention to detail. One of our drinks clearly wasn't quite to our taste. Before we even mentioned anything, a staff member noticed and kindly offered us a replacement free of charge. That level of attentiveness was truly remarkable and made us feel very well looked after.

The handling of the tip was also professional and courteous throughout our visit.

Overall, we were extremely happy with our experience. Great food, excellent service, and a welcoming atmosphere. We would definitely return the next time we're in New York and highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a great burger in the Theater District.

If you want the real American experience, with Burgers (really nice with the Sourdough bread) like the Masterpiece or Fried Chicken and fries....this is the place. Clean, real US atmosphere, Soo many Screen to watch sports. Have fun

top_reviews.content: Food was really well made and tasty. We had the mussels for starter, cacio e pepe, beef pasta, lobster pasta and the wolf burger. The lobster pasta is a tad too spicy but still good. Everyone loved the mussels! Albeit I had initially expected the grilled octopus that had really good reviews but it wasn’t in the menu anymore. The atmosphere was laid back but still high end. Great for dates as well as family lunches. I personally loved the open kitchen, it added to the culinary experience and I wish had taken more pictures. Want to go back really bad.

We made a reservation for counter seating and didn’t realize it was basically the same as bar seating, since the reservation site listed bar seating and counter seating as separate sections. The woman at the front seemed a little cold at first, but she kindly accommodated us with an actual table for our party of three, which we appreciated.

The beer and cider were both cold and refreshing, and our waiter was very friendly throughout the meal. Most importantly, the food was absolutely delicious — every dish we ordered was amazing. Since we live only a few minutes from Nordstrom, we’ll definitely be coming back to try more items on the menu.

The only downside was that the food took a little longer than expected to come out, but overall we still had a great experience.

Need to kill some time while the wife shops at Nordstrom? Hit Wolf on the 2nd floor between the elevators. You can look out over 57th Street from the window while enjoying octopus 🐙 and beef tartare. The tagliatelle was delicious too. I wasn’t in the mood for alcohol but the bar looked good, if you are so inclined. Nice!

the restaurant was super chill and nice. the food was also amazing. we ordered the grilled octopus, arancini, tagliatelle, and the lemon donuts (desert). we finished everything and didn’t let anything go to waste. our waiter and the people working here are also just extremely nice in general. definitely recommend for those looking for a chill meal when visiting or staying in the area.

Wolf at Nordstrom was such a pleasant surprise! I started with the Hamachi Crudo, and it was incredibly fresh, flavorful, and beautifully plated. For my entrée, I had the salmon, which was cooked perfectly—moist, flaky, and seasoned just right. I couldn’t leave without trying the cheesecake for dessert, and I’m so glad I did. It was creamy, rich, and the perfect way to end the meal.

The highlight of my visit was the service. Jazmine was absolutely wonderful! She was friendly, attentive, and made excellent recommendations while making sure everything came out perfectly. Her positive attitude and attention to detail really elevated the entire dining experience.

If you’re shopping at Nordstrom or just looking for a great meal, I definitely recommend stopping by Wolf. Great food, excellent service, and an overall enjoyable experience. I’ll definitely be back!
Nice place to make a brake from long walk. Food was good , Aperol spritz was very good ( not in many places you can meet good Spritz) . Service was very good . Perfect view while you having lunch

We planned this trip to New York way in advance so we had to research the best places to eat etc. Wolf was by far the best restaurant we ate in - the food was beyond fantastic with bold flavors both indulging and refreshing at the same time. Traditional fare with a modern take and almost Californian flair so it didn’t feel heavy although we devoured a table full of dishes. The ambiance is modern minimal and elegant the service flawless but the food I will remember for a while because it was just that good. We will be sure to book again before we leave and will be sad to leave it when we go back to Thailand because it now has become one of my favorites places of all time.

Addition July 9 - we just had our second visit here for lunch instead and it was just as good as the first or even better. We had the opportunity to try the desserts as well as the lunch special halibut and it was superb!
Server was amazing and overall was a great meal. Good pasta, but gnocchi was by far the best.

I had an amazing experience at Au Za’atar Midtown! The food was absolutely delicious—everything was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, making it a great spot to relax and enjoy a meal.
What really stood out was the exceptional service. Kylie was our waiter, and he did a fantastic job—attentive, friendly, and made sure we had everything we needed throughout the meal.
Overall, a wonderful dining experience. I’ll definitely be coming back and highly recommend it to anyone looking for great food and top-notch service in NY

I had a great experience here. The vibes were really nice and the service was excellent, the staff kept checking on us and everything came out quickly. The food was phenomenal. We ordered the lamb kibbeh nayeh, and it was incredibly fresh and flavorful. The grilled cheese was also really good. We tried the grilled quail as well; the quail itself was tasty, though the rice wasn’t my favorite since I prefer the fluffy aromatic Middle Eastern style.

One small suggestion: it would be even better if the tables were spaced a bit farther apart for more comfort.

We were greeted immediately right when arrived to check in for our reservation then got seated right away. The decor and ambiance of this place is so beautiful.

The menu is a little overwhelming so I suggest taking a peak before arriving just to have an idea of what to get. If you’re adventurous just ask your server, they’re very knowledgeable and will guide you.

We ended up ordering:

Fatayer Fitter
Mezze Mix Spinner
Mixed Grill Platter

for 3 people it was more than enough and we had a bunch of leftovers to take home! We all enjoyed our meal here. The bartenders know how to mix up a delicious cocktail. The service was top notch - I love dining at places where the staff are very knowledgeable of the menu. It definitely makes a huge difference when dining in.

Trendy Lebanese restaurant in Midtown Manhattan. They went viral for their “tableside shawarma” which is carved in front of you with a whole presentation.

For starters we got the classic Hummus and the Zaatar manaeesh. They were both fantastic and served with various dips and pickles to accompany. The drinks were also solid, definitely worth getting the strawberry vimto if you like fruity and sweet. Mint lemonade is OG and a good choice.

We figured since we were there we should try this viral tableside shawarma experience. We opted to get the chicken shawarma. From a presentation perspective, it was a 10/10. Served with a mountain of sumac spiced fries, pita bread and the same dips and pickles (all unlimited and complimentary). The chicken was bland and super dry, not a fan.

Overall: 6/10

I have been to Au Za'atar in the East Village. A few weeks ago I went again with my family to celebrate my father's birthday. It was out 1st time at the Midtown East one and it did not disappoint. The food was delicious and our server, Hassan, was so awesome. He was very nice, very helpful and patient with us. He helped us with the menu and what was delicious to order. The restaurant was beautiful ! We ordered for starters, the Mezze & Dips Spinner (2 tiers). Wow, it was so delicious. We also ordered the Shawarma.  There was no kid options and my kid is a picky one. They were nice enough to make her some plain fries and she also had some naan bread. We will definitely go back again.
Love the atmosphere! The food is incredible! We sampled a lot of dishes that had so much flavor! Cocktails were great, too! Highly recommend!

A lebanese middle eastern cuisine my friend introduced me to, and it did not disappoint! They have a MASSIVE menu, but we ended up ordering the Fattet al betenjane (eggplant dip), Halloum mekli (fried cheese), and the baby lamb chops for 2 and was very full after.
Fattet al betenjane — dish that stood out the most and my fav! I dont even like eggplant, but trusted my friend on this one. You eat it with the pita bread and each bite is divine. There’s so much going on in that singular bite that’s it’s perfection to me. It’s a bit sour, but sweet from the cranberries, but also hints of crunchiness from the pita chips. I didnt want the bites to end.
Halloum mekli — def a good app if you love cheese! There’s cheese is on the firmer side so it was almost like eating firm tofu, but the garlic honey olive oil really compliments the dish. It’s not too sweet and the cheese is not too overpowering.

We visited on August 13th and enjoyed lunch at Coast and a bike ride from the hotel.
We have been traveling to Los Angeles from Japan for three consecutive years, and we have visited Coast and enjoyed the cycling experience every time. The atmosphere on Coast’s terrace is wonderful, and the lobster roll is absolutely delicious. We are always grateful for how friendly and welcoming the staff are, even though we are visitors from overseas.

Cycling along the beach and through the Venice Canals is always a fantastic experience. This time, we noticed that one of the bicycles was the same one our child had ridden when we first visited two years ago. We shared this nostalgic story with the staff at the reception.

After finishing another wonderful bike ride and returning the bicycles, we received such a warm and thoughtful gesture from the staff. They kindly told us, “You are our guest,” and made us feel truly welcome, even as visitors. It became one of the most heartwarming memories of our trip.

We combined a celebration of my mother's 85th birthday with dropping my son off for his freshman year of college into a weekend at Shutters.  We arranged for a private birthday party in the Coast Restaurant in the private dining room, and we also gathered the whole family together the next morning for breakfast in our room with room service. ||The rooms, the service, and the food were all exceptional, and the hotel staff very consistently went above and beyond for the event. ||I've been visiting this hotel on and off for more than thirty years since I first came to Los Angeles, and it's really impressive how well they've kept up the standards!

I would like to leave a review regarding an experience I had at your restaurant “Coast” on 5/25.

My mother reserved a table for three at 8:15 PM to celebrate my birthday. Not only was it my birthday, but it was also the first time in over 10 years that I was reunited with my aunt visiting from Brazil, whom I had not seen in a very long time. This dinner was meant to be a special and joyful occasion for our family.

The evening started beautifully. Our server, Lex, provided excellent service throughout the dinner. He was attentive, patient, caring, and professional. The food was also excellent, and initially we were truly enjoying our experience.

However, around approximately 9:30 PM, the music in the restaurant was suddenly turned off while we were still eating our main course. At that point, we realized we were the last table remaining in the restaurant. Shortly after, we began hearing staff loudly speaking, handling dishes noisily, and clearly beginning their closing procedures around us.

I politely mentioned to our server that it felt uncomfortable to have the music turned off while we were still dining. Lex immediately apologized and even kindly offered to turn the music back on. I told him it was alright and that we would simply finish quickly and leave. Despite that, he offered to bring over the manager. I honestly had no intention of escalating the situation, but the manager, Sofia, came to the table.

I calmly explained that we felt rushed and uncomfortable due to the complete absence of ambiance, the loud closing noises, and the overall feeling that the restaurant wanted us out before we had even finished our meal.

Unfortunately, Sofia’s response was deeply disappointing. Rather than apologizing or acknowledging our experience, she stated: “Turning off the music is part of my closing list. I need to send my staff home, they cannot stay.” Her tone and attitude came across as dismissive and argumentative rather than empathetic or service-oriented. The conversation became uncomfortable enough that I had to stop it myself.

What makes this even more upsetting is that my mother had specifically arranged for a birthday dessert to be brought to the table at the end of dinner. Instead, the desserts were simply packed into boxes to take home, completely removing the celebratory moment she had hoped to create for me.

Seeing my mother with tears in her eyes over what was supposed to be a happy family celebration was honestly heartbreaking.

I truly do not understand how a restaurant located within a five-star hotel can make guests feel like an inconvenience rather than a priority. Hospitality should never end before the guests leave the table. While I understand restaurants have closing procedures and staff schedules, there is a respectful and gracious way to handle those situations without making paying guests feel rushed out of the establishment.

I have personally worked in the hospitality industry for nearly 20 years, so I fully understand operational realities. This is not about staff wanting to go home, that is understandable. This is about the way the situation was handled and the complete lack of hospitality and empathy demonstrated by management.

I am extremely disappointed by the way Sofia treated us, and I cannot simply overlook this experience, especially because of how much it affected my mother during what should have been a meaningful evening for our family.

You are more than welcome to contact me privately should you wish to discuss this situation further. I am not someone who typically complains, but this experience genuinely left a lasting negative impression.
