top_reviews.content:
Celebrating my 50th birthday on April 1st at Tao was already special, but our host, Precious truly made it unforgettable. From the moment we were seated, she guided us through the menu with incredible knowledge and care—recommending standout dishes from appetizers all the way through dessert, along with perfect pairings that elevated the entire experience.

Every suggestion was spot-on, and you could tell she genuinely wanted us to have the best possible evening. What meant even more was her kindness and attention to detail—she took the time to capture beautiful photos of us.

Her professionalism, warmth, and thoughtful service went above and beyond. I highly recommend Precious to anyone looking for an exceptional dining experience. She made a milestone birthday truly extraordinary.

Delicious Lunch!

Came after work because i finished early. Around 3pm and what a great time! Didn’t know they had a lunch special so i got drinks from that menu. $15 for 3 mini martinis!! They were all DELICIOUS!! I tried the fried rice from the regular menu and it was absolutely delicious too. Only thing, it was extremely dark inside and extremely cold at the bar. Other than that it was great!

Ambiance (5/5): The establishment is extremely ornate and decorated in theme from top to bottom. I love how much detail and elegance they put to each room (not to mention the 16-foot buddha statue in the main dining room!) Be aware that the lighting is dim and the background noise is loud! The front bar room is so loud that you have to shout with your guest. Our party of 6 was seated in a tiny booth which we had to ask for an additional chair to accommodate us.
Service (5/5): We were able to get someone’s attention to order and we were refilled on water often. The food was organized by appetizers and entrees that arrive all at the same time. The wait between ordering and food felt reasonable to short. The waiter also specified that certain dishes quantity (i.e. potstickers) could be increased to accommodate our party size for an extra cost.
Food (5/5): TLDR; every dish was honestly SO good; I was surprised and will rank the items by ‘must get’ to skippable:
Short Rib Bao Bun (3 pc): The short rib was so tender and flavorful. The bao bun was soft. The sauce was thick and worked well with the short rib.
Pork Potstickers (5 pc): I preferred this over the lobster and scallion dumplings. The exterior skin is pan-fried with a nice glaze, hint of truffle. The bite was umami from the creaminess of the Parmigiano Reggiano.
Chicken Satay (3 pc): The 3 pieces of chicken were relatively large, very tender, seasoned well. They were well complemented with the peanut sauce that is worth keeping to dip into other things! Don’t sleep on the side of spicy cucumber salad, which was so well balanced in tartness and flavor.
Pad Thai: This is one of the best Pad Thai I’ve ever had! The flavors are bursting, with a balance of sweetness, nuttiness from the peanuts, and tartness from a squeeze of lime.
Peking Duck for 2: This dish is definitely more than enough for our party of 6 and appeared to be a half serving of the whole duck. The duck pieces are pre-cut for us to self-assemble into the wraps (not the usual bao bun but like thin tortilla wraps). I think I counted 8 wraps?
Triple Pork Fried Rice: The rice has a lot of depth and generous chunks of pork. The rice is thicker than regular jasmine with a more chew which I liked.
Dragon Tail Spare Ribs: Although this has a nice flavor, handling with your fingers makes them super sticky for your whole dining experience. The restaurant should give out wet towelettes if this dish is ordered!! Meat was tender and easy to chomp off the bone.
Tuna Tartare: A small quarter-sized tartare dollop is served atop a small cube bread. The fish was fresh, presentation was beautiful. Was hoping for more tartare for the price point but it was very good. Overall, the dish was not filling so would skip if the party is hungry.
Lobster and Scallop Dumplings: Great flavor with reasonable chunks of meat inside. Just preferred the potstickers a lot more!
Bok Choy: Pieces were chopped in half and cooked with a nice crunch. Topped with something that gave it more texture. The garlicy taste was forward (in a good way).
Rainbow Roll: While it was fresh and the individual pieces were large in portion, this felt like any other sushi roll. Skip this!
Side of White Rice is $9?! That’s theft and is skippable

The area features a well-maintained walking and cycling path, known as the Marvin Braude Bike Trail, which connects Santa Monica to other iconic coastal spots like Venice Beach. top_reviews.content:
5 Stars + I came here on a Saturday night to celebrate my birthday and my best friend’s birthday. I was a little unsure because of the location as it is in the "Shops at Columbus Circle", which is a small mall. It is next to one of the most prestigious hotels in New York, which is the Mandarin Oriental Hotel.

All I can say is "WOW"!!! I am not sure where the last person who wrote a review is living, under a rock, but everything was spectacular.
Yes, prices are not cheap, although where can you go in New York City and not spend $35 to $50 on a fish dish? If you go to a diner and eat frozen fish, you will pay for that. Our bill with a generous tip was still more than $100 less than I thought I would have spent. I thought prices were fair, especially considering the overall experience, and the location in Manhattan by Central Park.

Bad Roman is a beautiful, chic spot. It is nice to see a restaurant that is as well staffed as they are. Our service was great, even down to the runners who kept our water glasses filled, tables cleaned and wiped down and provided fresh silverware with every course.

From the minute we walked in I knew it was going to be great night. There were two people at the host station who greeted us with a smile, our hostess asked if our entire party was here, and was ok with some of them being a few minutes late, as they were looking for parking. They also asked if we were celebrating anything and we informed them it was for both our birthdays.

Once everyone was here, we were seated. My friend and I were handed an envelope. In it was a nicely written birthday card for each of us. I thought that was a nice touch!

The manager Isaac came over to thank us for coming and said something that will stay with me for a lifetime when thinking about business and restaurants in general. He said "Thank you for coming and for choosing us. You could have gone anywhere to celebrate your birthday and out of all the restaurants in NYC, you choose us". What that tells me is that he and the restaurant do not take us for granted. We were not a number, and the rest of the night proved that.

The restaurant is hip and modern; there is a beautiful bar as you walk in. The bathrooms were chic and clean. The tables were spaced out, and you can breathe, you are not on top of each other. As mentioned earlier, they are well staffed and everyone was great. Hat's off to Isaac who really made the night special. He came over several times and each conversation was meaningful. It was not idle conversation, we spoke for a few minutes about food, customer service, and you could see his passion for the customer.

Our waiter Roosevelt was also great; he made sure everything was perfect. When asked, he shared his opinion on his favorite dish as did Isaac when we were torn on the selection. I am sure both dishes would have been great although each recommendation was spot on.

Now to the food. We did not have a bad dish. Portions were satisfying, with great flavor and each was nicely presented. Here are some must have dishes. For appetizers, the Babka, Pepperoni cups, the Filet Mignon meatballs which can be a side dish or appetizer, the Black Truffle Ricotta, and the Peekytoe Crab Luigi, which has an amazing presentation. Favorite dessert was the Lemon Tartuffe Cheesecake, and the chocolate cake with gelato. Favorite entrees if we had to pick one were the Grilled Pork Chop.

They have nice mixed drinks, wine selection, liquor choice, and beers. They also have a great pasta dish selection, and I will try one the next time we come back.

For entrees we had the Faroe Island Salmon, the Grilled Pork Chop, and the Filet Mignon topped with Cacio E Pepe Raviolo which you must taste. Another favorite from Isaac is the Roasted Branzino.

I highly recommend Bad Roman, a big shoutout to all their employees who work extremely hard and will be back again. Bad Roman will be one of the restaurants I recommend when asked for a special place to go if you want to have a wonderful time.

This place totally lives up to the hype — and it’s the perfect spot for a birthday dinner. The vibes and atmosphere were absolutely on point: lively, beautiful, and just the right amount of celebratory. From the moment we sat down, the service was amazing — attentive without being overbearing, and everything felt really thoughtfully paced.

We started with the Whipped Ricotta with Black Truffle Honey, which was honestly unreal — creamy, rich, and the perfect balance of sweet and savory. The Spicy Gem Caesar had a great kick, and the Cappelletti Bistecca was incredible — super flavorful and perfectly done. Of course we had to add fries (because how could you not).

Then came dessert… and wow. The lemon cheesecake was light and bright, the blood orange sorbetto with whipped zabaglione was refreshing and delicious, and the funnel cake bites were dangerously good — warm, sweet, and impossible to stop eating.

Yes, it’s definitely on the pricier side, but for a special occasion it absolutely feels worth it. Great food, great energy, and the kind of place where a birthday dinner actually feels like a celebration. I’d happily go back — maybe just after mentally preparing my wallet first. 🎂✨

You pay for the experience here. The vibe and service are both fantastic. It’s hard to beat.

The food was good, but most of the dishes didn’t quite live up to the hype for me. The garlic babka was decent, though I wished it had more garlic and buttery flavor. The pappardelle with ragu was also solid but lacked the bold flavor I was expecting. The pepperoni cups with ranch were fun to try, but exactly what they sound like and probably not something I’d order again. The meatballs were fantastic!

The standout was the cheesecake served inside the white chocolate lemon mold. It was unique, delicious, and a perfect way to end the meal.

Overall, I’d recommend Bad Roman for the experience, service, and atmosphere. The food was good, but the ambiance was what really made the meal memorable.

Everything was absolutely wonderful from start to finish. The food was delicious, the service was attentive and welcoming, and the decor created such a beautiful atmosphere. Every detail felt thoughtfully done.

A special highlight was the lemon dessert, which was honestly one of the best desserts I’ve had in a long time. Perfectly balanced, fresh, and unforgettable.

Highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a great dining experience with excellent food, outstanding service, and a beautiful setting. Will definitely be coming back.

Traveling for work allows me the opportunity to try lots of restaurants.  Some of my co-workers and I ventured to Water Grill for dinner after a long day of being in a conference room.  We made the short walk to Water Grill for some seafood.

We started with chilled wild jumbo Mexican shrimp.  I also ordered a ½ pound of chilled mussels.  We also split a salad.  For my main I ordered the wild Ross Sea Chilean sea bass with butternut squash gnocchi and sage brown butter.  Two of my friends got the tagarashi seared bigeye tuna.  They said it was rather spicy probably since tagarashi means “seven flavor chili pepper.”  My other friend also ordered the sea bass but she got the gluten-free version which came with grilled vegetables.  We were too full to get dessert.  I know...shocking because I love dessert.  But fret not....I came back for Round 2 the next day.

Yes, I came back the next day for lunch after a serious power walk on the beach.   This time I came in for a late lunch and sat up at the bar.  I ordered the chilled mussels again, a bowl of the claim chowder and the jumbo lump crab cake.  I was hungry!  I also ordered the key lime pie to go.  The New England-style chowder was topped with a few little neck clams.  The crab cake had a little spicy kick to it but it wasn’t overpowering. It was a lot of crab meat and not a lot of filler, just the way I like it.  I had the key lime pie later and it had the right amount of tartness one expects in a key lime pie with a huge amount of meringue topping.

If you’re in the mood for seafood, I recommend Water Grill.  It also has a patio so you can enjoy the California coast line and the Pacifica Ocean.

I’ve been wanting to try Guisados for a while, and it definitely lived up to the hype. The food was absolutely delicious—it took me right back to Mexico City. Everything tastes homemade, and the mini tortillas are incredible. Easily one of the best spots in DTLA.

Guisados in Downtown LA may look unassuming from the outside, but it ended up being the best Mexican meal we had during our entire trip to the US. The moment the food arrived, it was clear this place focuses on quality above everything else.

Our server recommended it, and her suggestion was spot on. She provided excellent service throughout the meal, friendly, helpful, and clearly proud of the food they serve.

This spot is a true gem, and I would recommend it wholeheartedly to anyone visiting Downtown LA.

Stopped by Guisados on Spring and I’m already planning my next visit. The tacos are legit — rich, slow-cooked flavors on soft, handmade tortillas. I had vegan tacos, steak picado, cochinita, chorizo tacos and every one was fire.

We started with the appetizers, and the duck hummus was the star of the night. It was so unbelievably good that we ordered a second one. For the main course, every dish was outstanding. The crispy quail had an incredible crunch while remaining tender and juicy. The lamb neck literally melted in your mouth and was one of the most memorable dishes of the evening. The bone-in ribeye was cooked perfectly, with a beautiful crust, rich marbling, and deep, beefy flavor that made it ideal for sharing. The grilled shrimp were large, fresh, and perfectly seasoned with just the right amount of char, complementing the other dishes without overpowering them.

Dessert was the perfect ending to the evening. The sticky date cake was warm, rich, and paired beautifully with the ice cream. The pavlova was light and airy with fresh berries that balanced the sweetness perfectly. We also had the warm chocolate-filled doughnuts with caramel ice cream, which were decadent, indulgent, and impossible not to love. This is my honest experience, and it’s not just about “personal taste.” I went to Bavel in Los Angeles with my husband because so many people recommended it, so my expectations were honestly pretty high. But the meal ended up being so upsetting that I almost cried at the restaurant, and I felt nauseous even after getting back to the hotel.

First, the overall charges already left a bad impression. Valet parking was listed as $13, but since it was cash payment and they didn’t provide change, we ended up paying $15. The bill also had the usual suggested minimum tip of 20% and around 10% tax, which I understand. But there was also an additional 4% employee health / wellness fee. I’m not saying a restaurant can’t charge that, but when the dining experience itself was already so disappointing, all these extra charges made the whole experience feel even worse.

We ordered four dishes.

The first dish was the hummus with duck ‘nduja. The sauce itself was okay, nothing too bad, but the bread served with it was honestly very hard for me to accept. It tasted overwhelmingly like flour, with no real aroma or satisfying texture. After eating it, that raw flour-like taste stayed in my mouth, and every time I saw the bread being baked nearby, I kept thinking about that taste and felt nauseous.

The second dish was the mushroom dish, around $28. For that price, I really couldn’t understand the flavor or value. It tasted like very ordinary grilled mushrooms to me, without the depth or quality I would expect from a restaurant at this price point.

The third dish was the shrimp, around $30. The flavor itself was average, not terrible, but what really ruined the meal for me was that the shrimp did not seem to be properly cleaned. While eating, I found a thick, visible black vein / digestive tract inside the shrimp. The moment I saw it after biting into it, I felt instantly nauseous. I was so disgusted in the moment that I didn’t take a photo, which I honestly regret now, but my husband was there with me and we still have the receipt.

The last dish was the $65 beef. Because the shrimp had already made me feel physically sick, I couldn’t eat a single bite of it.

I understand that everyone has different tastes, and I know many people like this restaurant. But for me, the overall experience, from the charges, to the food, to the way the shrimp was prepared, was extremely disappointing. The shrimp issue was not just a matter of preference. It made me genuinely uncomfortable and physically nauseous.

If you’re planning to go to Bavel, I would at least suggest going in with realistic expectations. Not every highly recommended or trendy restaurant is necessarily worth it for everyone.

The way it was presented made it look more like an optional add on or side charge rather than an extra charge for choosing that steak. It was really easy to miss, and no one mentioned the extra charges when we ordered. For a set menu, this should have been made much clearer.

The food was also disappointing. There was grit and sand in the salad, and the shrimp had a really strong fishy smell and did not taste fresh. The steak was extremely undercooked. The center was basically raw and the meat was very difficult to chew.

The chocolate cake also had a noticeable refrigerator taste, like it had been sitting in the fridge for a while.

Our final bill for four people ended up being over $500. For that price, the quality of the food and the overall experience were nowhere near what we expected. Completely not worth the money and we definitely would not come back.

I had the most amazing bread I’ve ever eaten .. honestly enough to make me want to come sit at the bar just for cocktails and bread alone. We had the wagyu flight and the 60-day dry-aged steak, and every single bite was unbelievable. The quality, presentation, and attention to detail throughout the entire meal made it feel like such a special dining experience.

The ambience was warm, upscale, and inviting without feeling pretentious, and the service from Valentina was absolutely phenomenal. She was knowledgeable, attentive, and made us feel genuinely taken care of from start to finish. It’s rare to find a place where the food, atmosphere, and service all exceed expectations, but this absolutely did. Already looking forward to my next visit.

Dinner at Meat On Ocean really delivered on every front. The dry-aged steak came out pre-sliced and smothered in melting herb butter, packing an incredible crust and that deep, concentrated richness you only get from serious aging. The seafood held its own just as well—the Chilean sea bass had a gorgeous golden sear with huge, buttery flakes over braised red cabbage, while the salmon nailed that elusive combination of paper-crisp skin and a juicy, flaky center. Even the lamb chops were a standout, perfectly charred on the outside with a tender, smoky pink bite paired with wild mushrooms. Paired with grilled asparagus, cheesy roasted cauliflower, and a warm, caramel-drenched bread pudding with melting vanilla ice cream to wrap things up, it was easily one of those meals where practically every dish was a hit.

I came here to celebrate my niece/nephew’s and my dad’s birthdays, and we had a really enjoyable experience.

Justin was an amazing server. He explained the menu in detail and gave us some great recommendations that we were very happy with. The atmosphere was also wonderful, especially with the beautiful view overlooking Santa Monica Beach.

We ordered several dishes:

• Clam Chowder Bowl – Savory, rich, and creamy. The soup had a nice thick consistency and was very flavorful.

• Wagyu Gold Filet Mignon, 6 oz & 8 oz – My parents felt these were a little too salty. It seemed like there may have been a bit too much sea salt sprinkled on top.

• 45-Day Dry-Aged T-Bone & 45-Day Dry-Aged Porterhouse – These were definitely my favorites! Both steaks were juicy, tender, and cooked beautifully. The portion sizes were also very generous and satisfying.

• Mashed Potatoes – A perfect side for the steaks. The flavor was mild and not too heavy, so it balanced the richness of the meat really well.

• Asparagus – Nicely tender and savory.

• Sautéed Mushrooms – Another favorite of mine. They were aromatic, flavorful, and had a great texture.

Overall, I really enjoyed this steakhouse. The food was delicious, the service was excellent, and the oceanfront atmosphere made our birthday celebration even more special. I would definitely come back!

The service was great. Our server gave us a lot of good recommendations. We had the mushrooms, asparagus, and macaroni for sides and they were all amazing. The wagu sampler was incredible. I had it rare and it melts in your mouth. Absolutely recommend

A great variety of wines and aged meat, with a western interior design. Portions are quite big for one person. Located next to the public parking. If you avoid the rush hours you will have a nice ocean view. Loved their pistachio creme Brule.

Very good. Expensive but great views. CJ at the bar is super friendly and on top of it.

Got the 60 day aged ribeye. It was very good. Little undercooked first go round but they fixed it quickly and gave me some more wine for the mistake. Mushrooms were good. Wine is reasonably priced.

I think POTS has great potential and I 100 percent support its role in our community, especially, since when I fell on hard times, they were there for me. But I have to be honest because I'm here to move humanity forward, not keep us where we've been. There's room for improvement.

Right now The Bronx is SUFFERING. Badly. I'm not sure where everyone's heads are, but our people are so physically unfit, unwell and unhealthy that many of them have literal mobility issues and cannot even walk without an assistive device, or a vehicle to get them from place to place. And that's just nowhere to live. While food is one of the most wonderful parts of life, I fear it is all many people know/prioritize. We've turned something that should be used for fuel and pleasure into a coping mechanism and anxiety crutch.

With that being said, I do believe POTS can be more intentional about the food that is being served. Yesterday I saw that the food pantry cans being given out were busted all over, and as I recently acquired my food handler's license, I've learned that that can actually be a major hazard. Not only that, but a lot of what gets given out is carb + white sugar heavy. Again, I 100 percent support us being here for our community. What I advocate is doing more than the bare minimum.

The majority of the people who show up for meals and pantry items are users of substances and people in shelters, which likely means that they experience symptoms of mental illness. Either way, that doesn't exclude them from deserving the highest quality of care. A famous mural in the Bronx quotes "no one is free until everyone is free" which means that if anyone of us is falling behind, we all are. Especially as a community. Our people (including the workers at Pots and any living being really) need high quality, nutrient dense meals. With a little persuasion to the government (I'd be more than happy to help) we can make that happen. Supplements, check ups from nurses/PAs (they can even be volunteers just like our kitchen helpers), so we know what's going on with our community's bodies. We need to take back control and charge by ensuring that no one is getting left behind. I think POTS should strive to do more than just provide basic hot meals. I think it should strive to change lives. To get more people off the streets, more importantly off drugs and having healthy, stable bodies again. Many farms would be happy to donate fresh/organic produce if they knew it was for a cause. If they knew it was for the chance to change a life. These are the kinds of things that are inspirational, and these are the kinds of things that make a difference in the community.

That brings me to another important thing. White sugar, the juice that was served the last couple of days that I was there was a grape juice highly concentrated in sugar. I understand that we often try to cut back on spending, but have we ever stopped to ask just how expensive it is to be cheap? By opting for higher sugar content materials, we are creating even more problems. Our people are more likely to become dehydrated. And worse, white sugar is one of, if not the, most addictive substances on the planet. When the brain gets it, it wants more. But it doesn't actually like it, it crashes out. This negative feedback loop creates the need to fill the void, and this is where our folks then fill that void with their drugs of choice. Drug use is not cute, and is far too casual and widely accepted in NYC. It's as if no one cares. What good is a free meal or free items if they're not actually doing anything to improve that person's life.

There is a liquor store right next to POTS that I see people stumbling in and out of all the time, regardless of time of day and not only is it not a good sight, it's uninspiring and worst of all, it sends a terrible message to our kids that this is normal.

This is why I believe POTS should use lunchtime to inform our clients of the cruciality of healthy living, healthy choices and what they should do in and out of the center. Not just provide a quick meal.

top_reviews.content: The food was pretty good! We ordered the shrimp, tuna, flatbread, and french onion soup as starters. I always enjoy coming to La Monde. Such a great spot for any time of day, especially brunch. This time I tried the steak from the graduation menu and it was so good — juicy, flavorful, and cooked perfectly.

Also have to mention our server Kara, who is always so kind and welcoming. She remembers us every time we come, which makes the experience feel even more special. Love this place and will definitely keep coming back.

My friend and I randomly walked in on a Wednesday during our break from work. We met up and stopped by a few places, trying to find the right atmosphere that matched our moods. Le Monde provided a sweet ambience that allowed us to enjoy our meal. It was also restaurant week, so we had a three course meal. Since we weren’t familiar with French cuisine, our wonderful server Sofia guided us through the menu. Everything was delicious. The fresh salad with goat cheese (fried) on top was incredible.  The coq au vins and the panna cotta that followed was also exquisite. By the time my friend and I left, we decided to make a reservation. Same day, same time. It’s our new favorite spot that will now become our tradition. You absolutely must go.

Our server Luis was very knowledgeable of the menu. He was able to recommend great selections for food and drinks. For appetizers we had the Shrimp, Prosciutto Flatbread and Escargots. For entrees we had the Short Rib, Mussels, and Chicken Cordon Bleu. Dessert was Creme Brûlée and Crepe Nutella. We enjoyed everything!! Wonderful service!! Fresh bread made in house. Tasty cocktails!!

This was our third visit to Le Monde, and once again, it exceeded our expectations. We absolutely love their steaks, which come with a side of salad and French fries. You can choose between two sauces — pepper or cheese — and honestly, both are delicious. The portions are generous, making it a truly satisfying meal.

For starters, we had the Caesar salad served with fish, which was fresh and flavorful. For dessert, I enjoyed the panna cotta, which was perfectly creamy, along with a rich brownie and some delightful ice cream. We also had tea, and the presentation of the tea sets was charming and unique.

It was my brother’s birthday, and the staff made it extra special — they put a candle on the brownie, didn’t charge us for it, and even gave my brother a birthday card. The warmth and friendliness of the staff really stood out, making the whole experience memorable.

The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating, and the atmosphere is cozy and welcoming. Overall, everything from the food to the service was fantastic. I highly recommend Le Monde — it’s definitely a place worth visiting!

top_reviews.content:
If you’re just looking for a quick bowl of ramen, there are plenty of places in New York City. But if you’re a true ramen lover, IPPUDO Westside should definitely be on your list.
I’ve been to several IPPUDO locations over the years, and this one certainly didn’t disappoint. The rich tonkotsu broth, perfectly cooked noodles, and tender chashu pork were exactly what I expect from the IPPUDO brand. Every bowl is consistently delicious, which is why I keep coming back whenever I visit a city with an IPPUDO.
The restaurant has a lively atmosphere, friendly service, and even though it’s popular, it’s well worth the wait. Founded in Fukuoka, Japan in 1985, IPPUDO helped introduce authentic tonkotsu ramen to New York when it opened its first U.S. location in Manhattan in 2008, and it has remained one of the city’s iconic ramen destinations ever since. (Ippudo US)
If you’re serious about ramen, this isn’t just another restaurant you happen to pass by—it’s a destination that’s worth seeking out. Highly recommended!

A dear friend of ours, who has lived in New York for many years, suggested IPPUDO after sharing how it had become a tradition to bring his family here, and for good reason. Everything here is absolutely phenomenal. IPPUDO makes their noodles and broth on site, and those details make all the difference. The ambience is relaxed and inviting. A great way to enjoy a great meal at your pace.

We showed for lunch on a Monday afternoon, and were seated and served very quickly.  Our server was very engaged, and took good care of us. For starters we had the edamame and pork buns. The edamame was wonderfully garlicky, and the pork buns were simply bite sized pieces of joy between two doughy pillows. As a main meal, I ordered the Karaka Spicy ramen. It had the perfect amount of spice, and extra noodles were complimentary. I had mine with a poached egg, which blended in seamlessly with all the savory textures and flavors. While the bowl seemed almost overwhelmingly large, it was easy to enjoy in full because of how delicious it was.

I've had a fair share of ramen dishes, and IPPUDO is right up there with the best.

Atmosphere was nice and felt comforting after a long day in NYC, while it was busy, the server sat our party of 5 with no reservation right away and was quick to bring our appetizers & entrees which was greatly appreciated! Been to this restaurant many times, including their NYC locations and Tokyo. All have been fantastic. I love their spicy ramen. Right now they have an offer that includes 1 round of free kaedama (refill of noodles). Definitely recommend if you are looking for a good ramen spot in the city.

Had a good time dining in here on a weekend. The ambience was good, quiet and peaceful. The service was great with the food being served quickly and also the staff checking for any allergies.

We had the Spicy Gyoza appetizer, Karaka Spicy, Yuzu Shoyu, and Spicy Tuna Roll. Everything was phenomenal!  We came a little early for dinner (around 4:20), and were seated immediately. The service was great and all three servers were attentive and gracious. Can’t wait to come back.

top_reviews.content: This park is pretty crazy. There are a bunch of boisterous youth being loud and obnoxious. If you walk over to the bay to try to get away from the noisy and disagreeable youth, be ready for a crazy amount of litter. Is there a beach? Egh, kind of. It has some unique features too. Not only broken glass on the beach, but partial bottles even. Large, like, composite plates that cut your hand when you try to move them, and buoys, and other things washing up on the shore. Last time I was there, there was an abandoned camp site complete with a stroller even. While the ocean isn't really welcoming, if you're looking to live on the edge, you can walk out into the extremely murky water and try not to get tetanus by stepping on a large piece of metal embedded in the ground. The cautiousness may prepare you for the walk back to the car, or wherever else you are going. Don't bother reporting it to the city. They basically come back and say, "What? This, is, the, way, I live. Nothing wrong with the way it is." Craziness.

Great park! It's peaceful, clean and beautiful. You do have to pay for parking though, $10 if you are not a resident or have a park pass. I don't think it's a big deal, worth it, but some of my friends hate it when visiting on a regular.
Love this park!

Came for a long weekend walk with the dog (leash rules apply). Wooded sections feel almost suburban-rural compared with Central Park. Signage is okay if you glance at a map first. Pack water and a snack; concessions aren't everywhere. One of the better 'get out of the density' options in the city.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
A Perfect Family Day at Pelham Bay Park!

We had such a beautiful day at Pelham Bay Park with the whole family! It’s truly a hidden gem in New York City — peaceful, spacious, and full of natural beauty. From wide open green spaces to scenic walking trails and picnic spots, the park offered something for everyone.

The kids had a blast running around, and we enjoyed a relaxing stroll while soaking in the fresh air and calm atmosphere. It was the perfect place to unwind and spend quality time together.

Whether you’re planning a quiet afternoon, a family picnic, or just want to escape the city noise for a while, Pelham Bay Park is a fantastic choice. Can’t wait to come back!
Great location for BBQ or Bdays. Grills will be taken but you can rent one if needed!

If you thought Central Park was big, you need to come to this park immediately. With a large track and field area that puts Soundview Park's to shame, easy accessibility from the 6 train, free parking, a bunch of pathways to walk along and enjoy the sights (especially now that it's Autumn), a few nice statues to look at, a big playground, a number of different sports courts, and a bunch of areas to sit down and have a barbecue with your family and friends. Great views of the water and city skyline as well, especially a bit closer to nighttime. You can't even see all of the park in one day unless you wanna challenge yourself. Not only that, I felt very safe during my walk through the park, and others that I've encountered have been quite friendly. 10/10 park and highly recommend it.

My only other critique is that the food came out extremely fast. We never felt rushed by the staff, but every course arrived almost immediately after the previous one. For a high-end dining experience, I would have preferred a little more time between courses to enjoy the meal and atmosphere.
Overall, everything was very good, and despite those minor criticisms, I would definitely come back.

name: Shoreside Restaurant and Bar
address: 1515 Ocean Ave, Santa Monica, CA 90401, United States

top_reviews.content:
So first of all let's thank The Misfit down the street for closing down their patio, since that's how we came to be at this gorgeous, high-quality outdoor restaurant for the first time. My partner's parents had offered to fund a nice gift dinner for us, and when our first plan fell through, we set to furiously searching for the perfect steak.

Fortunately, this great little spot absolutely made our night. It's a beautiful glass-walled garden with sofas and chairs and heaters: all the upsides of outdoor dining with none of the downsides.

We started by splitting a salad and a drink, and the staff separated them as a courtesy without being asked. The salad was quite decent in size and construction. The drink got us both pretty sozzled - very generous pour!

Then came the entrees and sides. My partner had the coffee-rubbed ribeye, and I had the salmon, and we shared each other pieces. Both were *amazing*.

Now, some background. I was raised vegetarian, & still eat less meat than average. I don't normally share my partner's taste for beef, but I'll try a bite now and again, and usually just become satisfied that I know my tastes well enough.

This is possibly the first & only time in my life that I've eaten a bite of steak and thought, "I could eat this whole thing. Gosh, wow, I *want* to eat this whole thing." It was juicy and flavorful and a delicate medium-rare texture. I now understand the appeal of steak in a way that I never did before today.

Fortunately, my salmon was also delicious, a generous portion, perfectly cooked, buttery-soft and hearty, with a mild flavor. And all the sides - broccolini, carrots, fingerling potatoes, black rice, an add-on of sautéed mushrooms - were also expertly crafted, and well portioned. So I didn't have to beg my partner for scraps of ribeye like the human golden retriever I am.

Now, I should also mention, she is a truly expert steak connoisseur as only a tiny anemic woman can be, having consumed hundreds of steak dinners over her lifetime. And *she* says it was among the top tier of steaks *she'd* ever had.

We finished off by sharing a perfectly pulled double espresso, to balance out the alcohol.

The staff were all very kind, communicative, and solicitous - I didn't catch everyone's name, but our server was Lily and she was fantastic.

Everyone was knowledgeable and responsive about our allergy concerns, so we had a great, celiac-safe, gluten-free dinner, with many options available. I would score this restaurant very highly on allergy friendliness. The atmosphere was good, and the warm, comfortable seating area was easily in the top tier of patios I've seen. We'll definitely be back.

Josh and Raul were so accommodating!!! The customer service is truly unmatched. It was truly a phenomenal experience. The food, drinks, vibe, views was amazing!!!! Be sure to try the seared tuna sandwich, and the Half Chicken meal, and ask for Josh and Raul!!  You’re guaranteed to enjoy!

Had a wonderful breakfast experience here. The food was really good, the service was very accommodating and kind, the vibe was great, and most importantly - the coffee was really good. Ordered avocado toast and added salmon and poached eggs, as well as waffles for the kids. The ingredients were high quality and very fresh. Highly recommended spot for breakfast right near Santa Monica Pier.

Really lovely place for breakfast! Would really recommend the breakfast wrap it was so fresh! Rafael was lovely and made sure we always had drinks! Thank you all.

Stephanie was an amazing server at Shoreside Restaurant! She was friendly, attentive, and made sure everything was perfect throughout our meal. She had a great attitude, checked on us regularly without being intrusive, and provided excellent customer service. Her positive energy and professionalism made our dining experience even more enjoyable. Thank you, Stephanie, for making our visit so memorable. We will definitely be back!

Excellent choice as our original plan was derailed. Our server Owen was awesome! All of our dishes were delicious, we cleaned our plates. Drinks were nice and sophisticated. Highly recommend Shoreside!

I didn’t think anything could make The Shore better than it is. I was so wrong!  This new restaurant is the cherry on the sundae!
We’ve been regular visitors to The Shore for years, so we knew the restaurant upgrade was in the works.  It totally exceeded our expectations!  It’s incredibly inviting from the street as well as the hotel lobby; the food, service and ambience live up to that invitation in every way.
The food is delicious, clearly there is an accomplished and imaginative chef on the premises.  From breakfast to dinner, with lunch and snacks available along the way this gem has you covered! I will say that I miss the previous version of the French Toast but breakfast overall is really, really good. Lots of great dinner choices, all prepared very well. Save room for dessert, every option is a worthy indulgence – yes, I have tried them all!
One last, and important comment: like the hotel itself, the service here is exemplary.  Raul just may be the greatest Food and Beverage Manager in the city, and his team will take very, very good care of you.

top_reviews.content:
After a long, wonderful day exploring LACMA and Hollywood, my friends and I wanted to end our last evening in LA on a high note—and BCD seemed like the perfect spot for our first authentic Korean dining experience. We arrived around 11 PM, ready for a feast, but immediately noticed a long line of guests waiting outside.

We put our name down and settled in for a 30-minute wait. While standing there, I couldn't help but notice that a significant portion of the restaurant sat empty, with used dishes still left uncleared from earlier seating. I totally understand that closing off a section might be due to a short-staffed kitchen or closing procedures (especially that late!), but it was a bit puzzling to see such a long queue out front while tables sat uncleaned and unused inside. A little transparency or a quick heads-up from the hostess would have gone a long way.

That said, once we were finally seated, the food completely made up for it! We ordered quite the feast—the LA Galbi Combo, Spicy Pork Bulgogi, and Chicken Teriyaki Combo. Every dish came with generous sides of Soon Tofu Soup, Hot Pot Rice, and a beautiful array of traditional Korean banchan. The flavors were rich, comforting, and absolutely worth the hype for a first-timer like me.

Overall, the meal itself was fantastic, and the service after we sat down was efficient. Just be prepared for a potential wait if you're coming late at night, even if the restaurant looks partially empty—hopefully, they can work on clearing tables faster to reduce that bottleneck. Would still recommend for the delicious food!

Visited BCD Tofu House in LA Koreatown, and this place is basically a must-visit if you’re craving authentic Korean food.

The soft tofu stew (soondubu) is the star here — rich, spicy, and full of flavor. It comes out boiling hot, and you can really customize the spice level and ingredients to your taste.

What I really liked is the side dishes (banchan). They keep refilling them, and the quality is solid across the board. The fried fish that comes with the meal is also a nice bonus.

The place is open late (some locations are even 24 hours), so it’s perfect for late-night meals or after drinks. That’s probably why it’s always busy.

The vibe is casual and a bit hectic, but that’s part of the experience. Service is fast and efficient.

Overall, if you want a real Korean dining experience in LA, this place delivers. Simple, satisfying, and consistently good.

​The French Toast: Decadent, golden, and melt-in-your-mouth tender. It hits the exact right balance of sweet and indulgent without feeling overly heavy.
​The beverage game here is just as strong:
​Bloody Marys: Bold, perfectly spiced, and served with just the right kick to kick off the morning.

I recently stopped by Grand Central Market and it’s one of those places that just feels alive the second you walk in. The energy is hard to miss—busy, loud, and full of people from all walks of life grabbing a bite. It’s not fancy, but that’s exactly the appeal.

What I like most is the variety. You’ve got everything from tacos and BBQ to ramen and fresh pastries all under one roof. It’s perfect if you’re with a group and everyone wants something different. I tried a couple different vendors, and everything was fresh and packed with flavor. You can tell a lot of these spots take pride in what they’re serving.
Seating can be a bit of a challenge, especially during peak hours, so don’t expect a quiet, relaxed meal. It’s more of a grab-your-food-and-find-a-spot kind of place. But honestly, that’s part of the experience. It feels authentic and unpolished in a good way.

Prices are reasonable considering the quality and the location in downtown L.A. It’s also a great place to just wander, try something new, and maybe step outside your comfort zone a bit.

Overall, I’d definitely go back. It’s not about a single restaurant—it’s about the whole experience. If you enjoy food halls with character and great variety, this place is worth the visit.

If you are going to visit Downtown LA you can't miss stopping by Grand Central Market. The energy is unmatched, though navigating the crowds and choosing where to eat can be a bit overwhelming.
​We decided to try Villa’s Tacos, and it was hands-down the best decision. Their “maximalist” style of taco is so unique—the combination of the thick blue corn masa tortilla, the molten Monterey Jack cheese skirt, fresh guac, and cotija cheese is incredible. Every ingredient tastes high-quality and fresh.
​Tip: The market gets incredibly busy on weekends, be prepared to hunt for parking and wait in a bit of a line at Villa's—but it moves fast and is 100% worth it.

Food: there is any food you can imagine here, and it’s all extremely good. We walked around for a few minutes to see what there was, and I ended up getting a pupusa and two empanadas. Both were delicious, but a special shout out to the pupusas. They are fresh, handmade, and you can watch the staff stuff the filling into the dough and put it on the grill. So much flavor in those things, I love it.

Service: it did take a while to get my pupusa, but that said, it was one of the more popular restaurants in the market. Worth the wait in my opinion. Be prepared to wait a while anywhere you eat, especially if it’s crowded.

Atmosphere: this is the best part of the market!! A perfect LA experience for those visiting. There is seating everywhere across the market, but it fills up super quickly since there are so many people in there.

We had vouchers to use at Grand Central Market, and we were so glad we did! There are so many food options, which made it perfect for our large group with a variety of dietary restrictions. Everyone was able to find something they enjoyed.

I highly recommend the lobster roll — it was absolutely delicious. If you’re on a budget, the $5 tacos are a fantastic deal and honestly more than enough for a full meal. The donuts were amazing, the smoothies were just as delicious, and the wine vendors were wonderful. Since we weren’t able to receive change back on our vouchers, they were kind enough to top off our glasses, which we truly appreciated.

We had a large crowd with lots of vouchers, and every vendor we interacted with was incredibly patient and friendly. The overall experience was welcoming and enjoyable from start to finish.

If we’re ever back in the area, we will definitely make sure to get vouchers again. I highly recommend this place if you’re looking for a great variety of food options in one spot!

I have mixed feelings about The Smith, but three stars feels fair — maybe even a touch generous. We booked a table for eight for a family brunch to celebrate my wife’s 40th, so expectations were (understandably) high.

Let’s start with what they absolutely get right. The ambiance is fantastic — very 1920s, F. Scott Fitzgerald energy — and it works. The interior design team clearly put serious thought into creating something transportive and polished. It feels intentional, not accidental.

The cocktails? Genuinely phenomenal. The Oaxacan Sunshine was a standout — bright, balanced, and memorable. My wife’s Frozen Pool Party tasted like something straight out of a Death & Co. mixology finals round. Creative, refined, and just plain fun.

The food was also impressive. The menu strikes a nice balance between healthier options and indulgent brunch staples, and everything we ordered delivered both in flavor and presentation.

Which is why it’s frustrating to say the service didn’t live up to the rest of the experience.

We were seated at a table set with visibly dirty dishes — traces of butter still on the plates. I quietly mentioned it to the server. He inspected them, said nothing, removed them… and never brought replacements or acknowledged the miss. No quick apology, no “we’ll fix that right away,” nothing.

It made me wonder how dishes leave the kitchen that way, washed by one person, set by another, without anyone noticing. It felt either like a simple mistake or a breakdown in attention to detail. And on a milestone birthday brunch, that lack of care stands out.

The Smith has the atmosphere, the drinks, and the food to be exceptional. I just wish the service matched the level of everything else.

At least the staff working at the small bar upstairs, where guests are asked to wait, were friendly. There was only one girl working alone behind a bar full of people. Bill's Hamburgers in Van Nuys has been open since 1965 on a quiet, industrial-leaning part of Oxnard where they serve American classics, hamburgers, cheeseburgers, hot dogs, sandwiches, breakfast items and chili. It's a cash-only business so make sure you bring some cash with you.

Bill's is one of those kinds of local spots where the 'ones in the know' will rave about and for good reason. They have a decent sized menu but I had heard many times over the years that their burgers are the way to go. While I was waiting for my order, I heard regulars ordering other items so it is safe to assume there is more to love than their hamburgers. I'd like to go back and try their breakfast sandwiches.

The burgers I had were delicious. There is an art in perfecting a menu and Bill's has achieved just such a perfection with his sixty years in business! The burgers were very well cooked, well seasoned, had nice crispy edges, and were extremely tasty.

The prices are still quite affordable. The service was quick and efficient for my visit. I would recommend you find street parking. The burger shack has a large parking lot next door but there are multiple signs warning Bill's guests from using the parking.

I also loved how cozy and personal the setting felt. While they don't have seating, they do have some bar counters outside. I took my burgers to my car. I loved the ramshackle shack look of their restaurant and the no-frills, effortlessly tasty food on their menu.

I recognize that Bill is set to retire or maybe he already has. But his legacy and his classic American menu will live on as long as there are people who care about quality food at good prices. They are worth the visit!

There are no tables. There is a bar you can stand at if you want but most people just took it to their cars.

The words classic, vintage, old school and no frills come to mind when describing Bills Burgers!

Probably one of the most consistent burger stands in California. Having grace this small stand for a decade, I can say this is one of my favorite burger joints.

This family business starts with Bill, who is currently retired but is seen around the stand premise. I recently had a pleasant conversation with this legend. Bill told me his back story and how he has been grilling burgers at this location for 35 years. Can you imagine all that seasoning on that grill throughout the decades. Bill is now 97 and I was honored to listen to him while I waited for my order. His wife (sorry I don’t know her name) and her son Douglas have taken reigns and they haven’t missed a beat. The legacy continues!

I absolutely love this place. My go to is the triple cheese with bacon and a side of lay chips. The patties are thin and seasoned well, with gooey American cheese, a nice soft bun with veggies and homemade sauce. The bacon is legit. You will get burger juice all over yourself as you bite into this heavenly sandwich.

I will keep coming here til they close. Thankful for Bill and his family. Great business to support.

Then I tried other day in August, around lunch hour. Waited 10 minutes to order and 35 minutes to get a cheeseburger.

The burger was good. Maybe nostalgic to some. The thin patty was well-done and well-crusted. It's weird to say, but it seems almost precursor of smash burger.

To me it was an hour round trip on top of the 45 minutes at the stand. I'm glad that I've tried, but I'm not sure if I want to come back.

It’s what you want in a true American cheeseburger: simple, classic and well executed. Skip In & Out and give Bills Burger a try. You won’t regret it.

top_reviews.content: My associate and I were there for a business meeting. The service was very good and quick, we got some appetizers to share for the whole table and then a full main course for each one of us. The filet mignon was very good and also the porterhouse pork chop. Very generous plates. Located in a wonderful neighborhood. Easy to walk.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Market Table has been on Carmine Street since 2007 and there is a reason this place has never needed to reinvent itself — it just gets it right, every single time.

From the moment you walk in, the room does something to you. Window seats overlooking the West Village, terracotta pots, candlelight even at lunch, a neighborhood buzzing outside the glass. It feels like New York the way New York is supposed to feel.

We ordered through the all-day menu and every single dish came out more impressive than the last. The heirloom tomato salad with cucumber, olives and a green herb dressing sounds simple and looks like art. The nori dish is quietly one of the most elegant things I’ve eaten in this city. The fish over summer corn was perfectly executed — charred skin, sweet vegetables, clean and confident.

Then came the chicken. Get the chicken. Crispy skin that shatters, pea risotto underneath, a rich jus pooling around it — this is Chef Mike Price doing what he does best, letting the season speak and not overcomplicating a single thing. It is the kind of dish that makes you put your phone down.

Two desserts to finish by candlelight. Both necessary. No regrets.

The service is warm without being performative. The cocktail list is considered. The wine list has real personality. And the all-day format means there is genuinely no wrong time to come.

If you have been walking past this place for years without going in, stop doing that. Market Table is the real thing.

They had placed a few tables in what felt like a smelly, dungeon-like area underneath the restaurant and genuinely expected people to dine there just to squeeze in a few more covers and make extra money.

Then came the service. Nobody came to take our order for at least 15 minutes until I personally had to ask someone to come over. One hour after arriving, we still had not received even our starters. When the starters finally arrived, they were incorrect. At that point, I spoke to one of the hosts and explained how extremely disappointing and unacceptable the entire experience had been.

It was around 11:30 AM by the time we were finally served our starters. Incredible, right?

I ordered a salmon bruschetta-type appetizer and a medium-well burger. The starter was nothing memorable, and the burger arrived rare. The fries were among the greasiest and most oily fries I’ve had in a long time , I barely touched them.

For context, this was their Mother’s Day brunch prix fixe menu priced at $48 per person. It was very obvious we were not the only table waiting excessively long for food. The restaurant clearly did not have the staffing capacity to handle a brunch service of this scale, yet they were charging nearly $50 per person for below-average food and service that was honestly a 2/10.

To their credit, they removed one person’s charge from the bill, but by then the damage had already been done.

Never again.

I started with a cocktail called Call Me By Your Name, made with Neversink gin, Lillet Blanc, peach, lemon, and jasmine florets. It was light, floral, and perfectly balanced — a refreshing drink that set the tone for the meal.

For food, the Gulf Shrimp Tacos were a standout — juicy shrimp with creamy coleslaw, avocado crema, and just the right kick from the Holland chili. The Buttermilk Pancakes with cheesecake filling and blueberry compote were pure comfort — rich, fluffy, and indulgent in the best way. I also tried the Market Breakfast, which came with two eggs, sausage links, home fries, a little salad, and a flaky buttermilk biscuit. Everything was well-seasoned and cooked just right.

Overall, Market Table nails both flavor and presentation. It’s the kind of place that works for brunch with friends or a relaxed solo meal. I’ll definitely be back!

we came back to ghisallo because our first experience was genuinely great. today was a completely different story.
when we got there, we were told the back tables were reserved, so we sat outside in the front. totally fair. the funny part was that the shaded tables in the front were also “reserved” and were empty when we arrived and still empty when we left. we sat in the sun the entire time and didn't complain.
i ordered wine and was told it was chilled. it wasn't. my boyfriend's water was basically warm. the pepperoni pizza i ordered was greasy, soggy, and literally buried in cheese, with cheese falling off the pizza. last time it was crispy and perfect. still didn't complain.
then my boyfriend ordered a cheese pizza. the bald/shaved-head guy in the hat and deftones shirt, with keys hanging around his neck, brought out a margherita. we asked him if it was cheese or margherita and he said cheese. we asked the woman who took our order and she said margherita. so... which is it?
there are literally cheese pizzas on the menu. if someone orders a cheese pizza, they're probably expecting a cheese pizza, not a margherita. if your restaurant interprets that differently, just tell the customer before bringing out something completely different. basic communication, especially when people can have allergies or dietary restrictions.
we really tried to just eat our food and make the best of our time. we weren't planning on complaining about any of this. we didn't complain about the seating, warm water, wine, pepperoni pizza, or even the pizza mix-up.
when we didn't tip, the deftones-shirt guy came over and said, “i'm sorry you were so disappointed with your service,” in a rude, patronizing tone. THAT is when we finally spoke up. we explained we'd ordered a cheese pizza and there had been some confusion.
instead of simply acknowledging it, he gave us a lecture about how “in italy” when you order pizza, you get a margherita. he told us that if we wanted an actual cheese pizza, we should've ordered the kids cheese pizza because apparently everyone knows this.
btw, we're in santa monica.
we've also been here before. we ordered a cheese pizza here before, and he was actually the same person who served us that time and gave us the cheese pizza. so apparently he knew what we meant then, but today we're supposed to know the secret rules?
he then called me “performative” while telling us he takes pride in his service. if anyone was being performative, it was the guy giving us a lecture on italian and sicilian cuisine and how to properly order pizza.
thank you for explaining that pizza is from italy. groundbreaking. we genuinely never knew.
he even offered us a loaf of bread. appreciate the gesture, but if you know there's a problem, just make the pizza we ordered or send one home with us. bread isn't a substitute for the wrong pizza.
also, there's already a 4% charge on every check for the team members, so the attitude was especially unnecessary.
this wasn't about wanting special treatment. we were literally trying to eat our food and leave it at that. we weren't going to say anything until his comment and the way he chose to speak to us.
it's not always what you say, it's how you say it.
we came back because we genuinely liked ghisallo. we'll leave it at one good experience.
lastly, i'll be including photos. the first is the pepperoni pizza from our first visit, which was crispy and perfectly done. the second is what we were served this time. the pictures speak for themselves.
so yeah, anyway… maybe let's reconsider the deftones guy.

If you are craving a sweet treat in the heart of Koreatown, **Honeymee** on Wilshire is an absolute staple that never disappoints! 🍦🍯
The absolute star of the show here is their signature soft serve ice cream. To make it even better, you have to get it paired with their **fresh honeycomb toppings**. 🐝 Clear, golden, and incredibly decadent, the real honeycomb adds a fantastic, chewy texture and a burst of natural sweetness that complements the subtle milk soft serve perfectly. It’s a match made in dessert heaven! 🤤🥄
The shop itself has a clean, minimalist, and bright aesthetic, making it a great little walk-up spot to grab a treat after having K-BBQ or dinner nearby in K-Town. 🌆 The service is always quick, friendly, and efficient, even when there’s a small line of people waiting for their honey fix. 🏃‍♂️💨
The only minor downside is that parking right on Wilshire can be a bit of a challenge during peak evening hours, but the dessert itself is absolutely worth the quick trek. It’s a rock-solid 4.5-star sweet spot that I highly recommend to any soft serve fan! 🌟🥇

top_reviews.content:
My birthday experience at Loulou Rooftop Restaurant & Lounge (brunch) honestly wasn’t one of the best.

The place has a very cute and fun atmosphere with Tulum vibes, and that energy definitely matches the decor. The vibe and aesthetics are probably the best part of the place.

However, my rating mainly comes down to the food, because it should match the overall experience they’re trying to offer. The menu is basically Mediterranean food that feels very basic, lacking flavor and nothing extraordinary for a brunch spot that’s supposed to stand out.

Even worse, the cocktails were terrible. We tried an Old Fashioned that tasted mostly like water, and the Palomas were way too sour. After that, we decided not to order more drinks because we didn’t want to keep getting disappointed.

As for the service, it wasn’t bad, but it definitely wasn’t outstanding either. We basically saw our waitress about three times.

Honestly, the price does not justify the experience. I would recommend it for the vibe and pictures, but if you’re looking for great food, drinks, and an overall memorable dining experience, I wouldn’t recommend it.

Had the pleasure of dining at LouLou Rooftop Restaurant & Lounge in Santa Monica and really enjoyed the experience. The space is absolutely beautiful with a fun Tulum-inspired vibe. I can only imagine how stunning it becomes later in the evening when the sun goes down and all the lights come on, it seems like the kind of place that completely transforms at night.

What stood out most was the teamwork among the staff. Everyone was helping each other, which created such a welcoming atmosphere. Our server, Sophie, was an absolute sweetheart. She took her time explaining menu items, answered all of our questions, and delivered genuinely professional service throughout the meal.

As someone who loves trying a little bit of everything, we ordered quite a few dishes. I always joke that a bigger table is better because I tend to order enough food for four people, even when dining for two! The team quickly accommodated us by bringing another table over, which was appreciated. The Caesar salad was flavorful, generously dressed, and far from dry. The Hamachi Crudo was incredibly fresh and one of my favorite dishes of the evening. The escargot was delicious as well, though slightly overcooked for my taste. We also tried two pizzas, the dough was excellent with a great texture and flavor, although I would have loved to see a few more topping options. Even with there toppings it was not well placed all the mushrooms were on 1 slice and the meat was scattered (not evenly made).

Overall, a very enjoyable dining experience with great food, beautiful surroundings, and wonderful hospitality. Looking forward to coming back and experiencing the rooftop after dark.

We made a last minute reservation at LouLou’s for dinner. The atmosphere was interesting and gave off a Tulum-like vibe, which made the experience feel unique. The food was good, but it didn’t quite wow me. The restroom was a bit dark and is a shared, gender-neutral restroom. top_reviews.content:
Quite disappointed by our first time at Benoît. Given the prices and the fact that it is a restaurant owned by Alain Ducasse, and as a French person myself, I was hoping to enjoy more delicious food and drinks. The service and atmosphere were great though.

We ordered food from the prix-fixe menu and the à la carte one, as well as mocktails. We were very disappointed by the mocktails — they both tasted weird… The appetizers and the filet mignon and gratin dauphinois were very good. However, I wasn’t particularly a fan of the side of the fish dish (branzino); it might be personal tastes though. We were also disappointed by the dessert (tropézienne); it was somehow not very yummy… it also didn’t seem freshly made.

Even though the place is open early for dining, we weren't allowed to eat in the main dining area and were forced to the bar snacks and wines. Which is fine I guess. The filet was not cooked to specifications but was tasty. Fries were a hit as were the cocktails. Charcuterie board was meh, I definitely expected more uniqueness. The cheese plate was eye opening and probably the star of the show. Once I got the bill though, that midtown "tax" really hit. There's better for the value out there.

Fantastic ambiance, I really enjoyed the decor and the design. Great place to grab drinks or a quick meal with a friend.

Food was good, not fantastic, is hard to compare especially due to the fantastic food in the rest of NYC.

I went to this French restaurant, open since 2008, for Winter Restaurant Week on one of these recent snowy days. As per many of the other spots, they serve three courses for $60 or two courses for $45 during lunch only. In terms of the food, it wasn't the biggest portion size, but they gave extra dishes, so it felt somewhat worth it, even if the food itself wasn't the best for any particular bistro dish. The service, whether it was the maître d', the busboy, the waiter, or otherwise, was all friendly and professional. The inside is a bit sparse but still feels refined, and the clientele was mostly middle-aged, with many ordering from the main menu, aside from the table next to me and a few others. To drink, I thought of getting a glass of the Bourgogne Aligoté, but instead went for a cocktail, the $18 Not Too Far From The Tree with Calvados, ABC Drouin, apple cider, caramel, and lemon. The drink was pleasant with plenty of apple flavor from the calvados, cider, and drouin, but it wasn't too sweet. There was a bit of booziness, but not overly so, and a piece of brûléed apple on top was a nice touch.

Before the appetizer came out, they first gave me a couple of gougères. This consists of a choux pastry with a bit of cheese baked inside. It was airy with a slight chew, and if you have never had one before, it's pretty similar to a pão de queijo in terms of saltiness and chewiness, but smaller. This was warm and good. Afterwards, there was a bread course with two types of bread as well as butter with a B carved into it. Both breads were of pretty good quality, but they weren't warm, and the butter was unfortunately also a bit chilled. This was alright, but would have been much better if either of these two things had been at the proper temperature.

From the menu, I ordered the Onion Soup Gratinée, which was alright, with some cheese, onions, and a standard broth comparable to most bistros. I would say there were fewer croutons than usual, but since I still had some bread, I used it as a replacement. There was also less crispy cheese around the edges than in some other places, and the broth was a bit less rich and nuanced. The soup is normally $20 on the dinner menu, and I hope it's at least larger to make up for all these other shortcomings. In terms of places nearby, it doesn't really compare to Le Bonne Soupe, for instance, which offers a larger portion and a much better-flavored broth.

For my entrée, I had a choice among three courses not listed on the main menu. I went with the Coq Au Vin, as I am generally a fan of this classic bistro dish, and I also saw someone else's fish at the table next to me, which looked paltry. Along with some button mushrooms, the dish had a nicely cooked-down red wine sauce, though it wasn't as rich as in other places. I did notice a lack of lardons, which could be the reason. The chicken, while tender, consisted of two small bony pieces, which I didn't really appreciate. Outside of them being more difficult to scrape off and enjoy with the sauce, a piece of chicken breast would have honestly worked better and been more substantial. My favorite thing on the plate was surprisingly the purée, which was silky smooth with likely plenty of butter. This was just fine.

For dessert, I went with the $12 Chocolate Mousse since it was the only item on the regular dessert menu. The mousse was presented in a unique way, with one of the waitstaff coming around with a large serving dish, removing a piece of mousse, and plating it. The bitter-sweet mousse was silky smooth, and there was also some unexpected crunch, maybe from hazelnuts or something else, which added a nice extra texture. This was my favorite dish overall and a satisfying end. After dessert and while arriving with the check, they came around with a pan of freshly baked madeleines, which was a nice touch.

This was an alright experience. I get there have to be shortcomings when the main dishes here tend to be $45 and up, but this was barely worth it and wouldn't have been at all without the freebies. Upper 2.

Very special occasion dinner. Forgot second glass of champagne for appetizer. Octopus appetizer way overcooked/tough and had to send back. Then orderd 1966 Sauternes for the next foie gras appetizer, but after they poured a 1976 Sauternes they indicated they were out of the 1966 and charges same $60 price. The sole entree was overcooked. They said the duck entree was normally served medium rare and it arrived medium well. Saturday evening dinner and was 1/4 full— Alain needs to either keep his eye on the ball on the service and cuisine at this place or shut it down. We skipped desert, as our experience was dashed at this point. We received the bill and got comped on the octopus but stuck with the sales tax of it. To be further nickel and dimed, we were charge $8 for Stillwater we thought was free. I’m a fan of Le Maurice and gladly paid $1k for two in Paris but our $400 bill at Benoit was not worth it at all.

Worst service ever! When we ordered, we had asked to switch something (from Skirt Steak to Filet Mignon, which was a more expensive item), at most 5 minutes after we ordered, and our server, Miguel, rudely said it was “too late”. We didn’t receive our food for another half hour at least. I am sure it was not too late to switch. I understand this can be annoying, but we were very nice about it and it was right after we had ordered. He could have at least been kinder or tried to accommodate.

Regardless of this, our server hardly paid attention to us after we ordered / had gotten our food. Didn’t check on us ONCE. We had originally wanted to order some coffee and dessert, but our server didn’t come over to us for another 20 minutes, so we just decided to leave. This is ridiculous for such a well rated restaurant. It was not overly busy and did not seem understaffed whatsoever, so that can’t be the reason. Note: The bussers however were kind and working very efficiently. We told a manager about this on our way out and he sort of tried to console, but didn’t really seem to care.

The food itself was good, and the interior of the restaurant was nice, but the service made us never want to come again. Service makes or breaks a customer experience. It ruined the atmosphere in the restaurant and at our table especially.

We adore this restaurant! The food is phenomenal and the service is top notch. You truly can’t find better service in the city - it keeps us coming back! The cod, gravlax, and bread baskets are amazing. Benoit is also very celiac-friendly.

I had a fantastic experience at this restaurant. The staff was welcoming and attentive from the moment we arrived. Every dish was prepared with fresh ingredients and presented beautifully. The flavors were rich and well balanced, and the portions were generous. The atmosphere was warm and relaxing, making it a perfect place to enjoy a meal with family or friends. I will definitely be returning.

you get a real sense of abundance in every bite.

top_reviews.content:
Outstanding.
You sign up for 6 or 7 courses and we got about 10 dishes (4 different deserts). The pairings were on point for the most part. But the beauty and flavor profiles of each dish were second to none! And the open kitchen, team prep style of the chefs was something to behold!
There are only 5 tables per service and the music atmosphere, course prep...EVERYTHING is coordinated right down to the timing that the wine pairing explaination completes and the next course is placed.
Worth every cent, and yes I'm going to do it again!

Mélisse is a best-in-class fine-dining experience that fully justifies its two Michelin stars. From end to end, the execution is flawless, with each course demonstrating precision, intentionality, and elevated craftsmanship. The tasting menu is thoughtfully orchestrated, balancing innovation with classic technique and delivering consistent “wow” moments. Service operates at an elite standard—polished, anticipatory, and seamlessly aligned with the overall experience. Every detail, from pacing to presentation, signals a team operating at the top of their game. Net-net, this is a world-class restaurant that not only meets but exceeds the Michelin bar.

Melissa is everything you hope for and more from a two Michelin star experience in Los Angeles. From the moment you walk into the intimate five table dining room, the evening feels special. The ambiance is understated and elegant, the service is warm and deeply knowledgeable without ever being overbearing, and the meal unfolds like a beautifully choreographed performance with every course more thoughtful and precise than the last.

The menu is a masterclass in balance, technique, and flavor. The Miyazaki wagyu first bite set the tone for the night, rich and perfectly marbled with layers of umami that lingered beautifully. The Croque Madame with truffle Gruyère fondue was indulgent yet refined, while the Caesar with smoked anchovy and parmesan was a clever and deeply flavorful reimagining of a classic. The golden tomato soup, paired with pistachio and strawberry sorbet and finished with Portuguese olive oil, was as vibrant and nuanced as summer in a bowl.

The progression of dishes shows a real depth of technical execution, from the delicate Santa Barbara spot prawn with umeboshi custard to the luxurious ossetra caviar course, every element was perfectly cooked, balanced, and plated with intention. The Wolfe Ranch “Dirty” quail was a standout, juicy and bold with apricot carrot curry and black olive caramel creating layers of unexpected harmony. The quail and lobster tortellini in carrot brodo was a study in finesse, and the lamb course and seasonal desserts struck the perfect chord between creativity and comfort.

What truly elevates the experience is the service. The waitstaff were impeccable, warm, intuitive, and eager to share the stories and techniques behind each dish, which added another layer of appreciation to an already remarkable meal.

Melissa is the kind of restaurant that makes an evening feel unforgettable. Highly recommended for a special occasion or simply to experience one of Los Angeles’ most accomplished kitchens at the very top of its game.

A great restaurant worthy of its 2 stars. The food was exquisite coupled with an interesting and spot on wine flight. It was also great fun to chat with the chef about his music choices. They have a record player set up and vinyl is played all evening - we disagreed about the Rolling Stones but bonded over the Fine Young Cannibals and the (English) Beat. All of the team were knowledgeable, friendly and attentive. It is hard to pull off such high quality in a relaxed atmosphere but Melisse does it really well

I have eaten at Melisse twice and both times were absolutely incredible. The staff are fabulous and attentive from the time of setting up the evening through the end of the meal. They are willing to make the evening special and attend to any needs you may have.

The food is superb: flawless execution and well balanced flavors.  Every bite is meticulously planned and explained by the staff.

I even noted to my guest that I’m often disappointed in desserts at high-end restaurants in comparison to the savory courses, but that was not the case at Melisse. Here, the dessert delivers on the same level as the savory courses as an equal: elevated and elegant without being so overly complex or reaching to lose the sweet punch expected in a dessert.

The finishing touch of the night was being sent away with a copy of the menu as you specifically experienced it (down to the supplements you selected) for both food and wine complete with the date you dined in an elegant envelope as a keepsake. I have dined at many 3-Star restaurants, and very few have done this: I love that Melisse includes this as a part of its standard practice; it’s a very special touch.

...wow...so many amazing dishes served with care and amazing flavors! The wine pairing was expensive, but worth it. Same for the truffle addition. We loved the intimate environment and kind staff. The "hidden door", was fun! The whole thing was worth going at least once!

Melisse is an intimate fine-dining restaurant located within Citrin restaurant. The 14 seat dining room is intimate and comfortable  and the team services up sophisticated French-inspired dishes. The multi-course tasting menu places an emphasis on seasonal ingredients and refined culinary techniques and dishes are delicate and refreshing. Favorites include the signature "golden chicken" and Hokkaido scallops.

Service here is extremely attentive and friendly and staff frequently check-in to address any needs. It was also a treat to see Joshua himself come by the table to introduce himself.

Reservations are highly recommended as seating is limited. Note that while the cost is on the higher side of tasting experiences ($399/person), both the quality of the cooking and the elevated service justifies the premium.

A special gem to visit if in the Santa Monica area!
