NOT DINING, BUT AN ELEVATED EXPERIENCE  -

Note: I make my own reservations and pay for my meals. I don't hold back and tell it always like it is.

If you're looking for a unique dining experience, and not just an expensive good meal in LA, Restaurant Ki is the place to be! This Michelin-starred (only a litle more than 1 year old and Young Chef Winner on top of that) gem serves up innovative Korean-inspired cuisine that's as Instagrammable as it is delicious.

The place: Tucked in a basement of a not so great building, no windows or outside light, just a focused experience in a Korean themed decor. Plates and silver are all different and unique to the experience. It's simple, focused and on point for what you are going to experience.

The Experience
It's not just about the food – it's about the entire experience. The staff is friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere is relaxed yet refined. Small space,  well done, 12 people, and you feel like you are at a play or performance, which is intended. It's not a perfect experience, but it's so much on a higher level than a Spago or Mastro's let's say.

It's interactive - so you get to talk to the Chef's and ask questions - very good!

What to Expect
A 12-course tasting menu ($300 per person, with optional wine pairing at $190)
Menu changes with the season - new dishes get added in and removed all the time.
Intimate setting with a maximum seating capacity of 12, making it perfect for special occasions
Creative dishes that blend traditional Korean flavors with global influences
Impeccable service from Chef Ki and his team

Standout Dishes
Gimbap-inspired amuse bouche with crispy fried laver shell and housemade kimchi (super good)
Octopus with estragon and a creamy sauce made from the octopus head (excellent)
Smoked Lobster with doenjang-boosted beurre blanc and dried raspberry powder (yum)
Squab  or Duck with maple and rhubarb, showcasing the chef's skillful pairing of flavors

So you think small plates and I won't get filled, but you do! The first 5 teaser courses are great, then the meal comes.....savory, unami, sweet, and refined. Well presented.  Not every dish hits and some better than others but overall very good! The pace of the meal is on point so you never feel like you are forgotten, as in many restaurants.

One note. They have paper over the lights - not quite Michelin worthy.....might want to fix that.

Is it worth the price?
If you're looking for a special night out, absolutely! While $300+ per person is a splurge, the experience and quality of the food make it worth it. To me, it was a game changing dinner, a day late - Valentine's Day dinner, to an shared dining experience is what makes this Michelin Star Restaurant worth it. Bill ended up being $750 for two of us. I had a beer and she had Sake, which was very good.

Bravo to this place and to young chefs that understand food culture the restaurant business and the art of a great experience.

Restaurant Ki, a modern fine‑dining spot in Little Tokyo, Los Angeles, has quickly become one of the city’s most talked‑about restaurants and a must‑visit for local food lovers right now.

As you’d expect from Chef Ki—who has cooked at top restaurants like Benu in San Francisco, Jungsik and Atomix in New York, and Meteora in LA—Restaurant Ki goes far beyond simple “Korean fusion.” It offers a refined tasting menu that presents modern interpretations of Korean ingredients and techniques.

When I first sat down at Restaurant Ki, my biggest curiosity was, “How far can you go using familiar Korean ingredients?” But as the course progressed, that curiosity turned into pure amazement. It was a continuous surprise to see ingredients so familiar to me as a Korean—transformed into something so refined, beautiful, and delicious. Ingredients you might typically see in a Korean restaurant—gim bugak (crispy seaweed chips), kimchi, jang (fermented sauces), seasonal vegetables, octopus, blue crab, noodles, duck, mushrooms—appeared with completely different faces through the plating and cooking techniques.

What stood out to me was the way each dish balanced umami without letting any single ingredient overpower the others; instead, they enhanced one another and came together in perfect harmony. With the first bite, there is a moment of “What is this?”—a pleasant unfamiliarity—but soon after comes the realization, “Ah, this is unmistakably a Korean flavor.” That curious tension between unfamiliarity and familiarity felt like the very identity of this restaurant.

For me, the greatest appeal of Restaurant Ki is that it “shows Korean ingredients in a new light.” Ingredients I thought I knew so well appear in entirely different contexts and combinations.

- Familiar jang and fermented ingredients are lightly transformed into Western‑style sauces, foams, and oils
- Korea’s seasonal ingredients stand confidently at the center as the main components
- The umami is distinctly Korean, yet the textures and aromas are expressed in the language of contemporary fine dining

Each ingredient’s character and aroma are maximized, yet when they come together on the plate, they feel as natural and coherent as a single, well‑written sentence.

The wine pairing was especially memorable. I had been curious how well wine would pair with dishes centered on Korean ingredients, but at Restaurant Ki, this question was completely resolved.

Every course was paired with champagne or wine that flowed naturally with the meal, turning it into a complete experience. Instead of competing with the food, the wines and dishes enhanced one another, each helping to highlight and explain the other.

As for dessert, I usually don’t expect much at fine-dining restaurants with set-course menus, because I’ve often been disappointed by desserts that don’t fit the overall concept, are too monotonous, or are simply cloyingly sweet. This time, though, the dessert was the perfect finishing touch. The three elements I care about most were all perfectly met, so from start to finish it was a truly enjoyable experience.

Restaurant Ki is not just “a new Korean restaurant in LA,” but a modern Korean fine dining restaurant that showcases how far Korean ingredients can go.

If you love Korean food and are curious to see how far it can evolve in the future, I think Restaurant Ki in LA’s Little Tokyo is definitely a place you should experience at least once — and probably more than that.

As a brief postscript, I’d like to add how truly moved I was by the Ki team’s warm hospitality and their meticulous attention to detail; everyone moved with such clarity and purpose in their respective roles, thoughtfully explaining each dish and taking care of every little thing, thank you once again!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

The pasta was absolutely delicious! We ordered the Carbonara and Vongole, and both dishes were fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. The Carbonara was rich and creamy, while the Vongole had a wonderful garlic and seafood flavor.

Overall, the atmosphere and outdoor seating were enjoyable, but the food and service left something to be desired.

Turgut was so kind and thoughtful and gave us a complimentary dessert and we chose the olive oil cake. The entire staff is super friendly and I will definitely check out the DC location and will come back here again when I’m back visiting NYC. Ask for Turgut as your server when you come visit Olio! Bonus that’s is only a 4-mins walk to Washington square park so you can walk off your pasta. The outdoor tables will also be great when weather is nice out and people watch while you enjoy some aperitivo.

We dined at Olio e Più and the experience was overall quite pleasant.

It was perfect for brunch and the flavors were just so rich and enlightening. The pancakes and eggs were very nicely done and pair beautifully with the maple syrup. The maple syrup itself was such an amazing experience, it was delicate , light and not too sticky, indicating a homemade saucy syrup which was a great experience! If you are searching for a cute brunch experience with light vibes and great service then this spot is definitely a must!

The service was warm and attentive, though admittedly on the slower side. If you’re thinking of going for Sunday brunch, be prepared to take your time. It’s not the best option if you’re in a rush.

That said, if you’re someone who enjoys a laid-back dining experience and doesn’t mind a slower pace, Lunetta is absolutely worth a visit.

Lovely atmosphere will definitely come back again and again.

top_reviews.content:
This place is the coolest, yummiest hidden gem 💎 in ktown!! My waiter was fast and attentive. My favorites were the Rigatoni, honey butter chips, tuna dip was fire and the soju selection blew my mind because I’ve only ever had the flavored green bottle.

The fried chicken was very tasty too! Next time I need to try the beer and other menu items. I found metered parking nearby but there is valet service in the back!

This place has been on my list for at least a year, but I didn’t get around to visiting until I got the red dining book for Christmas. The place exceeded all expectations. It’s very tiny, with a big bar and only a few tables. They accept reservations and I highly recommend making one, otherwise you might find yourself lining out of the door. Everybody there is just vibing. Because the place is so small, all the staff members know exactly how many people they have, their order and the status of each dish. The service was quick, super friendly, and the owner came up to chat with us for a while and signed my book himself, it felt so very special. The food and drinks are incredible! We had to get tteokbokki with sea urchin row sauce, and their kimchi a la vodka. Both dishes were so good that I desperately wished for a piece of bread or a bit of rice to soak up every last drop of the sauces. I ended up asking for a spoon… portions are not huge, one entry is perfect for one person. We also got a couple of their drinks, both tasted very good but not enough spirit-forward to my taste, next time I’ll stick to straight soju or makgeolli, they have a great selection. Parking is everything you should expect from Koreatown, meter or street parking which takes time to find.
Can’t wait to be back!!

this place is a MUST TRY!

The kimchi alla vodka pasta and risotto with egg jam were both amazing, and so were our cocktails.

The staff was very friendly too! Best LA dining experience we’ve had in awhile

Cool vibe, and really inventive menu.

However, we got the KFC and Galbi Frites, some of the pricier menu items and they were our least favorite parts of the meal.

I typically don’t give feedback to waitstaff but i felt I had to say something about the chicken which was very dry and the breading quite mealy, especially cause I think all their restaurants are known for the chicken. top_reviews.content: I was a bit skeptical about Danbi since it’s not traditional Korean and I love simple and authentic food. But with an open mind I wanted to try Danbi. They did a great job of keeping original Korean flavours and adding a nice modern twist. The Yukhoe with the bone marrow is a great example…had the traditional flavour and the pear but the added roasted bone marrow elevated the flavour. The scallop pancake with crispy and you can taste the scallops. Beyond the food, the service was attentive and informative. We also like the overall ambiance. Definitely a place to bring back out of town guests or to have a nice evening out.

Went to this place with a couple of my friends for dinner. We didn’t have a reservation but the staff were very accommodating and was able to get us seated even though they were full. Food here was good especially the chuck flat with the seasoning salt and chimichurri sauce which I think was the best. I would say though a bit pricey for the portions for 4 people in total but you know what do you expect from a michelin guided restaurant. Overall, good place and will come back with family.

I was vacationing in LA and saw this resto on Tik Tok. I had to come try for the uni bibimbap cause it looked sooo good! They’re also known for their scallop pancake so we got both plus a squid salad. The uni bibimbap was definitely our favourite out of the three things we ordered. I first had a taste of the uni and shrimp before mixing everything. The uni and shrimp were sooo good n fresh! After you mix everything, you can still taste the creaminess of the uni. It was delicious. However I wished the rice was a little less mushy. Definitely good quality uni though. My husband really enjoyed the scallop pancake but it was a bit oily for me. He thought it was so good though . As for the salad, the squid had no flavour, it seemed like it was just boiled maybe? The lettuce they used was also way too bitter for it to be enjoyable for me :( it wasn’t really a refined salad imo. lastly I ordered a strawberry drink. The description said there’d be bits of strawberry in it but there wasn’t and it tasted veryyyy artificial. Like they just poured me strawberry “juice” out of a juice box for kids… overall I’d come back for the uni bibimbap.

Not particularly impressed. It is by no means bad food but for the price and the reviews, I was expecting more from a Michelin guide worthy place. The crudo was the best dish of the night with an amazing sauce that had complexity. However I think it would have been better paired with hamachi instead of snapper. The uni bimbimbap is good too because the uni, shrimp and ikura are simply ingredients that can speak for themselves. The japchae was disappointing because the noodles were very stretchy and way too greasy. Just a grease ball. The pork jowl was my favorite, well seasoned and well cooked. The zabuten was probably sous vided steak and grilled afterwards and tastes of course, good. But there's nothing original about it that makes it stand out other than the price. This also brings me to the cocktails, which were expensive and very average. By far the most disappointing thing was that I had diarrhoea late last night and my friend had food poisoning afterwards. It is unclear if the food was to blame. It was very unfortunate for the waiters because the service was great but it was eclipsed by the average food. Overall the three of us spend over $110 per person.

Ate at Danbi, recommend to do family style and share the food. Dishes are pretty good. We ordered 5 dishes plus a starter and it was more than enough for 4 people. Located in Korea Town in Los Angeles. Overall, great place to try.

This meal was among the most pleasant I have ever had. Every item on the menu looked interesting. The waitstaff was extremely well informed about every aspect of the food preparation, and was eager to share that knowledge. In truth, it really doesn't matter what you order (unless you have allergies), you will not be disappointed. We shared bites, and I can honestly say that I would have been equally ecstatic about my food no matter what I had chosen. The attention to detail in food preparation and presentation was obvious and appreciated.
Every staff member was friendly and helpful, attentive without being over-present. They presented the impression of a unified team organized around a quality customer experience rather than making themselves appear to be "the expert". I look forward to my next visit to Southern California, I will definitely visit Citrin.

Citrin started strong with comfortable seating and an appealing, well-curated menu. With a Michelin-starred restaurant, I naturally came in with certain expectations for precision, depth of flavor, and seamless service.

Overall, the menu composition was thoughtful and promising. However, several dishes lacked the level of flavor and refinement I anticipated. I was especially excited about the lobster pasta with additional truffles, which carried a significant premium. Unfortunately, the tomato sauce was overpowering, completely masking the aroma and taste of the truffle. Instead of a layered and balanced dish, it felt like a straightforward tomato pasta that could have been found at a neighborhood restaurant. Given the additional $70 for the upgrade and truffles, this was particularly disappointing.

Service also felt disjointed. There did not seem to be a dedicated server, and different individuals delivered each course. While everyone was polite, the experience lacked cohesion. Dessert arrived before the coffee that had been ordered, and the coffee never came, even after dessert was finished.

The highlight of the evening was the steak, which was well-prepared and genuinely enjoyable. Aside from that course, however, nothing stood out in a memorable way.

$678 for two people. Absolutely ridiculous.

I genuinely don’t understand how Citrin has a Michelin star.

This was easily one of the worst value dining experiences I’ve ever had. The $165 tasting menu is basically a starting price — supplements and add-ons pile up quickly. Our bill for two came to $678.42 before tip.

And the food? Nowhere near Michelin-star quality. Nothing was memorable, and several dishes were simply disappointing.

The service was just as bad. Plates and spoons were brought out and then taken away, the course sequence seemed confused, and the whole experience felt disorganized.

At this price point, I expect exceptional food and flawless service. We got neither.

I left feeling completely ripped off. I didn’t even want to tip, but I did anyway.

$678 for this experience is absurd. Save your money and go somewhere actually worth it. Never coming back.

I’m posting our receipt so other people don’t get blindsided by the final bill like we did. Look closely at the supplements and extra charges before you order.

This is an amazing restaurant. Well deserving of the Michelin star. The food was amazing, well cooked and innovative. The steak was perfectly cooked, egg caviar is a fun dish. The cocktails were delicious and well mixed. The service was great. The price was okay considering it’s a Michelin star restaurant but then again I do live in NYC haha. Overall an amazing experience. I celebrated my birthday they give a little candle and a note.

Would recommend to try their happy hour too, seemed like a great deal.

One of my favorite things about Dine LA is the increased accessibility of Michelin quality restaurants. Citrin received its Michelin star in 2022 and is located in Santa Monica. The menu consists of modern Californian cuisine, and for Dine LA, they are offering a prix fixe menu that is $99 per person.

We made our reservation on OpenTable. Citrin accepts walk-ins, but I would advise against it. There was a sizable crowd of people collecting in the narrow entranceway that we were glad not to be a part of on our Saturday night. We actually arrived quite early for our reservation time, but the staff were able to seat us anyway. For reference, the entrance to Citrin is the bright red door on the gray building. Opening the door emerges you right at the bar, and the host stand is a bit hidden off to the left of the wall.

The dining area was elegant and softly lit by warm lighting. Our server was Evin, who took exquisite care of us the entire night. The staff move with precision and attention, clearing plates as soon as you finish them and exchanging your cutlery between each course.

We both got cocktails from the bar. I had the Soul Survivor, a refreshing tequila based drink with ginger and a variety of citruses. My friend had the Lady Jane, which was spectacular, served in a glass with the skinniest stem and visually resembled a Swedish princess cake. This drink had a lovely silky texture with matcha and coconut flavor.

Part of the reason I chose to dine as Citrin was due to their enticing Dine LA menu. I had already known which dishes I wanted for each course, but we were surprised with an amuse bouche as well! Our amuse bouche was a yuzu panna cotta with three types of melon and peppers, served in a dainty little double walled shot glass. To be honest, this dish was quite polarizing. I could understand why people would not like this dish. My friend didn’t like this dish, and it took me some getting used to as you would expect a dish with these ingredients to be sweet and dessert-like, but instead it was savory and quite sour. But, I thought it was interesting and the tartness woke up our palates, so I think the amuse did its job.

For our first actual course, we chose the bluefin tuna crudo, which was served with avocado, wakame, arare rice crackers, and garnished with radishes and edible flowers. Texturally, this dish was really fun. The fish was fresh and delicate and its soft texture melded beautifully with the avocado. The crunch of the spherical rice crackers and seaweed salad added nice contrast. There was a unique umami flavor present throughout this dish as well that I really enjoyed.

For our second course, we had the shinkejime vermillion rock fish. The fish was very flaky and tender and the skin was light and crispy. My favorite part about this dish, however, was the sauce. I also loved the touch of sweetness from the confit tomatoes.

For our third course, we had the koji cured duck breast. The duck was phenomenal. It was so juicy and flavorful, and the accompaniments of beet puree and figs complemented the protein well. The sweet and sour sauce was delicious as well, and I appreciated how subtle it was as to not overpower the dish.

Lastly, for dessert, we had a passionfruit parfait. I was especially partial to this dessert due to my Vietnamese heritage. The flavors were very southeast asian. Lemongrass… tapioca… coconut… and passionfruit. Visually and conceptually, it was reminiscent of che or sago, so pathos was definitely in the works for me. This dish was harmonious. The rich, creamy coconut sorbet was cut perfectly by the tartness of the passionfruit. And instead of one overpowering the other, their distinct notes shined individually and complemented each other. I really liked this dessert.

I thoroughly enjoyed the Dine LA menu at Citrin. Personally, I really like bluefin tuna, duck, and passionfruit, so it felt like this menu was catered to me! The menu was fun, summery, and delicious. I highly recommend Citrin for Dine LA 2026 patrons.

We were here for their Valentine’s Day tasting menu and combined it with their wine pairing. Absolutely amazing especially the egg caviar and lobster bolognese. The host was ok, but our server was top notch attentive. We’ll be back.

Elegant atmosphere, beautiful presentation, and absolutely delicious food. ✨
Service was warm and professional, and the entire experience felt refined yet welcoming. A perfect spot for a classy dinner in Santa Monica. Highly recommend!

Shredded parm and chili flakes helped a bit. Good thing we got full on bread and the pizzas we ordered for the table :)

All in all we agreed it was a nice experience and would return, but will stick with the dishes we enjoyed. The pre fixe price was very reasonable and parking convenient enough to warrant the next visit.

Settecento is one of my go-to spots in DTLA and it never disappoints. I come here often with my coworkers, and we are huge fans of both the lunch special and happy hour. The food is consistently excellent, and you can really tell they care about quality.

One of the coolest things about this place is that the pasta is made fresh in-house, and many of the ingredients are actually imported from Italy. Everything tastes incredibly fresh and authentic. The pizzas are another standout—they're light, flavorful, and absolutely worth spending a little extra on.

And if you're stopping by for happy hour, do yourself a favor and order an Aperol Spritz. They make one of the best I've had in the city.

Bird in Hand is one of the best restaurants and bars in New York City. I almost never leave reviews, but this place is absolutely worth it. After living all over the city for seven years and trying countless spots, I can confidently say this is one of my favorites. It works for everything — a special occasion birthday or anniversary dinner, a low-key but impressive first date, brunch with your mom, cocktails with friends, you name it.

It strikes the perfect balance in every category: cozy and eclectic, lively enough to feel like a night out but calm enough to actually hear the person across from you. The food and drinks are outstanding, the atmosphere is warm and inviting, and the service is genuinely unmatched. It’s stylish without being pretentious, energetic without being overwhelming, and polished without losing warmth.

So many NYC spots get one thing right and three things wrong — great food but miserable service, a cool vibe but deafening noise, strong cocktails but rushed tables. Bird in Hand is one of the rare places where every part of the experience works together. It’s the kind of place where you go in planning to stay for one drink and accidentally spend the whole evening there.

I’ve been here countless times, yet every visit still feels like they’re welcoming me for the first time and hoping I’ll come back.

For actual first-timers: get the house burger (both the brisket blend and Impossible versions are incredible), any cocktail on the menu, and the chocolate molten lava cake. Honestly, though, you can’t go wrong with anything here.

More concerning was how a severe allergy was handled. We informed the staff in advance of this allergy, yet a member of our group experienced a reaction during the meal. This was extremely distressing and caused us to leave promptly for health and safety reasons. Given the circumstances, we left a $0 tip, which was communicated at the time and directly related to the allergy incident and how it was handled - not out of negligence or bad faith.

Two days later, after checking my bank statement, I discovered that an additional ~$40 tip had been added without my consent or prior disclosure, despite the fact that no tip had been left due to the incident. This was never communicated at the time of payment and removed any opportunity to address it in the moment.

In an effort to resolve this directly and in good faith, we returned to the restaurant to give management an opportunity to address the situation and explain this billing practice. The response we received was simply, “Oops, it was a mistake,” with no further explanation, accountability, or meaningful attempt to address the seriousness of the issue. Given the circumstances-an allergy-related incident and an unauthorized charge-we expected a far more thoughtful and responsible response.

We expect transparency in billing, serious handling of food allergies, and a higher standard of accountability from an upscale restaurant, especially during a featured dining event. Experiences like this erode trust, and we hope management takes this feedback seriously and reviews both their service and billing practices moving forward.

Redbird delivered one of those rare group dining experiences where everything actually works, even with a party of 13. We came here for a birthday, and from the moment you walk into that stunning former cathedral space, it feels elevated but still warm and inviting. The lighting, the architecture, the energy, it all sets the tone for something special without feeling overly formal.

Chef Neal Fraser’s menu is thoughtful and really well executed, and we went deep into it. The hamachi crudo was my favorite, bright, citrusy, with that perfect sweet and sour balance and just enough crunch to make every bite interesting. The branzino was a standout, clean, delicate, and beautifully cooked. The burrata was another highlight, served over arugula with a balsamic glaze and nuts that added the right amount of texture. Even the brussels sprouts surprised us, a little kick to them and full of flavor. The steak frites were solid, and the fries across the board were fresh, crisp, and addictive.

Dessert sealed it. The pavlova, which I don’t usually gravitate toward, was incredible, light, balanced, and the grapefruit brought a brightness that made it memorable. The s’mores dessert was also a hit, fun, indulgent, and done really well.

Service and pacing, especially for a group this size, were seamless. Everyone felt taken care of, dishes came out smoothly, and the entire experience felt intentional from start to finish. Overall, food, service, and ambience were all excellent.

Their sandwich selection strikes a nice balance between familiar classics and creative combinations, all executed with precision and quality ingredients. Each component feels thoughtfully chosen, from the bread that maintains the perfect texture to the fresh produce and well-prepared proteins. The salads follow the same pattern of reliability - generous portions, fresh ingredients, and dressings that complement rather than overwhelm.

The bright, modern space offers a comfortable setting for a casual lunch, and the staff maintains an efficient operation even during peak hours. While prices sit at the higher end of the sandwich spectrum, the quality justifies the cost for what you receive.

I've lived in Los Feliz for many years, and Messhall remains one of my favorite places to dine.

The atmosphere is welcoming and relaxed, the staff are consistently friendly and attentive, and the food is always fresh and beautifully prepared.

What I especially appreciate is the combination of excellent service and a menu that offers something for everyone. Every visit has been enjoyable, whether stopping in for a casual meal or meeting friends for a longer gathering.

It's refreshing to find a local restaurant that maintains such high standards while still feeling comfortable and unpretentious. Messhall is a true neighborhood gem, and I highly recommend it to both locals and visitors alike.

Five stars well deserved.
Went for Happy Hour and had a great time! Oysters and the loaded fries were the highlights. Service was excellent! We will be back to try other things soon!
Loved the cozy atmosphere here! It’s the perfect spot for a relaxed hangout. Great food and decent service. Recommended!

We got reservations for 8 and were seated on the patio. Our server was really kind, super patient and helpful, and cracked jokes with us — all around really fun! We ordered a bunch, of course, but some highlights were the French toast. My kid couldn’t get enough of it. He would have licked the plate if I’d have let him! One of us had the Cobb salad and she said “I was almost regretting my choice to get a salad but then it ended up being the best Cobb salad I have ever had!” So, glowing review there. Another at the table ordered the car cafe burger and was definitely happy with it! And a couple of us ordered the standard — eggs were cooked to perfection, the fruit selection was excellent, and the potatoes. My goodness, those potatoes. Worth a visit for those alone. I’m gonna be thinking about them often. Plenty of food to go around, and prices were fair for the quality! The only bummer (for me, perhaps not as much for others) is that they do allow dogs on the patio. There was some barking involved and overall it’s just not my favorite to have pets in a food establishment. I’m not knocking off an overall star though, the food was worth it!

Whoa, just had my first experience here, and man am I glad I stopped in. Passed many times, saw a sign for oysters, literally turned around to give it a try. Started with the baked oysters, a boldly flavored cheese encrusted affair, pure Americana. We then had the baby backs which fell off the bone with a delightfully Louisana style BBQ sauce, it's vinegar forward as this style should be and which I love, but may be an adjustment for folks used to sweeter BBQ sauce. The Mac and cheese was killer. The slaw and fries that came with the ribs were as good as it gets. Bar was fast and had a nice assortment of upscale special cocktails in addition to a full bar. The entire staff was very friendly and accommodating from the moment we arrived. For sure plan to come back!

top_reviews.content:
A classic New York steakhouse with great food.

We ordered the Prime Rib ($82), Sirloin ($55) Clam Chowder ($16) Waffle Fries ($12), and Cheesecake ($11) and every dish was exceptional.

The Prime Rib was beautifully roasted with a rich, caramelized crust and a perfectly medium-rare centre. It was exceptionally juicy, buttery, and packed with deep beef flavour.

The Sirloin had a beautifully charred exterior with a well-developed crust while remaining tender, juicy, and full of rich beefy flavour.

The New England Clam Chowder was thick, velvety, and generously filled with tender clams and potatoes, making it rich and comforting without feeling overly heavy.

The waffle fries were perfectly golden and crispy, lightly seasoned with Parmesan, and had a fluffy interior an addictive side that paired perfectly with the steaks. We finished with the Cheesecake, which was rich, silky smooth, and perfectly balanced without being overly sweet.

We left completely full, and considering the quality of the food and the generous portions, we thought the prices were very reasonable.

We had a really good dinner at Smith & Wollensky. My husband ordered a steak, and it was delicious. I chose the crab cake and really enjoyed it as well. We visited on a Sunday evening, and the restaurant was surprisingly quiet, even though we'd heard reservations are usually needed. The service was fast, and the staff were warm, attentive, and welcoming. A great dining experience we would definitely recommend it.

Had a birthday celebration, and client closing lunch here today. Since it is lunch hour, the restaurant is not too crowded. Our waiter Adam is very attentive and super friendly!

He introduces the porter house and their special soft shell crap appetizers; they are super delicious!

Very happy with the selection of food we had here! Will definitely come again!
Highly recommended.

We visited Smith & Wollensky for a family dinner, and it was a wonderful experience from start to finish. The team greeted us warmly and professionally, setting the tone for a great evening, and the service remained attentive throughout.

The filet mignon was the highlight, cooked to perfection 👌🏽.

Thank you, and God bless you and your family 😊

We came to Smith & Wollensky for the Weekend Wine Dinner. The food was very good, and the waiters were generous with the wine. The restaurant is noisy, but the atmosphere is pleasant. The only slight downside was one of our waiters—a pleasant, older gentleman, but perhaps a bit tired from work that day. Other than that, it was a very pleasant experience.

The noise was nearly unbearable in the upstairs seating area. Felt like we were eating in a noisey cafeteria. The tables are small and rickety.

The calamari was bland and basic. A little soggy.

The steak was good, decent cuts and good recommendations from the staff.

Drinks were not up to par for a steakhouse. My Old Fashioned lacked a king cube and wasn't well made.

Maybe try to lower floor but if they take you upstairs. Make sure you go during off hours.

Smith & Wollensky remains a quintessential New York City experience, perfectly capturing the atmosphere of a classic, old-fashioned American steakhouse. Stepping inside feels like taking a step back in time, offering an authentic "big-city" vibe that is increasingly rare.
What sets this institution apart is its refreshingly straightforward approach. The menu is simple and easy to navigate, allowing the high-quality ingredients to take center stage. During my visit, we enjoyed a classic spread: fresh shrimp cocktail, crispy bacon, a tender filet mignon, and a flavorful New York cut sirloin. Each dish arrived prepared to perfection—so flavorful and expertly seasoned that adding condiments would have been an insult to the chef.
The service is another highlight; the staff is not only exceptionally fast but also remarkably attentive, intuitively understanding and anticipating the needs of their guests. For those looking for a top-tier steakhouse experience in New York but feeling constrained by a busy schedule or the stress of competitive bookings, Smith & Wollensky is an absolute must-recommend. It delivers consistently excellent food and professional service, proving that some traditions are worth preserving for a reason.

Probably will not go back.

Another visit to Trattoria Zero Otto Nove, because some traditions are non-negotiable.

One would think "Boiled eggs in pasta?", but trust me, the bechamel sauce takes it to the next level.

Ms. J. went for the daily special: Radiatori in Cartoccio, cooked inside a sealed pocket of aluminum foil and opened tableside like a little pasta reveal. Steamy, aromatic, and frankly a bit of a showoff -- in the best possible way.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ An authentic Italian gem on Arthur Avenue

Zero Otto Nove was recommended to us by the owner of Titles Brothers, where I regularly go to buy Italian cold cuts and cheeses. It turned out to be one of the best recommendations we’ve received.

My mom, my daughter, and I absolutely loved our experience. The food was outstanding, the wine was excellent, and every dish was full of authentic Italian flavor. We’ll definitely be coming back!

We got the burrata salad and the dressing is what got me. Just perfectly balanced and bright, letting the burrata actually shine.

Manuela in the Arts District is exactly the kind of restaurant that makes downtown Los Angeles feel layered, creative and alive. Tucked inside the Hauser & Wirth complex, it is not just a place to eat, but a full experience — part restaurant, part garden, part art-world escape.

The setting is easily one of its biggest strengths. You walk into a space where the art, open kitchen, patio, greenery and industrial Arts District character all come together without feeling forced. There is a calmness to the restaurant that makes it feel special, but not stiff.

The food leans modern American with a strong Southern influence, and the menu clearly celebrates seasonal produce, local farms and ingredient-led cooking. Among the starters, the cream biscuits were exceptional — warm, comforting, beautifully made and honestly one of those dishes that can set the tone for the whole meal. They are the kind of simple thing that only works when the execution is really strong.

What I enjoyed most about Manuela is that it has a point of view. The restaurant does not feel like it is chasing trends. It knows what it is: seasonal, relaxed, artistic, rooted in California produce, but with a Southern comfort thread running through the food. The menu moves comfortably between shareable starters, seafood, vegetables, wood-fired dishes and cocktails, making it a great place for brunch, lunch, dinner or even a slower afternoon meal in the Arts District.

Overall, Manuela is one of those LA restaurants where the environment and the food support each other beautifully. It is stylish without being cold, thoughtful without being precious, and memorable without trying too hard. I would go back for the setting, the garden, the atmosphere — and absolutely for those biscuits.

Lovely decor with semi-outdoor and indoor space, full bar, and lots of plants and lights.

The food is spectacular. Everything we ordered was excellent. Standouts include the cream biscuits from "small & to share" menu, the peads and barnett pork chop and venison burger. Our other two dishes consisting of the butterball potatoes and cast iron cornbread were also noteworthy.

This place is definitely up there with Bestia and Bavel. Easily the best meal I've had in 2026 by a mile.

I visited Manuela for brunch and ordered the venison burger and the shrimp and rice grits. Both dishes were excellent, with very well-balanced flavors.
The venison burger felt surprisingly light and didn’t have any strong or gamey taste. The crispy onions and sauerkraut inside were perfectly done and added great texture and contrast.
The shrimp and rice grits offered a unique experience. If you enjoy strong umami flavors, you’ll likely love the combination of mushrooms with the soft, almost melt-in-your-mouth rice.
Overall, I highly recommend this spot for brunch.

We came to Que Bárbaro looking for a good steak dinner and ended up having an amazing experience. I rarely complain about restaurants, but this experience genuinely felt overpriced for what we received.

Between dinner and drinks, we spent close to $400 expecting an upscale experience. The food didn’t help justify the cost either. The Lobster Tallarin sounded impressive on the menu, but the portion was surprisingly small for the price and nothing about it stood out flavor wise. A lot of the dishes looked designed more for presentation than actual value.

What disappointed me most was the overall hospitality. Aside from the hostess, who was genuinely kind and welcoming, the service throughout the night felt cold and disconnected. No one really checked in, and the energy from the staff made the restaurant feel more interested in appearances than customer experience.

For a place positioning itself as a premium dining spot, I expected much better attention to detail, stronger service, and food that actually matched the pricing. Unfortunately, this felt more like paying for the hype than the experience.

Even though I was seated, the person at the front desk was not very friendly.  It is very small but doable.  At least two people that walk by hit my bag and there was not a hook where they put the “single” folks.  I have attached the menu.  I had swordfish and lobster.  The bartender did not offer a side option so I had to look around to try and figure out what others were eating.  My swordfish and lobster were amazing.  And I ordered some amazing broccolini after I had eaten half the food.  The lobster was three bites.  The couple next to me ordered me an express martini.  It was delicious.

It was sort of overshadowed by the cook who was pulling out boxes and putting food on the grill.  Boxes?   It took away from the ambiance for sure.

Overall, it was a decent time but I had to keep checking my watch to make sure I was not embarrassed by the woman who checked me in a told me I had about two hours to eat.

It was about $130 after tip.

While we were seated promptly for our 4:30 PM reservation, the service quickly went downhill. Our server was consistently dismissive and rude, from making condescending comments when we asked a simple menu question to rolling his eyes when my brother tried to place a to-go order. We waited approximately 90 minutes for our entrées, which I understand can happen on a busy holiday, but what was unacceptable was the lack of communication and the fact that we had to repeatedly flag our server down for drink refills and updates.

At one point, the server told us our food was delayed because we had "chosen to come at the busiest time," despite having a reservation. Management was aware of the delay but never came to our table to address the situation. The restaurant also appeared poorly maintained, with dirty dishes piled near our table and no effort made to properly clear our table throughout the meal.

The final straw came when our leftovers were being packed up and dirty plates were stacked on top of food we were taking home. When my father questioned it, the busser simply replied, "That's how we do things here."

As someone who spent five years managing an upscale Italian restaurant and continues to work in the hospitality industry, I understand that holidays can be challenging. Delays happen. However, professionalism, communication, and basic hospitality standards should never disappear because a restaurant is busy.

This was easily the worst restaurant experience my family has had, especially disappointing given how much we were looking forward to celebrating Father's Day here. Unfortunately, we will not be returning.

After the meal, we took a look at the bakery and we were enamored with the amount of macaron choices, a huge variety and super affordable. The entry is stunning, with a charming cafe and a beautiful pastry area. The dining area is elegant and upscale with a modern touch. The service was amazing, with a special shout-out to the talent behind the pizza oven.

It's a great spot perfect for any time of day. It’s a must-visit when in LA.

top_reviews.content:
Spoiler alert: I rated this restaurant lower because of misleading Wagyu labeling. That said, Fia Steak is a very good steakhouse and worth visiting.

The service was the highlight of the experience. Every member of the staff was professional, attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely friendly. They made us feel welcome from the moment we arrived.

The restaurant has a very nice atmosphere, with an attractive bar overlooking the open kitchen and wood fire, creating a warm and enjoyable setting.

The Tuna Cigars were outstanding—easily one of the best dishes of the night. Creative, perfectly executed, and absolutely delicious.

The steak menu offers a good variety of cuts. Unfortunately, this is where my biggest criticism begins.

The menu labels some products simply as “Wagyu” when they are actually American Wagyu crossbreeds. For example, the Snake River Farms picanha should be described as American Wagyu crossbreed, not simply Wagyu. That distinction matters.

Would anyone accept ordering a bottle labeled Malbec only to discover it was a blend containing an unknown percentage of Malbec? Of course not. So why should we accept the same practice with Wagyu?

Restaurants need to start labeling Wagyu honestly and transparently. Customers deserve to know exactly what they are paying for.

I also tried the Australian Wagyu zabuton. It was less tender than I expected, leading me to believe it was probably a mid- to low-marbling Australian Wagyu crossbreed, although the menu doesn’t specify. That is exactly the problem with inaccurate labeling—you end up guessing what you’re actually eating.

Overall, Fia Steak offers a pleasant dining experience with excellent service, a nice atmosphere, and some very good dishes. My lower rating is not because it’s a bad restaurant, but because I believe misleading Wagyu labeling is something the industry should no longer accept.

This was our first time dining here, and it had been on our to-do list for quite some time, especially knowing that an Iron Chef is the owner. My wife and I met up with another couple for dinner and were excited to finally give it a try.

The space offers a vibrant and energetic atmosphere. The décor is nice simple, clean, filled with tasteful greenery, and thoughtfully spaced to create a comfortable dining experience.

We worked our way through the menu and ordered seven items along with cocktails: naan & dips, pickled pepper blueberry cornbread, sautéed green beans, wood-fired broccoli, goat shank, sticky glazed pork shank, and grilled kalbi-style short ribs.

The one dish we were most excited about was the goat curry, but we were told it wasn't available. While waiting for our food, a runner brought a bowl of goat curry to our table, only for us to find out it was meant for another table. Naturally, we asked our server what was going on, and he explained that the other guests had ordered it earlier. In reality, the restaurant had simply sold out. Our reservation was at 6:30 p.m., and the restaurant opens at 5:00 p.m., so it was surprising that such a popular menu item was already gone.

As for the food, everything was cooked very well and beautifully presented. The proteins were moist and tender, and the vegetables were cooked perfectly. The cornbread and naan were excellent standouts. While the proteins were certainly good, the flavors didn't quite reach that "chef's kiss" level for me. They were enjoyable but left me wanting a bit more depth and flavor. The Pork Shank was the better of the proteins.

Service, unfortunately, was the weakest part of the evening. Our server, David, seemed to lack attention to detail. He never offered clean plates as we shared multiple dishes, nor did he check in to see if we wanted additional cocktails or more food. It felt like several missed opportunities to enhance both our  experience and restaurants sales opportunity. Whether he was overwhelmed, distracted, or simply disengaged, the service came across as mediocre.

Overall, the restaurant has great potential. The atmosphere is inviting, the food is well executed.  With more consistent service and better communication regarding menu availability, the experience could easily be elevated.

An overall good dining experience for the ambience and people watching. I recommend the outdoor seating since the inside can be noisy. The food was all over the place and felt like it was trying too hard, reminiscent of when nouveau CA cuisine was starting. The naan and hummus was a blend of non complimentary flavors thrown together. The naan, heavily garlic seasoned did not pair well with the soy and carrot hummus. The top layer of the naan was delicious and the bottom layer was good with the sides but together with flavors negating each other. Less is more and pick a lane. The pork shank was good and probably the best dish we had with flavors very similar to a pastor taco…if that is the direction and comparison the kitchen wants to evoke then it’s a poor comparison for food that is different and slightly more elevated than the flavors of the LA pastor street taco for a much lower price point. The goat curry was muted and lackluster and was very similar to a chilaquiles with the fried naan chips. Are the slightly better flavors, presentation, and ambiance justifying the significant higher price point? The sad answer is no. There is a heaviness and sweetness to the food which made us feeling still hungry with leftovers. It lacked a savory filling element since the sweetness from the pork and the coconut in the curry negated and fullness from the meats. The accompanying pickled veggies in all three dishes with their bright acidity helped cut through the sweetness and heavy “bready” feeling in all of the dishes. Especially in the competitive LA restaurant scene where even the mom and pop hole in the walls are far better than even Bib Gourmand Michelin restaurants this place pales in comparison. It’s pretty and pleasant but lacking. The goat curry was better the next day as leftovers than at the restaurant.

Stopped by Prince Coffee House recently and had a nice experience overall. The service was solid -- staff were friendly and everything came out quickly.

Definitely not what I'm used to for a NYC coffee shop.

Prince Coffee House — Coffee Is Always A Good Idea For Real

Tucked into Arthur Avenue in the heart of the Bronx’s Little Italy, Prince Coffee House feels less like a New York coffee shop and more like something you’d stumble into on a cobblestone street in Prishtina or Vienna.

The tall windows, the hundred tin Turkish coffee cups hanging from the ceiling, and the warm ambient hum of a dozen languages being spoken at onc— the vibes are unapologetically European.

The coconut Raffaello cake was legit. Light, creamy, and dangerously easy to finish. The crêpes on previous visits have been equally great.

And the coffee. Let me be very clear. This coffee will put hair on your chest and keep you going for two to three weeks.

Plan accordingly.

Whether you settle in at the communal table upstairs, grab a window seat for some of the best people watching on Arthur Avenue, or disappear into the quiet basement to get some work done, Prince Coffee House delivers every time.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

What an incredible experience! This was our first visit to Prince Coffee, and by the time we left, it felt like we had been coming here for years.

The atmosphere is warm, inviting, and the kind of place where you want to linger instead of rushing out the door. Great coffee is easy to find, but genuine people who make you feel at home are rare. I first visited Back on the Beach Cafe off Pacific Coast Highway in October 2024, and I loved it so much that I now make it a point to visit every time I’m in Santa Monica, which is usually about once a year. I recommend it to anyone I know visiting the area.

My go-to meal is either the Pasta Mama or Pasta Papa depending on my mood. The Mama is vegetarian, the Papa is not, and both are absolutely delicious. The mimosas are good, just your classic basic mimosa, and their latte is so good that I always grab one to go before leaving.

Overall, I think the pricing is pretty affordable, especially considering the location. I usually sit outside because I love that the outdoor seating is literally in the sand. It gives you that full beach experience without being overly crowded or touristy.

The location is close enough to the Santa Monica Pier that you still get that Santa Monica beach vibe, but far enough away that you avoid the chaos and heavy crowds around the pier itself.

Parking is paid, flat surface, wheelchair accessible, and the indoor seating also seemed wheelchair friendly. In the early mornings, the atmosphere is quiet and relaxing, not loud or crowded, and the crowd feels more local. By late morning and lunchtime, it becomes more family-oriented and the indoor seating can get a little noisy in that cafeteria-style way. There’s a children’s area or activity space next door, which I think contributes to some of the family traffic later in the day.

The staff have always been polite during my visits as well. Anyway, hope this helps!

Highly recommend eating there.

- the Caesar salad

Here's what I sampled:
• blue corn cookies and coconut dulce de leche cookies -these cookies had a great texture. A more masa-like taste than a dessert or cookie, similar to a tamale. I was craving some milk after eating this. I drank all of my water.

• Déjà vu mocktail was prickly pear shrub, ginger beer, lime, and bitters blend. It was heavier on the bitters end. I'm not sure I'd order this again.

I am posting pictures of the Dark Winds cocktail- which is rum, rum fire, allspice dram, creme be banana, horchata, and pineapple. I did not drink this but my friend did. They do recommend it.

• Duck ham was smoked duck breast, duck skin chicharron, water cress and sorrel with radish and an orange and honey vinaigrette. small dish and big on taste and yum factor. I'd love to make an entire deli sandwich out of this duck ham. I should find their duck ham supplier.

• Tuna salad was a corn tostada served with pico de gallo, bell peppers, sesame seed and avocado (mushed up like guacamole). This tuna salad was served reminiscent of a ceviche, where you load up your own tostada.

• The corn husk steamed cod was a satisfying entree. Served with pickled corn puree, nopal pico de gallo, cilantro and lemon. A sort of sweet punch, versus spiciness. I think nopales/cactus is an underused dish in a lot of Mexican food.

• Roasted sweet potatoes are served up like giant French fries. Which is much more satisfying than pathetic thin sweet potato fries at so many other restaurants. The salsa macha the potatoes were paired with was dark and delicious, with a spicy kick that wasn't overpowering. I like the garlic and peanut kick of this particular salsa.
--------
According to our server, menus are rotated every 6 months and curated by a featured chef. Right now the feature chef is Pyet Despain, serving foods that are indigenous and native to the Americas. Bison, salmon, cod, quail, duck, etc. and no steak, chicken, or eggs. That's a good way cut out expensive eggs from a menu! A tip from our server was that everything on the dinner menu is in order of size, top-to-bottom and small-to-large. So the cod and bison meals are entrees that can be shared, although I feel like everything could be shared.

Good service here, too! Our server was attentive and mindful of time constraints. Our reservation was at 6:15PM, and we were on our way out of there by 7:35PM. Plenty of time to walk across the courtyard to the Mark Taper Forum for a performance of Fake It Until You Make It at 8:00PM.

The heaters in the outdoor seating tent are on full blast above each table, making the space warm and inviting. In fact, the table got hot to the touch and I started sweating at some point. I couldn't believe other patrons were wearing coats and scarves.

Bottom line: what a cool restaurant! It is inside of the Music Center on Grand. If you're attending a play, opera, or musical at the Dorothy Chandler Pavilion, Mark Taper Forum, or the Ahmanson, then you should make a reservation for Abernethy's.

top_reviews.content:
Took my dad here for a Father’s Day dinner, and holy moly.

This was not just delicious — this was one of the most unique and special restaurant experience I have ever had.

We ordered our sparkling water from a WATER MENU.

We selected our steak knives from a chest of options (my dad’s was made from the interior of a ‘67 Volkswagen Bug).

The duck fat potatoes were double-fried and among the best bites of food I (and my dad) have ever had.

The lamb ribs were like candy for adults.

The scallops were an absolute honor to enjoy.

My dad said the bread was the best he’s had. I think he wanted to kiss the baker.

And the steak was phenomenal — roasted over an open flame just feet from us. I could practically feel the heat as I dug in.

And we enjoyed it all at the Chef’s Counter, watching and listening to the beautiful show in front of us.

Gwen is sensational in every way. They even sent us home with applewood-smoked salt in silver tins.

My life is better because I dined at Gwen. If only my own children take me here one day…

Fabulous dining experience and exquisite food! We discovered the restaurant from the Eater youtube video about Gwen, which got us excited about the level of craftsmanship in the food. The actual experience far surpassed what we even expected after watching! We typically don’t like the Michelin restaurants that are too fine dining and try conceptual flavors. Gwen is nothing like that. Flavors are delicious, portions are large, you feel welcome as soon as you enter.

First the ambiance - it’s dark, moody, a little loud, open wood fired kitchen. We got sat upstairs which felt like a prohibition era speakeasy, already off to a great start.

All the food we ordered (listed below) was absolutely incredible, 10/10 on flavor and preparation. Favorites had to be the crudo, lamb ribs, corn pasta, and of course the ribeye. Everything was cooked to perfection, great texture, and again, just amazing flavor.

The service was also very attentive and you can tell they put a lot of pride in their work. They were easy to talk to, we made jokes together, they knew the menu like the back of their hand. But here’s what sets Gwen apart, if I could give 6/5 stars I would:

- they give you an amuse bouche, ours was a delicious tomato gazpacho with an herby oil, so refreshing and perfectly sweet/tangy.
- they let you choose your steak knife. We ordered the 36oz bone in ribeye off the special meat menu, and then the server came by with a closed wooden box, opened it and told us to each choose a knife, after which he would reveal their individual stories. It felt out of an adventure book! So we each selected and he proceeded to explain what they were made of, the brand, and special fun facts. Seriously elevated the experience, I’d bring back anyone you want to impress or have a good time: a date, family’s in town, your boss or a client.
- they finish the meal with a small tin of smoked salts made in house, as a takeaway token. We can’t wait to use them on a steak at home!

I can’t rave enough about Gwen. If you’ve been questioning whether to go, this is your sign to book the next available reservation.

Complimentary Food:
- the best crusty but soft bread and butter
- amuse bouche gazpacho
- finishing salts at end of meal

Food ordered:
- Yellowtail crudo
- lamb ribs
- stonefruit and smoked stracciatella
- garganelli corn pasta
- Busiate sausage and kale pasta
- 36oz bone in ribeye
- duck fat potatoes
- wax beans
- the banana passionfruit dessert
- the chocolate caramel dessert

My only recommendation to staff: half way through meal a different waiter started waiting on us. Neither the first waiter announced his leaving, nor the second announced her takeover, which would have been appreciated.

An Exceptional Dining Experience

We celebrated my birthday dinner at Gwen, and we had the opportunity to dine at the chef’s table. Watching the chefs work right in front of us made the evening feel like a truly unique and enjoyable experience.

Jason was our waiter and he was absolutely outstanding. He was incredibly kind, attentive, and professional. Every word and every interaction reflected genuine customer service and a true passion for hospitality. All of the other staff members were equally warm, welcoming, and attentive.

The level of service was truly another class. I understand Gwen may not receive a Michelin star this year, but honestly, the service we experienced felt beyond what I would expect even at a Michelin-starred restaurant.

From the food and chef’s table experience to the exceptional hospitality, everything came together to make my birthday celebration very special. Overall, fantastic experience, and definitely a place I would love to recommend and come back!

I loved my meal here, everything was delicious and the service was wonderful! My favorite items were the lobster ravioli (must order), the flat iron steak, and the side of creamed leeks & onions. We ordered a decent amount of food and they paced it out really well even though we had a later reservation time. I would definitely come back again!

From the moment we walked into Gwen’s, we knew we were in for something special. The filet mignon was absolutely outstanding—cooked to perfection and one of the best I’ve ever had.

What truly sets Gwen’s apart, though, is the service. Every staff member who passed our table seemed genuinely invested in making sure we had everything we needed. Empty dishes disappeared almost instantly, napkins were quietly refolded whenever we stepped away, and someone was always checking in without ever being intrusive. It’s first-class service that somehow still feels warm, comfortable, and homey—an incredibly difficult balance for any restaurant to achieve.

The highlight of the evening was when Chef Curtis Stone stopped by our table to ask how we were enjoying our meal. He was an absolute sweetheart and made us feel so welcome. Since we were celebrating my 66th birthday, he also surprised me with a beautifully boxed treat to take home, which was such a thoughtful touch.

At 66 years old, I’ve dined at countless restaurants, including many fine dining establishments, and I can honestly say this was my favorite dining experience. I’ve spent hundreds of dollars at other restaurants only to leave disappointed by the food or the service. At Gwen’s, every dollar was worth it. In fact, my husband—who usually has something to say about the bill—didn’t complain once. Instead, he couldn’t stop talking about how incredible the food and service were.

I had so many exceptional restaurants to choose from for my birthday celebration, and I am beyond grateful that I chose Gwen’s. It was an unforgettable evening, and we can’t wait to return.

The location is absolutely perfect if you want to be right in the center of the action, sitting directly across the street from Crypto.com Arena and L.A. Live. The rooms are sleek, modern, and exceptionally clean, offering a quiet sanctuary right in the middle of a bustling urban center. The bed was incredibly comfortable, the room tech was intuitive, and the large windows provided great views of the vibrant city streets below. Having top-tier amenities paired with a contemporary boutique aesthetic gives the property a very premium feel.

The service was excellent across the board. The front desk staff made check-in quick and welcoming, and the valet team was fast and organized. It is an ideal hub for anyone visiting for a weekend show or a city getaway.

Our stay at this hotel was okay but not outstanding in any way. The spaces were clean, the front desk staff was polite and efficient, and our room was spacious. However, the interior design feels a little dated — some chunky furniture in gaudy colors isn’t enough to create a modern boutique atmosphere. A small plus was the good free coffee in the café/breakfast room, though the one employee working there on weekend mornings didn't make much of an effort to be friendly or welcoming.|At our request, our room was in a quiet location — we did not experience the loud late night music described by some guests in previous reviews. On weekend nights, we only heard faint bass tones coming from a distance. The windowless bathroom had no functioning fan, so all the humidity always drifted into the room. |The gym, advertised on the website as “newly renovated” and “state of the art,” had several malfunctioning or broken machines, and there was visible water damage in one area om the ceiling. Also, a note inside our room incorrectly stated that the gym was open 24/7 (actual hours are 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.). |As for parking, the hotel participates in the same system used by many hotels and private lots in the area, making overnight parking anywhere other than hotel valet impossible. This hotel charges $66 per night for parking, taking ample advantage of that setup.|Overall, this place doesn’t quite live up to its self attributed image of a “trendy boutique hotel.” It would benefit from more careful maintenance, some design updates, and a more consistently professional, customer-friendly attitude. For what the hotel offers, it’s overpriced.

Simple, convenient, and a great base if you’re in the city for a game.

I rarely leave negative reviews, but after this happened for the second time, I felt it was important to share my experience.

I've been a loyal customer of Maisonetta since I moved to Bankside three years ago. I enjoy the food and have continued to support the restaurant, even paying extra for things like a very small side of sauce without complaint.

My first disappointing experience was with a Grubhub order. The lunch menu included a side dish, but when I went to pick up my order, I was told it was a "mistake" and that the meal didn't come with a side after all. Instead of honoring what was advertised, I was told no.

Today, on the Fourth of July, I had another frustrating experience. The restaurant was nearly empty; it was raining outside; there were plenty of open tables; and it was about an hour before closing. I chose to sit at a larger table and politely asked if it was okay. The employee initially said yes, then immediately changed his answer, saying, "The manager said no." When I asked to speak with the manager, I was told the manager wasn't around. Moments later, the employee changed his response again, saying it was actually okay to sit there.

Please don't tell customers, "The manager said no," when the manager isn't even present. That damages trust and puts employees in an awkward position. It gives the impression that "the manager" was being used as an excuse rather than providing an honest answer.

The issue isn't the table or the side dish—it's the inconsistent customer service and lack of confident leadership. Staff should be empowered and properly trained to make reasonable customer service decisions, especially when the restaurant is empty and there is no operational reason to say no.

As someone who has supported this restaurant for years, I found this experience disappointing. I hope management takes this feedback seriously by providing better on-site leadership and customer service training, because loyal customers deserve honesty and consistency.

Future brides looking for a wedding venue in LA -- DO IT!!!

I got married here on May 3rd, 2025, and I truly cannot rave enough about De La Nonna and The Let's Go Disco. We had a 120-person wedding and used both spaces -- De La Nonna for our ceremony and reception, and The Let's Go Disco for the after-party.

From the very beginning, the team was incredibly accommodating to all of our (many) creative requests. My husband is an illustrator and designer, so we created a fully custom escort wall where every guest was drawn by hand with their table number on the back. The team happily stored away and rearranged furniture to give us space between the two venues to make it happen.

In addition to the escort wall, we brought in some rentals like a photobooth, a heart-shaped arch, larger tables and chairs -- not because we needed to (they already had great options), but because we wanted big tables. They accommodated everything with no issues and no hidden charges, truly allowing us to transform the space into exactly what we envisioned.

We also wanted a champagne tower, and they had no problem letting us bring in a vendor -- they even helped serve champagne pre-ceremony so guests had drinks while they waited.

They provided two DJs, both of whom were amazing -- and if you can request DJ Seano, DO IT. He was truly incredible and MC'd our ceremony moments and wedding speeches flawlessly, collaborating with us to make sure the vibes were exactly what we wanted and that our favorite songs were played all night long.

The food was INCREDIBLE and this is another reason we wanted to do it here. Literally every single guest came up to us to tell us how incredible it was - the salads, the pizza, the oysters - everything was PERFECTION.

Our day flowed seamlessly from pre-ceremony champagne service, to ceremony, to cocktail hour with amazing hors d'oeuvres, to our dinner reception (complete with speeches and a family tradition game of bingo), and then into The Let's Go Disco for our first dance, cake cutting, and an unforgettable party.

We were a little nervous about getting married in DTLA, especially for out-of-town guests unfamiliar with the area, but between the Arts District's private security and the two dedicated security guards provided by De La Nonna/The Let's Go Disco, everyone felt completely safe and taken care of and we had zero issues!!!

What truly made this experience exceptional, beyond the food and the chic, beautiful space, was the staff. From planning through the wedding day itself, they were thoughtful, attentive, and genuinely invested in making sure everything felt special and seamless. As I was walking down the aisle, I made eye contact with one of the staff members -- and she was crying!! That moment says everything.

I truly cannot imagine a better place to get married in Los Angeles. Thank you to everyone -- and especially Jose, Mia, and Patrick -- for making all of our wedding dreams come true.

name: Kato Restaurant
address: 777 S Alameda St Bldg 1, Suite 114, Los Angeles, CA 90021, United States

top_reviews.content: Kato gives a very modern, minimalist vibe that I loved. I sat at the bar as a walk-in, but I’d recommend making a reservation. I ordered their shaved ice drink with yogurt base and guava, which was delicious and refreshing. I also had the toasted honey garlic bread:a pull-apart garlic bread that was absolutely amazing. Overall it feels like more of an experience than just a quick stop. The service was excellent, and the food looked incredible. That said, the tasting menu leans heavily toward seafood, so it’s definitely a great spot for non-vegetarians and seafood lovers. As a vegetarian, my options were more limited, but everything I had was fantastic.

Overall take: Kato is not “better Chinese food.” It is Chinese/Taiwanese memory translated into a Western tasting-menu operating system. That translation is disciplined, but it does not necessarily deepen the original cuisine.

The best course was the sour-cabbage fish: technically excellent fish texture and crisp scale, with clean fermented acidity. But the meal did not produce enough memory points, and the broths - supposedly the backbone of the concept - lacked the depth and layering of top-tier Chinese cuisine. The two savory courses overlapped, especially the sesame oil chicken/quail and roasted duck, and the star anise note was too heavy. Desserts were fine, with the white strawberry being more interesting.

Service at the late seating felt tired and impersonal, with slow pacing. Biggest gap between dishes was ~30mins. Their Kato Sauvignon matched really well with the seafood dishes, I’d have that over the pairing program.

Overall: strong one-star level, not convincing as two-star, and not a place I need to revisit soon

Kato honestly exceeded expectations. The flavors were rich, balanced, and incredibly refined. The caviar added a luxurious touch without overpowering the dish, and the presentation was absolutely beautiful. Every bite felt carefully crafted and full of flavor. Easily one of the most memorable dining experiences for anyone who loves elegant food and fine details.
Definitely a place I’d recommend if you enjoy elegant dining, unique flavors, and beautifully presented food.

Outstanding Service, Beautiful Space, but the Food Didn’t Quite Justify the Price

We booked a birthday dinner for two at Kato and were excited to experience one of Los Angeles’ most celebrated Michelin-starred restaurants. As fans of Asian-inspired cuisine, we were looking forward to creative flavor combinations and a memorable tasting menu.

The evening started with a small scheduling mishap on my part—I had booked from a different time zone and accidentally mixed up our reservation time. Thankfully, the maître d’ was incredibly gracious and accommodated a change, which we greatly appreciated given we were driving from Orange County and battling Saturday evening traffic into Downtown LA.

Kato’s location in the ROW DTLA complex is impressive, and the restaurant itself is stunning. The industrial design is warm and inviting, with personal touches from the chef and a full view of the kitchen that adds to the Michelin-star experience.

The cocktail program was excellent—creative, balanced, and delicious.

As for the tasting menu, the meal leaned more seafood-forward than I expected. Everything was technically well executed and beautifully presented, but surprisingly few dishes left a lasting impression. The menu felt cohesive, though many courses blended together by the end of the evening.

The standout moments were:

* The squab was outstanding. Meaty, well roasted.
*The duck course, served with foie gras, truffle, and warm seeded bread. Spreading the foie gras onto the bread and pairing it with a bite of duck was absolutely heavenly.
* The desserts, especially the Suannai, a tart Meyer lemon meringue creation accented with mint and osmanthus. As someone who loves bright, acidic desserts, this was easily my favorite dish of the night.
* The service, which was impeccable throughout. The staff were friendly, attentive, and professional, keeping the meal moving at a comfortable pace while always seeming to appear exactly when we needed water, another drink, or assistance.

We also opted for the Jinsha lobster supplement at an additional $55 per person. Unfortunately, this was the biggest disappointment of the evening. The portion was surprisingly small, and I struggled to detect the salted egg flavor that was supposed to define the dish.

By the time drinks, taxes, and service charges were added, dinner approached $550+ per person. While that’s not unusual for a Michelin-starred tasting menu in Los Angeles, I left feeling that the overall experience didn’t quite justify the cost.

I’m glad I finally had the opportunity to try Kato. The service, atmosphere, and a handful of dishes were excellent. However, considering the price point and the fact that most of the menu didn’t leave a strong impression, it’s probably not a restaurant I would return to. For those seeking polished service and a refined dining experience, it’s worth trying once—but it didn’t become a personal favorite.

We eat to live, but sometimes the experience is immersive art. Kato in Downtown LA is such a place. James Beard award winning Chef Jon Yao knows how to feed your soul and your senses. The minimalist decor with outstanding Taiwanese inspired courses, puts on a gastronomic show you won’t soon forget. A recent birthday dinner left me feeling pampered and satisfied with food that made you slow down and close your eyes. From the best ice cold martinis, creative cocktails, exemplary service and a tasting menu to die for, Kato is a must for that special date or celebratory occasion. Each dish on their lovely tasting menu was powerful. From the small bite starters like Yao’s yóutiao, to Tile fish, Cumin Lamb, oxtail, and the velvety, mouth- watering duck breast with crispy perilla leaf, the artistry just didn’t stop. So please go and become star-struck over each lovely bite, because there was not one disappointment or mis-step. Here’s to the meal of my dreams and I can’t wait to dine at Kato again!

4.8/5 ### Guzzu Bento-Ya: Elevating Lunch with Wild Salmon Perfection

Nestled in the vibrant Arts District at 1102 Lawrence Street in Downtown LA, Guzzu Bento-Ya is a breath of fresh air for anyone craving authentic Japanese bentos with a California twist. Opened by the innovative team behind MoMo Paradise, this spot channels the convenience of Japan's Shinkansen boxed lunches but amps it up with locally sourced ingredients and bold flavors. It's open for lunch only (10 AM to 3 PM, closed Sundays), making it an ideal midday escape—whether you're grabbing takeout for the office or dining in their sleek, minimalist space with communal tables and a nod to modern Japanese design.

What truly hooked me on my first visit was the Wild Salmon Bento, a standout that earns every bit of its glowing reputation. Priced at around $20, this bento arrives as a work of edible art: flaky, sustainably sourced wild salmon grilled to juicy perfection, its natural richness enhanced by a subtle soy glaze and hints of yuzu zest. The fish melts in your mouth, balancing buttery fat with a clean, oceanic freshness that's worlds away from farmed varieties. It's paired masterfully with a medley of sides that elevate the entire experience—a mound of fluffy rice sprinkled with aonori furikake for that umami punch, crisp pickled daikon from local Alvin Farms, tender miso-cured egg yolk that's creamy and indulgent, and seasonal veggies like roasted kabocha squash from Baloian Farms in Fresno. Every element harmonizes without overwhelming, creating a symphony of textures: the salmon's soft flakiness against the rice's subtle chew, the pickles' bright tang cutting through the richness.

I couldn't resist adding a side of chicken karaage—crispy, mildly spiced bites that were shatteringly golden and moist inside—but the salmon stole the show. Service is swift and warm; the staff explained sourcing details with genuine enthusiasm, and my order was ready in under five minutes during peak lunch rush. The overall vibe? Effortlessly cool, with prices that feel like a steal for such premium quality. Yelp raves align with my take, averaging 4.8/5 from over 276 reviews, praising the bentos' authenticity and value. I've since returned for the mackerel and pork katsu options, but the wild salmon remains my benchmark for excellence.
