top_reviews.content:
I randomly picked a breakfast spot near the hotel, and it was surprisingly delicious!!!

Breakfast Sandwich: Simple, classic ingredients, yet a dreamlike flavor. Made to order, the bacon was crispy but not hard, the avocado puree was smooth and fragrant, the vegetables were crisp and juicy, and the soft-boiled egg and cheese were perfectly runny; but the most beautiful part was the toast itself—crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and with each bite, the slightly charred edges gently cracked open—it was simply divine.

Breakfast Burrito: I chose the non-spicy avocado salsa (green sauce). The tortilla was soft yet chewy, the egg and bacon were aromatic, and the potatoes and pinto beans were delicate and firm. It had a slight spiciness, but not overpowering. The sauce was mainly tangy, which helped cut through the richness. Overall, it was pretty good, very filling, but definitely not as good as the Breakfast Sandwich.

Iced Latte, Iced Matcha Latte: The coffee was just average, but the portion was big! The latte was better than the matcha latte, the latter was a bit bitter.

Stopped by Tiago Coffee Bar + Kitchen for brunch after a long walk around the Walk of Fame, and it was exactly what I needed. The latte came in a generously sized mug, and the breakfast sandwich was much bigger than I expected. It was so filling that I managed to finish my coffee but couldn’t finish the whole sandwich!

The sandwich was delicious, with plenty of ingredients and perfectly toasted bread, and the café has a nice, relaxed atmosphere. It’s also in a great location if you’re exploring Hollywood and need a good brunch spot.

If your into punch cards to get coffee this is my favorite spot for this! The entire menu doesn't ever disappoint and I really love the I love the soups here. Christopher is a very kind person who I see before or after my yoga class and always lets me sit drink coffee and journal before or after my yoga class. The creative interiors and murals remind one that we are almost out of Hollywood and the crazy that happens there but West Hollywood where everything is cleaner and kinder.

The beef sandwich is amazing and I absolutely loved my honey cinnamon latte. Most places don’t add enough spice and this one had it just right. The music and atmosphere was awesome, inviting and clean. I’d definitely stop by the next time I’m in the area while visiting LA.

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Review:

Tiago Coffee Bar + Kitchen is easily one of the best coffee spots on Hollywood Blvd! They roast their own beans in-house, and you can really taste the difference in their house brews, cold brew, and specialty lattes.

The food menu is fantastic—the Breakfast Sandwich on sourdough and the Breakie Burrito are absolute must-tries, made with fresh, high-quality ingredients. The atmosphere is warm, bright, and welcoming, and the staff are always friendly and attentive. Plus, having parking validation right in Hollywood is a huge bonus. Highly recommend stopping by for coffee, breakfast, or lunch!

The breakfast was absolutely amazing—without a doubt, the best we’ve had in California throughout our entire trip. The presentation was stunning, and the meal itself was incredibly nourishing, rich in various components, and packed with healthy ingredients. There was a lot of fresh greens, pumpkin seeds, and the salad was perfectly dressed. A huge thank you to the chef and the owner for providing such delicious and high-quality food!

top_reviews.content: Wow!! Always wanted to go but every time I would think about it, it was booked.  I finally found a 5:00pm reservation and when we showed up there was a line outside.  It moved quickly once the doors opened and everyone was dressed casual and some were walk ins.  Our waiter said they offer counter service for walk ins.  They had a card for our anniversary waiting when we arrived and we got a cute booth in the main room.  We started with a cosmo martini and old fashion- both tasted great and have a nice kick.  We ordered the bone in ribeye which was cooked perfectly and over an open fire which gives it that crispy putter edge.  The steak was the best I’ve had in LA so far.. also had the popular fettuccine Alfredo and it was again cooked perfectly and tasted amazing.  They also bring out complementary sourdough bread and butter, and water.  They brought us a brownie dessert with a scoop of ice cream and candle for our anniversary and we also ordered the crème brûlée which had that amazing break thru crust, and was plenty for 2 of us.  Our server was Nick and he was amazing!!  We will for sure be back.

This was a very cool place and a trip into Hollywood folklore. This is Hollywood's oldest restaurant dating back to 1919! This was a bucket list experience for us. We were in town for a few shows on the strip and met up with my cousin that suggested we eat here and i'm glad we did! That onion soup and the filet were both great!! Great food, great ambience and great service too. Definitely hit this joint up while you're here!

A classic Hollywood experience. I ordered the onion soup and the filet mignon with a baked potato—everything was excellent. The steak was cooked perfectly and the soup was rich and flavorful. The waiters were very well trained and professional, which made the service feel polished and attentive.

The interior design is old and magnificent, giving the restaurant a timeless atmosphere that really adds to the experience. The complimentary bread and butter were also good, although the bread could have been a bit fresher. Overall, a wonderful dining experience and a great place to enjoy a classic meal on Hollywood Boulevard.

I heard so much hype of this place. Ill say the history is fantastic the vibe is amazing and the service is stellar. The food is less to be desired. Me personally I don't like to drink but I have been told they have excellent martinis. I came here to eat and their onion soup was amazing the meat itself was just okay. For the price I paid I would expected more. For the history alone, it's a place to stop by.

My wife and I finally had the opportunity to dine at Musso & Frank, and the experience exceeded every expectation we had.

We had an 8:30 PM reservation, and although they had already sold out of the famous prime rib, our waiter Robert recommended the bone-in pork chop instead. It turned out to be an outstanding recommendation—perfectly cooked, incredibly flavorful, and one of the best pork chops I’ve had.

My wife ordered the scallops, and they were absolutely phenomenal. We both agreed they were some of the best scallops we’ve ever had.

Of course, we couldn’t leave without trying the famous dirty martini, and it absolutely lived up to its reputation. It paired perfectly with the meal and is a must-order for anyone visiting.

We finished the evening with the crème brûlée, which was easily among the best we’ve ever had. The caramelized sugar had the perfect crack, and the custard was rich, smooth, and beautifully balanced.

What truly made the evening special was the service. Robert was attentive, knowledgeable, and happy to answer every question we had without ever making us feel rushed. His recommendations made an already memorable dinner even better.

From the classic atmosphere to the exceptional food and impeccable hospitality, it’s easy to understand why Musso & Frank has remained a Los Angeles institution for more than a century.

This won’t be our last visit. Thank you to Robert and the entire team for an unforgettable evening.

★★★★★

Outstanding old style, fine dining with out of this world food taste and quality. We’ve visiting this place every time we visit LA and for many years the quality is outstanding. This time we ordered beef tartare and salmon tartare for appetizers, scallops and sand dubs for the entree. Tartare were super fresh with homemade chips. Scallops were tender, while sand dubs were full of taste and done right. Will definitely get back.

Musso & Franks Grill is a world class dining experience. My wife and I are locals and came out celebrating our daughter that is about to be born.

Thankfully, despite having no reservation, we were able to snag comfortable bar seats at opening (the bar seats have a back and are comfortable!). Then, I was able to have a perfect martini with sidecar (good on you Musso & Franks). My wife had a lovely Mocktail. And then we enjoyed their delicious bread and some olives/cheese.

The entrees were amazing. I had the Ribeye and my wife the Salmon with us sharing the Gratin Potatoes. All delicious! The second dirty martini with blue cheese olives was even better than the first.

Overall, what sealed the night for us was the kindness of Robert who took care of us. We enjoyed our conversation. And we were thankful for his and Musso & Franks graciousness of the free desert. We weren’t expecting it at all and were touched.

It’s not often where you get to eat at an LA historical landmark, a place rooted in good food, and encounter a staff that saw us beyond just customers.

Thank you Musso & Franks. Never change.

Went here with a work party and so happy that we did. It was very surprising. Cool place that’s been around forever. It was neat to hear the history and legacy of this restaurant. Our server was Luis. He’s been there 14 years! The food was actually better than expected. Im not a wine connoisseur but I do know good from bad and thought the Musso and Frank wine was pretty good. The place is dark, it’s part of the charm and ambience. You do need to dress up a little bit. No hats! And wear a collard shirt. I got the short rib special and dang happy with that choice. Everyone said their dish was great. Good quality food at decent prices. Happy we got to experience this place.

Last night we had dinner at Dominick’s in the Bronx, and honestly, it became one of the highlights of our entire New York trip.

From the moment we walked in, the owner treated us like family. Not like customers. Family. The kind of place where you immediately feel welcomed, comfortable, and at home.

The food was absolutely spectacular the kind of Italian food that reminds you why New York is legendary. Every dish felt homemade, full of tradition, love, and pride. You could taste the history in every bite.

What made the experience so special wasn’t just the incredible food… it was the feeling. Sitting there felt less like eating at a restaurant and more like being invited into someone’s home for Sunday dinner.

In a city full of places to eat, Dominick’s gave us something unforgettable: authenticity, warmth, and a memory we’ll talk about for years. I wish I had photos to share but we enjoyed this so much we forgot about our phones.

Special Thank you to Charlie, from this Texas family for such a wonderful night. My family will absolutely be back next time we visit New York!
Love this place! Especially after a visit to NYBG.

I absolutely love coming to Dominick’s. Me and my husband make it a point to come to Arthur Avenue

I could not have asked for anything more and our expectations were exceeded on every level. Our server was fantastic and clearly explained the menu. The atmosphere is also something that truly transports you to Italy itself.

The chef’s dedication to his craft clearly comes through in the food. On top of it, Roberto’s is devoid of the artificial stuffiness and greedy price gouging that sometimes consumes successful establishments. It truly felt genuinely Italian and that is why we chose this restaurant.

I highly recommend eating here without any hesitation, and would 100% do so again. If only this was in our home state! Nevertheless, thank you for a truly memorable birthday for my husband and unforgettable experience for myself.

One of my all time fav outside of Rome.  Trust me the best best

The breakfast was excellent from start to finish. The eggs were light, fluffy, and full of flavor. The avocado, finished with a generous drizzle of olive oil, was simple but incredibly delicious. Every ingredient tasted fresh and thoughtfully prepared.

If you’re looking for a memorable breakfast in Los Angeles, Salt’s Cure is well worth the visit. I’ll definitely be back for those griddle cakes.

Salt's Cure is my favorite breakfast spot in Los Angeles. The pancakes are worth the trip on their own, delicious, and everything tastes fresh, carefully made, and full of intention. The food consistently delivers. Service, however, can be hit or miss, which makes a suggested tip that starts at 22% + feel a bit disconnected from the actual experience. Benny is the HUGE exception. He's welcoming, attentive, and a reminder of what great hospitality looks like. If the service matched the quality of the food, this place would be hard to beat.

It's a cute place for breakfast/brunch. Not as crowded for weekend brunch as other location. Solid option for classic breakfast.

Service was quick, accurate, and we had a lovely chat with our server.

Parking is a bit limited since it is street parking. Crap shoot on that.

The sourdough toast was a bit over toasted and oily. Will ask for a dry light toast next time to avoid the burnt bits. The coffee was good, and the eggs were cooked exactly as ordered.

Would return another time to try other menu items.

I went for the oat pancakes and wasn't disappointed. They top the pancakes with a nice molasses butter which is why they don't have syrup.

The All-Star plate was huge. The biscuit was fluffy and buttery. Their bacon is not your typical bacon so don't expect anything salty.

The sausage, egg, and cheese was extremely savory so it was nice that they served a side of pickles to cut the taste. It was really good.

The service could have been better. We got our menus and water and waited. The server came around to the tables adjacent and behind us on both sides. He didn't take our order. We waited more and still nothing. We put our menus aside to hint to the server that we were ready...nothing. He again, checked in on the three tables around us.

Salts cure was a mixed experience, came for brunch on a Saturday and had a great time however there were some sub par aspects. The food was for the most part delicious, the pancakes are actually out of this world and worth it on their own. The breakfast combo was solid but the meat was a little overcooked and a lot of the flavors just blended together. Service could be improved, took us a while to order and get our food but the wait staff were friendly and accommodating. Worth a stop for the pancakes alone but not incredible.

They will openly engage you in conversation and make you feel like you are a distant family member who has stopped into their living room for a visit. Its one of my mom and I'm favorite ways to spend an early Sunday evening.  You can feel the lovethey pour into the Ethiopian dishes and ambiance.  If you are anywhere the Bradhurst district in Harlem and are looking for an unassuming but magical casual dining experience,  definitely check out Benyam!

Ethiopian, intimate, clean.  Food is delicious.  Try the honey wine.  The staff accommodates.  I eat here as often as every weekend.

The sampler was ok I only likes the potatoes and lentils. I am not opposed to trying Ethiopian-food again if I could find a restaurant that offers mild not only hot spices.

top_reviews.content: Really a great and very unique restaurant. First of all, the bread is more than great and completely different from any other bread in the United States. In the restaurant, you feel as if you are in Egypt or any other Arab country. The prices are reasonable, and the area where the restaurant is located is very lively 🌸🌸

Review of Arth Aljanathain Restaurant – A Hidden Gem with Exceptional Service and Food

If you’re looking for a small yet extraordinary dining experience, Arth Aljanathain is the place to be. This hidden gem may be modest in size, but it delivers big on flavor and hospitality.

From the moment you step inside, you’re greeted with warm and friendly service that makes you feel right at home. The staff is attentive, ensuring that every detail of your meal is perfect, and their passion for hospitality truly shines through.

Now, let’s talk about the food—simply outstanding! Every dish is prepared with fresh ingredients, rich flavors, and an authentic touch that leaves a lasting impression. Whether you’re craving traditional dishes or something unique, the menu offers a delightful variety that caters to different tastes. The presentation is beautiful, and each bite is a burst of flavor that keeps you coming back for more.

Despite its small size, Arth Aljanathain has a cozy and inviting atmosphere that adds to the overall charm. It’s the kind of place where you not only enjoy a fantastic meal but also feel like part of a family.

If you haven’t visited yet, you’re truly missing out. This restaurant is proof that great things come in small packages. Highly recommended!

Yemeni food in the heart of the Bronx. Authentic, flavorful and economical. We had the Lamb Haneeth, 10/10 and also had the hummus with meat 9/10.  They start you off with broth soup & salad & the bread was perfect.  Cost about $20 a person and we got a few cold drinks.

Overall 4 stars. Not bad. We went as a family of seven .

I will first start with positive:

1. Salmon portions is large compared to other Yemeni restaurant around
2. Free tea for all customers
3. Free soup and salad with all dish
4. Soup is quite good
5. The food is ready very quickly.
6. This is located right next to the masjid. So I can pray and come back during prayer time.
7. The guy understood the English very well. Sometimes it is not the case.

Negative side:

1. Small restaurant. Difficult for a large family to sit together
2. The falafel is not cooked well inside.
3. Lamb hanith, I think the meat is not baby lamb. But not bad.
4. The meat portion is less compared to other Yemeni restaurants that we have visited.
5. Difficult to get parking specially during prayer time.
6. Kunafa desert seems not very authentic. It is full of coconut. I have kunafa before. It supposed to be very creamy and smooth.

Please see the latest menu as of January 2025 in the picture.

Delicious Yemeni food.

I was very impressed by the food I ate at Arth Aljanathain. I have eaten there a few times. I have had a chance to taste several of the dishes.

The restaurant interior is decorated with scenic images of Yemen framed with white border. That same white border is used to create decorative geometric patterns on the wall.

You get a good sized portion of food on each plate. So far, I have had the Zurbian chicken, which is aromatic rice and pieces of chicken buried within the rice. I tried the roasted chicken and rice dish, and salmon, both were superb. Some of the meals come with a small soup and salad. I really enjoyed the hummus and bread dish. You can taste the tahini in the hummus and the bread was light and soft. It is one of the best flat breads I have ever had.

For drinks, there are many to choose from. I had a Ayran mint flavored yogurt drink (one of my favorites). I also had a Laziza regular malt beverage. Laziza "regular" is an unsweetened malt beverage that is pleasant and refreshing.

On your way out do not forget to grab a small espresso sized cup of slightly sweetened tea.

The food at Arth Aljanathain does not disappoint. I will surely be going back for more.

An absolutely phenomenal restaurant experience. The first dish was probably one of the best things I’ve ever had. Everything was beautifully themed around fire, ash and charring food, but it was so balanced. The wine pairing was also unique and a surprising adventure on its own.
The restaurant is slightly too big and it didn’t feel like an intimate restaurant experience. But it was still in the top of my list!

Meteroa was one of the most memorable dining experiences we've ever had. Every aspect of the evening felt like a journey through sensory exploration and playfulness. The ambiance was beautifully curated, and the food carried just as much texture and depth as the space itself.

We spent nearly two hours enjoying the 6 course experience, and the pacing was absolutely perfect. Every dish had layers of complimentary flavor and textures.  Each course felt interactive. One dish was even audible! We especially loved the hearth-driven cooking, smoky flavors added incredible depth without ever overpowering the ingredients.

The team also accommodated our dietary restrictions with care.  From the atmosphere to the impeccable service and the creativity behind every dish, Meteroa delivered an immersive, intentional, and unforgettable evening.

Exceptional restaurant with not only amazing atmosphere and presentation but also perfect harmony is flavors. Each dish felt like they were carefully curated with flavors in perfect balance. Husband and I did the 6 course with hybrid pairing and was a phenomenal anniversary dinner.

I brought a small group to Meteora to celebrate a special achievement. The experience exceeded expectations in every way possible! The food was outstanding, with some really creative presentations. The service was absolutely impeccable ... the staff are all so personable and helped accentuate the overall experience. And the atmosphere/setting was truly unique.

I've eaten at numerous Michelin star restaurants in my life, including quite a few triple stars. This overall experience was among the best of my life, and was the very best for several of my guests. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

A calm retreat in LA, featuring a diverse, creative menu. Each dish yields a tasting sensation while portion sizes won’t overwhelm you. Service was professional; wait staff were knowledgeable and quietly present at all the right times. The wine list offered nice variety in a range of prices. The duck was fabulous. The seating offered comfort and appropriate privacy while not isolating diners. The environment was reflective and moody. Our evening was perfect .
Well done Team Mateora. I expect a second star soon.

This is one of those restaurants you wish there was a 6th star Google would allow you to give! Ambiance, service, food, experience...just everything is AMAZING!

We had the 6 course menu with the Avocado and caviar supplement. Every course was memorable!

Their wine list wasn't my thing, so we brought our own bottle and the corkage fee was $75. A little steep, but appropriate for a Michelin restaurant.

When you enter, take your time to appreciate the way they have brought nature into the environment. From twisted vines, to live greenery, to agate and other stone, you feel like you're exploring a lost jungle on the Amazon!

Nice spot. Very good decor, we had the tasting menu and enjoyed it.

The dishes were all very good, and we very much appreciated the service and stories with each item. The final dishes could have been more creative but were also tasty.

Vegan menu was same price as regular for one of our guests which we thought was a bit rich.

Mom and I are plant-based. Fine dining vegan can be hit or miss, so while I was pleased that they could accommodate us, I can’t say I had high expectations going in. But the vegan menu, wine pairing, and NA pairing were all really fantastic.

It’s quite obvious when a chef is thoughtful (or knowledgeable?) enough about their craft to create an inclusive experience that highlights plant-based ingredients with the same intention, creativity, and flavor as the standard menu. Seriously, wow!

The 6-course menu, with all accompaniments, was satisfying both in terms volume and flavor. We spent a lot of time reflecting on how energizing it is to be exposed to a variety of global ingredients prepared with new [to us] cooking techniques during the same sitting.

5 stars across for presentation. We loved the music. The restaurant is obviously gorgeous - while elevated, it wasn’t as stuffy as some of its industry counterparts. My only critique is that we were eating as fast as we could but different servers kept trying to clear our plates before we were finished.

Overall, I definitely recommend. I hope to come back and experience that gorgeous PDR soon! Thank you to the entire team.

Had dinner here with two friends on July 6th, 2025. The space has a warm and rustic-industrial vibe, fitting for a modern Italian restaurant that’s earned its Michelin nod. The service was attentive without being intrusive, and the staff gave helpful recommendations throughout the evening.

We started with the brodetto, a comforting bowl of steamed clams and mussels served with toasted crostini. The seafood was fresh and flavorful, and the broth had a savory depth that paired nicely with the crispy bread. A great way to begin the meal.

For pasta, we tried the mandilli, which were vibrant green, handkerchief-like sheets of pasta with a delicate, buttery sauce. The texture was silky and smooth—simple but elegant. The pappardelle with slow-braised pork was rich and satisfying, with wide ribbons of pasta soaking up the meaty, aromatic sauce.

We also shared one of their ligurian focaccinas—the funghi—which came with melted cheese, wild mushrooms, and fresh herbs on a thin, crisp pastry base. The crust was light and flaky, and the mushrooms added an earthy contrast to the richness of the cheese.

While the meal was overall delicious and thoughtfully prepared, we found that some dishes were a touch too salty, especially the pork pappardelle. It didn’t ruin the experience, but it’s worth noting for those sensitive to seasoning.

Portions were fair, and the pricing reflected the quality and presentation. All in all, this is a great spot for upscale Italian fare with bold flavors and creative execution. We’d gladly return, perhaps to try more from the seafood and vegetable sections of the menu.

The staff was warm, welcoming and very helpful. The food was absolutely delicious - from the breads, salads, pastas to main dishes. I had the best endive salad of my life here. The foccacia is absolutely brilliant. The pasta sauces are lovingly crafted to nestle the pillows of dough. The wine list was a wonderful survey of Italian wines, and the sommelier knew her craft. Most of all, I loved the true Italian cooking that was definitely not the Italian - American interpretation so many American restaurants disappoint us with.

Steel, Silk & Saffron: Dining at The Factory Kitchen
.
LOS ANGELES, CA - Tucked into the raw-boned charm of LA’s Arts District, The Factory Kitchen is the kind of place that makes you rethink what “Italian” means in America. This isn’t red-checkered tablecloths and marinara clichés — it’s Northern Italian soul food dressed in urban grit and Michelin polish.
.
Chef Angelo Auriana’s menu reads like a love letter to Liguria and Lombardy, with a few Hollywood winks. The Mandilli di Seta — silk handkerchief pasta draped in almond basil pesto — is the dish that’s earned cult status, and for good reason: it’s as delicate as it is decadent. The Focaccina Calda di Recco arrives crisp, molten with Crescenza cheese, and frankly deserves its own fan club. Seafood lovers will find the Ravioli di Mare a briny, buttery knockout, while carnivores can sink into the Porchetta—herb-perfumed, slow-roasted, and unapologetically rich.
.
Prices hover in the mid-to-high range — pastas around $26–$28, mains in the $30s — but the quality and execution make it feel like you’re getting away with something. Desserts like the Cannoli and Paciugo are worth lingering over, especially with a final Negroni in hand.
.
The space itself is a study in contrasts: exposed brick, steel beams, and wide garage doors that spill golden-hour light across polished concrete floors. It’s industrial, yes, but softened by the hum of conversation, the clink of wine glasses, and a staff that moves with the precision of a well-rehearsed ballet. Service is warm without being cloying—knowledgeable, confident, and quick to steer you toward the night’s best catch or a hidden gem on the wine list.
.
In a city obsessed with the next big thing, The Factory Kitchen proves that timeless craft, rooted in tradition but plated with modern swagger, will always be in style. This isn’t just dinner—it’s a masterclass in how to turn a factory floor into a temple of flavor.

We made this reservation a month in advanced but had a disappointing Valentine’s dinner.

When we arrived, the man who escorted us to our table sat us down, and said directly to me, “You’re taller than me, so you win” gesturing to my girlfriend. This was a very off putting way to start the night. Staff shouldn’t objectify women on Valentines Day.

15 minutes after sitting without any interaction from staff, Tyler approached our table and asked “has anyone offered you water yet?” We would’ve appreciated water sooner.

Tyler poured our water and took our drink orders. When he brought our drinks 10 minutes later, he took our order for starters. We ordered the palamita and scottona.

15 minutes later, a man that we hadn’t interacted with yet abruptly approaches our table and says “Ok, what can I get you?” in a harsh tone. I believe his name was Jeff (which I only learned from Tyler who asked shortly after receiving our starters). From him, we ordered the mandilli di seta, and the casonzei.

On the food, we were most happy with the palamita, but even that was just ok. The scottona was chewy and sinewy, only satisfactory on the edges where there was some roast flavor and seasoning. All other dishes were heavily underseasoned, and the pastas arrived only a tad over room temperature. After dividing between our share plates, our first bites were cold (<60 seconds after hitting our table).

When the expo brought our pastas, I asked what the first one was, and he said “that’s our flagship pasta” without further comment- we now know it was the mandilli, but he should’ve said.

As we ate, we both agreed that the food was just barely ok not to warrant mentioning it to our server(s?).

Still, we finished our pastas before anyone even came to ask how it was tasting. As our plates were bussed, we asked Tyler for the check and he responded “Ok, so we have some amazing deserts tonight, but I could bring you the check if you really want” slightly passive-aggressive.

For the price, we would not return considering the level of service and quality of dishes we experienced.

I want to get my pancake slice after cutting it. Hash brown was also breaking even I had it fried well...

We went for breakfast with four people. The place was big and spacious. Service speed was avarage but the staff were friendly and helpful. The breakfast had many tasty and good-quality options. Price were also reasonable and we had a nice experience.

We kicked things off with mozzarella sticks — crispy outside, gooey inside, a solid starter. For mains, we had the steak tips with scrambled eggs, hash browns, and onions, a stack of (protein) chocolate chip pancakes, and the cinnamon roll pancakes loaded with caramel, cream cheese drizzle, and whipped cream.

The steak tips were tender and flavorful with the sautéed onions and mushrooms, eggs were fluffy, and the hash browns had that perfect crispy edge. The pancakes hit both ends of the spectrum: the chocolate chip ones gave classic comfort, while the cinnamon roll stack was pure indulgence.

The coffee was great — smooth, hot, and refilled often, which is always a win. Service was quick and friendly too.

The only downside isn’t the food, it’s the location. The restaurant itself is good, but the area feels a bit unsafe with a lot of homeless activity around. The back door was locked, so we had to walk around to the front entrance, which was inconvenient.

Overall: solid IHOP food and service, but the surroundings may be off-putting depending on the time of day you visit.

top_reviews.content: I dinned here for a celebratory birthday dinner with high expiations. The day prior to my reservation I received a text message from the restaurant asking me if there were any food allergies and if I wanted to pre-order any of the specials which was nice. I confirmed the food allergies and requested a pre-order for the Dover Sole but received no reply after that.  When I arrived day of reservations the staff was welcoming and we were seated immediate. Dinner started off with the complimentary Amuse Bouche and dare I say it was the best bite of the night. For starters I ordered the beet salad and endive salad. Beet salad was favorite of the two. It was served topped with shaved ice and pickily beet juice which made it a little fun. Endive salad had good flavor as well but nothing significant or memorable. I do not recall the name of the NA cocktail I got but it was delightful. Now for the main course... I ordered the Dover Sole which is one of my favorite fish and have had it numerous times so had very high hopes for it. Sadly it was the biggest disappointment of the night. They bring it out cooked and it is deboned and prepared at your table. Firstly there was still bones in the fish after it was prepared. Second the fish was overcooked. Third it was served cold and fourth it barley had any flavor to it. This was a huge disappointment especially at $160. We obviously didn't finish it so the waiter asked if we liked it and I let her know what we thought. One of the staff members came by to apologies and said they would comp the coffee and dessert we ordered to make up for it. Does it make up for a terrible main course, I don't think so but it was a nice gesture nevertheless. It was a nice experience overall and the staff was wonderful but no need to go back.

⭐️⭐️ (1.6/5)

Made a reservation at Camphor after seeing the hype online—especially the $38 wagyu/duck burger. My wife and I were excited to try it, but the experience didn’t live up to expectations.

First impression matters, and unfortunately the hostess didn’t represent a fine dining environment well. She was dressed nicely, but her shoes were extremely dirty, which immediately gave an off-putting, almost unsanitary vibe. For a place at this price point, details like that shouldn’t be overlooked.

The restaurant itself is clean and thoughtfully arranged given the limited space. The tables were stable and well-kept, and the music was at a great level. However, the temperature inside was uncomfortable—warm and a bit muggy—which made it hard to fully enjoy the experience.

The menu was another issue: very small font and minimal descriptions. It felt like you had to rely heavily on the server to explain dishes instead of the menu doing that job. For a higher-end restaurant, I expected clearer and more informative presentation.

Food-wise, the Seabream dish (with uni and green apple) was actually very good—unique and nicely presented. However, the burger that drew us in was a major letdown. It wasn’t undercooked, but it was soggy and lacked flavor. For $38, I expected something memorable, but it honestly didn’t deliver. We ended up skipping dessert because of it.

Other downsides: limited parking, strict reservation system, and overall it felt like a lot of hype for a pretty average payoff.

There are definitely some positives—nice ambiance, solid presentation on certain dishes—but there are also some easy improvements:
•	Better attention to staff appearance
•	Improved temperature control
•	Clearer, more readable menus
•	More flavor and execution consistency, especially on signature items

Overall, if you’re just looking to try something trendy or go somewhere new, it might be worth a visit once. But if you’re going strictly for great food, there are better options for the price.

Service was good but the food is not worth Michelin star. Oysters were lukewarm, steak was too salty, seasonal vegetables were literally just steamed asparagus. Presentation of the onion soup was very creative but there was nothing special with the taste. Scallop was ok. The complimentary truffle cheese amuse bouche tasted the best. I have been to a lot of fine dining restaurants but I have never seen a single place charging 3% credit card fee to the customer. If I pay less than $10~15 with card then I will understand but if I’m spending over $300 you guys definitely make enough to pay the card fee yourself. The food price itself is already over priced for what you get. Tip is also after tax.

This French restaurant is a great option in LA

Absolutely exceeded expectations and is now on my must-return list. The DTLA location can be tricky for street parking, but plenty of public parking nearby—and it’s perfect for a post-meal city walk with great bars around (Death & Co is right next door!).

The food was consistently impressive. The savory cream puff was a fun opener. The Sea Bream with uni, cucumber, and apple granita was stunning—refreshing, creative, and incredibly well-balanced. The Scallop was the dish that truly wowed us, especially with the sauce that we ended up finishing with bread. The Chicken was surprisingly outstanding—juicy, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. The Ribeye was visually impressive but overly salty for our taste. The Kiwi dessert was refreshing and beautifully layered, and the complimentary madeleine at the end was delicious enough that we asked for another.
All dishes were good, except for Ribeye. Ribeye was expensive menu but the sauce on the meat didnt harmonize with the meat. It had too strong flavor and smell.

I visited Camphor on a Thursday evening specifically in search of a French-style steak frites experience similar to what you’d find at L’Entrecôte. They offer a prix fixe menu featuring steak, fries, green salad, and baguette with butter, so it seemed like the perfect place to try.

Ambience & Service
The restaurant has a beautiful setting — a restored warehouse with high ceilings, stylish decor, and a lively vibe. It feels both modern and comfortable. Staff were friendly, professional, and very attentive throughout the evening. I started with a St. Germain cocktail, which was light, refreshing, and well-balanced.

Starters
The green salad with tomato and shallot vinaigrette was fresh, bright, and a great way to start the meal. The baguette, however, was disappointing. It wasn’t clear if it was house-baked or sourced from elsewhere, but it was dry both inside and out, lacking the crisp crust and airy softness of a traditional French baguette. For a French-inspired menu, this felt like a missed opportunity.

Main Course – Steak & Fries
The steak was a hanger cut — a good quality piece of beef and cooked well. Unfortunately, the sauce accompanying it was quite underwhelming. Rather than evoking the classic, savory, mustard-herb complexity of an authentic entrecôte sauce, it leaned heavily toward sweetness and felt off-balance. For a dish where the sauce should be the star, this was the most disappointing part of the experience.

The fries were another letdown. They were a bit dry, the portion was modest, and unlike traditional steak-frites restaurants, there was no offer of a refill. Given the simplicity of the dish, the expectation is for generous, crisp, golden fries — and this fell short.

Dessert
The meal ended on a high note with a lemon tart that was excellent: bright, tangy, and well-executed.

Overall
Camphor is a beautiful restaurant with attentive service and a strong cocktail and dessert game. However, if you’re going with the expectation of a classic French steak frites experience, you may be disappointed. The baguette lacked authenticity, the fries were skimpy, and the sauce — the soul of the dish — was off balance and far from what you’d find at an entrecôte. On its own terms, Camphor offers a stylish night out with unique house interpretations, but given the portion sizes and uneven execution, it feels overpriced

Camphor feels intentional from the start. A couple of days before our reservation they called to ask if we wanted to pre order any specials, so we reserved the Dover sole for our party of four. It ended up being the star of the night, perfectly cooked and silky with capers, parsley and a bright lemon butter sauce that made the whole table pause for a second. After a dish like that, it is hard for anything else to feel quite as dramatic, but there were still some really fun standouts.

The chicken was one of the smartest plates. The base is a juicy chicken breast, the top is a truffled thigh pâté blended smooth, so you get two textures and layers of flavor in every bite, all tied together with a sweet and sour style sauce that really works. The scallop ravioli will make any scallop lover happy, slightly on the sweeter side, very buttery, with full pieces of scallop tucked inside instead of being minced. The carrots on purée were simple and really well done. Their “Fusion Caesar” was another surprise, very anchovy forward in the best way, with imported French cheese, fresh dressing and radicchio that somehow avoids the usual bitterness. The sourdough crouton situation is memorable, crispy on the outside, airy inside, and one of the best bites of the salad. I am normally not a brioche person and still found their brioche quite good and less sweet than most versions, though I still personally lean team sourdough.

The onion soup was another dish I would come back for. It takes all the comforting flavor of a classic French onion tartine, but without the heavy, soggy bread situation. Instead, you get that deep, savory onion broth with a beautifully crunchy sourdough element that keeps its texture, so every spoonful has both flavor and contrast. It is such a simple idea on paper, but they really elevated it.

Dessert felt a bit more restrained compared to the savory courses, but there were still bright spots. My favorite was the marshmallow vanilla ice cream, which tastes mostly like a really good vanilla with about twenty percent marshmallow in the background. It is familiar, nostalgic and very easy to finish. The marzipan style dessert reminded me of an elevated Hawaiian shave ice, more of a refreshing palate cleanser than a rich dessert. The tart leaned more custard than classic tart for me, almost like a crisp mille feuille with a very thin layer of pastry and a soft center. Next time I am definitely trying the bread pudding with ice cream, which sounds more in line with what I personally love in a dessert.

Service was spot on all evening, from our main server to the team clearing plates and answering detailed questions about every dish. I also met one of the owners and was genuinely impressed by his presence in the room and how tuned in he seemed to each table. It is very easy to see how they earned their Michelin star so quickly, and I am already planning to come back for another round of Dover sole, onion soup, and a visit to their Koreatown speakeasy.

If you’re looking for a great spot for a leisurely lunch with outstanding French-inspired cuisine and top-notch service, Petite Trois is definitely worth a visit.

I ts original location splits its personality: a narrow room lined entirely with counter seats where the kitchen feels part of the performance and a charming outdoor patio where white tablecloths invite you to linger.

The roasted beet salad opens the meal with sweet orange and purple beets, while toasted almonds and pistachios add great crunch. However, the horseradish cream and mignonette lean a touch heavy-handed. Then comes the real reason to walk through the doors: steak frites. The wagyu arrives cooked perfectly medium with a proper sear, topped with an herbaceous, luxurious béarnaise butter. Alongside it, the fries are textbook french brasserie style, crisp, golden, and lightly salted.

Dessert here feels mandatory rather than optional. The crème brûlée arrives with that iconic glass-like sugar shell that cracks dramatically under the spoon before giving way to cool tahini vanilla custard beneath. Gone embarrassingly fast. Finally, the towering chocolate soufflé arrives warm and deeply rich, paired with chocolate sorbet and chocolate sauce. If you are a chocolate fanatic, this is your nirvana. If you want a delicious steak frites and classic french dessert to fulfill a specific, deep craving, you pull up a chair here.

How can you not absolutely love eating here?! Grab a table out on the patio and order the delicious escargot, remember to tell them to keep the garlic butter to go with your steak later. Share the steak frites so you can order more stuff to try, but the steak frites is a must! The burger is definitely worth trying, but it’s very heavy so if you need to choose between that and the steak, go for the steak. Make sure you save room for the deserts!

top_reviews.content:
Starting off with the appetizer of the little grilled cheese and tomato bisque was phenomenal. The texture of the sandwiches was perfectly crisp on the outside and light and fluffy on the inside. The bisque was to die for and a perfect combination between the two. We ordered the fish platter was perfectly seasoned, cooked, and plated. All of our food came out hot despite the colder atmosphere on the rooftop. A few disappointing notes were just having to ask for the heaters to be lit, food service was kind of cold, and we didn’t see our server very frequently despite how slow it was with customers.
The setting included additional wax figures throughout the restaurant, which was neat to see carried from the museum up to the dining room.

Worth the Stop. Worth Going Back.

After spending a surprisingly fun afternoon wandering through Madame Tussauds, the family found ourselves debating where to grab lunch. We were considering the Hard Rock Cafe and a couple of other nearby options when the Madame Tussauds Rooftop Bar & Restaurant appeared almost by accident.

Sometimes those spontaneous decisions end up being the best ones.

This was one of them.

The food was very good, and the menu offered several appetizers that were a little different from the usual tourist fare. Everything was well prepared, thoughtfully presented, and arrived exactly as it should.

The seating is worth mentioning because it gives you a good sense of what this venue is designed to be. It’s more lounge than traditional restaurant, making it ideal for couples, small groups, or an evening out. With a family and several kids, it wasn’t quite as comfortable as a conventional dining room would have been, but everyone still settled in just fine. My impression is that this space really comes alive later in the evening rather than during lunch.

One of my favorite touches was something completely unexpected.

Scattered throughout the rooftop were wax figures posed as though they were fellow patrons, relaxing with friends and enjoying the restaurant. More than once I caught myself doing a double take before realizing I was looking at another remarkably realistic figure. It fit perfectly with the museum downstairs and added a fun bit of personality to the experience.

Our server, Jasmine, was outstanding. Friendly, attentive, and professional throughout the meal.

Just as impressive was the floor manager, whose name I unfortunately didn’t catch. She was constantly moving through the restaurant, quietly checking on guests and stepping in whenever needed to keep service flowing smoothly. Most diners probably never noticed everything she was doing, which is often the mark of someone who is exceptionally good at hospitality.

Good food, excellent service, a unique atmosphere, and a fun extension of the Madame Tussauds experience made this an easy recommendation.

If you’re already visiting the museum, don’t overlook what’s upstairs.

Worth the Stop. Worth Going Back.

My sincere thanks go to our server Anna, the kitchen staff and the owner for a delectable and delightful meal on Mother’s Day 2026.

The bun is amazing too and airy and able to absorb all the fantastic sauces and cheeses that comes with this. I suggest this is shared with a loved one or a good friend. I loved the wedge salasd and specifically the way it's served - chopped! This take the pressure off of cutting it at all and can be easily eaten. There was not a single care for the requests we made thru RESY.  This makes the consumer who really loves your restaurant to absolutely lie in the future just to be sat in a booth and warn anyone who needs a romantic anniversary to choose another spot entirely and maybe just come here for a drink.

I’ve been to the Benjamin a couple of times and think it’s one of the best restaurants in LA. The food is outstanding and everything I had is great - specifically the spicy lobster pasta, the baked potato is surprisingly amazing, and of course the burger. You can’t go wrong here. That being said, the drinks really blow me away every-time I come here. They’re refined, delicious, cravable, and I’ve had a variety that I liked (usually I just get old fashions but here I’m adventurous). It’s a great date spot or a spot to grab a booth to catch up with some friends. Highly recommend.

My name is Rudy Jason Rubio, born and raised in Los Angeles. I’ve been in the food service industry since I was 14 years old, and I consider myself well-seasoned, well-traveled, with a sharp eye and palate for great food. To be honest, I was starting to lose hope in the LA food scene—until I found The Benjamin.

What a beautiful blessing of a restaurant. We started with the marinated olives, which immediately set the tone, followed by a perfectly executed wedge salad. We originally came because of the rave burger reviews—and they absolutely did not disappoint. But the real showstopper was the lobster pasta. Epic. Memorable. The kind of dish that reminds you why you love dining out.

On top of the food, Natalie, our waitress/bartender, was beyond amazing—attentive, warm, knowledgeable, and genuinely elevated the entire experience. And just when we thought it couldn’t get better, we had the carrot cake for dessert. Incredible. The perfect ending to an outstanding meal.

Thank you, The Benjamin, for restoring my faith in the Los Angeles food scene. I’ll definitely be back—and I’ll be telling people. VAMOS ⚡️⚡️

After searching for the top burger spots in town, Benjamin quickly made it onto the list of visiting restaurants. Among them, Benjamin stands out with some of the best burgers around. The burger was very tasty and made with high-quality meat. Although it’s a bit pricey, I think it’s definitely worth trying. The service and atmosphere also contribute to a great overall experience. We weren’t sure if they took walk-ins, so we decided to make a reservation just in case.

Stepping into the venue would feel like you’re just transported into a totally different space. Classy look, dim lighting, somewhat giving the speakeasy’s vibe. Reservation’s highly recommended as the venue seemed to be pretty busy as early as 6pm-ish.

My friend and I started with their Crab Beignets, my pick being a crab lover. Wouldn’t say it’s not kinda steep being an appetizer, but when I took a bite I could tell it featured generous portions of crab meat. Pretty simple yet well-seasoned and flavorful.

As for the main, we shared The Benjamin Burger, which I would say was the crowd’s favorite as it seemed to be in almost all the reviews and we could see it served on lots of other tables. Just like how the picture showed it, ordering it medium, they did come at the precise wellness - juicy and tender. The sauce complemented the overall taste, but surely not overpowering. It’s served with fries on the side with nice garlic sauce and ketchup. Despite I did enjoyed my burger a lot, would admit it’s tad pricey being at mid $30s.

As if french fries weren’t enough, we did get their Baked Potato, their other dish that made it to the top reco on Yelp. To my surprise, it tasted super rich and the crispy delicious skin was doubtlessly the winner. SO SO GOOD, especially when you took a bite with all the elements in the plate - the sour cream, the scallion, and the bacon as add-on we opted for. If you felt like splurging, they also offered caviar add-on, which could turn your baked potato to be over $100.

Overall, I certainly had an impressive dinner. Would I come back? Prolly only on certain occasion when I would be willing to spend more.

One of my current favorites in the city. The ambiance is warm and moody in the best way—perfect for a catch up dinner with freinds or date night. The food is consistently great, and what I really appreciate is that it doesn’t feel like your typical Hollywood scene. It’s relaxed, unpretentious, and welcoming. Owner Ben is often there, genuinely kind and always up for a friendly chat. You can tell he cares about the place and the people in it.

Laurel Hardware is an easy 5/5 for me after this meal. The vibe is laid-back but the food feels way more elevated than your standard night-out spot.

The standout was the butternut squash tortellini – rich, silky sauce, perfectly cooked pasta, and those little pops of flavor in every bite. I don’t usually write reviews. In fact, I only leave one when I have a genuinely disappointing experience.

My friend and I came to Laurel Hardware for her birthday. The first thing that stood out was the hostess. She wasn’t rude or disrespectful, but she looked visibly unhappy and unwelcoming. First impressions matter, and when you work in hospitality, guests shouldn’t feel like they’re inconveniencing you the moment they walk through the door.

We sat down, and our server came over. I asked if I could try the non-alcoholic wine before ordering. She said yes and brought us a taste. She seemed a little bothered by the request, but she wasn’t rude, and everything was fine.

Later, I had a question, but our server wasn’t around, so I asked a gentleman nearby. He introduced himself as Nate and said, “I’m Nate. I only have one server on the floor tonight, so I apologize, but I’m happy to help.” He took care of us and was genuinely kind throughout the evening.

I ordered the tacos without onions, which meant I couldn’t have the pico de gallo. I asked if they could substitute sliced tomatoes instead. They said yes, but the tomatoes never came. When I asked about them, I was told they only had tomatoes in the pico de gallo. That seemed strange considering they serve burgers and several other dishes with fresh tomatoes. It’s not a huge deal, and I understand that not every restaurant accommodates requests like that, but it was still disappointing.

I also ordered the shrimp, and nowhere on the menu did it mention that it was deep-fried. I had to send it back because that’s not what I was expecting. Nate handled it with no problem at all.

My friend ordered the duck fried rice with egg, and it turned out to be extremely spicy. Again, that wasn’t mentioned on the menu. She had to send it back as well, and Nate helped us once again. He really made the experience much better.

What surprised me was that our server never checked on us. The restaurant wasn’t particularly busy—there were maybe four or five tables. She only came back to ask my friend how the replacement dish was after it had been remade. She never asked how my food was or if we needed anything. I think it’s important to check on your tables, especially when the restaurant isn’t busy.

My salad also turned out to be spicy, but by that point I didn’t want to keep complaining, so I just ate it.

Overall, I don’t think this was the level of service or attention to detail I’d expect for a restaurant at this price point.

I do want to say that Nate was wonderful. He was kind, helpful, and professional, and he honestly saved the experience. Without him, it would have been much worse.

But what really stuck with me was the hostess. She wasn’t rude, but she looked visibly unhappy, and that set the tone from the moment we walked in. In hospitality, the first impression matters, and I think guests should be welcomed with warmth rather than feeling like they’re interrupting someone’s day.

Overall I do recommend this restaurant as a trendy place to dine with delicious food.

A classic in the neighborhood. Their udon has a great texture to it, especially if served cold.

Got the cold Ikura udon with grated radish, green onions, seaweed, and broth served on the side. It was refreshing, the broth was salty yet served in a small potion so it wasn’t overwhelming. The Ikura was fresh and zesty.

Their tempura appetizer was a great crunchy addition to how soft, salty and chewy the udon noodles were.

The only drawback is that when it gets busy, a divider is put between tables, so there’s no privacy and you overhear conversations. Would recommend coming here when it’s more chill. Overall, would recommend for great udon with great texture.

Marugame Monzo definitely lives up to its reputation when it comes to udon — the noodles were genuinely very good, and I can see why so many people recommend the place. I ordered takeout, though, so I feel like the experience is probably much better when dining in. I tried the miso carbonara udon, and honestly, no regrets — it was rich, flavorful, and unique. That said, the portion size felt pretty small for the price, and overall it came across as quite overpriced for what you get. I enjoyed trying it once, but considering the cost and portion size, I probably wouldn’t go back.

Small udon restaurant that has a Michelin star. Absolutely delicious udon. Loved their seafood curry udon. My husband got a broth udon that he loved. The staff is super friendly and welcoming. Can’t wait to come back and try another dish.

The service was also very mid. I honestly didn’t know how to eat the cold udon and all I tasted was the daikon so I prob did it completely wrong but they didn’t seem to care. They were very curt with words until I left.

I love everything about this place but the wait to get in! Great atmosphere with amazing service.
The food is to gush for and it has very good portions as well. The pricing is good for the quality.
ANY time I want some udon, this is my spot hands down.

Came here with my friend at 3:30pm on a Wednesday; honestly the perfect time because it was empty and service was great. I’d come back to try the creamy options, but this visit was a bit of a mixed bag.

Beef with Fluffy Jidori Egg Udon (Double Portion) — 3/5 I’m used to the beef udon at places like Marugame where you get that sweet marinated meat and plenty of broth. I expected the egg to just be an accompaniment (like a soft-boiled egg you add on top), but this was different. The "fluffy egg" was more of a scrambled-boiled style that mixed in and turned the broth into a thick, creamy sauce.

The Issue: It was barely a soup. The egg sucked up all the liquid, and there wasn't even enough "soup" for one person, let alone the double portion of noodles we ordered. I was honestly pretty upset because I really wanted a noodle soup. We had to pay $2 extra for a side of dashi just to fix the dish ourselves, which shouldn't really happen. Once we fixed the broth level, the flavor of the beef and egg was yummy, and the dish was great, but I’d probably just stick to the regular beef udon next time.

The Noodles: The udon is super thick and very chewy. I personally prefer my noodles to be a bit more flour-based, but if you like a heavy chew, you’ll love these.

Mixed Tempura — 5/5 No complaints here! The batter was so nice, light, and crispy. Totally delightful.

The Spot: Shared the double portion and tempura and it was the perfect amount for two people who aren't starving. Just be careful with the egg dishes if you actually want broth!

top_reviews.content:
Nestled on Middletown Road in the Bronx, **Da Franco & Tony Ristora** is a testament to the enduring power of a well-executed meal. It is a place where the atmosphere feels like an extension of the neighborhood's heart, but the kitchen operates with a level of sophistication that rivals the city’s most lauded white-tablecloth establishments.

The Prelude: Perfection in a Bite
Our evening began with an order of **Crab Cakes**, and they set a high bar for what was to follow. These were not the breadcrumb-heavy iterations so common elsewhere; instead, they were packed with sweet, flaky crab meat, seared until golden. The texture was impeccable—offering a gentle crunch before melting into a savory, well-seasoned center.

The Main Event:
The entrées showcased a kitchen that understands both the nuance of the robust demands of meat. My wife’s selection, a **Skirt Steak and Lamb Shank combo**, was a carnivore’s dream. The skirt steak was expertly grilled, boasting a deep char while remaining incredibly tender. The lamb shank was the highlight of the plate—braised until the meat practically fell away from the bone in succulent ribbons. Paired with buttery mashed potatoes and crisp, vibrant vegetables, it was a masterclass in balanced, hearty dining.

For my own course, I turned to the **Gamberi Alla Scampi Con Risotto**. It was, quite simply, a revelation. The shrimp were plump and snapped with freshness, swimming in a classic scampi sauce that balanced garlic, lemon, and high-quality butter without overstaying its welcome. The true technical triumph, however, was the risotto. Creamy, rich, and cooked to a perfect *al dente*, it absorbed the brightness of the sauce, creating a dish that felt both indulgent and refined.

The Finale
To conclude, we shared the **Crème Brûlée**. The hallmark of a great custard is the "crack," and this delivered. The caramelized sugar topping shattered perfectly to reveal a cool, velvety interior that was neither too sweet nor too heavy. It was a sophisticated finish to a meal that felt like a celebration.

The Verdict
Da Franco & Tony Ristora isn't just a restaurant; it’s a destination for those who appreciate technical skill paired with genuine warmth. From the precision of the *Gamberi* to the soul-warming depth of the lamb, this is a kitchen that knows exactly what it’s doing. If you are looking for a meal that feels special from the first bite to the last, Middletown Road is calling.

Really enjoyed finding this little spot after work. The place is small and cozy, but that’s honestly part of the charm because it feels relaxed and comfortable instead of crowded or noisy. The food was fresh, satisfying, and came out quickly without feeling rushed. Definitely one of those low-key places that leaves a good impression. I’ll absolutely be making another trip back to the Bronx for this spot.

top_reviews.content:
Mel’s Drive-In in Hollywood is everything you hope a classic American diner will be. From the moment you walk in, you’re surrounded by an old-school atmosphere that perfectly captures the charm of vintage Hollywood. The retro décor, nostalgic vibe, and friendly service make it feel like you’ve stepped back in time.

The food is exactly what you want from a classic diner—delicious burgers, fries, shakes, and all the comfort food favorites done right. But what really made our visit special was seeing it through my son’s eyes. He absolutely loved that his kids’ meal came in a little cardboard classic car, and the vintage photo booth was a huge hit. It made for a fun keepsake and added even more to the experience.

If you’re looking for great comfort food and a memorable family-friendly stop while visiting Hollywood, Mel’s Drive-In is a must. It’s more than just a meal—it’s a fun slice of old-school Americana that both kids and adults will enjoy.

Mel's is the quintessential American diner. Housed in a classic 1950s "googie" architecture building, it's a great place to get comfort food in a cool environment.

There's also outdoor seating so you can sit on the famous Sunset strip (and watch traffic and billboards).

The food is uniformly excellent, but not inexpensive (this is an upscale diner). Breakfast is always available and their pancakes are especially good!

The service is friendly, attentive, efficient, and the servers have real personality!

There's FREE valet parking in the back ( a pleasant surprise in LA).

It's also one of the rare restaurants that's open late, Thursday and Friday it's open till 3:00 a.m. And it's 24 hours a day over the weekend.

Tourists and locals alike enjoy this old fashioned slice of Americana. You probably will, too!

top_reviews.content:
For many who come to visit Los Angeles, it’s easy to go to a sit down restaurant that’s pricey for the “LA” experience, but if you want good food, that hole in the wall vibe, and some of the juiciest Syrian shawarma in LA, I’d recommend nothing but Sincerely Syria. Everyone knows you here, they treat you like a close friend, and they hook it up on the portions. There’s outdoor seating and it’s right on Hollywood/Vine so you get to feel the chaos of LA while sitting down with a good bite to eat.
For all the driving addicts, this is Hollywood so parking is a bit difficult. However, I took the B line subway to get here, this joint is right in front of the Hollywood/Vine Station.

Absolutely amazing experience! The food was fresh, delicious, and full of flavor. The service was excellent, friendly, and welcoming, and the atmosphere made the whole experience even better. You can really feel the care and quality in everything they serve. Definitely one of my favorite spots in Hollywood. Highly recommended! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Incredible food and unmatched customer service. We were amazingly welcomed and the staff were super nice and friendly to us. On top of that, the chicken shawarma they offer is the best I’ve had in the United States. It’s really second to none! It’s even better than some shawarmas I’ve had back in the Middle East. Would heavily recommend for anyone to try and keep going again!!

This place has gone down so badly in quality. Not fresh, workers busy talking to each other rather than finishing peoples orders, messing up order and even being stingy with meat. Bought a 24” platter and asked to have it with garlic sauce instead of tahini. Got with tahini both inside the wrap and on the side. Two pieces of the shawarma had no meat. Charging $33 dollars for subpar food and not great customer service is beyond me. Used to love this place but now I will for sure never return.

Sincerely never again.

I love the Anaheim location but this one sucks. Service is really bad and food is not good. We asked for hot fries and we were served cold warmish ones. When we told them about it, they just say “what are you talking about and put extra 2 fries on the plate”

30$ wasted on bad food and never again on this location. I rather drive 1h away and enjoy a great shawarma than settle for this place!
Had an amazing time with them very great food and the service was super.Must try their beef shawarma.
Great food & customer service. If Im ever back in Hollywood, I will eat there again.
It was amazing, the guy who was inside was awesome and the food is incredible, I loved it too much, I will come back!

top_reviews.content: owner is so kind and food is incredibly cheap and delicious!!! not to mention with great portions for the price! i go here almost every week after school with my friends and it’s become such a lovely place to hangout and eat good food. amazing service and little wait time. i recommend this spot to every person who comes to hollywood/la. we love you sushiq!

Great service, she was so sweet! It’s a little hole in the wall place but that just adds to the charm of it. There are some pricey things on the menu but there are also affordable things. And they even have a student discount for the teriyaki bowl! And a 10% discount if paying with cash and the food smells amazing , Everytime I walk by it captures my nose
Am walking home now and can’t wait to try!
While the parking situation is definitely the worst aspect of this place. parking here is terrible, which is a real downside. The sushi was okay. Customer service could have been better.

This place has been around for awhile. My daughter likes their chicken teriyaki bowl, and we haven’t been here in a very long time.

She of course got the chicken teriyaki rice bowl and I got some shrimp tempura. Personally, I don’t like a lot of dark meat and they use nothing but dark meat which is why it’s probably cheaper. For the price the chicken teriyaki rice bowl is good. The shrimp tempura is disappointing, but again for the price…

The inside needs a revamp for sure. This is Hollywierd though. You need a little taste.

The service is great. The person taking our order was very helpful and nice.

Overall for the price it’s not shabby. If your in a budget definitely a great deal!

Parking, good food and service with fair prices, I’m glad that we went. The parking lot is not large, with a good number of stores it services, but cars are coming and going all of the time. It was not hard to find a place. The restaurant is not a big place and had plenty of seats when we went. You walk up to order, plus there is a good size menu with lots of options. It might take a bit to figure out what to get. We both ordered the Super Maki Combo bento box. There is plenty of food that comes with this meal. And it came pretty quick. Soup, tempura, steamed veggies, a couple of rolls, tempura, and a dumpling. They are not messing around here. The food was good, nothing really memorable, but nothing was questionable either. And for the price, not a bad deal. The staff was friendly and helpful when we were asking about the menu. When the food came to our table, we were happy with the freshness and presentation. The sauces were explained with what dishes they were for. It is a lot of soy sauce! The tempura dipping sauce was not what I am used to having with tempura but worked with the meal. It was very light and had a nice flavor. It is worth trying out for a low key Japanese meal.

Great sports bar. Well done sports theme decor inside. Plenty of TVs to watch a game. It's pretty spacious inside too. A good amount of seating. They also have a pool table and photobooth in the back. Good happy hour deals 4-8.

Service was good friendly staff. There's street meter parking or some parking structures Erin a block or two.

Was here during happy hour and had the smash burger and some beer. The smash was very good. They managed to get the edges nice and crispy (which I haven’t seen before) and added to a great tasting burger.

Olivia, the bartender, is incredibly friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. The first time I visited Palm Pine, she was behind the bar and made the experience memorable right away. Now I find myself coming back specifically when she's working. If you stop by, definitely say hello, she's easily one of the best bartenders in Los Angeles!

The Palm and the Pine is one of my favorite bars in Los Angeles. From the moment I first walked in I was welcomed with open arms. EVERYONE is so friendly and the vibe is always great. And they have a great happy hour that lasts until 8pm. I love all the bartenders but my favorites are Ben and Jose. They are always SO incredibly attentive, gracious and full of personality. The type of bartenders that give you a glass of water even when you didn’t ask. This is definitely my “Cheers” bar here in Hollywood. And when there are big games on it’s ALWAYS a great time!

Went last night with my gf on a Tuesday around 930pm. The tvs were blasting instead of playing music. It was $65 for 2 draft beers and 2 orders of wings 🤮 . It was freezing inside and pretty empty. This place is overpriced and very poorly run. Everything about it was wrong. No vibe & wings were dry. I would not return or recommend. Looked like no one cared about it in any capacity.

P&P is the best sports bar in Hollywood!! They always have really fun and exciting events and help keep the block alive. Ownership is really nice and welcoming as is the staff. The bartender Destiny is amazing she makes great drinks and really sets the vibe for this place! I will definitely be returning because of her and I can’t think of a better place to stop for a quick beer after work or to come party til 2 am on a Saturday night! Check it out!!!

I love this place! It’s got a great vibe, food is delicious and reasonably priced. Mondays-Wednesday it’s a little calmer, does become wild on the weekends though. If you’re lucky enough to have Liam be your bartender, he will make you some absolutely incredible drinks. This place is also very sober people/mocktails friendly. Definitely a place to be in Hollywood!

I’ve tried so hard to root for this bar. It’s walking distance from me, looks sleek yet classic, and I’ve given it a shot more than once. Sadly, this place seems to be all style, no substance. Two of my three outings were understaffed and overpriced—$25 for a greasy, overcooked In-N-Out burger and a “basket” of fries that arrived nearly 40 mins after ordering, while my friend got a chicken sandwich that took over an hour. I’ll be steering clear of The Facepalm & The Pine from here on out.

We also got the Santa Barbara juice at the end and it was very refreshing. I'll need the hydration to carry me through my day at Disney, lol.   Overall, as out-of-staters, it captured a vibe of L.A.; so I recommend for other travelers especially

I stopped by this coffee place this morning right when they open. I chose the street parking here in the front since I came earlier enough where it was available and traffic was light.

I came right when the place open to avoid the rush. I got my wife her iced chai latte with light ice and asked for regular milk. I got my sister the matcha latte with light ice and regular milk too. This store has a water station if you just want that. They have a nice seating area inside of the place, outside in front of the place and also a patio area in the back.

This store also has dog treats if you decide to bring your dog with you. The price is reasonable and customer service here is amazing. My wife and my sister loved their drinks, it was made exactly how I order them.

Fabulous breakfast spot, sandwiches and bagel were amazing, so is the matcha iced tea. We tried the mortadella sandwich and turkey-avocado sandwich, both were so delicious, they prepare  fresh.  Staff is very friendly and welcoming. Thank you

Delicious! They know how to make an Aerocano, which is iced Americano steamed to get that airy, fluffy texture of latte, but with milk involved.

The drink itself is subtly sweet with a hit of milk chocolate, and just very pleasant. Surprisingly, they use Counter Culture Forty-Six for their espresso, which is a dark roast. This taste a lot more like a medium toast, so more to what  enjoy.

Decor is very nice, open and airy with decent amount of seating without feeling crammed.

Not a green tea fan, but have heard throughout my life about the benefit of it. I had to stop by to make a video call. I chose this spot just randomly. I am so happy that I did. I didn’t know what to get, and I looked around to see what other ppl have for themselves.There was one table right in front of the counter. Looks like it was a mother and daughter date. They had this pretty drink so I pointed that to the Barista. He said it was a matcha green tea, and I asked for the cold version of it. Maybe they could only do cold…who knows. I was like Matcha…urgh…not my thing, but just happened to say yes for it and he asked me if I want sugar in it. I asked for the one with no sugar. I….loved it. They have a really nice space on the back area where you are unbothered and left alone. The customer service is great. Thank you for creating such a beautiful place.

STAY AWAY!! (Tl Dr at the end)(see photos for disgusting food)

I wanted to like this place, in fact I’ve ordered from here maybe 3-4 times. The food WAS decent (small portions for the price) the coffee is good but I’ve got to be honest. The service is…strange. It’s almost welcoming, half industrial, half cliche baristas who kind of ignore you. If you order online, I can confirm a 20-25% upcharge on menu prices. I can’t tell if they need to hire more people, or change their layout. But if you’re like me, and try to skip lines by ordering ahead, be aware of the increase in prices and the lack of expediency. I went in for my order today, it wasn’t fully ready, that’s totally fine. Having worked in F&B I don’t like to be one of those delivery guys who stands in the way phone out. So after being told it would be a few minutes I went to sit, well within eye-line. Literally 2-3 steps away on a stool. They had two guys working the counter and I believe the owner was sitting next to me. They proceed to finish making my coffee, take my food out of its bag for some reason and set it on the counter. The guy who helped me originally went back to making food and the other guy just totally ignored it. I wasn’t 100% sure if it was my order so I waited, even tho it was not busy. (Practically empty). A new customer, waiting for their online order walked right up, fully picked up my coffee, touching the lid with their entire palm, inspecting it before putting it back down. That’s where I’ve got to draw the line. It’s one thing to leave an order that is ready to go, (which is already suspect, why not tell me?) but to let a stranger touch where I’ll be putting my mouth? They then served her and a few other people. I had to get back up, mind you my seat was literally 2 steps away, and start the process again, get it re-bagged. I wasn’t going to make a scene but I was really grossed out a stranger unhygienically touched my drink all over. At least keep orders somewhere safe if you’re going to let them sit…which you shouldn’t be doing. On top of that check out how my
Burrito came out… I picked this up myself and it was handled with care. It’s completely inedible, or looks like it was stepped on.

Tl Dr: food was decent, coffee is okay, service is horrendous, upcharge for ordering ahead is wild. Check your order before leaving. Plenty of other cafes in hollywood for you to go instead. Parking is terrible since it’s on Sunset, just as an fyi
