top_reviews.content: The steak and chicken were amazing ever thing else we had was okay. Service was okay cause it was a crowded night. But they could have been a bit more attentive with the drinks and clearing up the plate for our section. The atmosphere was nice and chill really love their vibe I will give them that.

The overall atmosphere and interior design were pleasant and well thought out; however, as the evening progressed, the area around the bar became extremely crowded while dinner service was still ongoing.

The food was generally average and did not reflect a particularly chef-driven or gourmet character. The branzino I ordered as a main course was surprisingly full of bones, which was quite unexpected for a venue at this level.
Great show and atmosphere but the food was disappointing... a huge bone came out from the crudo and the scallops did not taste well. I did like the carrot souffle.

The wife and I went here for our wedding anniversary. The place opens at 6:30 PM and we were scheduled for that time. Valet parking was $20. A bit steep and I now understand why people come with Waymo.
The included pictures were taken as we were leaving so it was dark. However, when we arrived it was still very light. As we entered, it quickly became very dark. The hostess took us to our table and we sat down. It took several minutes before our eyes adjusted to the dim light. The light was not just dim, it was "Take your girlfriend here while your wife is at her book club so nobody will recognize you" dark. The longer we stayed, the more visible everything became.
This place immediately struck me as what Rick's club in Casablanca would be in real life. That is, if they did not have to light everything for a movie. They did not have a dance floor that I could see but they did have live music starting at 7:30 PM. At least on Wednesdays.
People were filtering in and the place became more alive with a constant background of low conversation. We ordered drinks and appetizers. The wife ordered one of their signature cocktails and I asked for a Brandy Alexander. I was surprised when the waitress came back and said that they could not make that but suggested something similar. (I thought, with a full bar and YouTube, even *I* could make a Brandy Alexander.) I went to my fallback of a Black Russian. The wife liked her drink and the Black Russian was pretty good.
We ordered appetizers. The wife had the pigs in a blanket and I had the shrimp cocktail. The wife had never eaten pigs in a blanket so I explained what they were. Of course, at a place like this, the pigs were not cocktail wieners like you would get at your uncle's party, these were made of wagyu beef (Pigs in a blanket? Cows in a blanket? Now I am confused). She let me try one and they were excellent. The shrimp cocktail was pretty good. I would just say that the cocktail sauce did not have enough of a kick for me. Personal taste, I guess.
With the table decked out like this, we asked our waiter to take a picture of us to commemorate our anniversary. He explained that photographs were not allowed inside the building. The story he told (and we all know that waiters NEVER fib, right?) was that the building previously housed a striptease school and, for this reason, there were no windows and photography was not allowed inside the building. He said he could take our pictures out on the patio but we declined.
Aside: a striptease school? Is this a vo-tech class or a college prep course? Do you get a certificate upon completion? Well, I guess you learn something new every day.
Back to the food. The wife ordered the baby back ribs and I had the NY strip steak. We both ordered a side of fries. The fries were pretty good, not McDonald's good but very tasty. The wife started on the baby back ribs but, being European, she was loath to eat them with her hands. Rather, she used a knife and fork. She chowed down on them quite well so I took this as an indication that the ribs were just what she wanted. There was a lot of meat on the ribs and she could not eat it all. I ordered my steak medium. I couldn't tell if it was pink in the center (search above for the keyword "dark") but it was very well cooked and tasted just right.
For dessert, we ordered the hot fudge sundae with two spoons. This was also a delight.
You may wonder about me only giving four stars for the service. I am one of those customers who likes to drink water. I also like it when the waitstaff notices and refills my water glass without me having to ask. That did not happen here. I had to ask to get it refilled.
We really liked the atmosphere, the vibes and the clientele. The recorded music included crooners from the 1950s and 60s. The live music was a singer and a guitar player. Their music selection fit right in with the whole scene.
We agreed that several of our friends would enjoy a meal at Delilah. We will be back.

🎄 Christmas at Delilah: Stunning Vibes, Average Food

⭐️⭐️⭐️

📍 Delilah – Christmas Season Experience

Finally got a peek into Delilah during Christmas time 🎄✨
Let’s be honest — this place is all about the vibes.

Atmosphere:
✨ The holiday decorations are festive, cute, and very photo-worthy.
📸 December is the only time photos are allowed, which makes the experience feel extra special.
🎶 Music, crowd, and overall ambiance were amazing.

Drinks:
• 🍹 Sunset Spritz (Non-Alcoholic) – Sounded great (grapefruit + non-alcoholic wine) but was extremely bitter. Couldn’t finish it.
• 🍸 Ketel One Martini – My husband loved it.
• 💄 Clausmopolitan – My friend really enjoyed this one.
• 🍾 Champagne Papi – Light, refreshing, and zesty. Solid choice.

Food:
• 🦞 Lobster Rolls – Good, but nothing special.
• 🍗 Chicken Tenders – Crispy outside but no flavor inside. Expected much more since it’s a “specialty.”
• 🌽 Roasted Sweet Corn – Surprisingly my favorite dish of the night. Simple and delicious.
• 🍄 Hen of the Woods Mushrooms – Another standout. Very flavorful and enjoyable.
• 🐟 Roasted Branzino – Okay, but bland and disappointing for the price.
• 🍝 Maine Lobster Cavatelli – Great flavors and generous portion, but extremely salty.

Overall:
💸 Very overpriced for the quality of food.
🍽️ Would I come for the food? Probably not.
✨ Would I come back for the atmosphere, music, and Christmas magic? Absolutely.

Great food with generous portions, and everything came out right on time. Our server was very friendly and attentive. Music was a bit loud and tables are very close together, making conversation difficult. Hostess could be warmer when welcoming guests.

Alex Steel is, without question, one of the best hospitality professionals in Los Angeles. Every time I visit Delilah, he goes above and beyond to make sure my experience is exceptional. What always stands out is his attention to detail—he somehow remembers exactly what everyone in my group likes and anticipates our needs before we even have to ask. He even remembers my drink down to the last detail, and lord knows I love a complicated order.

I’ve also had the pleasure of being served by Alex at several other restaurants throughout the city, and his level of service is consistently outstanding no matter where he is. He brings a genuine warmth, professionalism, and expertise that elevates the entire dining experience.

Delilah is incredibly fortunate to have someone like Alex on their team. In an industry where great service can make all the difference, Alex sets the standard. If you’re lucky enough to have him as your server, you’re in excellent hands.

I had a great time here! Super intimate and small but great vibes. The food was delicious. I think the highlight of the night though was definitely our server Alex! He was amaaaazing. So attentive and sweet. He really made us feel comfortable and cared for and anticipated every need!! I’ll definitely be back for another cute LA night out.

top_reviews.content:
I visited Osteria Mamma after seeing so many good reviews, and it truly lived up to the hype. They had a carrot soup as the special of the day, and since the weather was chilly, I ordered it — it was absolutely delicious. The bread you drizzle oil on felt a bit greasy, but the soup itself was incredible.

I also tried the squid ink pasta, which I’d been really looking forward to, and it was so delicious. The shrimp was super fresh, and the flavors were spot on — you can tell they really know how to cook.

I went on a weekday evening and the service was wonderful. The ambiance was beautiful too, and I thought it would be a great place to come back for a date. Valet parking is $15, but there’s plenty of street parking in the surrounding residential area.

Overall, if you’re craving truly delicious Italian food, I highly recommend this place. I came because of the great reviews, and it ended up being even better than expected.

The price is a bit high though it worth it to taste this flavorful pasta.

My review is largely based on my standards of what I consider good Italian.
I personally think it is scammy to price yourself as a high quality spot yet you serve boxed pasta and don't even make your own spaghetti. My pasta came undercooked - it happens. But it was crunchy in the middle. Raw fresh pasta is doughy, if the pasta is crunchy then that means it is undercooked boxed pasta.
I also added fresh truffles, I got between 7 and 9 of the thinnest translucent shavings of truffle. It basically was essence of truffle.
Even the fast casual Uovo chain makes their own pasta.
As a side note, other comments about the poor service and seemingly prejudice staff are 100% true. The sketchy street corner they are on fits their attitude perfectly.

This was on par with olive garden quality. Except olive garden is cheaper. When you want high quality italian, I recommend Chi Spacca, Oste on 3rd, or Locanda Ventana down the street from my house. Save your dollars and skip the overpriced boxed pasta.

Great place great service. Just a bit disappointed the pasta was salty. But at the end they gave us a complimentary dessert to kill the saltiness of the pasta we had. It’s either they changed the chef or the ingredients they used. 👍🏻

I visited on a Monday dinner time, so there weren't many people, so I was able to eat leisurely. An Italian restaurant with a nice atmosphere. The service was friendly and good. The food was a bit salty, but overall it was delicious. Parking is free at the back of the restaurant. Even if there is a space on the street, you should look carefully at the signs and park.
Amazing! Food and atmosphere was excellent. Staff friendly and professional. All items were very satisfying!

First time here and it was amazing. Went with a co-worker that raved about the restaurant and she wasn’t wrong. The lasagna was the best I’ve ever tried, the focaccia was amazing also. Will visit again.

Tried Osteria Mamma and started with the Crostini and Arancini both were very good, but the arancini was my favorite. The meatball with tomato sauce was also excellent full of flavor and very tasty.

For my main, I had the Maltagliati alla Vodka. The pasta and sauce were very good, but it only came with three tiny pieces of shrimp I finished all of them in my first bite. I wish they were more generous with the shrimp to match the price and portion.

Ended with the Panna Cotta and Sorbet both were delicious and a nice way to wrap up the meal.

Overall, I’d recommend this spot if you’re coming for the wine (which they’re known for), but since I don’t drink wine, it wasn’t a standout for me. Personally, I think there are way better pasta spots nearby, like Louise’s Trattoria down the street, that offer a fuller experience , generous portions,  and better pricing . Nice experience but probably wouldn't come back .

If you're in Los Angeles and in the mood for some of the best Italian food around, Osteria Mamma on Melrose Ave is a must-visit. Though it's not cheap, the quality and authenticity make it worth every penny 💸.

Our meal started with the pizza Nico Nico, which was delicious. The only minor critique is that it had a bit too much arugula for our taste, but the flavors were spot on 🍕. The Polipozzo was next, and it was spectacular. Easily one of the best octopus dishes I've ever had, complemented perfectly by the unique addition of purple mashed potatoes 🐙.

We also tried the Risotto Speciale, which was nothing short of amazing. Each bite was rich, creamy, and bursting with flavor 🍚.

One thing to note is that their portions are quite generous. If you’re dining as a couple, you might want to consider sharing dishes to fully enjoy the variety without feeling overwhelmed.

Overall, Osteria Mamma offers a phenomenal dining experience. From the attentive service to the exquisite dishes, it’s a place that Italian food lovers will appreciate and remember. Definitely worth a visit if you're in LA and craving a taste of Italy 🇮🇹🍷.

Having already visited the Woodbridge location, I was excited to finally experience the original Staten Island restaurant—and it absolutely lived up to the hype.

The atmosphere is intimate, cozy, and effortlessly charming. The cellar setting creates a warm, laid-back vibe that’s perfect for a date night or catching up with friends. There’s even a hidden speakeasy tucked away in the back, which was a fun surprise.

Service was exceptional from start to finish. Our server, June, was warm, attentive, and genuinely made the evening special. She even offered to take photos for us, which was such a thoughtful touch. Manager John also stopped by our table and was incredibly welcoming. If you’ve dined at the Woodbridge location, you may recognize him since he occasionally serves there as well.

Everything we ordered was delicious—the shrimp dumplings, Bang Bang eggplant, burrata, caviar arepas, and chicken satay were all flavorful and beautifully presented.

The star of the evening, however, was the Drops of Jupiter cocktail. This sparkling strawberry-lavender rosé cocktail, complete with shimmering edible glitter dust and garnished with a perfectly ripe strawberry, was every bit as beautiful as it was delicious. Refreshing, lightly floral, and just the right amount of sparkle, it was a truly delectable treat and one of the most memorable cocktails I’ve had in a while.

To top it all off, when we ordered a dessert cocktail after dinner, June happily accommodated our request to split it into two glasses so my friend and I could share it. It’s thoughtful touches like that that elevate an already wonderful dining experience.

Personally, I enjoyed the food here a bit more than I did on my visit to Woodbridge. I think that’s a testament to how well this location has refined its menu over nearly a decade, while Woodbridge is still settling into its stride as a newer restaurant.

Outstanding food, exceptional hospitality, and an inviting atmosphere make this an easy five-star experience. I’ll definitely be back.

📸 I also featured my visit on my foodie pages, @NatEatsNJ on Instagram and TikTok, if you’d like to see the food, cocktails, and atmosphere in action.

This was my first visit to the marina several weeks ago and I was very impressed. The floor to ceiling windows offer an incredible view of the marina from everywhere in the restaurant and gives the place a feeling of serenity. Some of the food I tried would rival some of the best Manhattan steakhouse and seafood restaurants. The food was perfectly prepared and plated beautifully
The seafood tower as an appetizer was very impressive with right off the boat fresh tasting clams, oysters, very large shrimp and lobster. My other two stand out appetizers were the seafood salad and, a surprise, what they call an Italian eggroll With really delicious Italian red sauce. I had such a great experience at Tu Madre Santa Monica this past Labor Day weekend! The atmosphere was so welcoming and had such a fun vibe to it, my friend and I really loved it. We ordered the duce flautas, potato taco dorado, and the shrimp and fish taco, and the portions were generous, plenty for two people to share. Our server was super accommodating and even helped me charge my phone, that kind of service goes a long way!

A Delicious Variety at Tu Madre

We tried several dishes at Tu Madre in Santa Monica, and each one had its own unique flavor and personality. It was so much fun tasting a little bit of everything!

The Ahi Crudo Tostada was fresh, light, and flavorful, with tender ahi paired perfectly with a crispy tostada. The Baja Kanpachi Crudo Tostada was another favorite--the kanpachi was fresh, delicate, and had a wonderfully clean flavor.

The Vegan Japanese Sweet Potato Taco was a pleasant surprise. The natural sweetness of the sweet potato worked beautifully with the savory taco flavors, and it was satisfying even without meat.

Street Taco Plate : Comes with  turmeric jasmine rice (soft jasmine + warm turmeric aroma) and  tomatillo poblano black beans (fresh acidity that balances the plate). Asada --  Charred asada with bold street flavor. Birria --  Rich, juicy birria with slow‑cooked depth. Chicken --  Light, clean chicken with a bright citrus finish.

And one of the most memorable dishes was the The Lowrider Burrito - Sweet Chile Crispy Shrimp! The crispy shrimp with the sweet and slightly spicy chile sauce was such a delicious combination. If you love shrimp and flavorful burritos, this is definitely one to try.

Overall, I loved how Tu Madre combines Mexican flavors with creative Asian-inspired ingredients. From the fresh crudo tostadas and vegan taco to the rich birria bowl and crispy shrimp burrito, everything was flavorful and fun to try.

A great spot in Santa Monica if you're looking for creative Mexican fusion with lots of flavor! Highly recommended.

We stopped by for breakfast and lunch, and everything was packed with flavor! 🌯🌮

We started with the breakfast burritos filled with sausage and fresh avocado. The burritos were hearty, flavorful, and made for a satisfying breakfast.

The Baja Sweet Chili Tempura Shrimp came with rice and beans. The shrimp was crispy, sweet, and slightly spicy—such a great combination!

The Carne Asada Protein Bowl was loaded with turmeric rice, poblano black beans, street corn, pico de gallo, guacamole, and pickled onions. Fresh, colorful, and full of different flavors and textures in every bite.

For dessert, we had the Red Velvet Churros with cream cheese icing—crispy on the outside, soft inside, and the cream cheese icing was the perfect sweet finish. ❤️

We also tried the Strawberry Rita and Aqua Fresca Mojito, both refreshing and perfect for the meal.

The outdoor dining area is spacious and inviting, and the service was amazing—friendly, attentive, and welcoming. Definitely a great spot for a flavorful meal and a relaxing outdoor dining experience! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Blue on Richmond Terrace is easily one of Staten Island's best waterfront spots. The Thai Calamari is the perfect crispy starter with a great kick, and the Pasta Carbonara is rich, authentic, and comforting. The standout, though, is the Stuffed Lobster Tail—generously filled and paired perfectly with their creamy risotto. Great vibes, attentive service, and even better food. Highly recommend!

top_reviews.content: Took my family to come and try this new spot. It’s a quaint casual fast food like atmosphere, which was fine. The staff was super friendly and they had a good selection on their menu of different burgers crispy chicken sandwich sandwiches cheesesteak sandwiches all with different twists. The cheesesteak was perfect and we absolutely love the elote fries!!!!!! And you can’t forget their crispy chicken sandwich. My kids loved everything and it didn’t break the bank like some of these other Staten Island spots. We will definitely be coming back.!!!

It was massive, only $9.00, and delicious. Even with my husband's help, we left the paper boat full. Great local spot!

This has become one of my favorite neighborhood spots within walking distance of my house. Food is excellent. I usually get one of the hot dogs and an order of the elote fries (which has become a huge obsession of mine). The quality is amazing and the restaurant is extremely clean. I like to dine in here because the atmosphere is nice enough to do so. The TV screens and fun art are a really nice touch. I really gotta try a burger and cheesesteak one of these days. top_reviews.content: Fantastic cocktail bar in LA. Make sure to make reservations for this spot. If you eat at Mother Wolf, great for after dinner cocktails. The service was friendly and the drink delicious. I ordered the Morso Di Vita, a cocktail combining Grey Goose, Chinola Passion Fruit, tomato, basil and lemon. The cocktail came with a hefty price tag - $28.

I’ll definitely be back to explore the food at Bar Avoja.

Ok, other things... be mindful of the seating here. It's more 'speakeasy' bar style seating. No dining tables. You'll likely be in a velvet chair, sinking into it. Enjoy it. It's enveloping.

Parking can be tricky here. Take time to find parking. No surprise... it's all metered or paid parking lots. Or one can always valet!

This is a great place for a group outing. The staff was accommodating/attentive and kept the food coming. Full disclosure, Bella Mama Rose is sponsoring our football team this season and we like to give back to our sponsors by hosting our get togethers with them when we can.

Thank you Justin and Ashely for your support and accommodating our group even with 20 kids who play tackle football. We’ll definitely plan another date.
The new owner is AMAZING. the plates were massive! family style is the way to go to. The pizza was also huge. Appetizers, dinners and service were amazing!!

Jinya was amazing and one of the best ramen shops I’ve ever had the pleasure of visiting! All 4 of us were very happy with our choices, and each of our dishes was full of flavor and complexity. Back at JINYA Ramen Bar in Santa Monica (first discovered it in Austin!) - they have multiple LA locations.

Their spicy vegan ramen is one of the best vegetarian bowls I’ve had—filling, flavorful, and customizable. I usually ask them to skip the tofu and sometimes add bok choy or cabbage. They also serve meat options, but honestly, the veggie ramen stands on its own. Some people add egg to the bowl :)

Indoor-outdoor seating is nice, service is friendly, and parking’s easy with a paid lot right behind.

The menu seems to have changed slightly this visit —missed the little “slurping” message at the bottom of the bowl this time! Still, one of my favorite spots for casual ramen in LA.

My family and I had an incredible dining experience at Salerno’s.

From the moment we walked in, we were welcomed like family. The staff was attentive, courteous, and genuinely cared about making sure every guest felt comfortable and appreciated. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, with beautiful decor that felt authentic without trying too hard.

The food was outstanding. Every dish tasted like it was made from scratch with pride, tradition, and love. Course after course kept arriving, and somehow each one was better than the last. You could tell there is a deep respect for family recipes, quality ingredients, and hospitality.

What stood out most was how Da DaMaso and his team created an experience that felt less like dining in a restaurant and more like sitting around a family kitchen table in Southern Italy. There was a genuine warmth that is hard to find today.

Amazing food, amazing people, and an unforgettable experience. We will absolutely be back and highly recommend it to anyone looking for authentic Italian cuisine and true hospitality.

—
Dolce Family

For anyone who hasn't visited Dadamaso in Great Kills, you're truly missing out. My husband and I order takeout from there almost weekly and have also dined in several times, and every experience has been consistently excellent.

Before even mentioning the food, it's important to highlight the heart behind this restaurant. The family who owns DaDamaso brings a piece of Italy with them, creating dishes that reflect the traditions of their hometown. What stands out most is their commitment to authenticity, everything is made with fresh, high quality ingredients, and you can genuinely taste the difference.

As for the food, it's nothing short of exceptional. Some of my personal favorites include the petto di pollo grigliato, scaloppine di pollo al limone, and pollo bostoniano. Their eggplant dishes are also a must try, whether you prefer the classic eggplant parmesan with red sauce or the version prepared in a rich white sauce.

I fell incredibly lucky to have a restaurant like this right in my neighborhood. Beyond the delicious food, the family who runs DaDamaso are genuinely kind, warm , and welcoming, making every visit feel special. It's the kind of place that keeps you coming back again and again.

Finally, something autnetic and delicious has come to Staten Island. There's no chicken Cutlets parmegian here and thats because this restaurant is the real deal!!! Not your typical SI "italian" restaurant.  Hidden on Amboy Road by Giffords Lane, this Italian restaurant is owned by an family from Italy. The service os friendly, fast and cery personable. You are getting first hand attention from the owners that are running the kitchen and tables.  Seating is limited, there are 4 tables and counter seating so make sure to call and make a reservation but they do take out as well. The menu ranges from Pasta dishes, paninis, a variety of meat dishes and even family tradition of the largest triple burger you will ever see that was worth every bite! Delicious with burger, egg and potatoes.  This can be a shared dish, it was so flavorful and giant!  Dont forget the homemade Tirimasu for desert!!Prices were comparable to everywhere else. 3 sodas, an app, 3 main dishes, one desert and 2 cappucinos came to about $120. Totally worth every penny!  My husband was able to use his Italian to converse with staff. Being here, brought me back to the authentic small towns of Italy where the restaurants are family run, everything is fresh and you feel like family.
This is a definite recomment 10 out of 10.

Really enjoyed this place. Not too many seats so we were a bit worried about not having reservations but they accommodated us immediately. Will definitely try and make reservations for next time since it did seem to get reasonably busy. Food was fresh and delicious. Great for Great Kills!

Unbelievably great food and wonderful add on to staten island authentic Italian food small but very personable restaurant made our reservations and seated right on time. Family owned italian restaurant. No hired cooks so full attention goes to there food we ate.

top_reviews.content: Me and my husband were passing by and had to try. And it did not disappoint. Everything was great. Food was fresh, orange juice natural, and the place is very nice and well kept. If we were from California, we would definitely come back.

We stopped by Mel’s Diner before seeing a Jimmy Kimmel taping, mostly because of its iconic reputation. The ambiance definitely delivers classic décor and a fun, nostalgic vibe. As for the food, it’s solid but nothing out of the ordinary. The patty melt was the standout and genuinely delicious. My girlfriend’s BLT was a bit underwhelming, though still enjoyable.
Overall, Mel’s is worth a visit for the ambiance and the experience, but for the price point, there are definitely other spots we’d try before returning.

As someone who deeply values operational excellence and tangible value, my dinner at Mel’s Drive-In was a masterclass in how a classic American diner should be managed. Located right in the vibrant heart of Hollywood, this iconic spot is an immediate standout for its pristine upkeep. The chrome accents gleam, the classic booths are immaculate, and the entire retro space radiates a level of cleanliness that commands immediate respect.

The menu delivers on the promise of true homestyle food, executed with premium ingredients. The grass-fed beef burgers are expertly seared and remarkably juicy, while the hand-dipped milkshakes offer a rich, authentic depth of flavor that puts modern fast-casual competitors to shame. It is comfort food elevated by a clear commitment to quality control and culinary consistency.

What truly elevates Mel's from a nostalgic novelty into a premier dining destination, however, is the service. The staff operates with remarkable efficiency and sharp attentiveness. Orders are processed swiftly, refills materialize seamlessly, and the hospitality is genuinely warm without ever feeling forced. Mel’s Drive-In isn’t just trading on its mid-century heritage; it is actively earning its reputation with every single shift. Unreservedly recommended.

Mel’s Diner definitely delivers on atmosphere, with its classic décor and nostalgic Hollywood diner vibe. The food was decent, but nothing particularly memorable. I ordered Mel’s Burger, which was pretty average and didn’t really stand out, and the fries were just okay.
Overall, Mel’s is worth visiting for the ambiance and the experience, but for the price, there are plenty of other spots we’d try before returning.

Stopped by Mel’s Drive-In with the family and had a pretty good time. The food tasted good, the kids menu had solid options, and the whole place had that classic diner feel.

The banana shake was probably the best part. It was thick, creamy, and tasted like an actual old-school diner shake, not something rushed or watered down.

Only real downside was the price. The food was good, but it was definitely more expensive than I expected for what it was. Overall I’d give it about a 7/10. Good stop with the family, just a little pricey.

Mel’s is a very interesting diner that’s on Hollywood boulevard. Location wise it’s  spectacular and close to the main attractions as well as having a dedicated parking lot for your vehicles.

Food though was very disappointing… breakfast burrito came out really bland and lacked any seasoning at all and I asked for double meat and literally only had four little chunks of sausage in it. Mozzarella sticks are almost $19 and they literally were flavorless while yet filled with cheese so I’ll give it that I suppose??? All in all It’s great for that retro aspect and to grab quick bite if your server is actually attentive (ours was not and we had to repeatedly ask for a refill) though with this being said, the ice coffee is delicious that they have.

ALWAYS FUN eating at Mel's Diner at any of their locations, nostalgically modeled after 1950s-1960s drive-in style restaurants pictured in "American Graffiti" movie. The Hollywood diner is in the Max Factor building, tucked-in next to the Hollywood Museum.

Huge, varied menu with breakfast, burgers and sandwiches (with of course, fries, sweet potato fries or onion rings and a milkshake 😋), great meatloaf and fresh roasted turkey dishes available. Kids menu choices served in a convertible car shaped box!

Small parking lot next to the restaurant validates for Mel's Diner and the Hollywood Museum at $20 flat rate (vs $30 maximum) if you're going to be in the area more than a couple hours (we visited the Hollywood Museum next door after we ate).

Classic Hollywood diner experience with a super fun retro atmosphere. The neon signs, old-school decor, and location right on Sunset Blvd make it feel like stepping into a movie scene. Great spot to stop after exploring Hollywood, especially at night when everything lights up. Food was solid, service friendly, and the vibe is really what makes this place special.

The area around Mel’s also felt much safer and cleaner than parts of Hollywood Boulevard, which made it a comfortable place to walk around and enjoy the atmosphere. There’s also a convenient paid parking lot right next to it for around $6, which makes visiting really easy for Hollywood standards. Touristy? Yes — but in a good, iconic LA way.

top_reviews.content:
This was my fourth Danny Meyer restaurant visit—after Shake Shack, Union Square Cafe, and Manhatta—and it was easily the best. Everything was exquisite: the ambiance, the food, and the service.

The Snowdance Farm Chicken was one of the best chicken dishes I've ever had. It was crispy yet chewy on the outside, beautifully tender on the inside, and brought together by an absolutely delicious Asian-inspired sauce. The tomato salad was also super refreshing, bursting with a vibrant, healthy summer flavor.

Best of all, our server, Marissa, made this the finest dining experience we’ve had in New York. She was welcoming without being intrusive, exceptionally professional, and genuinely friendly.

The presentation of the dishes was beautiful, but the food itself was just average. Nothing really stood out or surprised us in terms of flavor. The bread was excellent, and the fish and desserts were enjoyable, but overall the meal didn't quite live up to the expectations for the price.
The biggest disappointment was the atmosphere. The restaurant was extremely noisy, and it honestly felt more like a food court than a fine dining restaurant. It was difficult to have a conversation without raising our voices.
Another downside was the wait for dessert. We had to wait about 20 minutes after our main course before it was served. It may have been because the restaurant was busy, but it definitely affected the overall dining experience.
Overall, it's worth trying once, but I was expecting a more memorable meal and a much better dining atmosphere.

(Review from Dec. 2025): First time at Gramercy Tavern, we had lunch on the tavern side. We both really enjoyed everything we ate, they are serving some really solid American food. The flatbread and dips and the burger stood out above the rest. I think the burger is an all timer in the city. The milk and cookie dessert was fun but it didn’t blow us away. Gramercy also has a great cocktail program, so definitely keep that in mind. I had one of the best dirty martinis ever, it came with homemade blue cheese olives that were out of this world. As to be expected of this restaurant group, the service we experienced Michelin quality, attentive but warm and easy. They brought us a complimentary mini-cake to celebrate our anniversary, it was delicious. One great thing about Gramercy is how seasonal it is. It makes you want to return to see the new menu items and motifs. Overall, highly recommend Gramercy Tavern and can’t wait to return!

Gramercy Tavern is a tried and true establishment. You can safely expect their quality of both food and services to be excellent every single time.

One thing that really stood out to me is that even though I am a meat lover, I find myself looking forward to their veggie dishes over and over again. It is impossible to recreate these dishes at home which makes the price tag much easier to digest.

Overall, I wouldn’t hesitate to book the dinning room at GT for any special occasions or for when you just want to indulge on a random Tuesday

If I had to become a regular anywhere, this would be my pick. You can tell how impressive this restaurant is by the way they execute American cuisine—which, as you know, is usually my least favorite. But they absolutely nailed it.

I was genuinely so pleased with everything. The farm chicken with the onion rings were standouts. Crispy, perfectly fried. The beef steak sandwich looked incredible, but I was way too full to even take a bite—so I’ll definitely be back and will keep you posted. The beef carpaccio was delicious, and while the mushrooms pasta were slightly salty, the creamy, flavorful sauce paired perfectly with the sweet potato bun. (This is their restaurant week menu!)

And let me just say—the desserts are a must. You have to get the apple pie. It was amazing, especially with the hint of balsamic vinegar and Parmesan—holy moly!! The chocolate cake came with a woodside-flavored ice cream that I had never tried before, and I absolutely fell in love.

The back room is stunning, and the service is easily the kind to deserve 30% tip—attentive, polished, and welcoming. This is also an amazing spot to bring your partner to meet the family!

We celebrated our anniversary at Gramercy Tavern, and it was truly a memorable experience. Not only was the food amazing, but the service was also warm, welcoming, and highly professional from start to finish.

Every appetizer we ordered was absolutely delicious, especially the grilled oysters. The entrées were equally impressive—the burger was excellent, and the brick-pressed chicken was simply divine. It was one of the best chicken dishes we've had in a long time.

To top it all off, the desserts were fantastic. Every dish was thoughtfully prepared, and the attention to detail really stood out.

Overall, Gramercy Tavern delivered an exceptional dining experience with outstanding food and impeccable service. It was the perfect place to celebrate a special occasion, and we'll definitely be coming back again.

We ate at the tavern and ordered the monkfish, tavern burger, beignets, and a beer. The food was good, with the monkfish being the preferred entree. While not normally dessert people, the beignets were really well done with a good balance of warm sweet and salty dough, strawberry/rhubarb compote with good acidity, and very creamy vanilla ice cream. Ultimately I was most impressed with the service. Even in the less stuffy tavern area, our server Amanda and one other were attentive but not pushy. Our appetizer plates were cleanly swapped. The way that the burger is prepared normally was well communicated and they kindly cut it in half so we could share. The meal felt really seamless. I’d recommend this restaurant for 2-6 people so you can try things and share a table. The light airy environment makes it nice if you have guests visiting from out of town. There were also non-alcoholic cocktails on the menu.

Came to the Gramercy Tavern for a weekend lunch and was seated immediately once the restaurant opened up at 11:30 on the dot. Ordered the broccolini salad, roasted oysters, brick chicken and the meatballs. The broccolini salad was refreshing and had nice texture, roasted oysters was really tasty but there was barely any oyster - they were incredibly small tidbits. The brick chicken was good and chicken was tender but pretty salty. Meatballs were more like meatloaf and had good flavor but very heavy with the polenta and cheese, could have used some acid to cut the heaviness. Service was fine and efficient but not overly friendly. Decor of restaurant was nice and classy and I liked the fire oven that was open.

Overall good meal but wouldn't go out of my way to come here.

Finally made it to Mother Wolf Los Angeles after loving the Las Vegas location so much, and honestly, it completely lived up to the hype.

The focaccia, lemon pasta, cacio e pepe, and margherita pizza were all excellent — this place really knows how to work with dough, bread, and pasta. Even dessert was fantastic: an espresso-dark chocolate gelato with a crisp wafer on top that was perfect for sharing.

What stood out just as much as the food was the service. Our server asked whether I was vegetarian or Jain, which genuinely surprised me because that level of awareness almost never happens at restaurants. Everyone — from the valet team to the servers — was warm, attentive, and completely on top of things all night.

Definitely a special occasion place, but one that absolutely delivers.

Let me be clear—I’ve never had much patience for fine dining or the inflated egos and price tags that usually come with it. Give me a good sandwich over a delicate plate of pasta any day.

But this place… it got me. The kind of place that doesn’t ask for your approval—it just earns it. The gamberi had that perfect snap, the Diavola pizza came out blistered and unapologetic, and the oxtail pasta? Rich, slow, and indulgent in all the right ways.

I didn’t expect to like it. I definitely didn’t expect to come back.
But I will.

The food, service and ambiance were all really wonderful…but esp the food and service.  The meatballs, pizza and pasta were phenomenally toothsome and the arugula salad was refreshingly pleasing.  Our wonderful server had such a contagious, joyful, fun energy that elevated our experience.  He made thoughtful recommendations and always kept an eye on us to make sure we were want for nothing (without being intrusive).  All restaurants should have staff like him.  All in all, a wonderful meal…and we would heartily recommend and happily return here to try other dishes.

Mother Wolf is absolutely worth the visit. The food was exceptional, and the atmosphere is everything you’d hope for—energetic, stylish, and filled with an eclectic crowd that makes for a fun night out.
The only reason I’m giving four stars instead of five is the hostess experience. The welcome wasn’t particularly attentive, and for a restaurant of this caliber, first impressions matter.
Once we were seated, however, the experience completely turned around. We enjoyed a cocktail at the bar while waiting, and the bartenders were warm and welcoming. Our server, James, was charming, knowledgeable, and attentive throughout the evening. The sommelier was excellent, and even the bus staff was on top of every detail. The service from everyone after check-in was truly outstanding.
The food did not disappoint. The Sfincione was a delicious way to start, and the Pizza Rosa was light, crisp, and packed with flavor. The Misticanza di Campagna was fresh and perfectly dressed, while the Gamberi in Salsa Verde were cooked beautifully. Our favorites were the perfectly grilled Branzino alla Brace and the flavorful Tagliata di Manzo, both of which were outstanding. The roasted Carote al Forno made a surprisingly memorable side, and we finished with the Pistachio and Blood Orange desserts—both fantastic and the perfect ending to the meal.
I do wish the wine list had a little more variety beyond Italian selections, but given that Mother Wolf stays true to its Italian roots, it’s understandable.
The only disappointment was one we created ourselves! My dining companions are lactose intolerant, and since the restaurant encourages sharing, we skipped many of the pasta dishes. Watching gorgeous bowls of pasta come out all night gave me serious food envy, so that’s already at the top of my list for our next visit.
Mother Wolf delivers beautiful food, exceptional service, and one of the best dining atmospheres in Hollywood. Fix the hostess experience, and this would easily be a five-star restaurant. We’ll definitely be back—and next time, I’m ordering the pasta.

We don’t like noisy environments. the Lemon Grove blends a bustling environment with a nice, calm outdoor space. I especially love the garden and rooftop view of Hollywood. Kumquat and lime trees surrounded the patio which was a nice touch. Highly recommend the chill rooftop ambience.

The food was terrific. Great Caesar (filled with anchovies as it should be), runner beans, and bone marrow. The lamb rigatoni was to die for. The only gripe I’d have is the rigatoni was non-canonical with the pasta being a bit small like macaroni. The shiso pasta was also rich and good.

Finally, the dessert was OK. I like cheesecake  with crusts but at least they have a basque cheesecake (the worst type of cheesecake but cheesecake nevertheless). Would not recommend the peach cobbler.

A Night at Karl Strauss Brewing Co. — Food, Vibes & A Come-Through Save From Our Server

My wife and I hit Karl Strauss Brewing Co., expecting a simple night out — but it turned into one of those evenings that checks every box: great food, great drinks, great atmosphere, and a service recovery handled like a pro.

🍗 The Food: Straight-Up Flavor That Delivers

We opened with wings — Sweet Chili Garlic for me and Buffalo for my wife — and both plates came out looking ready for a photoshoot. Crispy, sauced perfectly, stacked over fresh diced cabbage with clean-cut carrots and celery.

The sweet chili hit that perfect balance of heat and sweetness, and the buffalo came in bold, creamy, and unapologetic. Every bite had crunch, flavor, and zero sloppiness.

Then the Duck Fat Pretzel Bites dropped in like little bombs of joy — crispy outside, soft inside, coated with parmesan and herbs. Easily one of the best appetizers we’ve had in a minute.

🍹 The Drinks: Off-the-Chain Fire

My wife ordered the Mongo Margarita, and it stole the show instantly — bright, icy, tajín rim, lime on the edge, and the flavor? Smooth, tropical, and “yeah, this one’s trouble” good.

I ordered… something. And look — I forgot the name, because the first sip shut my brain off. All I remember is that it was cold, balanced, refreshing, and straight-up fire. One of those drinks that just hits right.

🧑‍🍺 The Service: Shoutout to Art

Now here’s where the night showed its real character.

Art, our server, was slow getting to our table at first. We noticed it.
But the man didn’t duck it — he owned it.

To make it right, he brought us a couple samples of beer on the house, and from that moment on, he locked in. Friendly, attentive, solid service the whole way through.

That’s how you turn a slip into a save. Respect to Art.

🏙️ The Atmosphere: Industrial Warmth With Style

The place looks incredible — barrels stacked along the walls, warm lighting, exposed ceilings, neon art, brick accents, and that big glowing “WILL WORK FOR BEER” sign that sets the tone.

It’s roomy enough to talk without yelling, stylish without being pretentious, and comfortable enough to relax into the night.

👫 The Vibe: A King and His Queen, Enjoying the Moment

The best part? Seeing my wife relaxed, smiling, and loving her meal.
Food tastes better when the person across from you is glowing.
And tonight, everything lined up perfectly.

⭐ Final Verdict: A Full 10/10 Night

Karl Strauss delivered across the board:

Food: 🔥🔥🔥
Drinks: dangerous in the best way
Service: recovered strong thanks to Art
Atmosphere: classy, warm, and full of personality. It wasn’t just dinner it was a memory.
The kind you don’t rush.
The kind you repeat.

I’ve stopped into Ocean Prime several times for a quick meal and a drink at the bar, and it has become one of those places where I know I’m going to have a great experience. Everything I’ve tried has been top-notch—the oysters, sushi, Crab Louie salad, burger, lobster roll, butter cake, and carrot cake have all been excellent. The Ocean Roll is a particular standout, and the Hot & Dirty Martini, with olive-oil-infused Belvedere and Calabrian chili blue-cheese-stuffed Castelvetrano olives, is fantastic.

But what really makes me want to come back is the service. I’ve been fortunate enough to have Natasha take care of me four times now, and she is absolutely lovely. She’s warm, attentive, gracious, and has a wonderful way of making even a quick meal or drink at the bar feel special. Ocean Prime is already a great restaurant, but Natasha genuinely elevates the experience. I always look forward to seeing her when I come in.

Classy from the moment you walk in.

Service was outstanding. Friendly, personable, and the kind of staff that makes you feel genuinely welcome without being overbearing.

The whole place has a great vibe. Upscale without feeling stuffy, great drinks, great food, and an overall experience that just feels polished from start to finish.

There were 4 of us visiting during Winter Restaurant Week, and we basically tried everything on the pre fixie menu. The crab cake was ordered separately and ended up being my favorite dish of the meal.
I had the fish (tilapia perhaps), and I absolutely loved it. I would honestly come back just for that. I’m not usually a big fan of French onion soup in general, but that’s purely my personal preference. The grilled chicken was also very good—juicy and not dry at all. The salmon served with sticky rice was an interesting and enjoyable combination as well. The desserts were decent overall, though I personally wish the carrot cake had been a bit less sweet.

I tried the Beverly Hills location before and it was just okay, but the NYC spot is on another level.
The lobster linguini is incredible rich, flavorful, and unforgettable. Honestly, nothing else I’ve eaten lately compares.
Kids’ menu is excellent, cocktails are top-notch, and the service is friendly.
Great atmosphere, perfect for family or friends. Definitely coming back!

I wanted seafood but also wanted something that felt like a proper dinner, so Ocean Prime seemed like a good middle ground. I started with the lobster bisque, then ordered the sea scallops, lobster linguine, and carrot cake. I also spent far too long looking at the sushi section before deciding not to make the meal even larger.

The lobster bisque was smooth and rich without being completely overwhelming. The scallops were probably my favorite because they had a nice sear while staying tender inside, and the risotto underneath made the whole thing feel more substantial. The lobster linguine was messy in a very enjoyable way, with enough lobster that I wasn't just hunting around the pasta for pieces. The carrot cake was huge and rich, so sharing it would have been the smarter move.

The restaurant has a polished feel, but the food doesn't get lost behind it. I could see this working equally well for a special dinner or just an evening when you want seafood without going somewhere super casual.

The best dinner of my life!! After a day spent in the cold rain, Ocean Prime was a warm reprieve. The staff, service, and food were all exceptional. We started with the oysters, wedge salad, and lobster bisque followed by the bone-in ribeye and lobster linguine. Not a bad bite to be found. We ended the night with gooey butter cake. I used to order takeout from Jimmy Max all the time—their appetizers and pizza were always delicious. I don’t live five minutes away anymore, but I recently went back and was blown away, especially by their gluten-free options.

I have a daughter with celiac disease, and on Staten Island the options are usually very limited—pizza, pasta, or maybe a burger bun. Not at Jimmy Max. Their gluten-free menu is extensive. My daughter hadn’t had a rice ball in over six years, and the one she had here was excellent. The GF BBQ ribs were amazing, and they even had gluten-free mozzarella sticks—which is almost unheard of. Everything we tried was delicious.

For dinner, she had gluten-free chicken parm with penne vodka. I had the chicken rollatini, which was outstanding. Dessert didn’t disappoint either—my other two daughters and I shared the crumb cake and Mississippi mud cake, and my oldest had a gluten-free brownie cake ( we took a few bites before i remembered to take a photo). All fantastic.

What really makes Jimmy Max a must-try isn’t just the food—it’s the service and care. Our waiter, Matthew, was attentive and extremely mindful of my daughter’s condition. The wait staff truly worked as a team. Everyone backed each other up—clearing empty plates, refilling soda and water glasses, and even replacing silverware with fresh settings without being asked. That level of attentiveness really stood out and made the whole experience feel smooth and welcoming. The owner, Jimmy, even came over to our table and shared his story and why he’s so committed to offering safe options for guests with allergies.

It’s rare to find a restaurant on S.I. that truly takes food allergies seriously. Being able to go out to eat with peace of mind—knowing your child is safe—is priceless. Highly recommend Jimmy Max.

I came here on a Sunday afternoon after seeing a bunch of Middle Eastern restaurants in this area. This will have great ratings online. And a few people actually recommended it. The only issue is that I drifted off from ordering exactly what they told me to order and made a few mistakes. I will start off by saying that the bread service that’s complementary is amazing. As soon as we walked in, we were greeted with bread and water at the table. Also came with olive oil and other spices. That was really good. The only issue is that this is my first time and I’m not familiar with Middle Eastern cuisine. So I ordered a spinach pie, a ground beef pie, and a salad to start off with. All three of those issues were terrible in my experience the ground beef had no flavor whatsoever. The spinach literally tasted like lemon and lime juice. And the salad was $18. All it was was bell peppers, cucumbers, tomatoes, with pita chips, drizzled in a pomegranate sauce. If I would’ve known that, my entrée came with a side salad I would’ve never ordered a bowl of bell peppers. In terms of the service it was only good when the bride came out and the water was served. No one came around as how our food was. No one asked if if it was our first time there. No one gave recommendations. There was one dish that stood out to me, which was the grilled chicken platter. It came on a bit of rice. The flavors were amazing. The char of the chicken was outstanding. I understand why people would say that this is a great restaurant. But it’s only great Al Badawi is a place where the experience can vary significantly depending on what you order. The menu is extensive, but it lacks focus, and not every dish reflects the same level of execution. It feels like there are clear standouts that the restaurant is known for, and others that don’t quite live up to that reputation.

Unfortunately, we missed the mark with our initial selections. The first three dishes we ordered, including the ground beef pie and spinach pie, were underwhelming to the point where we only took a few bites before leaving them behind. In hindsight, it felt like a misstep in ordering, but also one where some guidance from the server could have made a big difference. A few recommendations or insight into what the kitchen does best would have helped steer the experience in a better direction.

That said, not everything fell short. The chicken and rice platter was excellent and gave a glimpse into why this place has built such a strong following. Portions are generous across the board, and pricing remains reasonable, especially considering the shareable nature of the dishes. The fact that it is BYOB is another major plus.

Looking back, skipping the hummus platter with multiple accompaniments was likely a mistake, as it seems to be one of the more talked-about items on the menu. It is something I would return specifically to try.

One noticeable gap in the experience was the lack of follow-up from the staff after dishes were left mostly untouched. A quick check-in or offer to adjust the order would have gone a long way in turning things around.

Al Badawi clearly has strong dishes and a loyal following, but the inconsistency in the menu and lack of guidance can make the experience hit or miss.

For now, I would rate it 3 out of 5 stars, with the expectation that a more informed second visit could tell a different story.

Chama Mama, situated at 373 Amsterdam Avenue, offers a dining experience that is at once refined, hospitable, and deeply rooted in a culinary tradition that deserves far wider recognition than it typically enjoys. From the moment of our arrival to our departure, the staff demonstrated a level of attentiveness and professionalism that one increasingly finds to be the exception rather than the rule in New York’s crowded restaurant scene.
Our selections provided a most agreeable introduction, or perhaps reintroduction, to the virtues of Georgian cuisine. The “Let’s Chama Sandwich” proved to be both hearty and thoughtfully composed, its flavors balanced in a manner that suggested restraint rather than excess. The charred eggplant wrap, faintly smoky and supple in texture, showed how even the humblest ingredient, when treated with care, can attain distinction. The Khinkali, those celebrated Georgian dumplings, were executed with notable precision, yielding a savory interior that rewarded proper appreciation. The lamb kebab, meanwhile, was tender and well-seasoned, its preparation reflecting a confident understanding of the ingredient rather than any need to disguise it.
To speak of Georgian cuisine more broadly is to acknowledge a tradition shaped by geography and history in equal measure. Positioned at the juncture of Europe and Asia, Georgia has absorbed influences from a variety of neighboring cultures while preserving an identity distinctly its own. The cuisine favors freshness, herbs, and a judicious use of spices, often bringing together walnuts, garlic, and pomegranate in combinations that are at once unfamiliar and entirely coherent. It is a cuisine that places a premium on conviviality, on the shared table, and on a sense of continuity with the past.
For me, the experience carries a somewhat personal resonance. Many years ago, in one of my earliest assignments as a writer for the Department of Defense, I was tasked with preparing a cultural orientation on the Republic of Georgia. In the course of that work, I first encountered the country’s culinary traditions, which left a lasting impression. It is no small matter, therefore, to encounter a restaurant that renders those traditions with both authenticity and evident respect.
Chama Mama does not strain for effect, nor does it indulge in theatrical excess. Instead, it offers something rather more valuable: a faithful presentation of a remarkable cuisine, accompanied by service that reflects genuine pride in what is being served. One leaves not merely satisfied, but quietly persuaded that Georgian food, in the right hands, can stand comfortably alongside more familiar culinary traditions.

The food was every bit as impressive as the setting. Each dish was colorful, beautifully plated, and packed with flavors that felt fresh and unexpected. The crab enchiladas were easily the standout of the meal—rich, balanced, and absolutely delicious.

Valet parking was $17 for a couple of hours, which is pretty standard for the area. Between the outstanding service, unique food, and inviting ambiance, Ka'teen is definitely a place we'll be coming back to.

This was by and far my favourite meal of my trip.

top_reviews.content: As a Polish woman born in Kartuzy, finding authentic Polish restaurants in Los Angeles isn't easy, but this is my absolute go-to spot and I love everything about it—the atmosphere, the service, and especially the food! My usual order is the Polish Taster Platter, which gives you a delicious sampling of potato pancakes, pierogies, kielbasa, and cucumber salad. Summary: Not on my “Must Try” list of restaurants in Santa Monica for vegans

Food: I truly love Eastern European foods and flavors. I’m spoiled in this department with having access to many great restaurants on the east coast, not to mention my partner is Polish. I was excited to try the food here during a work trip as it came highly recommended. I only had one option on the menu, which was a beet salad. Needless to say I was really disappointed this was the only option on the menu that was plant based. On a separate visit I was able to try their vegan stuffed cabbage (didn’t take a pic) and found the flavor to be underwhelming. The salad tasted good, but wasn’t filling as a meal and isn’t interesting culinarily (been there, done that). The stuffed cabbage tomato sauce was borderline bland and the filling was the same. Plant based doesn’t have to be flavorless and boring.

Service: Any time I’ve been to this restaurant the service has been good. Servers are friendly, seem to know the menu, and are quick to make sure everyone is taken care of.  I prefer the outdoor patio in the back over the dining room. The interior to me feels very dated and a little musty.

Recommendation: I wouldn’t suggest for vegans to visit this spot when in Santa Monica. The options are very limited and need some fine tuning, in my opinion. I’d highly recommend the restaurant take the dedicated vegan items off the menu if they can’t improve the flavor of options like the stuffed cabbage.

I visited Le Bernardin for the first time since before COVID and was really looking forward to coming back. My expectations were very high based on my previous experience.

The service was impeccable from beginning to end. The staff was attentive, professional, and made us feel very welcome throughout the evening.

The food, however, was a bit disappointing. Aside from the first complimentary appetizer, almost every dish felt like the sauce was the main focus rather than the seafood itself. The sauces were beautifully prepared, but they often overpowered the fish instead of complementing it. I also expected the seafood to taste fresher and more vibrant, but something just felt off that evening. It made me wonder whether it was simply an off night or if the restaurant’s style has shifted toward bold sauces instead of letting the freshness of the ingredients shine.

The desserts were outstanding. We were celebrating a birthday and received a complimentary carrot cake, and it was honestly the best carrot cake I have ever had. It was absolutely incredible and ended the meal on a very high note.

I still have a great deal of respect for Le Bernardin and hope this was just an off day because I remember thinking much more highly of the food before. I would happily return and hope for an experience that better matches the restaurant’s reputation.

Welcome to one of the top 10 dining experiences of my life. (Le Bernardin is actually on this list twice for me!) The food is spectacular. The portions are PERFECT. I have only been gone a couple of hours and am already trying to figure out when I can return. It's definitely an indulgence -but well worth it if you love an amazing experience.

As a fan of Eric Ripert, I had been wanting to dine at Le Bernardin for years. I decided to go for lunch without a reservation in the lounge.

Beautiful, understated, slightly dated decor and comfortable seating. Mario was an attentive waiter - consummate professional.

I chose the City Harvest menu - supporting a local nonprofit- for 94$. The lobster starter was lobster in mayonnaise with avocado between two discs of perfectly cooked potato. It was over-salted and the lobster didn’t shine. The sea bass second course was also over-salted, slightly undercooked and chewy with a strong cumin sauce. Unbalanced. The pistachio dessert featured four preparations- the ice cream being the most balanced and of beautiful texture.

Sadly, I was underwhelmed. Ripert, had he eaten the menu, would’ve certainly been upset. I came for what he is known for - brilliantly balanced ingredients with minimal intervention that lets the seafood shine. This was not my experience at Le Bernardin.

It took us some time to get a reservation but it was definitely worth the wait. You can taste and feel how delicate every single dish was prepared. The wine pairing is recommended. Avoid eating all the bread that was offered each course😂. We got the later spot because we really wanted to try this place , it was a bit rushed for the last couple of courses, but that does not take away all the good stuffs from this lovely dinner.

I really enjoyed this place and will be back to cherish the good food and homey energy.

Oh also they sell their dumplings frozen so a great way to enjoy their dumplings at home too!

La Grande Boucherie: A Standout Pre-Theater Gem (January 2024)
My partner and I visited La Grande Boucherie in January 2024, catching an early dinner before a show. We decided to take advantage of their pre-theater menu, and it honestly ended up being a highlight of our trip. For the price, it was a fantastic deal—one of the best values we’ve found for a set menu in Manhattan, and easily one of our favorite dining experiences in the city.

The food really hit the mark across the board. The mussels were incredibly fresh and served in a rich, savory broth that we couldn't stop dipping our bread into. The steak frites was a total win as well; the steak was seasoned perfectly and cooked to a flawless medium-rare, paired with those classic, crispy bistro-style frites. To finish, we tried both dessert options on the menu, and both were delicious. It was the perfect high note to end on before heading to the theater.

What really pulled the whole experience together was the service, which remained attentive and professional despite the pre-theater rush. The timing was handled perfectly for our curtain call, allowing us to enjoy the meal without feeling rushed. The atmosphere at La Grande Boucherie is stunning, with its soaring ceilings and bustling French brasserie energy. If you’re looking for a reliable spot near the theater district that actually delivers on quality and value, this is it. Even two years later, we still talk about this meal.

We asked if the bacon that came with one of the dishes could be replaced with something simple, such as extra potatoes, but were told substitutions were not possible. We had hoped there might be some flexibility given the dietary preference, but unfortunately there wasn't.
Our table was also located near the waiter station, which meant there was a constant amount of noise from dishes, utensils, and staff activity. It made the experience feel a little less relaxing than we would have preferred.
The service was perfectly fine, but nothing especially memorable or above and beyond what you might expect at this price point.
Overall, we enjoyed the food and the beautiful setting and would return again. Next time, we would hope for a quieter table and perhaps a few more vegetarian-friendly options.

La Grande Boucherie is a beautiful restaurant that truly captures the atmosphere of a Parisian brasserie. The decor is stunning, and the ambiance is easily its biggest strength—you really feel like you've stepped into Paris.

We tried the baguette with butter, oysters, steak tartare, escargots, octopus, and finished with the Basque cheesecake. The oysters were fresh, the tartare was very good, and I also enjoyed the octopus. The only disappointment was the bread, which I found quite dry.

As someone from France, I felt the atmosphere was more authentic than the food. The dishes were good, but they felt more French-inspired than truly French, especially considering the price point.

The service was mixed. Our servers were friendly, but the welcome at the entrance felt rather cold when we asked to switch from a high-top to a regular table.

Overall, it's a beautiful place with a great Parisian atmosphere, but I think you're paying more for the setting than for the food.

Seems ridiculous to not allow people up briefly after spending $175 for two people.

Tonight they had a prefix menu only for $65 per person with a set of first and third courses and for the main the choice between salmon or duck. The flavors were very good although the portions were pretty small especially for the amount they are charging. 1st course was the Red Pepper Campechana, which was delicious but was gone in 4-5 bites. I would have doubled the portion for the price. For my main course I chose the Salmon, which was also very good flavor wise, however I prefer my salmon to be crispier. The inside of this one was a bit cold to the touch. Finally for dessert came the Financier which was a fair portion with great flavors, but based on how much restaurants make for desserts and drinks I was sad to see they chose the make this the larger portion and not the starter or the main dish.

Overall a nice meal aside from the portion size and cost. This is why I don’t usually like to do prefix menus at non Michelin restaurants because I prefer to choose what I want to eat versus going with the suggestions.

My recent visit to Zaya DTLA was a mixed experience. While there were several highlights regarding the quality of the evening, the management of our seating situation left much to be desired.

**The Highlights:**
The food was undeniably delicious and served quickly, and we were thoroughly impressed by our server, who was both lovely and very attentive throughout our meal. The ambiance of the restaurant is also quite nice, making it an appealing spot for a night out.

**The Experience:**
The issue arose when we tried to coordinate seating with friends. We had a reservation for three, and our friends had a separate reservation for two. Upon our early arrival, we asked the hostess if the two parties could be seated together. We were informed that to do so, we would be required to pay a $150 deposit--a policy that felt unnecessary given that we were already physically present at the restaurant.

After declining the deposit, we requested to be seated at least near one another. The hostess denied this request, stating that they "randomly sit guests." This explanation felt illogical, particularly because upon our friends' arrival, there were clearly two empty tables for two available near us. Instead of accommodating our simple request, the staff walked our friends to the complete opposite side of the restaurant. It was disappointing to see such a lack of flexibility when the space was clearly available to provide a better guest experience.

ZAYA delivers a lively night out with great live music and a polished downtown vibe. Reservations for our group of six required a $150 deposit, which was smoothly deducted from the final check- no issues there.

The food landed mostly strong. The spinach artichoke dip was hands down the best I’ve ever had... rich, hot, and addictive (best with an order of bread). For dinner, the Alfredo Affair did its job and left me satisfied. One dish missed the mark: the Midnight Mushroom Marsala came out a bit too liquidy for my friend, and she sent it back.

I’m not a drinker, but the spritzy mocktail was fun enough to mingle, and the rest of the table genuinely enjoyed their cocktails. Service could use some polishing, but honestly, I’d rather average service than bad food—and ZAYA gets that part mostly right. A solid DTLA spot with room to grow.

top_reviews.content: This was our second time going to Red Rooster, and the first time we’d been in years. The service and atmosphere is excellent, and overall I think the food is good with great portions. I always think maybe it should be less expensive, and that they’re trying to be high end but not quite making it. If you want soul food, home cooked, hearty meals this is a great option though. The staff are super friendly, and their service is excellent. In terms of menu highlights, the fried chicken is superb - bowl, sandwich, or just the yardbird chicken, each and every variety is delicious. The collard greens are solid, most dishes come with a good amount of vegetables and things are well-seasoned. We really enjoyed the deviled eggs - so creamy, so much flavor, just delicious. They seem to come in 4s, we got 3 weirdly but maybe that’s the lunch menu item. I really enjoyed the rice bowl on the lunch specials, but the $10 charge for chicken made the dish $28 which is just a little too high. Overall, the experience was quite good and next time we’ve got the budget for it we will come back.

My family and friends were really looking forward to dining at Red Rooster in Harlem because of its reputation, but unfortunately our experience fell well below expectations.

We were told when we arrived that our table would only be available for an hour and a half, which immediately made the meal feel rushed instead of relaxed.

The restaurant only had two small restrooms, and they were extremely warm. The water wasn’t cold and came without ice or lemon. I also noticed there were no conversations or warnings regarding cross-contamination for guests with food allergies.

I will say this—the presentation of the food was beautiful. Every dish arrived looking like it belonged in a magazine, which made me even more excited to dig in. Unfortunately, the flavors and execution simply didn’t live up to the presentation.

As for the food:
• The sweet tea wasn’t sweet, or deeply brewed.
• The table was very small for our party.
• The chicken wings were overcooked, tough, and hard enough to scrape the inside of our mouths.
• The peach and tomato salad lacked flavor.
• The deviled eggs were supposed to come with sweet potato hummus, but what was served tasted like plain hummus.
• The cornbread had a nice thickness and decent texture, but the flavor was bland.
• The side bread that came with the pasta was extremely hard.
• My daughter’s seafood pasta contained shell fragments.
• The chimichurri tasted more like seasoned oil than chimichurri.
• One of the guest at my table ordered a medium-rare steak, but it arrived much closer to rare.

The silverware was noticeably bent, dirty plates sat on our table longer than they should have, and staff even removed an extra chair from our table while we were still dining. It wasn’t a major issue, but it added to the feeling that we were being rushed.

Now for the bright spot—the live jazz music was absolutely phenomenal! The musicians were incredibly talented, and the atmosphere they created was exactly what I had hoped for. Honestly, the music was the highlight of the evening and helped make up for what was otherwise a lackluster dining experience.

Finally, the banana pudding… as a Black woman, I’m just going to say it: it was not Black people friendly. If you know, you know. It didn’t have that rich, homemade Southern flavor or comforting texture that many of us grew up loving.

Overall, I expected much more from a restaurant with this reputation. I truly wanted to love it, but between the food quality, service, and lack of attention to detail, this visit missed the mark. The live jazz performance was outstanding, but unfortunately it wasn’t enough to outweigh the disappointing dining experience.

Harlem is known as the cradle of jazz in the US and has a rich history, also foodwise. After their gigs, musicians in the 1930s were often looking for a simple, hearty dish late at night. The restaurant is run by Ethiopian-born, Swedish-raised chef Marcus Samuelsson, who indeed wanted to create a community-driven gathering space that celebrates the roots of the American cuisine. As a visiting tourist, a local friend took me to Red Rooster to enjoy this typical New York "comfort food".

As appetizer I took the leading example: chicken & waffle. Served with maple syrup and hot sauce, this dish is both sweet and savory at the same time. The crunchy waffle and tender chicken leg combined very well.

As entree I opted for the shrimp & grits, without actually knowing what grits were. A famous food staple in the Southern regions of the US, this soft and creamy porridge is made from coarsely ground corn. The stew with okra, shrimp and chorizo had an earthy, briny taste.

As if the flavors that evening were not good enough already, we were able to enjoy live music while dining. The cozy, antique interior of the restaurant made me feel like I was transported back to the 1930s.

This was a great way to end our 2 day getaway! The food, service and atmosphere was on point.  Definitely a place to add to your agenda if you are planning a New York visit. Compliments to the chef, Jade and team!!!!❤️

My date and I explored this spot in Harlem. There's a $10 cover for live jazz music while we were eating our dinner. The band and singer were fantastic!

The ambiance, staff, and overall restaurant was inviting and fun. We started with a few cocktails and ordered a crab cake for our appetizer. Crab cake was crispy and thick with good flavor. Highly recommended for an appetizer.

My date got oxtail while I got Cicken and waffles. The oxtail was tender and delicious. My chicken and waffles weren't bad. The syrup was low viscosity but it added good sweetness to the chicken. Crispy batter along with a juicy bite and the waffle was decent.

I would definitely come back here again to try a different dish and enjoy live music. Thank you Red Rooster!

Kitchen 46 is very near the Al Hischfeld theatre! It’s a great place for a quick and quiet bite to eat before a show.

The food is great quality but not organic.

Nice little dinner spot -- small menu but lots of variation. Had the garlic shrimp and a fish plate. It was a great spot to get a bite to eat and a drink before heading to a show at night. Service was good -- and we enjoyed our time.

Efficient, friendly service and fantastic food! The lentil soup was super tasty. The chicken was cooked to perfection, full of flavour, juicy and so soft it was falling off the bones. Great spot for light Mediterranean fare.  Menu isn't so big that you'll have trouble deciding, but they may have seasonal options that aren't on the menus here on the Google. Nice Mediterranean restaurant near Broadway. Pleasant atmosphere and friendly staff. Prix fixe menu is nice. Homemade cheesecake was really good.

We were a party of four for dinner at Kitchen 46 on May 14, 2026. The dining experience was truly outstanding. The quality of the food is matched by the restaurant's commitment to its patrons. Based on both the exceptional meal and the excellent level of care shown by the management, I wholeheartedly recommend Kitchen 46. This is a business that truly values its customers.
